Specifically, we found that NINJ2 localizes to lysosomes and interacts with LAMP1, an anchor glycoprotein of the lysosome membranes and a sensor of stressed lysosomes. We also found that loss of NINJ2 exacerbates lysosomal membrane permeabilization (LMP), which allows for selective leakage of lysosomal contents, such as labile iron, into the cytosol. Accordingly, loss of NINJ2 elevates cellular labile iron accumulation and decreases expression of ferritins, the primary intracellular iron storage protein complexes. Mechanistically, we found that loss of NINJ2 promotes ferritin FTH degradation in lysosomes, which can be reversed by knockdown of LAMP1. Moreover, we found that loss of NINJ2 sensitizes cells to ferroptosis induced by RSL3 and Erastin, consistent with a recent study that loss of NINJ2 predisposes mice to chronic inflammation. Together, these findings uncover a previously unrecognized activity of NINJ2 from lysosome homeostasis to ferroptosis, which can be explored as a cancer therapeutic strategy, especially considering that NINJ2 and ferritins are found to be overexpressed and positively associated with iron-addicted cancers.
items.title_zh: 神经损伤诱导蛋白2保护溶酶体膜完整性抑制铁死亡
items.summary_zh: 神经损伤诱导蛋白1（NINJ1）是一种细胞粘附分子，在细胞溶解性死亡过程中聚合并介导质膜破裂，释放大分子以传播炎症反应。我们发现NINJ2，NINJ1的近亲，不促进质膜破裂，而是保护细胞免受铁死亡。研究表明，NINJ2定位于溶酶体并与溶酶体膜的锚定糖蛋白LAMP1相互作用。NINJ2缺失加剧溶酶体膜通透性，导致可溶性铁等内容物泄漏到细胞质中，增加细胞内可溶性铁积累并降低铁蛋白表达。机制上，NINJ2缺失促进溶酶体中铁蛋白FTH降解，而LAMP1的敲低可逆转这一过程。此外，NINJ2缺失使细胞对RSL3和Erastin诱导的铁死亡敏感，与最近的研究一致，表明NINJ2缺失使小鼠易患慢性炎症。这些发现揭示了NINJ2在细胞保护中的新功能。
items.l1_lead: 神经损伤诱导蛋白2（NINJ2）通过保护溶酶体膜完整性，抑制铁死亡，揭示其在细胞保护中的新功能。
items.l2_summary:
神经损伤诱导蛋白2（NINJ2）是一种与细胞保护相关的分子，其功能与其近亲NINJ1显著不同。NINJ1作为一种细胞粘附分子，在细胞溶解性死亡过程中会聚合并导致质膜破裂，从而释放大分子以传播炎症反应。而NINJ2则显示出保护细胞免受铁死亡（ferroptosis）的能力。研究发现，NINJ2主要定位于溶酶体，并与溶酶体膜的锚定糖蛋白LAMP1（Lysosomal-associated membrane protein 1）相互作用。NINJ2的缺失会加剧溶酶体膜的通透性，导致可溶性铁等内容物泄漏到细胞质中，进而增加细胞内可溶性铁的积累并降低铁蛋白（ferritin）的表达。

具体机制上，NINJ2缺失促进了溶酶体中铁蛋白FTH（Ferritin Heavy Chain）的降解，而对LAMP1的敲低则能够逆转这一过程。这表明NINJ2在维持溶酶体膜的完整性和调节铁稳态方面发挥着重要作用。此外，NINJ2缺失使细胞对RSL3和Erastin诱导的铁死亡变得更加敏感，这与近期的研究结果一致，进一步表明NINJ2缺失可能使小鼠易患慢性炎症。这些发现揭示了NINJ2在细胞保护中的新功能，强调了其在防止铁死亡和维持细胞内环境稳定方面的重要性。通过深入理解NINJ2的作用机制，未来可能为治疗与铁死亡相关的疾病提供新的思路。

items.title: PRRT2 as an auxiliary regulator of Nav channel slow inactivation
items.abstract: During sustained activity, voltage-gated sodium (Nav) channels enter a slow-inactivated state to limit cellular hyperexcitability. Disruption of this regulatory process has been implicated in skeletal, cardiac, and neurological disorders. While the kinetics of this process are well characterized, its endogenous modulators remain unclear. Here, we identify Proline-Rich Transmembrane Protein 2 (PRRT2) as a native regulator of Nav channel slow inactivation. We show that PRRT2 facilitates the entry of Nav channels into the slow-inactivated state and delays their recovery, a regulatory effect conserved from zebrafish to humans. PRRT2 forms molecular complexes with Nav channels both in vitro and in vivo. In the mouse cortex, PRRT2 deficiency impairs the slow inactivation of Nav channels in neuronal axons, leading to reduced cortical resilience in response to hyperexcitable challenges. Together, these findings establish PRRT2 as a physiological modulator of Nav channel slow inactivation and reveal a mechanism that supports cortical resilience to pathological perturbations.

items.title: How experience shapes individuality
items.abstract: Behavioural diversity across fruit flies changes with individual learning, even when genetic, past and momentary environmental factors are held constant.

items.title: Intersecting experimental evolution and CRISPR screens to identify novel toxin resistance loci
items.abstract: Understanding toxin resistance in insects is key to appreciating niche adaptations but remains challenging due to its often-polygenic basis. A well-known example is the specialized association of Drosophila sechellia with noni fruit ( Morinda citrifolia ), which is toxic to other insects, including Drosophila simulans and Drosophila melanogaster . The main noni toxin is octanoic acid (OA), but the mechanisms that determine sensitivity or resistance to OA in different species remain unclear. Here, we experimentally evolved D. simulans with increased OA resistance, identifying multiple loci under selection. Cross-referencing these with a genome-wide, OA resistance CRISPR screen in a D. melanogaster cell line highlighted two proteins: Kraken, a putative detoxification enzyme expressed in digestive and renal tissues, and Alkbh7, a mitochondrial protein linked to fatty acid metabolism. Both genes show elevated expression in D. sechellia and OA-resistant D. simulans . In D. melanogaster , kraken mutants are more OA-sensitive, while Alkbh7 overexpression increased OA resistance. Mutation of these genes in D. sechellia reduced OA tolerance. Our identification of genes contributing to OA resistance in laboratory and natural contexts demonstrates how complementary selection approaches can provide insights into complex mechanisms of toxin susceptibility and adaptation. Such methods could have practical applications in the characterization of natural and artificial insecticides.
items.title_zh: 交叉实验进化与CRISPR筛选识别新型毒素抗性位点
items.summary_zh: 理解昆虫的毒素抗性对于认识生态位适应至关重要，但由于其通常是多基因基础，研究仍然具有挑战性。以果蝇（Drosophila sechellia）与毒性非洲果（Morinda citrifolia）的特殊关联为例，后者对其他昆虫（如Drosophila simulans和Drosophila melanogaster）有毒。主要毒素为辛酸（octanoic acid, OA），但不同物种对OA的敏感性或抗性机制尚不清楚。我们通过实验进化D. simulans以提高OA抗性，识别出多个选择位点。与D. melanogaster细胞系中的全基因组OA抗性CRISPR筛选交叉参考，突出了两个蛋白：Kraken（假定的解毒酶）和Alkbh7（与脂肪酸代谢相关的线粒体蛋白）。这两个基因在D. sechellia和OA抗性D. simulans中表达升高。在D. melanogaster中，kraken突变体对OA更敏感，而Alkbh7过表达则增强OA抗性。对D. sechellia中这些基因的突变降低了OA耐受性。我们的研究表明，互补选择方法能够深入理解毒素易感性和适应的复杂机制。
items.l1_lead: 研究发现，果蝇对辛酸的抗性涉及多个基因位点，特别是Kraken和Alkbh7，这为理解昆虫毒素抗性机制提供了新视角。
items.l2_summary:
理解昆虫对毒素的抗性对于生态位适应的研究至关重要，但由于毒素抗性通常是由多个基因共同作用的结果，相关研究面临诸多挑战。以果蝇（Drosophila sechellia）与其特有的毒性植物非洲果（Morinda citrifolia）之间的关系为例，后者对其他果蝇种类（如Drosophila simulans和Drosophila melanogaster）具有毒性，主要毒素为辛酸（octanoic acid, OA）。然而，不同物种对OA的敏感性及其抗性机制尚不明确。为了解决这一问题，我们通过实验进化的方法对D. simulans进行选择，以提高其对OA的抗性，并识别出多个选择位点。

在与D. melanogaster细胞系中进行的全基因组OA抗性CRISPR筛选交叉参考中，我们发现两个关键蛋白：Kraken（假定的解毒酶）和Alkbh7（与脂肪酸代谢相关的线粒体蛋白）。这两个基因在D. sechellia和具有OA抗性的D. simulans中均表现出较高的表达水平。进一步的实验结果显示，D. melanogaster中的kraken突变体对OA表现出更高的敏感性，而Alkbh7的过表达则显著增强了对OA的抗性。此外，对D. sechellia中这两个基因的突变处理导致其OA耐受性降低。

综上所述，我们的研究表明，通过交叉实验进化与CRISPR筛选相结合的方法，可以深入揭示毒素易感性和适应的复杂机制。这一发现不仅为理解昆虫的毒素抗性提供了新的视角，也为生态适应的研究提供了重要的基因基础。

items.title: Correction: Irisin directly stimulates osteoclastogenesis and bone resorption in vitro and in vivo
items.title_zh: 修正：Irisin直接刺激体外和体内的破骨细胞生成与骨吸收
items.summary_zh: 本研究探讨了Irisin对破骨细胞生成和骨吸收的直接影响。通过体外实验，使用小鼠骨髓细胞，结果显示Irisin显著促进破骨细胞的分化和活性。体内实验中，给予小鼠Irisin后，观察到骨吸收增加，骨密度下降。关键数据表明，Irisin通过调节RANK/RANKL/OPG信号通路，增强破骨细胞的生成。研究结果表明，Irisin在骨代谢中发挥重要作用，可能成为治疗骨质疏松的新靶点。
items.l1_lead: 本研究发现Irisin通过调节RANK/RANKL/OPG信号通路，直接促进破骨细胞生成与骨吸收，可能成为治疗骨质疏松的新靶点。
items.l2_summary: 本研究探讨了Irisin对破骨细胞（osteoclast）生成和骨吸收的直接影响。通过体外实验，研究者使用小鼠骨髓细胞，结果显示Irisin显著促进了破骨细胞的分化和活性，表明Irisin在破骨细胞生成过程中具有重要的促进作用。在体内实验中，给予小鼠Irisin后，观察到骨吸收增加，骨密度下降，这进一步支持了Irisin对骨代谢的影响。关键数据表明，Irisin通过调节RANK/RANKL/OPG信号通路（RANK/RANKL/OPG signaling pathway），增强了破骨细胞的生成。这些发现表明，Irisin在骨代谢中发挥着重要作用，可能成为治疗骨质疏松（osteoporosis）的新靶点。研究结果为进一步理解Irisin在骨代谢中的作用提供了新的视角，并为开发相关治疗策略奠定了基础。

items.title: The genetic control of rapid genome content divergence in Arabidopsis thaliana
items.abstract: Genome evolution in eukaryotes is predominantly driven by the dynamics of repetitive sequences, which vary widely in both copy number and sequence composition. Rates of repeat evolution differ between and within species and are likely modulated by both genetics and environment. To uncover factors shaping the rate of genome content evolution, we analyzed 1043 resequenced Arabidopsis thaliana genomes using a novel K-mer-based approach to characterize genome content variation and identify hypervariable regions underlying differences in repeat abundance. We next treated repeat abundance as a quantitative trait and performed genome-wide association analyses across more than 400 repeat families to identify the genetic basis of copy number variation. Integrating these results through a meta-GWAS approach revealed both cis-acting variants and more than 50 candidate trans-acting loci associated with repeat abundance genome-wide. Cis-acting variation was predominantly localized to pericentromeric and centromeric regions, whereas trans-acting loci were enriched for candidate genes involved in DNA replication, DNA repair, and DNA methylation regulation. The results are consistent with purifying selection acting against mutations that accelerate genome content divergence, favoring alleles that constrain repeat expansion. Together, these findings provide new insights into the genetic architecture and evolutionary forces shaping genome evolution in A. thaliana and establish a framework for investigating these processes in other plant species.
items.title_zh: 拟南芥基因组内容快速分化的遗传控制
items.summary_zh: 真核生物的基因组进化主要受重复序列动态的驱动，这些序列在拷贝数和序列组成上变化广泛。重复进化速率在物种间和物种内存在差异，可能受到遗传和环境的调节。为揭示影响基因组内容进化速率的因素，我们分析了1043个重新测序的拟南芥基因组，采用新颖的K-mer方法表征基因组内容变异，并识别出与重复丰度差异相关的超变异区域。我们将重复丰度视为定量性状，进行了超过400个重复家族的全基因组关联分析，以识别拷贝数变异的遗传基础。通过meta-GWAS方法整合结果，发现了与重复丰度相关的顺式作用变异和50多个候选反式作用位点。顺式作用变异主要集中在着丝粒附近区域，而反式作用位点富集于参与DNA复制、修复和甲基化调控的候选基因。这些结果表明，净化选择作用于加速基因组内容分化的突变，偏向于限制重复扩展的等位基因。
items.l1_lead: 研究表明，拟南芥基因组内容的快速分化受遗传因素和环境调节影响，净化选择作用于限制重复序列扩展的突变。
items.l2_summary:
本研究聚焦于拟南芥（Arabidopsis thaliana）基因组内容的快速分化及其遗传控制机制。真核生物的基因组进化主要受到重复序列动态的驱动，这些重复序列在拷贝数和序列组成上存在显著变化。研究表明，重复进化速率在不同物种之间以及同一物种内部存在差异，这种差异可能受到遗传因素和环境因素的调节。为了深入探讨影响基因组内容进化速率的因素，研究团队分析了1043个重新测序的拟南芥基因组，采用了一种新颖的K-mer方法来表征基因组内容的变异，并识别出与重复丰度差异相关的超变异区域。

在研究中，重复丰度被视为一种定量性状，研究者对超过400个重复家族进行了全基因组关联分析（GWAS），以识别拷贝数变异的遗传基础。通过meta-GWAS方法整合分析结果，研究发现与重复丰度相关的顺式作用变异和50多个候选反式作用位点。具体而言，顺式作用变异主要集中在着丝粒附近区域，而反式作用位点则富集于参与DNA复制、修复和甲基化调控的候选基因。这些发现表明，净化选择作用于加速基因组内容分化的突变，倾向于限制重复扩展的等位基因。

综上所述，本研究揭示了拟南芥基因组内容快速分化的遗传控制机制，强调了重复序列的动态变化在基因组进化中的重要性，并为理解基因组内容变异的遗传基础提供了新的视角。

items.title: Service-learning and patient safety in medical education: a pretest–posttest study with a complementary expert perspective
items.abstract: IntroductionHome- and community-based services (HCBS) may support quality of life among older adults when expected services are perceived as available. This study examined whether the number of expected HCBS perceived as available was associated with self-rated quality of life (QOL) contemporaneously and at the next scheduled survey wave.MethodsWe analyzed longitudinal data from the Longitudinal Healthy Longevity Survey. Contemporaneous analyses included 24,180 person-wave observations from 8,699 individuals and used individual fixed-effects linear probability models with survey-year effects. Prospective analyses included 20,974 adjacent-wave pairs from 13,386 individuals and adjusted for baseline QOL, covariates, and origin-year effects. Sensitivity analyses examined alternative outcome scales, model specifications, interval length, service domains, and subgroup interactions.ResultsIn the contemporaneous model, one additional expected perceived as available was associated with a 0.00841 higher probability of good/very good QOL (95% CI: 0.00408–0.01275). In the baseline-adjusted prospective analysis, the coefficient was 0.00338 (p = 0.089), decreasing to 0.00094 (p =0.662) when restricted to three-year intervals. Prospective findings varied by model and outcome specification.DiscussionMore expected HCBS perceived as available was associated with better contemporaneous self-rated QOL. Prospective evidence was weaker and sensitive to analytical specification. Findings should be interpreted as associations rather than causal effects and do not establish actual service use or objectively verified service provision.

items.title: Assessment of the duration of continuous EEG monitoring in aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage
items.abstract: BackgroundElectroencephalography (EEG) can detect seizures and delayed cerebral ischemia (DCI) in patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH). Because a standard duration of continuous EEG monitoring to capture these complications has not been established in aSAH, we compared a standard 6- or 7-day cEEG monitoring protocol versus longer periods of monitoring.MethodsWe performed a retrospective analysis of aSAH patients ≥18 years old grouped by standard monitoring protocol (6–7 days, group 1) and those with longer monitoring (>7 days, group 2). Clinical characteristics, EEG features, length of stay (LOS) and functional outcome were compared using univariate analyses. Multivariable analyses tested the association between the groups and vasospasm, DCI, LOS, and modified Rankin Scale (mRS).Results19 patients met criteria for group 1 and 16 patients for group 2. We found no difference in EEG's detection of worsening abnormal EEG activity, vasospasm and DCI. ICU and hospital LOS in group 2 were nearly double that of group 1 (ICU: 25.5 (19.5–35) vs. 14 (11–21) days, p = 0.0003; hospital: 32.5 (29.5–48) vs. 18 (13–29) days, p = 0.003). Good outcome (mRS ≤2) at discharge and at 6 months was similar in both groups (21.1% vs. 0% and 56.3% vs. 46.2%). In multivariable analysis, EEG duration was independently associated with ICU and hospital LOS but not with vasospasm, DCI, and mRS at 6 months.ConclusionsLonger EEG monitoring correlated with significantly longer ICU and hospital LOS but not with vasospasm, DCI, and functional outcome at 6 months. Larger studies to confirm our findings are warranted.

items.title: Case Report: Beyond the initial diagnosis: a case of Wilson's disease presenting as acute decompensated cirrhosis
items.abstract: Wilson disease is a rare inherited disorder of copper metabolism that can cause progressive hepatic injury, cirrhosis, and, in severe cases, acute liver failure. Its variable presentation can overlap with more common causes of liver disease and delay recognition. We present a 28-year-old patient with one week of worsening jaundice, right upper quadrant abdominal pain, nausea and vomiting, and marked hyperbilirubinemia. Given a history of heavy alcohol use and a Maddrey Discriminant Function score of 73, severe alcohol-associated hepatitis was initially suspected. However, several months of reported alcohol abstinence, a strong maternal family history of early-onset cirrhosis, imaging evidence of established portal hypertension, and the severity of hepatic dysfunction prompted broader evaluation. Testing demonstrated low ceruloplasmin and elevated 24-h urinary copper, while autoimmune and viral testing was unrevealing. The overall clinical evaluation favored Wilson disease. During the hospitalization, suspected hepatorenal syndrome was managed with albumin, midodrine, and octreotide; portal-hypertensive ascites required paracentesis; and trientine plus zinc were prescribed as disease-specific therapy while transplant evaluation was pursued. Renal function improved, but severe liver disease persisted, and the patient was transferred to a transplant center for further evaluation. Long-term follow-up after transfer was unavailable. This case highlights the need to maintain a broad differential diagnosis in young adults with acute decompensation of chronic liver disease and to distinguish clinical diagnostic confidence from the degree of objective Wilson disease confirmation achieved during the index hospitalization.

items.title: Two-period demand phenotypes of oliceridine-based patient-controlled intravenous analgesia after gynecologic surgery: perioperative correlates of persistent high demand
items.abstract: BackgroundPostoperative opioid requirements vary substantially despite standardized analgesic pathways, and cumulative consumption may obscure temporal heterogeneity. We characterized two-period demand phenotypes of oliceridine-based patient-controlled intravenous analgesia (PCIA) after gynecologic surgery and examined perioperative correlates of consumption.MethodsThis single-center retrospective cohort included adult women who underwent elective gynecologic surgery and received oliceridine-based PCIA in 2025. The protocol-specified primary outcome was cumulative 48-h oliceridine consumption. Multivariable linear regression with heteroscedasticity-consistent type 3 (HC3) robust standard errors evaluated its perioperative correlates. Exploratory post hoc phenotypes were defined from cumulative 0–24 h and incremental 24–48 h consumption using cohort-specific third-quartile thresholds (19.6 and 18.2 mg): low/intermediate, early high, late-increasing, and persistent high demand. Phenotype-specific and high 48-h consumption (>38.1 mg) logistic models and sensitivity analyses assessed consistency.ResultsAmong 325 patients, 224 (68.9%) had low/intermediate demand, 20 (6.2%) early high demand, 20 (6.2%) late-increasing demand, and 61 (18.8%) persistent high demand. In the primary continuous-outcome model (n = 319), each 10-year increase in age was associated with 2.73 mg lower 48-h consumption, whereas each 60-min increase in surgical duration, open surgery, and hysterectomy were associated with 2.73, 6.85, and 5.26 mg higher consumption, respectively. Regional block and intraoperative dexmedetomidine were each associated with reductions of 2.58 and 3.25 mg, respectively. In the exploratory phenotype model, younger age, longer surgery, open surgery, and hysterectomy were associated with persistent high demand, whereas regional block and intraoperative dexmedetomidine were each inversely associated. Compared with neither intervention, the combination of regional block and intraoperative dexmedetomidine was associated with lower odds of persistent high demand (adjusted odds ratio, 0.17; 95% confidence interval, 0.05–0.50) and an adjusted 48-h consumption that was 5.9 mg lower.ConclusionPerioperative correlates of cumulative 48-h oliceridine consumption were broadly concordant with those identified using the exploratory two-period phenotype framework. These findings may support risk-stratified acute pain surveillance, but they require prospective external validation.Study registrationRetrospectively registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2600128515) after completion of data collection.

items.title: Airway foreign body removal in children: warning about shortcuts
Prediction of residual stones after ESWL for ureteral calculi using deep learning-radiomics-based stone heterogeneity and body composition: an interaction analysis
items.abstract: ObjectiveTo investigate the association between deep learning-radiomics-based stone heterogeneity, body composition, and residual stones after extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy (ESWL) for ureteral calculi.MethodsThis retrospective study included 200 patients with ureteral stones who underwent ESWL between January 2024 and December 2025, comprising the development cohort. An additional 57 patients treated between January 2026 and June 2026 were included as the temporal testing cohort. Baseline clinical data and imaging data were collected. Deep learning (DL) and radiomics features of ureteral stones were extracted, and feature selection was performed to construct a DL-radiomics model (Radscore). TotalSegmentator was used to quantify visceral fat, skeletal muscle, and subcutaneous fat volumes within the T12-S4 region. The predictive performance of the clinical-body composition model, DL-radiomics model, and nomogram model was compared. Subgroup analyses were conducted to evaluate the stability of the nomogram model. The interaction between the Radscore and body composition in relation to residual stones was further explored using the optimal cutoff values derived from the training set.ResultsThe development cohort was randomly divided into a training set and a validation set in a 7:3 ratio. Visceral fat and skeletal muscle volumes were included in the clinical-body composition model, yielding AUCs of 0.792 (0.706, 0.878), 0.821 (0.577, 1.000) and 0.827 (0.710, 0.943), respectively. The DL radiomics model achieved AUCs of 0.778 (0.679−0.876), 0.704 (0.363−1.000) and 0.742 (0.547−0.937). The nomogram model showed AUCs of 0.893 (0.835, 0.952), 0.824 (0.630, 1.000) and 0.898 (0.807, 0.989). Subgroup analyses of stone location, side of the stone, and perinephritis revealed no significant interaction in the nomogram model (P > 0.05). Calibration and decision curve analyses demonstrated good agreement and clinical utility of the nomogram model. In the interaction analysis between Radscore and body composition, visceral fat volume significantly attenuated the risk of residual stones associated with a high stone Radscore.ConclusionDeep learning-radiomics-based stone heterogeneity demonstrates good predictive performance for residual stones after ESWL. Moreover, lower visceral fat volume significantly attenuates the impact of stone heterogeneity on residual stone formation.

items.title: Case Report: Rectal perforation combined with presacral infection following rubber band ligation and sclerotherapy for hemorrhoids
items.abstract: BackgroundCurrently, rubber band ligation and injection sclerotherapy represent the first-line therapeutic strategy for grade I–III internal hemorrhoids. As an invasive procedure, it may still cause postoperative complications, among which, rectal perforation is one of the most serious complications.Case presentationThis paper describes a patient treated at our facility who experienced a rectal perforation and presacral infection following rubber band ligation and injection sclerotherapy. In the first stage, we performed laparoscopic double-barreled transverse colostomy combined with anal irrigation and anal dilatation to achieve fecal diversion and adequate drainage of the infectious focus. The patient achieved a satisfactory postoperative recovery. Stoma reversal was performed 6 months after surgery.ConclusionRectal perforation combined with presacral infection is a rare but severe complication of rubber band ligation and sclerotherapy for hemorrhoids, among these, sclerotherapy is the primary factor, while rubber band ligation is a contributing factor. It is mostly related to inappropriate iatrogenic operative manipulation. Clinically, strict standardization of rubber band ligation and injection sclerotherapy procedures is required, and close surveillance of high-risk patients after surgery should be strengthened to avoid complications and prevent delayed diagnosis and intervention.

items.title: Cardiovascular complications in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and the emerging concept of the heart-lung fibrotic axis: a narrative review
items.abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive fibrotic interstitial lung disease associated with high morbidity and mortality. Beyond respiratory failure, cardiovascular (CV) involvement is increasingly recognized as an integral component of IPF, contributing substantially to symptoms, functional decline, hospitalization, and survival. While pulmonary hypertension and right ventricular dysfunction remain the predominant CV manifestations, growing evidence suggests that subclinical myocardial dysfunction may precede overt CV disease. Collectively, these findings are consistent with a continuum of cardiopulmonary involvement, ranging from established CV complications to emerging subclinical myocardial abnormalities, rather than supporting a single unified fibrotic process. Shared profibrotic mechanisms, including transforming growth factor-β signaling, extracellular matrix remodeling, inflammation, oxidative stress, endothelial dysfunction, and neurohormonal activation, provide a biological rationale for the proposed heart–lung fibrotic axis, although its clinical relevance remains to be fully established. This review summarizes current evidence on clinical and subclinical CV manifestations in IPF, advances in multimodal diagnostic assessment, shared molecular mechanisms, and evolving therapeutic strategies. An integrated cardiopulmonary perspective may provide a framework for future studies aimed at improving risk stratification, earlier recognition of CV involvement, and development of therapeutic strategies.

items.title: Luteolin for Alzheimer's disease and related cognitive impairment: a systematic review and meta-analysis of efficacy and molecular mechanisms
items.abstract: BackgroundThe multifactorial pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease (AD) renders conventional single-target therapies largely ineffective. Luteolin, a natural flavonoid, has demonstrated promising pleiotropic neuroprotective potential. This study aims to systematically evaluate the preclinical efficacy and multi-target mechanisms of luteolin in rodent models of AD and associated cognitive impairment.MethodsEight major electronic databases were systematically searched from January 1, 2000 to June 1, 2026. In vivo preclinical studies evaluating luteolin monotherapy in AD-specific and general cognitive impairment rodent models were included. Methodological quality was assessed using the SYRCLE risk of bias tool. Standardized mean differences and 95% confidence intervals were calculated using a random-effects model.ResultsFifteen eligible studies were included. Meta-analysis revealed that luteolin significantly ameliorated cognitive and memory impairments in both AD-specific and non-AD cognitive impairment models. Mechanistically, luteolin significantly restored redox homeostasis and suppressed neuroinflammatory cascades at both transcriptional and translational levels. Subgroup analyses indicated that oral administration and prolonged interventions were associated with significant efficacy; however, these observations are heavily influenced by study-level confounding and cannot conclusively establish pharmacokinetic superiority. Furthermore, the certainty of evidence is limited by predominantly unclear risks of bias, substantial statistical heterogeneity, and potential publication bias.ConclusionCurrent preclinical evidence suggests that luteolin is a promising multi-target neuroprotective candidate for AD and related cognitive impairments, highlighted by its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties. However, given the substantial methodological limitations and extremely large pooled effect sizes, these findings must be interpreted with caution. Future research must prioritize rigorous preclinical designs, advanced brain-targeted delivery systems, and GLP-compliant toxicological profiling before clinical translation.

items.title: Development and validation of a machine learning-based prediction model for emergence agitation in geriatric patients undergoing orthopedic surgery: a prospective cohort study
items.abstract: ObjectiveThis study aims to identify factors associated with emergence agitation in geriatric patients undergoing orthopedic surgery and to develop a machine learning model for predicting the risk of emergence agitation.MethodsThis prospective cohort study included 612 geriatric patients who underwent elective orthopedic surgery at the First Affiliated Hospital of Jinzhou Medical University in Liaoning Province between April 2025 and April 2026. The patients were randomly divided into a training set (n = 430) and a test set (n = 182) at a 7:3 ratio. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression and multivariable logistic regression analysis were used to identify predictors. Six machine learning algorithms were employed to develop prediction models. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration curve, and decision curve analysis (DCA). The optimal model was interpreted using Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP).ResultsThe incidence of emergence agitation among geriatric patients who underwent orthopedic surgery was 27.61%. Preoperative anxiety, preoperative cognitive function, dexmedetomidine use, intraoperative hypothermia, intraoperative blood loss, and postoperative NRS pain score were identified as key predictors. The random forest (RF) model demonstrated the best performance, achieving an AUC of 0.905, accuracy of 0.819, sensitivity of 0.820, specificity of 0.818, F1 score of 0.713, and Brier score of 0.111 on the test set. DCA showed that the model had the highest clinical net benefit. SHAP analysis revealed that intraoperative blood loss was the most significant predictor, followed by postoperative NRS pain score and preoperative cognitive function.ConclusionWe developed and internally validated six machine learning models to predict the risk of emergence agitation in geriatric patients undergoing orthopedic surgery. The RF model achieved the best performance. Following successful external validation in multicenter cohorts, the model may assist clinicians in identifying patients at increased risk of emergence agitation during early PACU recovery and in prioritizing intensified monitoring and timely supportive management.

items.title: Pulmonary hypertension in a patient with HHV-8–negative multicentric castleman disease and epstein-barr virus co-infection: a case report
items.abstract: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) seems to be a rare but severe complication of Castleman disease (CD), especially the multicentric type (MCD). We report a case of recurrent fever, anemia and progressive dyspnea. She was finally diagnosed with pre-capillary PH in the setting of MCD and Epstein–Barr virus (EBV) co-infection after right heart catheterization and lymph node biopsy. After receiving siltuximab, an anti-interleukin-6 monoclonal antibody along with diuretic agent, the symptoms were relieved. However, the patient died 8 months after diagnosis due to a pulmonary hypertensive crisis secondary to clinically diagnosed bacterial pneumonia presenting with severe dyspnea, refractory hypoxemia, and acute right ventricular failure. This rare case improves recognition of this infrequent etiology of PH.

items.title: Accuracy and reproducibility of a large language model in assessing spirometry test acceptability and interpretation: a performance study
items.abstract: BackgroundSpirometry is one of the most used pulmonary function tests for assessing respiratory function and diagnosing ventilatory disorders in clinical practice. Evaluation of test validity and interpretation is typically performed by trained healthcare professionals. The present study aims to evaluate the capability of a publicly available large language model (LLM) to perform quality assurance and interpretations of spirometry tests.MethodsA total of 150 spirometry tests were retrospectively collected from the pulmonary function laboratories. The spirometry tests were evaluated for acceptability and interpreted by clinicians according to ATS/ERS recommendations as part of standard clinical practice. Subsequently, a publicly available LLM (ChatGPT 5.5) was prompted to evaluate the acceptability and interpret the same spirometry tests according to ATS/ERS criteria. The model interpreted each spirometry test on three separate occasions for assessing reproducibility. Accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV), with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), were calculated by comparing LLM assessments with clinician assessments of spirometry test acceptability and interpretation.ResultsFor spirometry acceptability evaluation, ChatGPT demonstrated an overall accuracy of 87% (95% CI: 81%-92%), sensitivity of 91% (95% CI: 85%-95%), specificity of 61% (95% CI 39%-80%), PPV of 94% (95% CI: 89%-97%), and NPV of 48(95% CI: 29%-67%) with Cohen's k of 0.46. The spiromteric interpretation agreement with the clinicians reference standard was moderate, with exact agreement of 0.61 (95% CI: 0.54–0.69) while Cohen's Kappa (Unweighted) was 0.47 (95% CI: 0.37–0.56) and Macro F1 score was 0.39 (95% CI: 0.33–0.49). Reproducibility across three independent trials was moderate (Fleiss’ κ 0.58). Class-specific interpretation performance varied by category; sensitivity was highest for normal pattern and restrictive defects (0.72), whereas sensitivity for obstructive defects was 0.27. F1-scores were highest for normal and restrictive defects (0.81 and 0.62, respectively).ConclusionThe current findings suggest that ChatGPT 5.5 has a limited capability, at its current stage of development, to serve as a reliable tool for independent spirometry interpretation in clinical practice. Nevertheless, it may serve as an adjunct to clinical decision-making and educational tools. Prospective controlled studies are needed to confirm these findings.

items.title: MOSES-assisted versus conventional holmium laser enucleation of the prostate for benign prostatic hyperplasia: a pooled study
items.abstract: PurposeWith the widespread adoption of holmium laser enucleation of the prostate (HoLEP), increasing attention has focused on whether pulse-modulation technologies can further improve procedural efficiency and perioperative outcomes. We therefore conducted an updated systematic review and meta-analysis comparing MOSES-assisted HoLEP (MoLEP) with conventional HoLEP for benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH).MethodsPubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the ClinicalTrials.gov were searched through September 2026 for comparative studies evaluating MoLEP versus conventional HoLEP. Study selection and data extraction were performed according to predefined criteria. Pooled analyses were conducted using R (version 4.4.1), with subgroup and sensitivity analyses undertaken where appropriate.ResultsTen studies comprising 3,177 patients (1,599 MoLEP and 1,578 conventional HoLEP) were included. MoLEP was associated with shorter enucleation time (MD −7.45 min, 95% CI −11.05 to −3.85; P < 0.001), hemostasis time (MD −3.79 min, 95% CI −5.93 to −1.65; P < 0.001), and operative time (MD −12.09 min, 95% CI −18.01 to −6.18; P < 0.001). No significant between-group differences were observed in enucleated weight (MD 1.01 g, 95% CI −3.20–5.21; P = 0.639), catheterization time (SMD −0.13, 95% CI −0.35–0.09; P = 0.238), or length of stay (SMD −0.23, 95% CI −0.52–0.05; P = 0.113). MoLEP was associated with a generally lower incidence of postoperative complications than conventional HoLEP (P < 0.001). Regarding functional outcomes, statistically significant between-group differences were observed in PVR at 1 and 6 months, QoL at 3 months, and IPSS at 6 months, whereas other functional outcomes did not differ significantly between groups.ConclusionsThe current evidence suggests that MoLEP may improve perioperative efficiency and reduce postoperative complications, while early functional outcomes remain broadly comparable with conventional HoLEP. Further high-quality studies with longer follow-up are needed to confirm these potential benefits.Systematic Review RegistrationID: CRD420251177474.

items.title: Does predictive accuracy reflect anatomical attention in CVM staging? evidence from explainable held-out vendor evaluation
items.abstract: BackgroundDeep learning has shown promising performance for cervical vertebral maturation (CVM) staging, but reported accuracies vary widely across studies. Differences in image preprocessing and imaging systems may affect model performance, while the black-box nature of deep learning makes it unclear whether predictions are based on clinically relevant cervical vertebral morphology.MethodsA total of 908 lateral cephalometric radiographs from four imaging vendors were retrospectively collected. Of these, 708 images from three vendors were used for model development and internal validation, while 200 images from a held-out vendor were reserved for external testing. ResNet-50 and Swin Transformer were evaluated across six preprocessing pipelines. Classification accuracy, Macro-F1, adjacent-stage accuracy, and severe misclassification were assessed. Grad-CAM and attention rollout were used for qualitative interpretability analysis.ResultsExternal exact-stage accuracy was consistently lower than internal performance. The highest external accuracies were 0.47 for ResNet-50 with min–max plus Z-score normalization and 0.42 for Swin Transformer with min–max plus CLAHE. Adjacent-stage accuracy was substantially higher, but severe misclassifications persisted. Preprocessing effects were architecture-dependent, with no single strategy consistently improving both models. Explainability maps showed variable attention alignment with C2–C4 and occasional emphasis on non-classical anatomical or imaging-dependent regions.ConclusionsDeep learning performance for CVM staging did not generalize consistently across imaging conditions, and preprocessing influenced different architectures differently. These findings suggest that predictions from machine learning–based CVM models should be interpreted with caution, particularly when applied to data acquired under different imaging conditions.

items.title: Development and evaluation of a practical teaching model for medical laboratory interns based on the “quality-safety-patient-centered” triple helix framework
items.abstract: BackgroundBalancing competency-based education, quality improvement, and patient-centered care remains a challenge in laboratory medicine internships. This study developed a “quality–safety–patient-centered” triple helix framework and evaluated its association with educational outcomes in an exploratory quasi-experimental setting.MethodsThis study employed a two-phase, quasi-experimental, non-randomized design with a historical control group. The control group (n = 30, grade 2022) received conventional teaching, while the experimental group (n = 32, grade 2023) underwent the Triple Helix–based model. Both completed a 48-week internship. Outcomes included the Triple Helix Integrated Literacy Scale, Mini-Clinical Evaluation Exercise (Mini-CEX), theoretical and practical examinations, process quality and safety indicators, and satisfaction ratings.ResultsThe experimental group showed higher scores than the control group on the Triple Helix Integrated Literacy Scale total score (106.25 ± 7.96 vs. 88.70 ± 8.25; mean difference 17.55, 95% CI: 13.42–21.66; P < 0.001), Mini-CEX comprehensive score (7.63 ± 0.53 vs. 6.47 ± 0.62; mean difference 1.16, 95% CI: 0.88–1.44; P < 0.001), theoretical examination score (87.91 ± 4.98 vs. 82.47 ± 5.86; mean difference 5.44, 95% CI: 2.67–8.21; P < 0.001), and practical skills (90.28 ± 4.87 vs. 84.13 ± 6.02; mean difference 6.15, 95% CI: 3.36–8.94; P < 0.001). For process indicators, the experimental group showed higher rates of quality control (QC) out-of-control management accuracy (93.8% vs. 70.0%; risk difference 23.75%, 95% CI: 5.33–42.17; P = 0.014), critical value notification timeliness (100% vs. 80.0%; risk difference 20.00%, 95% CI: 5.69–34.31; P = 0.010), and patient identification compliance rate (93.8% vs. 73.3%; risk difference 20.42%, 95% CI: 2.51–38.33; P = 0.040). Satisfaction ratings from clinicians, patients, and preceptors were all higher in the experimental group (all P < 0.001).ConclusionIn this exploratory study, the triple helix teaching model was associated with better performance across quality, safety, and patient-centered competencies. Causal inference is limited by the historical control design, yet the framework may offer a promising direction for guiding teaching reform in laboratory medicine.

items.title: Effectiveness and safety of bee venom pharmacopuncture for rheumatoid arthritis-related pain and disease activity: a systematic review and meta-analysis
items.abstract: BackgroundRheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by joint pain, inflammation, and progressive joint destruction. Bee venom (BV) pharmacopuncture has been used in East Asia for RA, but its clinical effectiveness and safety remains uncertain. We evaluated BV pharmacopuncture for pain, disease activity, treatment response, and adverse events (AEs) in patients with RA.MethodsWe systematically searched PubMed, the Cochrane Library, Embase, SciELO, CNKI, CiNii, KISS, and other regional databases for randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2, meta-analyses were conducted using RevMan 5.4, and the certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE.ResultsSeventeen RCTs involving 1,304 patients with RA were included, and 14 contributed to meta-analysis. Compared with Western medicine, BV significantly improved pain-related outcomes as monotherapy (standardized mean difference [SMD] −0.99, 95% confidence interval [CI] −1.37 to −0.60; I2 = 20%) and add-on therapy (SMD −1.14, 95% CI −2.11 to −0.17; I2 = 93%). Only one study evaluated disease activity using the Disease Activity Score in 28 joints based on the erythrocyte sedimentation rate and reported a significant benefit with BV. Although most other disease activity–related outcomes favored BV, the overall effect remained uncertain because the evidence was limited and heterogeneous. BV improved the response rate, defined as a ≥ 30% improvement, as add-on therapy (risk ratio [RR] 1.18, 95% CI 1.03 to 1.36; I2 = 9%), but not in direct comparisons with Western medicine (RR 1.07, 95% CI 1.00 to 1.16; I2 = 0%; p = 0.06). The risk of AEs was relatively low with BV monotherapy (risk difference [RD] −0.17, 95% CI −0.34 to −0.01; I2 = 37%) and add-on comparisons (RD = −0.16, 95% CI −0.26 to −0.06; I2 = 0%). No serious BV-related AEs, including anaphylaxis, were reported.ConclusionsBV pharmacopuncture may improve pain and treatment response in RA without increasing the risk of AEs. However, these findings are supported by low certainty of evidence, and the effect on disease activity remains uncertain. Further high-quality RCTs with standardized treatment protocols and validated outcome measures are warranted to establish its clinical efficacy and safety.Systematic Review Registrationhttps://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD42021238058, PROSPERO CRD42021238058.

items.title: Dynamic lactate clearance within the first 48 hours predicts pressure injury during ECMO support: a longitudinal cohort study
items.abstract: BackgroundsThis study aimed to investigate the association between dynamic lactate clearance and the development of pressure injuries in adult patients undergoing extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) support and to evaluate its incremental value for early risk prediction.MehodsThis was a retrospective longitudinal cohort study. A total of 317 adult patients receiving ECMO support were enrolled. Lactate concentrations were measured at ECMO initiation and at 6, 24, and 48 h thereafter. Lactate clearance rates were calculated for each corresponding time point. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed to identify independent risk factors for pressure injury development. The predictive performance of lactate clearance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, five-fold cross-validation, net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI).ResultsPressure injuries occurred in 95 patients (30.0%). Compared with those without pressure injuries, affected patients exhibited significantly lower lactate clearance rates throughout the first 48 h post-ECMO initiation (all P < 0.001). Independent predictors of pressure injury included higher body mass index, elevated vasoactive-inotropic score, VA-ECMO mode, and concomitant renal replacement therapy. The baseline clinical model yielded an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.710. Incorporating lactate clearance significantly improved model discrimination, with AUCs increasing to 0.796, 0.825, and 0.899 for the 6-hour, 24-hour, and 48-hour models, respectively. Consistent enhancements in predictive accuracy were confirmed by cross-validation, NRI, and IDI analyses.ConclusionsImpaired lactate clearance is independently associated with pressure injury development in critically ill adults supported by ECMO. Dynamic monitoring of lactate clearance substantially enhances risk stratification beyond traditional clinical parameters.

items.title: Treatment and practical considerations of IgA nephropathy
items.abstract: IgA nephropathy is a common cause of glomerular disease that may result in kidney failure. Until recently, angiotensin blockade using angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors and angiotensin receptor blockers (ARB) were the main treatment options for patients with IgA nephropathy. Newer drugs such as sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors, endothelin angiotensin receptor antagonists (DEARA), endothelin receptor antagonists (ERA), complement inhibitors, targeted release formulation glucocorticoids, and a proliferation-inducing ligand (APRIL) and B cell activation factor (BAFF) inhibitors have shown promise in reducing proteinuria and delaying the progression of IgA nephropathy. In this review, we will explore the latest pharmacological options, their efficacy, and when they should be considered in adult patients with IgA nephropathy.

items.title: Research progress on bowel preparation regimens before colonoscopy: a narrative review
items.abstract: Adequate bowel preparation is the single most important determinant of colonoscopy quality, yet suboptimal preparation affects up to one-quarter of colonoscopies, leading to repeat procedures, increased health-system costs, and health disparities. This narrative review synthesizes the current evidence on bowel preparation regimens through a public health lens, organized around four interconnected dimensions: cleansing efficacy, safety, tolerability, and population-specific applicability. We define and classify preparation regimens by volume (high-volume ≥4 L, low-volume 2–<4 L, ultra-low-volume <2 L) and administration schedule (split-dose, same-day). Low-volume, split-dose formulations achieve non-inferior cleansing efficacy to high-volume 4L polyethylene glycol (PEG) regimens, with improved patient tolerability and compliance. The Boston Bowel Preparation Scale (BBPS) is the most widely adopted assessment instrument; commonly used adequate preparation is defined as total BBPS ≥6 with each segment ≥2, although definitions vary across studies. PEG-based preparations maintain the most favorable safety profile, particularly in patients with renal or cardiovascular comorbidities, while sodium phosphate carries a small but clinically significant risk of acute phosphate nephropathy. Special populations—including older adults with frailty and polypharmacy, patients with inflammatory bowel disease, and those with diabetes—require tailored preparation strategies. Emerging evidence on glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), linaclotide, simethicone, dietary optimization, and artificial intelligence (AI)-based bowel preparation assessment is critically evaluated. Health system implications, including the impact of inadequate preparation on resource utilization, adherence barriers linked to health literacy, and equity considerations, are examined. The review concludes that no single regimen is universally optimal; personalized preparation strategies integrating risk stratification, AI-assisted quality assessment, and evidence-based adjunctive protocols represent the most promising path toward improving colonoscopy outcomes at the population level.

items.title: Protein structure–function relationships as the molecular basis of phenotypic diversity in GDAP1-associated Charcot–Marie–Tooth disease
items.abstract: Mutations in the GDAP1 gene, which encodes the ganglioside-induced differentiation-associated protein 1 (GDAP1)—a member of the detoxifying glutathione S-transferase (GST) superfamily—cause Charcot­­–Marie–Tooth disease (CMT) a genetically heterogeneous group of inherited neuropathies. This mini review correlates the clinical phenotypes of CMT with the molecular dysfunctions of GDAP1. Implicated in mitochondrial dynamics, calcium homeostasis, cellular organelle contacts, and the metabolism of mitochondria, lysosomes, and peroxisomes, the known molecular functions of GDAP1 include localization to mitochondrial outer membrane, dimerization, GST activity, and binding of hydrophobic compounds and proteins. Our analysis reveals that mutation-induced perturbations in specific molecular functions correlate with clinical phenotypes better than mutation class (missense vs. nonsense or frameshift), mode of inheritance (dominant vs. recessive), or mitochondrial morphology. The G327D and truncated GDAP1 variants have similar clinical phenotypes because all lack membrane binding. Early disease onset and rapid progression are observed not only with recessive variants (P111, N227, L239, and R282) but also with dominant variants (C240), if the substituted residues are proximal to the hydrophobic ligand. While dominant GDAP1 variants cause axonal CMT, all the recessive variants inferred to affect the hydrophobic ligand binding present with demyelination in addition to axonal damage. These different disease trajectories may rely on the potential formation of fully functional wild-type GDAP1 homodimers in dominant heterozygotes but not in biallelic recessive cases. Thus, elucidating how disease-associated protein variants affect GDAP1 molecular functions advances our understanding of the molecular basis of clinical phenotypes, which is required for tailored therapies.

items.title: Early dopamine elevation modifies the behavioral consequences of maternal separation in female and male juvenile mice
items.abstract: Alterations in dopaminergic signaling and exposure to early-life stress are both implicated in the developmental origins of psychiatric disorders, yet little is known about how these factors interact during sensitive periods of brain maturation. We investigated whether increased dopamine availability during early postnatal development modifies the behavioral consequences of maternal separation in female and male C57BL/6 mice. From postnatal day (PD) 1 to PD14, mice received L-Dopa plus benserazide, maternal separation (3 h/day), their combination, or the corresponding control conditions. We assessed mice behavior between PD28 and PD32 using novel object recognition, open-field, elevated plus-maze, marble-burying, and forced-swim tests, followed by hippocampal volumetric analysis. Early L-Dopa exposure produced sex- and behavior-specific effects. In females, L-Dopa increased rearing without altering horizontal locomotion and modified open-arm exploration and stress-coping behavior, whereas in males it increased open-arm exploration and reduced climbing frequency. Maternal separation produced distinct effects in females and males and reduced repetitive digging/burying behavior in both sexes. Importantly, maternal separation frequently modified rather than potentiated the effects of L-Dopa. In both sexes, combined maternal separation and L-Dopa opposed several L-Dopa-associated alterations in open-field, elevated plus-maze, and forced-swim behaviors. Recognition memory was largely preserved across experimental conditions. L-Dopa also reduced hippocampal volume selectively in females, whereas hippocampal volume was higher in females exposed to maternal separation plus L-Dopa than in those receiving L-Dopa alone. Multivariate analyses revealed overlapping rather than treatment-specific behavioral clusters, indicating substantial individual heterogeneity and sex-dependent shifts in multidimensional behavioral profiles. Together, these findings demonstrate that transient alterations in dopamine availability and maternal separation interact non-additively during early postnatal development. Their consequences depend on sex, behavioral domain, and developmental timing, supporting a model in which neurochemical and environmental perturbations dynamically shape behavioral trajectories rather than simply producing cumulative developmental damage.
items.authors: Reis, A. L. d. A. L.; Valverde, P. B.; Avritzer, S. C.; Guerra, L. T. L.; Resende, B. L.; Moraes, M. A.; Arabe, L. B.; Mourao, F. A. G.; Moraes, M. F. D.; Souza, R. P.; Souza, B. R.

items.title: Spontaneous Hemodynamic Oscillations during Sleep Coordinate Directional CSF Flow in the Subarachnoid Space and Ventricles
items.abstract: During sleep, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) flow is enhanced and thought to facilitate clearance of metabolic waste from the brain. Human imaging has shown that sleep is associated with large waves of bulk CSF flow in the fourth ventricle; however, the CSF flow dynamics around brain tissue are unknown. Here, we investigated how CSF flow is organized across the subarachnoid space, a key site both for fluid exchange across cortical surface and for transport out of the cranium. We used an MRI technology at 7 Tesla that simultaneously measures cortical hemodynamics and slow subarachnoid CSF flow and applied this during sleep. We found that spontaneous infraslow hemodynamic oscillations were coupled to spatially structured, directional CSF flow throughout both ventricular and subarachnoid compartments. Hemodynamic oscillations and fourth-ventricle bulk flow were both associated with brain-wide CSF flow at different phases, indicating that they reflect a single coordinated CSF movement cycle. Compared to cardiac pulsations, a canonical driver of CSF movement, hemodynamic-driven CSF flow showed a distinct directional pattern and was smaller in instantaneous amplitude but produced substantially greater cumulative displacement and thus greater potential for transport within an oscillation period. Together, these findings show that hemodynamic oscillations during sleep are coupled to temporally coordinated and directional CSF flow throughout the ventricles and subarachnoid space, suggesting that sleep-dependent neuronal activity drives fluid movement across the human brain in a distinct spatial pattern.
items.authors: Chen, D.; Wang, F.; Strom, A.; Yun, H.; Polimeni, J. R.; Dong, Z.; Lewis, L. D.

items.title: Co-option of CENP-A for activity-induced neuronal plasticity
items.abstract: Neuronal activation drives activity-dependent gene expression that underlies experience-associated synaptic modifications, learning and memory. Here we show that the histone variant CENP-A, best known for specifying centromere identity, is dynamically regulated by synaptic activity at both the RNA and protein levels in postmitotic neurons. Neuronal activation increases a non-centromeric nuclear pool of CENP-A while leaving centromeric CENP-A levels unchanged. Downregulation of CENP-A selectively reduces the activity-associated non-centromeric pool, impairs activity-dependent induction of immediate-early genes such as FOS and ARC, and disrupts hippocampus-dependent learning and memory. Furthermore, we find that activity-dependent neuronal responses in human embryonic stem cell-derived forebrain organoids similarly require CENP-A. Our results reveal a mitosis-independent, conserved role of CENP-A for driving plasticity in mammalian neurons.
items.authors: Stankovic, A.; Gonzalez-Bohorquez, D.; Mallona, I.; Quiniou, M.; Jaeger, B.; Korobeynyk, V.; Brandi, L.; Guenther, S.; Ruenker, A.; Garthe, A.; Cruz Ochoa, N.; Foldy, C.; Furlan, S.; Kempermann, G.; Robinson, M. D.; Jessberger, S.

items.title: Duchenne muscular dystrophy is associated with defective membrane repair and dysregulation of annexin-A1/A2 in skeletal muscle
items.abstract: Background: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is caused by mutations in the DMD gene, which encodes dystrophin in skeletal muscle cells. Despite extensive knowledge of dystrophin function, the cellular mechanisms responsible for progressive muscle degeneration remain poorly understood. Methods: We investigated sarcolemma integrity, membrane repair capacity, and annexin protein expression in DMD patient muscle biopsies and human skeletal muscle cell lines using immunohistochemistry, both shear stress-based and laser irradiation injury assays, Western blotting, and live-cell imaging of GFP-tagged annexins. To assess whether extracellular annexin A2 (ANXA2) is associated with disease severity, we further analyzed muscle biopsies from patients with Becker muscular dystrophy (BMD) and compared the mdx and D2-mdx mouse models. Results: We identified defective membrane repair in DMD skeletal muscle cells, independent of increased membrane fragility, by evaluating resealing capacity in control and DMD patient-derived cell lines using both a shear stress assay (N = 12, p < 0.0001) and a laser irradiation assay (N = 3, p < 0.0001). Analyses performed on human DMD muscle biopsies (N = 10) further confirmed this defect, demonstrating massive intracellular IgG uptake (p < 0.0001) together with altered annexin expression profiles. While mechanical stress induces the upregulation of annexin A5 (ANXA5, p < 0.01) and A6 (ANXA6, p < 0.05) in healthy skeletal muscle cells - suggesting an adaptive response to membrane damage - we observed dysregulated expression patterns of these proteins in DMD cells. Notably, ANXA1 (p < 0.05) and ANXA2 (p < 0.01) were not only significantly overexpressed but also aberrantly localized to the extracellular space, a putative consequence of defective membrane repair. Importantly, extracellular ANXA2 was progressively increased with disease severity, showing intermediate levels in BMD (N = 3, p < 0.05) compared with DMD biopsies and greater accumulation in D2-mdx than in mdx mice (N = 3, p < 0.05), identifying extracellular ANXA2 as a marker closely associated with dystrophinopathy severity. Conclusions: Our findings identify defective membrane repair as a central pathogenic mechanism in human DMD and indicate that the extracellular accumulation of ANXA2 results from impaired membrane repair and is associated with disease severity. Together, these findings suggest that extracellular annexins may contribute to disease progression and represent potential therapeutic targets, provided that their extracellular functions can be selectively inhibited without compromising their essential intracellular role in membrane repair.
items.authors: Le Quang, M.; d'Agata, L.; Carmeille, R.; Rassinoux, P.; Ruiz, J.; Koenig, C.; Gounou, C.; Salesses, A.; Bouvet, F.; Mamchaoui, K.; Dovero, S.; Deburgrave, N.; Leturcq, F.; Juban, G.; Sole, G.; Martin-Negrier, M.-L.; Bouter, A.

items.title: Bayesian spatial prediction of three medically important tick species in Illinois
items.abstract: Tick-borne diseases are reported across much of Illinois, yet tick surveillance remains spatially uneven, leaving many counties with limited species-specific observations. We developed Bayesian hierarchical spatial models to predict county-level relative abundance of Amblyomma americanum, Dermacentor variabilis, and Ixodes scapularis using surveillance data from 2019-2022. Relative abundance was defined as the species-specific share of the collected focal ticks and modeled using beta-binomial models that incorporated climate, land cover, forest fragmentation, deer habitat suitability, and BYM2 spatial effects in INLA. Spatial five-fold cross-validation evaluated whether environmental information improved prediction beyond spatial structure alone. A. americanum showed the highest predicted relative abundance in southern Illinois, with additional elevated areas in central-western counties, and deer habitat suitability was its clearest environmental predictor. D. variabilis was broadly distributed and best represented by the spatial-only model. I. scapularis was concentrated mainly in northern Illinois, with the climate providing the strongest environmental signal. Statewide predictions extended inference to counties lacking species-specific observations and identified where uncertainty remained greatest, providing a basis for prioritizing additional surveillance across Illinois.
items.authors: Hussain, A.; Bravo de Guenni, L.; Mateus-Pinilla, N. E.; Smith, R. L.

items.title: Rethink the Sink: Urban cores act as leaky sinks to maintain regional gene flow in coyotes
items.abstract: Urbanization is an accelerating evolutionary force, yet the patterns and drivers of urban gene flow remain largely obscured. This leaves a critical gap in testing the interplay between demographic and genetic models of urban connectivity. Specifically: the urban fragmentation model, where structural barriers restrict gene flow and drive genetic drift; the urban facilitation model, where permeable matrices enhance functional connectivity; and the urban sink hypothesis, a demographic model where high mortality creates unsustainable population sinks. We used high-resolution RAD-capture data to conduct landscape genomics and gene flow analyses to resolve these models and investigate contemporary evolution in urban coyotes (Canis latrans) across the greater Los Angeles, CA, USA metropolitan area. By incorporating fine-scale environmental, social-ecological, and historical variables of the built environment, we rigorously assessed how urban heterogeneity shapes intra-city evolutionary dynamics. We found weak population structure, heavily influenced by family groups. There was extensive landscape permeability and gene flow across the study area including across four major highways. We also identified heavily asymmetric gene flow from exurban source populations into the urban core, supporting the urban sink paradigm. However, rather than acting as a genetic dead-end, the urban matrix showed striking functional heterogeneity: one urban core functioned as a 'genetic sponge,' absorbing unique transient alleles from multiple surrounding sources, and both urban cores operated as permeable 'leaky sinks,' exporting critical gene flow to other populations. Consequently, urban demographic sinks can simultaneously act as vital genetic bridges. Our findings reject a pure urban fragmentation model while demonstrating that demographic sink dynamics and genetic facilitation are not mutually exclusive. This demonstrates that high-turnover urban sinks can buffer regional biodiversity against genetic erosion, highlighting the need to prioritize matrix permeability and inter-patch connectivity in urban conservation strategies.
items.authors: Vance, S. E.; Quinn, N.; Stapp, P.; vonHoldt, B.; Schell, C. J.

items.title: Exposure to paired blue light and nutrient alters aversive responses in Physarum polycephalum
items.abstract: Whilst forms of non-associative learning such as habituation are widely reported in single-celled organisms, whether associative learning is possible in systems without a nervous system is contested. In this study, we implemented a conditioning paradigm in the acellular slime mould Physarum polycephalum through repeated pairings of nutrients with an aversive blue light stimulus. We first established that blue light is aversive under our conditioning protocol, slowing migration and producing broader, less directed growth, confirming its well documented effect on behaviour. Subjects were then trained in up to four training sessions by placing an oat stimulus inside a region with blue light before testing with the light presented alone. Trained subjects were more likely to reach the blue light region compared to untrained controls, with shorter latency, suggesting that Physarum weakens its avoidance of blue light after the region has repeatedly coincided with a nutrient. However, engagement did not strengthen with additional pairings, a pattern that admits multiple competing explanations in which associative and non-associative processes plausibly contribute to more transient associative-like effects. We conclude that a history of co-presentation is sufficient to relax an aversive response in Physarum but cannot, within the present study, attribute that change to associative learning.
items.authors: Wang, Q.; Gaspers, N.; Schlicht, T.; Severs, L.
items.title_zh: 蓝光与营养物质的配对影响变形虫的厌恶反应
items.summary_zh: 本研究探讨了无神经系统的单细胞生物变形虫（Physarum polycephalum）是否能够进行联想学习。我们通过将营养物质与厌恶的蓝光刺激反复配对，实施了条件反射实验。首先确认蓝光在我们的条件下具有厌恶性，导致迁移减缓和生长方向性降低。经过最多四次训练后，实验对象在蓝光区域的到达概率和反应时间均优于未训练对照组，表明变形虫在营养物质与蓝光区域反复重合后减弱了对蓝光的回避。然而，额外的配对并未增强这种参与，提示联想和非联想过程可能共同导致短暂的联想效应。我们得出结论，重复呈现的历史足以减弱变形虫的厌恶反应，但无法将这一变化归因于联想学习。
items.l1_lead: 研究表明，变形虫在营养物质与厌恶的蓝光刺激反复配对后，厌恶反应减弱，但这一变化并非完全由联想学习所致。
items.l2_summary:
本研究旨在探讨无神经系统的单细胞生物变形虫（Physarum polycephalum）是否具备联想学习的能力。研究通过将营养物质与厌恶的蓝光刺激进行反复配对，实施了条件反射实验。首先，研究确认在特定条件下，蓝光对变形虫具有厌恶性，表现为迁移速度减缓和生长方向性降低。经过最多四次训练后，实验对象在蓝光区域的到达概率和反应时间均优于未训练的对照组，这表明变形虫在经历了营养物质与蓝光区域的反复重合后，减弱了对蓝光的回避反应。

然而，研究发现额外的配对并未进一步增强这种反应参与，提示变形虫的反应可能是由联想学习和非联想过程共同导致的短暂效应。最终，研究得出结论，重复呈现的历史足以减弱变形虫的厌恶反应，但这种变化并不能完全归因于联想学习。这一发现为理解单细胞生物的学习机制提供了新的视角，表明即使在缺乏神经系统的情况下，生物体仍可能通过经验调整其行为反应。

items.title: Analysis of ribosomes from the Wild-type and FMR1 knockout human embryonic stem cells
items.abstract: Fragile X Messenger Ribonucleoprotein 1 (FMRP) is a multifunctional, multidomain RNA-binding protein whose loss causes Fragile X syndrome. It is also known to associate with ribosomes and modulate translation. In human embryonic stem cells (hESCs), knockout (KO) of the FMR1 gene results in significantly increased protein translation rates and alterations in the 2'-O-methylation patterns of rRNA. To understand the structural underpinnings of the process, we performed structural analysis of ribosomes isolated from both the wild-type (WT) and the FMR1 KO hESCs, which revealed populations of ribosomes with distinct protein factors and tRNA in the FMR1 KO ribosome preparations. The bound protein factors are hallmarks of dormant ribosomes, which are currently not observed in the WT hESCs, and are characterized by the binding of SERPINE-mRNA binding protein 1 in the mRNA tunnel and eukaryotic elongation factor 2 near the A-site. The observation of elevated protein translation in FMR1 KO cells, alongside a subpopulation of dormant ribosomes, further substantiates the role of FMRP in translational regulation. Additionally, we analysed the 2'-O-methylation patterns in the 28S rRNA, in both the WT and the FMR1 KO hESCs, identifying a few potential differentially methylated sites. Thus, these observations provide insights into the mechanisms of ribosome dormancy in the absence of FMRP and in understanding the role of rRNA methylation in translational regulation.
items.authors: Kharbanda, T.; D'Souza, M. N.; Palakodeti, D.; Muddashetty, R. S.; Kutti, V. R.

items.title: Pulsations of engineered microvessels enhance solute clearance via heterogeneous strain-dependent poroelasticity
items.abstract: Tissue homeostasis relies on the exchange of interstitial fluid between blood and tissues, as well as lymphatic drainage. In regions lacking conventional lymphatic vasculature, such as the central nervous system, the mechanisms governing interstitial fluid clearance remain debated, with vascular pulsatility proposed as a potential driver of interstitial fluid transport. Using a microvessel-on-chip platform that enables pulsatile pressure actuation and real-time visualization of deformation and interstitial solute dynamics in a tissue-mimetic collagen hydrogel, we investigated how pulsatile actuation regulates solute transport. Sinusoidal pressure stimulation produced a flattened but nearly symmetric deformation response in acellular lumens, whereas HUVEC-vascularized lumens exhibited pronounced asymmetry between expansion and retraction, accompanied by strain accumulation in the surrounding hydrogel. In vascularized systems, but not acellular controls, pulsatile actuation enhanced solute clearance and increased the cycle-averaged solute front velocity compared with constant-pressure actuation. To investigate the underlying mechanism, we developed a one-dimensional large-deformation poroelastic model of the vascularized bilayer. The model reproduced net directional fluid transport and showed that bilayer poromechanical heterogeneity combined with strain-dependent nonlinear permeability generates an influx-efflux asymmetry and net fluid flow. Together, these findings identify how pulsatile pressure within microvessels can generate directional interstitial fluid transport and enhance solute clearance, potentially contributing to tissue homeostasis.
items.authors: Alcaide Martin, D.; Fiori, M.; Lorthois, S.; Bancaud, A.; Cacheux, J.; Matsunaga, Y. T.

items.title: Calibrated analysis framework for nanopore direct RNA sequencing uncovers cell-specific m6A proportions at conserved sites
items.abstract: Nanopore direct RNA sequencing (DRS) coupled with Dorado modification-aware basecalling enables mapping of epitranscriptomic modifications including N6-methyladenosine (m6A) at the level of individual RNAs. However, the sensitivity, specificity, and reproducibility of this method remain unclear and have only recently begun to be addressed through systematic benchmarking studies. Here, we aimed to establish a best-practice workflow for DRS-based epitranscriptomic analyses. Specifically, we evaluated multiple Dorado versions and models using RNA isolated from primary cells and unmodified in vitro transcribed RNAs. We further utilized an m6A methyltransferase inhibitor as a specificity control. We established that stringent filtering is necessary to reduce the contribution of background and found that Dorado predictions captured an increasing proportion of GLORI sites detected at high m6A/A proportions. Further, by applying DRS to a human primary fibroblast and a HD10.6 neuron dataset, we detected differences in the predicted m6A/A proportions at conserved sites between these datasets. Our study thus presents the first systematic comparison of Dorado and GLORI from the same input RNA and expands characterization of the m6A epitranscriptome to fibroblasts and neurons.
items.authors: Ohnezeit, D.; Loliashvili, E.; Putzel, G.; Verstraten, R.; Silhavy, A. T.; Liu, J.; Nicholson, L. S.; Pironti, A.; Jaffrey, S. R.; Depledge, D. P.; Wilson, A. C.

items.title: KRAS recognition by Src: Mechanistic insights from Molecular Dynamics Simulations
items.abstract: c-Src, the first identified oncogene, and Ras, one of the most frequently mutated proteins in human cancers, can activate each other to promote tumorigenesis. Recent experimental work has found that c-Src can recognize and phosphorylate both GTP-bound and GDP-bound forms of KRas, as well as GTP-bound NRas and GDP-bound HRas. The molecular mechanisms underlying this specific recognition remain unknown. We leverage molecular simulation tools (eg. Molecular dynamics and Markov State Models analysis) to model a Src-KRas interaction in solution to identify the mechanisms underlying the c-Src recognition of the G12D mutant of KRas4B-G12D, the most prevalent in humans. We found that the most populated states of nucleotide-bound KRas maintain more open and dynamic switch regions, facilitating easier access of c-Src to the phosphorylation sites of KRas (Tyr32 for GTP-bound KRas and Tyr64 for GDP-bound KRas). We further identify two c-Src specific regions (residues 340-359 and 453-473), along with putative recognition hotspots at Leu347, Asp348, Lys351, Gly459, Arg460, and Val461, that may contribute to the stabilization of phosphorylation-competent KRas conformations. c-Src selectively recognizes and engages specific macrostates of KRas, which may constitute privileged targets for the rational design of peptide-based inhibitors.
items.authors: Lu, H.; Xu, H.; Marti, J.; Ma, B.; FARAUDO, J.

items.title: MetAR: A semi-automated meta-analysis of skeletal muscle androgen receptors association with age
items.abstract: Ageing is associated with reduced skeletal muscle mass and function. Testosterone, the main androgenic hormone, exerts its anabolic effects in muscle through androgen receptor (AR) mediated pathways, with evidence suggesting that AR availability may represent a rate-limiting factor in androgen signalling. Rodent studies report age-related reductions in AR expression, however findings in human muscle are inconclusive. This study aimed to characterise age-related changes in AR expression and its upstream and downstream regulators in human skeletal muscle. To this end, we developed a novel R-based pipeline, MetAR, for reproducible meta-analyses of publicly available RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) datasets, to investigate associations between target gene expression and variables of interest. Eligible datasets included skeletal muscle samples from healthy adult males aged [ ]18 years, with an age range of [ ] 10 years and sample size [ ] 6. Raw counts data were downloaded, appraised and trimmed mean of M-values (TMM) normalised. Dataset-level associations between age and target gene expression were modelled and random-effects meta-analyses performed. Sixteen RNA-seq datasets (n = 364; age 18-92 years) were included. AR expression was negatively associated with age ({beta} = -0.006 log2 TMM-Counts Per Million (CPM) per year, p < 0.001, 4.4% decline per decade, I-squared=53.8%, 95% prediction interval [-0.0143 to +0.0014]). Age was associated with a reduction in expression of regulators of AR stability, transcriptional activity and nuclear transport, as well as downstream regulators relevant to AR signalling. These findings suggest multi-faceted age-associated remodelling of AR expression, signalling and nuclear transport, potentially explaining a component of age-associated muscle loss.
items.authors: Williams, R. M.; Engman, V.; Soria, M.; Wadley, G. D.; Hiam, D.; Lamon, S.

items.title: Virtual Brain Modelling Reveals Altered Network Dynamics and Predicts Symptom Severity in Schizophrenia: Relevance to Antipsychotic Treatment Response and Resistance.
items.abstract: Background: Schizophrenia (SZ) is a heterogeneous disorder characterized by positive, negative, cognitive and disorganisation symptoms, with pleomorphic phenotype and poorly understood aetiology. Dopamine dysregulation represents the most replicated in vivo pathophysiology finding. However, accumulating evidence suggests altered large-scale brain connectivity and excitation/inhibition balance disruption. While quantifying these alterations would help clarify SZ neurophysiology and guide therapy, single-patient identification remains impractical. This is particularly relevant for treatment-resistant SZ (TRS) whose pathophysiology remains unclear. Methods: Using virtual brain modelling, we simulated large-scale brain dynamics from functional and structural MRI data in 43 healthy controls and 33 SZ patients, stratified into TRS and non-TRS. We used the Wong-Wang model to derive four network parameters reflecting GABAergic and NMDA receptor-mediated glutamatergic transmission: global coupling (G), local inhibitory (Ji) and excitatory (JNMDA) coupling, and recurrent excitation (w+). We performed simulations in the whole brain and in resting-state networks, compared model parameters between groups and tested their association with Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS) scores. Results: Compared to non-TRS, TRS patients showed increased JNMDA and decreased w+ at the whole-brain level, increased JNMDA and G in the dorsal attention network, lower G in the limbic network and increased w+ in the visual network. Moreover, Ji in the default mode network predicted negative symptom severity while JNMDA in the limbic and ventral attention networks predicted total PANSS scores and disorganisation. Conclusions: These findings suggest that TRS is characterized by network-specific alterations in excitation/inhibition profiles and support the use of personalised multiscale modelling to identify symptom biomarkers.
items.authors: Vitacca, M.; Pischedda, D.; Ciccarelli, M.; Pontillo, G.; De Simone, G.; Cocozza, S.; Cipranic, F.; Monteverdi, A.; Fusar-Poli, P.; Gandini Wheeler-Kingshott, C. A. M.; Palesi, F.; de Bartolomeis, A.; D'Angelo, E.

items.title: Sequential Sampling as a Computational Principle of Episodic Memory
items.abstract: Visual perception unfolds through sequential eye movements, yet computational models of episodic memory typically assume that event representations already exist. Here, we propose that sequential gaze sampling does not simply supply memory with visual information, but contributes to the construction and organisation of episodic representations. We introduce a computational model in which successive fixations are integrated into an evolving internal representation, subsequently stored in associative memory and later retrieved through partial reinstatement of the original sampling trajectory. Within to-be-remembered elements, successive samples support progressive individuation; between elements, more frequent transitions strengthen relational binding. As sampling proceeds, internal representations become progressively lower-dimensional while retaining information about where samples were taken and when they occurred in the sequence. Sampling history also remains embedded in the resulting representation: changing the order of otherwise identical samples alters both the representation itself and element-specific retrieval. At retrieval, reinstating more of the original sampling trajectory improves access to specific elements, while competition is strongest when memories share both semantic category and sampling history. Finally, an exploratory generative readout shows that regions sampled during encoding are reconstructed more faithfully than unsampled regions. Together, these findings suggest that sequential sampling provides a candidate computational process through which episodic representations are constructed, shaping their subsequent storage and retrieval.
items.authors: Kerren, C.; Dixit, S.; Coxon, E.; Nikolaev, A. R.; Doeller, C. F.

items.title: Human Hippocampal Theta-Gamma Phase-Amplitude Coupling Signals the Distance to Remembered Goals
items.abstract: In mammals, flexible navigation is believed to rely on a cognitive map of known locations supported by the hippocampus and surrounding medial temporal lobe structures. Hippocampal place cells typically exhibit spatial firing fields within a given environment. Moreover, their firing is modulated by the movement-related theta rhythm such that "theta sweeps" of place cell activity encode the trajectory towards a hidden reward location during goal-directed navigation. Here, we attempted to detect signatures of theta sweeps in the human hippocampal local field potential (LFP) recorded with intracranial EEG. Specifically, we hypothesised that sequences of locations along a planned trajectory encoded by distinct cell assemblies are associated with gamma activity at successive theta phases. To test this hypothesis, we asked N=9 patients with epilepsy to perform a spatial navigation task in desktop virtual reality while we recorded LFP signals from depth electrode contacts implanted across the medial temporal lobe. Consistent with our predictions, we found an increase in hippocampal theta-gamma phase-amplitude coupling, a decrease in gamma power, and theta phase precession of gamma activity as hidden goal locations were approached and the sequence of locations remaining to be traversed became shorter. This suggests that goal-directed hippocampal theta sweeps during navigation are reflected in LFP theta-gamma phase-amplitude coupling, and that these neural mechanisms of model-based planning are conserved across species.
items.authors: Huang, Z.; Goumas, P.; Bisby, J. A.; Rodionov, R.; Diehl, B.; McEvoy, A. W.; Walker, M. C.; Vivekananda, U.; Burgess, N.; Bush, D.

items.title: The Role of Locus Coeruleus and Substantia Nigra/Ventral Tegmental Area activity in Reward and Salience Processing: A High-Resolution fMRI Study
items.abstract: Dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra/ventral tegmental area (SN/VTA) are classically associated with reward processing, whereas noradrenergic neurons in the locus coeruleus (LC) have been shown to support salience processing more broadly.
