However, rewarding stimuli are also inherently salient, and in most paradigms reward and salience are conflated, for example when rewarded targets are also rare and/or visually distinct. As a result, it remains unclear in how far these systems are sensitive to reward-specific properties or more basic salient properties of the stimulus. Using a visual oddball paradigm with high-resolution fMRI (n = 45), we compared oddballs that were rewarded, visually salient, or neutral, while keeping stimulus probability and motor requirements constant across conditions. Participants responded more accurately to rewarded than to neutral oddballs, and faster to rewarded than to both neutral and visually salient oddballs. At the neural level, SN/VTA activity was increased for rewarded oddballs compared with both neutral and visually salient oddballs, whereas LC activity was increased for rewarded compared with visually salient oddballs. Visual salience alone did not increase activity in either region relative to neutral oddballs. Together, these findings suggest that both the noradrenergic and dopaminergic systems are preferentially engaged by motivationally relevant stimuli, beyond more basic forms of salience.
items.authors: Hall, J. M.; Kukkonen, N.; Prinea, E.; Schomaker, J.; Krebs, R. M.

items.title: Neural abstraction of evidence accumulation enables flexible multidimensional perceptual decisions
items.abstract: Human perceptual decisions adapt to rich and changing contexts but are typically tested under impoverished conditions. To probe this flexibility, we examined decisions requiring both the selection and the combination of multiple sensory features across sequences of objects. Here we show that human decision flexibility extends beyond feature selection to combination, even across sensory modalities, supported by the abstraction of underlying neural representations. Rapid magnetoencephalographic (MEG) responses reveal a hierarchy of object representations that become increasingly abstract and gated according to their decision relevance. A shared abstract representation of updates reflects evidence accumulation collapsed onto the relevant axis across unidimensional (selection-based) and multidimensional (combination-based) contexts. Recurrent neural networks tested under the same conditions acquire and benefit from abstract representations only when operating under human levels of computational noise. Together, these findings provide a flexibility through abstraction account of human decisions across a broader range of everyday perceptual conditions.
items.authors: Benjamin, L.; Drevet, J.; Wyart, V.

items.title: Independently tunable subcortical oscillators enable prefrontal control of cortical coupling
items.abstract: Oscillatory coherence between brain regions varies flexibly with behavioral demands, yet the circuit mechanism underlying this control remains unclear. Theta rhythm, which coordinates prefrontal-hippocampal activity, is classically attributed to a pacemaker in the medial septum (MS), with the supramammillary nucleus (SuM) as its modulator. Here we show that SuM instead operates as an independently tunable theta oscillator. In rats performing a spatial alternation task, SuM theta frequency decreased before the choice point while MS theta frequency remained stable, reducing the SuM-MS frequency mismatch in both population spiking and local field potentials. The size of this mismatch predicted theta-rhythm coordination between the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) and hippocampal CA1 in both the alternation task and open-field foraging. Inhibiting direct mPFC input to SuM abolished the behavior-dependent modulation of SuM frequency and disrupted mPFC-CA1 coupling. These findings place a subcortical theta oscillator under top-down prefrontal control and identify the SuM-MS frequency mismatch as a control variable for interregional coordination.
items.authors: Mozaffarilegha, M.; Kolaxi, A.; Nikoletopoulou, V.; Ito, H. T.

items.title: A gαq signaling pathway in dopaminergic neurons suppresses memory
items.abstract: Which experiences persist as memories is a fundamental question in neurobiology. The balance between memory persistence and suppression is thought to be optimal for an organism to adapt to the ever-changing environment. Memory suppression is a process by which the brain limits the strength and expression of memories. Memory suppressors are genes whose disruption can enhance memory at different stages: acquisition, consolidation, forgetting, or recall. Here, using aversive classical conditioning in Drosophila, we show that Gq acts as a memory suppressor in PPL1 dopaminergic neurons. Knockdown of gq in dopaminergic neurons enhances acquisition, strengthens anesthesia-resistant memory, and impairs reversal learning. In vivo functional imaging revealed that gq knockdown amplifies shock-evoked responses in a type of PPL1 neuron. Additionally, using ex vivo imaging and pharmacological experiments, we reveal that both Gq and the OAMB receptor alter octopamine-evoked ER calcium responses in PPL1 neurons. Our results uncover a new role of Gq signaling within dopaminergic neurons that suppresses memory.
items.authors: Martinez-Cervantes, J. C.; Shah, P.; Cervantes Sandoval, I.

items.title: Nicotinic control of dopamine release shapes striatal output and engages adaptive action selection.
items.abstract: Acetylcholine and dopamine significantly modulate striatal circuits and are essential for reward learning and action selection. Cholinergic interneurons can locally trigger dopamine release through beta2-containing nicotinic acetylcholine receptors expressed on dopamine axons1-3. However, the causal contribution of this local cholinergic control of dopamine to behaviour and striatal output remains unresolved, with recent studies reaching contrasting conclusions about the extent and behavioural relevance of local acetylcholine-dopamine coupling4-6. Here, to directly test the causal contribution of this pathway, we conditionally deleted beta2-containing nicotinic acetylcholine receptors from midbrain neurons in adult mice. This manipulation selectively abolished cholinergic interneuron-evoked dopamine release in the striatum. In a reward-based instrumental task, mice lacking this pathway showed decrements in effort that depended on the reinforcement context, and failed to adjust actions in a choice task when effort and reward costs varied. Substantia nigra beta2-containing nicotinic acetylcholine receptor deletion also markedly weakened cholinergic interneuron-mediated disynaptic inhibition of striatal projection neurons, showing that disruption of beta2-dependent cholinergic control of dopamine alters how cholinergic activity is transmitted to striatal output. Together, these findings establish the importance of local acetylcholine-dopamine coupling for regulating striatal output and influencing whether actions are sustained and adjusted as effort, reward, and outcomes change.
items.authors: Guven, E. B.; Kocaturk, S.; Shiflett, M.; Assous, M.

items.title: Development of a genetically encoded fluorescent indicator for monitoring GPR52 activation
items.abstract: GPR52 is an orphan G protein-coupled receptor implicated in psychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders, but its endogenous ligand remains unidentified, limiting the exploration of its physiological functions and therapeutic potential. We pioneered a novel methodology for orphan GPCR ligand discovery utilizing the GPCR-activation-based (GRAB) strategy by developing GPR52-1.0, a genetically encoded fluorescent sensor. GPR52-1.0 exhibits excellent membrane trafficking and high sensitivity in HEK293T cells, cultured neurons, and acute mouse brain slices. Notably, it detects neuronal activity-dependent endogenous ligand release in the striatum, with responses abolished by a specific antagonist. This sensor provides a powerful tool for identifying GPR52's endogenous ligand(s) and enables real-time monitoring of its activation. Our work lays the foundation for uncovering GPR52's physiological roles and supports future efforts to develop GPR52-targeted therapeutics.
items.authors: Lan, G.; Wang, H.; Qian, T.; Xie, S.; Qian, C.; Ursu, D.; Bornemann, K. D.; Hengerer, B.; Li, Y.

items.title: Decoding super-enhancer regulatory grammar and pathogenic gain-of-function variants directly from DNA sequence
items.abstract: Super-enhancers (SEs) drive cell-identity gene expression, yet their identification relies on epigenomic profiling (e.g., H3K27ac ChIP-seq), precluding discovery in unprofiled cellular states and leaving their underlying sequence grammar unknown. Here, we present Borzoi-SE, a deep learning framework built upon the genomic transformer Borzoi that formulates SE discovery as hierarchical, cell-type-resolved genomic object detection directly from long-range sequence across 90 human lineages. Base-resolution attribution recovers lineage-defining master transcription factors across cell types. Within SEs shared across lineages, it reveals lineage-dependent motif usage, suggesting that the same regulatory regions can support distinct cell-type-specific programs. Using in silico ablation, Borzoi-SE decoded the functional hierarchy of the {beta}-globin super-enhancer, prioritizing hypersensitive site 2 (HS2) as the dominant constituent, which we experimentally verified via CRISPR interference. Trained without variant-effect labels, Borzoi-SE identified gain-of-super-enhancer variants in different tissues. At the CHRM2 locus, a single-nucleotide variant created a de novo glucocorticoid receptor (GR) motif that recruited activated GR and potentiated adjacent MEF2 regulatory syntax, nucleating a cardiac super-enhancer. Orthogonal multi-omics and population-genetic evidence linked this variant to increased CHRM2 expression and variation in resting heart rate and PR-interval duration. Borzoi-SE establishes a general framework for decoding SE regulatory grammar and prioritizing causal non-coding variants directly from sequence.
items.authors: Liang, Y.; Xu, X.; Mao, Y.; Zheng, Z.; Liu, N.

items.title: Percussive manipulations distinguish object play in capuchin and patas monkeys
items.abstract: Object play has been proposed as a developmental precursor of flexible tool use. We applied a standardized object play protocol, previously used with corvids and parrots, to tufted capuchin monkeys (Sapajus apella), a member of a genus known for tool use, and patas monkeys (Erythrocebus patas), for which tool use has not been reported. Both groups were tested in a zoo across 15 sessions with a standardized set of objects and activity plates. All capuchins smashed objects, whereas only two patas monkeys did so, a difference consistent with the per-cussive foraging of capuchins. The species did not differ significantly in behavioral variability, object combinations, manipulation time, number of body parts used, or tail use, and combination rates were low in both. The species thus differed in a specific form of manipulation rather than in overall or combinatory object play. With one species per category and small samples, these results cannot establish whether combinatory object play is associated with tool use in primates.
items.authors: Bier, T.; Auersperg, A. M.; Folkertsma, R.; Laumer, I. B.

items.title: scMTG reconstructs single-cell temporal dynamics with Markov transition generators
items.abstract: Single-cell time-series data offer a unique opportunity to study how cell states emerge, evolve, and diversify over time. However, cells are destructively measured across time points and individual cells cannot be directly tracked, making it challenging to reconstruct cell-state transitions and uncover the dynamic regulatory programs. Existing methods are predominantly based on optimal transport and typically require predefined low-dimensional representations, which can limit scalability, flexibility, and mechanistic interpretability. Here we present scMTG, a single-cell Markov transition generative framework that jointly learns cell representations and temporal cell-state transitions from unpaired single-cell time-series data. In a series of experiments, scMTG demonstrates superior performance in interpolating held-out missing-time-point data and inferring cross-time-point transition matrices, compared with state-of-the-art methods. More importantly, the learned Markov transition generator provides an interpretable framework for identifying the molecular programs that drive cell-state changes, enabling characterization of cell fate decisions and construction of time-resolved regulatory networks. Together, scMTG provides a unified generative framework for reconstructing cellular dynamics and uncovering regulatory programs that shape development, differentiation, and disease progression. scMTG is available as open-source software at https://github.com/liuq-lab/scMTG.
items.authors: Cui, X.; Wang, H.; Gao, Z.; Jiang, R.; Wong, W. H.; Liu, Q.

items.title: Joint Variable Selection for Omic Biomarkers in Time-to-Event Data
items.abstract: The incidence of the vast majority of neurodegenerative, cancer, and metabolic diseases generally increases exponentially with age. In large-scale biobanks, linking time-to-diagnosis information in electronic health records to multiple genomic (``multiomics'') measures has the potential to reveal the genes and biological pathways involved in the disease onset and progression. To date, association testing has commonly been conducted by testing one variable at a time using semiparametric Cox proportional hazards (CoxPH) models, which ignores correlation structure and increases the risk of false discoveries. To address these issues, we introduce a novel fully parametric Bayesian computational method, vampW, based on the Vector Approximate Message Passing framework applied to a Weibull model. vampW jointly models correlated features, while providing an interpretable hazard structure, producing a continuous survival curve, and incorporating prior knowledge. In an extensive simulation study, we demonstrate that joint modeling of omics data and time-to-event outcomes with vampW, substantially reduces false discoveries in comparison to marginal testing and other forms of joint CoxPH models. In 53,018 individuals from the UK Biobank, vampW identifies 219 protein associations with 24 disease outcomes, most of which are not among the top marginal discoveries. We further correct protein levels for exponential age effects, identifying 1,308 associations and highlighting the sensitivity of the analysis to age-correction methodology. Our findings replicate in independent cohorts using different measurement technologies, within data from Iceland and a novel Generation Scotland proteomics dataset. vampW also achieves significant improvement in the prediction of disease onset times: across 14 outcomes, it reduces the root mean squared error by over 30% and 26%, when compared to CoxPH variants and the deep learning approach DeepSurv, respectively, while maintaining predictive utility in minority populations. In summary, vampW offers accurate and interpretable variable selection and out-of-sample prediction within a single computational framework, making it a powerful tool for dissecting the genomic architecture of common complex disease onset.
items.authors: Bajzik, J.; Depope, A.; Zolfimoselo, Y.; Sharipov, A.; Lesayova, A.; Klein, H.; Richmond, A.; Vernardis, S.; Grauslys, A.; Andrejev, S.; Zelezniak, A.; Ralser, M.; Marioni, R.; Mondelli, M.; Robinson, M. R.

items.title: Multivalent Surface Search Dynamics Shape Bacteriophage Adsorption Efficiency: A Stochastic Model of Tail Fiber Optimization
items.abstract: Phages must locate and bind to bacterial surface receptors to initiate infection. Their tail fiber configuration critically influences this process. We develop a stochastic model describing surface search as a renewal process, incorporating attachment, detachment, and target-finding steps. Using both numerical simulations and analytical calculations, we quantify how tail fiber number, attachment-detachment rates, and geometric constraints impact the mean and the distribution of time to successful adsorption. Notably, the search efficiency shows a nonmonotonic dependence on tail fiber number, governed by a trade-off between binding stability and diffusion-mediated mobility. This optimum shifts depending on the effective bacterial density, target radius, and fiber reach. Short fiber reach imposes severe geometric constraints, reducing mobility at high tail fiber counts and leading to performance degradation. Our findings suggest that phage adsorption strategies are shaped by a balance between anchoring and exploration, with evolutionary implications for tail fiber design and infection efficiency.
items.authors: Yadav, A.; Sneppen, K.; Mitarai, N.

items.title: Drosben, an affordable system for scalable survival analysis in Drosophila
items.abstract: Survival analysis is a workhorse assay in Drosophila research to evaluate somatic fitness. It is indispensable in the study of ageing and insightful in immunity, metabolism, radiobiology, toxicology, ecology, and others. While conceptually simple, lifespan measurement is labour-intensive because it requires the continuous manual maintenance of large experimental cohorts. Here, we describe Drosben, an approach that combines a 3D-printed device to transfer flies from several vials simultaneously, a paper system for quick data recording and accompanying software that automatically digitalises life tables for analysis. We show that using Drosben reduces the time investment to perform lifespan assays by ~85% respect to handling individual vials, with improved speed regardless of user experience handling these. Using Drosben, we address the effects on longevity of chronic feeding of indole-acetic acid (IAA), naphthalene-acetic acid (NAA) and trimethoprim (TMP) - compounds used to control heterologous targeted protein degradation systems. We find that IAA and NAA mildly shorten lifespan, while TMP extends female longevity. We further show that strong static magnetic fields do not affect Drosophila lifespan. Our work suggests that Drosben can cheaply accelerate research where lifespan is used as a life history trait.
items.authors: Trinca, T. M.; Berenguer-Molins, P.; Fernandez-Garcia, C.; de Navascues, J.

items.title: Variovorax paradoxus alleviates bicarbonate-induced Fe limitation in cotton by altering the root-associated microbiome
items.abstract: Alkaline and calcareous soils can induce iron (Fe) limitation in plants, yet the responses of root-associated microbial communities to beneficial rhizobacteria under these conditions remain poorly understood in cotton. Here, we investigated the effects of Variovorax paradoxus on plant performance, Fe nutrition, and root-associated microbiome dynamics in cotton exposed to bicarbonate-induced Fe limitation. In this study, V. paradoxus inoculation under bicarbonate-induced Fe limitation significantly improved photosynthetic parameters, growth parameters, and tissue Fe status. V. paradoxus inoculation partially reduced Fe-deficiency-induced root ferric-chelate reductase activity without a significant increase in net rhizosphere CAS-reactive Fe-chelating activity. This response may reflect a reduced requirement for maximal Strategy I activation following improved plant Fe status. Despite improved plant health, V. paradoxus reduced root C levels, suggesting altered belowground carbon utilization associated with bacterial inoculation and stress conditions. Split-root experiments showed greater improvements in chlorophyll score and shoot growth following bilateral than unilateral inoculation, although the effects of increased inoculum dose and root exposure could not be distinguished. In autoclaved soil, V. paradoxus did not improve plant growth under Fe deficiency, suggesting a possible role for resident soil microorganisms. Although bacterial alpha diversity remained unchanged, V. paradoxus significantly altered bacterial community composition and enriched Cellvibrio together with the fungal taxa Funneliformis and Dominikia under Fe limitation. Exploratory network analysis identified Funneliformis and Serendipita as highly connected fungal taxa associated with V. paradoxus treatment under Fe limitation, while core microbiome and indicator species analyses identified additional candidate microbial partners, including Pseudomonas, Hydrogenophaga, Shinella, and Aquabispora. Spearman correlation analysis further associated Streptomyces with root Fe accumulation and biomass, while Epicoccum and Sordariales were positively associated with CAS-reactive Fe-chelating activity in cotton exposed to bicarbonate-induced Fe limitation and inoculated with V. paradoxus. These findings highlight the potential of V. paradoxus to improve cotton Fe nutrition under bicarbonate-induced Fe limitation and identify root-associated microbial taxa whose functional contributions require further validation.

items.title: Programming Targeted Immune Cell Migration Using Orthogonal Chemokine-Receptor Pairs
items.abstract: Chemokines orchestrate the migration of immune cells throughout the body, but harnessing chemokine signaling to engineer targeted cell trafficking is challenging because of their overlapping interactions and broad expression patterns. Here we used structure-guided protein design to engineer orthogonal chemokine-receptor pairs with minimal crosstalk to native systems. T cells engineered with an ortho-receptor selectively infiltrated tissues producing the ortho-chemokine, in vitro and in vivo. By engineering T cells that both sense and secrete the ortho-chemokine, we generated collective swarming behavior in which pioneer cells attract follower cells via an ortho-chemokine gradient self-organized by positive feedback. By providing orthogonal genetic control over both the generation and sensing of chemokine gradients, this system enables the construction of autonomous spatial targeting programs in engineered cells.

items.title: 13C-Metabolic Flux Analysis of Substrate Co-Metabolism in the Methylotrophic Acetogen Eubacterium limosum.
items.abstract: Acetogens are promising microbial catalysts for the sustainable production of fuels and chemicals, metabolizing a range of renewable single-carbon (C1) compounds with high energetic efficiency. The major challenge is their energy-limited anaerobic lifestyle, which results in slow growth and a limited product spectrum on individual C1 substrates. We previously showed in the acetogen Eubacterium limosum that co-metabolism of glucose-methanol or CO-methanol mixtures results in substantial improvements in growth and acetate productivity. To investigate the underlying mechanism(s), here we conducted 13C metabolic flux analysis (13C-MFA) of E. limosum grown on a glucose-methanol mixture, as well as in single-substrate controls. The results suggest that the main benefit of glucose cofeeding is not provision of additional ATP, but rather a reduction of flux through the ferredoxin-dependent and kinetically challenging reactions of the Wood-Ljungdahl pathway. Subsequent RNAseq analysis showed no significant differences in the expression level of genes involved in methanol metabolism between cofeeding and methanol-only controls, suggesting this reduction of flux is controlled post-transcriptionally. Most surprisingly, we found that under all growth conditions, flux through pyruvate:ferredoxin oxidoreductase (PFOR) was in the oxidative direction, with cysteine (added as a reducing agent) providing all required gluconeogenic carbon flux under CO2-fixing conditions. This work provides critical insights into the metabolic network of an emerging model acetogen that will facilitate future metabolic engineering efforts to channel flux to value-added products, and highlights the under-appreciated role of cysteine as a carbon source in acetogenic fermentations.

items.title: An mHealth intervention based on behavior change techniques to promote physical activity and nutrition in older patients with cancer: protocol for an N-of-1 trial
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Older adults with cancer often struggle to achieve recommended levels of physical activity and dietary intake. Ecological momentary assessment combined with accelerometry can provide insights into the temporal dynamics of psychological and behavioral processes at the individual level, such as motivation towards health behaviors. OBJECTIVE: This N-of-1 study aims to improve physical activity and dietary intake among older patients with cancer using an mHealth behavioral intervention. METHODS: A single-subject ABA' design will be employed among older patients with cancer ([ ] 70 years). A 2-week baseline phase (A) will be followed by an 8-week intervention phase (B) and a 2-week follow-up phase (A'). Throughout all these phases, participants will complete a daily data collection protocol combining ecological momentary assessment questionnaires and an ActiGraph wGT3X-BT accelerometer worn on the waist to measure physical activity. Ecological momentary assessment questionnaires will be delivered via a digital application to collect information on dietary intake, fatigue, and motivational constructs based on the Theory of Planned Behavior. The intervention (B) will consist of an mHealth intervention based on behavior change techniques, delivered via weekly calls, personalized messages, and a digital application. Data will be analyzed using piecewise regression models. In addition, a semi-structured interview will be conducted to assess patient experience. These qualitative data will help identify contextual factors, such as treatment-related side effects or variations in health status, that may have influenced behavior change and participation in data collection. CONCLUSION: This N-of-1 study explores intra-individual behavioral dynamics using intensive longitudinal data rather than testing a strictly reversible intervention effect. The mHealth intervention is based on behavior change techniques, with adjustments tailored to participants' progress and changing circumstances. The results will contribute to the evidence base for mHealth interventions designed to promote sustained physical activity and dietary intake among older adults with cancer.

items.title: A benign control-calibrated multiparametric functional assay supports CACNA1A variant assessment
items.abstract: CACNA1A-related disorders arise from altered function of the P/Q-type calcium channel Cav2.1 and encompass a broad spectrum of neurological phenotypes, including developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, familial hemiplegic migraine type 1 and episodic ataxia type 2. Although loss-of-function and gain-of-function mechanisms have both been implicated, interpretation of rare CACNA1A missense variants remains challenging because clinical presentation is heterogeneous and many variants identified through diagnostic sequencing remain classified as variants of uncertain significance. To generate clinically interpretable functional evidence, we developed a calibrated high-throughput automated patch-clamp assay to assess the CACNA1A variants. Twenty-six curated benign/likely benign and 30 curated pathogenic/likely pathogenic missense variants were expressed in Flp-In HEK293 cells with CACNB4 and CACNA2D1. We quantified current density, {Lambda}V0.5 activation,{Lambda}V0.5 inactivation and recovery from inactivation (T0.5 RFI), and used benign controls to define parameter-specific normal ranges with {+/-}3 Z-score thresholds. This multi-parameter framework classified all benign controls as functionally normal and 29 of 30 pathogenic controls as abnormal, yielding 100% specificity and 96.7% sensitivity. Current density identified 19 pathogenic controls with loss of function, while gating and recovery from inactivation identified additional abnormal variants with preserved or partially preserved current density. The assay generated likelihood ratios of 0.033 for normal function and 25.13 for abnormal function, supporting BS3 and PS3 functional evidence, respectively. Application to 23 CACNA1A variants identified in Australian patients showed abnormal function in all four variants already classified as pathogenic or likely pathogenic. Among 19 variants of uncertain significance, 11 were functionally abnormal and nine were reclassified as likely pathogenic after integration of PS3 evidence with other ACMG/AMP criteria. These data show that CACNA1A missense variants can produce loss-of-function, gain-of-function or mixed effects, and that multi-parameter functional assessment is required for accurate interpretation. This calibrated automated patch-clamp framework provides clinically interpretable evidence for refining CACNA1A variant classification in diagnostic practice.
items.authors: Tan, C.-Y.; Maksemous, N.; Ma, J. G.; Sivagnanasundram, S.; Shen, Q.; Sharma, S.; Goel, H.; Jacobs, M.; Stark, Z.; Kothur, K.; Griffiths, L.; Vandenberg, J. I.; Ng, C. A.

items.title: Estimating Lifetime Periodontal Burden Under Informative Tooth Loss
items.abstract: Background. Clinical attachment loss (CAL) is widely used in population oral health research as an indicator of periodontal tissue destruction but can only be measured on teeth present at examination. Retained-dentition summaries may therefore underrepresent cumulative periodontal destruction when tooth loss is partly periodontal in origin. Objective. To develop and evaluate a framework for estimating periodontitis experience from cross-sectional data by incorporating informative tooth loss under etiological uncertainty. Methods. Data came from 10,324 dentate adults aged [ ]30 years in NHANES 2009-2014 who completed periodontal and glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) assessments. Expected Periodontitis Experience (EPE) combined observed CAL among retained teeth with the expected periodontal contribution of missing teeth. Published extraction-cause studies informed age-specific weights for missing teeth. EPE was compared with mean CAL and extent CAL [ ]4 mm using survey-weighted age patterns and late-life curvature within glycemic groups. HbA1c was used as a theoretically related but distinct external measure. Results. Periodontal observability declined with age, particularly among adults with diabetes. Conventional observed-site measures showed weaker or declining fitted increases after age 70, whereas EPE retained a more consistently increasing age pattern. Late-life curvature was 0.06, 0.04, and -0.05 across glycemic groups for EPE, compared with -0.47, -0.91, and -2.70 for extent CAL [ ]4 mm. EPE also showed the strongest rank correlation with HbA1c ({rho} = 0.291 versus 0.238-0.255). Conclusions. Treating tooth loss as probabilistically informative may provide a more coherent representation of cumulative periodontal destruction in cross-sectional periodontal epidemiology, particularly at older ages.
items.authors: McCormick, K. M.; Amarasena, N.; Guzzo, G.

items.title: Genome-wide association and Mendelian randomization analyses of host response to Helicobacter pylori infection implicate HLA polymorphisms and immune-mediated diseases.
items.abstract: Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infects the gastric epithelium of approximately half of the global population, and is a well-known risk factor for developing gastric cancer. Despite the clinical significance of H. pylori infection, many genetic factors underlying host response to H. pylori remain unidentified. Moreover, although H. pylori infection has been implicated in a range of extra-gastric diseases, whether these associations share a common genetic architecture remains unclear. We performed a genome-wide association study (GWAS) of anti-H. pylori IgG antibody titers, a composite host phenotype reflecting susceptibility to persistent infection and subsequent immune activation, followed by gene-based and pathway analyses, involving up to 140,863 individuals. This included 56,967 individuals in the discovery phase and 68,211 in the replication phase from Japanese cohorts, together with an additional 15,685 from European populations in a cross-ancestry meta-analysis. We reveal significant associations between IgG titers and polymorphisms in the Human Leukocyte Antigen (HLA) class II region within the Major Histocompatibility Complex (MHC), as well as genes related to innate immunity, including CCDC80, NFKBIZ, TIFA, PSCA, and TRAF3. Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses revealed directionally consistent associations between genetic liability to higher anti-H. pylori IgG levels and a range of diseases, including immune-mediated diseases such as type 1 diabetes, Hashimoto's disease, atopic dermatitis, as well as quantitative traits like body height and weight. These genetic findings support the interpretation that host genetic determinants of response to H. pylori, particularly those mediated through HLA class II, form part of a shared immunogenetic architecture associated with susceptibility to multiple immune-related diseases.

items.title: Extracorporeal Shock Wave Therapy for Wound Management: Clinical Evidence, Energy Delivery Parameters and Mechanistic Insights - A Systematic Review
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Chronic wounds such as diabetic foot ulcers, venous leg ul-cers and burns are a major health-care burden. Extracorporeal shock wave therapy (ESWT) is a non-invasive treatment that promotes angiogenesis and tissue regenera-tion. This review synthesizes the clinical evidence for ESWT in wound management, and asks how contemporary reviews reflect it. Methods: PubMed and Ovid/Embase were searched from inception to 1 September 2026 according to PRISMA, regardless of wound type, study design or ESWT modality. Fifty-one clinical studies and 46 prior re-views were analyzed. Heterogeneity confined the primary synthesis to a qualitative one; an exploratory pooled analysis was performed for the one endpoint reported con-sistently enough to permit it. Results: None of the 46 previously published reviews covered the original evidence in its full breadth: each cited a median of 19.4% of the clinical studies available at its reference date (range 0-90.9%), and systematic reviews covered no more than narrative ones. Most studies reported improved healing across all four modalities. In seven controlled trials reporting complete healing as events and denominators, the pooled risk ratio favored ESWT (1.51, 95% CI 1.22-1.87; I2 = 0%; 689 patients). Such data existed for three modalities only, resting on one trial for two, so modalities could not be compared. Conclusions: ESWT is a useful adjunct for acute and chronic wounds. Because no previous review reflected the evidence base as a whole, conclusions drawn from it should be read with caution. Head-to-head trials with matched physical dose are needed before any modality can be preferred.

items.title_zh: 体外冲击波疗法在创伤管理中的应用：系统评估与机制探讨
items.summary_zh: 背景/目的：慢性创伤如糖尿病足溃疡、静脉性腿溃疡和烧伤对医疗系统造成重大负担。体外冲击波疗法（ESWT）是一种非侵入性治疗，促进血管生成和组织再生。本综述汇总了ESWT在创伤管理中的临床证据，并探讨当代综述的反映情况。方法：根据PRISMA标准，从创伤类型、研究设计或ESWT方式出发，检索了PubMed和Ovid/Embase数据库，时间范围为创刊至2026年9月1日。分析了51项临床研究和46篇先前的综述。由于异质性，主要合成限于定性分析；对一致报告的一个终点进行了探索性汇总分析。结果：46篇已发表的综述未全面覆盖原始证据，各自引用的临床研究中位数为19.4%（范围0-90.9%），系统综述不超过叙述性综述。大多数研究报告显示四种方式的愈合改善。在七项报告完全愈合事件和分母的对照试验中，汇总风险比支持ESWT（1.51，95% CI 1.22-1.87；I2 = 0%；689名患者）。此类数据仅存在于三种方式中，其中两种依赖于一项试验，因此无法比较不同方式。结论：ESWT在创伤管理中显示出积极效果。
items.l1_lead: 体外冲击波疗法在创伤管理中展现出积极的愈合效果，支持其作为非侵入性治疗的应用潜力。
items.l2_summary:
慢性创伤如糖尿病足溃疡、静脉性腿溃疡和烧伤对医疗系统造成了显著的负担。体外冲击波疗法（Extracorporeal Shock Wave Therapy, ESWT）作为一种非侵入性治疗手段，能够促进血管生成和组织再生，因而在创伤管理中引起了广泛关注。本综述旨在汇总ESWT在创伤管理中的临床证据，并探讨相关机制。

研究采用PRISMA标准，从创伤类型、研究设计及ESWT方式出发，检索了PubMed和Ovid/Embase数据库，时间范围涵盖创刊至2026年9月1日。共分析了51项临床研究和46篇相关综述。由于研究之间存在异质性，主要的合成分析限于定性分析，并对一致报告的一个终点进行了探索性汇总分析。结果显示，46篇已发表的综述并未全面覆盖原始证据，各自引用的临床研究中位数仅为19.4%（范围0-90.9%），且系统综述的质量普遍不高，往往不超过叙述性综述。

大多数研究报告表明，采用四种不同方式的ESWT均能改善创伤愈合。在七项报告了完全愈合事件的对照试验中，汇总风险比为1.51（95% CI 1.22-1.87；I² = 0%；样本量为689名患者），支持ESWT的有效性。然而，这类数据仅存在于三种方式中，其中两种方式依赖于同一项试验，因此无法进行不同方式之间的比较。

综上所述，体外冲击波疗法在创伤管理中显示出积极的效果，尽管现有的综述和研究在覆盖范围和质量上存在不足，未来仍需更多高质量的研究来进一步验证其临床应用的有效性和机制。

items.title: Haploinsufficiency, de novo and biallelic missense variants in CSMD2 are associated with neurodevelopmental disorders
items.abstract: CUB and Sushi domains-containing CSMD proteins are involved in neuron development. Variants in the CSMD1-3 paralogs were GWAS-associated with cognition, attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), schizophrenia and brain structure, suggesting that these genes could be linked to neurodevelopmental disorders (NDD). Indeed, rare biallelic variants in all three CSMD paralogs were recently associated with epilepsy, while rare biallelic variants in CSMD1 were also linked with intellectual disability and cortical malformations. We identified nine individuals from eight families carrying CSMD2 biallelic missense variants in developmental delay/intellectual disability cohorts. Affected individuals presented with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD and brain anomalies. Consistent with gnomAD metrics that suggest CSMD2 haploinsufficiency, we also report two families segregating monoallelic CSMD2 frameshift variants, which complement a described de novo truncation variant in an ASD proband. We concomitantly report two phenotypically overlapping individuals with de novo CSMD2 missense variants and compare them to twelve de novo CSMD2 cases identified in published trio analyses. UK Biobank analyses showed nominally significant enrichment of ADHD, ASD and neuroticism in volunteers carrying at least one rare CSMD2 variant. In silico modelling and immunofluorescence assays showed that mutated residues in affected individuals with biallelic and de novo missense variants are clustering in two regions and that the encoded proteins showed impaired membrane localization and an increased cytoplasmic aggregation. Zebrafish crispant larvae for the orthologous csmd2 presented with microcephaly, smaller cerebellum, and reduced Purkinje cell size. Larvae also displayed decreased swimming velocity, diminished connectivity between the optic tecta, and abnormal peripheral neuronal branching. We demonstrate that rare, likely pathogenic variants in CSMD2 are associated with both autosomal recessive and dominant forms of NDD further substantiating the functional significance of CSMD paralogs in neurogenesis/synapse formation.

items.title_zh: CSMD2基因变异与神经发育障碍的关联研究
items.summary_zh: CUB和Sushi结构域的CSMD蛋白参与神经元发育。CSMD1-3基因的变异与认知、注意缺陷多动障碍（ADHD）、精神分裂症及脑结构相关，提示这些基因可能与神经发育障碍（NDD）相关。我们在发展迟缓/智力残疾人群中识别出来自八个家庭的九名携带CSMD2双等位基因错义变异的个体，受影响者表现出自闭症谱系障碍（ASD）、ADHD及脑异常。我们还报告了两个家族中分离出的单等位基因CSMD2框移变异，补充了在ASD患者中描述的de novo截断变异。分析显示，携带至少一个稀有CSMD2变异的志愿者在ADHD、ASD和神经质方面有显著富集。
items.l1_lead: CSMD2基因的变异与神经发育障碍（如自闭症谱系障碍和注意缺陷多动障碍）存在显著关联，提示其在神经元发育中发挥重要作用。
items.l2_summary: CSMD2基因变异与神经发育障碍（NDD）的关联研究显示，CUB和Sushi结构域的CSMD蛋白在神经元发育中发挥重要作用。已有研究表明，CSMD1-3基因的变异与认知障碍、注意缺陷多动障碍（ADHD）、精神分裂症及脑结构异常相关，提示这些基因可能与神经发育障碍密切相关。在我们的研究中，我们在发展迟缓和智力残疾人群中识别出来自八个家庭的九名携带CSMD2双等位基因错义变异的个体，这些受影响者表现出自闭症谱系障碍（ASD）、ADHD及脑部异常。此外，我们还报告了两个家族中分离出的单等位基因CSMD2框移变异，这些变异补充了在ASD患者中描述的de novo截断变异。通过分析，我们发现携带至少一个稀有CSMD2变异的志愿者在ADHD、ASD和神经质方面有显著富集，进一步支持了CSMD2基因变异与神经发育障碍之间的关联。这些发现为理解CSMD2基因在神经发育障碍中的作用提供了新的证据，强调了该基因在相关疾病中的潜在致病机制。

items.title: A Growing Burden, a Persistent Gap: Cannabinoid Hyperemesis Syndrome Education and Emergency Department Trends in Michigans Legal Cannabis Market
items.abstract: Background: Since Michigan's legalization of recreational adult-use cannabis in December 2018, health care providers in the city of Kalamazoo, Michigan, have informally observed an increase in cannabinoid hyperemesis syndrome (CHS) presentations, although the extent of this increase has not been formally characterized locally. CHS is frequently underrecognized and misdiagnosed, often resulting in repeated emergency department (ED) visits and substantial diagnostic costs before a diagnosis is reached. Despite this clinical and financial burden, it is unclear whether consumers are adequately informed of this risk through point-of-sale or public health resources. Methods: A cross-sectional environmental scan was conducted to identify publicly available educational content about CHS on the websites of licensed cannabis retailers in Kalamazoo and relevant public health agencies. Provisioning centers and public health websites were screened using a structured coding rubric developed specifically for the environmental scan to assess the presence, depth, web page placement, and intended audience of CHS-related content. Additionally, the electronic medical records at a local teaching hospital in Kalamazoo were queried to identify ED visits with a primary diagnosis of CHS from January 1, 2010 to December 31, 2025. Results: Before the legalization of marijuana, the hospital recorded six ED encounters with the primary diagnosis of CHS between January 2010 and November 2018, and 274 ED encounters between December 2018 and December 2025 (mean age: 29 years; 157 females, 123 males). The incidence rate of CHS-related ED encounters was 57.2 times higher during the post-legalization period than during the pre-legalization period (95% CI, 26.0-157.3; exact Poisson rate-ratio test, p < 0.0001). Among the licensed Kalamazoo provisioning centers reviewed, only one mentioned CHS as a warning but did not describe symptoms or offer medical guidance. CHS content was not identified on the websites of the state or local health departments. Conclusion: Despite the growing clinical concern regarding CHS, consumer-facing educational resources remain scarce. Although this study cannot establish a causal relationship between the availability of CHS-related educational content and the observed increase in ED encounters following legalization, it identifies a substantial lack of CHS-specific warnings in the evaluated consumer-facing resources. Given the clinical and potential economic burden associated with delayed CHS recognition, we recommend that Michigans existing point-of-sale pamphlet requirement be amended to include CHS-specific warning language.
items.authors: Lorbeer, E. R.; Bronson, N.; Burgard, L. A.; Engle, M. E.; Randhawa, D. S.; Sotiroff, P. V.; Walker, H. R.; Zhu, H.; Mastenbrook, J. D.

items.title: OSS-DBS v2: Simulation Platform for Biophysical Modelling of Deep Brain Stimulation
items.abstract: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) is a well-established therapy for various neurological disorders. Clinical outcomes of DBS depend on electrode placement and stimulation programming, with growing evidence suggesting that targeting specific sites and networks can improve therapeutic efficacy. This targeting can be facilitated using high-accuracy, multi-modal biophysical models. In this article, we present the open-source platform OSS-DBS v2 that enables researchers and clinicians to build such biophys- ical models. Building upon previous work, the new version combines automated volume conductor generation, accurate and efficient electric field modelling and stimulation-driven neural simulations. OSS-DBS v2 provides an extensive library of intracranial electrodes, which can be modelled simul- taneously to test complex stimulation paradigms. Its application programming interface facilitates integration of external data workflows, such as impedance measurements. Furthermore, an integration with the Lead-DBS toolbox offered a straightforward graphical user interface for stimulation volume and pathway activation modelling, further complemented by an optimization framework. OSS-DBS v2 relies entirely on open-source software, supports all major operating systems and is designed for efficient execution on consumer-grade hardware.
items.authors: Zimmermann, J.; Payonk, J. P.; Che, L. V.; Schöberl, J.; Dembek, T. A.; Horn, A.; van Rienen, U.; Butenko, K.

items.title: Epigenetic patterns and methylation-based models for robust outcome prediction in osteosarcoma
items.abstract: Osteosarcoma (OSA) is an aggressive bone malignancy primarily affecting children and young adults. Survival has remained unchanged for at least three decades, and no robust molecular prognostic factors have emerged that might help improve this outcome. Complex genomic architecture and genetic heterogeneity of OSA have constrained identification and validation of such molecular predictors. Recent work has shown that DNA methylation is associated with outcome, yet clinically applicable models building on these findings have not been developed. To address this unmet need, we developed and validated region-based methylation models for individualized risk prognostication and treatment response prediction at the time of diagnosis. These findings were further contextualized through an unsupervised exploration of methylation features, showing that widespread global hypermethylation was associated with unfavorable outcomes. The prognostic effect of methylation was independent of known confounding factors. Additionally, an examination of methylation-derived epigenetic age provided orthogonal information with significant association to outcome. Finally, clustering phenotypes were compared between methylation and several other genomic layers (mRNA, miRNA, and copy number variation) and showed little overlap with one another. Together, these findings establish a foundation for unique methylation-based outcome stratification at the time of diagnosis and underscore the need for continued investigation toward clinical application.
items.authors: Bowers, J. J.; Ramavenkat, N.; Lietz, C. E.; Hugaboom, M.; Madupur, A.; Choy, E.; Cote, G.; Lee, H.; Aryee, M. J.; Spentzos, D.

items.title: Posttraumatic Stress Disorder Epigenome-Wide Association Studies in the Million Veteran Program
items.abstract: Genomic studies have improved our understanding of posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) biology. Epigenetic differences in DNA methylation can reflect environmental influences, which are critical in PTSD etiology, and may additionally differentiate between PTSD cases and controls or distinguish severity of PTSD symptoms. We conducted epigenome-wide association studies (EWAS) of PTSD in 22,141 subjects from the United States V.A. Million Veteran Program (MVP), using the PTSD Checklist (PCL-C), including 17,674 European ancestry (EUR), 3,430 African ancestry (AFR), and 1,037 admixed American descent (AMR) individuals. We evaluated the 17-item PCL-C and its symptom subdomains (re-experiencing, avoidance, and hyperarousal) and used our previously-reported algorithmically-defined PTSD diagnoses validated against clinical records. There were 9,413 total cases of Lifetime PTSD and 27,257 controls, with 5,184 cases and 19,382 controls in EUR, 3,095 cases and 6,240 controls in AFR, and 1,134 cases and 1,635 controls in AMR. We identified a total of 272 epigenome-wide-significant associated CpG sites across all PTSD traits, or 28 after adjusting for smoking status. We replicated 5 out of 11 CpG sites reported in a prior (Psychiatric Genomics Consortium) PTSD EWAS. There was significant enrichment of genes downregulated in somatostatin interneurons and of genes expressed in GABAergic interneurons. Regression analyses showed that PTSD case status was significantly correlated with accelerated DNA methylation aging. Contrary to previous PTSD EWAS findings, smoking status stratification suggested that the association between PTSD and methylation of the AHRR gene may be confounded by smoking status. This is the largest-scale PTSD EWAS in multiple ancestries and the first large PTSD EWAS on symptom severity. We replicate findings from previous EWAS and greatly extend knowledge of the epigenetics of PTSD.
items.authors: Beck, S. E.; Levey, D. F.; Galimberti, M.; Overstreet, C.; Chen, J.; Gupta, P.; Dao, C.; Lesch, B. J.; Montalvo-Ortiz, J. L.; Harrington, K. M.; The V.A. Million Veteran Program,  ; Gaziano, J. M.; Krystal, J. H.; Polimanti, R.; Girgenti, M. J.; Stein, M. B.; Gelernter, J.

items.title: Immune Training with BCG therapy in Diabetes: Outcomes of a Phase 2 randomized clinical trial
items.abstract: BCG is a well recognized old generic drug that can mold the human immune system through Immune Training. Broad basic science studies support Immune Training, but formal randomized placebo control trials are frequently lacking for confirmation of human benefits. Here we report on a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2 trial with up to 8 years of follow-up. The primary outcome was mean percent change from baseline in HbA1c. At year 5, HbA1c in the BCG group was reduced from baseline by 7.04% (P=0.0006) and at year 8 by 12.84% (P=0.0001), whereas HbA1c did not change from baseline in the placebo group at either time point. Longitudinal percentage changes in HbA1c from baseline using mixed model repeated measures analysis with a comparison of BCG versus Placebo arms was significant (p=0.0017). This shows durable long term improvements lowering of HbA1c only with BCG immunotherapy. Secondary outcomes were also significant. There was a statistically significant reduction in average insulin dose only in the BCG-treated group (P=0.024). Glycemic improvements occurred without recovery of C-peptide from negligible baseline levels, suggesting no pancreas contribution. Blood sugar values obtained from continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) similarly showed BCG immunotherapy lowers blood sugars compared to the Placebo arm (P=0.0189). CGM data also showed BCG immunotherapy resulted in an up to 183.7% improvement over baseline in time spent in normoglycemia (blood sugar in the normal range of 70-99 mg/dL) (P=0.0391). A sensitivity analysis confirmed BCG specific reductions in HbA1c were robust and durable at least to Year 08 (P<0.0001). BCG was safe. These finding support improved blood sugar control through immune training of metabolism without a contribution of the pancreas even after long standing T1D. Trial registration: NCT02081326.
items.authors: Faustman, D. L.; Braley, J. E.; Hullavarad, N. S.; Bulczynski, E. R.; Dorsey, J. L.; Kartsounis, N. G.; Tran, L. T.; Thach, B. J.; Hayashi, H. J.; Mounier, D. A.; Adams, L. A.; Bradley, S. E.; Hashiguchi, S.; Zheng, H.; Kuhtreiber, W. M.

items.title: Neuronal FICD shapes motivated behavior through modulation of dopamine receptor dynamics
items.abstract: Motivated behaviors rely on dopaminergic signaling, which in turn depends on the correct folding and trafficking of receptors through the endoplasmic reticulum (ER). Within the ER, the AMPylase enzyme FICD acts as a molecular rheostat through its modification of the chaperone BiP, dynamically tuning the organelle's responsiveness to folding perturbations and cellular stress. While the biochemistry of FICD is well-established, its role in complex animal behavior remains poorly understood. Here, we identify FICD as a conserved contributor to the generation of motivated behavior. In Drosophila, pan-neuronal knockdown of dFic significantly reduces feeding, spontaneous locomotion, and reward-seeking behavior. These alterations occur without disrupting circadian architecture, motor capacity, or homeostatic hunger, indicating a specific loss of motivational drive. Depleting dFic within subsets of dopamine receptor-expressing (Dop1R1) neurons recapitulates these behavioral alterations. Transcriptomic profiling reveals that dFic depletion does not induce a canonical unfolded protein response, pointing to a specific post-transcriptional alteration rather than global ER stress. At the molecular level, dysregulated dFic alters the localization and abundance of Dop1R1. Finally, we demonstrate that this regulatory axis is evolutionarily conserved, as loss of FICD similarly diminishes motivated behaviors in C. elegans and mice. Together, these findings implicate FICD in the generation of motivated behavior and link dynamic control of ER proteostasis to dopamine-receptor maturation.
items.authors: Weaver, K. J.; Abdon, B.; Toth, B.; Jack, A.; Giblin, W.; Burgess, C. R.; Pletcher, S. D.; truttmann, m. c.
items.title_zh: FICD通过调节多巴胺受体动态影响动机行为
items.summary_zh: 动机行为依赖于多巴胺信号传导，而这一过程又依赖于受体在内质网中的正确折叠和运输。AMP酰化酶FICD在内质网中通过修饰伴侣蛋白BiP，动态调节细胞器对折叠扰动和细胞压力的响应。我们发现FICD是产生动机行为的重要保守因子。在果蝇中，广泛敲低dFic显著减少了进食、自发运动和寻求奖励的行为，而不影响昼夜节律、运动能力或内稳态饥饿，表明动机驱动的特异性丧失。对表达多巴胺受体(Dop1R1)神经元中dFic的耗竭重现了这些行为变化。转录组分析显示，dFic耗竭未引发经典的未折叠蛋白反应，指向特定的转录后改变而非全局内质网压力。在分子水平上，失调的dFic改变了Dop1R1的定位和丰度。最后，我们证明这一调节轴在进化上是保守的，FICD的缺失同样减少了动机行为。
items.l1_lead: FICD通过调节多巴胺受体的动态变化，影响动机行为，其缺失会显著降低果蝇的进食和寻求奖励行为。
items.l2_summary:
动机行为的形成依赖于多巴胺信号传导，而这一过程又与多巴胺受体在内质网中的正确折叠和运输密切相关。研究发现，AMP酰化酶FICD（FIC domain-containing protein）在内质网中通过修饰伴侣蛋白BiP，动态调节细胞器对折叠扰动和细胞压力的响应，进而影响动机行为。具体而言，在果蝇中，广泛敲低dFic（果蝇FICD基因）显著减少了进食、自发运动和寻求奖励的行为，而对昼夜节律、运动能力或内稳态饥饿没有显著影响，这表明动机驱动的特异性丧失。进一步的实验显示，在表达多巴胺受体Dop1R1的神经元中耗竭dFic同样重现了这些行为变化。

转录组分析结果表明，dFic的耗竭并未引发经典的未折叠蛋白反应，指向特定的转录后改变而非全局内质网压力。这一发现提示FICD在调节多巴胺受体的动态方面发挥着重要作用。具体而言，失调的dFic改变了Dop1R1的定位和丰度，进一步影响了多巴胺信号的传递。最后，研究还证明了这一调节轴在进化上是保守的，FICD的缺失同样导致动机行为的减少。这些结果强调了FICD在动机行为中的关键作用，揭示了其通过调节多巴胺受体动态来影响行为的机制，为理解动机行为的生物学基础提供了新的视角。

items.title: Viral dispersal drives changes in population composition
items.abstract: In an acute viral infection, a small seeding population expands rapidly over several orders of magnitude, then declines. This vast population growth is accompanied by spatial expansion as infection spreads to new anatomical sites within the host. Evolutionary theory predicts that spatially expanding populations experience more extreme stochastic losses of genetic diversity than spatially unstructured populations. To test this prediction in the context of viral dynamics, we evaluated the impact of spatial expansion on viral population genetic structure and assessed how modulators of viral dispersal affected this structure. To this end, we developed a means of implementing the spatial expansion of influenza A virus in cell culture and applied it to a viral population carrying a diverse genetic barcode. Across this simplified cellular landscape, we found that spatial expansion produces a patchwork of distinct viral subpopulations. We then evaluated the consequences for population structure of two modulators of viral dispersal: extracellular viscosity and a common polymorphism in the viral attachment protein. Both physical constraint and viral phenotype altered the extent of genetic bottlenecking and spatial heterogeneity that developed during expansion, indicating that environmental features and viral traits that modulate dispersal also modulate viral population composition, diversity and evolution.
items.authors: Holmes, K. E.; Sims, A.; Ferreri, L. M.; Ortiz, L.; Elie, B.; Koelle, K.; VanInsberghe, D.; Lowen, A. C.

items.title: Reversible fixation of microbial cells for targeted genomics
items.abstract: Phylogeny- or activity-based fluorescent labelling of microorganisms coupled with fluorescence activated cell sorting (FACS) is a powerful approach to rapidly isolate cells of interest from complex communities for targeted genomics. However, the method has not been widely adopted because standard paraformaldehyde or ethanol fixation procedures hamper nucleic acid recovery and/or long-term sample storage. Here, we present dithiobis(succinimidyl propionate) (DSP) as a reversible fixative for microbial cells that enables fluorescence imaging and DNA extraction and amplification for sequencing. DSP fixation is compatible with widely used fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) approaches and bioorthogonal non-canonical amino acid tagging, and can be applied to diverse sample types, where it consistently performed as well as paraformaldehyde. Furthermore, high-quality genomes were obtained from individual and multiple bacterial cells selectively extracted from complex samples using FISH-FACS. Thus, DSP is a dual-use fixative for microbiome imaging and sequencing, improving targeted microbial genomics.
items.authors: Engelberts, J. P.; Wasmund, K.; Mussmann, M.; Solntseva, N.; Pereira, F. C.; Rinke, C.; Prabhu, A.; Volmer, J. G.; Hanson, B. T.; Hausmann, B.; Osvatic, J.; Tyson, G. W.; McIlroy, S. J.; Loy, A.
items.title_zh: 可逆固定微生物细胞以实现靶向基因组学
items.summary_zh: 基于系统发育或活性标记的微生物荧光标记结合荧光激活细胞分选（FACS）是一种强有力的方法，可快速从复杂群落中分离感兴趣的细胞以进行靶向基因组学。然而，传统的多聚甲醛或乙醇固定程序限制了核酸的回收和长期样本存储。本文提出了二硫代双（琥珀酰亚胺丙酸酯）（DSP）作为微生物细胞的可逆固定剂，能够进行荧光成像及DNA提取和扩增以进行测序。DSP固定与广泛使用的原位荧光杂交（FISH）方法和生物正交非典型氨基酸标记兼容，适用于多种样本类型，其性能与多聚甲醛相当。此外，通过FISH-FACS从复杂样本中选择性提取的单个和多个细菌细胞获得了高质量基因组。因此，DSP是一种双重用途的固定剂，适用于微生物组成像和测序，提升了靶向微生物基因组学的研究。
items.l1_lead: 二硫代双（琥珀酰亚胺丙酸酯）作为可逆固定剂，能有效提升微生物靶向基因组学研究的效率，兼容荧光成像和DNA提取。
items.l2_summary:
本文探讨了一种新型的可逆固定剂——二硫代双（琥珀酰亚胺丙酸酯）（DSP），用于微生物细胞的固定，以实现靶向基因组学的研究。传统的固定方法，如多聚甲醛和乙醇，虽然广泛应用，但在核酸的回收和长期样本存储方面存在显著限制。DSP的引入为解决这一问题提供了新的思路。DSP不仅能够进行有效的荧光成像，还兼容DNA的提取和扩增，适用于后续的测序分析。

研究表明，DSP固定的微生物细胞在性能上与传统的多聚甲醛相当，且能够与原位荧光杂交（FISH）方法和生物正交非典型氨基酸标记相结合，适用于多种样本类型。这种固定剂的双重用途使其在微生物组成像和基因组测序中均表现出色。通过FISH-荧光激活细胞分选（FACS）技术，从复杂的微生物群落中选择性提取的单个和多个细菌细胞，能够获得高质量的基因组数据，为靶向微生物基因组学的研究提供了有力支持。

总的来说，DSP作为一种可逆固定剂，不仅提升了微生物细胞的固定效果，还为后续的基因组学研究提供了更为灵活和高效的解决方案，推动了微生物研究的进展。

items.title: Birth synchronisation increases allonursing opportunities in free-ranging dogs
items.abstract: Over 50 years ago, the hypothesis emerged that co-resident women synchronise menstruation through pheromonal cues. This idea has persisted as a widespread narrative and has subsequently been extrapolated to other animals as well. Indeed, reproductive synchrony has many potential benefits, including creating allonursing opportunities and facilitating female mate choice. Nevertheless, little evidence exists of female vertebrates synchronising their oestrus beyond seasonal effects, through socially mediated cues. We analysed reproductive synchrony in free-ranging dogs, which combine weak, population-dependent reproductive seasonality with facultative cooperative breeding. Controlling for seasonality, we show that birth synchrony was higher among co-resident, maternally related females, suggesting synchronisation among individuals who are likely to cooperate. This was supported by our finding that birth synchrony and maternal kinship independently increased the probability and frequency of allonursing. Finally, preliminary evidence shows that oestrus synchrony decreased male monopolisation. These findings contribute to the debate on socially mediated reproductive synchronisation, suggesting that it may have mainly evolved because it facilitates cooperative breeding.
items.authors: Vanderheyden, M.; Truffaz, N.; Chaignon, B.; Car, C.; Pilot, M.; Cimarelli, G.; Marshall-Pescini, S.; Range, F.; Berghaenel, A.

items.title: Do LLM Proposers Improve Budgeted Search for Ionizable Lipids?
items.abstract: Efficient lipid design under limited experimental budgets is a central challenge in computational chemistry and drug discovery. We introduce LEAF (Lipid Evolutionary Adaptive Framework), a matched-budget protocol for testing whether language-model proposers improve combinatorial molecular search relative to classical baselines. The study uses a 30,044-candidate ionizable-lipid space, a frozen Gaussian-process oracle fitted to experimental potency labels, and a separate active-learning surrogate. Four language models evaluated over eight seeds and three splits show no significant improvement over genetic-algorithm or random-search baselines. For Llama 8B, 79.1% of acquisition-selected queries repeat previously evaluated archive members. Removing duplicates reduces the performance gap on some splits but increases proposal cost and can prevent budget exhaustion. Larger models reduce duplication without establishing superiority or equivalence. Exploratory scored prompts and stricter novelty controls yield positive median differences against the genetic algorithm, yet wide intervals and shared-seed dependence preclude stronger conclusions. A validated single-assay reanalysis preserves the chemotype-cold deficit at a smaller numerical scale, and exploratory expected hypervolume improvement does not reverse the result. Follow-up checks address whether proposers genuinely use injected evidence. These checks include a zero-shot leakage probe, rank-only and chain-of-thought-rationale prompts, a score-shuffle perturbation, an evidence-conflict probe, and a genuine reasoning-mode proposer. They show measurable engagement with supplied information without a corresponding performance gain. LEAF isolates proposal quality as the experimental variable and documents a concrete failure mode of zero-shot LLM proposers under controlled budgets.
items.authors: Singh, H.; SINGH, R. K.; Krishna, C. S.; Srivastava, S. P.; Gorantla, R.

items.title: BioMod: Biological Module Tokenization for Single-Cell Foundation Modeling
items.abstract: Single-cell foundation models typically represent cells as flat sequences of individual genes, requiring higher-order biological organization to be inferred implicitly from sparse expression profiles. Similar to the evolution from character-level to semantic tokenization in natural language processing,we hypothesize that cellular states can be more efficiently represented using biologically meaningful intermediate units. Here we present BioMod, a 50-million-parameter single-cell foundation model that introduces biological modules as representation units between genes and cells. BioMod constructs an overlapping vocabulary of 660 biological modules derived from curated pathways and data-driven gene programs, replacing thousands of gene-level inputs with compact module representations. Pretrained on approximately 73 million human cells using high-ratio module masking with an asymmetric decoder, BioMod achieves state-of-the-art performance across cell-type annotation, zero-shot batch integration, perturbation-response prediction and drug-response forecasting while maintaining a compact architecture that enables efficient inference on a single GPU. Module-level analyses further demonstrate that BioMod captures biologically meaningful cellular programs and preserves pathway-level organization.
items.authors: Meng, L.; Zhu, J.; Han, B.; Zang, Y.; Li, W.; Zong, K.; Zhong, J.; Yang, Y.; Liu, J.; Jia, J.; Sun, R.; Yu, G.; Han, J.; Chen, Y.; Zhang, L.; Xu, J.
items.title_zh: BioMod：单细胞基础建模的生物模块标记化
items.summary_zh: 单细胞基础模型通常将细胞表示为单个基因的平面序列，需要从稀疏表达谱中隐式推断更高阶的生物组织。我们假设细胞状态可以通过生物学上有意义的中间单位更有效地表示。本文提出BioMod，一个拥有5000万个参数的单细胞基础模型，引入生物模块作为基因与细胞之间的表示单位。BioMod构建了一个由660个生物模块组成的重叠词汇，这些模块源自经过整理的通路和数据驱动的基因程序，替代了数千个基因级输入。BioMod在约7300万个人体细胞上进行预训练，采用高比例模块掩蔽和非对称解码器，在细胞类型注释、零样本批次整合、干扰响应预测和药物响应预测等任务中实现了最先进的性能，同时保持紧凑的架构，支持在单个GPU上高效推理。模块级分析进一步表明，BioMod捕捉了生物学上有意义的细胞程序，并保持了通路级组织。
items.l1_lead: BioMod通过引入生物模块作为基因与细胞的表示单位，显著提升了单细胞基础模型在细胞类型注释和药物响应预测等任务中的性能，同时保持了高效的计算架构。
items.l2_summary:
单细胞基础模型通常将细胞视为单个基因的平面序列，这种方法需要从稀疏的表达谱中隐式推断更高阶的生物组织。为了解决这一问题，本文提出了BioMod，一个拥有5000万个参数的单细胞基础模型，旨在通过生物学上有意义的中间单位来更有效地表示细胞状态。BioMod引入了生物模块作为基因与细胞之间的表示单位，构建了一个由660个生物模块组成的重叠词汇，这些模块源自经过整理的通路和数据驱动的基因程序，替代了数千个基因级输入。

BioMod在约7300万个人体细胞上进行了预训练，采用高比例模块掩蔽和非对称解码器的策略，使其在细胞类型注释、零样本批次整合、干扰响应预测和药物响应预测等多个任务中实现了最先进的性能。尽管模型复杂度较高，BioMod仍保持了紧凑的架构，支持在单个GPU上进行高效推理。通过模块级分析，研究表明BioMod能够捕捉生物学上有意义的细胞程序，并保持通路级的组织结构。这一研究不仅为单细胞数据分析提供了新的思路，也为生物医学研究中细胞行为的理解和药物开发提供了潜在的工具。

items.title: HERO: A hierarchy-aware analysis pipeline for reducing and refining whole-brain atlas-mapped cellular datasets
items.abstract: Advances in high-throughput mesoscale microscopy and machine learning-based image analysis pipelines have made unbiased whole-brain imaging widely accessible. However, translating the resulting atlas-mapped datasets into biologically meaningful results remains a substantial barrier owing to their sheer magnitude and complex hierarchical organization. Consequently, reporting structure and analysis methods vary widely across studies, undermining rigor and reproducibility. To address this, we developed a user-friendly data reduction workflow, HERO (Hierarchy-aware Expression Region Organization), designed to perform hierarchy-aware selection, refinement, ranking, and visualization of whole-brain cell detection datasets. The workflow is customizable to specific needs, requires minimal coding experience, and outputs transparent, curated results. HERO functions as a seamless plug-in within larger-scale whole-brain cell detection analysis pipelines, providing efficient, unbiased region selection to streamline subsequent statistical analyses and comparative evaluations. Although HERO is developed with mouse cell-detection datasets, it can be applied to any atlas-mapped dataset that contains hierarchical information. Here, we applied the HERO pipeline to example cell detection datasets containing afferent cells from the bed nucleus of the stria terminalis (BST) and the insular cortex (insula). HERO provided top projecting regions consistent with historical tracing studies for the BST (e.g., amygdalar and hypothalamic regions) and the insula (e.g., somatosensory, autonomic, and interoceptive regions). Furthermore, the refinement step of HERO provides additional enriched regions originally obscured in the primary ranked outputs, such as memory- and emotion-associated structures. With HEROs dynamic processing, we were able to identify top-projecting regions consistent with the literature and, additionally, find regions often obscured in these large datasets. In sum, HERO offers a standardized analysis workflow to reduce whole-brain cell-detection datasets, transforming raw regional cell counts into curated results and advancing the effectiveness, interpretability, and accessibility of whole-brain imaging in neuroscience.
items.authors: Shipman, A. L.; Centanni, S. W.
items.title_zh: HERO：一种层次感知的全脑细胞数据集分析管道
items.summary_zh: 随着高通量中尺度显微镜和基于机器学习的图像分析管道的发展，无偏见的全脑成像变得广泛可及。然而，将这些地图化的数据集转化为生物学上有意义的结果仍然面临重大障碍，主要由于数据量庞大和复杂的层次组织。因此，研究报告的结构和分析方法差异很大，影响了研究的严谨性和可重复性。为此，我们开发了用户友好的数据减少工作流程HERO（层次感知表达区域组织），旨在对全脑细胞检测数据集进行层次感知的选择、精炼、排序和可视化。该工作流程可根据特定需求定制，需最少编码经验，并输出透明、经过整理的结果。HERO作为更大规模全脑细胞检测分析管道的无缝插件，提供高效、公正的区域选择，以简化后续的统计分析和比较评估。虽然HERO是针对小鼠细胞检测数据集开发的，但也可应用于任何包含层次信息的地图化数据集。
items.l1_lead: HERO是一种用户友好的数据分析管道，能够高效、透明地处理全脑细胞检测数据，简化生物学研究中的数据分析和比较评估。
items.l2_summary:
随着高通量中尺度显微镜技术和基于机器学习的图像分析管道的发展，无偏见的全脑成像（whole-brain imaging）变得越来越普及。然而，将这些庞大且复杂的地图化数据集转化为具有生物学意义的结果仍然面临诸多挑战，主要是由于数据量巨大和层次组织复杂，导致研究报告的结构和分析方法差异显著，从而影响了研究的严谨性和可重复性。为了解决这一问题，研究团队开发了一种名为HERO（层次感知表达区域组织，Hierarchical Expression Region Organization）的用户友好型数据减少工作流程。HERO旨在对全脑细胞检测数据集进行层次感知的选择、精炼、排序和可视化，能够根据特定需求进行定制，且对编码经验的要求最低，输出的结果透明且经过整理。

HERO作为更大规模全脑细胞检测分析管道的无缝插件，能够提供高效且公正的区域选择，从而简化后续的统计分析和比较评估。尽管HERO是专为小鼠细胞检测数据集开发的，但其设计理念和功能也适用于任何包含层次信息的地图化数据集。这一工作流程的推出，标志着在处理复杂生物数据集方面迈出了重要一步，为研究人员提供了一种高效的工具，以便更好地理解和分析全脑细胞的组织结构和功能。通过HERO，研究者能够更容易地从海量数据中提取有意义的信息，推动生物学研究的深入发展。

items.title: Criticality-related dynamics accompany long-term functional decline in primary cortical MEA cultures
items.abstract: Primary cortical neuron cultures are widely used to study network development and decline, but their long-term electrophysiological trajectories are poorly characterized. We used multi-electrode arrays to longitudinally monitor Wistar rat cortical cultures for up to ~730 days in vitro (DIV), combining activity measures with survival analysis and criticality metrics. Wells shared an early developmental phase, with mean firing rate peaking at 12-14 Hz around DIV 100-150, before diverging into two phenotypes: early-death wells, showing progressive loss of burst organization, longer inter-burst intervals, shorter bursts, and steep declines in active-electrode recruitment; and long-survival wells, which sustained organized bursting and measurable activity well beyond DIV 400, in some cases past DIV 700. Cox proportional-hazards modeling with FDR correction across thirteen candidate features identified burst duration, inter-burst interval, synchrony, mean firing rate, branching ratio, and Kappa index as significant predictors of time to network failure. Criticality metrics offered the most mechanistic insight: in early-death wells, branching ratio declined toward zero and Kappa index rose toward its upper bound as networks approached silencing. Beyond their average levels, the rate of change of branching ratio and Kappa index over recordings was the strongest correlate of survival time among all criticality metrics. Neuronal avalanche size and duration exponents and their scaling relation, remained consistent with scale-free dynamics in both phenotypes while networks were active, though avalanche occurrence rate declined progressively in early-death wells without reaching significance as an independent predictor. These results show that long-term network survival is not determined by firing rate alone, but by preserved burst organization, sustained electrode recruitment and near-critical propagation dynamics. This work offers one of the longest electrophysiological characterizations of rodent cortical cultures to date and identifies criticality-based metrics as promising tools for predicting network decline and evaluating interventions to preserve long-term neuronal function.
items.authors: Escobar, A.; Gil-Bea, F. J.; Rodriguez-Gomez, L.

items.title: Deciphering auditory neuroprogenitor stemness for large-scale neuronal screening
items.abstract: Sensorineural hearing loss can arise from damage to sensory hair cells, auditory neurons or their synaptic connections, with auditory neuropathy and cochlear synaptopathy highlighting the importance of neural integrity for hearing. The mammalian cochlea has limited capacity to regenerate lost auditory neurons. Understanding the molecular programs that sustain cochlear progenitor expansion and neurogenic competence could support neuronal regeneration and provide renewable models for auditory drug discovery. We previously established that WNT activation combined with dual SMAD inhibition (CHIR-DS) supports scalable expansion and neuronal differentiation of mouse auditory neuroprogenitors (ANPGs). Here, we characterize the transcriptional, chromatin and metabolic changes associated with the induced state. RNA-seq and ATAC-seq identified reduced Id1 and Id2 expression and increased accessibility at proneural basic helix-loop-helix motifs, alongside transcriptional enrichment of translation, mTOR and glucose-metabolism programs. Compared with growth-factor controls, CHIR-DS-treated ANPGs showed slight increase in glycolysis at early passage. However, after long-term expansion, both glycolysis and mitochondrial respiration were markedly enhanced. Human fetal ANPGs also responded to CHIR-DS with increased sphere growth and retained neural differentiation capacity, providing proof of concept beyond the mouse system. Finally, neurons derived from stemness-induced ANPGs (siANs) supported a 384-well reporter assay and a 2,560-compound pilot screen that nominated candidate neurite-outgrowth enhancers. Together, these findings validate the pathway basis of ANPG stemness induction, characterize the resulting molecular and metabolic state, and demonstrate human feasibility and a neuronal screening application.
items.authors: Rousset, F.; Pepe, L.; Sarhadi, M.; Lemeille, S.; Sgroi, S.; Oberhauser, L.; Daskalou, D.; Ilmjarv, S.; Braun, S.; Senn, P.
items.title_zh: 解码听觉神经祖细胞的干性以进行大规模神经元筛选
items.summary_zh: 感音神经性听力损失可由感觉毛细胞、听觉神经元或其突触连接的损伤引起，听觉神经病和耳蜗突触病凸显了神经完整性对听力的重要性。哺乳动物耳蜗再生失去的听觉神经元的能力有限。理解维持耳蜗祖细胞扩展和神经发生能力的分子程序可能支持神经元再生，并为听觉药物发现提供可再生模型。我们之前建立了WNT激活与双SMAD抑制（CHIR-DS）结合可以支持小鼠听觉神经祖细胞（ANPGs）的可扩展性和神经分化。在此，我们表征了与诱导状态相关的转录、染色质和代谢变化。RNA-seq和ATAC-seq显示Id1和Id2表达降低，神经前体基本螺旋-环-螺旋基序的可及性增加，同时翻译、mTOR和葡萄糖代谢程序的转录富集。与生长因子对照组相比，CHIR-DS处理的ANPGs在早期传代中糖酵解略有增加，但经过长期扩展后，糖酵解和线粒体呼吸显著增强。人类胎儿ANPGs也对CHIR-DS作出反应，表现出球体生长增加和保持神经分化能力。
items.l1_lead: 研究表明，通过WNT激活与双SMAD抑制结合的方法，可以有效扩展和诱导小鼠及人类胎儿听觉神经祖细胞的神经分化能力，为听力损失的再生治疗提供新思路。
items.l2_summary:
感音神经性听力损失通常由感觉毛细胞、听觉神经元或其突触连接的损伤引起，强调了神经完整性在听力中的重要性。然而，哺乳动物耳蜗对听觉神经元的再生能力有限。因此，理解耳蜗祖细胞（ANPGs）扩展和神经发生能力的分子机制，可能为神经元再生提供支持，并为听觉药物的发现提供可再生模型。研究中，科学家们通过结合WNT激活与双SMAD抑制（CHIR-DS），成功支持了小鼠听觉神经祖细胞的可扩展性和神经分化。

在对诱导状态进行表征时，研究者们利用RNA测序（RNA-seq）和ATAC测序（ATAC-seq）发现，Id1和Id2的表达水平降低，同时神经前体基本螺旋-环-螺旋基序的可及性增加。此外，翻译、mTOR信号通路和葡萄糖代谢程序的转录富集也得到了证实。与生长因子对照组相比，CHIR-DS处理的ANPGs在早期传代中显示出糖酵解略有增加，但经过长期扩展后，糖酵解和线粒体呼吸显著增强。这一发现表明，CHIR-DS不仅促进了ANPGs的生长，还增强了其代谢活性。

值得注意的是，人类胎儿的ANPGs同样对CHIR-DS表现出反应，显示出球体生长的增加和保持神经分化能力的潜力。这些结果表明，通过调控特定的分子程序，可以有效地扩展和诱导听觉神经祖细胞的分化，为未来的听力损失治疗和药物开发提供了新的思路和基础。

items.title: A foundation model for brain organoid network dynamics uncovers intrinsic computation and convergent disease phenotypes
items.abstract: Brain organoids develop self-organizing neural networks that can be used to model neurodevelopment and disease. Here we introduce PULSE, a foundation model developed using over 900 hours of high-density microelectrode array recordings of in vitro and ex vivo neural tissue. We show that this single model can address two open questions: how disease-associated variants alter network development, and how naive circuits encode information. PULSE revealed accelerated network maturation in held-out human 16p11.2-deletion organoids. It also revealed a change in network coordination shared with SHANK3 deficiency. Because organoids develop without sensory input, they let us ask how circuits encode information before any representation is learned. Closed-loop control of a virtual inverted pendulum engaged existing spontaneous activity patterns rather than creating new ones. PULSE provides a common reference frame for neural circuits across genotypes, protocols and tasks.
items.authors: Schweiger, H. E.; Robbins, A.; Hernandez, S.; Moreno-Ochando, A.; Cline, I.; Doganyigit, K.; Mouzaya, M.; Hussain, K.; Pang, Z. P.; Duan, J.; Salama, S. R.; Pollen, A. A.; Bhaduri, A.; Haussler, D.; Teodorescu, M.; Mostajo-Radji, M. A.

items.title: Reuse of learned subtask representations during human planning
items.abstract: The notion of a compositional reuse of previously learned problem solutions predicts that the human brain should reinstate such learned subtask representations during planning. Here, we test this in a value-ranking task implemented in an online and a magnetoencephalography (MEG) experiment, respectively. Participants first learned pairwise rankings and subsequently solved problems where these learned rankings could either be reused or required reordering. Behaviourally, in the online experiment, we show the availability of a reusable subtask structure improved accuracy, with computational modelling indicating a greater weighting of subtask-level value when participants could avail of this learnt structure. In MEG, during planning, we show enhanced reactivation of task-relevant subtask representations in the reusable condition, and particularly so early in the experiment. In a subsequent probe task, we show subtask-identity representations generalised to a novel context and that stimuli belonging to the same learned subtask manifest an increase in their neural similarity. Temporally delayed linear modelling (TDLM) revealed forward and backward sequential reactivation at a subtask level, alongside backward stimulus-level replay, with subtask sequenceness varying according to task context. The findings provide convergent behavioural, computational and neural evidence for reactivation and reuse of learnt relational structures for novel problem solving.
items.authors: Seak, L. C. U.; Luettgau, L.; Eckstein, M. K.; Moran, R.; Dolan, R. J.

items.title: Linking anterior cingulate sulcal variability to attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder behavior
items.abstract: Background: The anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) is consistently implicated in attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). ACC variability, including its most variable structure, the paracingulate sulcus (PCGS), has been known since the late 1800s, and since then, has been linked to cognitive control, impulsivity, and psychiatric conditions comorbid with ADHD, including autism spectrum disorder and schizophrenia. Yet, the role of the PCGS in ADHD remains unexamined at the individual level. Methods: We characterized PCGS incidence, asymmetry, and morphology in 247 children and adolescents (144 ADHD: 10.9 +/- 2.73 years old, 75% male; 103 neurotypical: 12.2 +/- 3.17 years old, 50% male) from the ADHD-200 dataset. The PCGS was manually identified in FreeSurfer cortical surface reconstructions. Morphometric measures, including sulcal length, depth, and cortical thickness, were extracted and normalized to hemisphere-wide variables. Between-group analyses tested whether PCGS presence, asymmetry, and quantitative morphology differed by diagnosis, while behavioral analyses examined associations with inattention, hyperactivity-impulsivity, and cognitive measures. Age and gender were included as covariates. Results: Analyses revealed that, in both NT and ADHD individuals, there was significant leftward asymmetry in PCGS presence. Between groups, the PCGS was less likely to be present in individuals with ADHD in the left hemisphere. Leftward PCGS absence was also associated with significantly higher ADHD index and hyperactivity-impulsivity scores. Conclusions: These findings advance understanding of how early neurodevelopmental variation in cortical folding may serve as a structural intermediary between genetic liability and the behavioral expression of ADHD.
items.authors: Hadveck, R. F.; Paras, A.; Anctil, M.; Martinez, E.; Gallardo, C. M.; Maboudian, S. A.; Willbrand, E. H.; Weiner, K. S.

items.title: Lysosomal Glycosaminoglycan Catabolism Regulates Microglial Cell State in the Developing CNS
items.abstract: Remodeling of the extracellular matrix (ECM), a complex structural and signaling network of the nervous system, is essential for CNS development, plasticity, and injury responses, yet how individual neural cell types contribute to this process remains poorly understood. Here, we show that phagocytic clearance of glycosaminoglycans (GAGs), major components of the ECM, is an intrinsic function of microglia in the developing CNS. Our studies reveal an unexpected finding that impaired GAG clearance shifts microglia toward a non-homeostatic cell state seen in immature and disease-associated microglia (DAM), supporting a reciprocal relationship between the ECM and microglia. Using mouse models of Mucopolysaccharidosis VII, we examined the consequences of deleting {beta}-glucuronidase (GUSB), a lysosomal enzyme required for GAG degradation. Loss of GUSB causes early accumulation of undegraded chondroitin sulfate within microglial lysosomes, as confirmed by LC-MS analysis of intracellular GAGs isolated from cortical microglia. Single-cell RNA sequencing identified Gusb-null microglia as a distinct transcriptional population enriched for a core transcriptome shared by immature and disease-associated microglia. Together, these findings establish lysosomal GAG catabolism as a pathway that links ECM remodeling to the acquisition of adult homeostatic microglial identity during CNS development.
items.authors: Hope, K. T.; Zhang, Y.; Basu, A.; Luo, B.; Chassie, K.; Weiss, R. J.; Yellajoshyula, D.
items.title_zh: 溶酶体糖胺聚糖降解调控发育中CNS小胶质细胞状态
items.summary_zh: 本研究探讨了糖胺聚糖（GAGs）在发育中中枢神经系统（CNS）中的清除作用，发现其为小胶质细胞的内在功能。研究表明，GAG清除受损会使小胶质细胞转变为非稳态状态，与未成熟和疾病相关小胶质细胞（DAM）相似，支持了细胞外基质（ECM）与小胶质细胞之间的相互关系。通过小鼠粘多糖贮积症VII模型，研究了缺失β-葡萄糖醛酸酶（GUSB）的后果，发现GUSB缺失导致小胶质细胞内未降解的硫酸软骨素早期积累。单细胞RNA测序显示，Gusb-null小胶质细胞为一种独特的转录群体，富含未成熟和疾病相关小胶质细胞共享的核心转录组。这些发现确立了溶酶体GAG降解作为连接ECM重塑与获得成年稳态小胶质细胞身份的途径。
items.l1_lead: 本研究揭示了溶酶体糖胺聚糖降解在发育中小胶质细胞稳态维持中的关键作用，缺失该过程会导致小胶质细胞转变为非稳态状态。
items.l2_summary:
本研究探讨了糖胺聚糖（GAGs）在发育中中枢神经系统（CNS）中的清除作用，揭示了其在小胶质细胞内在功能中的重要性。研究发现，GAG的清除受损会导致小胶质细胞转变为非稳态状态，这种状态与未成熟和疾病相关小胶质细胞（DAM）相似，进一步支持了细胞外基质（ECM）与小胶质细胞之间的相互关系。通过使用小鼠粘多糖贮积症VII模型，研究者分析了缺失β-葡萄糖醛酸酶（GUSB）所带来的后果，结果显示GUSB缺失导致小胶质细胞内未降解的硫酸软骨素早期积累。

为了深入了解这一现象，研究团队进行了单细胞RNA测序，结果表明，Gusb-null小胶质细胞形成了一种独特的转录群体，其转录组富含未成熟和疾病相关小胶质细胞共享的核心转录组。这一发现表明，溶酶体GAG降解在连接ECM重塑与获得成年稳态小胶质细胞身份的过程中起着关键作用。这项研究不仅为理解小胶质细胞的发育和功能提供了新的视角，也为相关神经疾病的机制研究奠定了基础。总之，研究强调了GAG降解在小胶质细胞稳态维持中的重要性，提示其可能成为未来治疗神经系统疾病的新靶点。
