items.title: Sex differences in depression and substance use disorder diagnoses and overdose risk in British Columbia
items.abstract: Background: Depression is a risk factor for overdose and is more commonly diagnosed among females. However, sex-differences in the association between depression, in isolation and in combination with substance use disorder (SUD), and overdose have not been examined at the population level in British Columbia (BC). This study described sex-and-age differences in associations between documented history of depression and/or SUD diagnoses and risk of fatal (FOD) and non-fatal overdose (NFOD). Methods: This study used linked administrative health data from the Provincial Health Services Authority Platform for Analytics and Data. The sample included BC residents aged 19-79 as of January 1st, 2015 (n=3,996,690). Exposures were classified as documented diagnosis history of 1) depression; 2) substance use disorder (SUD); 3) depression and SUD; and 4) neither condition, using physician billing and hospitalization records from 2010-2014. FOD (BC Coroners Service records) and NFOD (BC Emergency Health Services records) were ascertained from 2015 to 2024. Incidence rates per 10,000 person-years and unadjusted incidence rate ratios (IRRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) were estimated using Poisson regression, with neither diagnosis as reference, overall and stratified by sex and age. Results: There were 14,281 FOD (78.59% male) and 43,555 NFOD (69.45% male) cases. FOD incidence was higher among males overall; however, relative associations between diagnosis history and FOD risk were stronger among females. Depression diagnosis history was associated with a FOD IRR of 3.95 (CI: 3.56-4.38) among females and 2.46 (CI: 2.32-2.61) among males. IRRs for SUD and for depression and SUD were larger among females (108.07 [CI: 95.83-121.73] and 116.70 [CI: 106.51-127.96]) than males (26.69 [CI: 25.57-28.18] and 31.21 [CI: 29.81-32.67]). NFOD findings were similar but attenuated (depression IRR: 3.22 [CI: 3.08-3.38]) in females; 2.29 [CI: 2.21-2.37] in males). Conclusion: A documented history of depression and/or SUD was more strongly associated with FOD and NFOD risk among females, despite higher incidence overall among males. Future research should consider the potential role of other sociodemographic factors in explaining sex differences in associations between diagnosis history and overdose risk.
items.authors: Palis, H.; Vincent, J.

items.title: FERMAT: An Autoregressive Clinical Foundation Model for Disease Risk and Clinical Event Prediction
items.abstract: Clinical foundation models learn patterns in longitudinal health records that can be reused across prediction tasks. However, the relative strengths of representation-based and generation-based prediction across clinical tasks remain unclear. Using longitudinal electronic health records from 3.77 million patients at a single hospital, we developed FERMAT (Foundation model for Exploring Real-world Multimodal health data using Autoregressive Trajectory modeling), a 65-million-parameter clinical foundation model. We compared predictions from task-specific predictors trained on patient representations with those derived from generated clinical event sequences. Representation-based prediction performed better in the disease-risk comparisons. In detailed analyses of five-year chronic kidney disease, fatty liver, and diabetes risk in a test cohort of 10,000 patients, representation-based predictors exceeded generation-based estimates by 0.098-0.115 in observation-weighted AUROC and had lower probability error. Generation-based prediction, in turn, performed better in predicting diagnoses, prescriptions, and procedures recorded on the same day, a task motivated by the frequent presence of multiple events with the same date in hospital EHRs. Using 50 generated trajectories per patient, it achieved a Recall@10 of 71.0%, compared with 55.7% for representation-based prediction, with a paired improvement of 15.31 percentage points (95% CI, 13.92-16.79; n = 1,862). These findings demonstrate task-dependent strengths of representation-based and generation-based applications within a single clinical foundation model, providing an empirical basis for exploring how the two approaches can be used individually or combined to address clinical prediction needs.
items.authors: Jung, J.; Lee, H.-C.
items.title_zh: FERMAT：用于疾病风险与临床事件预测的自回归临床基础模型
items.summary_zh: 临床基础模型通过学习纵向健康记录中的模式，可在预测任务中重复使用。然而，基于表征的预测与基于生成的预测在临床任务中的相对优势尚不明确。我们利用来自单一医院的377万患者的纵向电子健康记录，开发了FERMAT（用于探索真实世界多模态健康数据的自回归轨迹建模基础模型），该模型包含6500万个参数。我们比较了基于患者表征训练的特定任务预测器与基于生成的临床事件序列的预测结果。在五年慢性肾病、脂肪肝和糖尿病风险的详细分析中，基于表征的预测在观察加权AUROC上超出了基于生成的估计0.098-0.115，并且概率误差更低。相反，基于生成的预测在预测同一天记录的诊断、处方和程序方面表现更好，Recall@10达71.0%，而基于表征的预测为55.7%。
items.l1_lead: FERMAT模型通过分析377万患者的健康记录，发现基于表征的预测在疾病风险评估中优于基于生成的预测，而后者在同日临床事件预测中表现更佳。
items.l2_summary:
FERMAT（用于探索真实世界多模态健康数据的自回归轨迹建模基础模型）是一种新开发的临床基础模型，旨在通过学习纵向健康记录中的模式来进行疾病风险与临床事件的预测。该模型基于来自单一医院的377万患者的纵向电子健康记录，包含6500万个参数。研究的核心在于比较基于患者表征（representation）训练的特定任务预测器与基于生成（generation）的临床事件序列的预测结果，以明确两者在临床任务中的相对优势。

在对五年慢性肾病、脂肪肝和糖尿病风险的详细分析中，结果显示基于表征的预测在观察加权AUROC（曲线下面积）上超出了基于生成的估计，差距在0.098至0.115之间，且概率误差更低。这表明，基于表征的模型在长期疾病风险预测方面具有更好的性能。然而，在预测同一天记录的诊断、处方和程序方面，基于生成的预测表现更为优越，其Recall@10达到了71.0%，而基于表征的预测仅为55.7%。这些结果表明，尽管基于表征的预测在长期风险评估中更为有效，但基于生成的预测在短期临床事件的即时预测中具有明显优势。

综上所述，FERMAT模型的研究为临床预测任务提供了新的视角，强调了在不同预测场景下选择合适模型的重要性。通过对比两种预测方法的性能，研究为未来在临床实践中应用自回归模型提供了实证依据，推动了个性化医疗的发展。

items.title: Efficacy of physiotherapy in reducing pain in subjects with temporomandibular disorders: a systematic review with network meta-analysis
items.abstract: Background: Temporomandibular disorders (TMDs) are common conditions in the general population. Several therapeutic approaches are available, but there is no consensus on the most effective, particularly in physiotherapy. Objectives: To assess the efficacy of manual therapy (MT) and therapeutic exercise (TE) in reducing pain in patients with TMDs. Methods: Four databases (MEDLINE, PEDro, EMBASE, CINAHL) were searched up to March 2025. We included randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating the effects of MT and/or TE in individuals with TMDs, compared to any other rehabilitation treatment, with pain intensity as the primary outcome. The methodological quality was assessed using the PEDro scale. A network meta-analysis was performed to compare the effectiveness of different rehabilitative approaches. Results: 25 RCTs for a total of 1,540 people were included. The main comparisons were: MT and/or TE vs no treatment or placebo, occlusal splint, and instrumental physiotherapy. In most studies, MT and TE were more effective than controls in reducing pain. However, the network meta-analysis indicated that multimodal treatments were the most effective. The methodological quality of the included studies ranged from 3 to 9 points. Conclusion: MT and TE are effective strategies for reducing pain in subjects with TMDs and should be used as first-line interventions before more invasive treatments; the combination of dry needling and manual therapy appears to be the most effective approach. Nonetheless, the variability in study quality suggests that further high-quality research is needed to confirm these findings.
items.authors: Alvisi, A.; Casalini, A.; Mammana, L.; Ugolini, A.
items.title_zh: 物理治疗在颞下颌关节紊乱患者疼痛缓解中的疗效研究
items.summary_zh: 背景：颞下颌关节紊乱（TMD）在普通人群中较为常见。虽然有多种治疗方法，但对物理治疗的有效性尚无共识。目的：评估手动治疗（MT）和治疗性运动（TE）在缓解TMD患者疼痛方面的疗效。方法：检索了四个数据库（MEDLINE、PEDro、EMBASE、CINAHL），截至2025年3月。纳入了评估MT和/或TE对TMD患者影响的随机对照试验（RCT），以疼痛强度为主要结果。使用PEDro量表评估方法学质量。进行了网络荟萃分析以比较不同康复方法的有效性。结果：共纳入25项RCT，涉及1540人。主要比较为：MT和/或TE与无治疗或安慰剂、咬合夹板和仪器物理治疗的对比。大多数研究表明，MT和TE在减轻疼痛方面优于对照组。然而，网络荟萃分析显示，多模式治疗效果最佳。纳入研究的方法学质量评分范围为3至9分。结论：MT和TE是减轻TMD患者疼痛的有效策略，应作为首选干预措施。
items.l1_lead: 物理治疗中的手动治疗和治疗性运动被证实是缓解颞下颌关节紊乱患者疼痛的有效策略，推荐作为首选干预措施。
items.l2_summary:
颞下颌关节紊乱（TMD）在普通人群中较为常见，尽管存在多种治疗方法，但关于物理治疗的有效性仍缺乏共识。本研究旨在评估手动治疗（MT）和治疗性运动（TE）在缓解TMD患者疼痛方面的疗效。研究团队检索了四个数据库（MEDLINE、PEDro、EMBASE、CINAHL），截至2025年3月，纳入了评估MT和/或TE对TMD患者影响的随机对照试验（RCT），以疼痛强度作为主要结果指标。通过PEDro量表评估了纳入研究的方法学质量，并进行了网络荟萃分析以比较不同康复方法的有效性。

最终，共纳入25项RCT，涉及1540名参与者。主要比较包括MT和/或TE与无治疗或安慰剂、咬合夹板和仪器物理治疗的效果。大多数研究结果表明，MT和TE在减轻疼痛方面优于对照组。然而，网络荟萃分析的结果显示，多模式治疗的效果最佳。纳入研究的方法学质量评分范围为3至9分，表明研究的质量存在一定差异。

综上所述，MT和TE被证实是减轻TMD患者疼痛的有效策略，建议作为首选干预措施。这一研究为TMD的物理治疗提供了重要的实证支持，强调了多模式治疗在疼痛管理中的潜在优势。

items.title: Anticholinergic Co-Medication Burden Does Not Predict Cardiac Toxicity in Adolescent Diphenhydramine Exposure: A Pharmacovigilance Study of the FDA Adverse Event Monitoring System
items.abstract: Objectives: Social media trends such as the "Benadryl Challenge" have increased adolescent misuse of diphenhydramine (DPH), an over-the-counter antihistamine with anticholinergic activity. Whether co-ingested anticholinergic medications compound cardiac risk is untested. Using the Anticholinergic Cognitive Burden (ACB) scale, this study examined whether co-medication ACB burden is associated with outcome severity and cardiac toxicity in adolescent DPH cases reported to the FDA Adverse Event Monitoring System (AEMS). Methods: This study extracted all adolescent reports (age 13-19) mentioning DPH in any drug role from AEMS, yielding 3,168 cases from 217,507 deduplicated records. Given non-normality (Shapiro-Wilk, all p < 0.001), non-parametric tests were used. A multivariable logistic regression predicted cardiac toxicity; logistic and random-forest models were compared by cross-validated AUC. Results: Co-medication ACB burden correlated positively with case severity ({rho} = 0.142, p < 0.001) and differed by age group (H = 19.52, p < 0.001). However, burden and cardiac risk diverged: cardiac cases carried a lower burden (mean 0.55 vs 1.27) and were younger, and burden did not independently predict cardiac toxicity (OR = 0.927, 95% CI [0.841, 1.022], p = 0.128). Younger age was the strongest predictor (OR = 0.865 per year, p < 0.001); cardiac events occurred in 10.2% of 13-15-year-olds versus 4.9% of older adolescents. Conclusion: Anticholinergic co-medication burden and cardiac risk dissociate: burden tracks overall severity, but cardiac events concentrate in the youngest, least co-medicated adolescents, a profile consistent with deliberate single-agent overdose rather than polypharmacy. A low co-medication burden should not reassure clinicians triaging young adolescents.
items.authors: Dong, Z.; Fadel, N.; Krishnan, S.; Cai, P.

items.title: Predictors of Activity and Concentration Interference in Adults with Migraine: An Ecological Momentary Assessment Study
items.abstract: Objective: To identify demographic and daily cognitive, affective, and contextual predictors of headache-related interference with activity and concentration in a smartphone-based migraine cohort, using statistical models appropriate to the ordinal structure of patient-reported interference. Background: Migraine burden extends beyond headache to encompass cognitive and affective disturbance, yet most disability instruments summarize functioning retrospectively and cannot capture day-to-day variability in interference. Ecological momentary assessment addresses this limitation, yet few studies have examined cognitive and affective correlates of interference independent of pain intensity or have modeled interference using methods that respect its ordinal, non-equal-interval structure. Methods: From May 2025 to April 2026, adult participants were enrolled in this prospective, decentralized observational study via specialty clinics and social media campaigns. Eligibility required fulfilling ICHD-3 diagnostic criteria for migraine using a validated electronic survey and experiencing between 3 and 20 monthly headache days. Enrolled individuals recorded daily smartphone diary entries and performed three brief cognitive tests over a 30-day monitoring period. Daily interference with activities and concentration were captured on 5-point ordinal scales and analyzed via cumulative link mixed-effects models incorporating participant-specific random intercepts. Predictor selection across nested specifications relied on likelihood ratio testing and Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) metrics, prioritizing the more parsimonious model when goodness-of-fit was comparable. Results: The analytic sample comprised 1,267 headache-day observations from 143 participants. In the final models, brain fog (OR = 2.49 for activity, 3.19 for concentration), forgetfulness (OR = 1.48, 1.65), and mood disturbance (OR = 1.19, 1.31) were each independently associated with both outcomes (all p < 0.01), while age, sex, and employment status showed no significant association with either. Sleep quality (OR = 0.86) and anticipated next-day enjoyment (OR = 0.81) provided additional explanatory value for activity interference (p < 0.05) but not for concentration interference, for which the three-predictor model of brain fog, forgetfulness, and mood alone was retained as the most parsimonious final model. Conclusions: Cognitive and affective symptoms, rather than demographic or socioeconomic characteristics, are the primary correlates of headache-related functional interference in this cohort. Activity and concentration interference are explained by partially distinct sets of daily influences, supporting the clinical value of assessing cognitive and affective symptoms alongside conventional pain-focused evaluation.
items.authors: Bina, A.; Rezaee, G.

items.title: Real-World Twelve-Month Weight Loss Outcomes in a Comprehensive Obesity Care Program Utilizing Individualized Nutrition Therapy and Incretin-Based Obesity Medications
items.abstract: Background: Incretin-based obesity medications (IOMs) produce substantial weight loss, but the incremental benefit of structured nutritional therapy when integrated with pharmacotherapy remains unclear. Objectives: To compare 12-month weight-loss outcomes between individualized carbohydrate-reduced nutritional therapy combined with IOMs (VINT+IOM) and IOM-based care without structured nutritional therapy (IOM only). Methods: This retrospective cohort study evaluated 4,269 adults enrolled in a comprehensive telemedicine obesity care program (VINT+IOM, n=1,658; IOM only, n=2,611). Both pathways included clinician-guided medication management and behavioral coaching. The primary analysis focused on GLP-1-naive participants receiving either semaglutide or tirzepatide without switching medications during follow-up. Adjusted weight changes were estimated using longitudinal linear mixed-effects models accounting for baseline demographic and clinical characteristics. Additional analyses evaluated weight-loss responders, prior GLP-1 exposure, and medication utilization. Results: Among GLP-1-naive semaglutide users, adjusted 12-month weight loss was greater with VINT+IOM than IOM only (30.7 vs. 24.1 lb; P=0.01), with corresponding observed weight loss of 13.3% versus 11.1%. Among tirzepatide users, adjusted weight loss was 45.9 versus 34.4 lb (P=0.003), with observed reductions of 19.7% versus 15.6%, respectively. Weight-loss responder rates consistently favored VINT+IOM. In the overall cohort, including GLP-1-naive participants, those with prior GLP-1 exposure, and participants with varying medication trajectories, adjusted weight loss was 29.4 versus 21.5 lb (P less than 0.001), with observed reductions of 12.7% versus 9.6%. Greater weight loss with VINT+IOM was also observed among participants with prior GLP-1 exposure. Weight loss continued between 6 and 12 months in both pathways. Medication coverage was high, with approximately 80% of participants achieving a proportion of days covered of at least 80% in both pathways. Conclusions: Integrating individualized carbohydrate-reduced nutritional therapy with IOM-based care was associated with greater 12-month weight loss than IOM-based care without structured nutritional therapy. These real-world findings support further evaluation of individualized nutritional approaches as an adjunct to incretin-based obesity pharmacotherapy.
items.authors: Athinarayanan, S.; Zoller, A. R.; Bergethon, K. E.; Goss, A. M.; Gower, B. A.
items.title_zh: 个性化营养治疗与胰高血糖素样肽药物结合的减重效果研究
items.summary_zh: 背景：胰高血糖素样肽药物（IOMs）能显著减重，但与药物治疗结合的结构化营养治疗的增益尚不明确。目的：比较个性化低碳水化合物营养治疗结合IOMs（VINT+IOM）与仅使用IOM的12个月减重效果。方法：本回顾性队列研究评估了4269名参与综合远程医疗肥胖护理项目的成年人（VINT+IOM组：1658人；IOM组：2611人）。两组均接受临床医生指导的药物管理和行为辅导。主要分析集中于未使用GLP-1的参与者，接受semaglutide或tirzepatide治疗。调整后的体重变化通过考虑基线人口统计和临床特征的纵向线性混合效应模型估算。结果：在未使用GLP-1的semaglutide用户中，VINT+IOM组的调整后12个月减重为30.7磅，IOM组为24.1磅（P=0.01），观察到的减重分别为13.3%和11.1%。在tirzepatide用户中，调整后减重为45.9磅对比34.4磅（P=0.003），观察到的减重为19.7%。
items.l1_lead: 个性化低碳水化合物营养治疗结合胰高血糖素样肽药物显著提高了减重效果，12个月内减重分别达到30.7磅和45.9磅，优于单独使用药物的效果。
items.l2_summary:
本研究旨在探讨个性化低碳水化合物营养治疗结合胰高血糖素样肽药物（IOMs）对减重效果的影响。研究对象为4269名参与综合远程医疗肥胖护理项目的成年人，其中1658人接受个性化营养治疗与IOMs结合（VINT+IOM组），2611人仅使用IOM（IOM组）。所有参与者均接受临床医生指导的药物管理和行为辅导。研究主要分析未使用GLP-1（胰高血糖素样肽-1）药物的参与者，重点关注使用semaglutide或tirzepatide治疗的患者。

结果显示，在未使用GLP-1的semaglutide用户中，VINT+IOM组在12个月内的调整后减重为30.7磅，而IOM组为24.1磅，差异具有统计学意义（P=0.01），观察到的减重比例分别为13.3%和11.1%。在使用tirzepatide的用户中，VINT+IOM组的调整后减重为45.9磅，相比之下，IOM组为34.4磅，差异同样显著（P=0.003），观察到的减重比例为19.7%。这些结果表明，个性化营养治疗与IOMs结合的减重效果优于单纯使用IOM，提示在肥胖管理中，结合个性化营养干预可能会增强药物治疗的效果。

items.title: HLA Genotype is Associated with Patient Reported Outcomes and Adverse Reactions to Metal Debris in Patients with Cobalt-Chrome Knee Arthroplasties
items.abstract: Purpose: To determine whether a cobalt-chrome genetic reactivity (CoGR) score - originally developed to identify patients at greater risk of developing adverse reaction to metal-on-metal hips - is associated with poorer patient-reported outcomes after knee arthroplasty (KA). Methods: In a prospective multicentre study, patients at a minimum two years post all cobalt-chrome KA were invited to research clinics. Participants provided samples for blood metal ion measurements and DNA sequencing and completed Forgotten Joint Scores (FJS). Component alignment was assessed on AP and lateral plain radiographs. The association between CoGR and FJS was assessed using regression adjusted for time since surgery, age, gender, BMI and tested for modification by blood cobalt. In a case-control analysis, CoGR scores of revised patients with histologically confirmed adverse reactions to metal debris (and specifically aseptic lymphocyte-dominated vasculitis-associated lesions (ALVAL)) were compared with controls (revised patients with no signs of ARMD and unrevised patients with FJS of 75 or more) using Firth logistic regression. Results: 376 patients were included: 312 unrevised patients and 64 patients who underwent revision. Each one-unit increase in CoGR score was associated with a 9.8 point lower FJS (95% confidence interval (CI) 4.2 to 15.4 points; p < 0.001). This increased to a 17.5 (9.4 to 25.5) point reduction per CoGR score unit in patients with blood cobalt above the median level. Comparing 28 ARMD cases (12 with ALVAL) with 177 controls, each one-unit CoGR increase was associated with odds ratios of 1.90 (CI 1.34 to 2.75) for ARMD and 3.05 (CI 1.89 to 5.34) for ALVAL. Conclusions: A higher CoGR score was associated with worse patient-reported outcome and higher odds of histologically confirmed adverse reaction to metal debris at revision. Adverse immune responses may be a more significant factor in unexplained pain after KA than is generally recognised.
items.authors: Langton, D.; Bhalekar, R.; Borikar, Y.; Wells, S.; Clement, N.; Deehan, D.; Guest, D.; Harrington, C.; Jameson, S.; Leitch, G.; McManus, R.; Pabbruwe, M.; Phillips, J.; Rushton, S.; Porteous, A.; Santini, A.; Tross, S.; Sidaginamale, R.
items.title_zh: HLA基因型与钴铬膝关节置换术患者的自报结果及金属碎片不良反应相关
items.summary_zh: 目的：确定钴铬遗传反应性（CoGR）评分是否与膝关节置换术后患者自报结果相关。方法：在一项前瞻性多中心研究中，邀请至少接受钴铬膝关节置换术两年的患者参与。参与者提供血液金属离子测量和DNA测序样本，并完成遗忘关节评分（FJS）。通过前后位和侧位X光片评估组件对齐。使用回归分析评估CoGR与FJS的关联，并调整手术时间、年龄、性别、BMI，并测试血钴的修饰作用。在病例对照分析中，比较了有组织学确认金属碎片不良反应的修订患者的CoGR评分与对照组（无ARMD迹象的修订患者和FJS≥75的未修订患者）。结果：共纳入376名患者，其中312名未修订患者和64名修订患者。每增加1单位的CoGR评分，FJS降低9.8分（95%置信区间4.2至15.4分；p < 0.001）。
items.l1_lead: 钴铬基因型评分与膝关节置换术后患者自报结果显著相关，评分每增加1单位，患者的关节功能评分降低约9.8分。
items.l2_summary:
本研究旨在探讨钴铬遗传反应性（CoGR）评分与膝关节置换术后患者自报结果之间的关系。研究采用前瞻性多中心设计，招募了至少接受钴铬膝关节置换术两年的患者，共计376名参与者，其中312名为未修订患者，64名为修订患者。参与者提供了血液金属离子测量和DNA测序样本，并完成了遗忘关节评分（FJS）。研究通过前后位和侧位X光片评估了组件对齐情况，并利用回归分析评估CoGR与FJS之间的关联，同时调整了手术时间、年龄、性别和体重指数（BMI），并测试了血钴的修饰作用。

研究结果显示，每增加1单位的CoGR评分，FJS降低9.8分（95%置信区间4.2至15.4分；p < 0.001），表明CoGR评分与患者自报的膝关节功能结果存在显著负相关。此外，在病例对照分析中，研究还比较了有组织学确认金属碎片不良反应的修订患者的CoGR评分与对照组（无金属碎片不良反应迹象的修订患者和FJS≥75的未修订患者）。这些结果提示，钴铬基因型可能在膝关节置换术后患者的自报结果及金属碎片不良反应中发挥重要作用，为临床评估和个体化治疗提供了新的视角。

items.title: Long-read sequencing and benchmarking of saliva against blood for genomic variant detection in autism
items.abstract: Autism is highly heritable, yet many cases remain genetically unsolved even after short-read sequencing (SRS). Long-read sequencing (LRS) increases sensitivity for pathogenic variant discovery, especially for complex structural variants (SVs) in repetitive regions missed by SRS. However, LRS largely relies on blood-derived DNA; whether saliva can support genome-wide LRS at population scale remains to be seen. We report the first systematic evaluation of saliva-derived DNA for genome-wide LRS in autism, benchmarking 105 new saliva samples against 68 new blood samples and integrating 189 previously published LRS blood samples to expand the autism cohort and improve ultra-rare pathogenic variant discovery. A matched blood-saliva quad provided direct comparisons of variant detection between sample sources. Saliva samples contained substantially more nonhuman DNA than blood (mean 10% versus 0.005% of reads), reducing mean effective genome coverage from an estimated 28X to 24X after removal of nonhuman reads, compared with 34X in blood samples. Despite this reduction, saliva and blood samples yielded comparable numbers of validated (22,591 versus 23,064) and rare (209 versus 213) SVs per sample, which was also observed in the quad when matching coverage. Saliva LRS identified four new pathogenic and likely pathogenic variants missed by SRS. We report variants affecting MECP2, DNMT3A, CHD8, LMBRD2, POGZ, and PHF3; four additional candidates with potential relevance to autism; and an increase of diagnostic yield of 9-18%. Saliva-derived DNA support blood-comparable discovery of pathogenic variants missed by SRS, including SVs, with increased sequencing coverage compensating for nonhuman DNA contamination and reduced assembly contiguity, thus showing saliva DNA collection as a feasible strategy for large-scale LRS studies of patients and population-scale sequencing of cohorts.
items.authors: Sui, Y.; Campos, G.; Kwon, Y.; Wong, I.; Koundinya, N.; Munson, K. M.; Hoekzema, K.; Ayllon, M.; Wang, T.; Neuhaus, E.; Eichler, E. E.

items.title: Proximity-mapped whole-genome sequencing for characterization of repeat expansions and variants in highly homologous genomic regions
items.abstract: Background: Short-read whole-genome sequencing (sWGS) has limitations in characterizing tandem-repeat expansions and variants in highly homologous or pseudogene-associated regions. Long-read sequencing can address some of these challenges but often benefits from high-molecular-weight DNA. TruPath Genome incorporates spatial proximity information into a short-read sequencing framework. This study evaluated its performance in characterizing selected complex genomic variants using archived clinical DNA specimens. Methods: Ten archived peripheral blood DNA specimens were analyzed, comprising seven cases with disease-associated short tandem repeat (STR) expansions and three cases involving homologous or pseudogene-associated loci (STRC, SMN1/SMN2, and CYP21A2). TruPath results were compared with previously available orthogonal assay results, including triplet repeat-primed PCR (TP-PCR), multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification (MLPA), quantitative PCR (qPCR), and sWGS-based ExpansionHunter analysis. Results: TruPath generated repeat-length estimates across the evaluated STR loci. For two FMR1 full-mutation alleles, TruPath estimated 284 and 295 CGG repeats, respectively, while TP-PCR reported expansions exceeding 200 repeats. In a DMPK case, TruPath estimated an expanded allele of 1,203 CTG repeats, compared with a TP-PCR result exceeding 100 repeats. At the STRC and SMN1/SMN2 loci, TruPath findings were consistent with available orthogonal results for deletion and copy-number status. At the CYP21A2 locus, TruPath reconstructed the RCCX gene arrangement and assigned the I2G variant and a chimeric allele to different haplotypes. Conclusions: In this small series of archived clinical DNA specimens, TruPath Genome enabled characterization of selected repeat expansions and homologous or pseudogene-associated variants. The findings support further evaluation of proximity-mapped sequencing as a complementary approach for complex genomic regions, particularly when conventional short-read sequencing is limited.
items.authors: Lin, Y.; Zhang, L.; Qiang, Y.; Yang, L.; Li, X.; Wang, K.

items.title: A national ecosystem for long-read genome sequencing: Integrating population genomics and rare disease diagnostics in Sweden
items.abstract: To evaluate the clinical implementation of long-read genome sequencing (lrGS) and establish the population reference resources needed to support its use in diagnostics, we integrate two complementary initiatives: Genome of Sweden (GoS), Sweden's contribution to Genome of Europe (GoE), and the Genomic Medicine Sweden - Rare Diseases (GMS-RD) long-read sequencing pilot. The initial GoS release of 576 individuals provides population-scale maps of genetic and epigenetic variation. Among 485 GMS-RD probands, 161 (33.2%) receive a molecular diagnosis, with lrGS providing added clinical value in 40 (24.8%). As a first-line test, lrGS could have avoided at least 42 follow-up analyses and an additional testing cycle in 7.2% of probands, reducing costs and the burden on patients. By integrating population and clinical long-read genomics, Sweden establishes a national ecosystem for genomic research and clinical diagnostics. Our findings support the clinical implementation of lrGS and offer a scalable model for national collaboration.

items.title_zh: 瑞典长读基因组测序的国家生态系统
items.summary_zh: 为了评估长读基因组测序（lrGS）的临床应用并建立支持其在诊断中使用的人口参考资源，我们整合了两个互补的项目：瑞典基因组（GoS）和瑞典基因组医学-罕见疾病（GMS-RD）长读测序试点。GoS首次发布了576个个体的数据，提供了人口规模的遗传和表观遗传变异图谱。在485名GMS-RD的样本中，161名（33.2%）获得了分子诊断，其中lrGS在40名（24.8%）中提供了额外的临床价值。作为一线检测，lrGS可以避免至少42次后续分析，并在7.2%的样本中减少额外的检测周期，从而降低成本和患者负担。通过整合人口和临床长读基因组学，瑞典建立了一个国家级的基因组研究和临床诊断生态系统。我们的研究结果支持lrGS的临床实施，并为国家合作提供了可扩展的模型。
items.l1_lead: 瑞典通过整合长读基因组测序项目，建立了国家级基因组研究和临床诊断生态系统，支持其在临床应用中的有效性和可扩展性。
items.l2_summary:
瑞典在长读基因组测序（long-read genome sequencing, lrGS）领域开展了重要的研究，以评估其在临床应用中的潜力，并建立支持其在诊断中使用的人口参考资源。为此，研究团队整合了两个互补的项目：瑞典基因组（Genomics of Sweden, GoS）和瑞典基因组医学-罕见疾病（Genomics of Sweden for Rare Diseases, GMS-RD）长读测序试点。GoS项目首次发布了576个个体的数据，提供了一个涵盖人口规模的遗传和表观遗传变异图谱，这为后续的研究奠定了基础。

在GMS-RD项目中，共分析了485名样本，其中161名（占33.2%）获得了分子诊断，而lrGS在40名（占24.8%）的病例中提供了额外的临床价值。这表明，lrGS作为一线检测手段，不仅能够有效识别疾病，还能在许多情况下避免后续的多次分析，具体而言，lrGS可以避免至少42次后续分析，并在7.2%的样本中减少额外的检测周期。这一结果不仅降低了患者的经济负担，也提高了诊断效率。

通过整合人口和临床长读基因组学，瑞典成功建立了一个国家级的基因组研究和临床诊断生态系统。这一研究成果为lrGS的临床实施提供了有力支持，并为未来的国家合作提供了可扩展的模型，显示出长读基因组测序在临床应用中的广阔前景。整体而言，瑞典的这一研究不仅推动了基因组学的发展，也为罕见疾病的诊断提供了新的思路和方法。

items.title: NESTApp: A GUI-Based MATLAB Application for Auditable TMS-EEG Preprocessing with EEGLAB
items.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) preprocessing determines signal quality and interpretation, particularly for transcranial magnetic stimulation combined with EEG (TMS-EEG), where recordings are affected by large and complex stimulation-related artifacts. Several preprocessing approaches have been developed, but substantial variability remains in how pipelines are implemented, documented, and evaluated across recordings, limiting reproducibility and comparability across studies. We developed NESTApp, a MATLAB-based graphical interface built on EEGLAB, to provide an accessible and reproducible framework for implementing and evaluating TMS-EEG preprocessing pipelines. Rather than prescribing a specific pipeline, NESTApp allows users to construct and consistently apply customisable workflows incorporating established EEGLAB and TMS-EEG processing tools, while automatically documenting processing decisions and parameters. Integrated quality-control procedures track data removal and flag recordings based on user-defined criteria, facilitating systematic evaluation across participants. The application also supports group-level visualisation and export of processed TMS-EEG measures for subsequent analyses. Applied to 29 recordings from 16 participants, NESTApp processed 27 and identified those requiring further inspection. By integrating pipeline implementation, documentation, quality control, and group-level evaluation within a single interface, NESTApp provides a transparent framework for TMS-EEG preprocessing that may improve reproducibility, facilitate consistent processing across cohorts, and lower technical barriers to the implementation of established preprocessing approaches.
items.authors: Pariz, A.; Dunne, W.; Lefebvre, J.; Tremblay, S.

items.title: Development and Evaluation of an Offline Vision-Language Model System for Estimating Nutrients from Meal Photographs on Personal Devices: The PLANS (Personal-device Local Assessment of Nutrients System) Study
items.abstract: Background: Estimating nutrient intake from meal photographs with vision-language models (VLMs) is now practical, but patient photographs often cannot leave the institution. We developed PLANS (Personal-device Local Assessment of Nutrients System), in which a small open VLM runs entirely on a personal device. Methods: Open VLMs were compared on two image sets with reference values (NutriImage, 887 Japanese meals; SNAPMe, 1,134 US meals), and the selected model (Qwen3-VL-4B, 4-bit) was run on an iPad Air without network access. Energy (primary outcome), protein, fat, carbohydrate and salt were evaluated by median absolute percentage error (MedAPE) and Spearman rank correlation (rho). The effect of supplying the food weight, including errors in it, was examined. Results: Energy estimates on the iPad were identical to those of a desktop-computer run for 84-86% of images (other values, 75-87%). MedAPE on the iPad was 37.0% and 36.5% for energy (26-28% of images within +/-20%), 43-65% for the macronutrients and 68-101% for salt (rho 0.51-0.85). On the desktop computer, supplying the true weight reduced MedAPE of the 4B model on NutriImage from 37.0% to 32.5% for energy and from 100.0% to 66.8% for salt; energy MedAPE stayed below the base value for declared weights of 0.5-1.25 times the true weight or rounded to 50 g, but rose markedly when the container weight was included. Conclusions: An offline VLM on a tablet reproduced server-side energy accuracy and is a candidate tool for dietary counselling where photographs cannot leave the institution; given the wide limits of agreement, its usefulness in practice remains to be examined.
items.authors: Nakagawa, S.; Yamamoto, A.

items.title: Development and Cross-Database External Validation of 24-Hour Landmark Models for ICU Mortality After Intracerebral Hemorrhage: Incremental Value of Routine Coagulation Markers
items.abstract: Background: Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) is associated with high early mortality. Although routine coagulation markers are clinically relevant, their incremental value for mortality prediction beyond neurologic and physiologic information is uncertain. We developed and externally validated models using first-24-hour ICU data and evaluated the added predictive value of routine coagulation measurements. Methods: We used MIMIC-IV for model development and eICU-CRD for external validation. The development cohort included 2,669 adults with non-traumatic ICH and 388 ICU deaths. Logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost were evaluated using a patient-level 70:30 holdout split and 5-fold stratified cross-validation. External validation used a high-specificity primary eICU cohort (396 patients; 39 deaths) and a broader secondary hemorrhagic-stroke/likely-ICH cohort (1,555 patients; 168 deaths). Performance was assessed using AUROC, AUPRC, Brier score, calibration, and paired bootstrap comparisons. GCS-only and age-plus-GCS models served as clinical benchmarks. Coagulation-only, clinical-only, and combined XGBoost models were compared to assess incremental value. Results: In the internal holdout cohort, AUROCs were 0.870 for logistic regression, 0.859 for random forest, and 0.867 for XGBoost. In the primary external cohort, corresponding AUROCs were 0.804, 0.839, and 0.817; AUPRCs were 0.342, 0.419, and 0.406; and Brier scores were 0.080, 0.072, and 0.074. In the broader cohort, AUROCs were 0.826, 0.848, and 0.838. Random forest showed the numerically strongest external performance, but pairwise AUROC differences among multivariable models were not clearly supported. GCS-only achieved AUROCs of 0.780 and 0.813 in the primary and broader cohorts. Coagulation-only XGBoost showed weak discrimination (AUROC 0.598 internally, 0.598 primary external, and 0.566 broader external). Adding coagulation variables to the clinical model produced AUROC differences of 0.014 (95% CI -0.009 to 0.037) and 0.003 (95% CI -0.007 to 0.013) in the two external cohorts. Conclusions: Multivariable models based on first-24-hour ICU data retained useful discrimination across external cohorts and provided modest gains over simple GCS-based benchmarks. Routine coagulation markers alone were weak predictors and did not provide clearly supported incremental discrimination beyond broader clinical information. Cross-database transportability should be interpreted together with phenotype alignment and calibration.
items.authors: Pathak, S.; Si, Y.; Sanjaya, J.; Haghi, M.; Kudrot, N. T.; Placencia, G.; Alaei, K.; Pishgar, M.
items.title_zh: ICU脑出血后24小时死亡预测模型的开发与验证
items.summary_zh: 背景：脑出血（ICH）早期死亡率高。尽管常规凝血指标在临床上相关，但其在超越神经和生理信息的死亡预测中的增值作用尚不明确。本研究开发并外部验证了基于首24小时ICU数据的预测模型，并评估常规凝血测量的附加预测价值。方法：使用MIMIC-IV进行模型开发，eICU-CRD进行外部验证。开发队列包括2669名非创伤性ICH成人患者及388例ICU死亡病例。采用逻辑回归、随机森林和XGBoost进行评估。外部验证使用高特异性eICU队列（396名患者；39例死亡）及更广泛的出血性中风/可能ICH队列（1555名患者；168例死亡）。结果：内部持出队列中，逻辑回归AUROC为0.870，随机森林为0.859，XGBoost为0.867。主要外部队列中，AUROC分别为0.804、0.839和0.817。
items.l1_lead: 本研究开发的ICU脑出血死亡预测模型在首24小时内具有较高的预测准确性，且常规凝血指标对死亡风险评估提供了额外的价值。
items.l2_summary:
本研究旨在开发和验证一个针对脑出血（ICH）患者在重症监护室（ICU）内24小时内死亡风险的预测模型。脑出血的早期死亡率较高，尽管常规凝血指标在临床上具有一定相关性，但其在超越神经和生理信息的死亡预测中的附加价值尚不明确。因此，研究者利用MIMIC-IV数据库进行模型开发，并在eICU-CRD数据库中进行外部验证。开发队列包括2669名非创伤性ICH成人患者，其中有388例在ICU内死亡。研究采用了逻辑回归、随机森林和XGBoost等多种机器学习方法进行模型评估。

在内部验证中，逻辑回归模型的曲线下面积（AUROC）为0.870，随机森林模型为0.859，而XGBoost模型则为0.867，显示出较高的预测能力。在主要外部验证队列中，包含396名患者（39例死亡），逻辑回归模型的AUROC为0.804，随机森林为0.839，XGBoost为0.817，表明该模型在不同人群中的有效性和可靠性。

通过本研究，开发的预测模型不仅能够有效评估ICU脑出血患者的早期死亡风险，还为临床提供了重要的决策支持工具。此外，研究还评估了常规凝血测量在死亡预测中的附加价值，为今后相关研究提供了基础。整体而言，该模型的开发与验证为改善脑出血患者的临床管理提供了新的思路和方法。

items.title: The impact of COVID-19 vaccination on long COVID prevention in the Omicron era: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis
items.abstract: Objectives To evaluate the impact of COVID-19 vaccination on the prevention of long COVID (LC) in the Omicron era through an updated systematic review and meta-analysis. Methods We performed an update of our previously published systematic review and meta-analysis of vaccination and LC risk (searches between 1 January 2022 and 1 March 2024). Databases (Embase, MEDLINE, PubMed, Europe PMC, LILACS, Cochrane COVID-19 Study Register) were searched for studies published between 1 March 2024 and 13 July 2026. Observational studies assessing the impact of vaccination on the risk of LC four or more weeks after SARS-CoV-2 infection were included. Vaccines were restricted to those centrally authorised in the European Union. Random-effects meta-analyses, restricted to adults, were performed to calculate pooled odds ratios (OR) of LC in three comparisons: vaccinated (any dose) versus unvaccinated; booster vaccination versus unvaccinated; and booster vaccination versus primary course vaccination only. Results Nineteen new studies were identified, of which ten were included in the updated meta-analyses alongside eight studies from the original review. The pooled OR of LC in vaccinated adults (any dose) versus unvaccinated was 0.75 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.67-0.84; 13 studies). ORs were also lower for booster vaccination versus unvaccinated (0.73; 95% CI 0.65-0.82; 6 studies), and booster vaccination versus primary course vaccination (0.63; 95% CI 0.53-0.75; 6 studies). Significant associations between vaccination and lower LC odds were observed in subgroup analyses of mRNA-only vaccination and LC outcomes three or more months after infection. Conclusions This updated review and meta-analysis reinforces our previous finding that vaccination may reduce the burden of LC in the Omicron era, with booster doses potentially providing additional protection. Although evidence in high-risk groups now prioritised for vaccination in most countries remains limited, these findings clearly demonstrate the benefits of vaccination and support current seasonal vaccination strategies.
items.authors: Marjenberg, Z.; Peluso, M. J.; Wynberg, E.; Abduljawad, S.

items.title: Artificiality's First Exam: An LLM-Referenced C-test for Supraintelligence
items.abstract: Under the accelerated pace of AI development, any benchmark whose difficulty is calibrated with humans or current AI systems becomes circular, or saturates soon. How can we then evaluate machines that may become more capable than the current machines and the people who write the tests? One answer to the question hinges on inverse problems, inductive inference questions for which difficulty depends on the complexity of the underlying mechanism, given the observations and the previous knowledge. Levin's Kt, a computable variant of Kolmogorov complexity, puts a theoretical upper bound to that difficulty, balancing the simplest representation encoding for the mechanism and the logarithm of the time steps to run that mechanism. Previous tests derived from Levin's Kt, such as the original C-test, are based on minimalistic Universal Turing Machines (UTM), capable of very limited representations and no previous knowledge. Reasoning large language models (LLM) are UTMs that capture a compendium of human culture as knowledge, using prompts as natural language programs. This paper presents the first test based on Levin's Kt with LLMs as representational machines. Fresh test items can be produced at high difficulties, estimated in a ratio scale measured in bits, before any human or frontier model can solve them. We formalise the measure, devise a lightweight generation and certification pipeline, explore the effect of the power of the reference machine and the gap between examiner and examinee. We produce a first battery of certified items administered to twelve LLMs. The resulting agent characteristic curves decrease with difficulty, down to the uncharted high-difficulty region, the supra-intelligence window of items we can certify, yet beyond generations of frontier intelligence.
items.authors: Jose Hernandez-Orallo

items.title: The Silent Failures in Agentic Data Science
items.abstract: Large language models have significantly lowered the barrier to writing code. Naturally, this has also led to the development of data science agents that promise automating the design and execution of data science from task formulation to model development. Existing evaluations of agentic data science (agentic DS) assess downstream predictive performance and code correctness, providing preliminary insight in agentic DS capabilities. We argue that these evaluations overlook the fundamental principles of data science: methodological data science- and domain knowledge. As such, only assessing downstream performance masks methodological failures such as data leakage and inappropriate validation, limiting the development of robust agentic DS systems. In this paper, we evaluate agentic DS beyond accuracy from three different angles: 1) a large-scale analysis of failure modes in common agentic DS frameworks and models across 220 data science tasks, 2) a reusable and extensible test suite with curated data science tasks that test for six specific failures in a controlled manner, and 3) a qualitative assessment of agentic DS pipelines against expert solutions on Kaggle competitions. We find that the majority of agentic solutions contain at least one failure mode despite the complexity of agentic harness or model capacity. Moreover, we identify a positive correlation between the occurrence of data leakage failures and predictive performance, confirming the necessity to evaluate agents beyond accuracy. Our qualitative analysis shows that DS agents generally lack problem solving creativity and domain knowledge, compared to competition-winning data scientists. We believe that principled failure mode analysis, as presented here, should be integral part of agentic DS evaluations, and that the insights we surface will be key in developing trustworthy agentic DS pipelines.
items.authors: Xue Li, Hongqian Xia, Daniel Gomm, A\'ecio Santos, Cornelius Wolff, Madelon Hulsebos

items.title: ClawLoop: Self-Improving Agents via Harness-Native Training Loop
items.abstract: The rapid advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs) has driven their deployment toward general-purpose harness environments, where LLM-based agents operate in sandbox workspaces and interact directly with file systems and shells. While numerous post-training pipelines exist for tool-use agents, their counterparts for harness-based agents remain scarce and are predominantly one-shot and teacher-dependent: a stronger external model synthesizes tasks and collects trajectories, the target agent is trained once, and evaluation results are consumed by human researchers rather than fed back into the loop. Such pipelines are inherently bounded by the capability of the external model and the scope of human prior, leaving no room for self-improvement. To address these limitations, we propose ClawLoop, a framework that enables self-improving without any external teacher model and with minimal prior dependencies. ClawLoop composes three phases into a self-sustaining cycle: Task Synthesis, which generates a diverse pool of training tasks via two complementary construction routines, applies diagnosis-conditioned difficulty growth followed by both agent-free and agent-based task validation; Training, which updates the agent via SFT and/or RL; and Diagnosis and Feedback, which analyzes the agent's rollout behaviors to produce a capability analysis report that will be used as feedback for task synthesis in the next iteration. Using Qwen3.6-27B as the loop model, ClawLoop yields consistent improvements on SkillsBench, Claw-Eval-Live, and ClawGym-Bench. The iteratively refined tasks are further transferred to smaller-scale Qwen3.5-4B and 9B models with gains across all benchmarks, validating data quality independently of the loop model.
items.authors: Hansi Yang, Linji Hao, Hongyan Hao, An Wang, Han Wu, Qi Gu, Xunliang Cai

items.title: Correction Training for Diffusion Models
items.abstract: Iterative sampling in diffusion models can lead to error accumulation due to exposure bias. The denoiser is trained on real images interpolated with noise, but at inference its inputs are constructed from its own imperfect predictions from the earlier steps, something it has never seen at training time. This might be one reason diffusion models often struggle without additional help, such as CFG. We introduce a correction step for diffusion models which attempts to reduce this training-inference gap. The corrector takes the base model's prediction as input and is trained against the same ground-truth target. This makes correction an explicit learning task, with training inputs provided by the base model. During sampling, at each denoising step, we iteratively refine the denoiser's clean-sample prediction. This allows us to correct predictions at intermediate denoising steps, preventing early artifacts from persisting into the final sample. Although the corrector is trained only on predictions from the base denoiser, it can be applied repeatedly to its own outputs at inference for better results. This simple framework leads to substantial improvement in sample quality while largely preserving diversity. We evaluate our method across DiT, SiT, and JiT. Our method substantially improves upon previously reported FID scores for unguided generation and, notably, unconditional generation, where producing high-quality samples without guidance has been particularly challenging. Our method achieves performance competitive with classifier-free guidance (CFG), and combining correction with CFG further improves diversity and reduces oversaturation typical of CFG. Finally, we show that the additional inference cost of correction can be amortized by distilling the refined predictions back into the base diffusion model, retaining the quality gains without additional inference-time overhead.
items.authors: Donghoon Ahn, Runqian Wang, Alexei A. Efros, Taesung Park, Yash Belhe

items.title: Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench 2.0: Automating Diverse Task Construction and Measuring Sustained Agent Progress
items.abstract: Long-horizon terminal benchmarks measure whether an agent can sustain progress through extended workflows with process rewards, not only whether its final state passes a binary check. We present Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench 2.0 (LHTB 2.0), an extension of Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench that preserves its 46 original tasks while correcting task and evaluation-infrastructure defects and extending 31 tasks. LHTB 2.0 contains 77 tasks across 13 domains and eight task types. The extended tasks are produced through a systematic reconstruction-task pipeline. We start from a working scientific or engineering artifact, then use a parameterized reference implementation to generate multiple scenarios, reveal six as behavioral evidence, hold out three for evaluation, and use dense progress ladders to reward partial progress while preventing memorization of public outputs. We also extend the evaluation horizon from 90 minutes to three hours and record verifier checkpoints every 30 minutes, enabling direct measurement of sustained progress within a run. Across 1,145 scored model-task runs from 15 frontier models, GPT-6-astra leads with dense mean reward 0.69 and 37 tasks at R at least 0.95, followed by GPT-5.6-sol with dense mean reward 0.67 and 32 tasks at the same threshold. On the 30 reconstruction tasks, binary verifier scores average 0.221, whereas dense ladder scores average 0.653, showing that outcome-only evaluation discards substantial intermediate progress. LHTB 2.0 provides a broader, hardened, and process-aware testbed for studying reliable agent execution over hours.
items.authors: Zongxia Li, Zhongzhi Li, Yucheng Shi, Ruhan Wang, Junyao Yang, Chengsong Huang, Zhichao Liu, Xiyang Wu, Anhao Li, Yue Yu, Ergan Shang, Fuxiao Liu, Tong Zheng, Ninghao Liu, Lichao Sun, Haitao Mi, Leowei Liang

items.title: VETNET: Assembling Benchmark Datasets for AI-Driven Veterinary Innovation
items.abstract: VETNET represents an ecosystem of live benchmark datasets and evaluation frameworks designed to accelerate AI-driven innovation in animal science and veterinary medicine through standardized, high-quality datasets and multi-institutional collaboration across academic and non-academic sectors. This framework addresses the gap between AI advances in human medicine and the fragmented state of veterinary AI development.
items.authors: Katherine J. Koebel, Renata Ivanek, Parminder Basran, Jennifer Sun, Casey Cazer, Gayatri Anil, Tommaso Banzato, Liz Barton, Dottie Cimino Brown, Leszek Bukowski, Marta Castelhano, Simon Coghlan, Christopher De Sa, Nikki Dutta, Hala Ghali, Julio Giordano, Joshua Glass, David C. Hogg, Nicholas Hollingshead, Adam Kiehl, Ziang Liu, Monica Meduri, Param Mohapatra, Kim Nayyer, Amelia Nelson, Peter-John Mantyla Noble, Christopher Pinard, Beryl Rabindran, Scott Ross, Ron Seccia, Moira Sheehan, Fei Wang, Tracy L. Webb, Kilian Q. Weinberger, Heather M. Whitney, Chen Xin

items.title: Unconstrained CTI-REALM with Open-Weights
items.abstract: Organisations that want language-model agents for security work face a choice between open-weight models, which they can run and audit themselves, and far more expensive closed frontier models. We study that choice on CTI-REALM (arXiv:2603.13517), a benchmark in which an agent turns a threat-intelligence report into a working detection by querying a live telemetry store. We evaluate twenty-six models, nineteen open-weight and seven closed, under a common harness, scorer and panel of LLM judges. Our main finding is that an open-weight model can match the strongest closed models at less than a tenth of their cost, provided it is given enough turns. The benchmark's published limit on agent messages is a confound: a task that exhausts the limit scores zero on every checkpoint, including those it had already passed, so results at that limit partly measure which models finish in time. At the published limit the leading open-weight and closed models cannot be distinguished. With the limit relaxed, the models it was truncating recover, and the highest rewards belong to open-weight models. Among the leading models, price is a poor guide to capability: models with similar rewards differ in cost by more than an order of magnitude. Because the benchmark's checkpoint scores largely record what an agent did or mentioned, we also introduce stage-level metrics that score what the agent submits, by executing its detection queries in the telemetry store and judging its outputs against the answer key. Rather than combining them into one more overall reward, we show that different models lead different stages, which suggests routing each stage of the workflow to the model that performs it best rather than choosing a single model by its overall score. We also report how many tokens each model generates, and find that the share of output spent on thinking does not track the reward.
items.authors: Sahil Garg, Ruhi Gottumukkala, Vishal Agarwal, Shubham Vishwakarma

items.title: Visualizing the World Model in an Agent's Value Function
items.abstract: Could model-free reinforcement learning algorithms actually be learning a model of the environment? In this work, we apply counterfactual interventions which hold everything about a state fixed, besides a targeted change, to explore if the value function of a Proximal Policy Optimization agent forms a world model of the Crafter environment. Despite only being trained to optimize reward, we discover that the value function learns concepts such as the rules governing when a diamond is collectible, water and food having an impact on health, heuristics regarding inventory, and more. Finally, we discuss the safety implications of our visualizations and some shortcomings of current reinforcement learning agents that will prevent us from building truly advanced machine intelligence.
items.authors: Shawheen Naderi, Fatemeh Akherati, Yubei Chen

items.title: Cross-Modal Latent Influence: Patch-Level Training Sample Attribution for Vision-Language Models
items.abstract: Explaining a vision--language model (VLM) prediction requires tracing training-example influence to the multimodal evidence that mediates it, yet existing attribution methods largely operate only at the sample level. Recent latent-mediated influence methods provide feature-level attribution in language models, but lack the multimodal and spatial structure needed to ground influence in VLMs. We introduce MOSAIC (Multimodal Orthogonalized Sparse Autoencoders for Influence Characterization). It learns a shared sparse image--text latent space whose concepts are 1) sparse within each modality, 2) supported on contiguous image regions, 3) aligned to the phrases that describe them, and 4) approximately decorrelated. It then applies EK-FAC to decompose training-example influence through these concepts and localize their contributions to specific text phrases and image regions. We evaluate MOSAIC on Qwen and Gemma across captioning, chest X-ray understanding, and visual question answering. The learned features are more localized and coherent without degrading task behavior, and ablating influence-ranked latents changes model outputs more than ablating latents ranked by activation or frequency. We find that visual evidence can substantially reorganize training-data attribution while preserving more of the shared latent structure. MOSAIC thus connects where model behavior comes from with what multimodal evidence carries that influence.
items.authors: Laura Yao, Shixing Yu, Jie Peng, Promit Ghosal, Kyra Gan, Tianlong Chen

items.title: Should SLMs be in the Driver's Seat? A Study of Local Models as Interpreters in Cloud-Written Agent Programs
items.abstract: The most accurate agents executing user-provided tasks are driven by large, cloud-hosted models, which solve them by reading the private data of the user. Agents powered by models small enough to run on edge devices keep that data local, but yield far worse results. A third option is to have cloud models write a program that devices execute: the data stays local, but as the program is written before any data is seen, it fails whenever a step depends on interpreting content that appears only at run time. We explore an intermediate architecture, in which the cloud-written program defers bounded questions over user data to a small local model through an ordinary function call. On AppWorld this improves the success rate of a code-only agent in all six combinations of backbone model and test partition we evaluate, by up to 14.9pp, recovering a substantial part of the gap to a cloud-hosted ReAct loop while keeping user data on the device.
items.authors: Boris Radovi\v{c}, Marco Canini, Veljko Pejovi\'c

items.title: Harness^2: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World
items.abstract: LLM agents' capabilities depend not only on their underlying models but also on their execution harnesses. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) offers a promising approach to automatically evolve these harnesses. However, deploying RSI in open-world settings still faces two critical challenges. First, open-world tasks are typically unseen during the harness design phase and novel at test time, leaving no ground-truth verifiers to reliably guide online harness edits. Second, the RSI process remains highly task-specific and fails to generalize to novel scenarios. We introduce Harness^2, a plug-and-play, recursive agent harnessing framework that addresses these challenges through two connected levels of recursion. Task-level recursion refines the current task's harness using a contrastive Propose-Probe-Compose step that reliably guides edits without ground-truth verifiers, and can be scaled further via parallel or sequential recursion. Harnessing-level recursion then extracts experience from these edits to update a continual improvement harness, enabling the agent to better adapt to future tasks. Across three professional benchmarks and four model-harness configurations, a single step consistently improves GLM-5 and Gemini 3.5 Flash over their base harnesses, yielding gains of up to 11.5 points on WorkBuddy-Bench, 4.5 points on JobBench, and 11.8 percentage points on LAB, with further gains as the task-level recursion budget increases.
items.authors: Ruiyao Xu, Yanfei Chen, Zhongying CuiZhu, Bhavana Dalvi Mishra, Yifei Ming, Han Yu, Rujun Han, Chen-Yu Lee, Tomas Pfister

items.title: Echo: Error-Compensated 4-Bit Tensor-Parallel Communication for LLM Training and Inference
items.abstract: Tensor parallelism ends every layer with an all-reduce that sits between two dependent matrix multiplications, so its cost cannot be hidden and grows as compute outpaces interconnect bandwidth. Sending 4-bit instead of 16-bit values would cut this cost by nearly 4x, but the all-reduce must add the values it carries, and rounding the sum injects an error at every call. Model quality depends on how these errors accumulate over layers, yet existing methods treat each call on its own. We present Echo, a 4-bit all-reduce for training and inference that controls the accumulated error. Echo moves data in 4 bits and sums in high precision, so each value is quantized at most twice per call for any number of GPUs. The summation reveals each injected error, and Echo feeds it back into later calls, so old errors cancel instead of accumulating. We prove that the accumulated error stays bounded independently of depth. On A100 GPUs, Echo is 2.09x faster than the 16-bit NCCL all-reduce on 1 GB messages. It speeds up the time to first token by up to 1.16x and the training step by up to 1.09x on an idle interconnect, and by up to 1.44x and 1.38x as background traffic grows. It keeps the average accuracy over seven benchmarks within 0.4 points of 16-bit inference on Qwen3-8B. In 10B-token pretraining, its final loss is less than 0.9% above that of 16-bit training. Echo needs no FP8 or FP4 hardware.
items.authors: Xingyu Xie, Xiaoyong Xie, Zhouchen Lin, Kim-Chuan Toh

items.title: Controllable Diverse Sampling through Pullback Directions
items.abstract: Conditional diffusion models can generate high-quality images that align closely with a given prompt. However, samples generated from different random seeds may remain visually similar, limiting creative exploration. Existing approaches can increase variation, but often require additional optimization or sampling overhead, while stronger perturbations may introduce distortions that degrade image quality or prompt alignment. We propose a training-free method that leverages the local pullback geometry induced by the mapping from the conditioning-embedding space to the image space to identify directions of maximal output sensitivity. By steering different sampling trajectories along these directions, we encourage distinct generations while maintaining consistency with the conditioning signal. Experiments on MS-COCO and BrushNet show the efficacy of the method in improving diversity on prompt-conditioned image generation and inpainting.
items.authors: Sylvain Dehayem Kenfouo, Aaron Zweig, Mingxuan Zhang, Elham Azizi

items.title: ConicFlow: constrained Inference-time optimal control for flow matching models
items.abstract: We propose ConicFlow, which frames constrained sampling from a flow matching model at inference time as an optimal control problem that balances deviation from the pretrained trajectory against reward, subject to hard terminal constraints. We discretize this problem and adapt receding-horizon control, optimizing only a short window of the trajectory at each step for computational tractability. We address the resulting sequence of receding-horizon subproblems with a receding-horizon primal-dual algorithm. Its dual multipliers capture the difficulty of satisfying each constraint and are refined throughout sampling, steering generation toward feasible final samples. We further propose a terminal-estimate variant that avoids accumulating local truncation errors by evaluating the reward and constraints at the predicted terminal point rather than at the end of the current horizon. Under standard regularity assumptions, we establish finite-horizon guarantees on suboptimality. Under convex-affine structure, we derive a sharper bound that scales linearly with omitted horizon length, and we show that the terminal-estimate variant is provably tighter when the flow dynamics change slowly. Experiments in both low- and high-dimensional settings with a recent large-scale flow matching model show that ConicFlow achieves high reward and strong constraint satisfaction while deviating less from the pretrained flow than recent baselines.
items.authors: Shervin Khalafi, Kasra Fallah, Sung Cho, Dongsheng Ding, James Anderson, Alejandro Ribeiro

items.title: Which Metadata Matters for LLM Tool Selection in MCP? Evidence from Controlled Factor-Level Interventions
items.abstract: In Model Context Protocol (MCP) systems, LLMs select tools from metadata rather than from their implementations. Names and descriptions summarize what a tool does, while the parameter schema specifies the fields a tool accepts and how they are organized. Our analysis of metadata for 367,174 MCP tools reveals substantial schema variation among functionally similar tools. Many of these tools share names and similar descriptions but expose different parameter schemas. This raises a key question: can parameter-schema differences influence tool selection before any call is made? We study this question through controlled metadata interventions across five LLMs and five tasks. Each comparison changes exactly one metadata factor (server name, tool name, description, or parameter schema) while keeping the others fixed. We balance tool positions and use conditional logistic regression to estimate position-adjusted effects. We find that: (1) parameter-schema changes produce the largest and most consistent selection shifts among the tested interventions. Models tend to favor separate top-level parameters over grouped or composite forms. (2) Descriptions that explain parameters also tend to increase selection, while name effects are weaker and less consistent. (3) Targeted comparisons show that schema effects depend on the specific parameter names and on how the request represents the same information. When only one schema satisfies an explicit request requirement, all five models select the compatible tool despite position preferences. These results show that parameter schemas influence not only how tools are called, but also whether they are selected. For MCP developers and evaluators, schema design and tool ordering can therefore affect which implementation is invoked even when functionality is unchanged.
items.authors: Xiaofan Li, Fengchun Qiao, Xing Gao

items.title: Actionable Meta-Requirements for AI Robustness Auditing
items.abstract: AI-enabled systems must remain dependable when the conditions under which they operate change (e.g., due to input perturbations, distribution shifts, or changes in external dependencies). This makes robustness auditing of such systems important for judging whether the available evidence is sufficient to support a defined robustness conclusion. However, designing an AI robustness auditing framework is challenging. A key unresolved issue is determining the requirements such a framework should support; these requirements have not yet been consolidated. We address this gap through meta-requirements: higher-order requirements specifying what a class of auditing frameworks should support. In design science research, literature and domain experts are common sources of meta-requirements; accordingly, we derive the initial set from literature and validate and refine it with practitioners. Our systematic literature review retained 74 of 2,890 records and derived 43 meta-requirements across 16 categories. We evaluated them with 128 practitioners, obtaining 5,504 ratings and 586 substantive comments. Overall, 81.20% of ratings indicated agreement or strong agreement. In particular, 41 of the 43 literature-derived meta-requirements were classified as strongly supported. Practitioner feedback refined the requirements and identified an additional requirement concerning external components and supply chain dependencies. The final set comprises 44 meta-requirements across 16 categories, of which 43 received quantitative validation. These meta-requirements can help organizations implement AI robustness auditing frameworks, assess existing frameworks for completeness, and refine them.
items.authors: Joshua Owotogbe, Roya Nasiri, Indika Kumara, Damian Andrew Tamburri, Willem-Jan van den Heuvel

items.title: When Pleasing the User Compromises Care: AI Sycophancy in Caregiver-Mediated Healthcare
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) alignment often assumes that the user interacting with a model is also the primary beneficiary of its behavior. Yet in many consequential settings, one person directs the system while another bears the consequences. We study this problem in caregiver-mediated healthcare, where parents, pet owners, and caregivers make decisions for children, animals, and older adults. We introduce an evidence-grounded benchmark spanning veterinary, pediatric, and older-adult care, and test whether AI advisors maintain appropriate care when users express clinically inferior preferences. Holding patient facts fixed, we vary stated care preferences and communication styles and evaluate both initial recommendations and multi-turn follow-up. Across frontier and open-weight models, inferior preferences substantially increase switching from appropriate to inappropriate care beyond neutral conversational drift and increase agreement with the requested action, while communication style alone has a smaller effect. These failures accumulate across turns, including on cases models initially answer correctly, and often carry moderate or severe potential harm. In matched eldercare cases, the effect of an inferior preference is similar whether it is expressed by the patient or by a caregiver. Together with models' limited tendency to elicit patient preferences in caregiver conversations, this suggests that current models are highly sensitive to expressed user preferences but less sensitive to whose preferences are represented and who bears the consequences. Our results expose a broader limitation of user-centric alignment in settings with multiple stakeholders.
items.authors: Priyadarsi Mishra, Arjun Beniwal, Ziyu Yi, Yu Ding, Sheng Liu

items.title: ACED-Bench: Evaluating How LLM Agents Acquire and Act on Causal Evidence
items.abstract: Large language models are increasingly used as scientific assistants, yet we still lack reliable ways to evaluate whether they can investigate a system rather than merely answer a prompt. A useful evaluation must let agents choose experiments, interpret finite evidence, and make causal decisions, while keeping the environment coherent across repeated observations and interventions and preserving objective ground truth. We introduce ACED-BENCH (Active Causal Evidence and Decision Benchmark), a neuro-symbolic benchmark built around this requirement. The key idea is to separate the readable scientific surface from the formal causal world: LLMs generate natural-language scenarios and task text, while hidden probabilistic graphical models define the causal graph, data-generating process, intervention semantics, validation checks, and oracle answers. This yields scientific worlds that are natural for agents to investigate but exact enough for scalable, programmatic evaluation. The main leaderboard ACED-CORE contains 180 tasks: 60 set-valued causal ancestry/descendancy questions and 120 constrained causal-decision tasks. We also report ACED-QUAL, a 150-question yes/no qualification check using the same hidden-PGM interface. We evaluate seven contemporary LLMs and two earlier-generation models across three active agent designs. ACED-QUAL checks whether agents can use the interface to draw conclusions from evidence, while ACED-CORE tests whether they can decide what evidence to collect and when to commit to an answer. Evidence-ledger analysis localizes failures within the investigation: agents test the wrong intervention, lose relevant evidence, or continue after sufficient evidence has appeared. These results suggest that reliable AI co-scientists need explicit support for experiment design, evidence retention, answer commitment, and stopping.
items.authors: Yiwei Chen, Amila Weerasinghe, Siddharth Biswal, Utkrisht Rajkumar, Olcay Boz, Taylor Berg-Kirkpatrick, Rose Yu

items.title: ANASSA: From High-Level Framework to Low-Level Architecture for Spatial Agentic AI
items.abstract: Agentic AI systems operating over geospatial data require more than autonomous reasoning and tool use; they must also support explicit orchestration, spatial validation, governance, provenance, failure handling, and human decision authority. Prior work introduced ANASSA, an agentic AI orchestration framework for spatial intelligence that established high-level components and responsibility boundaries for governed agentic execution (arXiv:2609.14824). However, the framework did not specify how those high-level responsibilities should be systematically decomposed into an implementation-facing low-level architecture. This paper addresses that gap by applying Design Science Research (DSR) to refine the ANASSA framework from high-level architectural (HLA) responsibilities into a low-level architecture (LLA). The resulting design preserves the responsibility boundaries of the foundational framework while translating them into executable architectural structures, including 47 logical roles, versioned task graphs, capability-based agent selection, typed contracts, explicit runtime states, spatial validation mechanisms, governance controls, failure and recovery paths, and provenance records. The architecture is demonstrated through an end-to-end execution trace and analytically evaluated for requirements traceability, internal consistency, responsibility preservation, and technology independence. The resulting high-level-to-low-level design provides an implementation-facing bridge between the ANASSA framework and future system implementations, defining how governed spatial agentic workflows can be made inspectable, reconstructable, and testable without binding the architecture to a specific AI model, geospatial platform, communication protocol, or deployment environment.
items.authors: Constantinos Papantoniou, Brian Hilton

items.title: Measuring the Inference Energy Efficiency of Open-Weight LLMs across Benchmarks, Reasoning Modes, and Hardware
items.abstract: Benchmark scores tell us what an LLM can do, but not how much energy is required to deliver that capability. We directly measure this trade-off for 86 open-weight model checkpoints, evaluated on seven benchmarks and six hardware platforms ranging from a consumer GPU to an eight-GPU server. We find large differences in energy efficiency even among models with similar capability. Most configurations lie away from the score--energy Pareto frontier: they use a median of 2.6--4.8$\times$ more energy than another configuration that scores at least as well, with differences reaching 27$\times$. Reasoning can improve capability, but enabling thinking increases energy by about 3.7$\times$ on average, and the benefit depends strongly on the model family and output budget. Generated-token count is also an imperfect proxy for energy, misordering 18--24\% of model pairs. In contrast, FP8 reduces energy by roughly a quarter with little change in score, while changing hardware largely rescales energy without changing the relative ranking of models. These results show that capability alone gives an incomplete picture of efficiency. We argue that benchmark scores should be reported together with measured energy consumption under a specified serving regime and output budget.
items.authors: Zeyu Yang, Wes Armour

items.title: SAT-RL: Training Language Models for Logical Reasoning with Symbolic Solvers
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have achieved strong performance in mathematical and logical reasoning, yet they still suffer from the curse of complexity and struggle as problem difficulty increases with the number of constraint interactions and the size of the search space. In contrast, satisfiability solvers such as Z3 provide scalable and verifiable reasoning through constraint solving under formal theories, but lack the flexibility to interpret natural-language problem descriptions. In this work, we propose SAT-RL, a reinforcement-learning (RL) framework that trains LLMs to interact with symbolic solvers through multi-turn tool execution. SAT-RL leverages synthetic data generation with verifiable solutions, supervised warm-up on solver-augmented traces, and solver-grounded reinforcement learning with tool-aware rewards. Experiments show that SAT-RL substantially improves symbolic reasoning with tools on both in-domain and out-of-domain logic tasks. Our code is available on https://github.com/sunjia72/SAT-RL.
items.authors: Jialiang Sun, Kuldeep Meel

items.title: Frustratingly Easy Agentic RAG via Portable Skills: A Case Study in Customer Support
items.abstract: Enterprise workflow automation typically requires retrieving a complete and accurate set of relevant information from large operational document corpora (SOPs, policy documents) given a specific scenario or request. In customer support (CS), for example, human specialists must determine the correct sequence of resolution steps for each case, a task that demands precise grounding in policy documentation. Meeting this bar in production typically requires complex document chunking, indexing, and retrieval pipelines, often layered with learned re-rankers, query rewriters, and bespoke agentic RAG infrastructure. We report a deployment case study of a simpler alternative: a portable skill consisting of a natural-language instruction, lightweight tools (a retrieval API, format-checking scripts), and a corpus enriched with an LLM-generated navigation layer, which is a structured "Wikipedia-style" index over the underlying documents. This agentic RAG approach is straightforward to implement (1-2 engineer days), portable across capable agentic harnesses (e.g., Claude Code), and performs strongly on the challenging task of CS resolution workflow generation, achieving 99.2% procedural equivalence to human-approved ground truth and 83.3% evidence sufficiency. It is also roughly an order of magnitude slower per case than our deployed production assistant (~90 s vs. ~8-9 s), so we claim no latency advantage. Our claim is scoped to that setting: a mature, well-curated corpus, a latency-tolerant workflow, and human review of every case. There, the skill did the work of a complex RAG stack, and maintenance became a matter of editing text and data rather than retraining models.
items.authors: Istok Bako, Bonan Min, Tiffany Shao, Claire Cheng, Yashar Mehdad

items.title: AlignPoison: Conditional Targeted Poisoning of Generative Recommenders via Decoding-Aligned Prefixes
items.abstract: Generative recommendation models based on autoregressive decoding have been adopted as alternatives to classical ranking-based systems. While their modeling flexibility has been widely studied, their resilience to data poisoning remains largely unexplored. In this work, we ask: how susceptible are generative recommenders to conditional targeted poisoning? Under a realistic setting where an adversary can inject limited malicious interactions and query a recommendation API as a black box, our empirical study shows that generative recommenders are vulnerable: injecting fewer than 1% synthetic interactions significantly increases the likelihood of promoting malicious targets under the trigger. To characterize this vulnerability, we analyze the synthesis of malicious interactions from two perspectives: (i) decoding alignment and (ii) prefix popularity. We observe that short, context-aligned prefixes that are both common under the model's induced transition dynamics and strongly linked to a frequent trigger consistently amplify targeted promotion. Motivated by this analysis, we develop AlignPoison, a black-box framework that discovers and samples context-aligned prefixes from API outputs. We conduct experiments on benchmarks in unimodal and multimodal generative recommendation settings. Results show that these prefixes outperform competitive baselines, improving ASR lift by up to 16.3 percentage points and highlighting a decoding-dependent, context-sensitive poisoning vulnerability in generative recommendation models.
items.authors: Zhuoxuan Zhang, Jinhao Duan, Xinyu Zhao, Jinduo Guo, Shuai Shao, Rui Li, Luke Simon, Zhun Deng, Tianlong Chen, Bo Sun

items.title: HiPPT: Physiology-Grounded Wearable PPG Representation Learning via Multi-Scope Text Alignment
items.abstract: Reusable wearable PPG representations should capture local pulse morphology and broader physiological regularities. Existing pretraining objectives, however, usually apply supervision at the recording or pair level, overlooking that different concepts become reliable over different scopes of waveform evidence. We propose HiPPT, a physiology-grounded framework that matches each supervision source to its appropriate evidence scope. We construct a PPG-Text corpus of over 4 million wrist-worn recordings from 202K users, pairing recordings with waveform-derived morphology and metadata-derived context descriptions. HiPPT combines record-level morphology alignment, which grounds individual recordings in pulse characteristics, with cross-recording context alignment, which aggregates recordings sharing the same metadata tuple to capture context-consistent regularities. Waveform-guided text modeling further recovers masked contextual concepts from PPG patch representations, providing fine-grained waveform-text supervision. Across six downstream tasks spanning blood pressure, vascular stiffness, physiological attributes, and cross-dataset heart-rate estimation, HiPPT achieves the best result on the primary linear-probing metrics. The aligned space also supports zero-shot profiling of age group, sex, and BMI category, individually and jointly, with performance improving as more recordings are aggregated. These results show that evidence-scope matching yields transferable and semantically accessible wearable PPG representations. Code and pretrained weights will be released.
items.authors: Jiaqi Wang, Wei Chen, Xiaoyu Li, Lexian Xia, ShuaiLong Tang, Chenran Zhang, Donglin Xie, Guangpu Zhu, Yelei Li, Yi Zhou

items.title: Reels-RSI: Program-Level Self-Improvement for Code-Rendered Explainer Videos
items.abstract: Explainer videos -- a worked geometry problem, why the sky is blue, how a dynasty fell -- are usually one more target for pixel video generation. We argue they are a different kind of artifact: a program (script, storyboard and per-frame animation code) that a deterministic renderer turns into frames. A program can be read, diffed, tested and audited; pixels can only be watched. Reels-RSI is an open-source reel director for any agent harness; its self-improvement happens at the program level rather than in weights or prompts. Every revision pass is logged with a code snapshot; a retrospective pairs each check finding with the diff that fixed it and proposes lessons; a lesson that a static check can catch is compiled into a rule with a must-fail and a must-pass example, so the memory is unit-tested; and a rule learned today runs over everything made before it. A bounded, benchmark-gated step lets an agent rewrite the director's playbook, kept only when blind pairwise judgments on held-out topics prefer it; nothing enters memory without a human decision.
