Episodic Memory preserves user inputs and compresses model replies, while heuristic retrieval selects raw text, compressed representations, or omission for each historical turn. On Long-MT-Bench+, REA improves the judge score from 6.32 to 7.36 on a 10-point scale, a 16.5% relative gain over the Vanilla baseline, and reduces average latency by 2.91$\times$. Additional evaluations show aggregate gains on three backbones spanning 1.7B-7B parameters and on Chinese and English role-playing tasks. These results support role-aware context management as a practical approach to maintaining conversational continuity and instruction adherence.
items.authors: Wanyang Hong, Zhaoning Zhang, Yi Chen, Libo Zhang, Baihui Liu, Linbo Qiao, Zhiliang Tian, Dongsheng Li

items.title: LLM-as-Jev: LLMs Are Already Jev-Style Decision Models -- When and How to Fine-Tune Them
items.abstract: Jev-style decision models have gained surging traction by making decision-making dramatically faster and more efficient, returning categorical probability distributions over predefined options without generating free-form text. However, because Jev's architecture and training methodologies remain proprietary, how to replicate these capabilities effectively remains an open question. In this work, we investigate the extent to which general-purpose LLMs already possess this capability out of the box, and when fine-tuning is actually necessary. We present LLM-as-Jev, an architecture-preserving framework offering both a training-free inference recipe and a fine-tuning objective with KL-divergence anchors. Across Qwen3.5-4B and Qwen3-0.6B, we find that modern LLMs are inherently effective decision models: off the shelf, frozen models match or exceed existing training-free readouts on the same 4B backbone, scale to arbitrary option counts, and natively handle multimodal decisions. They also seamlessly inherit the backbone's thinking mode: while Jev was introduced as a System 1 model, "Thinking Jev" leverages budgeted test-time reasoning to boost accuracy on challenging tasks without training. Fine-tuning provides targeted gains for smaller models and complex routing, while our KL anchors prevent behavioral degradation in general text generation.
items.authors: Yinheng Li, Justin Wagle

items.title: General Decision Models: Benchmarking and Insights Beyond Jev
items.abstract: General decision models, such as Jev, have recently emerged as efficient alternatives to LLMs for structured judgment and selection. But what kinds of decisions can these models reliably make, and how does their behavior change when individual decisions are composed into larger systems? To study this, we introduce JEVal, a bilingual benchmark comprising 11,257 instances from 36 datasets across 10 application domains, and evaluate 25 model configurations spanning general decision models and generative LLMs. Our results show that (1) general decision models are most competitive when decisions can be resolved from available evidence, but weaken when they require specialist knowledge or faithful uncertainty estimation: they can often identify the most likely outcome while substantially overstating its probability. (2) In more dynamic and realistic systems involving long-horizon, multi-step interactions, the advantages of fast local decision making are offset by reliability failures at the system level. on $\tau$-bench, faster local decisions reduce median episode time but lower task success as decision errors accumulate over long trajectories. (3) In large-scale social simulation, decision models approach strong generative LLMs on individual response prediction at substantially lower inference cost, yet remain weaker in user profiling and exhibit larger aggregate estimation errors and systematic bias. Finally, we propose SII-Decision-4B and SII-Decision-27B, which internalize an open-weight LLM's own reasoning into a single-pass first-token decision through Reasoning-to-Readout Self-Distillation, with SII-Decision-27B performing on par with Jev on JEVal while answering a typical query in about 0.1 s.
items.authors: Feiyu Duan, Jiayu Lin, Jia Wang, Jun Xiang, Jialiang Wu, Xinnong Zhang, Hanqi Yan, Siyuan Wang, Zhongyu Wei

items.title: IdeaScientist: Orchestrating Agents for Grounded Scientific Ideation
items.abstract: Despite rapid progress in automating scientific research, generating promising and well grounded research solutions remains a central challenge. We isolate research ideation as a standalone task and build our solution on the intuition that a challenge in one field can often be addressed by a mechanism that solved an analogous challenge in another. Accordingly, we introduce IdeaScientist, which decomposes ideation into gap finding, innovation, and report writing, and trains each role with reinforcement learning. These roles identify limitations in related work, draw solution intuitions from analogous problem settings, and develop those intuitions into complete research proposals. To facilitate discovery of insights across domains, we construct the Svalbard Idea Vault, a corpus of 2.77M decomposed research ideas for retrieval, training, and temporally controlled evaluation. Our evaluation restricts access to literature available before a cutoff date and assesses how closely proposed directions align with those later explored in 15K papers authored by human researchers. On Qwen3.6-27B, IdeaScientist outperforms the strongest open-source autoresearch baseline by 14.0%, driven mainly by gains in novelty. On this 27B open backbone, IdeaScientist even outperforms Claude Code SDK with Claude-4.8-Opus and Codex SDK with GPT-5.4, by up to 5.9%.
items.authors: Jiarui Liu, Renjie Tao, Yiwei Liao, Chuanyang Jin, Kai Sun, Xiao Yang, Xinyuan Zhang, Xilun Chen, Zhuangqun Huang, Lechen Zhang, Yongjin Yang, Yinghui He, Weihao Xuan, Rakesh Wanga, Anuj Kumar, Mona T. Diab, Wen-tau Yih, Xin Luna Dong

items.title: The \`{I}r\`{o}y\`{i}nSpeech Text Corpus: 24,905 Curated Yor\`ub\'a Sentences for Speech and Language Technology
items.abstract: \`{I}r\`{o}y\`{i}nSpeech is a 42-hour, 80-speaker Yor\`ub\'a read-speech corpus whose audio has been distributed by ELRA since 2024. This paper describes the release of its text component: 24,905 unique, hand-verified, tone-marked Yor\`ub\'a sentences (275,897 tokens; 15,687 types), curated in 2022 as recording prompts. Roughly 11,000 sentences were adapted from openly licensed news material; the remainder were written in-house to broaden coverage beyond the religious translation that dominates existing Yor\`ub\'a corpora. Every sentence was checked by hand for tone-mark accuracy, edited for read-aloud clarity and a neutral register, and localised so that non-Yor\`ub\'a personal and place names appear in Yor\`ub\'a form. Preparing the text for release surfaced systematic Unicode normalisation failures affecting more than 60% of lines (with precomposed and decomposed forms of the same letter co-occurring within single sentences) which we document and correct. The corpus supports diacritic restoration, grapheme-to-phoneme conversion, TTS front-end development and orthographic research, and serves as a validated prompt set for new recording.
items.authors: Kola Tubosun, Aanuoluwapo Aremu, Tolulope Ogunremi, Iroro Orife, David Ifeoluwa Adelani

items.title: JevCascade: Readout Stability and Inference-Time Compute Allocation for Prefill-Only Decision Models
items.abstract: We present JevCascade, an inference-time compute allocation framework for prefill-only decision models, built on readout stability and zero-label restricted readout prediction. Prefill-only decision models score every candidate in a menu in a single forward pass and never decode, which makes one call one to two orders of magnitude cheaper than a same-scale generative language model. We show that this read-out structure carries a testable property. When an intervention changes only the menu and leaves the input text fixed, the post-intervention accuracy is already determined by the cached first-pass distribution. The restriction predictor restricts the pass-1 probabilities to the menu, renormalizes and reads off the argmax, with no labels and no second pass. Across six model families, ten core datasets (sixteen in total) and two task types, menu-only interventions are predicted to within 4.2 points, exactly for one family. The property is ordinal, not probabilistic, since a probability-level variant of the same estimator errs by 21.0 points, and class-specific, since same-scale generative models err by 1.6 to 15.8 points and degrade as they grow. It makes inference-time compute decidable before deployment. Uniform extra passes buy calibration but almost no accuracy; at matched cost a confidence cascade beats every scheme that re-asks the same model, and curating the menu beats enlarging the model, a 0.8B model on a curated 5-candidate menu reaching 95.4% on CLINC150 against 80.0% for a 4B model on the full 150-label menu.
items.authors: Ran Li, Lei Chen

items.title: Nucleus Speculative Decoding: Plausibility-Aware Verification Beyond Exact Distribution
items.abstract: Speculative decoding (SD) accelerates autoregressive generation by letting a lightweight draft model propose tokens that a target model verifies in parallel. However, its standard acceptance rule, designed for exact distribution correction, rejects tokens to which the draft assigns excess probability, even when the target finds them highly plausible: over half of the rejected tokens lie inside the target's own nucleus. Since verification dominates the cost of SD, these rejections waste its most expensive operation. We introduce Nucleus Speculative Decoding (NSD), a plausibility-aware verification rule that accepts a draft token if it passes the standard test or belongs to the target nucleus, while keeping SD's residual correction and bonus sampling unchanged. NSD requires no training or extra forward passes and is compatible with any drafting mechanism. Because it preserves SD's recovery rule, its deviation from the target distribution can be characterized exactly: we prove that the single-step total variation error equals the draft's excess probability inside the target nucleus, which is precisely NSD's gain in acceptance probability. NSD thus trades fidelity for acceptance at an exact one-to-one rate, and we further derive sequence-level fidelity bounds. Across six target models and five mathematical reasoning and code generation benchmarks, NSD achieves the highest throughput among all compared methods, with speedups of up to $5.16\times$ over autoregressive decoding and $3.15\times$ over standard SD, while improving accuracy over SD on five of the six models and nearly halving verification time per output token. Our code is available at https://github.com/EIT-NLP/Nucleus-Speculative-Decoding.
items.authors: Shuhao Li, Fanghua Ye, Wanyu Lin, Tianyu Yuan, Xiaoyu Shen

items.title: Right Number, Wrong State? Measuring Cross-Jurisdiction Substitution in LLM Recall of State Policy
items.abstract: When an LLM answers a state-specific policy question wrongly, it may be hallucinating, or it may be returning a real value that holds in another state. We test this with a minimal-set design: the question wording is fixed and only the jurisdiction varies, across the 50 U.S. states and the District of Columbia (51 jurisdictions) and three exactly defined Medicaid income-eligibility quantities. Gold values come from an official data book and agree with an independent source in 101 of 102 checked cells. Under a pre-registered protocol, Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-5.6 Sol reproducibly give another state's current value, identical across two independent repeats, for 10 and 25 of 153 items. The count depends on the reference set: crediting any wrong answer that equals another state's value yields 3-5x more reproducible substitutions than checking every number in the asked state's own records, because many apparent cross-state answers are the asked state's own values under another convention or from an earlier year. Claims about cross-jurisdiction error need a complete same-state reference set. We will release the protocol, gold table, and all model outputs.
items.authors: Jiayu Feng

items.title: AdaptEvo: Learning under Imperfect Supervision through Confidence-Adaptive Training with Knowledge Evolution
items.abstract: Rule-governed contextual decision tasks require models to apply specified rules to case-specific context and evidence. Written rules can leave gaps in decision guidance and process evaluation, while reference judgments vary in their support from the rules and evidence. To address these challenges, we introduce AdaptEvo, a framework for learning under imperfect supervision that couples confidence-adaptive policy optimization with evolving decision knowledge and evaluation rubrics. Its Training module uses Confidence-Adaptive GRPO (CA-GRPO) to balance outcome and process rewards according to reference confidence. Its Evolution module synthesizes reusable decision knowledge from recurring failures across training cases and refines process rubrics to detect overlooked errors. To support empirical evaluation, we construct an industrial multimodal content moderation dataset comprising a training set and In-Period and Out-of-Period test sets, with the latter collected under changed rules. Using Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, AdaptEvo achieves 61.9% exact-label accuracy and 72.2% binary decision accuracy on In-Period, exceeding GRPO by 7.5 and 3.7 percentage points, respectively. On Out-of-Period, the policy trained with CA-GRPO retains exact-label accuracy gains over the base model across evaluated checkpoints without injected decision knowledge, while GRPO declines with continued training. CA-GRPO also outperforms the tested fixed reward mixtures on both Out-of-Period metrics.
items.authors: Shijun Wan, Jiancong Xie, Hang Xu, Jin Duan, Qixiong Wang, Xi Xiang, Maofei Que, Yahui Liu, Zhongyu Wei, Mu Chuan

items.title: SAIL: Scientific Agentic Intelligence via a Science-Aware Loop
items.abstract: We introduce SAIL, an open model with 35B total and 3B active parameters for literature research, scientific coding, and multi-step research workflows. SAIL is developed through a science-aware improvement loop: agents built on frontier AI models analyze its task failures and construct training tasks that address the underlying capability gaps. The diagnosis examines search and evidence selection in literature tasks, scientific assumptions and reasoning in coding, and planning and revision in longer investigations. The agents draw on paper collections and scientific code repositories to build problems, interaction trajectories, and executable tasks with the required environments and tools. We repeat this loop over multiple development cycles and train SAIL through supervised fine-tuning, specialist training, multi-teacher on-policy distillation, and agentic reinforcement learning. SAIL achieves competitive performance across scientific research tasks with substantially fewer parameters than leading open-weight models.
items.authors: SAIL Model Team, Boyuan Sun, Bryan Dai, Che Liu, Chi Liu, Derek Li, Hongming Piao, Mengzhuo Chen, Xidong Wang, Yan Shu, Yinda Chen, Ziyang Zeng

items.title: HarnessSQL: Harness-Native Training for SQL Agents in Realistic Database Environments
items.abstract: Text-to-SQL models are commonly trained to map questions directly to static queries, whereas real-world database agents operate through stateful, multi-turn interaction with live databases -- inspecting schemas, executing probe queries, diagnosing errors, and revising hypotheses. This creates a critical train-deploy mismatch, as the execution harness that mediates this interaction is introduced only at inference time. To bridge this gap, we propose HarnessSQL, a harness-native post-training framework that preserves the full interaction structure throughout both supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. HarnessSQL builds isolated, executable database environments paired with hidden execution oracles, rolls out teachers directly inside the target SQL harness, and retains only verified trajectories for full-sequence SFT, followed by execution-reward RL. Across Spider 2.0-SQLite, HarnessSQL dramatically boosts the execution accuracy of compact models, raising Qwen3-8B from 15.5% to 45.2% and Qwen3-14B from 22.2% to 54.8%, while transferring effectively to out-of-distribution interactive benchmarks such as BIRD-Interact and LiveSQLBench. Our findings demonstrate that training database agents directly within their execution harness is essential for mastering complex, long-horizon database workflows.
items.authors: Haolin Yang, Jipeng Zhang, Zhiqiang Qian, Jian Xie, Shuaishuai Gong, Sirui Han, Yike Guo

items.title: Latent Core Tokenizer: Compress, but Meaningfully
items.abstract: Tokenizers are commonly optimized for compression, but a compact vocabulary does not necessarily distribute its capacity evenly across languages. We introduce the Latent Core Tokenizer (LCT), a language-agnostic approach that separates structural discovery from vocabulary construction. LCT uses Minimum Description Length, entropy-based boundary signals, and morphotactic constraints to identify reusable linguistic units before constructing a shared vocabulary. Across 104 languages with a 200K-token vocabulary, LCT achieves lower fertility and higher MorphScore than BPE, Unigram, and parity-aware BPE, while maintaining comparable cross-lingual disparity in tokenization cost. Across four multilingual downstream benchmarks, LCT improves aggregate score by 1.48, 1.83, and 2.00 points over BPE, Unigram, and parity-aware BPE, respectively. Our findings show that compression alone does not predict representation quality and highlight the importance of morphology-driven structural discovery and how frequency is used to allocate the final vocabulary across languages.
items.authors: Felermino D. M. A. Ali, Millicent Ochieng, Ogbemi Ekwejunor-Etchie, Ade Famoti, Jacki O'Neill, Debjit Paul

items.title: Verifiable Retrieval for Legal Reasoning through Structure-driven Knowledge Graph
items.abstract: Any automation within reliability-critical contexts such as medicine or law has to be transparent and verifiable. Despite their advantages, current LLM-based systems do not meet these requirements due to their inherent black-box nature. Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) attempts to ground the generative process in the relevant interpretable documents, thereby reducing the risk of AI 'hallucinations' and potentially enabling verification of the initial generation context. However, as the number and size of potential sources increases, naive retrieval approaches tend to perform worse, ignoring critical context elements. In this paper we aim to tackle this problem in the context of German Legal Code. Using structure-driven parsing to create a Knowledge Graph (KG) for the source document navigation and retrieval, we compare several KG-informed chunking and retrieval strategies and evaluate their effect on the accuracy of retrieved citations.
items.authors: Ibrahim Siddig, Sviatoslav Tugeev, Munir Georges

items.title: Media Slant is Contagious
items.abstract: This paper examines the diffusion of media slant. We document the influence of Fox News Channel (FNC) on the partisan slant of local newspapers in the U.S. over the years 1995-2008. We measure the political slant of local newspapers by scaling the news article texts to Republicans' and Democrats' speeches in Congress. Using channel positioning as an instrument for viewership, we find that higher FNC viewership causes local newspapers to adopt more right-wing slant. The effect emerges gradually, only several years after FNC's introduction, mirroring the channel's growing influence on voting behaviour. A main driver of the shift in newspaper slant appears to be a change in local political preferences.
items.authors: Philine Widmer, Cl\'ementine Abed Meraim, Sergio Galletta, Elliott Ash

items.title: AEIOU: A Unified Defense Framework against NSFW Prompts in Text-to-Image Models
items.abstract: As text-to-image (T2I) models advance and gain widespread adoption, their associated safety concerns are becoming increasingly critical. Malicious users exploit these models to generate Not-Safe-for-Work (NSFW) images using harmful or adversarial prompts, underscoring the need for effective safeguards to ensure the integrity and compliance of model outputs. However, existing detection methods often exhibit low accuracy and inefficiency. In this paper, we propose AEIOU, a defense framework that is adaptable, efficient, interpretable, optimizable, and unified against NSFW prompts in T2I models. AEIOU extracts NSFW features from the hidden states of the model's text encoder, utilizing the separable nature of these features to detect NSFW prompts. The detection process is efficient, requiring minimal inference time. AEIOU also offers real-time interpretation of results and supports optimization through data augmentation techniques. The framework is versatile, accommodating various T2I architectures. Our extensive experiments show that AEIOU significantly outperforms both commercial and open-source moderation tools, achieving over 95\% accuracy across all datasets and improving efficiency by at least tenfold. It effectively counters adaptive attacks and excels in few-shot and multi-label scenarios.
items.authors: Yiming Wang, Jiahao Chen, Qingming Li, Tong Zhang, Rui Zeng, Xing Yang, Shouling Ji

items.title: Stability Regimes for Framing-Sensitive Fine-Tuning in Language Models
items.abstract: AI systems increasingly shape how individuals access and evaluate information, intensifying concerns about misinformation. Computational simulation offers a controlled complement to direct empirical study, with fine-tuned LLMs enabling powerful agent-based simulations. However, fine-tuning often induces broad behavioral shifts including bias drift, degenerate heuristics, and changes in baseline task behavior, which undermine experimental validity. The central challenge is inducing localized decision shifts while preserving the model's aggregate behavior outside the targeted intervention. We study this through a stability analysis of supervised fine-tuning, attenuating loss on selected training slices to shift false-claim acceptance. We introduce FrameRef, a large-scale dataset of semantically equivalent claims with controlled surface framings across five dimensions (Authoritative, Consensus, Emotional, Sensationalist, Prestige), with human validation confirming systematic framing effects on claim acceptance. We present a methodology for identifying model-specific stability regimes in which targeted error shifts can be induced while preserving aggregate accuracy and calibration, and demonstrate its application to selected language models. A sequential exposure task over FrameRef shows that small framing-conditioned shifts compound into substantially different cumulative outcomes under feedback, but largely disappear when feedback is removed, confirming that interventions modify specific decision tendencies rather than global performance. We release code, LoRA adapters, and data at https://github.com/infosenselab/framing-sensitive-ft.
items.authors: Victor De Lima, Jiqun Liu, Grace Hui Yang

items.title: Frequency-Ordered Tokenization for Better Text Compression
items.abstract: We present frequency-ordered tokenization (FOT), a simple preprocessing technique that improves lossless text compression by exploiting the power-law frequency distribution of natural language (Zipf's law). FOT segments text into the vocabulary of a pretrained Byte Pair Encoding (BPE) tokenizer, renumbers tokens by frequency with a fixed table, and writes them with a short byte code before any standard compressor. Because the FOT stream is less than half the size of the text, compressors produce smaller output and run faster at the same time. On enwik8 (100 MB of Wikipedia), FOT reduces the compressed size by 7.96 percentage points (pp) for zlib, 2.24 pp for xz (LZMA), 1.96 pp for brotli and 1.44 pp for zstd, while making total compression, including the transform, 1.6x, 3.2x, 1.8x and 5.0x faster. Gains hold from 100 KB to 1 GB (enwik9) and across texts of diverse languages, and outperform the classical Word Replacing Transform. On enwik9, FOT with tuned xz sets a new state of the art among LZ-based compressors on the Large Text Compression Benchmark. The method can be implemented in under 50 lines of code.
items.authors: Maximilian Kalcher

items.title: Lost in Adaptation: Layer-Selective Recovery of Temporal Reasoning in Video-Language Models
items.abstract: Multimodal adaptation can weaken temporal reasoning (TR) in video-language models (VLMs) even when the visual evidence needed for an answer is correctly perceived. This weakened competence, however, remains partly recoverable from the model's paired pre-adaptation language checkpoint. We introduce MERIT, a gradient-free framework that selectively restores this competence across the language backbone while protecting temporal perception (TP). It assigns each self-attention layer a VLM-dominant or LLM-dominant interpolation and uses the Covariance Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy (CMA-ES) to search the recipe space under a perception-constrained objective. Across three VLM families and five video benchmarks, MERIT improves reasoning-aligned performance in all 15 model--benchmark evaluations while preserving TP across all three Video-MME settings. Recipes selected using 232 diagnostic examples transfer to four unseen benchmarks, with relative gains up to 27.8%, and outperform full-backbone, uniform-attention, and alpha-tuned random-layer merging. Interventional masking shows that MERIT-selected layers are disproportionately important for TR, while frame-level attribution reveals increased reliance on temporally distributed, causally relevant evidence. These results show that adaptation-induced reasoning degradation can be repaired post hoc through selective reuse of pre-adaptation competence, without learning new parameters or adding inference overhead.
items.authors: Zihang Fu, Haonan Wang, Jian Kang, Kenji Kawaguchi, Jiaying Wu

items.title: Navigating the Conceptual Multiverse
items.abstract: When language models answer open-ended questions, they implicitly make decisions that shape their answers. However, the models do not show these decisions to the user, so users cannot contextualize answers: they cannot see the assumptions an answer rests on or the alternatives to it. Drawing on multiverse analysis from statistics, we introduce the conceptual multiverse, a representation in which language models express answers as the result of intermediate conceptual decisions. We build a system that generates such decisions explicitly, organizes them into a space of answers that users can see and change, and checks them against the norms of a specific domain. In a user study across three domains - philosophy, AI alignment annotation, and poetry - participants say that our system helps them see the decisions leading to an answer, explore the space of answers, and understand the decisions structuring this space.
items.authors: Andre Ye, Jenny Y. Huang, Alicia Guo, Rose Novick, Tamara Broderick, Mitchell L. Gordon

items.title: EARS: Explanatory Abstention for Reliable Sub-Agent Modeling in Large-scale Multi-Agent Systems
items.abstract: In large-scale enterprise settings, centralized multi-agent systems (MAS) are increasingly adopted, in which a coordinator delegates user requests to lightweight, domain-specialized sub-agents. While this architecture improves modularity, scalability, and cost efficiency, its reliability depends not only on accurate routing but also on sub-agents' ability to calibrate their responses to capability constraints. In particular, sub-agents built on smaller fine-tuned models often struggle with such calibration, leading them to over-answer ambiguous, underspecified, misrouted, or unsupported requests and produce hallucinated outputs instead of actionable feedback. To address this challenge, we present EARS (Explanatory Abstention for Reliable Sub-Agent Modeling), a production-oriented framework that reframes sub-agent abstention as an inter-agent communication protocol: a sub-agent does not merely abstain, but exposes an actionable failure state to the coordinator. EARS curates human-agent interaction data using an ensemble of calibrated LLM-as-a-Judge models, producing structured abstention labels and rationales under a taxonomy of sub-agent failure modes. These data are used to fine-tune sub-agents to detect failure conditions and return rationales for coordinator-level clarification, rerouting, or fallback. We evaluate EARS in a large-scale production e-commerce assistant supporting enterprise business intelligence workflows. EARS improves the overall response pass rate from 68.5% to 78.9%, demonstrating that sub-agent-side explanatory abstention improves MAS reliability.
items.authors: Shuang Xie, Yunan Lu, Han Li, Lingyun Wang

items.title: DELTA-TTS: Adapting Autoregressive Model into Diffusion Language Model for Text-to-Speech
items.abstract: Autoregressive (AR) text-to-speech (TTS) models generate discrete speech tokens sequentially, which makes inference slow and can degrade robustness, since local errors propagate to later positions and can escalate into hallucination. This limitation stems from their left-to-right AR commitment: each token must be determined before future speech-token context is available. However, such ordering is not an inherent requirement for TTS, since the model receives the full input text before synthesis. In this paper, we introduce DELTA-TTS, a lightweight LoRA-based adaptation framework that converts a pretrained AR TTS model into a discrete diffusion language model (dLLM) for confidence-ordered speech-token decoding. To better capture the local structure of speech, DELTA-TTS incorporates a convolution module that injects local acoustic context, together with a 1/t-weighted training objective and a time-shifted inference schedule that together defer low-confidence positions to later steps. Trained on only 585 hours of LibriTTS, DELTA-TTS achieves a 1.75% WER on Seed-TTS test-en, outperforming its AR backbone while generating tokens 3.3 times faster. Further analysis shows that DELTA-TTS produces sharper text-speech alignment, increases overall decoding confidence, and mitigates the hallucinations observed in AR generation. Audio samples, inference code, and model weights are available at https://slpr-lab.github.io/DELTA-TTS.
items.authors: Junwon Moon, Yejin Lee, Seungbeom Kim, Hoseong Ahn, Sewoong Park, Heeseung Kim, Kyuhong Shim

items.title: Preserving Structure, Strengthening Signals: A Grammar-Driven Approach to Optimize the Trade-off Between Quality and Detectability in Code Watermarking
items.abstract: Text watermarking has emerged as a crucial technique for identifying AI-generated content. However, current watermarking schemes entail a trade-off between text quality and watermark detectability, which is further intensified by the inherent low-entropy nature of code. To mitigate this dilemma, we propose Grammar-Driven Watermark (GDW), a training-free watermarking approach tailored to LLM-based code generation. GDW employs a three-level masking mechanism consisting of a green-list mask, a syntactic validity mask, and a structural role mask to regulate watermark injection. These masks are integrated through hierarchical modulation, which limits the scope of watermark injection to syntactically admissible green-list tokens and adjusts watermark strength based on structural roles through a role function. Accordingly, we design a role-aware weighted detection statistic. For comprehensive evaluation, we introduce the Area Under the Trade-off Curve (AUTC), a metric that quantifies the quality-detectability trade-off. Extensive experiments demonstrate that GDW outperforms existing baselines and achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) trade-off performance, while maintaining superior performance under seven semantics-preserving attacks.
items.authors: Licheng Yu, Aiwei Liu, Songze Li

items.title: A Situational Speech Synthesizer for Yoruba: System Design, Phonological Rule Architecture, and Orthographic Extensions for Contour
items.abstract: We present TTSYoruba, a rule-based concatenative diphone speech synthesizer for Yoruba, deployed at online as part of the YorubaName.com open dictionary of Yoruba personal names. The system takes tone-marked Yoruba text as input and produces audio output by applying a hand-crafted phonological rule system to a recorded inventory of 651 diphone units spanning five tonal variants of every consonant-vowel combination in the language. We describe the phonological architecture of the system in detail, including our complete tonal file-selection logic, our treatment of the three-way nasal disambiguation problem (oral /n/, nasalized vowel, and syllabic nasal), and the derivation of contextual rising and falling tones from level-tone input. We also present, as an orthographic contribution, the adoption of the caron and circumflex, which are symbols with prior standing in Yoruba phonological transcription, as standard single-vowel contour tone markers, integrated into the TTS normalization pipeline and the WriteYoruba keyboard input tool. The system's performance was evaluated through a listener study (N=50), with detailed results on Mean Opinion Scores (MOS) presented in Section 6. Keywords: Yoruba, text-to-speech, low-resource languages, diphone synthesis, contour tones, African language NLP, rule-based synthesis
items.authors: Kola Tubosun, Adedayo Oluokun, Hafiz Adewuyi, Dadepo Aderemi

items.title: GEB-Bench: Abstract Structures Told in Many Voices
items.abstract: Analogy allows models to apply relational knowledge from one situation to another. Benchmarks of equivalent representations test different ways of expressing the same underlying problem, whereas analogy often links situations involving different objects and content. To evaluate the analogy ability of models, we introduce GEB-Bench, a benchmark centered on cross-voice motif matching. A voice presents a motif as a scene, story, mathematical statement, or programmatic skeleton. The first task is identification across these voices. The second is matching scenes to stories or mathematical statements, and stories to mathematical statements, by their shared motif. A complete construction pipeline generates items in these voices from the relation specified for each motif, checks the order and repetition of story units, and assembles paired questions. We evaluate current models on our benchmark. Results show that matching performance depends on the target voice. The paired scene-to-story study reveals that (1) evaluated models still make matching errors when they separately identify the source and every candidate correctly, and (2) identification improves more consistently than scene-to-story matching across the evaluated Qwen model sizes. These findings show that successful motif identification does not ensure reliable matching across voices.
items.authors: Tong Zhang, Zhiyuan Shi, Yun Peng, Tao Xie

items.title: LoopVL: Recurrent Visual Intelligence
items.abstract: We introduce LoopVL to study whether Loop Transformers can be effectively extended to vision- language models. LoopVL combines Module-Loop and Model-Loop computation to iteratively update a unified vision-language state through shared modules. We train LoopVL from scratch through language pre-training, multimodal training, and post-training. LoopVL outperforms a range of similarly sized and larger non-recurrent models on multimodal understanding and visual reasoning benchmarks. We also observe Visual Aha Moments in LoopVL, characterized by pronounced shifts in visual attention across loops. LoopVL provides practical evidence for recurrent vision-language modeling and offers an intuitive perspective on how shared parameters can support deeper multimodal computation over continuously evolving visual-language states.
items.authors: Zhe Qian, Ziyang Gong, Zhongxing Xu, Hehan Li, Zhonghua Wang, Hanmeng Liu, Liwei Qian, Xin Pei, Peizhi Xu, Fei Luo, Mingxuan Wang, Xue Yang, Shiwei liu, Yanbiao Ma, Junchi Yan, Jungong Han

items.title: Decision-Oriented Recommendation Reranking: An Empirical Study of Its Promise and Limitations
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown promise for recommendation reranking, but their use introduces an important trade-off between recommendation quality and serving efficiency. We investigate whether decision-oriented systems provide a useful alternative when the reranking task is fundamentally a structured choice among predefined candidate items. Specifically, we conduct a controlled empirical study of two decision-oriented systems, TypeSafe Jev and OpenAI Decisions, for recommendation reranking. Across three Amazon Reviews domains and four candidate-set sizes, we compare these systems against recommendation-specific models and pointwise and listwise LLM-based rerankers, systematically evaluating recommendation effectiveness, candidate-order robustness, and efficiency and scalability. Our results reveal that Jev frequently achieves a favorable quality--latency trade-off, offering competitive recommendation effectiveness at substantially lower observed latency than stronger LLM-based alternatives. Overall, our findings suggest that specialization for decision-making does not inherently guarantee superior recommendation quality or robustness. Instead, the practical value of decision-oriented inference depends on implementation-specific characteristics and application requirements. These findings motivate further investigation of decision-oriented systems for recommendation and other ranking tasks with structured output spaces.
items.authors: Hanjia Lyu, Yinglong Xia

items.title: Intelligence as Useful Structure: A Thermodynamic Perspective
items.abstract: Thermodynamic accounts of intelligence have advanced rapidly, but they do not yet resolve a prior definitional problem: what makes internal structure intelligent rather than merely ordered? This paper argues that any thermodynamic intelligence metric should include a usefulness filter. The numerator must track internal structure that is relevant to viability, prediction, and control, not merely raw information or benchmark score. Intelligence is therefore defined as the resource-bounded capacity of an adaptive system to acquire, compress, and deploy useful internal structure so as to improve prediction, control, and robustness across a range of environments. Capability and efficiency are separated. Capability is adaptive reach, A, defined over a reference distribution of environments or task families. Efficiency is acquisition efficiency, I_eff = Delta C_u / W_diss, where C_u denotes useful internal structure and W_diss physically dissipated work. Concretely, C_u is the predictive and control-relevant information that a system's internal state carries about viability-relevant environmental structure, making it a semantic rather than purely syntactic information term. I_eff is a learning or adaptation metric, not a complete scalar measure of deployed intelligence: trained systems at steady state may have Delta C_u = 0 while still exhibiting high adaptive reach. A toy numerical example with exact Landauer-referenced dissipation costs, explicit boundary conditions, temperature-normalised reporting conventions, and falsifiable comparisons against size-based and energy-only baselines are provided.
items.authors: Boris Djordjevic

items.title: Autocatalytic order controls bistability in a conservative kinetic model of relational event progression
items.abstract: This version supersedes earlier versions and develops the three-class model of v1 into a closed, conserved network. On a relational view, the Universe is the happening of events rather than a container for them. A kinetic model gives this dynamical form: events are sorted as future, now or past; future events combine reversibly into now events; a now event meeting past events is activated and completes irreversibly into past events, which are renewed for future use. Past events thus catalyse their own production in a closed network conserving a weighted event count. We give a complete mass-action and bifurcation analysis. Conservation fixes the stoichiometry uniquely. When one past event participates in each activation, progression ignites softly at a transcritical threshold and no fold can arise, for every completion yield. When two participate cooperatively, the progressing branch folds: a past-rich attractor coexists with a past-poor state and ignition needs a finite perturbation. Cooperative order creates memory; nonequilibrium asymmetry only sets how hard it is to undo, strict one-way latching being a singular limit of hysteresis. In a partially reversible network where only renewal is reversible, two stable interior states coexist while activation and completion stay strictly one-way. The work is theoretical and does not derive time or its arrow: relational ordering and local irreversibility are assumed. As stated postulates, events are parcels of energy, the budget is conserved energy, and the activated class is the activated complex of transition-state theory. Around each cycle both the budget and the event number are conserved; at steady state the composition is stationary while energy is concentrated and dispersed locally, and whether entropy production vanishes globally is posed as a hypothesis.
items.authors: Bruce M Boman

items.title: Optical and magnetic penetration depths under a modified electromagnetic coupling in charged bosonic condensates
items.abstract: We establish the relation between optical condensate spectral weight and static magnetic screening in a proposed effective theory of charged bosonic condensates with an additional diamagnetic coupling. Starting from an explicit Ginzburg--Landau functional, we derive both the London equation and the transverse low-frequency conductivity. At fixed condensate parameter $q^2n_s/m^\ast$, the modified coupling doubles the inverse-square magnetic screening length and the optical condensate weight, giving $\lambda_{\rm mag}=\lambda_{\rm stiff}=\lambda_L/\sqrt{2}$, where $\lambda_L^{-2}=\mu_0q^2n_s/m^\ast$. Their ratio is therefore unity in both the standard and modified local theories: it tests consistency between measurement methods but cannot distinguish the couplings. A structured comparison of published results for Nb, Pb, YBCO, MgB$_2$, and Ba(Fe,Co)$_2$As$_2$ identifies the roles of sample matching, absolute calibration, nonlocality, and spectral-weight extraction. We formulate the requirements for a discriminating absolute-response experiment and discuss a complementary single-particle spectral prediction. The analysis separates experimentally accessible consistency checks from tests requiring independent information about condensate parameters or a different observable.
items.authors: F. Minotti, G. Modanese

items.title: Cluster Ages to Reconstruct the Milky Way Assembly (CARMA). VI. The age-metallicity relation of in-situ clusters and the age of the Universe
items.abstract: Within the homogeneous framework for the derivation of GC ages defined by the CARMA collaboration, we focus on the clusters born in-situ in the MW. As they are the oldest among the old GCs, their absolute age provides constraints about the age of the Universe. Moreover, the shape of their AMR is expected to show the imprints of past merger events, in case these were able to trigger GC formation in the Galaxy. We derive new homogeneous ages for 18 GCs dynamically and/or chemically classified as in-situ, and build the MW AMR from a total sample of 34 GCs. We find that all the selected GCs follow a well defined AMR, with the exception of NGC6642 and Pal1. While the former is likely a member of the LKH merger event, thus putting chronological evidence for the existence of this progenitor on even more robust ground, for the latter we propose an alternative scenario according to which it formed in-situ, but in a metal-depleted region of the Galaxy, possibly due to the interaction with an unspecified merger event. To find evidence of merger-driven GC formation, we use a GMM for the observed age distribution. This is statistically best-fit by 4 components, which we associate with significant events of the MW merger history. Cluster ages were finally calibrated to a more accurate absolute age scale based on asteroseismic measurements of the mass of red giant stars in NGC6791, and the resulting AMR was fit to compute the look-back time for the beginning of cluster formation in the MW. The fit yields t_GC,i=13.59+0.33-0.32 Gyr for initial cluster formation, and tU=13.79+/-0.34 Gyr for the age of the Universe. This value translates to H0=68.72+3.95-3.49(stat.)+2.65-2.32(sys.) km s-1 Mpc-1, where the systematic error comes from a realistic estimate of the zero point uncertainty on the GC absolute ages derived from stellar models.

items.title: A first view of interstellar Fe-bearing dust grains with XRISM
items.abstract: Understanding the reservoirs of iron (Fe) in our Galaxy is crucial for probing the mechanisms that drive dust grain growth in the interstellar medium (ISM). High-resolution X-ray absorption spectroscopy offers a powerful tool to investigate the chemistry of dust grains, particularly those containing Fe, through spectroscopic features near photoabsorption edges known as X-ray Absorption Fine Structures (XAFS). With the Resolve spectrometer aboard XRISM, we can now examine the Fe K-edge (7.1 keV) owing to its improved spectral resolution in this energy range. This enabled us to probe the dust grain chemistry in high Galactic column densities. In this work, we present a pilot study on dust grain chemistry through the Fe K-edge of the XRISM Performance Verification target GX 340+0. This source is a persistently bright low-mass X-ray binary with a hydrogen column density of 6.6x10^22 cm^-2 along the line of sight, providing sufficient optical depth at the Fe K-edge. By fitting combined dust and gas models, we find that Fe is depleted by 95% into dust along the line of sight towards the source. Moreover, we find evidence that 38% of the solid-phase Fe is in metallic iron, 47% in iron sulfides, and the remainder in silicates. The large contribution from metallic iron and iron sulfides differs from what is typically inferred from X-ray studies of diffuse ISM and may suggest that that these compounds become more significant reservoirs of Fe in higher column density Galactic sightlines.

items.title: Searching for Nearby Supermassive Black Hole Binaries with GRAVITY
items.abstract: We present a systematic interferometric search for close supermassive black hole (SMBH) binaries in 20 nearby type 1 active galactic nuclei (AGN) observed with VLTI/\grav. We investigate parsec-scale asymmetric emission by modeling the squared visibilities and closure phases with a single circular Gaussian component plus a background point source for the central AGN, and searching for additional compact companions through grid-based binary models. The robustness of the search is validated using injection-recovery simulations and point-spread-function diagnostics. Several features are identified in the initial significance maps, but only one candidate out of 20 shows a persistent compact asymmetry, corresponding to an observed incidence of $5\%$. If NGC~3783 is interpreted as a binary AGN, we derive a Poissonian one-sided $1\sigma$ upper limit of $f_{\rm bin}<16.5\%$ for GRAVITY-detectable binaries among bright nearby AGN (K<12.5) at separations of $\sim1$-$100$~pc. Conversely, if the observed asymmetry in NGC~3783 is associated with asymmetric circumnuclear dust emission, the corresponding upper limit on the binary fraction is $f_{\rm bin}<9.2\%$. We compare these results with predictions from the Horizon-AGN simulation, finding comparable binary fractions. We also noted that the expected fraction strongly depends on the assumed distribution of individual SMBH accretion rates within binaries, which is currently unresolved in cosmological models. Our results demonstrate the potential of infrared interferometry to identify parsec-scale binary AGN candidates and motivate future GRAVITY+ observations to expand the sample and follow up known candidates, helping to confirm their nature and distinguish genuine binaries from asymmetric nuclear structures.

items.title: Stellar discs and intermediate-mass black holes in galactic nuclei II. Fragmenting the disc and forming the S-stars in a live nuclear star cluster
items.abstract: We present direct $N$-body simulations of a stellar disc around the supermassive black hole Sgr~A*, perturbed by an intermediate-mass black hole (IMBH) and embedded in a live nuclear star cluster. A retrograde IMBH with $m_\bullet=2000\,M_\odot$, relative inclination $\theta_\bullet=150^\circ$, and initial semi-major axis $a_\bullet=0.15$~pc breaks the disc into three disc-like components and an angular momentum filament. The stochastic torques of the cluster, together with the IMBH's inward migration, increase the angular separation between these substructures. By ${\sim}5$~Myr, their separations become comparable to those among the observed Galactic-centre young star structures. The innermost ($a\le0.04$~pc) disc stars evolve into an S-star-like population. Relaxation driven by the cluster disperses their orbital planes, excites their eccentricities and depletes the `zone of avoidance' within ${\sim}10$~Myr even without an IMBH. The IMBH further accelerates their orbital-plane reorientation. However, the most eccentric S-stars may require an additional formation channel, such as the Hills mechanism. The distinctive signatures of the IMBH are the well-separated disc components and the eccentricity excitation confined to the radial range swept by its orbit. Dynamical friction from the cluster reduces the orbital size of a $2000\,M_\odot$ IMBH initially at $0.15$~pc by more than a factor of two within $10$~Myr. Prograde IMBHs tend to align with the stellar disc, whereas a $2000\,M_\odot$ retrograde IMBH can anti-align with the radially overlapping disc stars. We also quantify how the IMBH affects the supply of stars to the loss cone and the rates of stellar tidal disruptions and binary separations.
items.authors: Taras Panamarev, Bence Kocsis

items.title: Globular cluster Observations for Luminosity-dispersion Distances (GOLD): Project description and velocity catalogue
items.abstract: We introduce and describe the Globular cluster Observations for Luminosity-Dispersion distances (GOLD) project, which has the principal aim of determining independent distances based on the globular cluster (GC) absolute magnitude-velocity dispersion ($M_V - \sigma$) relation calibrated with Milky Way GCs with Gaia distances. The project comprises observations of GCs in 19 early- and late-type galaxies taken with FLAMES/GIRAFFE on ESO's Very Large Telescope. So far, 17 galaxies have been observed. The spectra cover the wavelength range 8483-9000 AA, including the calcium triplet region at a spectral resolution of $R\sim18,000$. The spectra provide line-of-sight velocities with typical uncertainties of $\Delta v = 1-2$ km s$^{-1}$. Using primarily velocities to separate extragalactic sources from foreground stars, we present here our initial sample of 1062 GCs and 101 ultra-compact dwarf galaxies (UCDs). For more than 650 of these objects we present the first velocity measurement. We discuss the available photometry and size measurements, and show that our velocities are in good agreement with previous studies. Our velocity catalogues are made publicly available. Beyond the principal aim of obtaining precision distances, additional science to be explored with these data includes host galaxy halo dynamics and clustering analysis, mass-to light ratios of GCs and UCDs in the sample, the stellar initial mass function and black hole occupation fraction of the GCs, and chemical abundances from high-dispersion spectra.

items.title: Beyond the Damped Random Walk: Multiband AGN Variability from SDSS to Rubin LSST
items.abstract: The flux variability of Active Galactic Nuclei (AGNs) is commonly modeled using the damped random walk (DRW), but increasingly rich multiband time-domain surveys motivate more flexible stochastic models that characterize variability beyond a single timescale and exploit dependence across bands. Multivariate continuous-time autoregressive moving average (MCARMA) processes extend the multivariate DRW to higher-order stochastic dynamics and provide a matrix-valued power spectral density for characterizing marginal variability and cross-band dependence. In a carefully selected Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) Stripe~82 sample, higher-order models are selected for 109 of 134 AGNs (81.3\%), with substantial rather than marginal support in most objects; convergence diagnostics indicate that this fraction is conservative. The fitted models also reveal strong cross-band dependence that generally decreases with wavelength separation. Motivated by this richer structure, we investigate its recoverability under Vera C. Rubin Observatory Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) observing conditions. Model-order recovery depends strongly on the underlying stochastic behavior as well as source brightness and observing cadence. Recovery is high across many of the simulated settings, but deteriorates when the characteristic features of higher-order variability become difficult to distinguish from the multivariate DRW. Additional simulations show that this loss of distinguishability can persist over a range of underlying variability behaviors. These results show that stochastic structure beyond the multivariate DRW is prevalent in our selected SDSS sample, while its recoverability with LSST depends on both observational conditions and the form of the underlying stochastic variability. The methodology is implemented in the Python package mcarma.
items.authors: Izak Schmidlkofer, Zhirui Hu, Weixiang Yu, Hyungsuk Tak

items.title: Multiphase Analysis of (U)LIRG Nuclear Activity (MAUNA). I. Spatially Resolved Optical Emission-Line Diagnostics
items.abstract: We present resolved optical integral-field spectroscopy of the 32 luminous and ultraluminous infrared galaxy systems of the Multiphase Analysis of (U)LIRG Nuclear Activity (MAUNA) sample, drawn from the GOALS survey and selected to have JWST/MIRI medium-resolution spectrometer (MRS) observations. The data set combines new Keck/KCWI observations of 10 systems with archival VLT/MUSE cubes for 22 systems, covering H$\beta$ to [S II] at ~1 arcsecond spatial resolution (~0.9 kpc at the sample median distance). Using the optical [N II]/H$\alpha$ BPT diagram, we find that composite and LINER-like excitation together account for most of the classified area (median fractions 0.44 and 0.26), while Seyfert-like gas covers a median fraction of 0.02 but carries a far larger proportion of the line luminosity where it is present. Both the projected size of the Seyfert-classified region, $R_{\rm Sy}=0.08$-$7.5$ kpc, and its [O III] luminosity increase with the bolometric AGN luminosity, with $R_{\rm Sy}\propto L_{\rm AGN,bol}^{0.54\pm0.18}$, as expected for gas photoionized at a constant ionization parameter. The scatter about the luminosity relation depends on dust opacity: the [O III] luminosity per unit AGN luminosity falls by $1.09\pm0.25$ dex per unit depth of the 9.7 $\mu$m silicate absorption feature (Spearman $\rho=-0.60$, $p=0.001$). Optical excitation diagnostics therefore locate AGN-excited gas reliably but systematically underestimate the luminosity the AGN supplies to the host in the most obscured (U)LIRGs.

items.title: The Galactic disk structure revealed by Gaia XP spectra
items.abstract: The spatial structures of chemical populations constrain Galactic disk evolution and its underlying physical processes. Gaia XP spectra provide one of the largest spectroscopic samples available. We use Gaia XP spectra to study Galactic disk mono-abundance populations (MAPs), measuring their scale heights as a function of radius and radial surface-mass-density profiles. We construct a red giant branch (RGB) sample and divide it into MAPs according to $[\alpha/{\rm M}]$ and $[{\rm M/H}]$. The sample covers a $6\times6$ kpc region centered on the Sun in the Galactic plane and extends to $|Z|<3.7$ kpc. We estimate XP completeness using a Gaia photometric parent sample and combine PARSEC isochrones with a Kroupa initial mass function (IMF) to calculate the selection function and convert observed stellar counts into intrinsic stellar mass densities. We fit vertical density profiles with an exponential model to derive scale heights and integrate the fitted profiles to obtain surface mass densities. The resulting profiles are generally consistent with those from APOGEE. All MAPs show flaring, with the high-$\alpha$ population exhibiting the strongest flaring and the metal-poor and sub-solar low-$\alpha$ populations showing the weakest. Surface-mass-density profiles differ significantly among MAPs: the high-$\alpha$ and metal-rich low-$\alpha$ populations show approximately exponential declines, whereas the other low-$\alpha$ populations exhibit plateau-like features, indicating that the Galactic disk cannot be described by a simple single-exponential profile. These differential structures suggest a complex Galactic disk assembly history likely regulated by birth conditions, secular dynamical heating, radial migration, and external perturbations.
items.authors: Zhenkang Tang, Jianhui Lian, Jialong Zhou, Jiadong Li

items.title: Photometric Identification and Dynamical Purification of Blue Horizontal Branch Stars in DESI MWS DR1
items.abstract: Blue horizontal-branch (BHB) stars are ideal tracers for mapping the structure of the Galactic stellar halo. However, traditional spectroscopic identification is limited by data quality and sample size, while broad-band photometric methods often achieve only moderate completeness and purity. Building upon the color-space BHB identification method of \citet{2025ApJS..278...62H}, we synthesize SkyMapper $(u,v,g,z)$ photometry from DESI MWS DR1 spectroscopy and identify 9,237 BHB candidates in the $(g-z)_0$--$(u-v)_0$ color space using the HDBSCAN clustering algorithm. We then construct a Kernel Density Estimation (KDE) Bayesian probability model with capture-recapture (C-R) prior to assign posterior membership probabilities, achieving a probability-weighted purity of 88.9\% and completeness of 94.2\%. Applying an escape-velocity cut based on the Galactic gravitational potential, we remove 1,461 contaminants with unphysical kinematic parameters, yielding a clean photometric BHB sample $\mathcal{S}_c$ of 7,776 stars (retention rate $R_{\rm keep} = 84.2\%$). Systematic analysis of the contaminants reveals that they are predominantly faint sources ($g\sim20$~mag) with very low signal-to-noise ratios (median SNR~$<$~5). When the BHB color--luminosity relation is incorrectly applied to these objects, their space velocities are amplified beyond the Galactic escape limit, confirming that the escape-velocity filter essentially acts as a physical detector of low-SNR--driven distance inflation.
items.authors: Shuai Zhang, Xiaolong Wang, Kai Xiao, Guozhen Hu, Wenyuan Cui, Ce Cai, Shuai Feng, Jie Ju

items.title: The NIVARIA-Local Group simulations: Unveiling the origin of rotation curve diversity in dwarf galaxies and its connection to galaxy morphology
items.abstract: Dwarf galaxies exhibit a large diversity in rotation curve shapes, challenging galaxy formation models within the $\Lambda$CDM paradigm. We present NIVARIA-LG, a new suite of cosmological simulations studying dwarf galaxy evolution in realistic Local Group environments. This intermediate-resolution pilot lays the groundwork for the full-scale NIVARIA project. The simulations combine constrained Local Group initial conditions from HESTIA with the NIHAO galaxy formation model. The simulated galaxies reproduce observed stellar-to-halo mass relations, match the Baryonic Tully-Fisher relation, and capture the distribution of stellar effective radii, including compact and diffuse galaxies. We analyse the structural and kinematic properties of isolated dwarf galaxies with $10^7 \lesssim M_\star/M_\odot \lesssim 10^{10}$, focusing on rotation curve diversity. NIVARIA-LG naturally produces a broad range of rotation curve shapes, including slowly rising systems underrepresented in previous simulations and steep rotation curves. We find that rotation curve diversity is primarily associated with gas extent and inner dark matter structure: more extended gas and shallower inner density profiles correspond to more slowly rising curves, while stellar effective radius shows little independent association. Individual galaxies show that rotation curve shapes change rapidly as gas is redistributed during assembly. Recent accretion events are also associated with more slowly rising curves in the most massive dwarfs. Together, these results suggest that rotation curve diversity is linked to the baryonic cycle, which shapes the inner dark matter distribution. The Local Group environment and its filaments influence this evolution by regulating gas accretion and redistribution, producing the observed diversity in rotation curve shapes.
items.authors: A. Contreras-Santos, A. Di Cintio, A. Negri, J. Sarrato-Al\'os, S. Cardona-Barrero, G. Garc\'ia-Bethencourt, C. Brook, N. I. Libeskind, A. Knebe, A. Macci\`o

items.title: Anisotropic Radiation in Super-Eddington Active Galactic Nuclei: The Responsivity of Broad-Line Regions to Continuum Variability
items.abstract: Anisotropic ionizing radiation is a natural theoretical expectation for super-Eddington accretion in active galactic nuclei (AGNs), implying that the ionizing flux incident on the broad-line region (BLR) clouds differs from that measured along the observer's line of sight. Reverberation mapping studies have revealed systematically shortened time lags of the broad H$\beta$ emission line relative to continuum variations in super-Eddington AGNs, a phenomenon that can be naturally interpreted as a consequence of anisotropic ionizing continuum radiation. To further investigate this anisotropy, we perform a systematic analysis of the H$\beta$ line responsivity, defined as the ratio of the variability amplitude of H$\beta$ to that of the driving continuum, for both sub- and super-Eddington AGNs. By combining the effective responsivities measured relative to the driving continuum, after correcting for the continuum--emission-line delay, with photoionization calculations, we infer the ionizing radiation field received by their BLRs. We find that, in super-Eddington AGNs, the ionizing flux inferred from the H$\beta$ responsivity differs significantly from that observed along the line of sight, whereas the two are in closer agreement in sub-Eddington AGNs. These results provide compelling evidence for strong anisotropy of the incident ionizing radiation in super-Eddington AGNs. We conclude by discussing the broader implications of this anisotropy, including its potential relevance to the "little red dots" recently discovered by the James Webb Space Telescope.
items.authors: Feng-Na Fang, Pu Du, Jian-Min Wang

items.title: Modelling the broken age-[Fe/H] relation and metallicity distribution function of mono-age populations
items.abstract: This study investigates the chemical evolution history and radial migration in the Milky Way utilizing high-precision age measurements based on large-scale stellar spectroscopic surveys. Recent observational data have revealed a distinct break in the age-metallicity relation of stars in the solar neighborhood, suggesting that stellar populations of the Milky Way can be divided into two evolutionary sequences. Based on galactic chemical evolution models, we confirm that this break in the age-metallicity relation can be explained by a recent major gas accretion event, which diluted the metallicity in the disk and triggered a starburst, leading to the formation of an independent age-metallicity sequence. To assess the impact of stellar radial migration, we incorporate a simplified treatment of this process into our multi-zone chemical evolution model. Radial migration is modeled as a probabilistic diffusion process, characterized by a Gaussian distribution. By fitting the model-predicted metallicity distribution functions (MDFs) of mono-age stellar populations to observations, we infer a migration strength of $\sigma = 2.15^{+0.100}_{-0.103}\,{\rm kpc}$ for stars with ages between 2 and 6 Gyr located at 9.5-11.5 kpc, corresponding to an average radial displacement of 1.92 kpc over 10 Gyr. This result is lower than previous estimates of stellar radial migration, suggesting that the role of radial migration in shaping the chemical structure of the Milky Way is less important than previously estimated.
items.authors: Qinhao Shao, Jianhui Lian

items.title: The Tilt of the Velocity Ellipsoid in the Milky Way Disk with GALAH-Gaia Data
items.abstract: We investigate the metallicity dependence of the tilt of the velocity ellipsoid using more than 572,000 stars selected from GALAH and Gaia. We find that the tilt angles of disk stars can be well described by the relation $\alpha = \alpha_{0}\,\mathrm{arctan}(Z/R)$, and the $\alpha_{0}$ differ significantly among different disk populations, with $\alpha_{0}$ are 0.78 $\pm$ 0.05, 0.86 $\pm$ 0.07, and 0.77 $\pm$ 0.07 for the whole sample, the Low-[$\alpha$/Fe] and the High-[$\alpha$/Fe] populations, respectively. These results indicate that Galactic disk populations are globally tilted toward cylindrical alignment, implying that the gravitational potential of the Galactic baryonic disk plays a dominant role in shaping the kinematics of dynamically relaxed stars. Our detailed analysis further reveals a metallicity dependence of $\alpha_{0}$ for various populations, with the Low-[$\alpha$/Fe] and the High-[$\alpha$/Fe] populations are respectively $\alpha_{0}$ = 0.12 $\mathrm{sin}$(3.72 [Fe/H] + 1.09) + 0.75 and $\alpha_{0}$ = 0.20 $\mathrm{sin}$(2.99 [Fe/H] + 1.90) + 0.71. These results indicate that the metallicity dependence observed in the Low-[$\alpha$/Fe] population may be primarily associated with resonances induced by the Galactic bar, while the behavior of the High-[$\alpha$/Fe] population may also have been affected by additional dynamical and evolutionary processes, such as violent heating associated with mergers, accretion, and/or the formation of these stars in an environment shaped by mergers of gas-rich systems and/or a turbulent ISM.
items.authors: Zhenzhen He, Ruilan Yang, Hui Li, Weixiang Sun

items.title: The DAWN JWST Archive: A spectroscopically-informed population study of the physical properties of galaxies at z>2
items.abstract: Charting the evolution of star-formation, stellar mass and dust build-up over cosmic time relies on the accurate characterisation of the stellar population properties of high redshift galaxies. We present a catalogue of spectroscopically derived physical properties for ~12,000 galaxies at z>2, with archival JWST/NIRSpec PRISM spectroscopy and JWST/NIRCam imaging from the DAWN JWST Archive. We present a custom version of the SED fitting code BAGPIPES, used to perform joint spectrophotometric modelling of PRISM spectra and broadband NIRCam photometry. In doing so, we publicly release a science-ready catalogue of the physical properties of galaxies beyond cosmic noon. We report key physical properties, such as stellar masses, star-formation rates (SFR) and timescales, and V-band dust attenuation (Av). We further probe the recent star-formation histories (SFH) of galaxies via their SFRs on 3 Myr, 10 Myr, and 100 Myr timescales, capturing both rising and falling recent SFHs. Through dust-corrected ugi colour-colour diagrams of massive galaxies, we show how quiescent and dusty galaxies populate this colour space at z>2, with galaxies experiencing a recent downturn in star-formation occupying distinct parameter space. We also study the dustiest galaxies in our sample, showing that they are preferentially more massive and strongly star-forming relative to the parent sample, residing on the high-mass end of the star-forming main-sequence. The slope of the attenuation curve has a strong dependence on Av, varying from steep to shallow as the dust attenuation increases and the specific star-formation rate decreases. Our findings show that the unparalleled number statistics of this catalogue of spectroscopically derived stellar population properties uniquely enables the study star-formation, quenching and dust properties of galaxies from cosmic noon to cosmic dawn.
