These results provide a theoretical basis for understanding the vortex topology of multi-pair production in strong-field QED and for its potential control.
items.authors: Z. L. Li, R. Z. Jiang

items.title: Principles and Techniques for Agentic Research in Experimental Physics
items.abstract: The use of artificial intelligence (AI) in physics research is increasingly common, yet few guidelines exist for its effective use. Starting with a principles-based approach, we outline a set of ten requirements for collaborative AI agents in experimental physics, spanning scientific norms, effective agent use, and domain expertise. We take a human-centered approach in which agents act as collaborators that amplify rather than replace the expertise of a human researcher (user) who directs the work and is responsible for its results. We then present a framework designed to enforce these requirements, detailing methods for improving off-the-shelf behavior of large language models (LLMs) with custom scaffolding and describing general-purpose scientific workflows and skills. In particular, we highlight the power of closed-loop campaigns where agents work iteratively toward a well-defined goal. We demonstrate the potential of this mode of research through six case studies in experimental physics, covering device design, hardware control, neural network optimization, physical model identification, and data analysis. All six case studies result in useful work products that add utility to our research, including a neural network architecture and solid-state quantum defect photodynamic model that substantially outperform our published work; a microwave waveguide design that extends a published design concept to a fabrication-ready device meeting our experimental constraints; a quantum control pulse sequence candidate that improves simulated performance by more than an order of magnitude; commissioning of an NMR spectrometer to $\sim$1~Hz frequency precision on live hardware; and finally a data-fitting pipeline that achieves, to our knowledge, the first reconstruction of the Ising microstate of an artificial spin-ice array from diffraction-limited magnetic imaging.
items.authors: Niko R. Reed, Declan M. Daly, Andrew J. Beling, Jordan D. Giandrea, Ronald L. Walsworth, John W. Blanchard, Daniel Ang

items.title: Revealing topological protection through unprotected operations in a Majorana parity qubit
items.abstract: A recent experiment reported coherent parity oscillations between minimal Kitaev chains, demonstrating a Majorana parity qubit (arXiv:2607.09511). Operations on this qubit are controlled by coupling two Kitaev chains and are intrinsically unprotected against noise in the coupling strength. Here we show how the exponential protection in the underlying chains can nevertheless be revealed through unprotected qubit operations. To this end, we develop an analytical theory of quasistatic dephasing for two coupled $N$-site Kitaev chains at the sweet spot. In Rabi experiments, protection can be resolved by adapting the operating point with chain length: depending on the coupling architecture, it appears as an exponentially increasing optimized number of coherent oscillations or as a longer coherence time. Ramsey experiments show an exponentially increasing coherence time, provided the chains can be sufficiently decoupled. Our analytical theory takes into account the non-Gaussian splitting statistics of the Kitaev chains, allowing us to quantitatively predict the scaling with chain length. Moreover, we determine how residual noise and imperfections limit the range of chain lengths over which this scaling can be observed. Our results show how qubit dynamics can be used to probe Majorana protection in experimentally realistic devices.
items.authors: Sebastian Miles, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Francesco Zatelli, Nick van Loo, Antonio Lombardi, Vincent P. M. Sietses, Florian J. Bennebroek Evertsz', Bart Roovers, Leo P. Kouwenhoven, Michael Wimmer

items.title: Observation of Photon Bunching in Broadband Multimode Thermal Light Enabled by Temporal Imaging
items.abstract: Photons emitted by incoherent sources exhibit temporal bunching, a fundamental manifestation of Bose-Einstein statistics first observed by Hanbury Brown and Twiss (HBT). While intensity correlation measurements originated in astronomy and are now central across quantum technologies, biophysics, and spectroscopy, observing temporal bunching in broadband thermal light remains limited by detector temporal resolution. Conventional approaches - such as streak cameras or optical upconversion - introduce severe trade-offs in efficiency, bandwidth, or setup versatility. Here, we propose and demonstrate a third route: pre-detection temporal magnification of the optical field prior to measuring its intensity autocorrelation function in a conventional HBT setup. Using an electro-optic time lens with a temporal magnification of 660, we resolve the temporal intensity autocorrelation of broadband thermal light generated via non-degenerate spontaneous parametric down-conversion with a bandwidth of 250 GHz. This enables direct observation of thermal photon bunching on sub-3.5 picosecond timescales without narrow spectral filtering, establishing pre-detection temporal imaging as a general platform for broadband statistical optics, with applications spanning ultrafast quantum optics, biophysical imaging, and potentially stellar intensity interferometry.
items.authors: Filip So\'snicki, Micha{\l} Miko{\l}ajczyk, Sanjay Kapoor, Dmitri B. Horoshko, Mikhail I. Kolobov, Micha{\l} Karpi\'nski

items.title: Turning a superconducting diode into a Feynman ratchet to realize a nanoscale heat engine
items.abstract: Feynman's ratchet illustrates how work can be extracted from thermal fluctuations in the presence of two heat baths at different temperatures. While some experimental realizations of the ratchet effect have been studied, most lack miniaturization, which is important for some applications. Here, we propose a physical implementation of Feynman's ratchet based on Josephson junctions exhibiting the superconducting diode effect. This setup functions as a heat engine that generates work solely from a temperature gradient via thermal fluctuations. We analyze its output power and efficiency, and, through the Seebeck coefficient, identify the conditions under which the device operates in reverse, functioning instead as a Peltier cooler.
items.authors: Konstantinos Kontogeorgiou, \.Inan\c{c} Adagideli, G\'eraldine Haack, Fabian Hassler

items.title: QGrAT: Quantum Grade-Aware Transformer for Jet Tagging
items.abstract: Lorentz symmetry and the three-prong structure of hadronic top decays provide physical guidance for designing compact quantum jet taggers. We introduce QGrAT (Quantum Grade-Aware Transformer), a quantum transformer that incorporates these structures into its interactions between constituent qubits. Geometric features constructed from the constituent four-momenta are organised by the grades of the spacetime Clifford algebra $C\ell(1,3)$, and their grade-specific inner products determine the pairwise attention couplings. For fixed constituents and co-transforming reference vectors, these couplings are Lorentz invariant, although the component-wise input encoding makes the complete classifier frame dependent. An auxiliary qubit introduces an explicit three-particle interaction through products of pairwise Minkowski inner products, while a trainable in-circuit readout converts the resulting quantum state into a classification score. We evaluate the architecture in state-vector simulation on the Top Tagging benchmarks. With ten constituents per jet, the configuration using grades $0\text{-}3$ and the three-particle ancilla requires twelve qubits and $144$ trainable parameters, reaching AUC $0.944 \pm 0.002$ and background rejection $1/\varepsilon_B = 35.7 \pm 2.4\ (96.8 \pm 7.7)$ at signal efficiency $\varepsilon_S = 0.50\ (0.30)$. This performance is competitive with the L-GATr-Slim baseline at matched constituent and parameter budgets. Adding the three-particle ancilla raises background rejection at $50\%$ signal efficiency from $19.9$ to $35.7$, whereas extending the representation to the tested grade-$4$ feature gives no consistent improvement. The study establishes a framework for incorporating spacetime geometry into quantum attention and identifies explicit three-particle correlations as the principal source of improved background rejection among the architectural variations tested.
items.authors: Pallavi Bhardwaj, Michael Spannowsky

items.title: Norm properties of quantum uniformity measures
items.abstract: We prove that for $k=4$ the quantum uniformity measures are norms, whereas for every $k\geq5$ the triangle inequality fails. This gives a complete answer to an open question of Bu, Gu, and Jaffe. The $k=4$ case is proved using the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality for the quantum uniformity pairing $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_{Q^4}$ introduced here, together with the triangle inequality in a suitable finite-dimensional Bochner $L^8$ space. For $k\geq5$, we construct systems of linear equations over a finite field and derive a contradiction from the structure theory of norming linear systems.
items.authors: Berke \"Unal

items.title: Time-Domain Observables for Resonant Scattering in Quantum Simulations of Lattice Gauge Theory
items.abstract: Quantum computing may allow unprecedented access to nonequilibrium quantum dynamics, including problems of interest in particle physics, like the real-time development of scattering processes. Although fault-tolerant simulations at scale are still in the future, recent advancements toward early fault-tolerant simulations motivate building increasingly elaborate benchmark problems in order to assess state-of-the-art capabilities and test new algorithms and observables. In this work, we study glueball scattering on a line-of-plaquettes lattice in pure $SU(3)$ lattice gauge theory. We characterize scattering of the lowest-energy glueball states using classical exact diagonalization methods, identifying the continuum resonance structure using real-time simulations and approximate analytic methods, and we propose time-domain observables for extracting properties of the resonance from quantum simulations. We furthermore construct a toy model that shares the spectral features of the lattice gauge theory and demonstrate extraction of the observables. Feasibility on near-term hardware is demonstrated through simulation of a resonant collision of this toy model on Quantinuum System Model $\texttt{H2-2}$, with a 14-plaquette chain encoded in 28 qubits. The Trotterized circuit after optimization and compression requires $\sim 25n$ entangling gates for $n$ Trotter steps.
items.authors: Praveen Balaji, Patrick Draper, Enrico Rinaldi

items.title: Mathematical framework for simulation of non-perturbative cavity optomechanics with plate-like dielectrics
items.abstract: Cavity optomechanical models typically treat a sensor either as a perturbative polarizable object in a pre-existing optical field, or solve the field at a fixed equilibrium and linearize in a fixed optical-mode basis. Neither self-consistently determines the spatially resolved cavity field, the optical force, the mechanical equilibrium, and the back-action when a finite-thickness dielectric plate intercepts the entire optical mode and restructures the intracavity field. In this companion paper to [1], we develop that treatment by extending the vacuum two-photon formalism to finite-thickness planar dielectrics, incorporating their Fresnel reflection, internal propagation, optical forces, and mechanical back-action directly into the field equations. We derive the carrier and sideband transfer functions needed to describe the coupled optical-mechanical system, including optomechanical cooling and the response to external perturbations. The result is a systematic starting point for calculating detector response and noise budgets for cavity experiments with intracavity dielectrics, including gravitational wave detectors deploying levitated sensors.
items.authors: Andrew Laeuger, Nancy Aggarwal

items.title: An Aubry-Andr\'e localized optical lattice clock
items.abstract: Optical lattice clocks in space could improve satellite navigation systems and enable new tests of fundamental physics, including gravitational-wave detection and tests of relativity. In microgravity, atoms can tunnel to degenerate neighboring lattice sites, broadening the clock transition and limiting coherence times. We demonstrate Aubry-Andr\'e localization in a bichromatic optical lattice formed by two magic-wavelength lasers, suppressing tunneling in a horizontal lattice clock emulating free fall. We recover a Fourier-limited clock Rabi spectrum and measure Ramsey coherence times of up to 2 s in shallow lattices, with up to 100-fold improvement over the delocalized regime. These results establish Aubry-Andr\'e localization as a practical route to controlling tunneling in future space-based clocks, and open a path to operating terrestrial clocks at shallower lattice depths.
items.authors: Shuo Ma, Anke St\"olzel, Bennett Christensen, Zhuoli Ding, Dhruva Ganapathy, Andrew Householder, Genyue Liu, Shimon Kolkowitz

items.title: How many switches does two-Hamiltonian universality require?
items.abstract: Any pair of sufficiently generic Hamiltonians on $\mathbb{C}^d$ generates the full unitary group, i.e., any $W\in U(d)$ can be synthesized to arbitrary precision by alternating between the two evolutions for suitably chosen durations. For any given pair of Hamiltonians, the minimal number of switches required to cover the entire group is at least $d$ and unbounded in general. Despite this, we show that it scales linearly in $d$ in expectation. Assuming that the two spectra are sufficiently generic, we derive constructive upper bounds on the minimal switching number as a function of the change-of-basis matrix between the two eigenbases. In particular, if this matrix has a column whose entries all have equal moduli, as for a complex Hadamard matrix, then $9d$ switches suffice to reach every unitary. To obtain these results, we construct a short exact representation of any unitary as a product of unitaries that are alternately diagonal in two given bases. All bounds are extended to non-generic spectra and bounded evolution times.
items.authors: Matas Garbaravi\v{c}ius, Michael M. Wolf

items.title: Dynamics of low energy wave packets in the one-dimensional quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet
items.abstract: Spin wave theory plays a central role in the analysis of low-energy properties of the quantum ferromagnetic Heisenberg model. In this work, we present a first step towards a rigorous justification of this approximation in the context of quantum dynamics in one dimension. According to spin wave theory, the evolution of a spin wave state should be well approximated by its free evolution with the appropriate energy of free quasiparticles called magnons. Our main result establishes this idea rigorously for a class of spin wave packets. We focus on spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ systems, and consider wave packets composed of two magnons. We argue our result is optimal with respect to the timescales.
items.authors: Mateusz Kwa\'snicki, Marcin Napi\'orkowski, S\"oren Petrat, Micha{\l} Pietruszka

items.title: Dynamical BEC formation and vanishing entropy for trapped bosons in non-relativistic QED via nonlinear resonance cascades
items.abstract: The dynamical formation of a complete Bose-Einstein condensate and the asymptotic purification of trapped bosons coupled to a quantized radiation field are rigorously established. By tracking the macroscopic one-particle density matrix $\kappa_T$ through a nonlinear resonance cascade, it is demonstrated that radiative relaxation irreversibly depletes all excited trap modes, even when the initial macroscopic state $\kappa_0$ is genuinely mixed. Here $\kappa_T$ is an average, with respect to a de Finetti measure $\mu_0$, over mean-field particle-field orbits, so that the mixedness of $\kappa_0$ reflects a statistical ensemble of orbits. Under the assumptions of a non-vanishing initial ground state component and strictly positive downward Fermi-Golden-Rule rates, strong trace-norm convergence to a pure condensate is proven, $$ \lim_{T\to\infty} \| \kappa_T-|\chi_0\rangle\langle\chi_0| \|_{\mathfrak{S}_1(\mathfrak{h})} = 0 \, . $$ Furthermore, the von Neumann entropy of the macroscopic one-particle density matrix is shown to vanish asymptotically, $$ \lim_{T\to\infty}S[\kappa_T]=0 \, , $$ without any claim of monotonicity in $T$. Thus, any initially mixed, positive-entropy state ($0<S[\kappa_0]<\infty$) is purified to the ground state $|\chi_0\rangle\langle\chi_0|$. For the proof, we derive the Hartree hierarchy of the coupled system of bosons and photons from the finite-$N$ BBGKY hierarchy of the microscopic quantum many-body system, establishing trace-norm convergence in the mean-field limit as $N\to\infty$. The limits are taken successively; first $N\to\infty$, then the weak-coupling limit, and finally $T\to\infty$. Although the global particle-field evolution remains unitary, the macroscopic one-particle state converges to a pure state as energy and correlations are continuously radiated into the dispersive field.
items.authors: Thomas Chen, Ali Mezher

items.title: WannierSTM: Efficient superconducting scanning-probe spectroscopy from maximally localized Wannier functions
items.abstract: We present a Python-based program that combines maximally localized Wannier functions-based first-principles electronic structure with the nonequilibrium Green's function formalism to enable efficient simulations of scanning tunneling microscopy (STM). The workflow builds upon standard density functional theory packages to construct compact transport Hamiltonians that preserve the properties of realistic materials. Superconductivity is incorporated via an effective pairing potential within the Nambu-spinor formalism, while coupling to the STM tip and substrate electrodes is treated using the wide-band limit approximation. Within this formulation, transport quantities such as current-voltage characteristics and differential conductance are evaluated in a closed analytical form. This avoids explicit numerical energy integrations and enables rapid spectroscopic calculations over broad parameter spaces. The framework provides a unified and computationally efficient approach for modeling superconducting hybrid nanostructures with spin-orbit coupling, magnetic textures, and spin polarization. Representative applications in spin chains, two-dimensional and molecular magnets on a superconductor demonstrate its robust capabilities for both simple model systems and realistic ab initio molecular structures relevant to modern STM experiments.
items.authors: Oscar Moreno Segura, Dorye L. Esteras, Andrei Shumilin, Gonzalo Rivero-Carracedo, Riku Tuovinen, Jos\'e J. Baldov\'i

items.title: Optical parametric amplification of spatiotemporal optical vortices
items.abstract: Spatiotemporal optical vortices (STOVs) are structured light featuring a phase singularity in the spatiotemporal domain, exhibiting unique topology that couples spatial and temporal dimensions. To date, amplification of STOVs remains unexplored, and their wavelength tunability is limited by available light sources. In this work, we present the theoretical analysis and experimental demonstration of optical parametric amplification (OPA) of STOVs. The pulse energy of the STOV signal is enhanced by a factor of 60, while its spatiotemporal structure is robustly preserved. The generated idler inherits the phase-conjugated STOV topology with the opposite topological charge, governed by simultaneous conservation of energy, linear momentum, and spatiotemporal orbital angular momentum. The intrinsic wavelength-conversion capability of OPA further provides a route towards spectrally tunable STOV generation, spanning from visible to near-infrared wavelength regimes. This work paves the way toward further development of multi-stage amplification architectures, facilitating applications of wavelength-tunable spatiotemporally structured light at ultrahigh intensities.
items.authors: Houan Teng, Chenhao Wan, Qiwen Zhan

items.title: Role of dissipation dilution in achieving high mechanical quality factors in van der Waals resonators
items.abstract: Dissipation dilution has driven a revolution in the quality factors ($Q$) of top-down nanomechanical resonators. Yet it has not been leveraged for van der Waals (vdW) materials. Here we report quality factors up to $372{,}000\pm37{,}000$ in monolayer MoS$_2$ drums at 4 K, nearly an order of magnitude beyond the previous best for any vdW material at this temperature, enabled by a clean, polymer-free exfoliation technique. We develop a dissipation-dilution model for circular drums and analyze the contributing intrinsic and extrinsic dissipation mechanisms. The MoS$_2$ monolayer exhibits a dilution factor of order $1,000$, establishing sub-nanometer-thin resonators as ultimate dilution materials. The intrinsic quality factor, however, is limited by surface losses at atomic thickness. Conversely, multilayer drums show a lower dilution factor but a high intrinsic quality factor, on par with established top-down materials of similar dimensions, both resulting from the increased thickness. A two-level-system analysis of the temperature-dependent damping confirms this bulk-versus-surface picture and provides first insight into its microscopic origin. Our results identify dissipation dilution as the governing mechanism for high-$Q$ mechanical vdW resonators. Combined with strategies such as soft clamping or stress engineering, they establish atomically thin resonators as a platform for ultrahigh-$Q$ quantum transduction and sensing.
items.authors: Lukas Schleicher, Leonard Geilen, Alexander Musta, Niklas Walter, Anne Rodriguez, Philipp Bredol, Alexander W. Holleitner, Eva M. Weig

items.title: Orbital Angular Momentum Transfer and Beam-Quality Limits in Fork-Grating Electron Diffraction
items.abstract: We analyze fork-grating generation of electron vortex beams beyond the ideal single-mode approximation. The incident beam is described as a paraxial Gaussian ensemble with finite transverse momentum spread and a first electromagnetic Hartree phase accumulated before the grating. Within Fresnel propagation we derive an analytical expression for each diffraction order and determine the corresponding orbital-angular-momentum statistics. The mean OAM of a selected order remains fixed by the topological rule, $\langle L_z\rangle_m=mp\hbar$, while its variance is set by the residual transverse momentum spread of the beam prepared at the grating. For the Gaussian mixture, the transverse purity is $\mathcal P_{\perp,m}=[1+2(\Delta L_{z,m}/\hbar)^2]^{-1}$. The observed annular profile is governed by a separate propagation-dependent blurring scale, so a beam can retain well-defined mean OAM while having low transverse purity or a partially filled vortex minimum. Within the radial phase-screen approximation, the Hartree self-field modifies the propagated profile while preserving the full-plane OAM moments and transverse purity.
items.authors: P. K. Tsiopa, S. S. Baturin

items.title: Phases of a rotating Bose-Einstein condensate trapped in a hard-wall potential
items.abstract: We investigate the rotational properties of a zero-temperature Bose-Einstein condensed gas, which is confined in a hard-wall potential. For weak interactions the gas carries its angular momentum via vortices of multiple quantization. As the coupling increases and for sufficiently slow rotational frequencies of the trap, the multiply-quantized vortex states become unstable against a mixed state. For stronger couplings, as the angular frequency of the trap increases, there is a transition from a vortex lattice, to a vortex lattice with a hole at the trap center, and finally to a giant vortex. For weak effective attractive interactions we still have vortices of multiple quantization. These states become unstable towards states which break the axial symmetry of the problem and resemble center-of-mass excitation, as the coupling becomes more negative. Finally, for even more attractive forces, the system becomes unstable against collapse.
items.authors: H\'el\`ene Perrin, G. M. Kavoulakis

items.title: Dark state preparation in a zero-field-split molecular triplet
items.abstract: We propose a protocol to prepare and probe dark states in a single-molecule electron spin resonance based on atomic force microscopy (ESR-AFM), thus extending existing techniques developed to address Rabi oscillations. To this end, we simulate in analogy to atomic physics the coherent manipulation of a three-level system in the V-configuration using a multifrequency magnetic field. More specifically, we consider a neutral molecule with a zero-field-split (ZFS) first excited triplet and analyze within a pump-probe scheme the dynamics of the total triplet population. In the triplet subspace, the dark state is a coherent superposition formed by two ZFS states which does not evolve in time despite a continuous resonant driving towards the third one. We characterize the properties of this state comparing it to its fully incoherent counterpart. Within a density-matrix formalism for open systems, we then compute the expected dark state signatures both for ideal scenarios and for the realistic parameterization of ESR-AFM on pentacene.
items.authors: Maria Pfahler, Andrea Donarini

items.title: Converting long-range entanglement into mixture: tensor-network approach to local equilibration
items.abstract: In the out-of-equilibrium evolution induced by a quench, fast degrees of freedom generate long-range entanglement that is hard to encode with standard tensor networks. However, local observables only sense such long-range correlations through their contribution to the reduced local state as a mixture. We present a tensor network method that identifies such long-range entanglement and efficiently transforms it into mixture, much easier to represent. In this way, we obtain an effective description of the time-evolved state as a density matrix that captures the long-time behavior of local operators with finite computational resources.
items.authors: Miguel Fr\'ias-P\'erez, Luca Tagliacozzo, Mari Carmen Ba\~nuls

items.title: All you need is Trotter
items.abstract: The work here enables a cost scaling of $\tilde{O}\left( \frac{T ^{1+o(1)}\,{\rm log}^2 (1/\epsilon)}{\varepsilon}\right)$ and maximum depth $\tilde{O}\left( \frac{T^{1+o(1)}\,{\rm log} (1/\epsilon)}{\varepsilon}\right)$ for estimating observables after some Hamiltonian evolution $e^{i H T}$ using no extra block-encoding qubits, where $\epsilon$ is the algorithmic error of the target Hamiltonian evolution and $\varepsilon$ is the statistical error from the observable estimation. Throughout, $\tilde{O}$ suppresses factors that are doubly logarithmic in $1/\epsilon$ (i.e. ${\rm polyloglog}(1/\epsilon)$), which are subdominant to the displayed ${\rm polylog}(1/\epsilon)$ factors. This is achieved through product formulas, stable interpolation (Chebyshev), and to calculate the needed fractional queries, cardinal sine interpolation is used. This is an improvement over similar work using interpolation methods which have a superlinear scaling of the form $5^p T^{1+1/p}$, where $p$ is the order of the product formula used and an improvement on required qubits over Quantum Signal Processing methods while maintaining scaling with ${\rm polylog}{1/\epsilon}$. This is accomplished through an optimized and variable (with $T$) order $p$. The slightly better $\log^2(1/\epsilon)$ compared to $\log^3(1/\epsilon)$ comes from the use of cardinal sine interpolation compared to other methods using Chebyshev interpolation and product formulas. The work presented here also provides an alternative to Quantum Signal Processing techniques to calculate observables or amplitudes after a fractional query evolution with a cost $O(T\log{1/\epsilon})$ through this cardinal sine interpolation.
items.authors: Gumaro Rendon

items.title: A minimal example of quantum non-classicality without freedom of choice
items.abstract: Bell's theorem is often considered the most stringent notion of non-classicality. The generalization of Bell's theorem to causal networks offers interesting new perspectives on the phenomenon of quantum non-classicality and prompts us with a fundamental inquiry: What is the simplest scenario leading to the incompatibility between quantum correlations and the classical theory of causality? Here we demonstrate that quantum non-classicality is possible in an entanglement swapping network consisting of only three dichotomic variables, without the need for the locality assumption or external measurement choices. We also show that interventions, a central tool in the field of causal inference, significantly improve the noise robustness of this new kind of non-classical behavior, making it feasible for experimental tests with current technology.
items.authors: Pedro Lauand, Davide Poderini, Rafael Rabelo, Rafael Chaves

items.title: Operator representation of spatiotemporal quantum correlations
items.abstract: While quantum correlations between two spacelike-separated systems are fully encoded by the bipartite density operator associated with the joint system, there does not exist an analogous operator representing general quantum correlations across space and time. This is in stark contrast to the case of classical random variables, which make no distinction between spacelike and timelike correlations. Despite this, we show that spatiotemporal correlations between light-touch observables (i.e., observables whose eigenvalues are all equal in magnitude) admit a unique operator representation for arbitrary timelike-separated quantum systems. A special case of our result reproduces generalized Pauli observables and pseudo-density matrices, which have, up until now, only been defined for multi-qubit systems. In the case of qutrit systems, we use our results to illustrate an intriguing connection between light-touch observables and symmetric, informationally complete, positive operator-valued measures (SIC-POVMs).
items.authors: James Fullwood, Arthur J. Parzygnat

items.title: Noncontextuality inequalities for prepare-transform-measure scenarios
items.abstract: We provide the first systematic technique for deriving witnesses of contextuality in prepare-transform-measure scenarios. More specifically, we show how linear quantifier elimination can be used to compute a polytope of correlations consistent with generalized noncontextuality in such scenarios. This polytope is specified as a set of noncontextuality inequalities that are necessary and sufficient conditions for observed data in the scenario to admit of a classical explanation relative to any linear operational identities, if one ignores some constraints from diagram preservation. While including these latter constraints generally leads to tighter inequalities, it seems that nonlinear quantifier elimination would be required to systematically include them. We also provide a linear program which can certify the nonclassicality of a set of numerical data arising in a prepare-transform-measure experiment. We apply our results to get a robust noncontextuality inequality for transformations that can be violated within the stabilizer subtheory. Finally, we give a simple algorithm for computing all the linear operational identities holding among a given set of states, of transformations, or of measurements.
items.authors: David Schmid, Roberto D. Baldij\~ao, John H. Selby, Ana Bel\'en Sainz, Robert W. Spekkens

items.title: A General Framework for Gradient-Based Optimization of Superconducting Quantum Circuits using Qubit Discovery as a Case Study
items.abstract: Engineering the Hamiltonian of a quantum system is fundamental to the design of quantum systems. Automating Hamiltonian design through gradient-based optimization can dramatically accelerate this process. However, computing the gradients of eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a Hamiltonian--a large, sparse matrix--relative to system properties poses a significant challenge, especially for arbitrary systems. Superconducting quantum circuits offer substantial flexibility in Hamiltonian design, making them an ideal platform for this task. In this work, we present a comprehensive framework for the gradient-based optimization of superconducting quantum circuits, leveraging the SQcircuit software package. By addressing the challenge of calculating the gradient of the eigensystem for large, sparse Hamiltonians and integrating automatic differentiation within SQcircuit, our framework enables efficient and precise computation of gradients for various circuit properties or custom-defined metrics, streamlining the optimization process. We apply this framework to the qubit discovery problem, demonstrating its effectiveness in identifying qubit designs with superior performance metrics. The optimized circuits show improvements in a heuristic measure of gate count, upper bounds on gate speed, decoherence time, and resilience to noise and fabrication errors compared to existing qubits. While this methodology is showcased through qubit optimization and discovery, it is versatile and can be extended to tackle other optimization challenges in superconducting quantum hardware design.
items.authors: Taha Rajabzadeh, Alex Boulton-McKeehan, Sam Bonkowsky, David I. Schuster, Amir H. Safavi-Naeini
items.title_zh: 基于梯度优化的超导量子电路设计框架研究
items.summary_zh: 量子系统的哈密顿量工程是量子系统设计的基础。通过基于梯度的优化自动化哈密顿量设计可以显著加速这一过程。然而，相对于系统属性计算哈密顿量的特征值和特征向量的梯度，尤其是对于任意系统，面临重大挑战。超导量子电路在哈密顿量设计上具有较大灵活性，成为理想平台。本文提出了一种全面的超导量子电路梯度优化框架，利用SQcircuit软件包，解决了大规模稀疏哈密顿量特征系统梯度计算的挑战，并在SQcircuit中集成了自动微分。该框架实现了对各种电路属性或自定义指标的高效精确梯度计算，简化了优化过程。我们将该框架应用于量子比特发现问题，展示了其在识别具有优越性能指标的量子比特设计方面的有效性。优化后的电路在门数、门速上限、去相干时间以及对噪声和制造误差的抗性等启发式指标上均有所改善。

items.title: Symmetry defects and gauging for quantum states with matrix product unitary symmetries
items.abstract: In this work, we examine the consequences of the existence of a finite group of matrix product unitary (MPU) symmetries for matrix product states (MPS). We generalize the well-understood picture of onsite unitary symmetries, which give rise to virtual symmetry defects given by insertions of operators in the bonds of the MPS. In the MPU case, we can define analogous defect tensors, this time sitting on lattice sites, that can be created, moved, and fused by local unitary operators. We leverage this formalism to study the gauging of MPU symmetries. We introduce a condition, block independence, under which we can gauge the symmetries by promoting the symmetry defects to gauge degrees of freedom, yielding an MPS of the same bond dimension that supports a local version of the symmetry given by commuting gauge constraints. Whenever block independence does not hold (which happens, in particular, whenever the symmetry representation is anomalous), a modification of our method which we call state-level gauging still gives rise to a locally symmetric MPS by promotion of the symmetry defects, at the expense of producing gauge constraints that do not commute on different sites.
items.authors: Adri\'an Franco-Rubio, Arkadiusz Bochniak, J. Ignacio Cirac

items.title: Coherent State Assisted Entanglement Generation Between Quantum Memories
items.abstract: Generating entanglement deterministically at a capacity-approaching rate is critical for next-generation quantum networks. We revisit previous protocols and present a readily-realizable coherent-state-assisted protocol that can generate entanglement near-deterministically between reflective-cavity-based quantum memories at up to twice the rate attainable using the dual-rail photonic-qubit mediated scheme. The most pronounced rate benefit occurs in the low-channel-loss regime and persists even with moderate noise. The protocol can be generalized to entangling an array of memories into various multi-qubit entangled states, including a GHZ state.
items.authors: Chaohan Cui, Prajit Dhara, Saikat Guha
items.title_zh: 相干态辅助的量子记忆纠缠生成
items.summary_zh: 在接近容量的速率下确定性地生成纠缠对于下一代量子网络至关重要。我们重新审视了之前的协议，并提出了一种易于实现的相干态辅助协议，该协议能够在反射腔量子记忆之间近乎确定性地生成纠缠，速率可达到双轨光子量子比特介导方案的两倍。最显著的速率优势出现在低信道损耗的情况下，并且即使在中等噪声下也能保持。该协议可以推广到将多个记忆纠缠成各种多量子比特纠缠态，包括GHZ态。

items.title: A Constructive Definition of Space via Dynamical Evolution and Observational Acts
items.abstract: We propose a constructive and dynamical redefinition of spatial structure, grounded in the interplay between mechanical evolution and observational acts. Rather than presupposing space as a static background, we interpret space as an emergent entity that arises through observational acts. Given a time evolution and a physically specified measurement context, we construct a reachability structure and a context-dependent measurable structure. Using the framework of pre-topologies, measurable structures, and the GNS construction, we analyze how the choice of observables and the system's time evolution dynamically determine the topological and measure-theoretic features of space. Time evolution and the measurement context are inputs to this construction. Deriving time itself or a complete dynamics for the selection and stabilization of the measurement context lies outside the scope of this paper. This approach highlights the observer-dependent and context-sensitive nature of spatial concepts in both classical and quantum domains.
items.authors: So Katagiri

items.title: Polarization-sensitive vector magnetometry using nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond
items.abstract: The phase relationships between the vector components of a time-varying field define its polarization, which can provide insight into the structure of a magnetic field source and its environment. The goal of this work is to measure magnetic field elliptical polarization parameters, and demonstrate their utility through direct observation of field source rotations and environmental coupling. An ensemble of nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond is used to perform phase-sensitive ac vector magnetometry, enabling direct measurement of field polarization ellipses using complex spin-resonance solutions to the NV Hamiltonian. Measurements of wire-coil sources demonstrated retrieval of linear and elliptical magnetic polarizations, allowing direct observation of source rotation and mutual coupling between coils. These results establish magnetic polarimetry as a practical extension of ac vector magnetometry, and promise applications in vector ac susceptometry for anisotropic materials characterization, and the analysis of reactive electrical systems.
items.authors: M. S. J. Barson, T. J. Christie, J. P. Duff, K. Helmerson

items.title: Improving Quantum Recurrent Neural Networks with Amplitude Encoding
items.abstract: Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) are widely used to model complex temporal dependencies in sequential data. Quantum Recurrent Neural Networks (QRNNs) extend this idea to quantum machine learning by using quantum circuits inspired by classical recurrent architectures. In this paper, we propose three modifications to existing QRNN implementations that improve performance, generalization, and circuit efficiency. First, we introduce a simple preprocessing technique that augments amplitude encoded inputs with their prenormalized magnitudes, improving generalization on two financial data sets. Second, we show that a trained model can achieve comparable results with an approximate feature map rather than an expensive exact state preparation circuit. Third, we present a novel QRNN circuit architecture that is mathematically equivalent to the original model on ideal processors, but significantly reduces circuit depth. We demonstrate how these techniques can be put together to improve the performance of a QRNN when making predictions on real world financial data sets.
items.authors: Jack Morgan, Hamed Mohammadbagherpoor, Eric Ghysels

items.title: The gauge freedom in the Aharonov-Casher theorem: The problem in two and one dimensions
items.abstract: In this note, we investigate the role of gauge freedom in the Aharonov-Casher theorem in one and two dimensions. In particular, we analyze the asymptotic behavior of the gauge freedom. We show that in two-dimensional space the gauge field is uniquely determined, whereas in one dimensional space a residual gauge freedom allows for an infinite family of equivalent gauges. This freedom is determined by a constant k. However, the number $k$ must be restricted in order to guarantee the existence of a normalizable zero mode. This restriction is determined by the inequality $|k| < \frac{1}{2} \int dx B(x)$, where $B(x)$ is a scalar field localized in a finite region of space. We show that this condition is equivalent to the gauge field taking opposite-sign values at $+\infty$ and $-\infty$. Finally, we illustrate these results with an explicit example.
items.authors: Lucas Sourrouille

items.title: Completeness for Fault Equivalence of Clifford ZX Diagrams
items.abstract: Two circuits are considered to be equivalent under noise if the effect of faults on one circuit is no worse than the effect of faults on the other circuit. We call this relationship fault equivalence. Fault equivalence offers a way to transform circuits while provably preserving their fault-tolerant properties, enabling a framework for fault-tolerant circuit synthesis and optimisation that is correct by construction. The ZX calculus offers a diagrammatic way to represent and reason about quantum circuits and is a useful tool for manipulating circuits while preserving fault equivalence. For this, the usual set of ZX rewrites has to be restricted to not only preserve the underlying linear map represented by the diagram, but also fault equivalence. In this work, we provide a set of ZX rewrites that are sound and complete for fault equivalence of Clifford ZX diagrams. This means that any equivalence that can be derived using the proposed rules is certain to be correct, and any correct equivalence can be derived using only these rules. For this, we utilise diagrammatic constructions called fault gadgets to reason about arbitrary, possibly correlated Pauli faults in ZX diagrams. Fault gadgets allow us to separate the diagram into a fault-free part, which captures the noise-free behaviour of a diagram, and a noisy part that enumerates the effects of all possible faults. Using this, we provide a unique normal form for ZX diagrams under noise and show that any diagram can be brought into this normal form using our proposed rule set. Leveraging the constructive nature of our proof of completeness, we implemented a software library to check whether two ZX diagrams with given noise models are fault-equivalent.
items.authors: Maximilian R\"usch, Aleks Kissinger, Benjamin Rodatz

items.title: Learning and certification of local time-dependent quantum dynamics and noise
items.abstract: Hamiltonian learning protocols are becoming valuable tools for benchmarking and verifying quantum computers and simulators, yet few rigorous protocols address explicitly time-dependent dynamics. We give a scalable protocol for learning the time-dependent coefficients of a locally interacting $n$-qubit system on a graph $\mathsf{G}$ of effective dimension $D$. The unknown generator contains geometrically local Hamiltonian terms and weak onsite Pauli-dephasing terms with time-dependent, nonnegative rates. Its coefficient functions and their derivatives admit a certified simultaneous $C^1$ approximation in a known finite-dimensional function class that supports stable interpolation. The only experimental primitives are preparation of product Pauli eigenstates, evolution for chosen times, and product-Pauli measurements. Under an explicit weak-dissipation condition, the Lieb--Robinson estimates proved here, and a certified effective approximation/interpolation degree $m_{\rm eff}$, the protocol reconstructs every coefficient uniformly on a constant interval with error $\epsilon$ and success probability $1-\delta$ using $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\!\left(\epsilon^{-2}\operatorname{poly}(m_{\rm eff})\log(n\delta^{-1})\right)$ samples and polynomial classical processing. The method estimates derivatives of finite-time channel overlaps by stable interpolation, uses process shadows to learn the required local transfer matrices, and constructs sparse diagonally dominant systems through localized semidefinite programs.
items.authors: Daniel Stilck Fran\c{c}a, Cambyse Rouz\'e, Albert H. Werner, Tim M\"obus

items.title: One-dimensional tunneling of the two-body bound state
items.abstract: We consider bound and scattering states of the one-dimensional dimer formed by two coupled non-identical atoms when one of them also interacts with the zero-range potential located at the origin. By calculating the dimer localized and scattering wave functions, we identify properties of the system without the two-body bound-state breakdown. In general, we predict an enhancement of the dimer reflection compared to a single atom, except for a narrow region on the attractive side of the external potential.
items.authors: N. Shypka, O. Hryhorchak, V. Pastukhov

items.title: Quantum Voting Protocol for Centralized and Distributed Voting Based on Phase-Flip Counting
items.abstract: We introduce a quantum voting protocol that uses superposition and entanglement to enable anonymous voting with trusted voting machines, in a centralized setting with a single machine and in a distributed setting where several machines are linked to a voting center through quantum channels. A voter selects a candidate through a restricted ballot interface; the machine encodes the vote as a phase-flip operation, controlled by the voter's identity register, on an entangled candidate state. Tallying is performed by interference with a reference branch followed by a measurement of the candidate register, which reproduces the vote distribution without iterative classical counting. Because every tallying run consumes the quantum state, the machines store the cast choices classically and replay the voting stage for each run. The protocol uses only basic quantum gates (Hadamard and controlled-Z). We provide analytical examples (4 voters with 2 candidates and 8 voters with 3 candidates) and numerical experiments that simulate ideal conditions, depolarizing, memory, readout, and gate noise, faulty or mistaken ballots, larger instances with confidence intervals, and sampling convergence. The simulations reproduce the theoretical tally probabilities in the ideal case and show how the tally is distorted by noise and by faulty ballots; no error correction or mitigation is applied. Voter anonymity is formalized as the indistinguishability of tallying transcripts under vote permutations, and an identity-dephasing step renders the identity register exactly maximally mixed under the stated trust assumptions. The numbers of protocol runs needed for exact tallying and for winner identification are analyzed explicitly.
items.authors: Ali Emre Aydin, Ammar Daskin

items.title: From Discrete to Continuous-Variable Systems via Jordan-Schwinger Tomographic Transformation
items.abstract: Hybrid quantum systems that combine discrete-variable (DV) and continuous-variable (CV) architectures represent a promising direction in quantum information science. However, transferring concepts, information, and states between these platforms poses practical and theoretical challenges, as their formalisms assign different properties and physical interpretations to many shared notions. We construct a bridge between DV spin systems and restricted CV bosonic systems within corresponding sectors using the tomographic probability representation of quantum states and the Jordan--Schwinger and Holstein--Primakoff maps. Although these maps are well known at the operator level, their action on tomograms and other probability representations has not been addressed in the literature. To the best of our knowledge, we provide the first explicit demonstration of their action on tomographic probability distributions and Wigner functions, establishing direct correspondences between the measurement statistics of DV systems and the corresponding restricted CV bosonic representations. Our tomographic mapping transfers measurement data between quantum architectures through an intrinsic data compression kernel that selects the Hilbert space sector relevant to the target representation. It yields the tomogram of a target sector directly from experimental data in another representation, without reconstructing the density matrix. This provides a unified framework for transferring and comparing quantum information across different hardware platforms within the corresponding restricted sectors, with applications to hybrid protocols, device benchmarking, and the validation of error correction schemes based on mappings between finite-dimensional systems and sector restricted bosonic representations.
items.authors: Liubov A. Markovich, Vladimir A. Orlov, Alexey N. Rubtsov, Vladimir I. Man'ko

items.title: Simulating Clifford Circuits with Gaussian Elimination
items.abstract: Quantum circuits are considered more powerful than classical circuits and require exponential resources to simulate classically. Clifford circuits are a special class of quantum circuits that can be simulated in polynomial time but still show important quantum effects such as entanglement. In this work, we present an algorithm that simulates Clifford circuits by performing Gaussian elimination on a modified adjacency matrix derived from the circuit structure. Our work builds on a ZX-calculus tensor network representation of Clifford circuits that reduces to quantum graph states. We give a concise formula of amplitudes of graph states based on the LDL decomposition of matrices over GF(2), and use it to get efficient algorithms for strong and weak simulation of Clifford circuits using a tree-decomposition-based sparse LDL algorithm. The complexity of our algorithm matches the state of the art for weak graph state simulation and improves the state of the art for strong graph state simulation by taking advantage of Strassen-like fast matrix multiplication. Our algorithm is also efficient when computing many amplitudes or samples of a Clifford circuit. Further, our amplitudes formula provides a new characterization of locally Clifford equivalent graph states as well as an efficient protocol to learn graph states with low-rank adjacency matrices.
items.authors: Yuchen Pang, Edgar Solomonik

items.title: Robust Two-Qubit Geometric Phase Gates using Amplitude and Frequency Ramping
items.abstract: We demonstrate a method for generating entanglement between trapped atomic ions based on adiabatically ramped state-dependent forces. By ramping both the amplitude of the state-dependent force and the motional mode frequencies, we realize an entangling operation that is robust to motional mode occupation and drifts in the mode frequencies. We measure Bell state fidelities above 0.99 across a broad range of ramp parameters and with motional occupations up to 10 phonons. This technique enables high-fidelity entangling operations without ground-state cooling, has a reduced calibration overhead, and is well suited for both quantum logic spectroscopy applications and scalable quantum computing architectures.
items.authors: Christina Bowers, Deviprasath Palani, John Barta, Tyler Guglielmo, Stephen Libby, Dietrich Leibfried, Daniel Slichter

items.title: Critical quantum sensing via backaction-evading continuous measurement
items.abstract: Continuous monitoring of open quantum-optical systems offers a promising route towards quantum-enhanced sensing. In such sensing schemes, the ultimate precision limit is dictated by the quantum Cram\'er-Rao bound. However, reaching this fundamental bound with established continuous measurement techniques has remained an outstanding challenge. Here, we present an approach tailored to open quantum-optical sensors operating near dissipative critical points. The key insight of our approach is to exploit a synergy between the intrinsic critical dynamics and the unavoidable quantum measurement backaction of continuous homodyne detection. By carefully aligning the homodyne phase to the squeezing angle of the sensor state, quantum backaction can be evaded in the critical dynamics, thereby significantly boosting the attainable precision. We demonstrate the broad applicability of this approach across several sensor models and for both single- and multi-parameter estimation, showing that it consistently narrows the gap toward the ultimate precision bound.
items.authors: Cheng Zhang, Mauro Cirio, Xin-Qi Li, Pengfei Liang

items.title: Strengthening the quantum data processing inequality for maximal $f$-divergences via unraveling
items.abstract: Maximal $f$-divergences, among them the Belavkin--Staszewski relative entropy, are non-increasing under completely positive trace-preserving maps, which is the quantum data processing inequality (DPI). We quantify this decrease for Lindblad evolutions with Hermitian jump operators by lifting the problem to a stochastic unraveling, in which the two states become measures on pure states evolving under a classical Fokker--Planck equation. The lift rests on the identity that the infimum of the classical $f$-divergence over ensembles realizing two states is equal to their maximal $f$-divergence. This infimum is attained on a common basis of pure states, which is admissible initial data for the unraveling. The result is a strengthened DPI, with the loss bounded below by the time integral of a relative $f$-Fisher information. Given a two-sided bound on the unraveling's transition kernel, we derive two exponential decay estimates. For bracket-generating jump operators, the rate reaches twice the spectral gap of the symmetrized generator after an explicit delay. Without bracket generation, the kernel bound alone gives any rate below twice the spectral gap of the full generator.
items.authors: Marcos Ruibal Ortigueira, Robert de Keijzer, Luke Visser, Oliver Tse, Servaas Kokkelmans

items.title: Phase-space representation of classical simulability for arbitrary bosonic encodings
items.abstract: Phase-space representations can be used to reveal resources for quantum computational advantage. In odd-dimensional qudit systems, states and operations admitting non-negative quasi-probability representations are efficiently classically simulable, and analogous conclusions hold for bosonic systems, usually represented in quadrature phase space. However, when quantum information is encoded in bosonic systems, the link between physical phase-space representations and computational resources becomes nontrivial: large negativities may arise in the physical space even when the encoded model remains efficiently simulable. We establish a general framework connecting physical phase spaces of bosonic systems to the effective computational phase spaces associated with arbitrary encodings. We show that bosonic Hilbert spaces with finitely many modes can always be exactly encoded on a quantum computer, without truncation or approximations, and that for any encoding there exists an adapted physical phase-space representation in which all provably classically simulable states and protocols are non-negative. Conversely, negativity can always persist in physical representations for arbitrary encodings. Our results formalize the operational meaning of phase-space negativity in bosonic quantum information and its relation with computational resources.
items.authors: Eloi Descamps, Astghik Saharyan, Arne Keller, P\'erola Milman

items.title: Finite-size clocks in quantum field theory and the twin paradox
items.abstract: Vacuum fluctuations in quantum field theory impose fundamental limitations on our ability to measure time at arbitrarily short scales. To investigate the impact of universal quantum field theory effects on observer-dependent time measurements, we introduce a clock model based on the vacuum decay probability of a finite-sized quantum system. This model defines an effective notion of proper time that depends on the microscopic properties of the clock and on how it samples vacuum fluctuations along its trajectory. We show that, in the long-time regime, this notion of time reduces to the usual proper time of special relativity. However, by studying a microscopic twin-paradox scenario, we find that, in general, time is not determined solely by the trajectory connecting two events, but also by how vacuum fluctuations interact with the internal structure of the clocks.
items.authors: Matheus H. Zambianco, T. Rick Perche

items.title: Geometric Quantum Computation
items.abstract: We present a new model of quantum computation rooted in the representation theory of the mass less sector of unitary irreducible representations of the extended Poincare group developed in [1].
items.authors: Marco Zaopo

items.title: The Lieb-Robinson correlation function for long disordered transverse-field Ising chains
items.abstract: The Lieb-Robinson correlation function can be used to characterize the propagation of quantum information in Ising chains. Considerable work has been done to establish bounds on this correlation function in various circumstances. To actually calculate the value of the correlation function directly typically requires a state space which grows exponentially with system size, and so is intractable for all but relatively small systems. We employ a recently-developed method that enables direct calculation of the Lieb--Robinson correlation function and which scales linearly with system size. This enables the computation for systems with more than a thousand qubits, revealing the propagation of quantum information down the chain. We extend this technique to the problem of Ising chains with randomly disordered coupling strengths. Increasing disorder causes localization of the quantum correlations and halts propagation of quantum information down the chain. We see light-cone isocontours therefore becoming vertical. The decay of correlations down the chain is characterized by a correlation length which in the paramagnetic phase increases quadratically with mean coupling strength and inverse quadratically with disorder level. The correlation length peaks at the phase transition. We map our general expression for the correlation function in the Ising system onto the probability density in the single particle tight-binding Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model for a specific initial condition.
items.authors: Brendan J. Mahoney, Craig S. Lent

items.title: Spectator-transition crosstalk in a spin-3/2 silicon-vacancy qudit in silicon carbide revealed by broadband Ramsey interferometry
items.abstract: Color-center spins in 4H-SiC offer a rare combination of wafer-scale materials maturity with long spin coherence and chip-level photonics, making them promising building blocks for scalable quantum technologies. In particular, the silicon vacancy hosts an S=3/2 ground state, a native qudit that enables compact encodings and subspace-selective control but also introduces spectator transitions: short, detuned pulses can coherently drive nonaddressed level pairs and create crosstalk. Here we use broadband Ramsey interferometry to reveal and quantify such spectator-transition crosstalk. Experimentally, the Ramsey Fourier spectra display multiple lines beyond the addressed single-quantum transition. Analytically, we map each line to a pairwise energy difference between qudit levels of the rotating-frame Hamiltonian and assign its weight via compact amplitudes set by the prepared state and the microwave pulse parameters, predicting a deterministic six-branch structure. Numerical time-domain propagation with the experimental sampling reproduces the detuning map, and the measured peak positions coincide with the analytic branch lines without frequency fitting. Together these results provide a practical, spectator-aware framework for multilevel control in the silicon-vacancy qudit. The approach offers clear guidance to suppress crosstalk or, conversely, to exploit spectator lines, e.g., as additional constraints for in situ pulse calibration and for phase-sensitive quantum state and process estimation.
items.authors: Jun-Jae Choi, Seung-Jae Hwang, Seoyoung Paik, Juhwan Kim, Jawad Ul-Hassan, Nguyen Tien Son, Hiroshi Abe, Takeshi Ohshima, Jaekwon Suk, Hyeon-Ho Jeong, Dong-Hee Kim, Sang-Yun Lee

items.title: Enhanced quantum parameter estimation based on the Hardy paradox
items.abstract: Statistical paradoxes such as the Hardy paradox and the enhancement of phase estimation via post-selection both draw upon the same non-classical features of quantum statistics described by non-positive quasi-probabilities. In this paper, we introduce a post-selected quantum metrology scenario where the initial state, the dynamics associated with the phase shift, and the post-selection are all inspired by the Hardy paradox. Specifically, we identify an anomalous weak value that is characteristic of both the Hardy paradox and the potential enhancement of sensitivity by the post-selection. We find that the efficiency of the enhancement is reduced when the expectation value associated with the anomalous weak value is different from the inverse of this value. We conclude that the relation between enhanced phase estimation and the Hardy paradox requires a detailed understanding of the relation between weak values and expectation values.
items.authors: Ming Ji, Yuxiang Yang, Holger F. Hofmann

items.title: Accessing Levinson-Smith and Li\'{e}nard equations in a nonlinear framework of quantum mechanics
items.abstract: In this paper, we present the reduction of a recently introduced generalized quantum scheme of Chodos and Cooper to Levinson-Smith and Li\'{e}nard classes of nonlinear system that enable us to furnish a wider class of acceptable solutions. In particular, for the Levinson-Smith equations, we find their relevance to position-dependent mass quantum systems, with an interesting off-shoot that solitonic-like solutions emerge from the condition of the level surface in the system. On the other hand, for the Li\'{e}nard type, which has coefficients of odd and odd symmetry in the present set up, we demonstrate that closed form solutions exist on carrying out conversion to the typical Abel form.
items.authors: Bijan Bagchi, Anindya Ghose-Choudhury

items.title: Differentiable Maximum Likelihood Noise Estimation for Quantum Error Correction
items.abstract: Accurate noise estimation is essential for fault-tolerant quantum computing, since decoding per formance depends critically on the fidelity of circuit-level noise parameters. We introduce a differ entiable Maximum Likelihood Estimation (dMLE) framework that learns these parameters directly from experimental syndrome data using likelihood gradients, with no decoder in the training loop. Mapping syndrome likelihoods to statistical-mechanical models enables exact and efficient evalua tion via planar solvers for repetition codes and tensor networks (TNs) for surface codes, extending the exact treatment to code distance d = 5 with a small number of rounds, and, via spatial subsam pling combined with time-translation symmetry, to larger codes and larger round counts. Across four experimental superconducting datasets, dMLE reduces logical error rates by up to 30.6% for repetition codes. On the Sycamore d = 3 surface code, a TN decoder using the dMLE prior attains a logical error rate comparable to that reported for state-of-the-art AlphaQubit, using standard syndromes alone without auxiliary leakage data. On the larger d = 5 surface code the dMLE prior lowers the logical error rate of the TN and Tesseract decoders by 7.18% and 5.23% relative to a prior optimized by reinforcement learning; at d = 7 it lowers that of Tesseract by 4.56% and 4.83% in the X and Z bases.
items.authors: Hanyan Cao, Dongyang Feng, Zixuan Lu, Cheng Ye, Feng Pan

items.title: Preparing pre-established quantum correlations with pulse-level control
items.abstract: In this work, we present a technique for quantum state preparation in transmon qubit system that employs optimized electromagnetic pulse sequences rather than discrete quantum gates. By focusing directly on quantum correlations rather than specific target states, we optimize the pulse parameters to generate the desired entanglement structures in two and three qubits systems. The resulting protocols reproduce the characteristic entanglement properties associated with the Bell, GHZ, and W classes, reaching values of the corresponding entanglement measures consistent with these entanglement structures. The approach uses a reduced set of parameters to characterize the control pulses, thereby restricting the space explored during optimization while retaining the entanglement properties of interest.
items.authors: K. De La Ossa Doria, T. Merlo Vergara, D. Goyeneche

items.title: Optimal quantum metrology protocols with erasure qubits
items.abstract: We investigate the precision limits and optimal protocols for sensing single qubit signals in the presence of erasure noise. We study a hierarchy of precision limits achievable with metrological strategies of differing complexity, and identify the optimal protocol for each. The detectability of erasure noise is shown to lead to enhanced precision limits and simplified sensing protocols. For energy gap estimation, we demonstrate that a simple product-state strategy with continuous erasure detection yields significant improvements, outperforming optimal passive entangled protocols over a broad range of finite system sizes. We show that for other single-qubit signals, quantum error correction provides a substantial advantage by correcting the dominant erasure processes, and can restore Heisenberg-limited precision in certain erasure configurations. As a byproduct of our analysis, we find erasure-conversion schemes for qubits subject to thermal noise that attain the corresponding ultimate precision limits.
items.authors: Michal Arieli, Alex Retzker, Tuvia Gefen

items.title: History state formalism for time series with application to finance
items.abstract: We present a method for analyzing general time series by employing the history state formalism of quantum mechanics. This formalism allows us to describe a complete evolution based on a single quantum state, the history state, which simultaneously includes -also as a quantum system- the reference clock. It naturally leads to the concept of system-time entanglement, with the ensuing entanglement entropy constituting a measure of the effective number of distinguishable states visited in the history. Through a quantum coherent state embedding of the time series data, it is then possible to associate a quantum history state to the series. The gaussian overlap between these coherent states provides thus a smooth measure of distinguishability between the series data. The eigenvalues of the corresponding overlap matrix determine in fact the entanglement spectrum and entropy of the history state, which provide a rigorous characterization of the evolution. As illustration, the formalism is applied to typical financial time-series data. Through the entanglement entropy and spectrum, different evolution regimes can be identified. Entanglement based volatility indicators are also derived, and compared with standard volatility measures.
items.authors: F. Lomoc, N. Canosa, A. P. Boette, R. Rossignoli

items.title: Asymptotically good bosonic Fock state codes
items.abstract: We study the error-correction properties of multi-mode Fock-state codes under amplitude-damping (AD) noise, focusing on the asymptotic regime in which the total excitation of the code states grows without limit and the number of photon losses induced by the noise scales linearly with it. In this setting, existing code families, which correct only sublinearly many photon losses, do not protect against amplitude-damping (AD) noise with a constant loss parameter. As our main result, we address this gap by constructing asymptotically good Fock-state codes relying on random classical codes in the discrete simplex. Unlike many standard constructions of random quantum codes, our construction introduces randomness through the underlying classical indexing structure. Randomization also enables another desirable feature: bounded per-mode occupancy, which limits the number of photons in any individual mode and thereby increases the coherence lifetime of the code states. Finally, via a relation between Fock-state codes and permutation-invariant codes, our results also yield asymptotically good families of qudit permutation-invariant codes as well as codes in monolithic nuclear state spaces.
items.authors: Dor Elimelech, Arda Aydin, Alexander Barg

items.title: Postselection-induced localization and coherence in quantum walks on heterogeneous networks
items.abstract: Postselection of quantum trajectories is known effectively introduce nonlinearity into dynamics of open quantum systems. We study the effect of such non-linearity in continuous-time quantum walks (CTQWs) on networks with homogeneous and heterogeneous degree distributions. Using the recently proposed nonlinear Lindblad master equation (NLME), we investigate the dynamics under two decoherence mechanisms: Haken-Strobl and quantum stochastic walk (QSW). Our analysis reveals a striking dichotomy: under Haken-Strobl decoherence the nonlinear contributions precisely cancel, yielding a uniform steady state independent of postselection details under imperfect detection. In stark contrast, QSW decoherence permits postselection in this regime to break dynamical balance on heterogeneous networks, inducing robust localization preferentially at low-degree (peripheral) nodes. Remarkably, this localized state maintains finite quantum coherence. Extending our results to many-body spin systems, we demonstrate that degree heterogeneity similarly stabilizes localization of spin-up excitations in spin-down backgrounds, enhancing entanglement preservation. These findings establish degree heterogeneity and postselection as joint control parameters for engineering quantum transport and localization in dissipative dynamics.
items.authors: Adithya L J, Suraj S Hegde, Chandrakala Meena

items.title: Photon-echo synchronization and quantum state transfer in short quantum links
items.abstract: The short quantum link regime, where the photon travel time $\tau$ is comparable to the emitter lifetime $1/\gamma$, is experimentally relevant but theoretically underexplored: existing few-mode descriptions lose validity as retardation and multimode effects become significant. Using a Delay Differential Equation (DDE) framework that admits exact analytical solutions from the single-mode cavity limit to the multimode waveguide continuum, we show that emitters coupled to a short link spontaneously lock into self-synchronized Rabi oscillations driven by coherent photon echoes, breaking the link's discrete time-displacement symmetry. The resulting spectral structure -- persistent quasi-dark states and vacuum Rabi splitting, including in the superstrong coupling regime -- enables efficient quantum state transfer (QST): benchmarking three protocols across the full $\gamma\tau$ parameter space, we find that STIRAP exploits the quasi-dark-state structure to achieve a quadratic infidelity floor $\mathcal{O}((\gamma\tau)^2)$, outperforming both SWAP (linear error $\mathcal{O}(\gamma\tau)$) and wavepacket engineering for $\gamma\tau \lesssim 1.44$, even in regimes where retardation cannot be neglected. These results establish photon-echo synchronization as an engineering resource for quantum state transfer, with DDE modeling providing the exact analytical predictions needed to design and optimize short-link experiments on current circuit-QED hardware.
items.authors: Hong Jiang, Carlos Barahona-Pascual, Juan Jos\'e Garc\'ia-Ripoll

items.title: A Phase-Space Geometric Measure of Magic in Qubit Systems
items.abstract: Magic -- the resource enabling quantum computational advantage beyond stabilizer circuits -- has a clean phase-space characterization in odd prime dimensions that qubits notoriously lack. We study C(rho), the l_1 distance from a state's discrete Wigner function to the stabilizer polytope, and determine its exact geometry. For a single qubit with Bloch vector r we prove the closed form C = max(0, ||r||_1 - 1)/2, so the maximum is (sqrt(3)-1)/2, attained at the eight face states. For products of single-qubit states, C(rho_1 x ... x rho_n) = 1 + C/2 against the robustness of magic Gamma is frame independent. Within the Wootters frame we prove integer values 1, 2, 1 of the tightness ratio kappa := (Gamma-1)/C for three families in the two-qubit repetition codespace, with explicit certificates. For n-qubit GHZ phase states we prove Gamma = |sin phi| + |cos phi| for all n and C >= 2^(floor(n/2)-1) (|sin phi| + |cos phi| - 1), tight for n = 2 and, by exact linear programming, for n = 3, 4, so kappa decays exponentially. Finally, C is not a magic monotone, so it cannot replace Gamma in distillation bounds.
items.authors: Soumyojyoti Dutta, Tushar

items.title: Non-Gaussianity from superselection rules
items.abstract: The quantum theory of the electromagnetic field enables the description of multiphoton states exhibiting nonclassical statistical properties, often reflected in non-Gaussian phase-space distributions. While non-Gaussianity alone does not fully characterize quantum states, several classifications have been proposed to hierarchize non-Gaussian states according to physically or informationally relevant resources. Here, we provide a physical interpretation of non-Gaussianity and connect it to a computational perspective by showing how a prominent classification-the stellar rank-emerges as a limiting case of the roots of polynomials that univocally represent bosonic states defined with a quantized phase reference, namely the Majorana polynomials. A direct consequence of our results is a revised interpretation of both the stellar rank and non-Gaussianity itself: when superselection rules are properly taken into account, quadrature non-Gaussianity - and nonzero stellar rank - act as witnesses of particle entanglement, rather than being linked with photon addition to Gaussian states as previously assumed. In addition, we show that because the stellar rank depends on a specific choice of coherent states, its relation to computational resources and potential quantum advantage is inherently basis-dependent, being naturally tied to quadrature eigenstates as the computational basis. Motivated by this observation, we generalize the notion of stellar rank to arbitrary computational bases, thereby establishing it as a genuine witness of bosonic resources that may enable quantum advantage.
items.authors: Nicolas Moulonguet, Eloi Descamps, Jos\'e Lorger\'e, Astghik Saharyan, Arne Keller, P\'erola Milman

items.title: Time-frequency Talbot effect as Clifford operations on entangled time-frequency GKP states
items.abstract: The Talbot effect -- a near-field diffraction phenomenon in which a periodic wavefront self-images at regular distances -- can be transposed to the time--frequency domain via the space--time duality between diffraction and dispersive broadening. We exploit this analogy to define the time--frequency (TF) Talbot effect and show that it implements different Clifford operations on TF Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (TF-GKP) qubits (Phys. Rev. 102, 012607), a class of qubit states encoded in the discretised frequency and time-of-arrival degrees of freedom of entangled photon pairs, whose logical basis corresponds to even and odd components of an entangled frequency combs. These states are intrinsically robust against small frequency and temporal displacements, which can be further corrected by linear or nonlinear quantum error-correction schemes. We analyse the role of the comb envelope and peak width relative to the free spectral range, and show that a compromise must be made between the gate fidelity of the Clifford gates induced by TF-Talbot operation and the error-correction capacity of the code. We then demonstrate that the signature of the TF-Talbot effect is directly accessible via the generalised Hong-Ou-Mandel interferometer: all six logical GKP states can be unambiguously distinguished by introducing a frequency shift of half the comb periodicity in one interferometer arm. We conclude with a feasibility analysis based on current experimental technology, identifying the comb finesse as the key figure of merit for both gate performance and correctability. This conclusion extends naturally to quadrature GKP states, where a shear in quadrature phase space is precisely a Talbot effect.
items.authors: Thomas Pousset, Romain Dalidet, Laurent Labont\'e, Nicolas Fabre

items.title: Open-System Adiabatic Quantum Search under Dephasing
items.abstract: Adiabatic quantum algorithms must evolve slowly enough to suppress non-adiabatic transitions while remaining fast enough to be practical. In open systems, this trade-off is reshaped by decoherence. For Hamiltonians subject to dephasing Lindbladians, Avron et al. [Phys. Rev. A 82, 040304(R) (2010)] showed that a unique timetable exists that maximizes the fidelity with a target state. This optimal schedule is characterized by a constant tunneling rate along the adiabatic path. In this work, we revisit their analysis and apply it to the adiabatic Grover search framework, obtaining closed-form expressions for the optimal evolution schedule, the minimum runtime, and the resulting achievable fidelity. Moreover, by invoking an energy-time uncertainty argument, we identify a critical dephasing threshold beyond which further noise-assisted acceleration is prohibited, showing that the apparent advantage of strong dephasing is a Zeno-type stabilization mechanism rather than a conventional algorithmic speedup over unitary Grover search.
items.authors: Afaf El Kalai, Peter J. Eder, Christian B. Mendl

items.title: Weak-Field Expansion: A Time-Closed Solution of Quantum Three-Wave Mixing
items.abstract: We present a systematic derivation of the Heisenberg evolution of a trilinear bosonic Hamiltonian system in presence of a strong drive beyond the standard approximation of a classical, undepleted driving field. We employ a perturbative expansion of the Hamiltonian propagator in orders of the input field amplitudes, as opposed to the standard Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff (BCH) expansion of the propagator in orders of time. Our method automatically provides time-closed expressions; and converges considerably faster than BCH, especially in the regime of high parametric gain because the small parameter it uses is natural to the problem. We obtain the well-known quantum solution for optical parametric amplification of down-conversion simply as the first order of the expansion, and present the rigorous procedure to derive higher order corrections one by one. To demonstrate the utility of higher corrections, we discuss the 2nd order correction to the pump field as an ideal detector of time-energy entanglement in parametric down-conversion.
