We also use the 3rd order correction to calculate the limits on the achievable squeezing with parametric amplification and on the fidelity of quantum state-transfer from one optical mode to another with sum/difference frequency generation, due to the quantum properties of the strong driving field.
items.authors: Hanzhong Zhang, Avi Pe'er

items.title: Photon pairs, squeezed light and the quantum wave mixing effect in a cascaded qubit system
items.abstract: We develop a theoretical description of quantum wave mixing (QWM) in a cascaded waveguide-QED system of two superconducting qubits, where the probe is driven by an external coherent tone and by the resonance fluorescence of a strongly driven source qubit. Starting from the field correlation functions of the source emission, we derive an effective master-equation treatment for the probe and identify the regime in which the incident fluorescence is characterized by anomalous correlations. When the coherent Rayleigh component of the source spectrum is suppressed, the probe equations of motion become equivalent to those for a qubit driven by a coherent tone and broadband squeezed light, although the ligt emitted by the source is non-Gaussian and antibunched. This equivalence implies a selection rule for the peaks of the QWM spectrum, with a strong suppression of sidebands associated with processes involving an odd number of photons taken from the source field. Numerical simulations of the full cascaded two-qubit model for different ratios of radiative decay rates unambiguously confirm the participation of correlated photon pairs in QWM processes. The current research illustrates that the analysis of peak amplitudes can be used to probe photon statistics in the incident nonclassical field.
items.authors: R. D. Ivanovskikh, W. V. Pogosov, A. A. Elistratov, S. V. Remizov, A. Yu. Dmitriev, T. R. Sabirov, A. V. Vasenin, S. A. Gunin, O. V. Astafiev

items.title: Entanglement and photoelectron holography in dissociative photoionization: molecular quantum eraser
items.abstract: In a double-slit experiment with a bipartite system, the visibility of interference fringes depends on the availability of which-way information. Here, we report a Bell-like state of photoelectron and residual ion in the multiphoton dissociative ionization of the D$_2$ molecule. Evidence for entanglement is provided by the correlated emission directions of photoelectron and ion, which is observed using a COLTRIMS reaction microscope. In the presence of this correlation, the holographic interference fringes contained in the photoelectron momentum distributions are suppressed, indicating the existence of which-way information. The interference pattern persists when a single ionic state is populated and thus no which-way information is available. The experimental observations and conclusions are supported by the numerical solution of the electronic-nuclear time-dependent Schr\"odinger equation. Our work demonstrates that coincidence spectroscopy of ions and electrons is a powerful method for studying fundamental concepts of quantum information science within the context of ultrafast light-matter interactions.
items.authors: Sebastian Hell, Paul Winter, Martin G\"arttner, Julian Sp\"athe, Saurabh Mhatre, Dejan B. Milo\v{s}evi\'c, Gerhard G. Paulus, Manfred Lein, Matthias K\"ubel

items.title: Efficient Quantum Fully Homomorphic Encryption
items.abstract: Quantum fully homomorphic encryption (QFHE) enables arbitrary quantum computations on encrypted data, but prior constructions require prohibitive quantum resources--specifically, O(lambda^2) EPR pairs per T-gate evaluation using the Barrington-based approach (DSS16). This paper introduces a unified framework achieving exponential improvement over the generic Barrington-based approach in program length. The central innovation is a novel modular arithmetic program (MA-Program) tailored to learning with errors (LWE) decryption. We show that LWE decryption computes the inner product mod q, a modular inner product that is NOT a symmetric function. Thus, prior symmetric-function optimizations (Sinha's O(n)-state branching programs) do not apply. Our MA-Program tracks partial sums modulus q with state space Z_q requiring O(log q) bits, yielding programs of state count O(lambda) with binary encoding O(log lambda) and length O(lambda log lambda). This reduces the quantum gadget size from O(lambda^2) to O(lambda log^2 lambda) EPR pairs. To achieve a fully classical client, we transfer all quantum resources (EPR preparation, Bell measurements, adaptive error correction) to the server via the MA-Program gadget framework. Clients only perform classical LWE key generation, Pauli key encryption under classical FHE, and no quantum operations; a layered key structure further eliminates circular security assumptions. For parallel computation, we adopt the MBQC framework with flow functions, supporting up to O(log lambda) parallel measurements per layer. This separates offline resource preparation from online adaptive measurement, enabling parallel processing while maintaining deterministic evaluation.
items.authors: Fengxia Liu, Zixian Gong, Kun Tian, Yi Zhang, Zhiming Zheng, Maozhi Xu

items.title: Chaotic Billiard Lasers
items.abstract: This chapter provides an overview of chaotic billiard lasers as a prominent branch of quantum chaos. These lasers offer an ideal experimental platform for demonstrating the principles of quantum chaos within a physical system. We begin by introducing the fundamental principles of chaotic ray dynamics in optical microcavities, where the transition from regular to fully chaotic dynamics fundamentally alters the underlying wavefunctions and lasing properties. A central focus is placed on "chaos-assisted light emission," which serves as a practical manifestation of "chaos-assisted tunneling" -- a hallmark phenomenon in the study of quantum chaos. We discuss both theoretical frameworks and experimental validations, demonstrating how chaotic orbits facilitate the coupling between evanescently localized modes and far-field emission. Furthermore, exploring how the presence of a gain medium influences established results from quantum chaos research remains a fundamental and intriguing problem in physics. To address this, we establish a rigorous and comprehensive derivation of the Maxwell-Bloch equations for two-dimensional microcavity lasers, specifically examining their application to fully chaotic, stadium-shaped billiard lasers. By bridging the gap between nonlinear lasing processes and chaotic wavefunctions, this chapter highlights the unique potential of chaotic billiards for controlling light-matter interactions and shaping the next generation of unconventional coherent light sources.
items.authors: Takahisa Harayama

items.title: A gate-time feasibility analysis of quantum breadth-first search for maximum flow problems
items.abstract: The maximum flow problem asks to find the largest possible flow from a source to a sink in a capacitated network. It arises frequently in scheduling, project selection, and as a core subroutine in broader optimisation tasks. Classically, it can be efficiently solved using Dinic's algorithm, which repeatedly performs breadth-first search (BFS) and blocking flow computations on the graph. As a potential candidate for quantum speedups, these BFS subroutines can be naturally replaced with quantum BFS (qBFS), an instantiation of Grover's search algorithm. In this paper, we evaluate the expected performance of qBFS on standard classical datasets. These instances are too large to be solved directly on current quantum hardware, so we adopt a hybrid benchmarking approach: (i) we run a classical implementation of Dinic's algorithm and isolate the runtime of its BFS subroutines; (ii) we analytically estimate the number of two-qubit gates required to implement qBFS, where we use the classically logged data. Our results indicate that, on every tested instance, matching classical BFS would require two-qubit gate operation times below the current physical record by one to two orders of magnitude for most instances, and by a factor of about 1.3 for the smallest, most favourable ones. Since this comparison uses physical rather than error-corrected gate times, the actual gap is larger still.
items.authors: Andreea-Iulia Lefterovici, Lara Lelakowski, Michael Perk

items.title: Multi-Objective Optimization with Quantum-Annealing-Inspired Algorithms
items.abstract: Combinatorial optimization is widely regarded as a primary application for near-term quantum processors, although a definitive demonstration of the practical quantum advantage remains elusive. Recent studies have reported that both gate-based quantum circuits and quantum annealers can outperform state-of-the-art classical heuristics on multi-objective optimization (MO-MaxCut) problems. However, these studies did not fully account for the substantial pre- and post-processing overheads intrinsic to quantum solvers, leading to incomplete comparisons between quantum and classical approaches. In this work, we re-examine the same benchmark suite using GPU-based quantum-annealing-inspired algorithms (QAIAs), which, analogously to quantum processors, generate probabilistic samples and thus serve as formidable classical contenders. Our results show that QAIAs can sample candidate solutions approximately two orders of magnitude faster than previously studied quantum processors. In terms of end-to-end runtime, QAIAs also surpass industry-leading classical solvers, thereby establishing themselves as the superior performers among the quantum and classical solvers evaluated thus far for the MO-MaxCut instances.
items.authors: Xian-Zhe Tao, Pavel Mosharev, Zhaofeng Su, Man-Hong Yung

items.title: Spectral functions on a quantum computer through system-environment interaction
items.abstract: Spectral functions measured with angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) provide key insight to elucidate the band structure of materials. Comparison with theory requires computing dynamical one-point functions in some equilibrium state, which can be classically challenging. Their measurement on quantum computers poses multiple problems and comes with a large sampling overhead when standard techniques are used. We introduce an efficient way of measuring spectral functions on a quantum computer by directly modeling the interaction of the system with the environment involved in ARPES experiments. We develop quantum circuits whose local expectation values are proportional to the spectral function $A(k,\omega)$ for all momentum $k$ and a specific chosen frequency $\omega$. Although coming with a qubit and two-qubit gate overhead, our approach requires $O(N)$ times less sampling than previous approaches, translating into a factor $O(N)$ faster in runtime, and is particularly adapted to ion-trap quantum computers. The algorithm requires to implement a fermionic Fourier transform (FFT). We write out an efficient gate decomposition for generic radix-$n$ FFT and benchmark it on hardware for radix-$3$ on $27$ qubits. We finally demonstrate our algorithm on a Quantinuum System Model H2 ion-trap system, computing the spectral function on a one-dimensional system of $27$ sites, using $54$ qubits.
items.authors: Etienne Granet, Ramil Nigmatullin, David T. Stephen, Henrik Dreyer

items.title: Clock-transition-enabled long electron spin coherence of telecom emitters in \texorpdfstring{$\mathbf{CeO}_2$}{CeO2}
items.abstract: Rare-earth-ion-doped crystals has emerged as a promising platform for quantum technologies, owing to their narrow telecom-band optical emission, long spin memory, and compatibility with silicon integrated photonic architectures. However, the realization of scalable quantum devices requires host materials with intrinsically dilute spin environments to suppress decoherence. In this context, erbium (Er$^{3+}$) doped cerium oxide (CeO$_2$) is an attractive candidate due to the ultra-low concentration of nuclear spins in the host matrix and its compatibility with silicon-based technologies. Here we perform a comprehensive investigation of the coherence properties of Er$^{3+}$ electron spin qubit in CeO$_2$ via semiclassical as well as detailed cluster correlation expansion simulations. By systematically exploring magnetic field strength, pulse sequences, erbium concentration, and spin temperature, we identify regimes where decoherence from the spin bath is strongly suppressed. Our investigations illustrate that at dilute doping concentration (of the order of 10 ppb) and sub-Kelvin temperatures, operation near clock transitions enables Hahn-echo coherence times to approach the second timescale even at natural isotopic abundance. Importantly, from a practical standpoint, coherence times on the order of $\sim 10$ ms are expected even at liquid helium temperature (about 2 K) for similar concentrations. Moreover, we demonstrate that an additional enhancement can be obtained with conventional multi-$\pi$-pulse dynamical decoupling protocols. Thus, our findings establish Er$^{3+}$ doped CeO$_2$ as a front-runner for realizing spin qubits, quantum memories, and integrated quantum networks.
items.authors: Basanta Mistri, Vishal Ranjan, Siddharth Dhomkar

items.title: Entanglement recovering under local non-positive reduced dynamics
items.abstract: Consider a bipartite quantum system S=AB such that each part interacts only with its local environment. Under such circumstances, one expects that the entanglement between parts A and B does not increase after the time evolution. In fact, this is the case if the reduced dynamics of the system is given by $\mathcal{E}_{A}\otimes \mathcal{E}_{B}$, where $\mathcal{E}_{A}$ and $\mathcal{E}_{B}$ are quantum channels, i.e., completely positive trace-preserving maps. But, the reduced dynamics of the system may be given by a map as $\Psi_{A}\otimes \Psi_{B}$, where $\Psi_{A}$ and $\Psi_{B}$ are local non-positive maps. Then, the entanglement between A and B can exceed its initial value, as was shown in the case studied by Jordan et al. [Phys. Rev. A 76, 022102 (2007)]. In this paper, we first explore the general circumstances under which one can find such cases as they found. Next, we introduce another general procedure which leads to local non-positive maps that exhibit entanglement exceeding. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this apparent entanglement increase in the two above procedures corresponds physically to the retrieval of pre-existing inaccessible entanglement stored across the global system-environment degrees of freedom, rather than genuine generation of the entanglement $\textit{ex nihilo}$.
items.authors: Iman Sargolzahi

items.title: Zeno-Enhanced Probabilistic Error Cancellation with Quantum Error Detection Codes
items.abstract: Probabilistic error cancellation (PEC) is unbiased but suffers exponential sampling overhead set by noise-weighted circuit volume, whereas quantum error-detecting codes (QEDCs) remove many physical faults by stabilizer post-selection but leave an undetectable logical residue. We exploit this complementarity by using post-selection to map physical noise to a weaker accepted logical channel, and then applying PEC only to the residual channel. The resulting feedback-free QED+PEC scheme interleaves Clifford logical blocks, stabilizer measurements, post-selection, and probabilistic cancellation on accepted trajectories, without real-time decoding or active recovery. A key complication is that post-selection correlates accepted fault branches through stabilizer-commutation constraints, so the sparse Pauli-Lindblad factorization underlying bare PEC no longer applies directly. We therefore construct the inverse channel perturbatively: for fixed order $K$, only accepted fault branches up to order $K$ are retained, reducing preprocessing from $2^m$ branches to $O(m^K)$ per block. The order-$K$ protocol cancels the normalized post-selected channel through degree $K$, leaving a per-block error $O(W^{K+1})$ that accumulates at most linearly. For logical GHZ-state preparation with the $[[n,n-2,2]]$ Iceberg code under circuit-level depolarizing noise and ideal stabilizer measurements, first-order QED+PEC reaches $n=200$ physical qubits and lowers sampling overhead by three to four orders of magnitude relative to standard PEC while maintaining $F\simeq0.956$. Syndrome-noise tests show that readout-only flips mainly increase post-selection cost, whereas noisy GHZ-assisted global stabilizer extraction can remove the advantage. This identifies a discrete-Zeno trade-off: cheap detection reshapes the effective channel PEC must invert, rather than simply adding overhead.
items.authors: Yi Yuan, Yuanchen Zhao, Dong E. Liu

items.title: Entropy Concentration and Universal Typicality for Almost i.i.d. Quantum Sources
items.abstract: We establish two concentration principles for almost i.i.d. quantum sources under the weakly almost i.i.d. condition, the broadest condition in the established hierarchy of almost i.i.d. sources. Our results therefore apply also to Wasserstein- and Mazzola-Sutter-Renner almost i.i.d. sources. Weakly almost i.i.d. sources are sequences of multipartite states whose fixed-size marginals converge, on average, to tensor powers of a reference state, while allowing arbitrary global correlations and entanglement. We prove a noncommutative weak law of large numbers for empirical observables, and a universal entropy-concentration principle showing asymptotic concentration on subspaces of exponential dimension governed by the von Neumann entropy of the reference state. These concentration principles provide a unified and conceptually transparent approach to several information-theoretic applications beyond the i.i.d. setting, including direct proofs of universal compression within classes of weakly almost i.i.d. sources sharing a common reference state and asymmetric quantum hypothesis-testing bounds. They also yield concentration of empirical local-measurement frequencies and of empirical averages of commuting single-site observables, with applications to single-site generalized Gibbs ensembles, together with bounds on smooth and spectral entropies.
items.authors: Nilanjana Datta

items.title: Entanglement Growth from Structured Initial States in Many-Body Localized Systems
items.abstract: Understanding how complex entanglement structures emerge is a central problem in quantum many-body physics. Recent work by Zhang et al. [Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020404 (2026)] has considered structured initial states prepared by evolving a product state under a chaotic Hamiltonian for a finite time before quenching to the target Hamiltonian. In this setup, total entanglement entropy growth in many-body localized systems exhibits two distinct regimes, first increasing and then decreasing as the initial entanglement is tuned. In this work, we identify the physical origin of this behavior by analyzing the dynamics of both the R\'enyi entanglement entropy and the Wehrl-R\'enyi entropy in the random-field XXZ model, the latter of which characterizes multipartite entanglement. We show that a similar non-monotonic dependence on the initial entanglement also appears in the net growth of the Wehrl-R\'enyi entropy for product states polarized along the $z$-direction. The first regime is governed by a finite magnetization associated with local integrals of motion, while the second reflects inter-site correlations. In contrast, for product states in the $x/y$-direction, the entanglement growth exhibits a monotonic decay. Our results provide a more fine-grained picture of how distinct initial-state properties shape entanglement dynamics in many-body localized systems.
items.authors: Chen Xu, Pengfei Zhang

items.title: Elfs, transducers and quantum walks
items.abstract: Electric flow sampling (elfs) is a new tool in the quantum walk toolbox and a useful primitive for solving search, sampling and optimization problems on graphs. We refine this tool by showing that there exists a zero-error transducer for implementing elfs. More broadly, we establish a zero-error transducer for reflecting about the intersection of two subspaces, yielding an errorfree transducer version of the effective gap lemma. Building on this result, we obtain improved quantum walk algorithms for estimating effective resistances and span program witness sizes with an optimal error scaling, and for sampling from the random walk arrival distribution, via the composition of many elfs. Using this last algorithm, we obtain an up-to-quadratic quantum speedup for semi-supervised learning on expander graphs.
items.authors: Simon Apers, J\'er\'emie Roland, Yuxin Zhang

items.title: Algebraic Kolmogorov--Arnold representation theorem for quantum measurement
items.abstract: We establish an operational framework connecting the classical Kolmogorov--Arnold (KA) representation theorem to quantum information theory. By introducing and proving an algebraic, bounded-degree polynomial version of the theorem, we demonstrate that any target physical property of an unentangled multi-qubit product state can be exactly decomposed using a finite, fixed set of local ``inner'' observables and a shallow architecture of univariate polynomials. We further analyse the stability of this Quantum Kolmogorov--Arnold (QKA) representation under adversarial perturbations. In stark contrast to the pathological instabilities and severe reparameterisation sensitivities inherent to the classical Kolmogorov--Arnold representation theorem, our algebraic quantum framework exhibits remarkable resilience. We prove that the representation remains stable against bounded physical perturbations acting on the inner measurement operators, and show via the Heisenberg picture that it is inherently immune to adversarial quantum channel attacks acting on the input states.
items.authors: Sviatoslav V. Dzhenzher

items.title: Characterizing the functional role of quantum coherence in energy transfer
items.abstract: Quantum coherence has been suggested to play a role in excitation energy transfer in open quantum systems, yet a quantitative approach to assessing its influence on the transfer process is still missing. Using Nakajima-Zwanzig projection operators, we derive a general memory kernel identity that enables us to characterize and quantify the impact of coherence in the eigenenergy basis on a generalized rate of energy transfer. Applying our approach to the electronic dynamics of a dimer coupled to a structured phonon bath, we demonstrate how quantum coherence acts to modulate energy transfer.
items.authors: Hallmann \'Oskar Gestsson, Alexandra Olaya-Castro

items.title: A thermodynamic analysis of nonsecular master equations, beyond strict energy conservation and Gibbs equilibrium state
items.abstract: We present a systematic thermodynamic analysis of nonsecular GKLS master equations. When some energy transitions in the system are comparable with the dissipative rate, the secular approximation is not valid, and the positivity of the dynamics must be ensured via other approximations. The dynamics then presents features reminiscent from strong coupling to the environment: e.g. the equilibrium state with an environment at thermal equilibrium is not a Gibbs state of the local system Hamiltonian and the dynamics couples energy coherences and populations. Nonetheless, we build a unified, consistent thermodynamic framework for those dynamics. We focus on two approximations beyond the full secular approximation (the local and the more accurate geometric-arithmetic approximations), and then employ systematic perturbation theory on microscopic expressions for the first and second law of thermodynamics which relate irreversibility to the increase of system-environment correlations. We show that, in spite of the weak system-bath coupling, the system-bath interaction energy participates to the energy balance, and is directly linked to the Lamb-shift Hamiltonian. We compare this microscopic entropy production with the definition based on the contractivity of the reduced system dynamics (Spohn inequality). We show that, unlike for secular master equations, the two entropy production rates differ because of the presence of non-vanishing stationary coherences in the energy eigenbasis. However, in the case of a single thermal bath, the difference is purely transient, and no work can be cyclically extracted from the steady-state despite its non-Gibbs form. Finally, we illustrate our results with simple examples, clarifying and completing the thermodynamic picture of Markovian dynamics in the quantum regime.
items.authors: Mohamed Boubakour, Talia Szikman, Cyril Elouard

items.title: Helical Dirac Current with Local Coupling to a Chiral Potential
items.abstract: We show that a propagating electron wave in the lowest cylindrical channel carries a spin-resolved helical conserved current, and connect this current texture to its local chiral coupling. In a weakly relativistic positive-energy Dirac projection, the two sectors have the same azimuthally symmetric charge density and opposite circulation superposed on longitudinal flow, even though their nonrelativistic orbital harmonic is $l=0$. The current is radially distributed and extends into the evanescent tail. A scalar screw potential couples these modes through a derived vertex expressed by the \emph{chiral current overlap}, $\mathcal J_\chi$. Both spatial textures determine the coupling: the environmental radial profile weights the electronic circulation, while the screw harmonic selects correlated changes of spin sector and longitudinal momentum. For a uniform static harmonic, elastic energy conservation makes the first-order spin-flip amplitude vanish within the same transverse mode. Environmental energy exchange is therefore required to activate these selected channels. The same current overlap supplies the spatial kernel for heliciton-assisted inelastic scattering in a companion study and for a subsequent transport treatment of chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS).
items.authors: Ju Gao, Fang Shen

items.title: Engineering entanglement and transport in interacting quantum walks with tailored potentials
items.abstract: Controlling the interplay between particle propagation and quantum correlation generation is a central challenge in quantum transport. Here, we investigate two distinguishable continuous-time quantum walkers evolving on parallel one-dimensional lattices, interacting via distance-dependent potentials. While on-site interactions reproduce the typical bosonic behaviour, extending the interaction to a linear potential over multiple neighbors introduces controlled Bloch-like oscillations and shifts the bound-pair regime to stronger couplings. More generally, we explore a Coulomb-like interaction parameterized by strength, spatial scaling, and decay rate. This reveals a rich dynamical diagram including four distinct regimes: (i) a high-entropy, oscillatory regime akin to a linear potential; (ii) a strongly localized, bound-pair regime; (iii) a novel intermediate regime combining near-ballistic spreading with strong correlations; and (iv) a weakly interacting, free-propagation regime. Notably, regime (iii) achieves concurrent optimization of transport efficiency and entanglement, offering a sweet spot for correlated quantum dynamics. Our results provide a tool for designing interaction-engineered quantum walks with potential applications in quantum information processing and simulations.
items.authors: Gaia Forghieri, Matteo G. A. Paris

items.title: Quantum circuit knitting using a weak-coupling approximation
items.abstract: We present a method for performing distributed quantum computing with controlled approximations for circuits that are weakly coupled via a single qubit. Exact distributed quantum computing requires exponential classical information to reconstruct the quantum process. However, we show how the classical cost is reduced to polynomial if the quantum procedure can be partitioned between a qubit that is weakly coupled to the other qubits. We demonstrate our method for a layered circuit based on the circuits used for the quantum approximate optimization algorithm.
items.authors: John P. T. Stenger, Daniel Gunlycke, Nikos Chrisochoides

items.title: Emergence of Gaussian entanglement and non-Gaussianity in high-harmonic generation driven by bright squeezed light
items.abstract: High harmonic generation (HHG) is a highly nonlinear optical process in which radiation from a strong driving field is up-converted into its high-order harmonics. In atomic systems, this nonlinearity manifests itself through the intensity scaling of the emitted harmonics with the driving field strength. Despite the highly nonlinear nature of HHG, when the driving field is prepared in a classical Gaussian state and atomic depletion remains negligible, the quantum statistical properties of the generated harmonics retains classical Gaussian quantum statistics. Driving HHG with bright squeezed vacuum (BSV) light challenges this paradigm, as its enhanced field fluctuations can modify the statistical properties of the generated harmonics. In this work, we investigate the conditions under which BSV-driven HHG gives rise to non-classical Gaussian states, and identify the regimes where this Gaussian description breaks down. For bichromatic driving by a strong coherent field at frequency $\omega$ and a perturbative BSV field at $2\omega$, the even-harmonic response is approximately linear in the BSV quadrature, leading to non-classical multimode Gaussian entanglement in the harmonic field. We show that this state can be described as a distributed collective squeezed mode over the even-harmonic manifold, and characterize its covariance matrix, entanglement structure, and quantum teleportation fidelity as an operational benchmark. Our results highlight the potential of non-classically driven HHG as a platform for engineering Gaussian and non-Gaussian states of light in the extreme ultraviolet regime.
items.authors: J. Rivera-Dean, M. Even-Tzur, M. F. Ciappina, C. Granados, O. Cohen, P. Stammer

items.title: Initial-state-dependent dephasing effect in non-Hermitian Su-Schrieffer-Heeger models
items.abstract: Understanding the dynamical evolution of non-Hermitian systems under external dissipation is essential for devising realistic non-Hermitian quantum devices that surpass the capabilities of their Hermitian counterparts. Dephasing, a major realistic dissipation, has an impact on non-Hermitian systems that remains largely unexplored. Here, we focus on finite-sized non-Hermitian Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) lattice models with alternating gain and loss in real space and examine the dynamical evolution of the trace distance under pure dephasing. By tuning system parameters, this model supports phases with either parity-time or anti-parity-time symmetries, enabling us to explore the dephasing effect across different non-Hermitian symmetry regimes within a single platform. While the trace distance exhibits distinct dynamical behaviors across the different phases in the absence of dephasing, its response to dephasing is largely symmetry-independent but instead initial-state dependent. By varying the initial states, we find that dephasing affects the trace distance in two qualitatively different ways. For initial states that differ only in their coherences, dephasing accelerates the decay of the trace distance, destroying the phase information in much the same way as in Hermitian systems. In contrast, for initial states that differ only in their populations, strong dephasing can partially or completely stabilize the trace distance over a wide transient regime before its eventual decay. We attribute these metastable stabilization phenomena to the alternating gain and loss in the system and confirm their absence in Hermitian counterparts. Our findings reveal the intricate dynamical response of non-Hermitian SSH models to dephasing, thereby facilitating their potential applications.
items.authors: Tao Min, Junjie Liu

items.title: Multipartite quantum synchronization in driven-dissipative spin networks
items.abstract: Traditional studies of quantum synchronization in finite-dimensional spin systems usually focus on entrainment of a single spin to an external drive, leaving mutual synchronization among multiple spins poorly understood. We investigate mutual quantum synchronization across bipartite and tripartite spin architectures in a driven-dissipative cavity-coupled quantum Rabi network in the dispersive adiabatic regime. Inspired by the Kuramoto model of classical phase synchronization, we introduce a phase-space measure of quantum synchronization using the first angular moments of Husimi-Q phase distributions. To compare the collective phase localization with reduced-subsystem contributions and local individual phase locking, we construct a bipartite and tripartite synchronization gap. For two spins, the steady-state synchronization gap is negative. This reflects that the relative phase is localized more strongly than the individual spin phases can account for, signaling mutual synchronization beyond independent entrainment by the drive. For three spins in a triangular network, the synchronization gap is positive in the parameter regime studied, i.e., the collective three-body localization is bounded by the pairwise measures. Our results underscore that quantum phase synchronization strongly depends upon network topology and establish the phase-sensitive synchronization gaps as an effective diagnostic for multipartite phase correlations in open quantum systems.
items.authors: Jatin Ghildiyal, Shubhrangshu Dasgupta, Asoka Biswas

items.title: Improving device-independent quantum key distribution protocols through multiple routed Bell tests
items.abstract: Device-independent quantum key distribution (DI-QKD) guarantees security with a minimal set of assumptions about the experimental setup. The challenge posed by its implementation could be tackled using routed Bell tests with entanglement swapping, or distant Bell state measurement (BSM) units. However, practical distances still require local tests with close-to-ideal violations or BSMs with high efficiency. We propose a DI-QKD protocol based on a multi-port BSM, and multiple sources and measurement devices, where in each round, routed tests are performed on randomly selected local devices. The violation of local Bell tests is checked even for the subset of rounds where successful BSM projections are achieved. By requiring that this violation remain consistent with the overall average, we specifically show improvements in the critical efficiencies of a three-port BSM, of up to $6\%$ in absolute terms for high visibilities. Without ideal violations, we also achieve arbitrarily small efficiencies with arbitrarily many BSM ports. Our approach enables long-distance DI-QKD, with access to highly efficient loophole-free routing setups, and multiple local tests (possibly imperfect) with very high local detection efficiencies. Remarkably, it avoids the use of quantum memories and the need for long-range Bell tests. Finally, we extend the concept of routing to dimension witnesses, where qubit-bounded sources send states to the BSM. This can be seen as a semi-device-independent extension of the aforementioned protocol.
items.authors: Sujan Vijayaraj, Mauro Paternostro

items.title: Signatures of the circular Unruh effect in electric and magnetic dipole transitions of multilevel atoms
items.abstract: The circular Unruh effect is the excitation of a detector moving along a planar circular trajectory within an electromagnetic vacuum. We demonstrate that the magnetic dipole transitions in an atom, acting as the detector, dominate the electric dipole transitions. Our analysis of both free-space and cavity schemes shows that the sensitivity to the circular Unruh effect can be maximized by balancing the minimization of mode volume against the resulting decrease in mode density. Moreover, we propose a novel measurement scheme that uses the atom's multilevel structure to suppress the spontaneous emission rate, thereby enabling the experimental detection of the circular Unruh effect.
items.authors: Gregor Janson, Fabio Di Pumpo, Lorenz Thoma, Maxim A. Efremov

items.title: A Validation Framework for Quantum Simulation of Spin Dynamics against Inelastic Neutron Scattering and Classical Simulation
items.abstract: Establishing quantum simulations as reliable tools for materials research requires quantitative validation against experiments and, where available, classical many-body calculations. For dynamical spin response, such validation remains challenging because experiment, classical simulation, and quantum simulation do not produce the same native observables. This challenge is increasingly relevant as quantum simulation protocols for dynamical response progress from theory to hardware-level benchmarking against neutron scattering data. The longer-term goal is to extend validation to classically intractable regimes accessible through future fault-tolerant implementations. Here, we develop a cross-pipeline validation framework for quantum simulation of dynamical spin response, using inelastic neutron scattering and classical many-body simulation as complementary experimental and computational anchors. The framework brings these pipelines to common momentum- and energy-resolved comparison levels through explicit forward and inverse observable maps, propagates uncertainty via covariance matrices or resampling, tests robustness to structured distortion, and evaluates agreement using a hierarchy of complementary metric families. It distinguishes stochastic uncertainty from robustness-induced distortion, carries both through the comparison chain, and uses the resulting metric-level uncertainty and distortion information to support layered validation at the pipeline, solver, and model levels. We also introduce actuator-aware feedback logic to improve agreement without obscuring the physical origin of any remaining mismatch. We close by outlining future extensions of this methodology, including upstream uncertainty and distortion modeling, adaptive feedback, asymmetric validation beyond full classical benchmarking, fault-tolerant workflows, and community infrastructure for reproducible validation.
items.authors: Gilles Buchs, Elaine Wong, Anshumitra Baul, Kathleen E. Hamilton, Arnab Banerjee, Stephan Eidenbenz, G\'abor B. Hal\'asz, Paul Kairys, Keerthi Kumaran, Thomas Maier, Thomas Naughton III, Elijah Pelofske, Vincent Russo, Allen Scheie, Yigit Subasi, D. Alan Tennant, Akram Touil, Travis S. Humble, Andrew T. Sornborger

items.title: Magic Gate Teleportation: Structure, Useful Resource States, and Simpler Feedforward
items.abstract: Quantum gate teleportation is a key technique in fault-tolerant quantum computation that uses resource states to implement logical gates. Here, we develop a theory of magic gate teleportation (MGT), a form of quantum gate teleportation that uses non-stabilizer resource states to implement non-Clifford unitary gates on arbitrary input states without revealing information about those states. This setting is motivated by the canonical approach to implementing logical non-Clifford gates in fault-tolerant quantum computation. We uncover a hidden structure within MGT---after backpropagating the Pauli measurements, MGT protocols can be viewed as encoding the input state into a stabilizer code heralded by the measurement outcomes, followed by a logical non-Clifford gate. Using this structure, we construct MGT protocols for any resource state obtained by applying commuting Pauli rotations to a stabilizer state, and provide an efficient algorithm for synthesizing their circuit implementations. Conversely, we prove that directly useful single-qubit resource states are necessarily Clifford-equivalent to diagonal states, and establish the same constraint for multi-qubit resource states used in a broad class of MGT protocols. In particular, the output state distilled from the $[\![5, 1, 3]\!]$ protocol is not directly useful for any MGT protocols, though it can be probabilistically converted into directly useful states. Finally, we identify conditions under which the feedforward operators can be implemented by Pauli operators, shedding light on the paradigm of algorithmic fault tolerance and simplifying the feedforward operations needed for quantum computing.
items.authors: Yunzhe Zheng, Allen Zang, Aleksander Kubica

items.title: Auditing Syndrome-to-Decoder Mappings for Repetition, Surface, CSS, and Digitized-GKP Interfaces
items.abstract: Quantum error-correction experiments increasingly require a verified interface between measured syndrome bits and decoder-native correction requests. We report a four-branch syndrome-to-decoder mapping audit spanning a five-data-qubit repetition code, a distance-five surface Z-check interface, a compact Steane CSS benchmark, and a digitized-GKP proxy. For the surface interface, an independent noiseless interpreter verifies 40/40 single-X syndrome columns and data-bit round trips, while a reversed-register negative control fails for all 40 targets. Sampled hardware and local-noise streams are then analyzed with exact binary minimum-weight representatives to separate mapping validity from noisy localization. The results establish a narrow interface-conformance claim, not a decoder benchmark, threshold estimate, or logical-QEC demonstration.
items.authors: Dennis Delali Kwesi Wayo, Chinonso Onah, Rodrigo Alves Dias, Leonardo Goliatt, Sven Groppe

items.title: Beyond Calabrese-Cardy Scaling: Exceptional-Point Sensitivity and the de Sitter RT Surface
items.abstract: Entanglement entropy at one-dimensional criticality typically follows the Calabrese--Cardy scaling. In the non-Hermitian critical free-fermion systems studied here, however, we find an additional interval-independent contribution $S_{\rm res}=\log(\Delta L)$, which allows the entropy to remain sensitive to energy gaps below the finite-size scale, $\Delta<1/L$. We refer to this term as the residual entropy. To understand its infrared origin, we examine finite-depth non-unitary continuous multiscale entanglement renormalization on a ring. Terminating the critical RG circuit before its singular final layer leaves a two-site infrared state. We calculate the entropy of this state directly from its correlation matrix and recover the same \(\log(\Delta L)\) dependence. The emergent de Sitter geometry provides a complementary geometric interpretation: extremal curves associated with different boundary intervals extend to a common infrared endpoint, suggesting how the entanglement retained there can contribute equally to their entropies.
items.authors: Kuang-Hung Chou

items.title: A geometric framework for spin relaxation
items.abstract: Spin relaxation is conventionally described by two independent phenomenological rates - longitudinal ($R_1$) and transverse ($R_2$) - whose separation obscures a deeper structural unity. Here we develop a geometric framework in which dissipation is represented by a single covariant relaxation tensor acting in Liouville space, from which $R_1$ and $R_2$ emerge as complementary projections. This tensor structure is not merely formal but is experimentally accessible through pulse sequences that probe noncommuting directions in spin space. Using hyperpolarized $^{13}C$ spins in diamond with nitrogen-vacancy centers, we show that commuting pulse trains yield effective relaxation matrices that are approximately diagonal, while noncommuting sequences produce off-diagonal components that vary with transmitter frequency offset and pulse ordering, providing evidence that relaxation is a directional process governed by a tensor rather than a pair of scalar rates. Complementary measurements of geometric phase demonstrate that noncommuting dynamics introduce ordering-dependent effects that are separable from dissipation, consistent with the interpretation of relaxation as geometric transport on the state manifold. This framework unifies Bloch, Redfield, and Lindblad descriptions within a coordinate-independent formulation and provides a natural language for relaxation in driven, anisotropic, and non-equilibrium spin systems.
items.authors: Sophia N. Fricke, Kieren A. Harkins, Ashok Ajoy, Jeffrey A. Reimer

items.title: Spatial-Order Hierarchy of Time-Dependent Exchange-Correlation Potential
items.abstract: Exact time-dependent density-functional theory (DFT) separates the exchange-correlation potential into interaction and kinetic-correlation components, but the structural relation between them remains unclear. We establish a representability constraint based on the off-diagonal expansion of the one-electron reduced density matrix (1RDM) relative to a chosen reference dynamics. A non-zero linear off-diagonal term of the 1RDM generates a current density beyond the representable space of the reference, while a nontrivial quadratic off-diagonal structure activates the kinetic-correlation component. The resulting hierarchy provides a criterion for assessing, from the spatial locality of electronic correlation, whether a given exchange-correlation functional or a more general electron-correlation approximation remains adequate. In a one-dimensional two-electron correlation quench, retaining the exact interaction component while setting the kinetic component to zero suppresses the density broadening of the exact evolution. These results establish a spatial-order hierarchy among the force components governing the density dynamics and provide an exact constraint for the construction and assessment of nonadiabatic approximations.
items.authors: Naoki Negishi

items.title: Contextuality in Sequential State Discrimination
items.abstract: Generalized contextuality is known to be required in optimal strategies for quantum state discrimination protocols. More recently, sequential discrimination tasks have been studied; n players attempt to determine in which state a qubit was prepared, in such a way that they all have a finite probability of success. We consider the extent to which contextuality plays a role in sequential versions of both unambiguous and minimum error discrimination. In the standard nonsequential case where n = 1, we use the COPE formalism to demonstrate that the presence of contextuality is guaranteed not only for the optimal measurement, but for a specific set of nonoptimal measurements as well. In the sequential case n > 1, we show that the presence of contextuality depends on which states are prepared, and on the protocol (unambiguous or minimum error) selected.
items.authors: Nyan Raess, Farid Shahandeh

items.title: Constant-round quantum advantage in communication complexity for total functions
items.abstract: We show that there exists a total function for which there is a polynomial gap between the randomized and the constant-round quantum communication complexity. Previously, such a separation was known only for quantum protocols using polynomially many rounds.
items.authors: Atsuya Hasegawa, Fran\c{c}ois Le Gall

items.title: Fluctuation-dissipation structure of quantum geometry
items.abstract: Geometry of quantum states is a fundamental research area with applications ranging from topological materials in condensed matter to variational algorithms in quantum information. Due to their relative simplicity, pure states are often studied, while mixed states are generally needed, for instance to have nonzero temperatures or other statistical mixtures. Mixed-state geometry, however, is much more challenging and has so far lacked any overall structure that relates distance and curvature, like the K\"ahler structure does for pure states. This work introduces that missing structure. We show that it has the physical meaning of fluctuation-dissipation---by identifying distance with fluctuations and curvature with linear response---and becomes the known structure for pure states, but is non-K\"ahler otherwise. This paints a simple picture that unifies fluctuation-dissipation and geometry of quantum states. It also applies on parameter spaces, as encountered in condensed matter or estimation theory. Our picture implies that the geometry contains all linear responses and fluctuations, proves the usual fluctuation-dissipation relation, explains that quantum geometry is present in any sum rule, and allows one to geometrically characterize generic transport behaviors.
items.authors: Per Moosavi

items.title: Quantum Mechanics as a Relativistic Statistical Theory: A Mass-Shell Factorisation Approach
items.abstract: Spinor structure is usually introduced as part of relativistic quantum theory. We show that its underlying algebra can instead emerge without quantisation from a covariant statistical description of a massive relativistic particle subject to an explicit finite-dimensional linear factorisation of the complete massive mass-shell constraint motivated by requiring the theory retain both sheets of the massive mass shell. A finite-dimensional factorisation of the complete mass-shell constraint, linear in all four momentum components, forces a Clifford algebra. In (3+1) dimensions its minimal complex representation is four-dimensional, while each on-shell factor selects a rank-two sector; in this representation statistical completeness requires an arbitrary $2\times2$ matrix distribution within that sector before quantisation. Projecting the Weyl-ordered matrix Liouvillian gives relativistic transport while preserving all internal populations and coherences. For universal deformations on flat canonical phase space satisfying the stated covariance, matrix-neutrality, homogeneity and associativity assumptions, the resulting product is the matrix Weyl--Moyal product. Its parameter has dimensions of action and, when identified with $\hbar$, supplies the scale of physical spin-$\tfrac12$. Requiring all-order constraint preservation gives a vanishing star commutator, while preservation of the selected star-spectral sector yields the two-sided Dirac--Wigner equations. Our central conclusion is therefore that relativistic mass-shell factorisation supplies spinor structure, while completion of the constraint-preservation hierarchy within the stated deformation class leads to the Weyl--Moyal phase-space formulation of quantum mechanics.
items.authors: Mark Everitt

items.title: A Backend-Agnostic MWIS Kernel for Stochastic Unit Commitment with Neutral-Atom Hardware Validation
items.abstract: Quantum hardware is beginning to address structured combinatorial optimisation, but two steps still block practical use: mapping real operational models onto hardware-compatible instances, and converting noisy hardware output back into feasible decisions. Here we introduce a backend-agnostic computational interface that compiles the discrete decision layer of stochastic unit commitment into a move-based maximum-weight independent set (MWIS) problem, while retaining continuous dispatch and feasibility recovery in the classical computational layer. We validate the approach in a green hydrogen scheduling setting and deploy it on the QuEra Aquila neutral-atom quantum processor. This is the first end-to-end industrial scheduling workflow that connects real operational decisions to programmable neutral-atom hardware through a solver-agnostic MWIS representation. Across a 15-day hardware campaign on 50-node instances, hardware-generated solutions after classical refinement match or exceed the dispatch margins obtained from exact MWIS on every day. When scaling to 144 nodes, encoding quality remains stable, while the probability that the full atom array survives, rather than graph embedding, emerges as the dominant bottleneck to further scaling. Together, these results establish a hardware-compatible computational pathway toward larger problem scales, and lay the groundwork for exploring regimes in which exact classical optimisation may no longer scale efficiently.
items.authors: Jiying Chen, Min Lin, Jingwei Wen, Zhihong Zhang, Chuixiong Wu

items.title: Q-Edge: Symmetry-Reduced Quantum Simulation of Structured Extreme Dependence
items.abstract: High-dimensional simulation of multivariate extremes is fundamentally limited by the combinatorial complexity of dependence, often more than by the scarcity of extreme observations. We show that symmetry admits a lossless orbit-space representation that preserves structured extreme dependence while replacing an exponentially large dependence space with a compact set of symmetry classes. Based on this principle, we develop Q-Edge (Quantum Extreme Dependence Engine), a symmetry-reduced quantum framework that operates directly in orbit space, enabling scalable simulation and digital twins of structured extreme systems. By transferring symmetry into the data representation rather than the quantum circuit, Q-Edge allows unconstrained quantum generative models to exploit dramatically reduced state spaces. For a 30-dimensional problem, approximately 1.6 million angular states collapse to 256 orbit states, reducing the required quantum representation from about 21 qubits to 8. Our results establish a general computational principle for scalable quantum simulation of structured extreme dependence.
items.authors: Hongrui Zhang, Paolo Recchia, Ying Chen

items.title: Conditional Error Exponents of Probabilistic Quantum Resource Distillation
items.abstract: Quantum resource distillation converts imperfect resource states into highly resourceful targets and is a central task in quantum information processing. When distillation is probabilistic, unfavorable outcomes may be discarded and the quality of the output is evaluated conditioned on success, leading to a notion of reliability that differs from the deterministic setting. Here we study the conditional error exponents of probabilistic quantum resource distillation under approximately resource-nongenerating instruments and derive its general connection to the postselected composite quantum hypothesis testing against the corresponding set of free states. This reduction leads naturally to scale-invariant projective distinguishability measures and provides finite-blocklength bounds for a broad class of resource theories. We apply the framework to entanglement, coherence, and magic. For entanglement and magic, we obtain exact zero-rate asymptotic characterizations of the conditional error exponent in terms of regularized projective distinguishability, while for coherence we derive general finite-blocklength and asymptotic bounds. For representative entangled and magic states, the resulting quantities can be evaluated analytically and reveal regimes in which postselection yields a strictly larger conditional error exponent than deterministic distillation. Furthermore, we also show that the conditional error exponents for probabilistic entanglement distillation under a strictly positive success probability constraint are smaller than those with no constraints on the success probability.
items.authors: Xian Shi

items.title: Finite Realizations and Effective Memory in Nonlinear Quantum Filtering
items.abstract: Nonlinear dynamics generate non-Gaussian states and operations, but they also make continuously monitored quantum systems difficult to track. A quantum filter performs this task by compressing a noisy measurement record into a set of evolving variables that predict future observables. For Gaussian dynamics, this compression is exact and finite. In nonlinear systems, conventional moment equations generally expand without bound, but the failure of one representation does not prove that every finite description is impossible. Here we formulate quantum filtering as a realization problem for general quantum input--output maps. We introduce the linearized observable Hankel operator $K_O$, which maps changes in the past measurement record to changes in a future conditional observable. Any finite-dimensional smooth filter forces $K_O$ to have finite rank, so infinite rank provides a coordinate-independent proof that no exact finite-dimensional filter exists. Applied to single-mode polynomial bosonic systems under continuous quadrature monitoring, this yields a sharp boundary: Gaussian dynamics and the measurement-aligned Conditional Momentum Moment class admit finite realizations, whereas dynamics outside these classes produce infinitely many response directions and admit no finite-dimensional smooth exact filter. Exact impossibility, however, need not imply large practical complexity. The singular values of $K_O$ quantify how many response directions matter at a chosen local accuracy, defining the effective memory of an observable. For the Kerr and Duffing oscillators, these singular values decay rapidly despite infinite exact rank, showing that infinite exact memory can coexist with low finite-accuracy complexity. The framework therefore separates exact realizability from effective complexity in nonlinear quantum filtering.
items.authors: Jacob Emerson

items.title: Low-cost algorithm-to-execution framework for surface-code quantum computing
items.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing is progressing from demonstrations of individual logical components toward the execution of useful quantum algorithms on large-scale error-corrected processors. Realizing this transition requires co-design across algorithms, fault-tolerant implementations, and hardware resources. Here we develop an algorithm-to-execution framework for low-cost surface-code quantum computing that carries the structure of a computation from hierarchical logical descriptions to circuit-specific spatial organization, non-Clifford resource planning, and physical resource evaluation. We apply the framework to twenty benchmark circuits spanning seven algorithm families and to a hierarchically reconstructed application-scale elliptic-curve discrete-logarithm workload. Under the stated error and resource-supply models, combining circuit-specific layouts with hybrid non-Clifford implementation reduces space--time volume by up to 12.70x relative to an all-synthesis Litinski fast-block baseline. Circuit-specific layouts reduce both modeled runtime and space--time volume in eighteen benchmarks, while the remaining two retain the fast layout. These results show that the physical cost of fault-tolerant computation emerges from the interaction between algorithm structure, error-corrected implementation, and hardware organization rather than from aggregate logical resource counts alone.
items.authors: Yunxin Tang, Zixuan Huo, Junxiang Huang, Zhou You, Zhirao Wang, Zhenai Ding, Yumeng Zeng, Yangyu Lu, Yiming Huang, Zongkang Zhang, Haipeng Xie, Ruipeng Xing, Qiming Ding, Ying Li, Jinzhao Sun, Xiao Yuan, Yuan Yao

items.title: Quantum ensembles as waves on state space
items.abstract: A quantum ensemble contains preparation weights that are lost in its average density operator. We show how optimal decisions read these weights as a wave on projective state space. Varying the input prior sweeps a surface of fixed Born overlap through the ensemble; the resulting response propagates according to the geometry of pure states and reconstructs their distribution in every finite dimension. Conditional preparations can fix this wave through contact, selecting the ensemble at a steering boundary. Positive propagation gives exact biased-qubit solutions and explicit parent measurements for noisy channels. When measurement records are combined, their state directions are averaged and the wave acquires a source whose growth measures the lost discrimination advantage. Preparation, inference and noise can thus be understood as operations on the same recoverable distribution, linking quantum correlations to measurement resolution.
items.authors: Yu-Xuan Zhang, Leong-Chuan Kwek, Jing-Ling Chen

items.title: Detectability of Post-Quantum Correlations in Symmetry-Restricted Bell Scenarios
items.abstract: Searches for post-quantum correlations depend on two distinct ingredients: how abundant such correlations are in the underlying correlation space and how efficiently the chosen representation preserves their distinguishability from quantum correlations. We quantify these effects by introducing the popularity rate and the projection acceptance, whose product defines the search performance. We apply these concepts in binary-outcome Bell scenarios with symmetry-related sites, using the CHSH and pyramid representations. Particular attention is paid to the distinction between exchange-symmetric synchronous correlations and correlations satisfying only exchange symmetry. In the synchronous quantum sector, the common-vector representation follows automatically from synchrony, whereas exchange symmetry alone defines a substantially larger correlation space. We show that this distinction can qualitatively change the effectiveness of a projected search: the pyramid representation, which retains substantial discriminatory power in the synchronous sector, has no discriminatory power when only exchange symmetry is imposed. Our results provide a simple framework for assessing and comparing searches for post-quantum correlations.
items.authors: Marek Gazdzicki, Francesco Giacosa

items.title: Exact damping-basis continued fractions for few-atom lasers: collective correlations beyond second-order cumulant closure
items.abstract: We combine the Briegel--Englert damping basis of a lossy cavity mode with the permutation-invariant Liouville basis of \(N\) identical, incoherently pumped two-level emitters. The resulting Liouvillian is exactly block tridiagonal in a single radial field index, with atomic blocks of dimension \(\binom{N+3}{3}\). The stationary state follows from a matrix continued fraction whose asymptotic closure is a linear matrix equation that we prove to be uniquely solvable throughout the dissipative regime \(A>0\), and the same construction in the coherence-one sector yields the emission spectrum. The method is validated against direct diagonalization, weak-pump perturbation theory, and closed-system spectra, reaches \(N=16\) in tens of seconds in the few-quanta regime, and has a quantified precision limit at large photon number. We use it to derive an exact two-atom photon-balance identity that isolates the cavity-induced pair coherence and relates it to a singlet--triplet population difference; to establish an exact pump-order hierarchy of connected correlations for a zero-temperature cavity and a parity property of the minimal collective-spin sector; and to benchmark the second-order cumulant closure used in few-emitter laser theory, which we find to be semi-quantitative for the photon number but to predict the wrong sign of the inter-emitter coherence above inversion. In a good-cavity regime the exact solution shows near-Poissonian statistics and strong line narrowing for two and three emitters.
items.authors: Stephan Hartmann

items.title: Exact Local Optimality Does Not Compose: Invariant Simplices and the Complexity of Chronological Stochastic Realization
items.abstract: Probabilistic models constructed separately for different families of experiments are often expected to share one latent dynamical system. We formalize the resulting shared finite partial-realization problem as \emph{chronological stochastic realization}: deciding whether finite partial response specifications admit a \emph{chronological shared stochastic model} (CSSM) within a prescribed state budget. A CSSM is a normalized probabilistic automaton in which multiple named preparations share stochastic transitions and a single terminal effect. Local and tagged-static optimality do not compose at fixed dimension. For every $k,L\ge1$, we construct finite menus with local and tagged-static widths $k$, yet chronological width exactly $k(L+1)$, isolating compatibility with word composition as an independent state resource. In the ordinary-rank-tight calibrated regime, an exact $k$-state CSSM exists if and only if a $(k-1)$-simplex contains the root responses, lies in the response polytope, and is forward invariant under every primitive affine update. For finite rational menus, deciding whether an exact CSSM with at most $K$ states exists is $\exists\mathbb{R}$-complete. The promise problem distinguishing zero minimax defect from defect at least $\epsilon$ is $\mathsf{PromiseNP}$-complete, with hardness already holding for inverse-polynomial $\epsilon$. Both classifications hold over a fixed five-letter alphabet on instances where every individual menu and the tagged independent-query static relaxation have exact minimum state count $K$. They also hold with Boolean terminal effects, and the robust soundness gap remains valid over all effects in $[0,1]^d$. Thus chronological compatibility remains computationally hard even when the local and tagged-static optima are fixed at $K$.
items.authors: Yixin Zhao

items.title: Quantum Simulation of Dissipative Non-Markovian Coupled Classical Oscillators
items.abstract: We present a quantum algorithm for simulating classical oscillator networks characterized by non-Markovian dissipation and time-varying material properties, extending recent speedups for undamped harmonic systems to viscoacoustic and viscoelastic media. We embed the history-dependent dynamics into a Markovian state space governed by a non-Hermitian operator by approximating memory kernels through a Prony series. We then use linear combination of Hamiltonian simulation to estimate the instantaneous kinetic and potential energy for a subset of oscillators at time $t$ within error $\epsilon$ using a number of queries to the oscillator system that scales as $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\alpha_{\rm tot} t/\epsilon)$, where $\alpha_{\rm tot}$ is polynomial in the strength of the dissipation, spring constants, inverse masses, and sparsity of the connections in the network. We further show that this energy estimation task is in the worst-case classically hard (i.e., a corresponding decision problem is $\mathsf{BQP}$-complete), even in the presence of strong dissipation. For time-dependent materials, we show that changes in material properties appear as effective dissipation or growth in the energy representation. Additionally, we prove the infeasibility of exponential quantum advantages in locally coupled topologies through a novel form of Lieb-Robinson-like bounds that apply to differential equations. This allows our quantum algorithms to provide quartic speedups for locally coupled damped oscillator systems in three dimensions, raising the possibility of practical quantum speedups for realistically damped oscillator networks and approximated wave equations.
items.authors: Malte Schade, Sophia Simon, Nathan Wiebe, Scott Keating, Cyrill B\"osch, Andreas Fichtner

items.title: Locally optimized variational evolution for quantum many-body systems
items.abstract: Quantum many-body dynamics is difficult to simulate because the global wavefunction develops extensive complexity, whereas local observables may retain only an intrinsic, system-size-independent complexity. This distinction is especially relevant in thermalizing systems, where local subsystems lose microscopic information and relax towards equilibrium. We introduce a variational time-evolution principle that exploits this separation by replacing global-state fidelity with a cost function defined on local reduced density matrices. The resulting locally optimized matrix-product-state (LOMPS) algorithm retains coherent short-time dynamics while using the simplification generated by thermalization at later times, and admits closed-form equations of motion analogous to the time-dependent variational principle. The same principle yields a quantum-classical algorithm in which a quantum processor evaluates the local cost and a noise-robust classical procedure performs the optimization. Proof-of-principle implementations on Quantinuum H2 and IBM Heron processors recover the characteristic local dynamics.
items.authors: Carolin Wille, Maximilian Marvell, Lauren Stewart, Maximillian Murphy, Vinul Wimalaweera, Lesley Gover, Andrew G. Green

items.title: Microwave dielectric properties of LiNbO$_{\mathbf{3}}$ and AlN at millikelvin temperatures and single-photon power
items.abstract: Efficient bidirectional microwave-optical photon conversion is a key capability for scaling superconducting quantum processors into distributed networks. However, achieving the necessary conversion efficiency requires filling a critical knowledge gap in understanding the loss mechanisms of electro-optic materials. Here, we characterize the microwave properties of single-crystal bulk LiNbO3 and AlN over a broad range of powers, down to single-photon levels, and spanning from millikelvin temperatures to above 1 K. We demonstrate that both materials exhibit two-level systems (TLS) behavior, while piezoelectric-related losses are excluded. We show that TLS-induced dissipation is predominantly localized on the surface rather than being an intrinsic bulk property, a result further corroborated by room-temperature 3D XPS and time-of-flight SIMS analyses. These findings provide useful insights to engineer hybrid architectures that integrate bulk electro-optic crystals within superconducting cavities, proving that microwave quality factors compatible with high-efficiency microwave-optical transduction are within reach.
items.authors: Alessandro Reineri, Francesco Crisa, Maithlee Shinde, Daniel Bafia, Akshay Murthy, Changqing Wang, Tanay Roy, Alexander Romanenko, John Zasadzinski, Anna Grassellino, Silvia Zorzetti
items.title_zh: LiNbO$_{\mathbf{3}}$和AlN在毫开尔文温度下的微波介电特性
items.summary_zh: 高效的双向微波-光子转换是将超导量子处理器扩展到分布式网络的关键能力。然而，实现所需的转换效率需要填补对电光材料损耗机制的关键知识空白。本文对单晶体块状LiNbO$_3$和AlN的微波特性进行了表征，涵盖了从毫开尔文温度到超过1 K的广泛功率范围，直至单光子水平。我们证明这两种材料表现出两能级系统（TLS）行为，同时排除了与压电相关的损耗。研究表明，TLS引起的耗散主要局限于表面，而非内在的块体特性，这一结果通过室温下的3D XPS和飞行时间SIMS分析得到了进一步证实。这些发现为设计集成块状电光晶体与超导腔体的混合架构提供了有益的见解，证明了与高效微波-光子转换兼容的微波品质因子是可以实现的。

items.title: New lower bounds for CDS and $f$-routing
items.abstract: Understanding the entanglement cost of non-local quantum computation (NLQC) is relevant to complexity theory, cryptography, quantum gravity, and other areas. A central special case is $f$-routing, motivated in part by quantum position verification. Proving lower bounds on its entanglement cost in the fully robust setting has been a major open problem in NLQC. Motivated by this problem, we establish two related lower bounds. First, we study the shared-randomness cost of robust conditional disclosure of secrets (CDS). The connection between CDS and $f$-routing established by Allerstorfer et al. (Quantum 2024) makes understanding the randomness complexity of robust CDS a natural step toward lower bounds for the fully robust routing problem. We show that the shared-randomness cost of robust CDS is lower bounded by the logarithm of deterministic SMP communication complexity, even when communication and private randomness are unrestricted. Our lower bound is tight for the equality function. Second, we consider one-sided-perfect $f$-routing, in which the protocol is exact on one input class and has constant error on the other. By exploiting the positivity of the low-rank matrix in the method of Asadi, Culf, and May (ITCS 2025), we derive a lower bound on the entanglement cost in terms of sign rank. In particular, this yields a linear lower bound on the entanglement cost of routing for the inner-product function in both one-sided-perfect settings, matching the known upper bound.
items.authors: Atsuya Hasegawa, Ranitha Mataraarachchi

items.title: The quantum lifetime of a future-referential feedback loop: certified index, architecture floor, and thermal bonus
items.abstract: A quantum feedback loop that returns information from a forward simulation to an earlier internal time induces a completely positive trace-preserving map on a message register; iterating that map eventually destroys its ability to carry entanglement. The entanglement-breaking index N = n_EB(Phi), the round at which this happens, is studied along two axes, interaction and bath. On the interaction axis, strict contraction onto a full-rank fixed point forces N finite in every dimension, via an explicit separable ball around the limiting Choi state, and across 3997 sampled channels index and stability gap are one clock, N [1 - rho(A)] in [0.60, 1.50]. On the bath axis, a thermal ancilla at polarisation p = tanh(hbar omega / 2 k_B T) makes every channel quantity an exact quadratic in p, and one-sided certificates (no eigensolver) establish N = 3 at the reference circuit at every temperature. The infinite-temperature index is an architecture floor with closed form and exact measure (46.427% of circuits break entanglement in one round at infinite temperature). For exchange collisions (generalised amplitude damping) the index has a closed form and is monotone in p; for the loop the floor is not a bound: certified circuits dip below it in interior temperature windows, at a rate with Gaussian cutoff in epsilon = 1 - ||A_0||_2 (marginal exponent 2.02 [1.90, 2.16], 4.1 million circuits), and shallow-floor valleys survive to epsilon = 0.125. On a certified coupling-temperature surface, temperature moves the index by at most 3/2, the interaction by 1213/3. Applied to quantum-cognition proposals, a per-bath polarisation table at 310 K shows nuclear spins maximally hot and intramolecular vibrations frozen, and a four-input checklist replaces decoherence times by round budgets; Fisher's nuclear-spin proposal specifies its bath and storage coherence, not its processing interaction or rate.
items.authors: Eran Kopel

items.title: Quantum Uncertainty and Particle Trajectories: From Heisenberg and Schr\"odinger to Constructive Dynamical Models
items.abstract: Quantum uncertainty emerged from two strikingly different routes to quantum mechanics. Heisenberg's matrix mechanics replaced the classical description of atomic orbits by relations among observable transition quantities and led, in 1927, to the uncertainty relation and its influential measurement-based interpretation. Schr\"odinger's wave mechanics grew instead from the Bose--Einstein and de Broglie developments and restored a continuous space-time description through matter waves. The two formalisms were soon shown to be closely related, but neither historical route by itself settles the ontological question of whether particles may possess underlying trajectories. After reviewing these developments, including Einstein's criticism of a simple observability doctrine and Mott's wave-mechanical account of straight cloud-chamber tracks, we distinguish precise quantum uncertainty relations from the stronger claim that quantum mechanics excludes definite microscopic histories. We then compare Feynman paths, Bohmian trajectories, Nelson's stochastic mechanics, and finite-speed persistent Goldstein--Kac dynamics. The Kac process has continuous, piecewise differentiable finite-speed paths; its diffusion limit approaches Wiener kinematics, while analytic continuation of its two-sector dynamics is related to Dirac evolution. These examples show that quantum uncertainty relations constrain observable statistics without, by themselves, uniquely determining an underlying path geometry.
items.authors: Partha Ghose

items.title: Colored Weingarten Calculus for Block-Unitary Ensemble
items.abstract: Haar randomness is the standard null model for quantum typicality, scrambling, and random-matrix formulations of thermalization. In many physical settings, however, randomness is naturally constrained to subspaces of Hilbert space. This structure arises, in particular, both in systems with symmetry-resolved sectors and in the Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis (ETH), where mesoscopic energy windows define subspaces in which nearby energy eigenstates are mixed. Motivated by these settings, we consider a Block-Unitary Ensemble consisting of independently Haar-random unitaries acting on each subspace. We develop a constructive Weingarten Calculus for this ensemble, providing a unified framework across quantum information and many-body physics. This construction reveals a symmetry-resolved Schur-Weyl duality, where the relevant commutant is not the ordinary permutation algebra, but the one of color-preserving permutations. We apply this framework to quantum states under symmetry constraints and to energy-resolved ensembles for ETH.
items.authors: Daniele Iannotti, Elisa Vallini

items.title: Supporting functionals and singular boundary geometry of two-qubit entanglement of formation
items.abstract: We give a criterion for the existence of a global supporting affine functional for the entanglement of formation at an entangled two-qubit state. It exists if and only if the spin-flip bilinear form is nondegenerate on the support of the state, or equivalently, if the last concurrence root associated with the support is nonzero. In this case the entanglement of formation satisfies a two-sided Lipschitz bound relative to the reference state. In the degenerate case the state has rank two or three, and its projective support is tangent to the product-state quadric. By suitably choosing a perturbation outside the original support space, the decrease in the entanglement of formation is, to leading order, proportional to the square root of the mixing parameter. We give an explicit expression for the leading coefficient. Such a square-root decrease violates the one-sided Lipschitz bound, and therefore no globally supported affine functional exists at this state.
items.authors: Wei Song, Xiao-Lan Zong

items.title: Stable Long-Range Charging and Boundary-Mediated Thresholds in a Waveguide Quantum Battery
items.abstract: The waveguide-integrated architecture holds promise for scalable on-chip integration of a charger, a transmission channel, and a quantum battery in a modular, independently optimizable design. We investigate a minimal charging configuration consisting of two emitters coupled to a semi-infinite waveguide and identify the optimal charging mechanism, wherein non-Markovian dynamics driven by out-of-band bound states give rise to single-frequency oscillations of the stored energy. We show that near-unity charging efficiency is achievable at weak to moderate coupling strengths via detuning control, provided that the battery-to-boundary separation $n$ is less than three times the charger-to-boundary separation $m$ ($n<3m$)---a constraint imposed by the mirror-induced feedback---while the average charging power decays exponentially with the spatial separation $n-m$. These findings offer useful insights for monolithic solid-state quantum energy storage and transport.
items.authors: Li-Hong Yu, Zhuo-Yu Zhang, Yu Wang, Xin Li

items.title: Monotonicity of the R\'enyi channel capacity under non-signaling assisted channel simulation
items.abstract: We give an alternative variational proof that non-signaling correlations shared between the sender and receiver cannot increase the R\'enyi capacity of a classical channel. This monotonicity follows from the data-processing inequality for channel divergences established by Oufkir, Yao and Berta. Our approach works directly with the information-radius representation of the capacity. The constraints defining non-signaling boxes are linear in the box, while the R\'enyi capacity depends on the channel nonlinearly. We use a Legendre transform to express the capacity as an extremum over a family of affine functionals in which the channel appears linearly.
