Combining this method with separate arguments for the Shannon capacity and endpoint orders, we recover monotonicity at every order from zero to infinity. We then derive consequences for standard coding exponent functions: non-signaling simulation cannot increase the random-coding or sphere-packing exponent below capacity, or decrease the strong-converse exponent above capacity.
items.authors: Tina Shariat, Matt Hoogsteder-Riera, Marco Tomamichel

items.title: Genuine Multipartite Nonlocality Is Fermionic Magic
items.abstract: Free fermion dynamics is classically simulable, and a single non-Gaussian state makes it universal. We show that the same boundary governs quantum nonlocality. Measured as fermionic qubits, fermionic Gaussian states reach at most the biseparable bound of the Mermin inequality for three parties and, for any number of parties, violate the Mermin family by exactly the factor of a single entangled pair. They are never genuinely multipartite nonlocal. Genuine multipartite nonlocality and computational universality are thus one resource for fermions, the opposite of the stabilizer case. The mechanism is fermion parity. The bound is monogamous and certifies non-Gaussianity from measured correlations alone. On superconducting processors we watch nonlocality beyond free fermions switch on under an interaction between densities, confirm the monogamy law on 96 qubits, and measure the ground state of twelve interacting fermions on a ring cross the bound as the interaction grows, detecting the charge density wave transition.
items.authors: Jamal Slim

items.title: QMA(2) with Limited Shared Entanglement
items.abstract: A $\mathsf{QMA}(2)$ protocol involves two provers submitting unentangled witnesses to a polynomial-time quantum verifier. In The Power of Unentanglement (ToC, 2009), Aaronson et al. proposed $\mathsf{QMA}(2;h)$, a variant of $\mathsf{QMA}(2)$ in which the two provers may share $h$ EPR pairs. Our main result shows that the power of $\mathsf{QMA}(2)$ remains unchanged for up to logarithmically many shared EPR pairs: $\mathsf{QMA}(2;h)=\mathsf{QMA}(2)$ for $h=O(\log n)$, where $n$ is the input length. The result follows from a simulation using four unentangled witnesses, combined with the Harrow-Montanaro equality $\mathsf{QMA}(4)=\mathsf{QMA}(2)$ (FOCS, 2010). We also prove monotonicity in the EPR budget: $\mathsf{QMA}(2;h)\subseteq\mathsf{QMA}(2;H)$ for $h\le H$, preserving completeness and soundness. Combined with input padding, this shows that establishing $\mathsf{QMA}(2;n^\varepsilon)=\mathsf{QMA}(2)$ for any fixed $\varepsilon>0$ would imply equality for every polynomially bounded budget, resolving the open problem raised by Aaronson et al. Finally, we extend these results to a variant of the model in which the provers may use local operations and classical communication (LOCC) during witness preparation. For logarithmic-size witnesses and inverse-polynomial gaps, both models remain equivalent to their unentangled counterpart when $h=O(\log n)$. We show that extending this equivalence to any superlogarithmic EPR budget in the LOCC model would imply $\mathsf{NP}\subseteq\mathsf{BQP}$.
items.authors: Alex Della Schiava, Ranitha Mataraarachchi

items.title: Two-Stage Quantum-Classical Distribution Network Reconfiguration via Cycle-Edge Encoding
items.abstract: Distribution network reconfiguration (DNR) is a combinatorial optimization problem that seeks a low-loss network topology subject to topological and electrical operating constraints. In this work, we propose a two-stage quantum-classical method for DNR. First, an iterative linear-ramp Quantum Alternating Operator Ansatz (LR-QAOA) searches topologically feasible subspaces constructed using a novel cycle-edge encoding. The encoding guarantees that every represented configuration is a spanning tree while allowing the size and coverage of each subspace to be adjusted to the available qubit budget. Second, the resulting sample distribution is used to guide a mixed-integer second-order-cone programming (MISOCP) solver. The method is evaluated on six distribution networks ranging from 33 to 417 buses through ideal simulation and execution on trapped-ion quantum hardware. For the 417-bus network, quantum hardware sampling identifies a configuration within approximately $1.4\%$ of the literature reference loss. Across all six test systems, the MISOCP solver guided by hardware-derived distributions reaches an incumbent within $1\%$ of the target with a lower median solver time than the corresponding unguided solver. These findings establish a concrete framework for applying current quantum hardware to DNR, with the potential to become increasingly competitive as hardware improves.
items.authors: Nowar Alashkar, Cade Kennedy, Phillip C. Lotshaw, Shaked Regev, Miguel Angel Lopez-Ruiz, Ananth Kaushik, Paul Smith, Claudio Girotto, Martin Roetteler

items.title: Stationarity as a One-Mode Constraint on Quantum Correlation
items.abstract: A stationary scalar correlation energy admits an exact one-mode terminal representation even when the microscopic correlated return is strongly multimode. We test predictive realizations built from specified stationary information carriers in two complementary two-electron systems with the same Coulomb repulsion but different confinement: He-like ions and harmonium (Hooke's atom). For the Coulomb sequence, canonical RHF supplies the symmetry-faithful information carrier. The repeated same-mode return gives a He correlation error of $+0.1164$ m$E_{\mathrm h}$ and no more than $0.0157$ m$E_{\mathrm h}$ for Li$^+$--Ar$^{16+}$; H$^-$ is nevertheless bound and $93.3\%$ of its conventional correlation energy is recovered even though the RHF carrier is qualitatively strained. The dimensionless confinement factor $R_{CC}=D_{CC}/Z$ tends to $1.092394$. For harmonic confinement, an independently constructed response-compressed one-mode return gives $R_H=D_H/\sqrt{\omega}$; for $\omega\ge0.1$ it agrees with reference-inferred values within $0.21\%$ and tends to the literature high-density limit $1.309283$. Cioslowski and Pernal locate the qualitative crossover to the radially localized strongly correlated harmonium regime at $\omega_{\rm crit}\simeq0.04012$, below the quantitative domain used here. The H$^-$ endpoint and $\omega_{\rm crit}$ are therefore complementary carrier-validity boundaries: they limit the predictive realization, not exact terminal one-mode representability. A broad helium Bethe--Goldstone spectrum confirms that this terminal statement is not microscopic one-pole dynamics.
items.authors: Itai Panas

items.title: Simultaneous Circuit Tests for Finite Reversible Models of Quantum Control
items.abstract: A finite reversible model can approximate individual quantum gates while retaining freedom in its transition tables and preparation contexts. We formulate the simultaneous certification problem in which one stationary controller and one preparation law must reproduce an entire collection of circuit probabilities. For a specified frame catalogue, accuracy graph and calibration constraints, we give an exact shared-table feasibility formulation and distinguish certificates for a fixed table from certificates for the complete model class. A four-frame qubit example exhibits a strict separation between fitting two circuits individually and fitting them jointly. A larger exact benchmark uses 464 frames and a phase symmetry that removes preparation-prior dependence. We independently reconstruct its admissible graph and certify a sharp repeated-circuit horizon: one controller stays within probability error 1/3 through 192 blocks, whereas every allowed controller violates that threshold by block 193. A separate controller reproduces all 8,190 nonempty Hadamard-phase words of length at most twelve within the same tolerance. We also derive a finite-window spectral obstruction and finite-shot confidence tests, illustrated by a reproducible sampling experiment. The conclusions concern the stated finite reversible model classes; they do not establish a universal memory bound or a discrepancy for physical quantum hardware.
items.authors: Josef Bruzzese

items.title: Distance Structure of Insertion Kernels and Local Port Response in Non-Reciprocal Su--Schrieffer--Heeger Chains
items.abstract: Non-reciprocal lattices offer a flexible setting for directional wave transport, raising the question of how enhanced internal scattering translates into transmission between fixed external ports. We address this question for non-reciprocal Su--Schrieffer--Heeger (SSH) chains with staggered gain and loss by relating the reference-dependent insertion kernel $K_p=VG_pV$ to the coherent transmission intensity $T$. On a fixed finite graph, a strong-insertion expansion gives a contribution proportional to $\gamma^{1-d}$, whose coefficient is the signed sum of shortest directed paths of length $d$. When this sum is nonzero, it sets the leading behavior independently of fixed diagonal losses; when it cancels, those losses can enter the first surviving higher-order term. For a fixed cross-sublattice endpoint channel, transmission has a strictly negative slope at every nonzero differentiable stationary point of the kernel magnitude. In the weak-insertion regime, the reference-system coefficient $\chi=-\mathrm{Re}\,\mathrm{Tr}[(G_{0p}Z)^2]$ predicts the initial transmission change for symmetric SSH ports, and $\chi>0$ together with a strictly stable baseline guarantees local stable enhancement. Finite-chain calculations and driven dynamics connect these results to observable response and distinguish asymptotic convergence from transient settling. A strictly dissipative short-chain example exhibits local enhancement without net power gain. Together, these results separate graph-path structure, coherent port response, and dynamical establishment, providing channel-specific criteria for interpreting internal scattering.
items.authors: Xudong Zhang, Bin Guo

items.title: Automated reduction of fault-tolerant circuits
items.abstract: We present an automated method for reducing fault-tolerant circuits through fault-equivalent rewrites. Starting from a known fault-tolerant circuit, the search applies non-reducing enabling rules to expose Bell-pair reductions, each of which removes an ancilla preparation and a CNOT gate. Because every search transition preserves fault equivalence, the resulting circuits inherit the fault-tolerance properties of the input circuit. Candidate circuits are evaluated using circuit-level Monte Carlo simulation. For Shor-style syndrome extraction with the $[[7,1,3]]$ code, our method reduces one syndrome-measurement round from 30 to 18 ancilla preparations and from 54 to 42 CNOT gates. At a physical two-qubit error rate of $p = 10^{-3}$, the optimized circuit lowers the logical error rate by approximately 21% for both logical basis states. The reduction ranges from 13% to 23% over a range of $p$ spanning two orders of magnitude. We also apply the method to Steane-based dynamic syndrome extraction constructed from Goto's verified logical-$\lvert 0 \rangle$ preparation, in which the verification qubit serves as a flag. The search selects a circuit using four ancillas and 14 CNOT gates, matching the resource counts of the previous design but with an improved CNOT depth. Under depolarizing idle noise at $3p/10$ the selected circuit lowers the logical error rate by approximately 15% for both logical basis states, and by approximately 10% at $p/10$. These results demonstrate that automated fault-equivalent rewriting can identify circuits with lower resource costs or improved logical performance without separately verifying the fault tolerance of every candidate.
items.authors: Hyeongjun Jeon, Jeonghoon Lee, Taehyun Kim

items.title: Quantum Networking at the Speed of Quantum Computation: Kilohertz Entanglement in a Heterogeneous Quantum System
items.abstract: Distributed quantum computing requires rapid, high-fidelity entanglement between qubits in separate processor modules. Photonic links between single-atom qubits provide switchable, long-range connections, but photon loss limits their entanglement rate. Here we entangle a trapped $^{138}$Ba$^{+}$ ion with a silicon-vacancy (SiV$^{-}$) center in a diamond nanophotonic cavity. A photon emitted by the ion is converted in wavelength and encoding, reflected from the SiV$^{-}$--cavity system and detected, so that a single detected photon heralds entanglement. Including all conversion losses, we generate ion--SiV$^{-}$ Bell pairs at an average rate of 1.03(1) kHz with a fidelity of 87.9(7)%. This is four times the rate of the fastest photonic link between two trapped ions and corresponds to one Bell pair per millisecond, matching the cycle time of planned trapped-ion processors.
items.authors: Lukas Hartung, Pierre Barral, Noah Glachman, George Toh, Jacob H. Davidson, Sagnik Saha, Alexander Chuang, Matthew C. Cambria, Madison Sutula, Alexander Abulnaga, Julia Brevoord, John Chiaverini, Ian Counts, Aos Dabbagh, Christian Dangel, Skylar Deckoff-Jones, Chawina De-Eknamkul, Jonathan Dietz, Riley Forst, Prithvi Gundlapalli, Jeonghoon Ha, Michael Haas, Ezekiel Meulbroek, Andrea Mucchietto, Daniel Riedel, Jonah Sachs, Jeremy Sage, Mikhail Shalaev, Harriet Shi, Denis Sukachev, Yichao Yu, Christopher Monroe, Nicholas Mondrik, Mihir Bhaskar, Bart Machielse, Matteo Pompili, Carsten Robens, David Levonian
items.title_zh: 量子计算速度下的量子网络：异质量子系统中的千赫纠缠
items.summary_zh: 分布式量子计算需要在不同处理模块之间快速、高保真地纠缠量子比特。单原子量子比特之间的光子链提供了可切换的长距离连接，但光子损失限制了其纠缠速率。本文中，我们将一个被捕获的$^{138}$Ba$^{+}$离子与钻石纳米光子腔中的硅空位（SiV$^{-}$）中心纠缠。离子发射的光子经过波长和编码转换后，从SiV$^{-}$-腔系统反射并被探测，从而实现单个探测光子预示纠缠。考虑所有转换损失，我们以平均1.03(1) kHz的速率生成离子-SiV$^{-}$贝尔对，保真度为87.9(7)%。这一速率是两个被捕获离子之间最快光子链速率的四倍，相当于每毫秒一个贝尔对，匹配计划中的被捕获离子处理器的周期时间。

items.title: When Does Interference Help Learning? Kernel Geometry as a Pre-Experimental Test for Photonic Reservoir Computing
items.abstract: Multi-photon interference is the resource most native to photonic quantum machine learning, yet experiments on photonic reservoirs have reported advantages, null results, and train-only effects. These outcomes cannot be compared: each measures task-dependent accuracy on different tasks and platforms. Here we resolve the question task-independently through the kernel geometry of boson-sampling feature maps. Interference redistributes feature variance across roughly twice as many effective dimensions as distinguishable-particle statistics, generating a large geometric separation between the corresponding kernels. The separation grows superlinearly with indistinguishability, is linear in Hong--Ou--Mandel visibility at small visibility for two to four photons, and retains approximately 80% of its magnitude at the source quality of current quantum processors. Under experimental sampling budgets the separation is learnable on adversarially constructed tasks (accuracy advantage +0.22 plus or minus 0.05) and an order of magnitude smaller on natural tasks, gated by kernel--task alignment. The results reconcile the existing experimental record and supply a pre-experimental protocol: kernel geometry establishes that an interference-specific learning resource exists, and task alignment determines whether a given task can access it; both are computable before committing significant hardware resources.
items.authors: Oishik Kar, Aswath Babu H
items.title_zh: 干涉何时有助于学习？光子储备计算的核几何预实验测试
items.summary_zh: 多光子干涉是光子量子机器学习中最基本的资源，但光子储备的实验结果显示出优势、无效结果和仅训练效应。这些结果无法比较，因为每个结果测量的是不同任务和平台上的任务依赖性准确性。本文通过玻色取样特征图的核几何独立于任务地解决了这一问题。干涉将特征方差重新分配到大约两倍于可区分粒子统计的有效维度，产生了相应核之间的大几何分离。该分离随着不可区分性超线性增长，在小可见度下对于两到四个光子的Hong--Ou--Mandel可见度呈线性增长，并在当前量子处理器的源质量下保持约80%的幅度。在实验采样预算下，该分离在对抗性构造的任务上是可学习的（准确性优势+0.22±0.05），而在自然任务上则小一个数量级，受限于核-任务对齐。结果调和了现有实验记录，并提供了预实验协议：核几何确定了存在特定于干涉的学习资源，而任务对齐决定了特定任务是否能够访问该资源；两者在投入显著硬件之前均可计算。

items.title: Warm-Start Quantum Computation: Spectral-Weight Resources for Energy Readout and State Preparation
items.abstract: Estimating a ground-state energy and preparing a ground state both split into a front-end that supplies an approximate state $|\chi\rangle$ and a back-end that reads or refines it. We argue, and measure at every step, that the only thing crossing that split is the front-end's spectral weight distribution $p_n=|\langle E_n|\chi\rangle|^2$ over the eigenstates of the problem Hamiltonian $H_P$. Everything downstream is priced in it, so the front-end is a swappable module, and we swap it seven times without altering anything to its right. We call the arrangement WARP. Four back-ends spend that distribution. A readout (A) samples $g(t)=\langle\chi|e^{-iH_Pt}|\chi\rangle$ on the device and extracts true eigenvalues by classical signal processing, returning an energy below the variational bound of the state it was handed, from a signal $50\times$ shorter than a Fourier transform needs. Three routes spend the same account on a state instead. An adiabatic schedule (B) has a minimum gap set by the overlap; a discrete amplification (C) is cheaper in depth but must halt at an index the overlap fixes, so it needs a measured value and not a bound; a recursion (D) of depth $\mathcal{O}(3^m)$ raises the question of whether it can be run at all. The interactions are the substance. On stretched N$_2$ a sample-based diagonalisation reports a variational bound 79 mHa high, fifty times outside chemical accuracy; reading the state it has already prepared returns $E_0$ to $1.4\times10^{-6}$ Ha, three orders of magnitude inside it, and needs no new front-end and no new circuit. And because the weights price everything, they must be measurable when scarce, so we beat a weak reference against a strong one and recover overlaps four orders of magnitude below the shot-noise floor. We map the operating envelope throughout, and state the limitations.
items.authors: Tien D. Kieu

items.title: Bicycle Race: small two-block codes on the Pareto frontier
items.abstract: Two-block group-algebra codes are among the simplest quantum LDPC codes, and many of them are translation invariant on a twisted torus, which suits neutral-atom arrays and other platforms with movable qubits. We ask how far they go at small sizes when searched systematically across all groups. We use algebraic constraints and screens to design a search pipeline capable of enumerating broad and complete swathes of two-block codes on a laptop. With it we census about $10^8$ two-block codes with up to $320$ qubits at check weights five to nine. Several of these censuses are exhaustive, and support complete statements; for instance, the Gross code is, up to equivalence, the only abelian weight-six two-block code with $n \le 200$ to reach $kd^2/n=12$, no weight-six two-block code with $n \le 300$ beats $[[288,16,16]]$, and the known $[[64,18,8]]$ is the best two-block code by $kd^2/n$ across weights five to nine with $n \le 94$. The censuses are also large enough to give insights into where good codes live - they concentrate in a handful of groups; abelian groups give the best codes at small $n$ and non-abelian groups at large $n$, with the crossover appearing to move out as the check weight grows; and high quality codes become $100$ to $1000$ times rarer per draw from weight six to weights eight and nine. Using the group algebra and the census data to steer a statistical search finds four to fifteen times as many good codes as uniform draws in equal time. Among the codes found are $[[102,20,10]]$ and $[[120,24,10]]$ at check weight nine, which we simulate in noisy syndrome-extraction circuits, and $[[186,20,18]]$, a weight-nine code with every check in a $5\times5$ window. At check weights seven to nine, our best codes exceed the best published $kd^2/n$ with exact distance at the same check weight in most length bands up to $320$ qubits. All codes are available in a public database.
items.authors: Gideon Lee

items.title: Quantum Imaging as alternative readout in atom interferometry: The case of Gravity
items.abstract: We propose a quantum imaging-inspired setup for measuring gravitational fields using an atom that emits a photon at one of two possible locations. The atom acquires a gravitationally induced quantum phase that it shares with the photon. By restoring the path identity of the atom after its interaction with the gravitational field, the gravitationally induced phase can be measured using photon interferometry without the need for additional measurements on the atom. Through repeated measurements with varying interferometric setups, the gravitational potential and inertial acceleration can be deduced.
items.authors: Marian Cepok, Dennis R\"atzel, Claus L\"ammerzahl

items.title: Gravitational redshift of broadband relativistic quantum photons
items.abstract: Gravitational redshift is a key prediction of general relativity that has been experimentally verified. Nevertheless, its existence in the context of relativistic and quantum physics has not yet been established. We employ linearized quantum gravity to study the effects of quantum coherence on gravitational redshift of broadband photons that interact with a planet via graviton exchange. We find that gravitational redshift, as predicted by general relativity, occurs when the initial photonic state contains no quantum coherence between orthogonal photonic modes, such as position states. If quantum coherence is initially present, different photonic modes overlap, a genuine quantum correction occurs solely for single-photon states. Our work not only explains gravitational redshift as the interaction of gravitons and photons in flat spacetime, but also shows that deviations from the theory occur already at low energies when quantum interference of photonic states is important.
items.authors: David Edward Bruschi, Alessio Lapponi, Alessandro Ferreri, Andreas Wolfgang Schell

items.title: RISC-Q: A Generator for Real-Time Quantum Control System-on-Chips Compatible with RISC-V
items.abstract: Quantum computing imposes stringent requirements for the precise control of large-scale qubit systems, including, for example, microsecond-latency feedback and nanosecond-precision timing of gigahertz signals-demands that far exceed the capabilities of conventional real-time systems. The rapidly evolving and highly diverse nature of quantum control necessitates the development of specialized hardware accelerators. While a few custom real-time systems have been developed to meet the tight timing constraints of specific quantum platforms, they face major challenges in scaling and adapting to increasingly complex control demands-largely due to fragmented toolchains and limited support for design automation. To address these limitations, we present RISC-Q---an open-source flexible generator for Quantum Control System-on-Chip (QCSoC) designs, featuring a programming interface compatible with the RISC-V ecosystem. Developed using SpinalHDL, RISC-Q enables efficient automation of highly parameterized and modular QCSoC architectures, supporting agile and iterative development to meet the evolving demands of quantum control. We demonstrate that RISC-Q can replicate the performance of existing QCSoCs with significantly reduced development effort, facilitating efficient exploration of the hardware-software co-design space for rapid prototyping and customization.
items.authors: Junyi Liu, Yi Lee, Haowei Deng, Connor Clayton, Gengzhi Yang, Xiaodi Wu

items.title: Pseudo-critical localization
items.abstract: We uncover a novel localization phenomenon, termed pseudo-critical localization, in non-Hermitian critical systems. This phenomenon is induced by the synergistic interplay between weak localization and non-Hermitian skin effects. It exhibits critical-like behavior at finite scales and undergoes a crossover to Anderson localization as the system size increases, which is in sharp contrast to critical localization that universally exhibits persistent criticality in the thermodynamic limit. Concretely, we use the non-Hermitian quasiperiodic mosaic model and non-reciprocal Aubry--Andr\'e model as minimal models to present the general features of size-dependent critical localization, and use entanglement entropy analysis to confirm the size-dependent nature. This discovery challenges the established paradigm of critical localization, opening new avenues for understanding and controlling critical behavior in non-Hermitian systems.
items.authors: Hui-Qiang Liang, Linhu Li, Guo-Fu Xu

items.title: Fock-space fragmentation in quenches of disordered interacting fermions
items.abstract: Fock-space fragmentation, as it is currently investigated, primarily originates from specific kinematic constraints or emergent conservation laws in many-body systems with translation invariance. It leads to non-ergodic dynamics and possible breakdown of the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis. Here, we demonstrate that also in disordered systems, such as the XXZ model with random on-site fields, fragmentation appears as a natural concept offering fresh perspectives, for example, on many-body localization (MBL). Specifically, for a given quenched initial state, we identify a potential-energy shell in Fock space, defined by its energy and energy uncertainty, which represents the energetically accessible part of the many-body configuration space. For example, the drastic sample-to-sample fluctuations observed in the weak disorder regime, $W<W_{\mathrm{frag}}$, represent fluctuations of the mass of the shell. Upon increasing disorder, the potential-energy shell becomes increasingly fragmented. Its finite-size evolution exhibits a turnaround flow; extrapolating this flow to the disorder at which the turnaround vanishes provides a heuristic estimate of the strong-fragmentation scale $W_{\mathrm{frag}}$. We conjecture that the fragmentation identified here provides a geometric mechanism contributing to the finite-time slowing down of relaxation observed in studies of disordered interacting systems.
items.authors: Ishita Modak, Rajesh Narayanan, Ferdinand Evers, Soumya Bera

items.title: Anyonic time exchange in hierarchical Hall states: emergent Luttinger scaling and cross-correlations at finite temperature
items.abstract: We address hierarchical fractional quantum Hall edges coupled by a spatially local quantum point contact within the Unified Nonequilibrium Perturbative (UNEP) framework. Without assuming a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid (TLL) tunneling correlator, we impose a local anyonic time-exchange (ATE) constraint with phase $\bar{\theta}$, yielding a nonequilibrium fluctuation-dissipation integral equation relating DC tunneling current and noise. For thermal initial states, detailed balance closes this equation for the current. Using the Wiener-Hopf method, we find a unique physical solution of local TLL form, with scaling dimension $\delta$ determined by $\bar{\theta}=\pi\delta\pmod{\pi}$, emerging from the solution rather than being imposed via a TLL correlator. By contrast, ATE and inversion symmetry alone fix the exchange monodromy but not the full transport dynamics. We then study the "anyon collider" beyond Laughlin states at finite temperatures. Detailed balance is broken and noise becomes super-Poissonian, but the relation between nonequilibrium and equilibrium correlators determines current and noise. The output cross-correlation and balanced generalized Fano factor depend on both $\delta$ and statistical phase $\theta$, identical to $\bar{\theta}$ for co-propagating modes with short-range interactions. A temperature-dependent current scale separates the zero-temperature asymptotic regime from the low-current regime, where the balanced Fano factor saturates to a function of $\theta$ and $\delta$ distinct from its zero-temperature value. This latter regime is particularly relevant to ``anyon collider'' experiments. These complementary regimes constrain the statistical phase and scaling dimension, subject to the symmetry $\delta\mapsto1-\delta$ at fixed $\theta$. For independent statistical phase and scaling dimension, the thermal crossover can reverse the sign of output cross-correlations.
items.authors: Aleksander Latyshev, Ines Safi

items.title: Groupoid Representation of Lorentz Transformations Including Superluminal Observers
items.abstract: We construct a Minkowski-pointed Poincare groupoid that extends the geometric description of Lorentz transformations to frames superluminal relative to a distinguished rest frame. Real four-dimensional superluminal boost matrices factorize into ordinary Lorentz boosts and finite infinite-speed limits. For each spatial direction, the two oriented limits define arrows between the Minkowski metric object and a directional metric object; their composition yields an involutive isotropy loop generating a direction-dependent extension of the Poincare group. These arrows induce *-isomorphisms of Poincare observable algebras, transporting generators and their tensor products. Since all metric objects share a common affine spacetime and dual momentum space, transported spectral data can be classified relative to the distinguished Minkowski metric. This Minkowski-pointed classification recovers ordinary massive and massless Wigner sectors and assigns spacelike orbits, with SO(2,1) little groups, to massive momentum representatives transported to directional objects. It thus provides a geometric interpretation of tachyonic Wigner wavefunction classes without postulating intrinsically tachyonic states. As a kinematic application, we examine polarized cobalt-60 beta decay. Under an explicit source-arrow correspondence, reversal of nuclear polarization exchanges oriented arrows and reverses the preferred momentum direction, consistently with the observed reversal of the Wu counting asymmetry. The measured angular law is compatible with this correspondence; a derivation of decay amplitudes and asymmetry coefficients remains open.
items.authors: Marco Zaopo

items.title: On the Feasibility of Simulation-Secure Quantum Functional Encryption
items.abstract: Functional encryption is a powerful cryptographic primitive that enables fine-grained access to encrypted data and underlies numerous applications. Although the ideal security notion for FE, simulation security, has been shown to be impossible in the plain classical setting, those impossibility results rely on inherently classical arguments. This raises a fundamental question: can simulation-secure FE be realized in the quantum regime or in alternative models? We resolve both directions of this question. On the negative side, we show that the classical impossibility results largely extend to the quantum setting. When the adversary can submit an unbounded number of challenge messages, we establish an unconditional impossibility, matching the classical barrier. In the case where the adversary may obtain many functional keys, classical arguments only yield impossibility under the assumption of pseudorandom functions; we strengthen this by proving impossibility under the potentially weaker assumption of pseudorandom quantum states. We additionally give an independent impossibility based solely on public-key encryption with classical public-keys. Since public-key encryption is not known to imply pseudorandom states, this yields complementary evidence of the barrier and, in particular, establishes unconditional impossibility of public-key functional encryption with classical public-keys. A key technical ingredient in our proofs is a novel incompressibility property for pseudorandom states, which may be of independent interest. On the positive side, we show how to circumvent these fundamental barriers in memory-restricted models, where the adversary's quantum or classical memory is bounded. In this setting, we obtain new feasibility results for simulation-secure FE that allow many challenge ciphertexts or many functional key queries.
items.authors: Mohammed Barhoush, Arthur Mehta, Anne M\"uller, Louis Salvail

items.title: Enhancing entanglement asymmetry in fragmented quantum systems
items.abstract: Entanglement asymmetry provides a quantitative measure of symmetry breaking in many-body quantum states. Focusing on inhomogeneous $U(1)$ charges, such as dipole and multipole moments, we show that the typical asymmetry is bounded by a universal fraction of its maximal value. Multipole charges naturally arise in systems with Hilbert-space fragmentation, where the dynamics splits into exponentially many disconnected sectors. Using the commutant algebra formalism, we generalize entanglement asymmetry to account for fragmentation. While the asymmetry grows logarithmically for conventional symmetries, it can scale extensively in fragmented systems and distinguish classical from quantum fragmentation. We derive general upper bounds for the asymmetry and identify states that saturate them. To study the typical behavior of the asymmetry, we consider the ensemble of random matrix product states. By identifying the bond dimension with an effective time parameter, we qualitatively reproduce recent results on asymmetry dynamics in random quantum circuits, suggesting a universal behavior for the asymmetry of $U(1)$ charges in local ergodic systems.
items.authors: Lorenzo Gotta, Filiberto Ares, Sara Murciano

items.title: Limitations of Avila-inspired theory in the diamond chain with quasiperiodic disorder
items.abstract: The mobility edges (MEs) that separate localized, multifractal and ergodic states in energy are a central concept in understanding Anderson localization. In this work we study the effect of several mutually commensurate quasiperiodic frequencies on the mobility edge formation. We focus on the example of the addition of a constant offset to the quasiperiodic potential of the one-dimensional all-bands-flat diamond chain. We show that this additional offset can transform the anomalous mobility edges (AMEs), i.e. the energies, separating localized and multifractal states, into conventional mobility edges, separating localized from delocalized states. Also this appears to be the first example which shows the inability of Avila's global theory to analytically predict the ME location. We observe this both quantitatively, through the ME location mismatch, and qualitatively, via the formation of multiple MEs, not predicted by the theory.
items.authors: Manish Kumar, Ivan M. Khaymovich, Auditya Sharma

items.title: Entanglement in the $\theta$-vacuum
items.abstract: We compute the entanglement entropy and the entanglement spectrum of the vacuum state in the massive Schwinger model at a finite $\theta$ angle. By computing two-point correlation functions we show that the correlation length diverges in the critical region. We clarify the physical origin of entanglement entropy enhancement at $\theta=\pi$ by relating it to the competition between distinct electric-flux vacuum branches. We show that the peak near $\theta=\pi$ persists across the range of masses studied and corresponds to the point of maximal competition between distinct vacuum branches with opposite electric-field orientation, where quantum fluctuations due to fermion pair creation are maximized. While this entropy enhancement is generic, a pronounced compression of the low-lying entanglement spectrum at $\theta=\pi$ distinguishes the near-critical case ($m/g\simeq0.33$). Using the Bisognano--Wichmann (BW) theorem, we construct a lattice BW entanglement Hamiltonian and compare it with the exact modular Hamiltonian obtained from the reduced density matrix. We observe agreement in the infrared sector, indicating that the entanglement Hamiltonian is well approximated by a spatially weighted Hamiltonian. Finally, we discuss possible applications to entanglement in topological insulators and quantum wires. In this work, we used the chirally rotated formulation of the Schwinger model Hamiltonian. We identify an additive vacuum-energy artifact induced by the discretization of the chirally rotated lattice and derive its exact free-lattice form to subtract it in the continuum limit.
items.authors: Sebastian Grieninger, Dmitri E. Kharzeev, Eliana Marroquin

items.title: Fate of emergent Hilbert space fragmentation and information insulation upon softening of hard dual constraints at PXP-chain junctions
items.abstract: We demonstrate emergent Hilbert-space fragmentation in a composite chain of PXP and dual-PXP subchains separated by junctions with simultaneous blockade and anti-blockade projection constraints. The Hilbert space shatters into disjoint Krylov fragments growing exponentially with junction number. Freezing does not require a unique allowed junction state: multiple configurations remain locally allowed, but the dual constraints remove dynamical links between them. Each fragment is labeled by frozen junction configurations and contains compatible basis states. This fragmentation produces dynamical caging of quantum information between neighboring junctions and novel states with partially thermal and athermal regions. Softening the junction by admitting other local states with variable nonzero diagonal amplitudes destroys the direct-sum block structure and fragmentation. Nevertheless, information remains dynamically insulated and inhomogeneous thermal properties persist up to an onset time scaling with the diagonal energy penalty of the previously restricted junction states, followed by longer prethermal behavior. Energy-level statistics in each symmetry-resolved sector evolve from Poissonian in the hard-junction limit toward Wigner-Dyson behavior upon softening, with finite-size non-monotonicity. This signals the breakdown of the tensor-sum structure yielding pairwise sums of chaotic subchain spectra, restoring chaotic thermalization. In the hard-junction case, we find a chirally protected zero-energy mode with density peaks at physical edges and near the junction, pinned to zero under chirality-preserving disorder. The tensor-product eigenfunction structure also enhances the number of nonzero-energy scar states. Finally, we discuss routes to these junction architectures in programmable Rydberg atom platforms using optical tweezers, local addressing, and facilitation techniques.
items.authors: Akshay Panda, Anwesha Chattopadhyay

items.title: Entanglement dynamics after quenches with inhomogeneous Hamiltonians
items.abstract: We investigate entanglement dynamics in bipartite systems governed by inhomogeneous Hamiltonians of the form $H = H_L + H_R$, where $H_{L/R}$ acts only on the left or right region and is homogeneous within each region. Focusing on the XX chain and the transverse-field Ising chain, we derive analytical formulas for the entanglement entropy between the two regions in the hydrodynamic limit of long times. In this regime, fermions incident on the interface undergo scattering, generating entanglement between reflected and transmitted modes. The resulting quasiparticle picture is controlled by the transmission coefficient, which we obtain analytically by solving the stationary lattice Schr\"odinger equation. Due to the bounded dispersion, strong inhomogeneity suppresses both transport and entanglement growth. We benchmark our analytical predictions against numerical simulations in paradigmatic setups. Finally, we extend the analysis to the interacting XXZ chain using tDMRG. The numerical data show qualitative agreement with the quadratic case: entanglement growth remains suppressed in the strongly inhomogeneous limit. Notably, however, entanglement continues to increase even when transport is suppressed, at least at intermediate times.
items.authors: Andrea Di Pasquale, Federico Rottoli, Vincenzo Alba

items.title: Affine Left--Right Dirac Data on the Moyal Plane, with an Application to $U(1)_\star$ Gauge Coupling in Noncommutative Quantum Mechanics
items.abstract:
We study even non-unital Dirac data on the two-dimensional Moyal plane with fixed deformation parameter \(\vartheta
eq0\), whose Dirac operator is affine in the left and right regular coordinate multipliers, with coefficient matrices \(T_L\) and \(T_R\). Two invariants organize this class. The right block controls algebra--Dirac transversality: local compactness holds if and only if \(\det T_R
eq0\), with \(|\det T_R|\) determining the local volume coefficient and \(\operatorname{sgn}\det T_R\) the oriented Gaussian \(K\)-homology pairing. Independently, \(\Gamma=\vartheta(\det T_L-\det T_R)\) controls the spectral regime and, together with \(|\det T_R|\), the exact localized heat trace: \(\Gamma
eq0\) gives infinitely degenerate Landau levels, while for \(\Gamma=0\) in the transverse regime the spectrum is \(\mathbb R\) with empty point spectrum. Applied to Wallet's Landau--Moyal family, the criterion shows that local compactness survives at the metric-degenerate point \(\xi_{\mathrm W}=1\) but fails at \(\xi_{\mathrm W}=-1\), thereby resolving the local-compactness behaviour at both exceptional one-sided points. We then derive a distinguished affine family from a fixed nondegenerate sector \((\hbar_0,\vartheta_0,B_0)\) of the kinematical symmetry group of two-dimensional noncommutative quantum mechanics. The sector fixes the effective Moyal scale \(\vartheta_{\mathrm{eff}}=\vartheta_0/(1-\vartheta_0B_0/\hbar_0)\) and \(T_R\), while an affine \(U(1)_\star\) background coupling deforms only the left affine part of the Dirac operator. Consequently, local compactness, noncommutative volume and \(K\)-homology class remain unchanged, whereas \(\Gamma=	frac12(1-eF_{xy}/B_0)\) drives a transition at \(eF_{xy}=B_0\) from Landau levels to spectrum \(\mathbb R\) with empty point spectrum.
items.authors: Tanmoy Kumar Sarkar, Md. Rafsanjany Jim, S. Hasibul Hassan Chowdhury

items.title: A general proof of integer R\'enyi QNEC
items.abstract: We prove the R\'{e}nyi quantum null energy condition for every integer R\'{e}nyi order $n\geq2$. In local Poincar\'e-invariant quantum field theory, this states that the sandwiched R\'{e}nyi divergence (SRD) of an excited state relative to the vacuum is convex along a future-directed null deformation. We assume that the deformation is realized by the canonical translations of a half-sided modular inclusion and that the divergence is finite for the initial, undeformed algebra. The proof establishes convexity of the SRD along the induced positive contraction semigroup on Haagerup $L^n(M)$, for every non-zero positive initial element. We also establish a R\'enyi ant formula at every even integer order and, under an additional regularity assumption, at odd integer orders. The R\'enyi ant formula identifies the negative first null derivative of SRD with a multiple of the infimum of the canonical null-translation energy over vector purifications of an escort state constructed from the excited state and the vacuum.
items.authors: Tanay Kibe, Pratik Roy

items.title: Lieb-Schultz-Mattis constraints for hyperbolic lattices
items.abstract: The Lieb-Schultz-Mattis (LSM) theorem and its higher-dimensional extensions forbid the existence of a unique, symmetric, and gapped ground state at fractional fillings in quantum many-body systems with a conserved particle number (or spin angular momentum) and the conventional translation symmetry of Euclidean lattices. In this work, we propose a generalization of the LSM theorem to quantum many-body systems on hyperbolic lattices, i.e., regular tessellations of two-dimensional negatively curved space. By leveraging concepts from hyperbolic band theory in a many-body setting, we adapt Oshikawa's flux-threading argument to periodic hyperbolic lattices with a non-Euclidean (Fuchsian) translation symmetry and compute a lower-bound to the ground-state degeneracy as a function of filling and lattice geometry. We explore the consequences of LSM constraints for gapped phases of hyperbolic quantum matter and suggest frustrated spin models on hyperbolic analogs of the square and triangular lattices as promising platforms for realizing symmetric spin liquids in hyperbolic space.
items.authors: G. Shankar, Joseph Maciejko

items.title: Influence-solvability: a systematic theory of $(1+1)D$ solvability and its application to brickwork circuits
items.abstract: `Solvable' circuits, such as dual unitaries and its generalisations, have arisen as paradigmatic examples of tractable chaotic non-equilibrium dynamics, both in classical and quantum systems. However, while increasingly complicated sufficient conditions have been proposed, a systematic theory classifying and understanding general features of Solvable circuits is missing. In this work we develop such a theory by deriving the most general local necessary and sufficient conditions under which a $(1+1)D$ circuit is Solvable. Concretely, we define a circuit to be \emph{influence-solvable} if its influence matrix, representing the `bath' generated by its own evolution, is given by a uniform MPS with finite bond-dimension $\chi$. This property allows for efficient computation of subsystem dynamics and essentially contains all known examples of Solvable circuits. The set of necessary and sufficient local conditions follows from a new version of the fundamental theorem of MPS for open boundary conditions. Next, we apply our theory to brickwork circuits with $\chi=1$ influence-solvability and perform a systematic classification of classical brickwork circuits with local dimension up to $d=3$ and quantum brickwork circuits with $d=2$. Our search reveals new Solvable circuits that are not captured by known conditions.
items.authors: Friedrich H\"ubner, Sun Woo P. Kim

items.title: When does a state-dependent proto-area define a bulk geometry?
items.abstract: A holographic code assigns a state-dependent entropy remainder to every boundary region, but such remainders need not be the extremal lengths of any one bulk metric. We study this common-source question for the proto-area of a calibrated recovery, the entropy of a boundary region minus that of the matter recovered from it. At zeroth order the reference values must match the lengths of one reference geometry in a fixed renormalization scheme, and this matching also determines the entropy-to-length factor. On a graph with a fixed minimum-cut chamber the data derivatives must lie in the image of the cut-incidence matrix, whose left null vectors are witnesses. On the hyperbolic disk the first variation of renormalized length is the rank-two geodesic X-ray transform, with closed range in an adapted data space, and the geodesic displacement, fixed by a forced Jacobi equation, enters at second order. The resulting normal Hessian gives a gauge-invariant criterion, necessary and sufficient, for a regular pair of response coefficients to come from one metric two-jet. For the constant-curvature family generated by a boundary reparametrization the Hessian has a nonzero rank-four mode, so the image of the length map is curved. For a fixed recovery the proto-area Hessian is minus the Bogoliubov-Kubo-Mori information lost in recovery, which the Petz map decomposes orthogonally at a product reference, and which, on a finite-dimensional space of logical directions with positive minimum retained fraction, is at most a sharp multiple of the retained information. Geometric realization requires this loss to reproduce the normal length Hessian on every interval. Two codes show that exact regional area operators can fail to sew into one graph geometry, and that a matched reference with vanishing first response can fail at second order. All criteria refer to one recovery branch and one extremal-surface branch.
items.authors: Ruiliang Li

items.title: Digital Quantum Simulation of Nonequilibrium Dynamics in the Schwinger Model under a Strong External Electric Field
items.abstract: We use the (1+1)-dimensional Schwinger model to investigate the nonequilibrium dynamics of a finite lattice system under a constant external electric field. The lattice Hamiltonian is constructed under open boundary conditions. The vacuum state is prepared using the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE). Scans over the external field strength show the flip of the vacuum state at several field strengths. The critical field strengths agree with theoretical predictions. We further investigate the real-time evolution of the zero-field vacuum under an external electric field using a second-order Trotter-Suzuki decomposition. By comparison with exact diagonalization (ED), we verify that the quantum-simulation protocol reproduces the main features of field-induced boundary charge separation, decay of the vacuum-state fidelity, and quasiperiodic energy redistribution between the electric-field energy term and the fermionic sector. Our results indicate that combining VQE-based state preparation with digital real-time evolution provides a useful approach for studying nonequilibrium dynamics in strong-field lattice gauge theories.
items.authors: Haobin Chen, Lin Cheng, Xingyu Guo

items.title: No off-diagonal quantum focusing for R\'enyi divergences
items.abstract: The quantum focusing conjecture (QFC) is a mathematical expression of the idea that semiclassical gravity remains universally attractive. In its non-gravitational limit, the diagonal inequality is the quantum null energy condition (QNEC), which requires convexity of relative entropy with respect to the vacuum under null deformations. R\'enyi divergences generalize relative entropy, and positive results for the diagonal R\'enyi QNEC raise the question of whether they also satisfy the off-diagonal inequalities required by a full focusing principle. We show that classical correlations between distinct null generators obstruct this extension for any non-affine R\'enyi-type divergence satisfying data processing, tensor additivity, and matched classical-quantum conditioning.
items.authors: Tanay Kibe, Pratik Roy

items.title: The Information Content of Krylov Observables: A Machine Learning Approach
items.abstract: We employ machine learning techniques to estimate the amount of information contained in three Krylov-space observables: the spread complexity $C(t)$, the discrete Wigner negativity $N(t)$, and the normalized negativity $\chi(t)=N(t)/|S(t)|$, where $S(t)$ is the survival amplitude. We study thermofield-double evolutions on GUE, GOE and Poisson spectra, and on the integrable $SL(2,R)$ Krylov chain of a two-dimensional CFT primary, with Lanczos coefficients $b_n=\alpha\sqrt{n(n+2h-1)}$. To introduce chaos we add a GUE random matrix to the integrable chain, $H(\varepsilon)=H_{SL(2,R)}+\varepsilon R_0 W_{GUE}$, where $R_0$ is its spectral half-width. Either $C(t)$ or $N(t)$ alone determines the thermofield temperature, with $R^2\simeq0.999$. However, neither can reconstruct the fine structure of the spectral form factor. In the integrable sector all three observables carry the same information. When we turn on chaos an asymmetry appears: $\chi$ predicts $C$ better than $C$ predicts $\chi$. This gap grows from $+0.33$ to $+0.77$, while the same gap for the raw negativity decays to zero. The extra information comes from the survival amplitude, and $\chi(t)$ carries it while $C(t)$ can still be recovered from $\chi(t)$. We derive a lower bound on this gap, set by the fraction of the variance of $\chi$ that comes from $S$.
items.authors: Ritam Basu

items.title: Quantum Uncomputation of Clean and Dirty Ancilla Qubits
items.abstract: Automatic uncomputation aims to provide programming-language-level support to facilitate the correct and safe use of ancilla qubits in quantum computing, but efforts have only been made for clean ancillas, leaving dirty ancillas unexplored. We present a unified formalization of the uncomputation of both clean and dirty ancillas. For the first time, we prove that checking the existence of uncomputation is coNP-hard. We introduce two complementary synthesis-oriented existence checking methods: a syntax-directed static reasoning system and a rewrite-based normalization procedure (\RwUnx), together forming a top-down pipeline. We implement \RwUnx in Qiskit. Compared with the state-of-the-art \Reqompx, \RwUnx handles practical benchmarks with complex dependencies where \Reqompx does not, and achieves higher success rates in random-circuit experiments.
items.authors: Chenke Liu, Li Zhou, Boning Meng

items.title: Statistics as a local phase: crystalline order and quench dynamics of emergent dimers in Ising gauge theories
items.abstract: How does the Bose or Fermi statistics of microscopic particles survive when confinement binds them into emergent bosonic composites? We address this question in the strong-coupling limit of a $2+1$D $\mathbb{Z}_2$ lattice gauge theory, where charges are confined into tightly bound pairs that can be described by an effective dimer model. We find that the statistics of the underlying matter is encoded entirely in a single local hopping phase $\varphi$ -$0$ for bosons, $\pi$ for fermions. Treating $\varphi$ as a continuous parameter that interpolates between the two, we map the ground-state phase diagram with the help of tensor-network methods. The angle $\varphi$ itself drives a transition between a dimer-superfluid and a dimer-charge density wave state, while the magnetic coupling binds neighboring dimers into resonating pairs, in competition with the inter-dimer repulsion. We identify a novel gapped phase in which dimer pairs crystallize into an ordered pattern of resonating plaquettes. Finally, we propose a quench protocol under which identical dimer configurations evolve in markedly different ways depending on the statistics of their constituents. This provides a dynamical probe of the internal structure of dimers, and allows to detect ordered phases through real-time signatures, within reach of simulators that natively realize bosonic degrees of freedom.
items.authors: Umberto Borla, Riccardo Cioli, Jad C. Halimeh

items.title: Integrable Chiral Quantum Field Theories with Spacetime-Dependent Interactions
items.abstract: We construct a class of integrable chiral fermionic quantum field theories with interactions that depend on both space and time. The construction starts from a unitary, regular, difference-form two-body scattering matrix satisfying braiding unitarity and the Yang--Baxter equation. Each freely moving right- or left-moving particle carries a characteristic coordinate that remains constant along its trajectory, and the scattering matrix depends on differences of these coordinates. The many-body amplitudes form a discrete connection over the coordinate-ordering sectors. The Yang--Baxter equation gives local path independence, while periodic winding on a spatial circle produces quantum Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov (qKZ) difference equations expressing global flatness. Once a reference amplitude satisfying the exchange and qKZ constraints is specified, these transport equations determine the exact wavefunction in every fixed-particle-number sector. Independent reparametrizations of the right- and left-moving characteristics give couplings that depend on both space and time. For the chiral $SU(2)$ Gross--Neveu realization, we solve the qKZ equations for this full characteristic family using off-shell Bethe vectors. The resulting amplitudes are written in the characteristic labels, and their pullbacks give exact many-body wavefunctions for the corresponding space-time-dependent couplings. The two-body amplitude is a ratio of Gamma functions that resums the phase shifts from successive scattering processes. Equal-slope affine maps give a spatially homogeneous specialization in which the coupling depends only on time, and the Bethe ansatz with constant coupling is recovered when the qKZ step vanishes.
items.authors: Pradip Kattel

items.title: Genuine Multi-Entropy of Fully Symmetric Gaussian States
items.abstract: We study the tri-partite genuine R\'enyi multi-entropy of fully symmetric Gaussian states as a function of the squeezing parameter for different total number of bosonic modes under different subsystem configurations. Exact results for a few modes are obtained, and we conjecture an asymptotic formula at the limit of large squeezing parameter as a function of the replica index $n$, while also finding subleading subsystem-size dependent terms for $n=3$ under a specific tripartition. We analytically show that the genuine $n=2$ R\'enyi multi-entropy of any pure bosonic Gaussian states is zero for any number of modes and for any tripartition. Furthermore, to investigate the dependence on subsystem size, we plot the curve of genuine R\'enyi multi-entropy as a function of the number of modes in the subsystems while keeping the total number of modes fixed. We discuss differences and similarities between this result and studies of the multi-entropy curve for Haar random states. In particular, we identify a subsystem size configuration related with the multi-entropy time in an evaporating black hole for which the behavior of the genuine multi-entropy changes.
items.authors: Hugo A. Camargo, Mitsuhiro Nishida

items.title: The equivalence of topological indices for $\mathrm{U}(1)\rtimes\mathbb{Z}_2$-symmetric quantum spin chains
items.abstract: Symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phases in quantum spin chains are distinguished by topological indices. Ogata's operator-algebraic indices apply to a broad range of symmetry classes without requiring continuous symmetry, whereas the elementary twist index of Tasaki requires $\mathrm{U}(1)$ symmetry. We prove their equivalence in the common setting of integer-spin chains with on-site $\mathrm{U}(1)\rtimes\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry and a symmetric locally-unique gapped ground state, without assuming translation invariance or a matrix product representation. A charge-fluctuation estimate yields a strong-limit construction of half-chain rotations with their phases fixed. An exact group commutator identity then identifies the Ogata index with the limit of local twist expectations and gives an explicit error bound. This provides a computable formula for the index when a lower bound on the gap and the relevant ground-state expectations are available. Combining the equivalence with a recent boundary-field gap theorem of OpenAI and our earlier twist-index calculation, we obtain a spin-rotation-invariant locally-unique gapped ground state of the infinite $S=1$ antiferromagnetic Heisenberg chain with both indices equal to $-1$, without assuming infinite-volume uniqueness. The author formulated the problem and proposed the basic strategy, while ChatGPT Astra made substantial contributions to the development of the proof.
items.authors: Hal Tasaki

items.title: Stability of isometries of quantum states
items.abstract: We prove dimension-independent Hyers--Ulam stability for surjective approximate isometries of the positive trace-class cone in both the trace and Bures metrics. Here $\varepsilon\geq0$ is a uniform upper bound on the additive error in preserving distances. Such an approximate isometry is uniformly approximated by a Wigner symmetry (a unitary or antiunitary conjugation), with error at most $9\varepsilon/2$ in the trace metric and $2\sqrt2\varepsilon$ in the Bures metric, even if it does not fix zero. For maps fixing zero, the trace bound improves to $3\varepsilon$ even under the hypothesis of $\delta$-surjectivity, independently of $\delta$. In infinite dimensions, we construct spectrum-preserving homeomorphisms of the full state space, including mixed states, whose distortions tend to zero in both metrics but which stay a fixed uniform distance from every Wigner symmetry. For state spaces, stability holds in each fixed finite dimension with a dimension-dependent modulus tending to zero as $\varepsilon\to0$, but no such modulus can be chosen independently of dimension.
items.authors: Sam Looi

items.title: Imaginary magnetic fields for ultracold atoms
items.abstract: We propose a four-level scheme for generating a uniform imaginary magnetic field for ultracold atoms using Raman coupling and state-dependent particle losses. Eliminating two lossy auxiliary states and subsequently projecting onto one of the two remaining Raman-dressed atomic states, we find that the atomic motion is affected by an imaginary vector potential which is engineered to have a constant curl corresponding to a spatially uniform imaginary synthetic magnetic field. We analytically derive the Gaussian wavepacket dynamics for atoms in such a synthetic magnetic field and study the width-dependent transport, unlike motion in a uniform real magnetic field. We find numerical agreement between the two-level non-Hermitian Hamiltonian and the adiabatic projection description, confirming the applicability of the latter adiabatic approach.
items.authors: Saulius Alminas, Domantas Burba, Gediminas Juzeli\=unas

items.title: Correspondence between Asymptotic Quantum Many-Body Scars in Closed Systems and Diffusive Nambu-Goldstone Modes in Open Systems
items.abstract: Hydrodynamic relaxation in open quantum many-body systems can be understood in terms of diffusive Nambu--Goldstone (NG) modes associated with strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking (SWSSB). Here, we find a common structure underlying weak ergodicity breaking in closed quantum systems and diffusive hydrodynamics in open quantum systems. We establish a spectral correspondence between the parent Hamiltonian of rainbow quantum many-body scar (RQMBS) states in closed systems and the effective Lindbladian of strongly dissipative open systems with strong $U(1)$ symmetry and local charge-dephasing Lindblad operators. For broad classes of spin, fermionic, and bosonic systems, we construct asymptotic RQMBS (ARQMBS) states. Within the enlarged scar subspace, the parent Hamiltonian admits a local Rokhsar--Kivelson-type frustration-free decomposition. A single-mode variational construction gives an $O(k^2)$ upper bound on its lowest excitation energy and yields states satisfying the defining ARQMBS criteria: orthogonality, vanishing energy variance, and characteristic entanglement scaling. Under vectorization, RQMBS states are mapped to maximally mixed infinite-temperature states in fixed-charge sectors, which exhibit long-range SWSSB order under finite-density conditions. Assuming uniformly bounded positive transition rates, the effective Lindbladian has the same local projectors as the parent Hamiltonian but with positive transition-dependent weights, yielding two-sided spectral bounds and the same system-size scaling of their gaps. For uniform rates, the two operators are proportional to each other and their eigenmodes coincide. Therefore, an exact quadratic parent-Hamiltonian branch maps directly to a diffusive NG mode. Our results connect different mechanisms of slow relaxation in closed and open quantum many-body systems.
items.authors: Masaya Kunimi, Taiki Haga, Masaya Nakagawa

items.title: A note on decoherence in quantum cosmology by thermal perturbations: an open quantum systems approach
items.abstract: We study, within a toy model, how a thermal bath of cosmological perturbations can decohere the minisuperspace degrees of freedom of the universe, treating the perturbations as an environment in the framework of open quantum systems. Instead of tracing out the perturbations from a semiclassical ansatz for the total wave function, as in earlier approaches, we incorporate their backreaction on the background through an effective second-order coupling and derive a master equation. The model describes a spatially flat semiclassical universe during slow-roll inflation with a dust clock field, while scalar cosmological perturbations in a phenomenologically assumed thermal state constitute the environment. The master equation is non-Markovian, since the bath correlation functions do not decay in time. Within this framework, we find that, for a representative set of parameter estimates, the characteristic decoherence timescale corresponding to the thermal contribution can be shorter than the Hubble timescale. In addition, we address the question of whether the pointer-state structure induced by the decoherence in such a framework could provide a criterion for the choice of semiclassical states in quantum cosmology.
items.authors: Alexander Kulyabin
items.title_zh: 热扰动下量子宇宙学中的去相干研究
items.summary_zh: 我们在一个玩具模型中研究了宇宙的迷你超空间自由度如何受到宇宙扰动的热浴去相干，采用开放量子系统框架将扰动视为环境。与早期方法不同，我们通过有效的二阶耦合考虑了扰动对背景的反馈，并推导出主方程。该模型描述了在慢滚膨胀期间的空间平坦半经典宇宙，尘埃时钟场作为时钟，而标量宇宙扰动在假定的热态中构成环境。主方程是非马尔可夫的，因为浴的相关函数随时间不衰减。在此框架下，我们发现，对于一组代表性的参数估计，热贡献对应的特征去相干时间尺度可能短于哈勃时间尺度。此外，我们探讨了去相干引发的指针态结构是否能为量子宇宙学中半经典态的选择提供标准。

items.title: Energy, Information, and the Limits of Neuropsychiatric Classification
items.abstract: Importance: The search for reliable neuroimaging biomarkers of mental disorders has remained elusive despite decades of research. Why clinically consequential disorders yield weak neuroimaging separability remains unresolved. Drawing on statistical thermodynamics and the metabolic costs of neural coding, we propose that psychiatric disorders produce constrained deformations of a largely shared repertoire of brain activity patterns, limiting the class-specific information available for classification. Observations: We develop a framework linking physical resource constraints, landscape deformation, distributional separation, and attainable classification, and examine its components using human neuroimaging, synthetic data, and an exactly specified physical model. In resting-state fMRI from 1952 FOR2107 participants (823 with major depressive disorder; 1129 healthy controls), held-out energy-landscape estimates and nonlinear classifiers agreed across 13 comparisons (r = 0.996). Similar results emerged at both FOR2107 centers and in 900 SRPBS participants spanning multiple psychiatric diagnoses. In synthetic data, classification improved with distributional separation and approached the optimum. In an equilibrium three-well model, statistical energy equaled physical potential energy scaled by inverse temperature. Modest deformation redistributed state occupancy while optimal snapshot classification remained weak. A literature map found insufficiently comparable evidence to test the human metabolic constraint. Conclusions: Clinically consequential differences may arise within a largely shared neural repertoire. The thermodynamic framework connects physical deformation to classification under specified assumptions; its metabolic implementation in humans remains untested. Testing this mechanism requires joint measurements of brain activity, bodily physiology, and metabolism.
items.authors: Farbod Khodadadi, Mina Kheirkhah, Bita Shariatpanahi, Sarah Alizadeh, Madleen Stenger, Amaia Zurinaga Gutierrez, Shakiba Bakhshian, Jos\'e C. Garc\'ia Alanis, Nils R. Winter, FOR2107 Consortium, Frank Bremmer, Stefan G. Hofmann, Udo Dannlowski, Tilo Kircher, Sharmili Edwin Thanarajah, Igor Nenadi\'c, Tim Hahn, Hamidreza Jamalabadi

items.title: Full Lyapunov Spectra of Random Neural Networks, Part I: Finite-Time and Asymptotic Theory
items.abstract: We develop a dynamical mean-field framework for the full finite-time and stationary asymptotic Lyapunov spectra of random recurrent neural networks. At finite observation time, an exact log-determinant representation of tangent-propagator singular values leads to a closed-contour matrix Dyson equation for the smoothed spectral tail. In the stationary setting, a cocycle representation yields an operator equation for the asymptotic cumulative spectrum. Both formulations retain complete local gain histories and the repeated action of quenched connectivity. Direct singular-value calculations and network QR spectra support the predictions in the regimes examined, with sampling uncertainty and numerical cutoffs assessed separately. The stationary equation also recovers the known maximal exponent, and controlled gain-history replay illustrates how temporal correlations redistribute instability. This work was carried out in collaboration with ChatGPT 5.6 Sol. Toward the end of preparation we became aware of David G. Clark's contemporaneous work, \emph{Lyapunov spectrum of random neural networks}[arXiv:2610.12426], which reports overlapping mean-field results for the full Lyapunov spectrum using a cavity approach.
items.authors: Haoyu Albert Wang, Wei P. Dai

items.title: Predicting Cognitive Tasks from Single-Channel EEG through Task-Semantic Alignment
items.abstract: Studies of data scaling in electroencephalography (EEG) and related noninvasive recordings suggest that simple wearable devices could eventually reveal more about cognitive states. However, publicly available EEG data are difficult to combine. Different laboratories record different tasks, participants, and devices. Task-agnostic self-supervised learning can exploit such data, but representations learned only with EEG signals have not consistently produced feature representations that are directly effective for decoding the cognitive state. We therefore aimed to incorporate task information by embedding experimental instructions, stimuli and response demands in a common semantic space, and trained an EEG encoder to align signals from a single anterior--posterior differential channel with those task vectors. This framework supports zero-shot prediction without target-condition calibration and few-shot prediction using labeled samples. On a reserved ten-class evaluation, the highest observed zero-shot balanced accuracy was 30.13% (chance 10%). In a separate developmental few-shot experiment, balanced accuracy reached 34.47% using 16 labeled EEG examples per class from another participant, and 74.99% using examples from the test participant's own task recording. Our experiments suggest that training models on datasets with multiple tasks per participant appeared useful, whereas adding datasets containing only one or a few tasks sometimes reduced established performance despite broader task coverage. These exploratory results suggest that EEG datasets that repeat varied cognitive tasks and everyday activities within the same individuals across days, devices and independent studies would be particularly useful for training an EEG foundation model for predicting cognitive states.
items.authors: Ryota Kanai

items.title: Simple model of neurogliovascular unit activity with noradrenaline leading force
items.abstract: In this work we present a model of a neuroglivascular unit associated with a neuronal ensemble. We combine calcium dynamics in the astrocyte, the cascade of synthesis of arachidonic acid and its derivatives, as well as the activity of the network of inhibitory and excitatory neurons with changes in local blood flow. We add equations to the model for extracellular neurotransmitters such as GABA, glutamate, and norepinephrine. We show that the resulting model can exhibit different types of behavior, and also shows a significant connection between the functioning of the neural network and its supporting components.
items.authors: Andrey Yu. Verisokin, Darya V. Verveyko, Alexey R. Brazhe, Stanislav V. Lagosha

items.title: Rethinking World Models for Biosignals
items.abstract: World models promise to learn how systems evolve and respond to actions, enabling simulation, planning and decision-making. Bringing this promise to biosignals requires more than accurate prediction of physiological recordings. We examine existing biosignal world models through two requirements for intervention use: a genuine action and evidence of its causal effect. We identify three fundamental bottlenecks rooted in physiology: Temporal Latency, the variable delay between an action and its observable effect; System Openness, the influence of drivers beyond the modelled intervention; and Endogenous Dynamics, the system's ongoing evolution without that intervention. Drawing on published evidence, we outline corresponding research directions and propose an Intervention-Effect Validation Checklist to guide evaluation. The aim is to help the biosignal community realise the core promise of world models by learning the latent mechanisms that govern physiological evolution and responses to interventions.
items.authors: Xianglong Bao, Bosong Huang, Xiaoda Wang, Keqi Han, Carl Yang, Ming Jin, Shirui Pan

items.title: Rewiring of adult neural networks - learning from structural plasticity across multiple scales
items.abstract: Synaptic connections are continuously formed and eliminated even in adult neuronal networks. This process - called structural plasticity - allows networks to change their topology to learn and adapt to their environment or compensate for lesions. Yet, in contrast to synaptic plasticity, structural plasticity is less well studied and understood. We here present the current state of knowledge as well as open problems in the field along three guiding questions: (1) What regulates structural plasticity in biological neural networks? (2) What are the functional consequences and advantages of structural plasticity in adult neural networks? (3) How can our understanding of structural plasticity be translated into clinical and technological applications? We argue that understanding structural plasticity is a problem involving multiple temporal and spatial scales. Solving this problem thus requires collaborative efforts of experimentalists, theoreticians as well as computational modelers, and has the potential for comprehensive neuroscientific insights that can guide the development of medical applications, artificial neural networks as well as neuromorphic computing.
items.authors: Michael Fauth, Han Lu, Jannik Luboeinski, Johanna Senk, Simone Albani, Valentina Armuzza, Paolo Carloni, Richmond L. Crisostomo, Hermann Cuntz, Ulrich Egert, Eugenio F. items.title: Sense-Making phase transition framework for Affect
items.abstract: Contemporary accounts of affect emphasize different perspectives, ranging from the regulation of bodily states in allostatic approaches to the relational and sense-making character stressed by enactive theories. Here, we show that affect can be made explicit within the sense-making phase transition framework previously introduced for the perception of an inner sensation. Within this same formal structure, each stable minimum of the sense-making potential defines an affective state: its position determines valence, while its depth determines arousal. Affect therefore is not introduced as an independent ingredient, but emerges as the associated state in the valence-arousal space, providing a link between allostatic and enactive approaches to affect. This formulation distinguishes valence intensity from arousal, allows for dominant and secondary affective states, and naturally accommodates mixed-valence configurations beyond a strictly bipolar description. Revisiting representative landscapes of the model, we show how neutral, uncertain, polarized, and mixed-valence regimes arise as a function of contextual sensory information, learned historical evaluation, and externally supplied information. We further show that the resulting valence-arousal relation provides a theoretical basis for the upper-open V-shaped organization discussed in the affect literature, while also opening a natural route toward a dynamical description of affect and emotions.
items.authors: Miguel Bosch, Laura Fanfarillo, Gustavo Diez, Victor G\'omez Mayordomo, J. Ricardo Arias-Gonzalez, Bel\'en Valenzuela

items.title: NeuroVolve: Evolving Visual Stimuli toward Programmable Neural Objectives
items.abstract: What visual information is encoded in individual brain regions, and how do distributed patterns combine to create their neural representations? Prior work has used generative models to replicate known category selectivity in isolated regions (e.g., faces in FFA), but these approaches offer limited insight into how regions interact during complex, naturalistic vision. We introduce NeuroVolve, a generative framework that provides brain-guided image synthesis via optimization of a neural objective function in the embedding space of a pretrained vision-language model. Images are generated under the guidance of a programmable neural objective, i.e., activating or deactivating single regions or multiple regions together. NeuroVolve is validated by recovering known selectivity for individual brain regions, while expanding to synthesize coherent scenes that satisfy complex, multi-region constraints. By tracking optimization steps, it reveals semantic trajectories through embedding space, unifying brain-guided image editing and preferred stimulus generation in a single process. We show that NeuroVolve can generate both low-level and semantic feature-specific stimuli for single ROIs, as well as stimuli aligned to curated neural objectives. These include co-activation and decorrelation between regions, exposing cooperative and antagonistic tuning relationships. Notably, the framework captures subject-specific preferences, supporting personalized brain-driven synthesis and offering interpretable constraints for mapping, analyzing, and probing neural representations of visual information.
items.authors: Haomiao Chen, Keith W Jamison, Mert R. Sabuncu, Amy Kuceyeski

items.title: Interoceptive Attention as Dynamic Homeostatic Prioritization in a Foraging Agent
items.abstract: Biological systems must regulate competing needs under limited perceptual bandwidth, where sharpening one estimate costs the capacity to sharpen the others. Any fixed-budget system therefore has to decide where to allocate its perceptual precision. We study this in a foraging agent that must keep several bodily needs satisfied to survive, modelled with active inference. At each step it reads its own body-state beliefs, identifies the most-needed channel, and reallocates a fixed budget of interoceptive precision toward it, so that the same precision-shaped likelihood feeds both belief update and planning. In AffectWorld, a four-channel foraging gridworld, this selective allocation more than doubles learning-phase survival at matched budget against a uniform-precision agent ($0.414$ vs $0.199$ across 11 layouts, $n{=}32$ seeds each, paired cluster-bootstrap $p \leq 10^{-4}$). Two further results sharpen the mechanism. The benefit runs through planning as well as perception, since denying the shaped likelihood to the planner alone removes about half of it. It is also need-aligned, since aiming precision at the least-needed channel does worse than spreading it evenly. The attended channel additionally learns its own dynamics about twice as fast, and stays ahead even at matched observation count, a behavioural trace of the same precision routing, visible in learning speed, not survival.
items.authors: St John Grimbly, Nicolas Kuske, Evert A. Boonstra, Bruce A. Bassett, Charel van Hoof, Rowan Hodson, Benjamin Rosman, Ryan Smith, Mark Solms, Jonathan P. Shock

items.title: Bayesian adaptive design for neural recruitment curves
items.abstract: Nonlinear response models remain ubiquitous across disciplines with recruitment curves describing muscle response to neural stimulation. Conventional acquisition methods typically rely on static uniform sampling, requiring many stimuli, while adaptive threshold-hunting designs such as ML-PEST forfeit accurate characterization of the overall curve. We present a Bayesian adaptive design that uses posterior uncertainty over curve parameters to propose stimuli that maximize information gain across the full recruitment curve. We additionally implement a focused acquisition method that can target arbitrary subset of curve parameters, which we use to evaluate and interpret our design.
