In simulations, our design outperforms uniform sampling in recovering threshold while matching ML-PEST, and outperforms ML-PEST in predictive curve accuracy while matching uniform. It likewise matches our threshold-focused acquisition, suggesting our design doesn't trade off threshold estimation for recovering the curve. We further show data collected using our design yields greater power when detecting a change in threshold in intervention studies. Our design proposes the next stimulus within 5 seconds, making it feasible for transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) experiments. Finally, we validate our design in TMS experiments and provide a library for Python, called onMEP, for online acquisition of neural recruitment curves.
items.authors: Vishweshwar Tyagi, Saihari S. Dukkipati, Daniel Twili, Jonas M. Mikhaeil, Andrew Gelman, Jason B. Carmel, James R. McIntosh

items.title: Collective Benefits and Efficiency in Coupled Echo State Networks
items.abstract: Simple aggregation of independent responses ("wisdom of crowds") generally improves collective performance through statistical facilitation, but interaction among members can sometimes hinder group outcomes. However, under certain circumstances, coordination studies show that interacting groups can outperform their individual members and nominal groups, and interaction can also be more efficient than independence. We present a reservoir computing model to investigate how interaction can enhance joint performance in terms of accuracy and efficiency. Echo state networks were trained independently to identify Japanese speakers from vowel recordings and tested jointly with and without coupled feedback. Model pairs reproduced the dyadic advantage reported by Bahrami et al. (2010) with interaction via pooled-feedback, but not when independent responses were aggregated together. Model dynamics revealed that interaction was beneficial whereas aggregated outputs were prone to diverging from runaway feedback over time. In terms of efficiency, larger groups of smaller interacting models outperformed smaller groups of larger models while equating for total amount of group computation. Our results offer a formal framework for explaining when and why interaction enhances collective intelligence.
items.authors: Polyphony Bruna, Rick Dale, Michael J. Spivey, Christopher T. Kello

items.title: Spin-Based Modeling of Perception as Emergent from contextualized Internal Evaluation
items.abstract: We develop a microscopic model of perception of an interoceptive sensation in which spin-like variables encode an organism's internal evaluation of embodied vital norms associated with the sensation. Spins can take positive, negative, or neutral values. These local valorizations interact on a lattice embedded in the environmental context, and their collective configuration gives rise to a macroscopic perceptual state. By applying a coarse-graining procedure to a family of symmetric spin models, we derive a macroscopic Landau-type functional that makes explicit the mechanism by which key phenomenological features of perception, emerge from microscopic evaluative interactions. A central result is that the inclusion of a neutral evaluative state fundamentally alters the structure of the perceptual landscape, enhancing entropy, lowering the critical threshold, and increasing sensitivity to contextual input. These results establish a principled link between microscopic evaluative processes and large-scale perceptual organization, offering a flexible framework for integrating perceptual regulation and neurobiological modeling. The model integrates notions of neuroscience and cognitive science using the formalism of condensed matter field theory and providing novel theoretical insights and experimental predictions for conditions such as mental disorders and chronic pain.
items.authors: Laura Fanfarillo, Gustavo Diez, Victor G\'omez Mayordomo, Miguel Bosch, J. Ricardo Arias-Gonzalez, Bel\'en Valenzuela

items.title: Information in a recurrent Retina-V1 network with realistic noise, feedback and nonlinearities
items.abstract: Quantitative estimation of information flow in early vision with psychophysically realistic networks is still an open issue. This is because, up to date, the necessary elements (general and plausible network, accurate noise, and reliable information measures) have not been put together. As a result, previous works made different approximations that limit the generality of their results. This work combines the following elements for the first time: (1) General and plausible recurrent net: a cascade of linear+nonlinear psychophysically tuned layers [IEEE TIP.06, J.Neurophysiol.19, J.Math.Neurosci.20, Neurocomp.24], augmented to consider top-down feedback following [Nat.Neurosci.21,Neurips.22]. (2) Accurate noise in every layer, which is tuned to reproduce psychometric functions both in contrast detection and discrimination following [J.Vision 25]. (3) Reliable information measures that have been checked with analytical results, both in general [IEEE PAMI 24], and in similar visual neuroscience contexts [Neurocomp.24], and hence can be applied in this (more general) case where analytical results are difficult to obtain. The joint use of these elements allows a reliable study of information flow depending on different connectivity schemes (different nonlinearities and interactions), different noise sources, and different stimuli. Results show the benefits of feedback in two ways: (1) the information loss in the data processing inequality along the pathway is reduced by the V1 -- > LGN recurrence for values of feedback that give stable steady state solutions, and (2) the stability of the net is assessed though standard Poincar\'e analysis and we find an optimal value for the feedback in terms of the accuracy of the reconstructed signal from the cortical representation.
items.authors: Javier Rodr\'iguez, Raquel Gim\'enez, Jes\'us Malo

items.title: EEGDash: An open-source platform for machine learning on public neurophysiological data
items.abstract: Public recordings of electroencephalography (EEG), magnetoencephalography (MEG), intracranial EEG (iEEG), functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) and electromyography (EMG) are easy to find and hard to train on. Turning a deposit into model input still means writing download, parsing, repair and windowing code for each dataset, and a dataset that meets a metadata standard can still fail to load. EEGDash is an open-source registry over public Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) datasets from the OpenNeuro and NEMAR archives and from local deposits. Each dataset becomes a Python class; format defects are repaired lazily; signal handling, windowing and format checking are delegated to MNE-Python, Braindecode and the official BIDS validator. Semantic search, a web browser, publication-derived dataset tags and a feature-extraction module share the registry. EEGDash indexes the metadata of 892 public BIDS datasets (43,911 participants and 126,672 hours across the five modalities), loads any of them into a PyTorch dataset without custom data-loading code, and shows on 503 OpenNeuro EEG datasets that passing the BIDS validator does not predict whether a dataset loads (Spearman $\rho = -0.05$), so an archive built for machine learning has to track both.
items.authors: Bruno Aristimunha, Aviv Dotan, Pierre Guetschel, Aman Jaiswal, Gal Ashkenazi, Dung Truong, Kuntal Kokate, Amit Majumdar, Oren Shriki, Arnaud Delorme

items.title: Towards a full-stack functionalist theory of consciousness: Identifying its functional profile
items.abstract: If consciousness is functional, a basic question is what awareness of a content actually changes in how a system operates on it. We ask, for a particular content X and mental or bodily process Y, whether awareness of X changes whether, or how well, X can be used in process Y. Crucially, X-aware and X-unaware conditions must be compared in ways that rule out poorer information about X as a sufficient explanation. Our current literature sweep yields a small but informative functional profile. The clearest current evidence concerns goal-sensitive control, especially regulation of attentional influence, with additional evidence linking awareness to metacognitive evaluation. Meanwhile, one feature-binding paradigm suggests that short-lived feature-location binding and retrieval can remain possible without awareness. This preliminary profile suggests a selective rather than universal immediate functional role for awareness. But such a functional profile is not yet a theory of consciousness. A full-stack functionalist theory must also account for the broader phenomena associated with consciousness - the explanatory profile: the structure and manner of presentation of perceptual and affective experience, subject-world organisation, awareness judgments, and problem reports. Finally, the functional and explanatory profiles constrain theory construction from different directions, but neither determines the process architecture that could connect them. Bridging this gap requires abductive construction: proposing candidate architectures, implementing and intervening on them, and progressively revising them as further constraints accumulate. In sum, we propose a framework for constructing full-stack functionalist theories of consciousness, and take the first step towards detailing the functional profile.
items.authors: Sushrut Thorat, Paras Chopra

items.title: Calibrating AlphaFold confidence scores for interface quality
items.abstract: AlphaFold confidence scores are widely used to rank protein complex predictions and to select subsets of models for downstream applications. Although these scores provide strong discriminatory power for distinguishing prediction quality, their numerical values were never intended to represent the probability that a prediction satisfies a given structural quality criterion. In this work, we calibrate commonly used confidence scores to estimate the probability that a predicted complex exceeds a chosen threshold of DockQ, an established measure of interface quality. On antibody-antigen and general multimer datasets, post-hoc isotonic calibration consistently improves agreement between predicted probabilities and observed DockQ success rates while preserving the underlying score ordering. The calibrated probabilities also provide more accurate estimates of the fraction of selected models expected to pass a given structural quality threshold. Although the mapping is fitted within a given prediction distribution and therefore transfers imperfectly across prediction domains, we show that reliable estimates are recovered from a small number of labeled target-domain samples. Because the calibration is entirely post hoc and requires no underlying AlphaFold model fine-tuning, it provides a straightforward and customizable way to convert existing model quality rankings into calibrated probabilities of passing a chosen structural quality threshold.
items.authors: Sagyndyk Sagadinov, Vsevolod Viliuga, Arne Elofsson

items.title: Homogeneity and heterogeneity of functional element composition of genome units across human and seven model organisms
items.abstract: Is a chromosome a miniature of its genome, with the same mix of functional elements as the whole? We ask this of eight annotated genomes: human, mouse, zebrafish, Caenorhabditis elegans, Drosophila melanogaster, Saccharomyces cerevisiae, Arabidopsis thaliana and maize. Elements are classified in a four-level hierarchy, from five major classes (protein-coding genes, ncRNA genes, transposable elements (TEs), pseudogenes, IG/TR gene segments) down to finer classes. Units are chromosomes or arms, cytogenetic bands, equal cuts of each chromosome, and random segments of matching size. We compare each unit with the genome and with other units, call compositions homogeneous when they differ by less than 5%, and score each against a random sample of the same size. The first finding is a surprising homogeneity. The level-1 compositions of the major chromosomes match each other and the genome in maize, zebrafish, yeast and C. elegans, and in fly down to the major arms. Finer classes can be homogeneous too: protein function in Arabidopsis, and the Wicker TE orders in maize. Enzyme reaction classes are interchangeable between chromosomes in all eight genomes. The second finding is a structured heterogeneity. Where a unit departs from its genome, it does so in one of three ways: clusters of named elements, such as rRNA genes or immune receptor loci; megabase-scale compartments, such as TE-rich pericentromeric heterochromatin; and lineage-specific gene families, visible only at the finest levels. Corrected for chance, the genomes fall into groups. For protein function and gene families, composition is more uniform in plants and fly than in vertebrates, and least uniform in C. elegans. For the major classes and TE orders, uniformity follows where each genome places its repeats, along the arms (maize, zebrafish) or around the centromeres (Arabidopsis, fly), not its lineage.
items.authors: Yanying Wu

items.title: manylp: reproducible, exact, and batched linear programming for genome-scale dynamic flux balance analysis
items.abstract: Dynamic flux balance analysis (dFBA) and its community, spatial and ensemble variants predict microbial metabolism by solving one linear program (LP) per species and time step, often 10^6 to 10^8 LPs per study. These LPs share their constraint matrix and objective and differ only in their bounds, yet general-purpose solvers treat each one independently, and GPU first-order solvers struggle with the degenerate, badly scaled matrices of genome-scale models. Moreover, metabolic optima are usually faces rather than vertices, so solvers return arbitrary flux vectors and dFBA predictions depend on the solver used. We present manylp, a batched solver for such bounds-parametric LP families that returns certified vertex solutions. Building on the bunching technique of stochastic programming, manylp caches optimal bases and certifies whole batches with one dense matrix product per basis on CPUs or GPUs; LPs outside the cached critical regions are re-solved by a warm-started lexicographic dual simplex, and new bases are propagated across the batch. Each LP is certified optimal and unique under a lexicographic flux rule, or infeasible, in independent double-precision arithmetic. On a genome-scale dFBA workload, manylp certified 47,889 LPs per second on a CPU, 12 to 33 times faster than HiGHS, Gurobi, FICO Xpress, GLPK and OR-Tools (32 processes), and reached 682,000 LPs per second on one GPU for community ensembles, needing 76 simplex solves for 94.6 million LPs. Integrated into the muODE simulator, it accelerated single trajectories 84-fold and 16-member ensembles 635-fold, and made adaptive Runge-Kutta integration affordable, reducing biomass errors 83-fold. Integrating 49 equally optimal flux policies in one batched run showed that alternative optima change predicted acetate 4.2-fold and shift community composition. manylp is open source: https://github.com/cumbof/manylp.
items.authors: Fabio Cumbo

items.title: Training-Data Extraction from Genomic Language Models
items.abstract: Genomic language models generate long nucleotide continuations from short prefixes, exposing a direct route for studying training-sequence extraction through the generation interface. We present an output-only black-box attack on Evo 2 that selects convergent groups of repeated generations without gradients, token likelihoods, or training-corpus access during candidate selection. Recovered content is then scored by an evaluator combining aligned length, nucleotide identity, match multiplicity, and sequence complexity. Across 304 runs on Evo 2 7B with bacteriophage and plasmid prefixes, the attack yields 888 candidate clusters, of which 85 match training segments of at least 500 bp, giving a cluster-level attack success rate of 9.57%. Final filtering retains 22 uniquely matched extraction events at the 500-bp threshold and 15 at 1,000 bp, covering 14 and 7 distinct training-sequence regions, respectively. Within-category source-homology screening retains 11 of the 22 events at a 99% exclusion threshold and four at 98%, with the latter mapping to two reference regions. The results establish convergence among repeated nucleotide generations as a practical output-only signal for recovering long training-sequence segments and characterize how recovery depends on prefix length, cluster size, perplexity, early stopping, and sequence domains.
items.authors: Tianhao Mao, Zihao Wang, Dongfang Zhao, Rui Zhu, Xiaofeng Wang, Haixu Tang

items.title: CellChain: Benchmarking Cross-Scale Evidence Use for Perturbation Reasoning
items.abstract: Recent advances in foundation models and large-scale cellular perturbation datasets have driven growing interest in using LLMs to predict and reason about cellular responses. Biological reasoning in this setting involves relating molecular mechanisms, cellular responses, and functional outcomes across scales. Evaluating foundation models therefore requires assessing not only whether their predictions are correct, but also how those predictions depend on the biological evidence provided. We introduce CellChain, an experimentally grounded benchmark comprising 590 biological cases and 2,360 matched evidence-condition instances across gene-dependency prediction, cytokine-axis identification, and drug-sensitivity ranking. CellChain links perturbation experiments and external biological resources through a provenance-aware evidence graph spanning molecular, pathway, transcriptional, and phenotypic information. Task-specific conditions vary evidence coverage, composition, or assignment while preserving questions, candidate answers, reference targets, and scoring rules. Across 18 foundation models, the highest accuracies under prespecified target-evidence conditions are 57.5%, 75.5%, and 70.8%, respectively, and broader evidence coverage does not consistently improve accuracy. On the drug-sensitivity benchmark cohort, matched reference histories outperform swapped histories by an average of 13.0 percentage points in cluster-weighted accuracy. Decision-transition analysis separates corrections, newly introduced errors, and wrong-answer switches, revealing substantial answer changes hidden by small net accuracy differences. CellChain provides controlled comparisons for attributing changes in model predictions to prespecified expansions of biological context, including changes in evidence coverage, composition, and biological assignment.
items.authors: Xue Xia, Yue Wang, Shuizhou Chen, Lang Yu, Hao Wu, Wenxuan Huang, Chengkai Yao, Zhangyang Gao, Siqi Sun

items.title: Spatial Kernel Restricted Canonical Correlation Analysis: Population Targets, Identifiability, and Stability
items.abstract: Relating observations of different categories across space requires methods that accommodate distinct sampling locations and spatial dependence. Spatial kernel restricted canonical correlation analysis (skrCCA) uses spatial weights to identify associated feature combinations across data categories. Here, we develop a statistical theory of its covariance form after feature reduction. Conditional on the observed locations and under a mean-zero model, the pairwise association matrices target kernel-weighted averages of cross-covariances. For prespecified directions, we derive the exact null variance under independence between blocks. We establish recovery and stability bounds in two- and multiblock settings under explicit population models, and show that exact cyclic updates have convergent objective values. The variance characterization shows how spatial weighting and within-block dependence jointly determine the effective information available for estimating association. The recovery bounds separate statistical and optimization error, relating stability to population separation and the strength of connections between blocks. These results clarify what fitted spatial association axes estimate and provide conditions under which they can be recovered reliably.
items.authors: Zhen Miao, Yilong Qu, Nancy R. Zhang

items.title: Taxonomic Classification with Tag Arrays
items.abstract: Taxonomic classifiers based on exact matches differ in which matches they use and in how each match splits its credit among the taxa containing it: Kraken~2 gives a $k$-mer's credit to the lowest common ancestor of those taxa, SPUMONI~2 labels each position of the read, Tagger gives each maximal exact match (MEM) one label, and Cliffy splits a match's credit evenly over a roughly logarithmic sample of the taxa. We compare these schemes on the same long MEMs, mainly on short 16S rRNA reads classified to genera with SILVA, where credit proportional to the number of occurrences of the MEM in each taxon is the most accurate, by 1.0 to 6.8 percentage points. We compute long MEMs with Boyer--Moore--Li on a run-length compressed suffix array, and count their occurrences in each taxon with a complete, run-length compressed tag array, in time proportional to the number of tag runs in the MEM's BWT interval, without locating any occurrence. We bound the number of tag runs in terms of the BWT runs and of how often suffixes with long common prefixes have different tags, and show that tags constant on $d$ blocks of the text have a macro scheme with at most $r + 2d$ phrases. On SILVA our index takes 1.44\,GB and classifies a read in 66\,$\mu$s with one thread at 93.8\% accuracy, about what Cliffy reports for its 9\,GB index; over minimizer digests it takes 0.49\,GB and reaches 92.5\%, against 84.2\% for Cliffy's digested index on the same reads. On nanopore reads from whole genomes, where almost every long MEM occurs in one species, we instead use each read's longest MEMs, found in one pass of a variant of Boyer--Moore--Li with a $k$-mer filter, which assigns 99.6\% of the reads to their species with no length threshold.
items.authors: Travis Gagie, Gonzalo Navarro

items.title: Satisfiability and freezing in random integer programs
items.abstract: We study a model of a random centrally symmetric polytope and ask about the existence of points in the polytope with non-zero, integer coordinates. Our main results are the location of a sharp threshold for the existence of these integer points, a characterization of the typical empirical distribution of their coordinates, and showing that near the feasibility threshold these integer points are almost always totally isolated --- at linear Hamming distance to the nearest other integer point in the polytope. The behavior of these random integer programs is related to that of the symmetric binary perceptron (the case when coordinates of points are $\pm 1$-valued). The lack of symmetry in the set of potential solutions leads to new questions and phenomena, such as the distribution of the coordinate sizes in typical solutions, and requires the development of new information-theoretic techniques to deal with higher-dimensional optimization problems arising in the method of moments.
items.authors: Dylan J. Altschuler, Ruben Ascoli, Will Perkins

items.title: Linear stability and divisibility gaps for Gaussian maxima
items.abstract: We study Gaussian maxima arising from isotropic families of unit vectors and show that their excess expected maximum is controlled by the distance from an orthonormal basis. We apply this stability result to correlation matrices with equal nonzero eigenvalues, obtaining an exact minimum when the matrix size is divisible by the rank and a quantitative gap otherwise. In dimension two, we determine the leading asymptotic term and describe the structure of near-optimal configurations. We also obtain covariance-block recovery results and a finite-dimensional lower bound for the higher-rank limiting problem.
items.authors: Chahel Paatur

items.title: Geometry of semi-infinite geodesics in the Airy line ensemble
items.abstract: We study the geometry of semi-infinite geodesics in the Airy line ensemble. We establish sharp estimates for disjointness probabilities involving geodesics with nearby directions and endpoints in the top line of the Airy line ensemble. Moreover, we obtain a power law upper bound on the coalescence depth of two semi-infinite geodesics with same asymptotic direction and establish exponential concentration estimates for geodesic jump times more generally. We also establish pathwise H\"{o}lder $1/2^-$-continuity of Busemann profiles associated to semi-infinite geodesics with common asymptotic directions (in terms of the asymptotic direction). We characterize exceptional behaviour of semi-infinite geodesics through their Busemann profiles and establish geometric properties of the associated sets of non-coalescence and non-uniqueness. Finally, we determine the Hausdorff dimensions of collections of semi-infinite geodesics: collections with a fixed top-line endpoint and arbitrary positive asymptotic direction almost surely have Hausdorff dimension $1$, while collections with a fixed positive direction and arbitrary endpoint almost surely have Hausdorff dimension $3/2$.
items.authors: Pantelis Tassopoulos, Sourav Sarkar

items.title: Fluctuations of the quadratic matching cost on the flat torus: dimensions five and higher
items.abstract: We prove a central limit theorem for the quadratic matching cost between the uniform measure and its empirical counterpart on the flat torus in dimensions $d\ge5$. Let $\mu$ be Haar probability measure on $\mathbb{T}^d$ and let $\mu_n$ be the empirical measure of $n$ independent samples from $\mu$. Then $$ \begin{aligned} \frac{W_2^2(\mu_n,\mu)-\mathbb{E}W_2^2(\mu_n,\mu)} {\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}(W_2^2(\mu_n,\mu))}} &\Longrightarrow N(0,1),\\ c_dn^{-1-4/d} \le \operatorname{Var}(W_2^2(\mu_n,\mu)) &\le C_dn^{-1-4/d}, \end{aligned} $$ for positive constants $c_d,C_d$ depending only on $d$ and all sufficiently large $n$. The proof introduces a random-walk approach to matching fluctuations. We construct a random walk that jumps between neighboring cells of the optimal partition and use it to describe how the matching cost responds to changes in the sample. Estimates for this walk control the effect of replacing one sample point and the interaction between two replacements. These bounds yield the variance estimates and allow us to apply a martingale central limit theorem.
items.authors: Shi Feng

items.title: Variance Bounds for Minimum Perfect Matching Problem by Random Walk on Multinomial Distribution
items.abstract: We establish variance upper bounds for the minimum perfect matching problem in general metric spaces under a geometric partition condition. As a principal application, let $H_n$ be the minimum perfect matching cost of $n$ independent uniform points in $[0,1]^d$, where $n$ is even and $d\ge2$. We prove $$\operatorname{Var}(H_n)\le C d n^{1-2/d},$$ where $C$ is independent of $n$ and $d$. This removes the logarithmic losses in earlier upper bounds in every dimension (Talagrand, 1995); in particular, the variance remains bounded in dimension two, answering an open question (Rhee, 1994). The proof relies on constructing a rapidly mixing Markov process with a multinomial stationary distribution.
items.authors: Shi Feng

items.title: Poisson contingency tables, Gibbs permutations, and entropic optimal transport
items.abstract: We study random contingency tables obtained by conditioning a matrix of independent Poisson entries on its row and column sums. We identify such a table with the block counts of a random permutation drawn from a Gibbs measure of Mallows type, an exact coupling whose normalizing constants recover Barvinok's permanent identity. We use this correspondence to study the table at three scales. For finite dimensions, a transference principle compares the table with a matrix of independent Poisson entries whose means form the static Schr\"odinger bridge, the solution of a discrete entropic optimal transport problem. As the dimensions grow and the margins and prior means converge, the normalized histogram of the table converges to a limiting Schr\"odinger bridge at a quantitative rate. The fluctuations of the table around the bridge are characterized in two complementary ways. Linear statistics satisfy a central limit theorem for bounded test functions, with limiting variance equal to the squared $L^2$-distance, under the bridge, of the test function to the subspace of additively separable functions; as a process they converge to white noise with intensity given by the bridge, conditioned to have vanishing marginals. Spectrally, the limiting spectral distribution of the centered table is governed by a Dyson equation whose variance profile is the density of the bridge. The key ingredient is an asymptotic formula for the partition function of the Gibbs measure in terms of a Fredholm determinant given by the canonical correlations of the bridge. For Mallows-type random permutations, our results prove Pal's conjecture on the limiting partition function and Mukherjee's conjecture on the central limit theorem for linear statistics, both in greater generality.
items.authors: Danny Duan, Hanbaek Lyu, William Powell

items.title: Occupation Times at a Moving Interface and Sharp Yosida Rates for MacKean-Vlasov BSDE with Jumps and Fuzzy Selections
items.abstract: We study a forward-backward McKean-Vlasov system with jumps whose backward equation contains a source obtained by evaluating the minimal-norm selection of a maximal monotone operator along the forward state. This selection changes branch across an interface that moves with the state law, the control, and an imprecisely known parameter described by fuzzy cuts. Assuming normal non-degeneracy and finite-statistics dependence of the interface on the law, we prove that the first and second moments of the time spent within a given distance of the interface are bounded, respectively, by a constant times that distance and by a constant times its square. The second-moment estimate makes it possible to integrate the source error before squaring it, which yields a Yosida error of first order in the regularization parameter in the natural solution norm; a first-moment argument gives only order one half. An explicit example shows that the first-order rate is sharp. For compact classes of admissible selections, the corresponding solutions form the cuts of a fuzzy solution set. These cuts are compact, stable with respect to the fuzzy level and the data, and approximated at the same first-order rate in Hausdorff distance. All estimates are uniform over a non-dominated family of probability measures representing volatility uncertainty. The quantitative results are obtained for separable quadratic potentials with finitely many affine branches.
items.authors: Kayembe Tshiswaka Tcheick, Mabela Matendo Rostin, Kabengele Mpunga Yannick, Bosonga Bofeki Jean-Pierre

items.title: Upper tail large deviation for the first passage time in the frog model on $Z^d$ with $d\geq 2$
items.abstract: We study upper tail large deviations for the first passage time in the frog model on $\mathbb Z^d$, $d\ge 2$. Let $\mathrm{T}(0,x)$ denote the first time at which the infection, started from the origin, reaches $x$, and let $\mu$ be the associated time constant. We prove that, for any Euclidean unit vector $v\in\mathbb R^d$ and $\xi>0$, \[ \lim_{n\to\infty} -\frac{1}{\mathfrak{s}_d(n)} \log \mathbb{P}\bigl(\mathrm{T}(0,\lfloor nv\rfloor) \ge (\mu(v)+\xi)n\bigr) =\mathfrak{r}_d\xi, \] where $\mathfrak s_2(n)=n/\log n$ and $\mathfrak r_2=\pi$ for $d=2$; $\mathfrak s_d(n)=n$ and $\mathfrak r_d$ is the escape probability of simple random walk for $d\ge3$. Moreover, on the upper tail large deviation event, we show that a certain slowdown mechanism occurs near the endpoint. To rule out other mechanisms, we analyze the growth of the infection near the starting point using a modified exploration process, and investigate its propagation through the intermediate region using the renormalization and covering arguments.
items.authors: Van Hao Can, Naoki Kubota, Shuta Nakajima

items.title: Poisson occupancy of paths on permuted regular graphs
items.abstract: In the classical occupancy problem, $B$ balls are placed independently and uniformly into $d$ boxes. We study a graph analogue of this model. Let $G$ be a directed $r$-regular graph on $d$ vertices and fix a vertex $i$. Consider all paths of length $L$ starting from $i$, and let $N_L(i,j)$ denote the number of such paths ending at a vertex $j$. Thus the vertices play the role of boxes and the $r^L$ paths play the role of balls. In general, these occupancies depend strongly on the geometry of $G$. We show that inserting independent uniform permutations between successive layers restores the classical Poisson behavior at the empirical level. Although the path endpoints remain strongly dependent, their empirical occupancy distribution has the same limiting Poisson law as independent balls thrown into boxes. More precisely, at the critical scale $r^L/d\to\lambda\in(0,\infty)$, provided $rL/d \to 0$, the empirical path multiplicity distribution converges in Wasserstein distance to $\operatorname{Pois}(\lambda)$, independently of the geometry of the underlying graphs. We also prove a local Poisson limit theorem and a Berry-Esseen bound for the empirical distribution functions. These estimates determine the full total-variation transition of the normalized path multiplicities toward uniformity. For arbitrary doubly stochastic kernels, we further establish exact covariance and Frobenius norm identities, together with an exact contraction formula for the chi-square divergence. As applications, we study synchronous opinion averaging, obtaining an explicit cutoff profile for equal-size groups and quantitative convergence to consensus for heterogeneous group sizes.
items.authors: Rafael Chiclana

items.title: Multi-type $\Lambda$-Wright--Fisher processes with polynomial drift: Bernstein duality, long-term behaviour, and simulation of moments
items.abstract: The $(d+1)$-type $\Lambda$-Wright--Fisher process with polynomial drift is a L\'evy-type process on the $d$-dimensional unit simplex whose generator entails a particular jump and diffusive component, as well as a polynomial drift component. In this work, the process is connected to a (Bernstein) dual process, which admits an interpretation as an urn model with coloured balls. Exploiting this duality, we identify various parameter regimes: one in which the $\Lambda$-Wright--Fisher process is absorbed almost surely at a vertex of the simplex, and others in which it admits a unique nontrivial ergodic probability measure. The results include verifiable criteria for absorption versus persistence, as well as representations of absorption and stationary measures. Moreover, the duality relation is exploited to devise and implement a simulation-based approach for estimating moments of the $\Lambda$-Wright--Fisher process.
items.authors: Sebastian Hummel

items.title: From Cauchy to Gaussian: Sharp Lower Deviations and Ehrhard-Type Inequality
items.abstract: We establish dimension-free, pointwise optimal lower-deviation bounds for convex functions under spherically symmetric Cauchy-type measures. These bounds use either mean-variance normalization or moments about the median, the latter covering the Cauchy case where the mean and variance are unavailable. By approximation with a parametrized family the Cauchy-type measures, our results recover the Gaussian setting of Paouris and Valettas \cite{PaourisValettas18} and strengthen their variance-sensitive estimate to a sharp bound, with a complete equality characterization. This goes beyond the partial improvements obtained in subsequent work. We also prove an Ehrhard-type inequality for arbitrary convex sets under these Cauchy-type measures in every dimension and characterize all equality cases. This resolves a conjecture posed by Byczkowski, Ma\l ecki and \.{Z}ak \cite{ByczkowskiMaleckiZak22}. The proof follows from a variational argument combined with the joint concavity of fiber rearrangement. The geometric inequality reduces distributions of convex observables to one-dimensional convex transforms, yielding the sharp lower-deviation bounds.
items.authors: Yong Huang, Shengyu Tang, Sinan Wang

items.title: Overlap distributions under the Gibbs measure of a Haar model of $\log|\zeta|$ on and near the critical line
items.abstract: We study the Gibbs measure of $H(h) = \Re\sum_{p^{j} \leq X}U_{p}^{j}/(j p^{j(\sigma + i h)})$, a random field modeling large values of the log-modulus of the Riemann zeta function on and near the critical line, where the $U_{p}$ are independent and uniformly distributed on the complex unit circle. Writing $t = \log \log T$, the cutoff $X$ and real part $\sigma$ may vary with $T$ subject to $T^{1/t^{\Phi}} \leq X \leq T^{1/t^{\phi}}$ and $0 \leq \sigma - 1/2 \leq C_{\sigma}t^{\Phi}/\log T$, for fixed $\Phi \geq \phi > 1/2$ and $C_{\sigma} > 0$. On $I_{\theta} = [ - (\log T)^{\theta},(\log T)^{\theta}]$, define the Gibbs measure $G_{\beta,\sigma,T}^{\mathrm{H}}(\mathrm{d}h) := e^{\beta H(h)}\mathrm{d}h/\int_{I_{\theta}}e^{\beta H(h')}\mathrm{d}h'$. For every fixed $\theta > - 1$ and inverse temperature $\beta > 0$, the limiting joint distributions of correlations (overlaps) among points sampled from this measure are determined after averaging over the Haar phases. At and below $\beta_{c}(\theta) = 2\sqrt{1 + (\theta \vee 0)}$, the limiting two-overlap distribution is concentrated at $q_{0} = |\theta \wedge 0|$. Above this threshold, it assigns masses $\beta_{c}(\theta)/\beta$ and $1 - \beta_{c}(\theta)/\beta$ to $q_{0}$ and $1$, respectively, and the limiting joint overlap distribution is described by a Poisson-Dirichlet process of parameter $\beta_{c}(\theta)/\beta$. Approximate Ghirlanda-Guerra identities are shown to hold uniformly for bounded deterministic functions of the sampled positions. This paper is the first in a series devoted to extending these results to $\log|\zeta|$ near the critical line.
items.authors: Fr\'ed\'eric Ouimet

items.title: Non-uniqueness for McKean--Vlasov SDEs with H\"older diffusion coefficients
items.abstract: We show that uniqueness may fail for one-dimensional McKean--Vlasov stochastic differential equations with H\"older continuous diffusion coefficients. More precisely, for every \(\alpha\in(1/2,1)\), we construct an equation with a diffusion coefficient that is \(\alpha\)-H\"older continuous in the state variable, Lipschitz continuous in the measure variable, and of linear growth, for which uniqueness in law and pathwise uniqueness fail. The construction relies on a spreading estimate together with a Schauder fixed-point argument.
items.authors: Martin Bergerhausen, Paul Nikolaev, David J. Pr\"omel

items.title: An Exact Hausdorff Measure as Natural Length for SLE
items.abstract: Fix $0<\kappa<8$ and put $d=1+\kappa/8$. Recent work by OpenAI identifies an explicit exact Hausdorff gauge \( h_\kappa(r)=r^d\bigl(\log\log(1/r)\bigr)^{(2-d)/2} \) for sufficiently small $r$ for chordal $\mathrm{SLE}_\kappa$: the corresponding Hausdorff measure is almost surely positive and finite on every segment $\gamma([s,t])$ with $0<s<t<\infty$, and has finite expectation in bounded subsets of the plane. We show that this Hausdorff measure is a deterministic positive constant multiple of the occupation measure (natural length) constructed by Lawler and Rezaei.
items.authors: Dapeng Zhan

items.title: Killing random motions with finite velocity
items.abstract: In this paper, we study finite-velocity random motions subject to a killing mechanism acting at direction changes: at each change of direction, the motion is killed with a fixed probability and remains at its current position thereafter. We first consider the one-dimensional case of a standard telegraph process. We derive the exact distribution of the position at the killing time and show that it is Laplace distributed. We also characterize the law of the process conditional on survival up to a fixed time, proving that it coincides with that of a standard telegraph process driven by a thinned Poisson process with reduced switching intensity. We further derive the full time-dependent distribution of the killed process, including both its absolutely continuous and singular components. We then extend the analysis to a planar finite-velocity random motion with infinitely many possible directions. In this setting, we derive the distribution of the killed process and obtain an explicit representation of its density in terms of modified Bessel functions and a series involving Bessel polynomials.
items.authors: Enzo Orsingher, Manfred Marvin Marchione

items.title: Last-Coverage Probabilities of Random Walks on Cycle Graphs for Symmetric, Biased, and Time-Dependent Walks
items.abstract: This paper studies the last-coverage vertex of a nearest-neighbour random walk on a cycle: the vertex most likely to be the final one discovered. We show that the visited vertices always form a single contiguous arc of the ring, a property we call the Connected Arc Property. This lets the walk be replaced by a two-state time-inhomogeneous Markov chain, which we call the interval-expansion representation, in which each expansion step has a probability given by the classical gambler's ruin formula. Within this framework we prove that the last-coverage probability of node k in an n-node cycle is (1-r)r^(n-1-k)/(1-r^(n-1)), where r = (1-p)/p and p is the clockwise transition probability. As p approaches 1/2, we recover the uniform distribution, giving an independent derivation of a classical result. For a walk with a deterministic time-varying bias, we give an exact series representation for the last-coverage probabilities, together with a finite truncation that serves as a computable, error-bounded approximation. All results are validated by Monte Carlo simulation, and we run experiments on sinusoidal time-varying bias. Finally, we compare generalized Petersen graphs with Erdos-Renyi graphs of matching size, finding that structural symmetry is associated with more uniform last-coverage distributions.
items.authors: Kiyan Idnani, Jad Salem

items.title: Weak universality of global dynamics for the fractional hyperbolic $\Phi^4_3$-model
items.abstract: We continue the study of weak universality for the fractional hyperbolic $\Phi^4_3$-model initiated by Tzvetkov, Wang, and the author (2023). In this work, we establish weak universality in a regime where the associated Gibbs measure is mutually singular with respect to the underlying Gaussian measure. We first investigate the weak convergence of the Gibbs measures associated with macroscopic models to the fractional $\Phi^4_3$-measure constructed by Tzvetkov, Wang, and the author (2023). We then obtain a structured representation for these Gibbs measures via the stochastic quantization method. Finally, we prove dynamical weak universality for the fractional hyperbolic $\Phi^4_3$-model by using an extended second order expansion and exploiting the invariance of the Gibbs measures.
items.authors: Ruoyuan Liu

items.title: Explicit descriptions of all 1-Meixner random vectors
items.abstract: The 1-Meixner random vectors consist of $d$ real-valued random variables, having finite moments of all orders, for which the commutators between their joint semi-quantum operators and the multiplication operators that they generate are linear combinations of these multiplication operators and the identity operator. This property of random variables imposes a system of first-order partial differential equations on their joint Laplace transform on a neighborhood of $0$ in a Euclidean $d$-space. We provide explicit descriptions of all solutions of the system just mentioned in every dimension $d$.
items.authors: Florin Catrina, Andrzej Derdzinski, Aurel I. Stan

items.title: Weighted moments and sharp convergence rates for supercritical multitype branching processes
items.abstract: Let $Z_n^i=(Z_n^i(1),\cdots,Z_n^i(d)), n\geqslant0$, be a supercritical $d$-type branching process starting from a single particle of type $i\in\{1,\cdots,d\}$, where $d$ is a positive integer. The Kesten-Stigum theorem states that if the mean matrix $M$ of the offspring distribution has spectral radius $\rho>1$ with the associated positive left and right eigenvectors $u$ and $v$, then for all $1\leqslant i \leqslant d$, the sequence $W_n^i=\langle Z_n^i,u\rangle/\rho^n u(i)$ forms a non-negative martingale, and hence converges almost surely to a random variable $W^i$ as $n\rightarrow\infty$. In this paper, we investigate the asymptotic properties of the martingale $\{W_n^i\}$, focusing on weighted moments and sharp rates of convergence. We establish necessary and sufficient conditions for the finiteness of $\phi$-moments of $W^i$, where $\phi(x)=x^{\alpha}\ell(x)$ with $\alpha\geqslant1$ and $\ell$ is a positive function slowly varying at infinity. We also determine the sharp exponential rate of convergence of $W_n^i$ to $W^i$ in the $\phi$-moment sense, identify a phase transition at the critical rate $\rho^{1/2},$ and characterize the behavior at the critical value. Our proofs rely on the double martingale structure of the fundamental martingale and on convex inequalities for martingales.
items.authors: Sheng Xiao, Yingqiu Li, Xingang Liang

items.title: Invariant Measures for Interacting Continuous-State Population Models
items.abstract: We study invariant probabilities for nonlinear two-population branching systems with competition, cooperation, or predator--prey interaction, driven by Brownian noise and spectrally positive stable jumps. Without immigration, every invariant probability of a conservative competitive or predator--prey system is concentrated on the boundary under either boundary convention. With nontrivial axis dynamics, coordinatewise continuation admits only the point mass at the origin. For cooperative systems, we give criteria for boundary concentration and interior stationarity, including a sharp criterion for bilinear cooperation with a common relative noise exponent. With immigration, explicit parameter conditions yield existence and stationary moment bounds. For square-root diffusions with positive immigration, these conditions ensure interior concentration and full support on the closed quadrant. Further lower bounds on immigration rates give uniqueness and convergence of time-averaged transition laws.
items.authors: Lina Ji, Jie Xiong, Wen Xu, Xu Yang

items.title: A Berry--Esseen Bound of Order $(1+\log n)/\sqrt n$ for Peng's Central Limit Theorem
items.abstract: We derive a quantitative central limit theorem under sublinear expectations from a spatial endpoint regularity estimate for the one-dimensional \(G\)-heat equation. For bounded Lipschitz initial data, the second spatial derivative and the time derivative of its solution are Lipschitz in space and \(1/2\)-H\"older in time away from the initial time. In particular, \([u_{xx}(t,\cdot)]_{\mathrm{Lip}}\le C_G\Lip(\phi)/t\). Combining this estimate with the nonlinear Stein identity introduced in Song \cite{Song2020} and a replacement argument yields a bound of order \((1+\log n)/\sqrt n\) for bounded Lipschitz tests when the third absolute moment is finite and the lower variance is positive. The final replacement step is estimated directly, avoiding the nonintegrable singularity at time zero.
items.authors: Yongsheng Song

items.title: Maximum degree for random geometric graphs in the connectivity regime and beyond
items.abstract: A random geometric graph is a random graph model whose vertex set is a binomial point process, where two vertices are connected by an edge if each lies within the ball of radius $r$ centered at the other. In this paper, we investigate the asymptotic fluctuations of the threshold radius required for the maximum degree of the graph to reach a target value. Assuming this target value grows with the number of vertices $n$ at an order of at least $\log n$ but strictly less than $(\log n)^d$, we show that these fluctuations follow a Gumbel distribution. We also investigate the spatial configurations of vertices with extremely large degrees, and show that the point process marked by their degrees converges in distribution to a Poisson point process.
items.authors: Junpei Otsuka

items.title: Sharp Rogers--Shephard Inequalities for R\'enyi Entropy
items.abstract: We establish sharp weighted Rogers--Shephard inequalities for R\'enyi differential entropy. For independent copies $X,X'$ of a log-concave random vector in $\R^n$, we prove $h_p(aX-bX')\le h_p(X)+n\log(a+b)$ for all $a,b>0$ and $1\le p\le\infty$, where orders $1$ and $\infty$ correspond to Shannon entropy and min-entropy, respectively. The Shannon case settles the entropic Rogers--Shephard conjecture of Madiman and Kontoyiannis and its higher-dimensional formulation. For $1\le p<\infty$, equality holds precisely for invertible affine images of random vectors with independent exponential coordinates. At $p=\infty$, the larger equality class is characterized by possibly extended-valued convex potentials that are positively homogeneous of degree one. For every $0<p<1$, uniform laws on sufficiently high-dimensional simplices violate the unweighted bound. Thus $p=1$ is the critical order for this bound to hold in every dimension. The proof combines weighted convex intersections with an exponential lift to a log-affine probability density. At the Shannon endpoint, this lift yields an exact deficit decomposition with a conditional mutual information term for an additive channel with asymmetric Laplace noise.
items.authors: Bang-Xian Han, Guoqing Zhan, Chiyu Zhou, Zhuo-Nan Zhu

items.title: Uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for singular $L^k$ interaction kernels with rates
items.abstract: Based on a semigroup approach, we prove quantitative uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for two systems of interacting particles with singular interaction kernels $K$ of type $L^k$, $k>d$, and a contractive Lipschitz confinement force field. First, we consider a system with moderate interaction, which means that the particles interact through the mollified kernel $K\ast V^N$, for some approximation of identity $V^N = N^{d\alpha} V(N^\alpha \cdot),\, \alpha>0$. Assuming that $\|K\|_{L^k}$ is sufficiently small, we obtain that for any $\varepsilon>0$ the uniform-in-time rate is of order $N^{-\min\left(\alpha,\frac12-\frac{d\alpha}{2}-\varepsilon\right)}$, plus an exponentially small in time contribution of the initial condition. Second, for the classical, non-mollified particle system we establish uniform-in-time propagation of chaos with rate $N^{-\min\left(\alpha,\frac12-\frac{d\alpha}{2}-\varepsilon\right)} + \|K-K\ast V^N\|_{L^{k}}$, plus an exponentially small in time contribution of the initial condition. The method relies on the regularity properties of the solution of the associated nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation combined with estimates of the Duhamel formulation of the mollified empirical measure, together with partial Girsanov transforms for the non-mollified system of particles.
items.authors: Nicoleta Cazacu, Alexandre Richard, Milica Tomasevic

items.title: A clarification of Fermi's formula for the maximum of partial sums
items.abstract: In Fermi's 1926 note, the expression assigned to the probability that all partial sums remain below a threshold is the complementary crossing probability. We obtain the correct probability from the same diffusion equation and locate the inconsistency in the final integration. We then state the limit for independent increments under the Lindeberg condition. A counterexample with smooth densities shows that small individual variances do not suffice to justify this limit. The probabilistic results are classical; the purpose of this note is to reconcile the stated event with the printed calculation and to make the sufficient hypotheses for the discrete limit explicit.
items.authors: Alessandro Lodi

items.title: Uniform-in-Time and Uniform-in-Temperature Particle Approximations of Coulomb MMD Flows
items.abstract: We study particle approximations of maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) flows with the Coulomb kernel on the torus $\mathbb{T}^d$, $d\ge2$, driven by thermal noise of strength $\tau\ge0$. For smooth, strictly positive initial and target densities and i.i.d. initial positions, we prove that the expected Wasserstein-1 distance between the empirical measure and the mean-field solution is at most of order $N^{-1/d}$ for $d\ge3$ and $\sqrt{(\log N)/N}$ for $d=2$, uniformly in time and in the temperature $\tau\ge0$, including the deterministic case $\tau=0$. At each fixed $\tau>0$, we also prove propagation of chaos in total variation for any $k$-fold marginal distributions of particles, uniformly in time, with a bound of order $\sqrt{k/\tau}$ times the empirical convergence rate. Our proof uses the modulated free-energy method of Bresch, Jabin, and Wang to reduce the particle convergence estimate to a relaxation estimate that controls the time integral of the mean-field velocity gradient uniformly in $\tau\ge0$. Near zero temperature, where the smoothing effect of the noise degenerates, we obtain this estimate by recentering the dynamics at thermal equilibrium and using the damping generated by the Coulomb interaction.
items.authors: Junho Lee, Promit Ghosal

items.title: A Khintchine type inequality for non-independent random variables
items.abstract: In this short note we give a Khintchine-type inequality involving non-independentrandom variables. The basic setting is inspired by Breuer-Major theorem and the proof is based on a hypercontractivity argument.
items.authors: Jingyu Huang, Wenxuan Tao

items.title: A Generalized Elephant Random Walk with Time-Dependent Memory
items.abstract: The elephant random walk (ERW) is a discrete-time random walk with complete memory. At every step the walker chooses one of the previous increments at random and then either repeats with a constant probability $p\in [0,1]$ or reverses it. Since its introduction by Sch\"utz and Trimper, the model has become a useful probabilistic framework for studying long-range dependence, anomalous diffusion, reinforcement, and phase transitions. This paper proposes a generalized ERW model with time-dependent memory. In this generalized model, the usual constant memory parameter $p$ in the standard ERW is allowed to change with time. The cental limit theorems, and the law of the iterated logarithm and some other strong laws are obtained.
items.authors: Xiequan Fan, Yongcheng Qi

items.title: Regularity lemma for Gaussian polynomials
items.abstract: We prove a regularity lemma for polynomials with fixed degree $d$ and any number of standard Gaussian input variables. Following modern approaches to the Szemer{\'e}di regularity lemma, we deduce our results from a general formulation of the regularity lemma using ultraproducts. Along the way, we give a direct combinatorial proof of the celebrated ``fourth moment theorem'' of Nualart and Peccati, which characterizes the asymptotically Gaussian polynomials inside degree-$d$ Gaussian chaos as those such that $\mathbb{E} p^2 \to 1$ and $\mathbb{E} p^4 \to 3$.
items.authors: Chris Jones

items.title: Limiting distributions of the rightmost eigenvalue of the truncated circular Unitary ensemble across all truncation regimes
items.abstract: We study the limiting distribution of the largest real part of the eigenvalues of truncated unitary matrices. Let \(U_m\) be an \(m\times m\) Haar-distributed unitary matrix, and let \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n\) be the eigenvalues of its upper-left \(n\times n\) principal submatrix. We determine the limiting distribution of \(\max_{1\le i\le n}\Re Z_i\) under a unified normalization: the limiting law is Gumbel when $q:=m-n\to\infty$ and is of Weibull type when $q$ is fixed. The fixed-\(q\) limiting laws converge to the Gumbel law as \(q\to\infty\). We also give a unified formulation of the normalizing constants for the spectral radius that recovers the previously known limiting laws.
items.authors: Yutao Ma, Xujia Meng

items.title: Optimal information loss for Liouville spectral responses
items.abstract: We study Fisher information about the amplitude of a known smooth mean shift from the first Dirichlet eigenvalue and spatial responses of a Liouville random medium. The complete response record determines the speed measure and the Gaussian free field, whereas every finite record strictly loses information; an optimal design exists in each finite-dimensional probe space. We quantify this gap as the known Liouville parameter $\gamma$ tends to zero. If the probe space contains an explicit matching probe, the minimum loss equals $\gamma^2$ times a positive compression error for a deterministic second-chaos operator, up to $o(\gamma^2)$, with designs allowed to depend on $\gamma$. After enlarging the probe dictionary, the optimal $m$-response coefficient is asymptotic to $\|Lg\|_{L^1(D)}^2/(8m)$, where $L=-(2\pi)^{-1}\Delta_D$ on the unit disk $D$. A quadratic correction of the readouts attains the same fixed-design loss to second order.
items.authors: Chunhao Cai

items.title: Distinguishing sets and measures from their planar Brownian images
items.abstract: Motivated by a question of Hochman, we investigate whether two deterministic time measures or time sets can be distinguished almost surely from a single planar Brownian image. Using rescaled correlation integrals, we give a criterion for mutual singularity of the laws of the image measures, even when the time measures have the same dimension. For self-similar time sets satisfying the open set condition, we also recover the natural occupation measure from the compact image. Together, these results allow us to distinguish lattice and non-lattice self-similar sets and their natural measures within this class. For a naturally parametrised family with two contractions, with fixed dimension, each parameter can be distinguished from all but finitely many others. If the dimension is sufficiently small, every distinct parameter can be distinguished.
items.authors: Sascha Troscheit

items.title: Large deviation principles for 2D stochastic $g$-Navier--Stokes equations on unbounded channel-like domains
items.abstract: This paper investigates the large deviation principle for 2D stochastic $g$-Navier--Stokes equations driven by multiplicative noise and defined on an unbounded channel-like domain. We first prove the existence and uniqueness of probabilistically strong solutions for the stochastic equation under small noise perturbations by means of the local monotonicity method. Subsequently, we show the well-posedness of solutions to the corresponding control equation and the convergence in distribution of the solutions for the stochastic equation as the noise intensity tends to zero. Finally, we establish the Freidlin-Wentzell type large deviation principle for the solutions of the stochastic equation by using the weak convergence method. To overcome the lack of compactness of Sobolev embedding on unbounded domains, we employ a scalar stream function together with a truncation technique to derive uniform tail estimates for the solutions of the control equation.
items.authors: Gang He, Ji Shu, Huixia Wen, Longyu Wu

items.title: $\mathcal{D}$-Pullback Measure Attractors of McKean-Vlasov Stochastic Lattice Wave Equations
items.abstract: This paper deals with the pullback measure attractor for a non-autonomous distribution-dependent stochastic lattice wave equation with nonlinear noise on $\mathbb{Z}$. We establish well-posedness in the energy space $\ell^{2}\times\ell^{2}$ and show that the solution generates a continuous non-autonomous dynamical system on $\mathcal{P}_{4}(\ell^{2}\times\ell^{2})$, which possesses a unique pullback measure attractor $\mathcal{A}$. Furthermore, we prove the convergence of the attractor $\mathcal{A}^{\varepsilon}$ as $\varepsilon\to 0^{+}$ to the attractor of the corresponding distribution-independent limit system.
items.authors: Huixia Wen, Ji Shu, Gang He

items.title: Axioms and internal rigidity of spectral duality structures
items.abstract: Spectral duality structures (SDS) explain why a distinguished family of initial distributions makes the absorption probabilities of resetting processes insensitive to the resetting mechanism. Here we study their axioms. We prove that the six defining conditions are mutually independent and determine what each one contributes. The key tool is a structure theorem valid for an arbitrary permutation and an arbitrary positive weight: every insensitive distribution is supported on a union of cycles balanced at a common level, and the level of a cycle is fixed by the geometric mean of the weight on it. From it, positivity selects the admissible root, the constant orbit product is equivalent to the existence of an insensitive distribution of full support, and the involution is equivalent to the response rank being equal to the number of free weight parameters. Without the duality relation, insensitivity of a single distribution is cheap and generically isolated; duality turns it into structural neutrality of the separatrix. The full-rank condition splits into two layers: a weaker condition is equivalent to maximal response rank, while full rank also excludes insensitivity at any other level. We then show that a single SDS is internally rigid: compatible semigroup structures force a constant weight, compatible abelian group structures obey a precise arithmetic condition, congruences form a simple lattice, and the automorphism group is computed explicitly. Finally, the axioms do not determine the orientation of the response; in the two-site case we give the exact condition under which the geometric and analytic sign criteria agree.
items.authors: Juan Antonio Vega Coso

items.title: Poincar\'e inequalities, logarithmic growth and doubling
items.abstract: We investigate when a Poincar\'e inequality forces the underlying measure to be doubling, with particular attention to the space \(X\) controlling the oscillation. We identify \(L\log L\) as the sharp threshold: under a natural local growth condition on the measure, doubling is forced precisely when \(L\log L(0,1)\not\hookrightarrow X\). We also obtain a doubling criterion under a weaker geometric assumption when the oscillation norm is sufficiently stronger than \(L\log L\). We show that this threshold is sharp in every fixed Euclidean dimension, using a dimension-free local \(L\log L\)-Poincar\'e inequality for log-concave measures and non-doubling Gaussian examples. We then turn to infinite-dimensional spaces, where doubling is impossible for the measures under consideration. Nevertheless, the \(L\log L\)-Poincar\'e inequality continues to hold, and we establish sharp characterizations for infinite product models, Gaussian measures on Hilbert spaces under power-type small-ball estimates, and Wiener measure with the uniform norm.
items.authors: Joaquim Martin

items.title: Dudley-type bound for stationary Bernoulli processes
items.abstract: This is preliminary, AI-generated note on the Dudley-type bound for stationary Bernoulli processes postulated by M. Talagrand based on the unpublished notes of the authors and the recent note \cite{invariant} which in turn is an alternative proof of the result by Hu, Wang, Wu.
items.authors: W. Bednorz, R. Martynek, R. Meller

items.title: Closed-form evaluation of the cumulative distribution function and absolute moments of the variance-gamma distribution
items.abstract: Closed-form formulas are derived for the cumulative distribution function and odd-order absolute moments of the variance-gamma distribution. As a special case, closed-form expressions are deduced for the cumulative distribution function and odd-order absolute central moments of the product of two correlated zero-mean normal random variables.
items.authors: Robert E. Gaunt, Heather L. Sutcliffe

items.title: The periodic Airy line ensembles
items.abstract: In this paper we construct a one-parameter family of periodic Airy line ensembles $\mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{per},R}$ for $R>0$ as weak scaling limits of Borodin's periodic Schur processes. We establish several properties of $\mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{per},R}$, including a determinantal point process structure with an explicit correlation kernel. We also show that, after a parabolic shift and normalization, $\mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{per},R}$ satisfies, on its domain $[-R/2,R/2]$, the same Brownian Gibbs property enjoyed by the usual Airy line ensemble. A main technical contribution of the paper is a general tightness criterion for determinantal line ensembles, which extends the argument used by Johansson in [Comm. Math. Phys. 242 (2003), 277-329] to prove a functional limit theorem for the discrete polynuclear growth model.
items.authors: Evgeni Dimitrov, Samir Sarieddine, Zongrui Yang, Zhengye Zhou

items.title: Graph Matching in Random Geometric Graphs I: Efficient Algorithms
items.abstract: We study the recovery of the hidden vertex correspondence between two correlated dense random geometric graphs. Each graph is generated from $n$ latent unit vectors in $\mathbb R^d$; the vectors $u_i^A$ and $u_i^B$ of corresponding vertices satisfy $\langle u_i^A,u_i^B\rangle=\rho$, and the vertex labels of the second graph are permuted by an unknown permutation $\pi$. For every fixed correlation $\rho\in(0,1]$ and every edge density bounded away from zero and one, we give a randomized polynomial time algorithm that recovers $\pi$ exactly with probability tending to one whenever $d\ge(\log n)^L$, where $L$ depends only on the correlation and the density bounds. The algorithm assigns to each vertex a signature formed by counting decorated paths with a constant number of seeds. The number of such seeded templates grows exponentially with the path length, with an arbitrarily large constant base, so the resulting statistics amplify an arbitrarily small constant correlation. We control the dependencies created by the latent geometry in two ways: when $d$ is larger than $n/(\log n)^{L_0}$ for a suitable constant $L_0$, by comparing local moments with those of correlated Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi graphs; for smaller $d$, by spectral estimation of the latent geometry combined with a harmonic correction. We also provide low-degree evidence for a tradeoff between the correlation and the computational cost.
items.authors: Dong Huang, Ankang Jiao, Shuangping Li, Zhangsong Li

items.title: Revisiting the Bobkov-Chistyakov-G\"otze theorem on approximately Gaussian marginals
items.abstract: We study one-dimensional marginals of an isotropic, log-concave probability measure in $\mathbb{R}^n$. We show that the Kolmogorov distance between a typical marginal and the standard Gaussian distribution is at most $C/n$, for a universal constant $C > 0$. This bound is optimal in general, up to the value of the universal constant. It improves the Gaussian approximation bound of Bobkov, Chistyakov and G\"otze by a logarithmic factor in the log-concave setting.
items.authors: Boaz Klartag

items.title: Small perturbations of the $2d$ classical Heisenberg model
items.abstract: Polyakov predicted in 1975 ([Pol75) that the spin $O(3)$-model (or classical Heisenberg model) should have exponential decay of correlations at all positive temperatures on $\mathbb{Z}^2$. Our main result is as follows: if we replace the Euclidean scalar product \begin{align*} \langle \sigma_i , \sigma_j\rangle = \sigma_i^x \sigma_j^x + \sigma_i^y \sigma_j^y + \sigma_i^z \sigma_j^z \end{align*} by the $\lambda$-modified scalar product \begin{align*} \langle \sigma_i , \sigma_j\rangle_\lambda := \sigma_i^x \sigma_j^x + \sigma_i^y \sigma_j^y + \lambda \sigma_i^z \sigma_j^z \end{align*} we show that for all $\lambda\in(-1,1)$, the $\mathbb{S}^2$ valued spin system with Gibbs measure $\exp(\beta \sum_{i\sim j} \langle \sigma_i,\sigma_j\rangle_\lambda)$ has power-law decay of correlations if $\beta$ is chosen large enough. This is the first evidence that arbitrary small smooth modifications of the classical Heisenberg model produce a BKT phase in $2d$. It was proved in the 1970s and 80s that there exist arbitrary small smooth modifications of the classical Heisenberg model which produce instead an Ising phase. In these work, they considered the regime $\lambda>1$ while in this paper, we consider the regime $\lambda<1$ which cannot be analyzed via reflection positivity and chessboard estimate. The two main ingredients used in our proof are the stability of the BKT phase under percolation type disorder ([DG25]) and weak regularity type properties of the groundstates or $\mathbb{S}^2$-valued harmonic maps associated to our $\lambda$-energy functional. This analytic step is interesting on its own. Finally, the exponential and power-law decay regime should be separated by a curve $\lambda \mapsto \beta_c(\lambda)$. We prove a rigorous lower bound in the case of the $\lambda$-anisotropic hemisphere model $\mathbb{S}^2_+$ which matches with RG flow predictions.
items.authors: Christophe Garban, Nathan de Montgolfier

items.title: Entropy, isoperimetry and the total variation profile of random walks
items.abstract: The total variation profile $\mathrm{TV}_n$ of a random walk measures how far its distribution at time $n$ is from being invariant under the generators. Three lower bounds are given: an elementary bound $\mathrm{TV}_n \geq 1/\big(44\,L(n)\big)$ in terms of the speed $L(n)$; a bound by the entropy increment $H(P^{n+1}) - H(P^n)$, which is a reverse Pinsker inequality; and a bound in terms of the entropy and the isoperimetric profile. Deciding whether the entropy-increment bound always improves on the isoperimetric one is related to conjectures on the growth of the entropy and of groups. The motivation comes from the question of whether the distributions of a random walk can be transported back onto their translates at bounded cost.
items.authors: Antoine Gournay

items.title: Iterated Graph Systems (III): Alexander-Orbach conjecture on hierarchical lattices
items.abstract: Can the Alexander-Orbach conjecture hold on hierarchical lattices? We construct Gromov-Hausdorff-Prokhorov scaling limits of critical percolation clusters on hierarchical lattices in the chemical metric and determine the typical spectral dimensions of the associated diffusions. These dimensions are dense in $(1,2)$; however, outside a narrow region in dimension space, we prove that the Alexander-Orbach conjecture fails on every hierarchical lattice under consideration.
items.authors: Ziyu Neroli

items.title: Determinantal linear spanning forests
items.abstract: We introduce a determinantal linear process on the space of $1$-forms over a weighted graph endowed with a unitary local system, which we call the determinantal linear spanning forest (DLSF). This process is the analog of the uniform spanning tree in the presence of an arbitrary rank $n$ quenched gauge field in ${\rm U}(n)$ (or ${\rm O}(n)$, ${\rm SO}(n)$, ${\rm SU}(n)$, ${\rm Sp}(n)$), and generalizes the determinantal random cycle-rooted spanning forest which corresponds to the case of ${\rm U}(1)$ and ${\rm SU}(2)$. We describe the support of this process by means of a polymatroid which is described in terms of the circular and bicircular matroids. We also explain how the DLSF relates to the computation of currents in an electrical network in the presence of a gauge field. The partition function of the DLSF is shown to be the determinant of the twisted Laplacian, for which we also give a matrix-tree type theorem that computes its characteristic polynomial. We initiate the study of the twisted Laplacian determinant as a functional on the space of connections, and give a first order expansion of it in a neighborhood of the trivial connection, for which we provide a probabilistic interpretation. We extend the construction to infinite graphs, exhibiting the analogs of the classical wired and free distributions on spanning forests. We give a sufficient geometric condition on the local spectral gap for the existence of a Poincar\'e inequality as well as the uniqueness of the infinite volume measure, and the exponential decay of correlations. We show that on any recurrent graph, the wired and free DLSF coincide. We construct examples where they do not, for example, unlike in the classical case, on $\mathbb Z^d$ for $d\geq 3$.
items.authors: Adrien Kassel, Thierry L\'evy

items.title: A quantitative CLT for the zeros of random trigonometric polynomials
items.abstract: Let $X_N(t)$, $t\in[0,\pi]$, be a stationary Gaussian trigonometric polynomial, and let $\mathcal Z_N$ denote the number of zeros of the rescaled process $X_N(t/N)$ on $[0,N\pi]$. We establish the quantitative central limit theorem \[ d_{\mathrm W}\left( \frac{\mathcal Z_N-\mathbb E[\mathcal Z_N]} {\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}(\mathcal Z_N)}},Z\right) \le C\frac{(\log N)^2}{\sqrt N}, \] where $Z$ is standard Gaussian and $d_{\mathrm W}$ denotes the Wasserstein-1 distance. The proof combines Ornstein--Uhlenbeck regularization of the singular Kac representation with direct estimates of the covariance between the Malliavin--Stein factor and Stein test functions. A lattice lower bound of order $N^{-1/2}$ shows that the convergence rate is optimal up to logarithmic factors.
items.authors: Ao Huang, Zhonggen Su, Xiaolin Wang

items.title: Half-space polynuclear growth: a multipoint Fredholm--Pfaffian formula
items.abstract: We derive a Fredholm-Pfaffian formula for the one-time multi-point transition probabilities of half-space polynuclear growth with any nonnegative boundary nucleation rate and general deterministic upper semi-continuous initial profiles. We prove the formula by showing that it satisfies an integral Kolmogorov equation with a unique bounded solution. We also discuss the formal 1:2:3 scaling limit of the kernel and its relation to the half-space KPZ fixed point.
items.authors: Kailun Chen, Xincheng Zhang

items.title: Spectral Measure and Tail Process for Multivariate Dynamical Extremes
items.abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior of extreme events in multivariate stationary sequences, with particular emphasis on stochastic processes generated by dynamical systems. We develop a general framework for describing the dependence structure of extremes through two complementary objects: the tail process and the spectral measure. We first extend the enriched point-process convergence of the univariate theory to the multivariate setting, proving that the decorated point process of exceedances converges to a marked Poisson cluster process whose marks retain the componentwise and temporal structure of extreme clusters. We then construct a spectral measure for stationary sequences, which assigns weight to distinct extremal profiles and characterizes the asymptotic dependence between components, and establish a de Haan-Resnick type representation. We also relate the spectral measure to the tail process, showing that its normalized profile distribution is recovered from the angular component of the tail process. Finally, we recover the classical univariate and multivariate exceedance processes as special cases. We illustrate the theory through applications to dynamical systems, using examples in which different dynamical mechanisms give rise to distinct extremal clustering patterns and cross-dependence structures. These applications demonstrate the ability of the proposed framework to capture genuinely multivariate features of extreme events and to extract information about the underlying dynamics that is not accessible through classical exceedance processes.
items.authors: Alessio Corveddu

items.title: Discrete total variation under the multinomial, Part 2: variance under the uniform null
items.abstract: For the counts $(X_1,\dots,X_n)\sim\mathrm{Mult}(N;1/n,\dots,1/n)$ of $N$ observations in $n$ ordered bins we study the variance of the discrete total variation $d=\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}|X_{i+1}-X_i|$. An exact decomposition splits $\mathrm{Var}(d)$ into per-edge, adjacent-pair and disjoint-pair terms and yields, for fixed $n$ as $N\to\infty$, $\mathrm{Var}(d)/N=\alpha(n)-\beta(n)/N+\gamma(n)/N^2+o(N^{-2})$. For every $n\ge 2$, $N\alpha(n)$ is the classical normal-theory variance (Hoel, Kamat) of the sum of absolute successive differences of $n$ independent $N(0,N/n)$ variables; the correction $\beta(n)$ is obtained in closed form for $n\ge 3$ (the case $n=2$ is treated separately). Two disjoint edge differences $D_1=X_2-X_1$ and $D_3=X_4-X_3$ are exactly uncorrelated and asymptotically independent, yet $\mathrm{Cov}(|D_1|,|D_3|)=-1/(\pi n)+O(1/N)$: a correlation of relative order $1/N$, invisible in the Gaussian limit and absent under Poissonized sampling, whose constant is proportional to the exact joint fourth cumulant $\kappa_{2,2}(D_1,D_3)=-4N/n^2$ and is proved here on the lattice. The adjacent pair contributes the lattice-Edgeworth constant $a_*=-2\sqrt{3}/(9\pi)$, of which one quarter is a smooth Edgeworth term and three quarters a lattice-corner term; the disjoint skeleton $h(m)$ is closed through a Bessel generating function; and $\gamma(n)$ ($n\ge 5$) is expressed through a single triangular-lattice constant whose closed form we conjecture. Together with the mean of Part 1, the variance supplies the two moments used by moment-matched approximations to the null law of $d$. This is Part 2 of a series; the cyclic statistic $d^{c}$ will be treated in Part 5.
items.authors: Nikola Bani\'c, Neven Elezovi\'c

items.title: Higher-Order Paracontrolled Calculus for Geometric Rough Paths
items.abstract: We study the rough differential equation $$ \frac{du_t}{dt}= F(u_t) \zeta_t, \ \ u(0) = u_0 \in \mathbb{R}^d, $$ where $F : \mathbb{R}^d \to L(\mathbb{R}^d, \mathbb{R}^d)$ is a sufficiently regular vector field, and the noise $\zeta$ is a distribution in $\mathscr{C}^{\alpha-1}(\mathbb{R})$ for $\alpha \in (\frac{1}{4}, \frac{1}{3})$. We construct solutions to this equation at lower regularity than previous work of Gubinelli-Imkeller-Perkowski and Pr\"omel-Trabs using ideas from the high-order paracontrolled viewpoint of Bailleul-Bernicot. The key tool in our work is the development of a harmonic-analytic framework for proving a set of iterated commutator estimates which are necessary for the solution theory. We also show the procedure of enhancement when the noise $\zeta = dZ$, where $Z$ is a realization of fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter $H \in (\frac{1}{4}, \frac{1}{3})$.
items.authors: Tim Van Hoose

items.title: Kinetic SDEs and kinetic Fokker-Planck equations with critical Morrey-type drifts, and local blow-ups
items.abstract: We develop a Sobolev theory for the kinetic Fokker-Planck equation subject to a singular Morrey-form $L^\infty+M^q_K$ force field which can produce local blow-ups due to strong attraction to a submanifold. Our approach is based on the fractional representation for the Duhamel series of the equation and on establishing kinetic Adams-type estimates. Accordingly, we construct weak solutions of Brownian-driven kinetic SDEs in a critical Morrey set-up, obtain kinetic Krylov-type estimates and a strongly continuous Feller propagator, and establish uniqueness criteria for a large class of weak solutions.
items.authors: Jean-Fran\c{c}ois Jabir, Damir Kinzebulatov, Chengjun Yue

items.title: Large Network limit for Latent Variable Process Models with Endogeneously Evolving Interactions among Multiple Types
