items.authors: Shuji Yamamoto

items.title: On strongly minimal asymptotic bases of order $h$ generated by powers of $2$
items.abstract: Let $h\geq2$ be an integer and let $\mathbb{N}_0=W_1\cup\cdots\cup W_h$ be a partition into infinite sets. For $W\subseteq\mathbb{N}_0$, let $A(W)$ denote the set of all finite nonempty sums of distinct powers $2^w$ with $w\in W$. We give a necessary and sufficient condition for $A=A(W_1)\cup\cdots\cup A(W_h)$ to be a strongly minimal asymptotic basis of order $h$. This provides a complete answer to a problem posed by Nathanson in 1988.
items.authors: Shi-Qiang Chen, Xin-Yue Yan

items.title: On the OpenAI proof that Landau-Siegel zeros do not exist
items.abstract: A recent manuscript of OpenAI asserts that Landau-Siegel zeros do not exist. Here, we give a detailed account of its argument, arranged as a direct proof with explicit constants. There are absolute constants $q_0$ and $\delta_0>0$ such that, for every primitive real Dirichlet character $\chi$ of conductor $q\ge q_0$, every real zero $\beta\in(0,1)$ of $L(s,\chi)$ satisfies $(1-\beta)\log q\ge\delta_0$, and one can take $q_0=10^{10}$ and $\delta_0=3.0\times 10^{-3}$. Combined with a recent computation of Lu, Zaman, and Zhao, this result yields the bound $(1-\beta)\log q\ge 3.0\times 10^{-3}$ for every conductor $q\ge 3$. The proof is an interpolation determinant argument in the biquadratic field generated by $\sqrt{2}$ over the quadratic field attached to $\chi$. A real zero close to one forces $\chi(p)=-1$ for most primes $p$, and the Frobenius congruence at these primes makes a certain nonzero determinant divisible by higher powers of these primes than its Archimedean size allows. The underlying ideas are those of the OpenAI manuscript. The explicit constants, and the presentation, are new.
items.authors: William D. Banks

items.title: A linear independence criterion for $p$-adic Hurwitz zeta values at odd integers
items.abstract: In this article, a new criterion is established to obtain the linear independence of some values of the $p$-adic Hurwitz zeta function at odd integers $s\geq 3$. We generalize a theorem of F.~Beukers, who gave, among others, an alternative proof---using Pad\'{e} approximation theory---of a result originally due to F.~Calegari on the irrationality of the $p$-adic Riemann zeta value $\zeta_p(3)$ for $p = 2, 3$. To prove our main theorem, we work in a general setting, where we construct and study new Pad\'e approximants of Laurent series satisfying the functional equation $f(z) = f(1-z)$. This complements our previous work on the linear independence of $p$-adic polygamma values.
items.authors: Makoto Kawashima, Anthony Po\"{e}ls

items.title: The Goldbach exceptional set: an exponent 7/12 and conditional refinement
items.abstract: Let \(E(X)\) count the even integers between \(4\) and \(X\) that are not sums of two primes. We combine Pintz's explicit formula for the major arcs with the exponential-sum estimate of Maynard, Pandey, and Radziwi{\l}{\l} to prove \(E(X)\ll_\varepsilon X^{7/12+\varepsilon}\) whenever all Dirichlet \(L\)-functions have a common fixed zero-free half-plane \(\Rea s>\theta_0\), with \(\theta_0<1\). The uniform \(7/8\) theorem reported in the OpenAI mathematics release supplies this input. Under the stronger hypothesis that every nontrivial Dirichlet zero has real part at most \(\theta\), where \(1/2\leq\theta\leq2/3\), we prove \[ E(X)\ll_{\theta,\varepsilon}X^{g(\theta)+\varepsilon}, \qquad g(\theta)=\frac{\theta(5-4\theta)}{2(2-\theta)}. \] Thus every fixed \(\theta<2/3\) gives an exponent strictly below \(7/12\). The latter argument uses a classical fixed-modulus zero-density estimate and is independent of the new exponential-sum theorem.
items.authors: J\'anos Pintz, Ingo Alth\"ofer

items.title: Bloch torsion and modular combinations of Nahm sums
items.abstract: We construct a positive-definite symmetric integral $12\times12$ matrix $A$ such that, for every solution $Q$ of Nahm's equations $1-Q=Q^A$ with $Q_i\ne0,1$ for all $i$, the associated element $\sum_i[Q_i]$ is torsion in the Bloch group of $\mathbb{Q}(Q_1,\ldots,Q_{12})$. However, the Nahm sum $F_{A,B,C}(\tau)$ is nonmodular for every $B\in\mathbb{Q}^{12}$ and $C\in\mathbb{Q}$. Thus the torsion condition for all solutions in Nahm's conjecture is not sufficient for the existence of a modular Nahm sum.
items.authors: Xuejun Guo

items.title: Coprime pairs with equal sum of divisors, assuming smooth shifted primes
items.abstract: Let $h(x)$ be the number of pairs $1\le a x^{2-o(1)}$. By an argument of Pollack and Pomerance, this follows if for every fixed $\delta>0$ there are $y^{1-o(1)}$ primes $p\le5y$ with $p+1$ free of prime factors exceeding $y^\delta$. We write this implication out with explicit parameters and formalize it in Lean 4. We then check that the argument of the recent OpenAI preprint "Weighted dilation graphs, smooth shifted primes and totient fibers", which claims the corresponding statement for $p-1$, applies to $p+1$ after a change of sign in two of its sections. Consequently $h(x)=x^{2-o(1)}$, conditionally on the correctness of that preprint, which has not been refereed and whose main new estimates we have not independently verified.
items.authors: Shisheng Li, Zhong Zhuang

items.title: Counting subspaces with prescribed Welch sums
items.abstract: Let $q=2^n$ with $n=2m+1$ for an integer $m\ge1$, and let ${\mathbb F}_q$ be the finite field with $q$ elements. Let $W_n(x)=x^{2^m+3}$ be the Welch function on ${\mathbb F}_q$. For $1\le k\le n$ and $b\in{\mathbb F}_q$, denote by $N_{n,k}(b)$ the number of $k$-dimensional ${\mathbb F}_2$-subspaces $E$ of $\mathbb F}_q$ such that \[ \sum_{x\in E}W_n(x)=b. \] In this paper, we determine $N_{n,k}(b)$ for all $k$. The only nontrivial case is $k=3$, for which the answer is given in terms of a binary Kloosterman sum. As a consequence, we prove a recent conjecture of Hou and Zhao on the third-order sum-freedom of the Welch function.
items.authors: Kaimin Cheng, Jie Hu

items.title: Poissonian Pair Correlation for Bernoulli Orbits
items.abstract: Let \(\alpha, \beta \in \mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}\), and let \((\xi_n)_{n \ge 1}\) be independent random variables taking the values \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) with equal probability. We study the random walk \[X_n = \xi_1 + \cdots + \xi_n \pmod 1\] and present a deterministic Diophantine condition on \((\alpha, \beta)\) that implies almost sure Poisson pair correlation. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first result providing explicit examples in this framework where the increment measure is purely discrete. The classical Fourier contraction method fails in this setting; a different approach is required. Our proof uses the parabolic geometry of returns to \(1\) and an exact covariance formula for overlapping blocks.
items.authors: Bo Tan, Zhen Zhang, Qing-Long Zhou

items.title: Solutions of $x_1^2+x_2^2-x_3^2=D$ with small $x_3$: a spectral approach
items.abstract: We count the integral solutions of x_1^2+x_2^2-x_3^2=D weighted by Phi(x_3/M), for M smaller than sqrt(D). Such solutions correspond to binary quadratic forms of discriminant D, and the count becomes a sum, over the geodesics of discriminant D, of a function of their distance to the point i, which we evaluate by the spectral theory of automorphic forms. For square D=n^2 the geodesics run from cusp to cusp, and Hecke theory reduces them to a single geodesic. For every n and both parities of x_3 we obtain an asymptotic formula with error O(n^{1+theta+eps} M^{-1/2}), theta=7/64, using the Kim-Sarnak bound and the large sieve of Deshouillers and Iwaniec; it is non-trivial for M >= n^{71/96+eps}. This improves the range n^{5/6+eps} of the elementary method and confirms the corrected main term of the author's earlier work. For non-square D=f^2 D_0 the geodesics are closed, and a Hecke relation for their traces reduces everything to the fundamental discriminant D_0. For odd D_0 we obtain an error O(D^eps f^{1+theta} D_0^{2/3} M^{-1/2}), using the formulas of Duke-Imamoglu-Toth and Baruch-Mao together with Young's cubic moment. For D = 5 mod 8 this counts all solutions, and the range M >= D^{1/2-1/1332} of Friedlander and Iwaniec improves to M >= D^{4/9+eps}. This paper was written in collaboration with Claude (Opus 5.5, High), an AI model developed by Anthropic.
items.authors: Stephan Baier

items.title: On the inverse Goldbach problem
items.abstract: We establish two quantitative results concerning additive decompositions of the set $\mathbb{P}$ of primes. First, we prove that, if $A,B\subseteq\mathbb N$ have at least two elements and $A+B$ differs from the primes by only finitely many elements, then $$ \frac{\sqrt{x}}{\log x}\ll A(x),B(x) \ll \sqrt{x}. $$ Second, we show that, if $A,B,C\subseteq\mathbb N$ have at least two elements each, then $$ ((A+B+C)\mathbin{\bigtriangleup}\mathbb P)(x) \gg \frac{\sqrt{x}}{(\log x)^2}. $$ An analogous estimate is obtained for sumsets of $k\ge 3$ sets. The proofs use Montgomery's large sieve, Gallagher's larger sieve, a mean-value argument for a certain multiplicative function, and a submultiplicative sumset inequality.
items.authors: Paolo Leonetti

items.title: Tribonacci numbers that are palindromic concatenations of two distinct repdigits
items.abstract: Let $(T_n)_{n\ge1}$ be the Tribonacci sequence, defined by $T_1=T_2=1$, $T_3=2$, and $T_n=T_{n-1}+T_{n-2}+T_{n-3}$ for $n\ge4$. In this paper, we study the Tribonacci numbers whose decimal representation is a palindromic concatenation of two distinct repdigits, that is, numbers of the shape $\overline{d_1\cdots d_1\,d_2\cdots d_2\,d_1\cdots d_1}$ with $1\le d_1\le9$, $0\le d_2\le9$, $d_1\ne d_2$. We prove that no Tribonacci number is a palindromic concatenation of two distinct repdigits. The proof combines lower bounds for linear forms in logarithms, the Baker-Davenport reduction method, and a finite computational verification.
items.authors: Khady Faye, Bernadette Faye

items.title: $6$ powers of $2$ in the Linnik--Goldbach problem
items.abstract: Linnik's approximation to Goldbach's conjecture concerns the representation of sufficiently large even integers as the sum of two primes and a bounded number of powers of two. We prove that $6$ powers of $2$ suffice unconditionally and that $5$ suffice under the GRH, improving previous works.
items.authors: Huixi Li, Zhixin Liu

items.title: A note on the $p$-adic inhomogeneous Littlewood conjecture
items.abstract: Bugeaud, Haynes and Velani (2011) resolved a metric version of the $p$-adic Littlewood conjecture. We establish a fully inhomogeneous generalisation of their result, as well as a partially inhomogeneous generalisation of a result of Harrap and Haynes (2013) in the more general mixed setting.
items.authors: Sam Chow, Owen Jones

items.title: Iwasawa cohomology of pseudorigid families of $(\varphi,\Gamma)$-modules
items.abstract: We study the Iwasawa cohomology complex attached to a pseudorigid family of $(\varphi, \Gamma)$-modules and prove coadmissibility of its cohomology groups, perfectness and compatibility with base change. We apply this result to give another proof of perfectness of the Herr complex in pseudorigid family. We also use it to prove perfectness of Selmer complexes and obtain a result on variation of ranks of Selmer groups in analytic family.
items.authors: Yashi Jain

items.title: Nonlinear twists of Rankin-Selberg coefficients in the eigenvalue aspect
items.abstract: Let $g$ be a fixed primitive Hecke--Maass cusp form, and let $f$ vary with spectral parameter $k_f=K$, at a fixed level and with trivial nebentypus. We study smooth sums of $\lambda_f(n)\lambda_g(n)e(\alpha n^\beta)$ for fixed real $\alpha\ne0$. The crucial input is the smooth spectral second moment of Lau, Liu, and Ye, for which the window length can be taken to be $L=K^{1/3+a}$ for arbitrarily small fixed $a>0$. We show that, for every $\kappa>0$, there is $\beta_0>0$ such that the sum is $O(K^{2/3+\kappa}X^{1/2})$ for $1\le X\le K^2$ and $0<\beta\le\beta_0$. We give a detailed Baire category argument which makes the dependence on the smooth weight uniform through one finite derivative norm. A second argument keeps the phase explicit, applies Voronoi summation and shifted convolution estimates, and gives the numerical bound $O(K^{423/224+(5/7)\beta+\varepsilon})$ at $X=K^2$ for $0<\beta<5/32$.
items.authors: Yangbo Ye

items.title: Zero density in short strips and short-interval bounds toward Hypothesis S
items.abstract: We deduce zero-density estimates in short vertical strips from short-interval moments of globally tempered automorphic $L$-functions, by adapting the large-value estimate of Guth and Maynard and the Type II zero argument of Maynard and Pratt to the framework of Ye and Zhang. For the Riemann zeta function, we obtain $N_\zeta(\sigma;T,T+T^a)\ll T^{15a(1-\sigma)/(3+5\sigma)+\varepsilon}$ for $2/3\le a\le1$ and $7/10\le\sigma\le4/5$. This improves Ye--Zhang's exponent for $7/10 0$. The cusp-form applications do not require the Ramanujan conjecture.
items.authors: Yangbo Ye

items.title: On bass orders in division algebras
items.abstract: A result by F.-T. Tu dating from 2011 states that the orders in a local matrix algebra of dimension four that can be written as a finite intersection of maximal orders are those having an Eichler Gorenstein closure. In a more recent paper, we gave a similar characterization for orders with a Bass Gorenstein closure. More precisely, we prove that these orders are the ones that can be written as a ghost intersection, i.e., the set of points defined over the base field of an intersection of maximal orders that is defined over a field extension. Although we proved this result only for the local four-dimensional matrix algebra, the statement makes sense also for a local quaternion division algebra, since the latter turns into a matrix algebra when we extend the base field to an even degree extension. In this work, we prove an analog of our previous result in the latter setting.
items.authors: Luis Arenas-Carmona

items.title: Low Lying Zeros of Dedekind Zeta Functions
items.abstract: Let $K$ be a number field of degree $n_K$, and let $h(K)$ denote the smallest absolute value of the imaginary part of a non-trivial zero of its Dedekind zeta function. In 1979, Hoffstein proved the unconditional bound $h(K)\leq 0.87+o(1)$ as $n_K\to\infty$. In a 1990 survey article, Odlyzko stated without proof that a different kernel in Weil's explicit formula could produce $h(K)\leq 0.54+o(1)$. No further improvement on Hoffstein's $0.87$ threshold accompanied by a published proof has since appeared. We choose a linear kernel and first show that Hoffstein's original parameters already yield the improved constant $0.825$. We then generalise his linear kernel method using Stechkin's trick and prove the unconditional bound $h(K)\leq 0.6+o(1)$ as $n_K\to\infty$, giving the best proved asymptotic bound to date.
items.authors: Timothy S. Trudgian, Sebastian Zuniga-Alterman

items.title: The Multiplicity One Defect and Congruence-Modular Exponent Ratios
items.abstract: We introduce a multiplicity one defect that quantitatively measures the failure of multiplicity one for the Jacobian of the Shimura curve \(X^D(M)\) attached to an indefinite rational quaternion algebra of discriminant \(D\) and level \(M\), localized at a maximal ideal of the Hecke algebra. By constructing a certain lattice inside the local Tate module, we obtain an explicit upper bound for the defect in terms of congruences between eigenforms and the lattice-Tate module discrepancies associated with the individual newforms. We then show that the local ratio between the congruence exponent and the modular exponent of modular abelian varieties attached to newforms is bounded above by the multiplicity one defect. Finally, we examine the relation with the Gorenstein property and give an explicit example at level \(126\) where the local Hecke algebra is Gorenstein even though multiplicity one fails. In this example, we compute the multiplicity one defect to be \(3\), which is also the local congruence--modular exponent ratio.
items.authors: Mohammad Masih Hamidi

items.title: Cohen-Lenstra heuristics and vanishing of zeta functions for superelliptic curves over finite fields
items.abstract: We prove a Cohen-Lenstra type result commenting on the distribution of class group structures amongst function fields of superelliptic curves over finite fields. We also prove a result commenting on the sparsity of such superelliptic curves whose zeta functions vanish at a fixed complex number. These results are proven via point-counting techniques on certain Hurwitz schemes generalizing techniques of Ellenberg-Venkatesh-Westerland and Ellenberg-Li-Shusterman. To obtain these point counts, We prove a unitary big monodromy theorem generalizing big monodromy theorems of Yu and Achter-Pries by appealing to an arithmeticity theorem of Venkataramana.
items.authors: Hyun Jong Kim

items.title: Irreducible components of crystabelline deformation rings: the wildly ramified case
items.abstract: Let $p\geq11$ be a prime, and let $\bar\rho:\Gal(\bar\QQ_p/\QQ_p)\rightarrow\GL_2(\bar\FF_p)$ be a reducible and very generic representation. In this paper, we use ghost series \cite{Lghost2} to study the irreducible components of Kisin's potentially crystalline deformation rings of $\bar\rho$. For wildly ramified principal series inertial types and arbitrary regular Hodge--Tate weights, we distinguish the components by the crystabelline slopes on their generic fibers and determine the total number of irreducible components. Combining this with an explicit formula for the total Hilbert--Samuel multiplicity of the special fiber obtained from the Breuil--M\'ezard conjecture, we compute the Hilbert--Samuel multiplicity of the special fiber of each component. Every such multiplicity is one when $\bar\rho$ is non-split, and is either one or two when $\bar\rho$ is split, according to whether the generic fiber of the corresponding component parametrizes reducible or irreducible Galois representations.
items.authors: Jiawei An

items.title: A Lean formalisation of the disproof of Ramaekers's conjecture
items.abstract: We describe Redhill, a Lean formalisation of the major results in H\"olzl, Kleine and Stephan's "Improved Lower Bounds for Strong $n$-Conjectures" (arXiv:2409.13439). Design decisions regarding types and data structures are justified as enabling canonical versions of the paper's claims, and from there the most direct proofs of said claims. The formalisation process also uncovered many errors, omissions and optimisation opportunities in the informal proof, all of which are addressed in the final library. Although Redhill is meant to stand alone, a few lemmas were upstreamed to the primary Lean mathematics library mathlib. We discuss the tension between upstreaming and leaving lemmas in separate libraries. Unlike many other contemporary formalisation projects, Redhill was completed without any assistance from large language models (LLMs). We compare our work with LLM-assisted projects, in particular an extension of arXiv:2409.13439 to $n=4$, aiming to establish design and style guidelines that define good Lean formalisations.
items.authors: Jeremy Tan

items.title: Dynamical generalizations of the two-point Chowla conjecture
items.abstract: In 1965, Chowla conjectured that the values of the Liouville function become asymptotically uncorrelated at consecutive natural numbers. Recently, the two-point case is resolved by OpenAI. In 2026, Charamaras and Richter conjectured a generalization of the Chowla conjecture to the asymptotic independence of the consecutive prime Omega functions. In this article, we prove the two-point case of their conjecture. As a consequence, we obtain a dynamical generalization of the two-point Chowla conjecture.
items.authors: Biao Wang, Shaoyun Yi

items.title: Stable reduction and large Nielsen orbits on generalized Markoff surfaces
items.abstract: We establish lower bounds on the orbit cardinalities of $\text{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ on the $\mathbb{F}_p$-points of the generalized Markoff surfaces given by $x^2 + y^2 + z^2 - xyz = \tau+2$. We show that outside of the reductions of a certain exceptional finite set of $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$-points found by Dubrovin and Mazzocco, every orbit has cardinality $\ge p$. Together with a recent result of Nathaniel Kingsbury-Neuschotz, this establishes, for all but finitely many primes $p$, the classification conjectures of McCullough-Wanderley (2013), and gives a complete classification of the connected components of the Hurwitz stack of $\text{SL}(2,\mathbb{F}_p)$-covers of elliptic curves, only branched above the origin. This extends earlier work of Bourgain-Gamburd-Sarnak and the author in the Markoff case $\tau = -2$. Our method studies certain noncongruence modular curves attached to a $\text{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$-orbit. These modular curves parametrize elliptic curves with a $\text{PSL}(2,\mathbb{F}_p)$-cover. We use this moduli interpretation to show that the noncongruence modular curves involved have bad reduction, as a cover of the $j$-line, at some place above $p$. This implies that the degree of the cover is $\ge p$, which translates into the desired bound on orbits. Key inputs include a result of Bouw-Wewers on bad reduction of three-point $\text{PSL}(2,\mathbb{F}_p)$-covers of the projective line, and the general stable reduction theory of Henrio, Obus, Raynaud, and Wewers.
items.authors: William Y. Chen

items.title: Hecke modules associated to certain even ternary lattices of half-discriminant $\mathbf{N^2}$
items.abstract: We consider Hecke modules of orthogonal modular forms attached to definite even ternary lattices of half-discriminant $N^2$, where $N > 1$ is odd and square-free. We prove explicit Jacquet-Langlands style correspondences with spaces of classical modular forms (in the spirit of Birch and Hein-Tornaria-Voight). This is done by applying sequences of Watson-style transformations that reduce the discriminant while preserving the adelic orthogonal group.
items.authors: Samadrito Bhattacharyya, Giovanna De Lauri, Dan Fretwell

items.title: Bounded continued fractions and quadratic orders in $\Q(\sqrt{127})$
items.abstract: We study the least periods and multiplier orders in two constructions of Mercat for continued fractions with bounded partial quotients. Our main explicit result concerns a family in $\Q(\sqrt{127})$ with partial quotients at most $4$. For every integer $j\geq1$, we prove that its primitive period has length $92j+2$ and its multiplier order has conductor $y_{4j}/4$, where $(4730624+419775\sqrt{127})^k=x_k+y_k\sqrt{127}$. The totally positive unit group of this order has index $4j$ in that of the maximal order. These exact formulas give divisor-sum lower bounds at fixed traces and a lower bound of order $(\log X)^2$ for the number of bounded continued fractions with discriminant at most $X$. We also prove a primitive-period refinement of Mercat's palindromic construction. Combining this refinement with Hensley's counting theorem gives, for every $m\geq2$ and $\eta>0$, at least $X^{\delta_m/2-\eta}$ quadratic fields, up to a positive constant, that admit infinitely many purely periodic continued fractions with partial quotients at most $m$. Here $\delta_m$ is the Hausdorff dimension of the corresponding continued fraction Cantor set.
items.authors: Shirali Kadyrov, Aiken Kazin, Alibek Orynbassar, Nurdaulet Shynarbek

items.title: The Davenport constant of low-dimensional boxes
items.abstract: In this paper, we study the maximal length of a minimal zero-sum sequence over $\left[\!\left[ -m,m \right]\!\right]^d$ having a support of size $d+1$. When $d=2$, we find the exact value of this maximal length for all $m \ge 2$, as well as the exact structure of all extremal sequences for this problem. When $d=3$, we obtain lower and upper bounds that asymptotically match each other as $m$ tends to infinity. This allows us to improve on the best known lower bounds for the Davenport constant of low-dimensional boxes.
items.authors: Benjamin Girard, Alain Plagne

items.title: The ring of values of $E$-functions is not a field
items.abstract: Let $\mathbf{E}$ be the ring of values taken at algebraic points by $E$-functions. The exponential function and the Bessel function $J_0$ are classical examples of $E$-functions. We prove that $\mathbf{E}$ is not a field. More precisely, we prove that it is neither noetherian nor factorial, and construct non-units of $\mathbf{E}$ explicity, including $e+1$, $J_0(1)$, and ${}_1F_1(a;b;1)$ for rational parameters $a$ and $b$ such that $0
items.authors: St\'ephane Fischler (LMO), Tanguy Rivoal (IF)

items.title: Sparse Lifts of q-Linearized Permutation Polynomials with Explicit Inverses
items.abstract: We give a higher unit-torus lift from q-linearized permutation polynomials over Fqn to generally nonlinear sparse permutation polynomials over Fqns. The construction preserves compositional inverses: if a linearized polynomials and its inverse have coefficients (ai) and (Ai), then the lifted polynomial and its inverse have the same coefficients. As a consequence, we obtain nonlinear binomial lifts whose inverses are again binomials in the two-dimensional case, including an explicit inverse for a binomial family over Fq4. The three dimensional specialization yields permutation trinomials whose compositional inverses are again trinomials, together with explicit involution criteria and examples.
items.authors: Yi Li

items.title: Pointwise improvement of the error term in the higher rank hyperbolic lattice counting problem
items.abstract: We prove an upper bound for the error term in the higher rank hyperbolic lattice counting problem for ${\hbox{SL}(n, \mathbb{Z})}$. Blomer and Lutsko achieved recently a significant improvement of previous known results by Duke--Rudnick--Sarnak and Gorodnik--Nevo--Yehoshua. We deduce an improved upper bound for the error which holds for almost all pairs $z,w \in {\hbox{SL}(n, \mathbb{R})}$. We also derive a $\Omega$-result for the error term, in the spirit of Rudnick--Phillips.
items.authors: Dimitrios Chatzakos, Panagiotis Dimakis, Christos Katsivelos

items.title: On Solvable Automorphism Groups of Function Fields over Finite Fields
items.abstract: The classical Hurwitz bound gives a linear upper bound for automorphism groups of algebraic curves in characteristic zero, whereas algebraic curves in positive characteristic can have much larger automorphism groups. In this article, we firstly investigate the solvable subgroups and $p$-subgroups of $\operatorname{Aut}(F/\mathbb{F}_q)$ where $p=\operatorname{char}(\mathbb{F}_q)$ and $F/\mathbb{F}_q$ is a function field of genus $g_F\ge2$ with full constant field $\mathbb{F}_q$. We prove that there are explicit constants $C_q^{(\mathrm{sol})}$ and $C_q^{(p)}$, depending only on $q$, such that, for every solvable subgroup $G\le\operatorname{Aut}(F/\mathbb{F}_q)$ and every $p$-subgroup $P\le\operatorname{Aut}(F/\mathbb{F}_q)$, \[ |G|\le C_q^{(\mathrm{sol})}(g_F-1), \qquad |P|\le C_q^{(p)}(g_F-1). \] In particular, one may take $C_q^{(\mathrm{sol})}=12q^2(q-1)$ for $q\ge4$ and $C_q^{(p)}=5q$ for every $q$. In the second part of this article , we give the asymptotic lower bounds for solvable automorphism groups. For every $q$ there is an explicit constant $L_q>0$ and a sequence of function fields $F_i/\mathbb{F}_q$ with $g_{F_i}\to\infty$, together with solvable subgroups $G_i\le\operatorname{Aut}(F_i/\mathbb{F}_q)$, such that \[ |G_i|\ge L_q(g_{F_i}-1). \] For $q\ge5$ one may take $L_q=2q(q-1)/(q-2)$. If $q=r^2$ with $r\ge3$, an unramified tower construction over the Hermitian curve gives the stronger choice $L_q=2r^3(r-1)/(r-2)$. Moreover, as an application of our tower construction above, we improve the lower bound of Ma and Xing to $B_q\ge 2(q-1)/(q-2)$ for $q\ge 5$. As another application, we extend our method for bounding solvable automorphism groups to $p$-solvable subgroups, obtaining explicit linear bounds in terms of the genus.
items.authors: Henning Stichtenoth, Chaoping Xing, Zugan Xing

items.title: Automorphisms and canonical forms of integer lattices
items.abstract: We improve the Plesken--Souvignier algorithm for computing automorphism groups and isometries of positive definite integer quadratic lattices by exploiting characteristic sublattices and refining vector enumeration. For lattices with roots, we also use the Weyl group to accelerate the computation of canonical forms. Experiments with concrete implementations demonstrate substantial speedups and show that canonical forms can be computed at a cost comparable to that of computing automorphism groups.
items.authors: Simon Brandhorst, Tommy Hofmann

items.title: The WZ pair and finite congruences
items.abstract: We construct a meromorphic Wilf--Zeilberger pair for the hypergeometric series for \(3\ln 2\), completing the WZ proof left open by Guillera and Rogers. The same pair yields a one-parameter identity and, after a half-integer shift and differentiation, an inverse-binomial series for \(\zeta(3)\). We also study the finite truncations of the logarithmic series. For every prime \(p\ge 5\), we prove that the lower truncation is congruent to \(q_p(2)-1\) modulo \(p\), while the upper truncation is congruent to \(-\frac{7}{16}p^2B_{p-3}\) modulo \(p^3\). The proofs combine the WZ method with terminating hypergeometric identities, the Pfaff--Saalsch\"utz identity, and classical congruences for harmonic sums.
items.authors: Xiang Chen, Junyan Liu, Hengfei Lu

items.title: CM fibers of Shimura parametrizations and thirteen proofs of the class number one theorem
items.abstract: We determine thirteen entirely CM identity fibers of Shimura parametrizations attached to elliptic curves of rank two and conductor below $2000$. Each yields a proof of the imaginary quadratic class number one theorem. The argument combines the Gross--Zagier formula with the Ribet--Takahashi degree comparison to show that the fiber is completely explained by known CM points.
items.authors: Jingxuan Geng

items.title: Distribution of central values of Hecke $L$-functions of $n$-th order characters
items.abstract: We prove a one-sided central limit theorem for $\log |L(\tfrac 12,\chi)|$ in a thin family of $n$-th order Hecke characters, for $n \geq 3$. The proof combines the method of Radziwi{\l}{\l} and Soundararajan with a recent asymptotic formula of Diaconu, Ion, Pa\c{s}ol, and Popa for the twisted second moment with a power-saving error term. We also obtain upper bounds of the conjectured order of magnitude for the $2k$-th moments for $0< k< 1$.
items.authors: Lewis McGoldrick

items.title: A Half-Constant Upper Bound for Chowla's Cosine Problem
items.abstract: Let lambda(n) denote the infimum of -min_x sum_{a in A} cos(ax) over all sets A of n positive integers. While the classical Sidon-difference construction yields lambda(n) infinity} lambda(n)/sqrt(n) = cn^(1/4) for every n-element set A subset of [1, Cn]; and (2) (-min f_A)^3 ||f_A||_1^2 >= cn for every n-element set A subset of N. The second bound recovers the 1/5 exponent of Bedert and Shankar and improves it whenever ||f_A||_1 is small relative to -min f_A. Numerical values of the construction are reported up to |A| = 25,440.
items.authors: Bryan Bu, Fayzan Khan, Hyunjun Yi, Atharv Jha, Vihaan Vajpeyi, Ishaan Chandupatla, Madhav Nagpal

items.title: Holonomic sequences arising from meromorphic modular forms
items.abstract: We introduce a systematic framework for constructing holonomic recurrences from meromorphic modular forms. Its central ingredient is a modular analogue of creative telescoping, which turns finite-dimensional quotients of spaces of meromorphic modular forms into explicit recurrence operators. This provides a common explanation for several previously isolated examples: it recovers Ap\'ery's recurrence, Beukers' modular constructions and Zagier's seven sporadic recurrences. The framework also produces a large collection of new examples across different weights and groups. The modular origin of these sequences also confers them with non-trivial arithmetic properties, such as denominator bounds, irrationality statements, and $p$-adic congruences.
items.authors: Kam Cheong Au

items.title: An Enhanced Higher Green's Function on the Modular Curve
items.abstract: The higher Green's functions $G_{k/2}(z,w)$ on the modular curve are real-valued eigenfunctions of the hyperbolic Laplacian in each variable, with logarithmic singularities along the diagonal. Gross and Zagier conjectured that their values at CM points, after multiplication by suitable powers of the discriminants, are logarithms of absolute values of algebraic numbers. The conjecture was proved by Li, Bruinier, and Yang. Mellit proposed a complex refinement of this conjecture, predicting that the normalized CM values of a complex lift of the Green function are logarithms of algebraic numbers modulo periods. For $\Gamma=\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)$ and $k\in{4,6,8,10,14}$, we follow Zagier's construction of CM invariants from Eichler integrals of the Eisenstein series $E_4$. By applying Maass raising operators in both variables to a normalized iterated Eichler integral of a Bergman-type kernel, we obtain a complex-valued extension $\mathcal G_{k/2}^\bullet(z,w)$ whose real part is a constant multiple of $G_{k/2}(z,w)$. We study the normalized CM values of $\mathcal G_{k/2}^\bullet$ and describe their dependence on the choice of representatives of quadratic form classes. In particular, we show that replacing the quadratic form corresponding to the first variable by an equivalent one changes the exponential of the normalized value only by a root of unity. We also prove the algebraicity of these exponentials in the special case where the second CM point is $w_*=(1+i\sqrt d)/2$, with $d>3$ and $d\equiv3\pmod4$, and the class of the quadratic form corresponding to the first variable is equal to its inverse.
items.authors: Nina Sakharova

items.title: Likely and unlikely ramification of algebraic points on curves
items.abstract: This paper initiates the study of arithmetic properties of closed points of arbitrary degree on curves. We show that a pointless curve of rank $0$ can have only finitely many cyclic degree $\ell$ points for all sufficiently large primes $\ell$. More generally, we show that the residue fields of points on curves of genus at least $2$ and rank $0$ are often biased away from total ramification. The proof technique illuminates a natural intermediate conjecture between the Manin--Mumford conjecture and the Zilber--Pink conjecture for self-products of abelian varieties. This intermediate conjecture implies analogous results for other splitting profiles.
items.authors: Bianca Viray, Isabel Vogt

items.title: Denominators in the Farey Sequence, the Stern Sequence, and the Frobenius Problem with Relatively Prime Multipliers
items.abstract: The Frobenius problem asks, given two positive, relatively prime integers $a$ and $b$, what is the maximum integer that cannot be expressed as a linear combination of $a,b$ using non-negative coefficients? This problem is resolved. However, if we add the restriction that the coefficients themselves must also be relatively prime, we create an open problem with connections to the Stern and Farey sequences and the Jacobsthal function. We prove that under this new restriction, a maximum inexpressible integer still always exists, and explore its values and properties as functions of $a,b$.
items.authors: Grace Natalie Jaffe

items.title: Arithmetic jet spaces and the unramified Zilber--Pink conjecture for subvarieties of abelian varieties
items.abstract: We show how the methods of delta geometry can be used to bound the degree of points in the Zilber--Pink locus of a subvariety of an abelian variety, if the varieties are defined over a number field and we restrict to points with bounded ramification at a fixed prime.
items.authors: Netan Dogra, Arnab Saha

items.title: Higher derivatives of the Gram function
items.abstract: We study the nonlinear phenomenon of the asymptotics of higher-order derivatives of the Gram function $t_u$. We also prove the uniform distribution and continuous uniform distribution modulo one of $t^n_u$ for $n = 1, 2, \dots$. We use AI to formalize our proofs in Lean.
items.authors: Marius Dundulis, Ram\=unas Garunk\v{s}tis, Antanas Laurin\v{c}ikas, Raivydas \v{S}im\.enas

items.title: Roth's theorem on weighted projective lines
items.abstract: Let ${\mathbb P}^1_{\mathfrak q}$ be the weighted projective line with coprime weights ${\mathfrak q}=(q_0,q_1)$ and $L=q_0q_1$. The weighted Veronese map $\Phi\colon {\mathbb P}^1_{\mathfrak q}\to {\mathbb P}^1$ satisfies $h\circ\Phi=L\,{\mathfrak s}$. Pulling back Roth's theorem gives the optimal exponent $2L$ for the full rational orbit set. For points represented by coprime integral coordinates, counting suggests the smaller exponent $q_0+q_1$. We formulate this as a conjecture and prove an $S$-adic radical form under the $abc$ conjecture. For ${\mathfrak q}=(2,3)$ the resulting inequality at the target $[1:1]$ is the coprime Hall-type inequality, and Danilov--Elkies examples show that the exponent $5$ is sharp. We also prove the expected exponent unconditionally over characteristic-zero function fields for constant targets and polynomial approximants, and for almost every real target. A weighted $abc$ formulation is introduced; in signature $(3,2)$ finitely many coefficient pairs are equivalent to $abc$, and weighted Belyi maps transfer this input to arbitrary algebraic targets. Applications include a pullback form of Schmidt's subspace theorem, weighted Thue inequalities, and a counterexample to a naive weighted rescaling of Roth's index construction.
items.authors: Sajad Salami

items.title: The local structure of refined class groups in cyclotomic Iwasawa theory
items.abstract: We give an explicit local description of ray class refinements in cyclotomic Iwasawa theory. For distinct primes $p\geq5$ and $\ell$, and even $2\leq k\leq p-3$, we prove that the $\omega^{1-k}$-component of the $p$-primary ray class group of $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_p)$, with squarefree modulus supported above $\ell$, is nonzero if and only if $p\mid\ell(1-\ell^k)B_k$. In the cyclotomic tower, we determine the local modules and their correction modulo the diagonal global Tate module, obtaining an explicit determinant formula. Their Frobenius Euler factors, combined with the Mazur--Wiles theorem, yield a ray class form of the Iwasawa main conjecture for nonexceptional odd characters. We also obtain exact class number valuation comparisons at every layer, including those before stabilization, recover Finat's formula for $\ell=2$, and deduce refined $\mu$-vanishing from Ferrero--Washington. The cyclotomic character explains the Wieferich exception, while existing Eisenstein congruence theorems connect the divisibility criteria with prime-level Ramanujan-style congruences.
items.authors: Su Hu, Min-Soo Kim

items.title: Simultaneously preperiodic points and colliding orbits for families of polynomials in characteristic $p$
items.abstract: Let $k=\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$ and let $f\in k[X]$ be a polynomial of degree at least $2$ such that $f-f(0)$ is non-additive. For $\alpha,\beta$ in an algebraically closed extension $L$ of $k$, we prove that there are infinitely many $\lambda\in L$ for which both points are preperiodic under $f(X)+\lambda$ if and only if $\alpha,\beta\in k$ or $f(\beta)-f(\alpha)\in E_f$. Here $E_f=\{c\in G_f:(f-f(0))^n(c)\in G_f\text{ for every }n\ge0\}$, where $G_f=\{c\in k : f(X+c)-f(X)\in k\}$. We also provide a necessary and sufficient criterion for the corresponding colliding orbits set to be infinite.
items.authors: Jungin Lee, GyeongHyeon Nam

items.title: A sharp lower bound for the sextic large sieve
items.abstract: We establish a matching lower bound for the sextic large sieve over the Eisenstein integers in an unbalanced range, with both indices restricted to squarefree ideals. Let $\Xi_6(A,B)$ denote the squared operator norm of the sextic residue-character matrix with row and column norms at most $A$ and $B$, respectively, outside a fixed finite set of primes containing those above $6$. For every fixed $0 0$, we prove $\Xi_6(A,B)\gg_{\delta,\varepsilon}(AB)^{-\varepsilon}A^{5/6}B^{1/3}$ for $B^{16/11+\delta}\le A\le B^{2-\delta}$. Consequently, the full-cutoff norm satisfies $\Xi_6(X,X)\gg_\varepsilon X^{17/16-\varepsilon}$. The main difficulty is to preserve the large second moment supplied by Gauss sums when the column moduli are restricted to be squarefree. We prove a second-moment formula uniform in the prime exclusions and character twists arising from M\"obius inversion, and use it to show that the squarefree projection retains a positive proportion of the original moment. A separate argument combining cubic and sextic large-sieve bounds then transfers the lower bound to squarefree rows.
items.authors: Yuanda Xu, Hejian Sang

items.title: Yau's number-theoretic conjecture and sharp spectral bounds for quantum harmonic oscillators
items.abstract: We prove Yau's number-theoretic conjecture on positive integral points in real right simplices in every dimension $n\ge3$, and apply the resulting sharp polynomial bound to quantum harmonic oscillators. The lattice-point bound holds for every choice of positive real intercepts for which the count is nonzero, with equality precisely when all intercepts equal the same integer. For oscillators in dimensions $n\ge3$, we obtain explicit upper bounds for eigenvalue counts and spectral remainders for arbitrary positive frequencies at every threshold at or above the lowest eigenvalue. For frequencies with rational ratios in dimensions $n\ge2$, an additional lattice coordinate and interpolation give bounds for energy sums, or first Riesz means, at every threshold. When all frequencies are equal (the isotropic case), the oscillator attains these bounds: the counting bound is exact at its energy levels, and interpolation on its natural energy grid recovers the energy sum at every threshold. In three dimensions, the exact formula displays the periodic contribution associated with the resonance discussed by Fefferman and Seco. The proof builds on the slicing method of Yau and Zhang. Arithmetic and geometric consequences include explicit bounds for smooth numbers and lattice-point discrepancies.
items.authors: Zhiwen Liu, Stephen S. -T. Yau, Hao Zuo

items.title: A recurrence in logarithmic M\"obius sums with coprimality conditions via Euler--Maclaurin
items.abstract: We derive a recurrence for logarithmically weighted M\"obius sums by combining M\"obius inversion with the Euler--Maclaurin summation formula. Consequently, starting from estimates of orders zero, one and two, we obtain polynomial approximations for these sums for every nonnegative integer exponent of $\log$. We then extend these estimates to sums with coprimality conditions via a convolution identity and to sums weighted by the reciprocal of the sum-of-divisors function. We also establish the nonnegativity of the latter sums for every positive integer logarithmic order, proving that they never change sign.
items.authors: Sebastian Zuniga-Alterman

items.title: Fine structure of even Galois deformation rings
items.abstract: For every even Galois representation in a family of prime conductor $\ell$, we prove that if $k \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$ is maximal such that \[\ell \equiv 1 \bmod 3^k\] then the even mod $3$ deformation ring $R_S \otimes_{\mathbb{Z}_3} \mathbb{F}_3$ of level $S=\{\ell,3\}$ does not have a quotient isomorphic to $\mathbb{F}_3[T]/(T^{2+3^{k-1}})$. As a corollary, we deduce that the global even deformation rings $R_S$ are finite and flat in the category of $\mathbb{Z}_3$-modules.
items.authors: Peter Vang Uttenthal

items.title: A generating function identity for finite and symmetric multiple zeta values via Dougall's bilateral ${}_2H_2$ summation
items.abstract: We establish a generating function identity for finite and symmetric multiple zeta values using Dougall's bilateral ${}_2H_2$ summation formula. As an application, we prove a restricted sum formula in which the parity of each component of the index is prescribed. We also derive a generating function identity for finite multiple zeta values $\zeta^{}_{\mathcal{A}}(\{1,2\}^n)$ and symmetric multiple zeta values $\zeta^{}_{\mathcal{S}}(\{1,2\}^n)$, thereby proving Kaneko's conjecture for finite multiple zeta values and its symmetric analogue.
items.authors: Takumi Maesaka, Masataka Ono

items.title: On Berndt-Straub conjectures about zeros of generalized Ramanujan polynomials
items.abstract: We settle two conjectures of Berndt and Straub asserting that all nonzero zeros of the generalized Ramanujan polynomials $R_k(x;\chi,\psi)$ and $S_{2n}(x;\chi,\chi)$ lie on the unit circle for real nonprincipal Dirichlet characters. We prove their conjecture for $R_k$. For $S_{2n}$, we prove that at most four nonzero zeros lie off the unit circle, all purely imaginary. If $\chi_{163}=\left(\frac{\cdot}{163}\right)$ is the primitive quadratic character modulo $163$, then $S_6(x;\chi_{163},\chi_{163})$ has four exceptional zeros, showing that this bound is sharp. This disproves the second conjecture and establishes that the `Riemann hypothesis for period polynomials' can fail for Eisenstein newforms. Further, we introduce a transcendental invariant whose sign determines whether exceptional zeros of $S_{2n}(x;\chi,\chi)$ occur in all sufficiently large degrees, and show that these zeros converge to transcendental limits off the unit circle. For primitive odd characters, we relate this invariant and these limits to Fekete polynomials.
items.authors: Siddhi Pathak

items.title: A certified classical-strip comparison for the de Bruijn-Newman constant
items.abstract: We give a directed comparison beginning with the classical zero strip \(\lvert\Ima z\rvert\le1\) for the de Bruijn--Newman heat deformation. Under explicitly stated complete model-to-function source, localisation and global contact premises, translated-probe estimates imply \[ \Lambda\le\frac{148611789321711}{10^{15}} =0.148611789321711<0.148612. \] The construction uses Raymond's finite source data and 57 fixed translated kernels, independently checked by rational Bernstein certificates. An explicit finite Weyl estimate improves the positive first-head tail and its centred logarithmic moment. A centred cone transfer retains the original physical error allowances, exceptional debit and additive cone reserve, and charges the change in existing phase-surplus credits. Directed tail enclosures are regenerated at 192 and 256 bits; a separate exact-rational auditor accepts all 19,023 comparison steps. The controlled decrease from the complete two-source comparison is \(0.000021760452379\). We also prove a compatible matched logarithmic tail transfer and identify the finite requirements for stronger exponent pairs. A supplementary section records Raymond's ceiling below \(0.116398\) under the distinct \(7/8\) zero-free hypothesis.
items.authors: Michel Planat

items.title: Counting matrices with given characteristic polynomial
items.abstract: Let $f$ be a monic polynomial of degree $n$ with integer coefficients. We use Fourier analysis to prove a new upper bound on the number of $n\times n$ matrices with characteristic polynomial $f$ and integer entries in $[-T,T]$, as $T\to \infty$. The implied constant in our bound only depends on $n$ and is otherwise uniform in $f$. Our bound improves on recent work of Habegger, Ostafe and Shparlinski for $n\geq 4$.
items.authors: Tim Browning, Fabian Gundlach, Will Sawin

items.title: Higher rank elliptic sieve via CM endomorphisms
items.abstract: A theorem of Landau and Ramanujan states that almost all integers are not sums of two squares (when ordered by their absolute value). Equivalently, almost all integers are not norms from the Gaussian rationals $\mathbb{Q}(i)$. In this paper, we prove a version of this norm result for elliptic curves $E$. Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over a number field $K$ with complex multiplication, such that $K$ contains the endomorphism ring of $E$. For a fixed non-torsion point $P \in E(K)$ and an abelian extension $L/K$, we show that subject to a technical condition, the $y$-coordinate of almost all multiples of $P$ does not belong to the norm group of $L$. The proof is an adaptation of an argument of Bhakta et al. , whose main tools are elliptic divisibility sequences and a sieve technique known as the elliptic sieve. To account for the points in $E(K)$ arising from the additional endomorphisms, we apply the elliptic sieve to elliptic nets, a higher-rank generalisation of elliptic divisibility sequences. This approach demonstrates the possibility of applying the elliptic sieve to $\mathbb{Z}$--linear combination of points on elliptic curves and the usefulness of elliptic nets to counting problems on elliptic curves.
items.authors: Hang Lok Edison Au-Yeung

items.title: Untrodden pathways in the study of partitions with parts separated by parity
items.abstract: In this paper, we study a partition function with parts separated by parity from a family of partition functions introduced by Andrews in 2019. We first show that its generating function admit representation in terms of mock modular forms of weight $3/2$. We then initiate a study of smallest-part partition function analogues of partitions with parts separated by parity, which, to the best of our knowledge, has not previously been investigated in the literature. We show that the generating functions of these smallest-part partition functions are likewise expressible in terms of mock modular forms, mock Maass theta functions and Zagier's $q$-series $H(q)$, which he describes as a ``half-derivative of the Dedekind eta-function". Our study also leads to new combinatorial interpretations of the coefficients of the aforementioned mock modular form, function $\sigma^*(q)$, and mock theta functions $\psi(q)$ and $A(q)$ in terms of odd Ferrers graphs. Moreover, we provide a quantum $q$-series identity involving Ramanujan's famous $\sigma(q)$ function. We also derive the leading asymptotic term of one of these partition functions, whose generating function we first express in terms of $\sigma^*(q)$.
items.authors: Nargish Punia, Rahul Kumar

items.title: A Combinatorial Proof of Partition Identities for the Number of Distinct Part Sizes
items.abstract: In 1984, Bressoud and Subbarao established an interesting weighted partition identity connecting the partition function and the divisor function. Recently, the first author, jointly with Bhoria, Eyyunni, and Maji, extended the work of Bressoud and Subbarao and obtained the following analogous weighted partition identity. For any $n \in \mathbb{N}$, they obtained \begin{equation*} p^{(2)}(n) = \sum_{\pi \in \mathcal{D}(n)} (-1)^{ \# (\pi) }s(\pi) \left( \ell(\pi) - s(\pi) \right). \end{equation*} In the present paper, we provide a combinatorial proof of the above identity and extend the result for $p^{(k)}(n)$, where $p^{(k)}(n)$ denotes the number of partitions of $n$ into exactly $k$ distinct part sizes.
items.authors: Archit Agarwal, Meghali Garg

items.title: On Permutations Whose Adjacent-Sum Reciprocals Sum to One
items.abstract: In this paper, we give a constructive proof that for any integer n>7 (resp. n>6), the numbers 1,2,...,n can be arranged in a circle (resp. in a line) such that the sum of the reciprocals of all adjacent sums equals 1. The above conjecture was originally posed by Zhi-Wei Sun. Partitioning the integers according to n mod 12 into nine residue classes, we prove a recursive proposition and inductively construct new examples. Main lemmas and propositions in introduction are proved in Section 2. The rest of the cases are handled by explicit constructions in appendix.
items.authors: Jinggao Ai, Dingsheng Hu, Junmin Yan

items.title: Some applications of the quasi-Riemann hypothesis to class groups and small generators of number fields
items.abstract: We prove an effective version of the Chebotarev density theorem, conditional on the quasi-Riemann hypothesis for the Dedekind zeta function. Drawing on recent breakthroughs of OpenAI and Cureton--Thorner, we make unconditional the Ellenberg--Venkatesh bounds on $\ell$-torsion in class groups of number fields and extend an averaged result of Lemke Oliver--Smith to arbitrary families of degree-$d$-fields. Further applications are given to the least prime splitting and to small generators in number fields.
items.authors: Christopher Frei, Efthymios Sofos, Martin Widmer

items.title: Linking numbers and special differential characters in arithmetic hyperbolic manifolds
items.abstract: We construct non-holomorphic Siegel modular forms whose coefficients encode linking numbers in arithmetic hyperbolic manifolds of simplest type. Our proofs rely on an improved understanding of the transgression forms appearing in Kudla--Millson theory, and along the way we establish some structural properties including in particular their expected current equations.
items.authors: Mads Bjerge Christensen

items.title: Wendt's determinant and finiteness of prime characteristics for permutation binomials
items.abstract: For $f(X)=X^r(X^s+a)\in\mathbb F_{p^m}[X]$, with $m,r,s\geqslant1$ and $a\in\mathbb F_{p^m}^\times$, put $g=\gcd(s,p^m-1)$. We prove that, for each fixed $g$, only finitely many prime characteristics $p$ admit such permutation binomials, even as $m,r,s,a$ vary. If $6\nmid g$, every such $p$ divides Wendt's determinant $W_g=\operatorname{Res}_X(X^g-1,(X+1)^g-1)$, which is nonzero. When $6\mid g$, this determinant vanishes; inverse power sums and iterated resultants yield an explicit nonzero integer divisible by every such $p>2g+1$. We determine the exact admissible characteristics for $1\leqslant g\leqslant10$, obtain a further divisibility condition over prime fields, and show that in prime fields $g=11$ occurs precisely when $p=23$.
items.authors: Zhichao Tang, Xiang Fan

items.title: Geometric bounds on norms of signed indecomposable integers
items.abstract: We establish bounds on the norm of signed indecomposable integers in totally real number fields, via a geometric argument. We also improve the bound on the norm of totally positive indecomposable integers in real quadratic fields by Tinkov\'a and Voutier.
items.authors: Siu Hang Man, Zden\v{e}k Pezlar, Pavlo Yatsyna

items.title: Counting quaternion extensions by multi-heights
items.abstract: We prove a case of a conjecture of Gundlach on the number of Galois extensions over $\QQ$ with bounded multi-invariants for the group $G=Q_8$. We also obtain results when imposing local conditions at the wildly ramified place. As an application, we prove asymptotics for the number of $Q_8$-extensions with bounded product of ramified primes.
items.authors: Willem Hansen

items.title: Uniformly Bounded Orthonormal Bases of Homogeneous Polynomials on the Complex Sphere
items.abstract: We resolve the long-standing problem of Rudin concerning uniformly bounded orthonormal bases of homogeneous polynomials on complex unit spheres. Specifically, we show that for every $K \geq 2$ and $N \geq 0$ there exists a basis of degree $N$ homogeneous polynomials in $\mathbb{C}^K$ that is orthonormal with respect to the surface measure of the unit sphere of $\mathbb{C}^K$ and uniformly bounded by a constant depending only on $K$ on the unit ball of $\mathbb{C}^K$. Bourgain resolved the case $K = 2$ in 1985 and the case $K = 3$ in 2016. No cases $K \geq 4$ were previously known.
items.authors: Felipe Gon\c{c}alves, Jo\~ao P. Ferreira, Maksym Radziwi\l{}\l{}

items.title: Dynamical degrees of automorphisms of non-projective hyperk\"ahler manifolds
items.abstract: We determine the dynamical degrees of bimeromorphic automorphisms of hyperk\"ahler manifolds of all known deformation types with irreducible characteristic polynomial.
items.authors: Eva Bayer-Fluckiger, Stevell Muller, Matthias Sch\"utt

items.title: A series with a Cantorval set of subsums and ratio of consecutive terms tending to $1/2$ (the second Jones problem)
items.abstract: The second Jones problem (2011) consists in determining whether there exists a convergent positive series for which the ratio of consecutive terms has a limit and the set of subsums is a Cantorval; in the survey by G{\l}{\k a}b and Prus-Wi\'sniowski (2026) this problem is included in the list of open problems. In this paper, a family of such series is constructed explicitly as combinations of blocks of the form $\frac{2^k-1}{2^t} + \frac{2^{k-1}}{2^t} + \frac{2^{k-2}}{2^t} + \cdots + \frac{2}{2^t}$, where $t$ is the index of the last term of the block in the series and $k\ge2$ is the length of the block. For each series of the family it is proved that its set of subsums contains an interval and is not a finite union of closed intervals, and hence is a Cantorval. The proof relies on mixed-radix numerical systems with a redundant alphabet and uses an idea of Guthrie and Nymann (1988). If the lengths of the blocks tend to infinity, then the limit of the ratio of consecutive terms of such series is $\tfrac{1}{2}$, which, by a result of Jones, is the only possible value of the limit for which the set of subsums of a series can be a Cantorval. Thus, an affirmative answer to the second Jones problem is obtained.
items.authors: Mykola Pratsiovytyi, Yaroslav Vynnyshyn, Oleh Vynnyshyn

items.title: Schauder and Riesz Bases for Higher-Dimensional Lebesgue Spaces Inspired by ReLU Neural Networks
items.abstract: Motivated by the role of piecewise linear functions in ReLU neural networks, we study systems of dilated functions in the Lebesgue spaces $L_q([0,1]^d)$, $q\in(1,\infty)$. For a sequence $\tau\in\ell_1$ we consider the operator $T_\tau g(x)=\sum_{k=1}^\infty \tau_k g(kx)$ and the function system $\mathcal Z^\tau$ obtained by applying it to the trigonometric system. We show that $\tau\mapsto T_\tau$ is an isomorphism of algebras from $\ell_1$ with the Dirichlet convolution as multiplication onto an algebra of operators and connect the inverse of $T_\tau$ to the inverse of $\tau$ with respect to the Dirichlet convolution. We give explicit conditions on $\tau$, under which the resulting system $\mathcal Z^\tau$ is a Schauder basis of $L_q([0,1]^d)$ and, for $q=2$, a Riesz basis for which we estimate the Riesz constants in terms of $\tau$. We characterise the Riesz bases of this type in terms of a sequence space of Dirichlet convolution multipliers, and we treat mixed systems of cosine and sine functions with different sequences. Finally, we apply these results to the system generated by two piecewise linear functions inspired by ReLU networks and improve the known lower Riesz constant to $2/3$, independently of the dimension.
items.authors: Julian Billner, Cornelia Schneider

items.title: Lattices with Large Kissing Number from Local Density
items.abstract: Let $\kappa_p(n)$ denote the maximum kissing number of a lattice $\mathcal{L} \subset \mathbb{R}^n$. We prove that $\kappa_p(n) \geq 2^{\Omega(\sqrt{n})}$ for all $p\ge 1$ and that $\kappa_p(n) \geq \Omega(\alpha_p^n)$ for all $p > 2$, where $\alpha_p > 1$ is a constant depending only on $p$. In particular, our former result improves on the previously best known lower bound of $\kappa_2(n) \geq 2^{\Theta(\log^2 n)}$ for the $\ell_2$ kissing number, which has stood for over $60$ years. (In concurrent and independent work, Laarhoven and Kominers [arXiv, 2026] showed a similar lower bound on $\kappa_2(n)$ using similar techniques.) In fact, our lower bounds follow from efficient (randomized) constructions of lattices with large kissing number. Our results use a general construction of lattices with large kissing number. Specifically, we show a simple equivalence between such lattices and a new object that we call an exact locally dense lattice. Closely related objects appear throughout the literature on computational lattice problems. Our constructions of lattices with large kissing number then follow as corollaries by showing that constructions due to Bennett and Peikert [RANDOM, 2023] (using Craig lattices) and Aggarwal and Stephens-Davidowitz [STOC, 2018] (using sparsification of $\mathbb{Z}^n$) in fact give exact locally dense lattices, as well as a new construction of exact locally dense lattices built from rotations of the $m$-dimensional checkerboard lattice $D_m$.
items.authors: Huck Bennett, Minki Hhan, Zihan Li, Noah Stephens-Davidowitz

items.title: Survivor Set of Gauss Map with a Hole at $1$
items.abstract: Let $T$ be the Gauss map. For each $\alpha\in [0,1]$, let $E(\alpha)$ be the survivor set consisting of all $x\in [0,1]$ whose orbit $\{T^k(x):k\ge 0\}$ never enters the interval $(\alpha,1]$. We prove that the set-valued function $\alpha\mapsto E(\alpha)$ is increasing and locally constant almost everywhere. Moreover, we explicitly characterize all intervals where the function $\alpha\mapsto E(\alpha)$ remains constant. We also describe the points at which the map $\alpha\mapsto E(\alpha)$ is not locally constant. Further, we obtain the Hausdorff dimension of $E(\alpha)$ for all $\alpha\in [0,1]$. We prove that the function $\alpha\mapsto \dim_H(E(\alpha))$ forms a devil's staircase on $(0,1]$, but is not continuous at $0$. This discontinuity implies that the result of Raith [Acta Math. Univ. Comenian. 63 (1994), 39-53] fails for piecewise monotone interval maps with infinitely many branches. Finally, we give an application quantifying the set of points sharing identical $\alpha$-continued fraction expansion and regular continued fraction expansion.
items.authors: Cheng Liu, Lingmin Liao

items.title: How iterated sumsets grow under the assumption of small doubling
items.abstract: Let $K>1$ be a real number and let $A\subsetneq \mathbb Z$ be a finite and nonempty subset. Suppose $|A+A|<K|A|$. A fundamental open problem is to characterize the size of higher iterated sumsets $nA = A+\cdots+A$ ($n$-fold sumset). In 2004, Terry Tao formally posed the problem of determining the optimal growth function governing iterated sumsets of small-doubling sets. In this manuscript, we give a solution to this long-standing open problem for large enough $n$.
items.authors: Dongchun Han, Qinghai Zhong

items.title: Polynomial Identities for Generalized Fibonacci Sequences
items.abstract: The Fibonacci, Lucas, and Pell sequences satisfy certain families of ``polynomial'' identities. While a few members of these families are well-known, we are not able to find a general statement of these identities in the mathematical literature. We show that such polynomial identities exist for many generalized Fibonacci sequences, and we classify sequences that have these identities obtained by two distinct approaches. One approach uses the Girard-Waring formula, while the other relies on Binet's formula and linear algebra.
items.authors: Joey Glampe, Aryaman Joshi, Swagat Malla, Matthew Richey, Matthew Wright

items.title: A trace Paley-Wiener theorem for $\mathrm{GL}_{n}(F)\backslash \mathrm{GL}_{n}(E)$, with $E/F$ a quadratic extension of non-Archimedean local fields
items.abstract: We extend the classical trace Paley-Wiener theorem for $p$-adic reductive groups, given by Bernstein, Deligne and Kazhdan in 1986, to a relative case. That is when $E/F$ is a quadratic extension of $p$-adic fields, the main result is a scalar Paley-Wiener theorem for relative Bessel distributions on $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)\backslash \mathrm{GL}_n(E)$. These distributions are relative character of the form $$\pi\mapsto I_\pi (f), \ f\in C_c^\infty(\mathrm{GL}_n(E)),$$ as $\pi$ ranges over $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$-distinguished irreducible tempered representations, and are constructed from a $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$-invariant functional and a Whittaker functional. Using the local Langlands correspondence, and the base-change from a unitary group, we show that the relative characters can be described as elements of the "generic" Bernstein center of the unitary group $U(n)$.
items.authors: Juliette Coutens

items.title: Crystals and the parabolicity conjecture
items.abstract: These notes introduce crystals and crystalline Dieudonn\'e theory through the example of abelian varieties. After discussing $p$-divisible groups, $F$-isocrystals, slope filtrations, and overconvergence, we explain the parabolicity theorem for $F$-isocrystals and some of its applications to monodromy and Hecke orbits. Two appendices formulate research projects on isocrystals over formal schemes and on monodromy beyond the constant-slope setting. The exposition is intended for readers familiar with basic algebraic geometry and the \'etale and fppf topologies; prior knowledge of Witt vectors is helpful but not required.
items.authors: Marco D'Addezio

items.title: Post-critically finite polynomials in characteristic $p$
items.abstract: It follows from the compactness of the connectedness locus that the locus of PCF polynomials in the moduli space of polynomials of degree d (at least 2) over the complex number is a countable union of zero-dimensional subvarieties. Over fields of characteristic p the analogous claim is certainly false, so it is natural to ask how large the components of the PCF locus can be. We show that the components of the PCF locus in the moduli space of polynomials of degree d over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p>0 have dimension at most d/p and that this bound is sharp, in the strong sense that for every p and d there are infinitely many distinct PCF components whose dimension is the greatest integer no greater than this bound (except in the case $p=d=2$).
items.authors: Patrick Ingram

items.title: Universal Shift Congruences for Weighted Permutation Sequences
items.abstract: The involution numbers $1,1,2,4,10,26,\ldots$ repeat modulo $3$, $5$ and $7$. We explain this, and many similar patterns, by one rule. Many sequences count permutations in which every cycle of length $m$ carries a weight $w_m$ (involutions, derangements, "sets of lists", and many others in the OEIS). Writing $A(n)$ for such a count, the rule is $A(n+k)\equiv A(n)A(k)$ modulo $\mathrm{lcm}(n,k)$. It generalizes our earlier proof of the case modulo $k$ for one such sequence, but now it holds for all weights at once, as a coefficientwise congruence between universal polynomials, and we find the largest modulus that works for the universal polynomials, $nk/\mathrm{rad}(\gcd(n,k))$, and show that nothing larger does. We then show that passing from $k$ to $pk$ behaves like raising to the $p$-th power modulo a high power of $p$, with a sharp exponent for the polynomials, which gives $A(p^r)\equiv(w_1+(p-1)w_p)^{p^{r-1}}$ modulo $p^r$ for odd $p$, and explains why the prime $2$ is special. A family of sequences defined by Lagrange inversion fits the same framework, which proves Bala's conjecture for the whole family (the single sequence A278070 had been proved earlier by an automated system) and the divisibility observed in the entries A251568 and A251569. As further applications we prove OEIS conjectures of Richman, Hanna, van Hoeij and Bala (A227937), and the theorems apply to 101 OEIS sequences, whose congruences are recorded in a supplementary catalogue. Higher-order versions of the content formula are treated in a separate paper.
items.authors: Ahaan Kallat

items.title: Cubic moments of eigenfunctions on surfaces
items.abstract: We identify Gaussian curvature as a local mechanism for cubic cancellation of Laplace eigenfunctions on Riemannian surfaces, without arithmetic or dynamical assumptions. For $L^2$-normalized local solutions at frequency $\lambda$, cubic integrals against smooth compactly supported weights tend to zero whenever the curvature is nonzero almost everywhere where the weight is nonzero. Finite-order nondegeneracy yields sharp polynomial decay rates. In particular, on closed surfaces with nowhere-vanishing curvature, we obtain the rate $O(\lambda^{-1/6})$, attained by spherical harmonics on the round sphere. This proves the cubic case of the Gaussian moment conjecture for all normalized real eigenfunctions on closed negatively curved surfaces. The local proof rests on an exact identity relating the reduced phase at a Fermat point to Gaussian curvature. On complete hyperbolic surfaces with positive systole, we also prove global $O((\log\lambda)^{-3/2})$ decay for $L^2$-normalized eigenfunctions and smooth weights with bounded covariant derivatives through order two, without assuming finite area.
items.authors: Xing Wang, Cheng Zhang

items.title: Nonarchimedean discrete groups and quasi-isometric doubles of free groups
items.abstract: For any nonarchimedean local field $k$, we exhibit the first examples of Zariski-dense, discrete subgroups of special linear groups over $k$, which are not commensurable to any lattice in the points of a semisimple group over a local field, and contain an infinite index subgroup isomorphic to a lattice in the $k$-points of a higher rank $k$-semisimple group. We prove that any Gromov-hyperbolic double of a non-elementary free group along a cyclic subgroup embeds as a quasi-isometrically embedded subgroup of $\mathsf{SL}_5(k')\times \mathsf{SL}_5(k')$, where $k'$ is a discretely valued field. More precisely, $k'$ is the field of rational functions $k(t)$ equipped with the Gauss valuation and $k$ is any nonarchimedean local field of characteristic not equal to $2$ or $3$.
items.authors: Konstantinos Tsouvalas

items.title: Depth-zero local Langlands via shtukas in mixed characteristic
items.abstract: Assuming a smoothness property for mixed-characteristic shtuka spaces and hyperbolic localization for twisted sheaves, we determine the inertial restriction of the Fargues-Scholze $L$-parameter for irreducible depth-zero representations. Let $E$ be a non-archimedean local field of residue characteristic $p$, let $G$ be an unramified connected reductive group over $E$, and let $\pi$ be an irreducible smooth depth-zero representation of $G(E)$ over $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_{\ell}$ where $\ell$ is a prime number which does not divide $p|\pi_0Z(G)|$. Let $\varphi_{\pi}^{\operatorname{FS}}$ be the Fargues-Scholze $L$-parameter associated to $\pi$. We describe the restriction of $\varphi_{\pi}^{\operatorname{FS}}$ to the inertia subgroup in terms of Deligne-Lusztig theory. We prove this by computing the inertia action on the cohomology of shtuka spaces with depth-zero level structure. As an application, we prove that the Fargues--Scholze $L$-parameters agree with DeBacker--Reeder $L$-parameters over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_{\ell}$.
items.authors: Chenji Fu

items.title: $2$-large sets are sets of nil-Bohr recurrence
items.abstract: A set $S$ of positive integers is $2$-large if every two-coloring contains arbitrarily long monochromatic arithmetic progressions with common difference in $S$. We prove that every such set meets every nil-Bohr neighborhood of $0$. This proves a conjecture of the first author and gives a sharp answer to a question of Host, Kra, and Maass. We also show that, for every fixed nil-Bohr neighborhood \(B\) of \(0\) and every \(\eps>0\), restricting the common difference to \(B\) increases the extremal number for \(k\)-term arithmetic progressions by at most a factor of \(1+\eps\), provided \(k\) is sufficiently large.
items.authors: Ryan Alweiss, Sohail Farhangi

items.title: Galois coinvariants and fundamental groups of arithmetic schemes
items.abstract: We study Galois coinvariants of the geometric \'etale fundamental group and \'etale cohomology of varieties over a finitely generated field $k$. We establish finiteness properties of these coinvariants for (possibly infinite) Galois extensions $L/k$ such that $\operatorname{Gal}(L/k)^{\mathrm{ab}}$ has finite exponent. As an application, we obtain a finiteness result for \'etale fundamental groups of arithmetic schemes over number fields.
items.authors: Benjamin Steklov

items.title: The weak cylinder conjecture for polynomial graphs of bounded degree
items.abstract: Ball's weak cylinder conjecture asserts that a set of $p^2$ points in $\mathrm{AG}(3,p)$ with at least $p$ non-determined directions is a union of $p$ parallel lines. We prove the conjecture for sets admitting a polynomial graph representation of total degree at most $D$, provided that $p>D^{9/2}$. More precisely, a non-cylindrical graph of degree $D\ge3$ satisfies $|\mathcal{N}_S|\le p+1-\lceil p/(D-1)\rceil$ under the same hypothesis. This bound is attained when $p\equiv1\pmod{D-1}$. The proof relates non-determined directions to permutation polynomials on parallel affine lines. A rigidity lemma for moving line restrictions, together with a reconstruction of their compositional components, bounds the number of contributing directions uniformly in $p$. Directions with affine restrictions are treated separately; all other contributions are bounded using geometric indecomposability and the Weil bound for plane curves.
items.authors: Daniele Bartoli, Alessandro Giannoni

items.title: Microlocal Arthur packets as a quasi-canonical basis of stable distributions
items.abstract: We show that microlocal Arthur packets can be reconstructed from an otherwise underdetermined system of linear equations arising from Kashiwara's local index theorem. The key is a geometric rigidity property of Arthur orbits which, together with Fourier symmetry, uniquely determines the microlocal multiplicities defining these packets. This realizes the associated Arthur distribution as the unique normalized element in the intersection of two filtered spaces of standard stable distributions related by Fourier transform. Under standard enhanced local Langlands hypotheses and Aubert compatibility, this gives an alternative representation-theoretic definition of microlocal Arthur packets for general connected reductive $p$-adic groups that does not use twisted endoscopy and ensures stability through the stability of tempered packet distributions. In the unipotent setting, we use this characterization to prove agreement between endoscopic and microlocal Arthur packets for split $\mathrm{SO}_{2n+1}$ when the residue characteristic is at least $6n+4$. We further use this characterization to compute all unipotent Arthur packets with unramified real infinitesimal character for inner-to-split adjoint exceptional $p$-adic groups. In this exceptional setting, we prove the microlocal weak Arthur packet conjecture and give counterexamples to the microlocal analogues of the least- and greatest-parameter conjectures.
items.authors: Dan Ciubotaru, Emile Okada

items.title: p-adic Hodge theory of unipotent completions revisited
items.abstract: Let $K/\mathbb{Q}_p$ be a finite extension, and let $X/K$ be an algebraic variety. We present a new proof that the unipotent completion of the \'etale fundamental group of $X_{\bar{K}}$ is a pro-de Rham representation, and show that it is pro-semi-stable whenever $X$ has semi-stable \'etale cohomology. We also reprove, using syntomic methods, that it is pro-crystalline at integral base points whenever $X$ admits a smooth proper formal model. All three proofs use the bar construction and are inspired by Wojtkowiak's approach to unipotent fundamental groups.
items.authors: Ruth Wild

items.title: Privileged $\mathrm{SL}_3$-local systems are motivic
items.abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth projective variety over the complex numbers, and let $\mathbb{V}$ be an irreducible privileged $\mathrm{SL}_3$-local system on $X$ in the sense of Esnault and Groechenig. We show that $\mathbb{V}$ is of geometric origin. We also give an example of a privileged but non-rigid $\mathrm{SL}_3$-local system.
items.authors: Julia Meng, Charlie Wu

items.title: Square integrable representations and Hecke eigenvalues over a local non-archimedian field
items.abstract: Let $G$ be a split connected semi-simple group over a local non-archimedean field $F$. In this paper we study the action of Hecke operators on the Schwartz space of half-densities on the moduli stack $\bpo$ of $G$-bundles on ${\mathbb P}^1$ endowed with a trivialization at $0$ and $\infty$. This space is a representation of $G(F)\times G(F)$ which contains the regular representation of $G(F)$. We show that this inclusion is an isomorphism on the cuspidal part. In addition we show that every irreducible square-integrable representation $\pi$ of $G(F)$ defines a Hecke eigenvalue. As a byproduct we show that every irreducible square-integrable representation of $G(F)$ with an Iwahori fixed vector defines a ${\mathbb C}$-point on the Calogero-Moser space associated to $G$. We also show that for $G=PGL(N)$ the eigenvalues of certain "simplest non-trivial" Hecke operators are essentially equal to the values of the character of $\pi$ on regular elliptic elements. These results are parallel to some of the results of our previous publication where some analogous statements are proved in the case when $F$ is a finite field.
items.authors: Alexander Braverman, David Kazhdan

items.title: Hyperelliptic curves on $K3$ surfaces
items.abstract: We study hyperelliptic curves on $K3$ surfaces. We show that any number of general points on a $K3$ surface of Picard rank one can be connected by a hyperelliptic curve. As a by-product we recover the Beauville--Voisin decomposition of the small diagonal, together with some new bounds on its torsion order in the integral Chow group. On the arithmetic side, given a $K3$ surface $X$ of geometric Picard rank one defined over a number field $k$, we show that there exists a finite extension $k\subset k'$ such that quadratic points are dense in $X_{k'}$, extending a theorem of Corvaja--Zucconi to $K3$ surfaces of arbitrary degree.
items.authors: Federico Moretti

items.title: Moduli descriptions of v-sheaf local models
items.abstract: We propose a uniform moduli-theoretic description of the v-sheaf local model $\mathbb{M}_{\mathcal G,\mu}$ for an arbitrary parahoric group scheme $\mathcal G$ and an arbitrary dominant cocharacter $\mu$. Our approach is Tannakian and builds on a new theory of parahoric induced modules. When $\mu$ is minuscule, this framework explains the linear-algebraic conditions arising in the theory of local models of Shimura varieties.
items.authors: Jo\~ao Louren\c{c}o, Timo Richarz, Eva Viehmann, Torsten Wedhorn

items.title: Integral trace duality and the Witt filtration on Lubin--Tate space
items.abstract: Let $\mathcal O$ be the Lubin--Tate deformation ring of a one-dimensional commutative formal group of finite height $n\geq1$ over a perfect field $k$ of characteristic $p$. We identify Rezk's Witt filtration $\{I_d\}$ with the divisibility filtration of integral trace pairings on subgroup algebras of fixed source lifts. This gives the geometric recursion \[ I_{d+1}=pI_d+J_{d,z}\qquad(d\geq0), \] where $J_{d,z}$ defines the targets of order-$p^d$ quotient isogenies from a $W(k)$-valued lift $z$ of the closed point. The corrected ideal is independent of $z$. We also compute the cokernel of the universal source trace pairing over $\mathcal O$: it is $\bigoplus_{j=1}^d(\mathcal O/p^j)^{r_j-r_{j-1}}$, where $r_j$ counts order-$p^j$ subgroups of $(\mathbf Q_p/\mathbf Z_p)^n$. The same duality extends the generic trace along two-step isogeny flags to an integral surjection, even when the flag-forgetting map is not flat. This computes composition in the subring of weighted trace operations. Applications include sharp projector denominators and congruence fibre products for full-torsion loci.
items.authors: Andrea Taccani
