items.title: Proof of a nonnegativity conjecture of Prellberg--Stanton
items.abstract: In 1994, Friedman, Joichi and Stanton conjectured that coefficients of the power-series $q+(1-q)\prod_{i=n}^{2n-1}\frac{1}{1-q^{i}}$ are nonnegative for $n\geq3$ and $n$ being odd. Let $\qbinom nm$ denote the Gaussian polynomial. In 2003, Prellberg and Stanton conjectured that coefficients of the power-series $(1-q)\qbinom nm\prod_{i=0}^{m-1}\frac{1}{1-q^{i+m}}$ are nonnegative for $0<m<n$, except when $n$ is even and $m\in\{2,n-2\}$. The latter conjecture implies the former. In this paper, we prove a stronger result concerning coefficientwise nonnegativity of another power series, which implies the conjecture of Prellberg and Stanton. The proof uses a M\"obius correction from Gaussian polynomials, weight-preserving injections on partitions, explicit linearly independent vectors in the kernel of a derivation operator and the KOH identity.
items.authors: Hong-Zhang Ai, Lili Mu, Bao-Xuan Zhu

items.title: Multidimensional Szemer\'edi Theorem for Pairwise Independent Jointly Intersective Polynomials
items.abstract: We develop a new approach to the Joint Intersectivity Conjecture of Bergelson, Leibman, and Lesigne for commuting transformations. The conjecture asserts that the necessary divisibility condition is the only obstruction to polynomial multiple recurrence and, consequently, to the multidimensional polynomial Szemer\'edi theorem. We establish the conjecture for pairwise independent polynomials, obtaining the first general result for sequences of arbitrary length beyond the classical one-transformation setting. Our argument is inspired by the Furstenberg-Katznelson approach and its polynomial enhancement due to Bergelson-Leibman. Its main novelty, however, lies in the development of new techniques that allow us to bypass the use of the polynomial van der Waerden theorem, on which these methods traditionally rely, and for which no suitable analogue is currently available in our setting. In particular, we prove a Nil-Bohr returns theorem for compact extensions in systems with nilpotent structure, as well as a nil-plus-null decomposition for polynomial multicorrelation sequences that preserves joint intersectivity and positivity.
items.authors: Nikos Frantzikinakis, Davide Sclosa

items.title: Proofs of four Takigiku--Tsuchioka conjectures on level $2$ principal characters of $A_{2\ell-1}^{(2)}$
items.abstract: We prove four conjectures of Takigiku and Tsuchioka consisting of eight Rogers--Ramanujan type identities. Two conjectures involve triple sums and a third involves quadruple sums, and their product sides are certain level $2$ principal characters of $A_{13}^{(2)}$. The fourth conjecture gives multisum representations of certain level $2$ principal characters of $A_{2\ell-1}^{(2)}$. The proofs rely on the Bailey pair method, finite sum identities involving Gaussian polynomials, and the quintuple product identity.
items.authors: Liuquan Wang

items.title: T-modules and Pila-Wilkie estimates
items.abstract: The $T-$modules, introduced by G. Anderson in the '80s, are the natural analogue of abelian varieties in Function Field Arithmetic in positive characteristic. For a special class of them we highlight that a totally similar description of the classic Weierstrass function still holds. In particular, torsion points correspond modulo a finite-rank lattice to rational points of the tangent space. We present in this work an upper bound estimate of the number of rational points of the trascendent part of the analytic set corresponding, into the tangent space, to a nontrivial algebraic subvariety of a $T-$module of this special class. Such an estimate, which takes the same shape of that proved by J. Pila and J. Wilkie, represents our first step of our strategy to prove Manin-Mumford conjecture for such special $T-$modules, based on the ideas developped by U. Zannier and J. Pila.
items.authors: Luca Demangos

items.title: Level one automorphic representations of an anisotropic exceptional group over $\mathbb{Q}$ of type $\mathrm{F}_{4}$
items.abstract: Up to isomorphism, there is a unique connected semisimple algebraic group over $\mathbb{Q}$ of Lie type $\mathrm{F}_{4}$, with compact real points and split over $\mathbb{Q}_{p}$ for all primes $p$. Let $\mathbf{F}_{4}$ be such a group. In this paper, we study the level one automorphic representations of $\mathbf{F}_{4}$ in the spirit of the work of Chenevier, Renard, and Ta\"ibi. First, we give an explicit formula for the number of these representations having any given archimedean component. For this, we study the automorphism group of the two definite exceptional Jordan algebras of rank $27$ over $\mathbb{Z}$ studied by Gross, as well as the dimension of the invariants of these groups in all irreducible representations of $\mathbf{F}_{4}(\mathbb{R})$. Then, assuming standard conjectures by Arthur and Langlands for $\mathbf{F}_{4}$, we refine this counting by studying the contribution of the representations whose global Arthur parameter has any possible image (or "Sato-Tate group"). This includes a detailed description of all those images, as well as precise statements for the Arthur's multiplicity formula in each case. As a consequence, we obtain a conjectural but explicit formula for the number of algebraic, cuspidal, level one automorphic representation of $\mathrm{GL}_{26}$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ with Sato-Tate group $\mathbf{F}_{4}(\mathbb{R})$ of any given weight (assumed "$\mathrm{F}_{4}$-regular"). The first example of such representations occurs in motivic weight $36$.
items.authors: Yi Shan

items.title: On a determinant involving linear combinations of Legendre symbols
items.abstract: In this paper, we prove a conjecture of the second author by evaluating the determinant $$\det\left[x + \left(\frac{i-j}p\right) + \left(\frac ip\right)y + \left(\frac jp\right)z + \left(\frac{ij}p\right)w\right]_{0\le i,j\le(p-3)/2}$$ for any odd prime $p$, where $(\frac{\cdot}p)$ denotes the Legendre symbol. In particular, the determinant is equal to $x$ when $p\equiv 3\pmod4$.
items.authors: Keqin Liu, Zhi-Wei Sun, Li-Yuan Wang

items.title: On sparsity of integral points in orbits and correspondences with big iterated pullbacks
items.abstract: We prove new unconditional results of sparsity of integral points on orbits under many maps and correspondences in arbitrary dimensions, generalizing theorems of Yasufuku(2015) and others. The main ingredients are new diophantine approximation tools and recent constructions for correspondences due to Ingram (2011).
items.authors: Jorge Mello

items.title: The global exceptional theta correspondence for the dual pair $\mathbf{F}_{4}\times \mathbf{PGL}_{2}$
items.abstract: Let $\mathbf{F}_{4}$ be the unique (up to isomorphism) connected semisimple algebraic group over $\mathbb{Q}$ of type $\mathrm{F}_{4}$, with compact real points and split over $\mathbb{Q}_{p}$ for all primes $p$. A conjectural computation by the author in arxiv:2407.05859 predicts the existence of a family of level one automorphic representations of $\mathbf{F}_{4}$, which are expected to be functorial lifts of cuspidal representations of $\mathbf{PGL}_{2}$ associated with Hecke eigenforms. In this paper, we study the exceptional theta correspondence for $\mathbf{F}_{4}\times\mathbf{PGL}_{2}$, and establish the existence of such a family of automorphic representations for $\mathbf{F}_{4}$. Moreover, we show that for the automorphic form on $\mathbf{PGL}_{2}$ associated with any even weight $k\geq 12$, level $N$ cuspidal eigenform, its global theta lift to $\mathbf{F}_{4}$ is non-zero. For the other direction, motivated by the work of Pollack, we develop a notion of "exceptional theta series" on $\mathbf{PGL}_{2}$, arising from certain automorphic representations of $\mathbf{F}_{4}$. These theta series are holomorphic modular forms on $\mathbf{SL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})$, with explicit Fourier expansions, and span the entire space of level one cusp forms.
items.authors: Yi Shan

items.title: Root numbers for twisted Fermat quotient curves
items.abstract: Let $\ell$ be an odd prime, $N \geq 1$ be an integer, and $\delta \geq 1$ be a $\ell^N$-th power free integer such that ${\rm ord}_{\ell}(\delta) = 0$ or $\ell \nmid {\rm ord}_{\ell}(\delta)$. In this paper, we give an explicit formula for the root number of the Hecke character associated with a certain quotient curve of the twisted Fermat curve $X^{\ell^N} + Y^{\ell^N} = \delta$. This result gives a generalization of Stoll (2002) and Shu (2021).
items.authors: Ryosuke Yanagihara

items.title: Truncated Hypergeometric Functions and Discretized Integrals
items.abstract: We introduce a kind of finite truncation of the hypergeometric series and provide its discretized integral representation. This is motivated by recent results of Maesaka-Seki-Watanabe and Hirose-Matsusaka-Seki on the identity between truncated series and discretized integrals which comes from the mutliple zeta values and multiple polylogarithms. We also prove the formula of Ohno-Zagier type which relates the truncated multiple polylogarithms and the truncated hypergeometric series.
items.authors: Shuji Yamamoto

items.title: A central limit theorem for partitions involving generalised divisor functions
items.abstract: We let $p_f(n,k)$ count the $f$-restricted coloured partitions of $n$ with $k$ parts, for a positive integer valued function $f$, given by the bivariate generating series \[ Q_f(z,u) := 1+\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} p_f(n,k) u^kz^n =\prod_{k=1}^{\infty}(1+uz^k)^{\Delta_f(k)}, \] where $\Delta_f(n)=|f(n+1)-f(n)|$. A part of size $n$ has $\Delta_f(n)$ distinguishable colours, and each coloured part is available at most once. In this article, we establish a central limit theorem for the number of summands in such partitions when $f(n)=\sigma_r(n)$ denotes the generalised divisor function, defined as $\sigma_r(n)=\sum_{d|n}d^r$ for integer $r\geq 2$. This problem is related to the work of Lipnik, Madritsch, and Tichy on restricted partitions into the indexed values $\lfloor m^{\alpha}\rfloor$, with $0 r+1$. We study this problem employing the identity involving the Ramanujan sum. Furthermore, we analyse the Euler product arising in this analysis by adopting the argument of Alkan, Ledoan and Zaharescu. The absolute values are handled using an eventual parity pattern, and the required continuation is obtained from the corrected character decomposition.
items.authors: Madhuparna Das, Nicolas Robles

items.title: Estimating the number of zeros of Dedekind zeta-functions
items.abstract: In this article, I develop a new approach to estimating the number of non-trivial zeros of a Dedekind zeta function with absolute height at most $T\ge1$, counted with multiplicity. The method yields an explicit zero-counting estimate with constants $(C_1,C_2,C_3)=(0.194,7.806,1.808)$. For the Riemann zeta function, it gives the error bound $0.097\log T+4.807$.
items.authors: Victor Amberger

items.title: Second moments of general Dirichlet series and Selberg zeta functions at $\sigma = 1$
items.abstract: In this paper, we prove the existence of the second moment at $\sigma=1$ for a general Dirichlet series with positive coefficients whose partial sum of the coefficients up to $x$ satisfies $\varrho x+O(x/(\log x)^{1+\varepsilon})$ for some $\varepsilon>0$. The result extends a theorem of Broucke and Hilberdink. As applications, we establish the existence of the second moment for Beurling zeta functions satisfying a prime number theorem with a power-saving error term and for the Selberg zeta function for every cofinite Fuchsian group.
items.authors: Ram\=unas Garunk\v{s}tis, Jok\=ubas Putrius

items.title: Sporadic points on $X_0(N)$
items.abstract: We determine all integers $N$ for which the modular curve $X_0(N)$ admits a sporadic CM point (of any degree), as well as all $N$ for which $X_0(N)$ admits a sporadic point, whether CM or non-CM. In a sense, our results generalize the classification of isogenies of elliptic curves over $\Q$ due to Mazur and Kenku: their work determines the $X_0(N)$ with degree 1 sporadic points, whereas we classify all $X_0(N)$ that have a sporadic point of arbitrary degree.
items.authors: Maarten Derickx, Filip Najman

items.title: Computational Study of Irrational Rotations via Exact Discontinuity Tracking: A New Experimental Framework
items.abstract: We present an algorithm for studying the sum $$ G_N(x,\rho) = \sum_{k=1}^N \left[ \{x+k\rho\} - \frac{1}{2}\right],$$ which is closely related to the discrepancy of the irrational rotation. Computation of $ G_N $ and associated statistics is notoriously difficult due to numerical instability and the failure of sampling to capture the discontinuities. Our algorithm instead fully defines $G_N$ through its discontinuities, which allows computation of $ G_N (x,\rho)$ with errors on the order of $N$ times machine epsilon in $O(N)$ time for practical $N$. The associated probability density function can then be computed in $O(N \log N)$ time. Presented as a tool for experimental mathematics, the algorithm enables reliable plots of the descriptive statistics of $G_N$ over $N$, in particular the length of the support of the $\text{pdf}$ (the discrepancy), revealing extremal behavior related to the arithmetic properties of $\rho$. We also observe a new pattern: when $\rho$ is well approximated by a continued-fraction convergent $\frac{p_n}{q_n}$, the $\text{pdf}$ exhibits a predictable spiked-trapezoidal pattern when $N=kq_n$, eventually degrading at a rate that appears to depend on approximation quality.
items.authors: Hannah Kravitz

items.title: Finite fields whose members are the sum of a potent and a 5-potent
items.abstract: We show that there are only finitely many finite fields whose members are the sum of an $n$-potent element and a $5$-potent element. Combining this with the algorithmic results provided by S.D. Cohen {\it et al.}, we confirm in the affirmative the conjecture posed in \cite{Cohen} concerning all finite fields satisfying this condition. Furthermore, we obtain several elementary results related to the more general problem of decomposing every element of a finite field into the sum of an $m$-potent and an $n$-potent (as formulated in \cite{Cohen}), proving that the number of finite fields satisfying this condition is finite.
items.authors: Juncheng Zhou, Peter V. Danchev, Hongfeng Wu

items.title: Lattice coverings and homogeneous covering congruences
items.abstract: We consider the problem of covering $\mathbb{Z}^2$ with a finite number of sublattices of finite index; this may be viewed as a projective, or homogeneous, version of the well-known problem of covering systems of congruences. We give a construction of minimal coverings which produces many, but not all, minimal coverings, prove an inequality relating the size of a covering to the least common multiple of the lattice indices, and determine all minimal coverings with at most $8$ sublattices.
items.authors: J. E. Cremona, P. Koymans

items.title: Improving bounds for value sets of polynomials over finite fields
items.abstract: Let $\mathbb{F}_{q}$ be a finite field of characteristic $p$, and let $f \in \mathbb{F}_{q}[x]$ be a polynomial of degree $d > 0$. Denote the image set of this polynomial as $V_{f}=\{f(\alpha)\mid\alpha\in\mathbb{F}_{q}\}$ and denote the cardinality of this set as $N_{f}$. A much sharper bound for $N_{f}$ is established in this paper. In particular, for any $p\neq 2, 3$, and for nearly every generic quartic polynomial $f \in \mathbb{F}_{q}[x]$, we obtain $$\lvert N_f - \frac{5}{8} q \rvert \leq \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{q} + \frac{33}{8},$$ which holds as a simple corollary of the main result.
items.authors: Jiyou Li, Zhiyao Zhang

items.title: BSD Invariants and Murmurations of Elliptic Curves
items.abstract: We study how the murmurations of elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ depend on the invariants in the Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer formula, using the Frobenius traces at all primes up to $10^5$ for one curve in each isogeny class of conductor below $10^5$. In these data, at the murmuration scale the rank-$0$ profile depends on the central value $L(E,1)$, in its shape and in the position of its sign changes. Through the series for $L(E,1)$, the covariance of $a_p$ with $L(E,1)$ is exactly a sum of covariances of $a_p$ with the coefficients $a_n$ weighted by a factor that depends on $n$ and the conductor; numerically, in this conductor range, the terms with $n\le50$ reproduce its shape (correlation $0.998$, largest deviation $0.29$ against a largest absolute covariance of $3.03$). Empirically, for $q=3$, $5$, $7$ and $11$ the unweighted covariance of $a_p$ with $a_q$ has nearly the shape of the rank-$0$ profile dilated by a factor near $q$; for $q=2$ the agreement is weaker. Weighting by the Tamagawa product changes the rank-$0$ profile substantially on $0.025<y\le0.125$; after standardisation to the deciles of $\log L(E,1)$, the change summed over these bins is 13% of the unstandardised one (17% for sums of absolute values), and in the lowest bin the standardised change is larger than the unstandardised one and of opposite sign. This version replaces the earlier versions (v1 and v2); their claim that the Tate-Shafarevich group carries information about Frobenius traces beyond the other invariants taken together cannot hold, because its analytic order is defined by the BSD formula, and it is withdrawn.
items.authors: Dane Wachs

items.title: Murmurations, Periods, and Local Factors
items.abstract: This note replaces arXiv:2603.22807v1 and withdraws its three theorems, which do not stand as stated. Theorem A, that the order of the Tate-Shafarevich group of $y^2=x^3+x+D(t)$ over $\mathbb{F}_q(t)$ is determined by the cyclotomic type of the $L$-polynomial, holds at rank $0$ when $D$ has degree $5$ but fails at positive rank; we give a counterexample and cite the correct statement. Theorem B is Tur\'an's inequality for modified Bessel functions; we prove a version for general even weights and a class of increasing tilts that includes the Euler factor, which gives the Euler-factor tilt at every prime. Theorem C, a limit law for the covariance of $a_p$ with the real period at fixed $L(f,1)$, was not proved, and we explain why. We also recompute the empirical section of the first version from Cremona's tables, correct its numbers, withdraw those we could not reconstruct, and show that its sign flip at $p=3$ and its "100% Tamagawa channel" are artefacts of decile conditioning and of the rank-$0$ BSD formula.
items.authors: Dane Wachs

items.title: There are infinitely many Hilbert cubes of dimension 3 in the set of squares
items.abstract: For an integer tuple $(a_0,a_1,\ldots,a_d)$ with $a_i\neq0$ for $i=1,\ldots,d$, we define the associated Hilbert cube by \[ H(a_0;a_1,\ldots,a_d) = \left\{ a_0+\sum_{i=1}^d \varepsilon_i a_i: \varepsilon_i\in\{0,1\} \right\}. \] We call $(a_0,a_1,\ldots,a_d)$ a $d$-dimensional Hilbert-cube presentation. We prove that there are $\gg N^{1/4}$ reduced Hilbert-cube presentations $(a_0,a_1,a_2,a_3)$ with $a_0,a_1,a_2,a_3\in[0,N]$ such that \[ H(a_0;a_1,a_2,a_3)\subset \mathcal{S}, \] where $\mathcal{S}=\{m^2:\;m\in\Z\}$. Moreover, we prove that for each $i, j\in\{0, 1, 2, 3\}$ with $i 0\;\text{for}\;i=0, 1, 2, 3\;\right\} $$ is dense in the set of positive real numbers (in the Euclidean topology).
items.authors: Andrew Bremner, Christian Elsholtz, Maciej Ulas

items.title: On the Number of Prime Factors of Consecutive Integers
items.abstract: We prove that there are infinitely many $n$ such that $\omega(n+k) \ll \log k$ for all integers $k \ge 2$. This improves on a result of Tao and Ter\"{a}v\"{a}inen (2025), who have $O(k)$ in place of $O(\log k)$. As corollaries, we make progress on a number of questions posed by Erd\H{o}s. The proof is based on a quantitative refinement of the Tao-Ter\"{a}v\"{a}inen probabilistic argument, combining a refined sieve construction with upper bounds for high moments and the resulting tail estimates. Moreover, we formulate a conjecture on integers with many prime factors based on Cram\'{e}r-type random models. Assuming this conjecture, the main bound is essentially sharp.
items.authors: Cheuk Fung Lau

items.title: The sum-product phenomenon for dense subsets of finite fields
items.abstract: Let $\mathbb{F}_p$ be a finite field of prime order $p$ and let $A \subset \mathbb{F}_p$ be a subset. In the dense regime when $|A| \geq \alpha p$ for some $\alpha \in (0,1)$, we determine the optimal constant $f(\alpha)$ in the inequality $$ \max(|A+A|, |A\cdot A|) \geq (f(\alpha) - o(1))p. $$ The proof relies on a structural result for sumsets of dense subsets, established via a regularity lemma in general finite abelian groups.
items.authors: Xuancheng Shao

items.title: Reductions of $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb Q_{p^f})$-Banach spaces of slopes in $(0,1)$
items.abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime and $f \geq 1$. We consider a $p$-adic locally algebraic $\text{GL}_2(\mathbb Q_{p^f})$-representation attached to a tuple of $f$ weights $k=(k_i)$ for $0 \leq i \leq f-1$ and a $p$-adic integer $a_p$ with valuation in $(0,1)$. We give conditions under which the irreducible quotients of the subquotients in a filtration on the reduction mod $p$ of the natural integral structure on this space are supercuspidal. We also check that for small $k$ and $f$ the integral structure is a lattice so that the mod $p$ reduction is nonzero.
items.authors: Eknath Ghate, Shivansh Pandey

items.title: Hecke Eigenvalues of Ikeda Lifts
items.abstract: In this paper, we study the Hecke eigenvalues of Ikeda lifts. Using the spherical map for the Hecke algebra of the symplectic group, we obtain an explicit formula for the eigenvalues $\lambda_F(p^r)$. From this formula, we show that $\lambda_F(p^r)$ can be written as a polynomial in $p^{\pm 1/2}$ with a positive leading term. Furthermore, we prove that the coefficients of this polynomial are bounded and, as a consequence, the Hecke eigenvalues $\lambda_F(p^r)$ are positive for all sufficiently large primes $p$.
items.authors: Nagarjuna Chary Addanki, Ameya Pitale

items.title: On modular forms of rational weight satisfying the canonical second-order linear modular differential equation
items.abstract: In this paper, we completely classify the rational weights $k$ for which the Kaneko-Zagier (KZ) differential equation admits a fundamental system of solutions consisting of modular forms for a principal congruence subgroup $\Gamma(N)$. By transforming the KZ equation into a hypergeometric differential equation, we study the global analytic continuation of its solutions, adopting an approach analogous to Stiller's work on Picard-Fuchs equations. We explicitly construct the monodromy representation matrices corresponding to the elements of the principal congruence subgroups and completely determine the algebraic conditions under which these connection matrices commute. Leveraging these stringent commutativity constraints, we prove that the weights $k$ yielding modular solutions are strictly limited to $k \equiv 1/2, 7/2, 1, 2, 3 \pmod{6}$ and $k = (6n+1)/5$, thereby demonstrating that no modular solutions exist beyond those previously discovered by Kaneko and Koike. Furthermore, the commutative algebras generated by these connection matrices reveal a profound analogy with commuting transfer matrices in quantum integrable systems.
items.authors: Yuichi Sakai, Hiroyuki Tsutsumi

items.title: Counting the number of $1_{m}$-preperiodic $\mathcal{O}_{K}$-points of a discrete dynamical system with applications from arithmetic statistics, VII
items.abstract: In this follow-up article of a multi-part series on (strictly) preperiodic point-counting, we inspect an astonishing relationship between the set of (strictly) $1_{m}$-preperiodic points of a polynomial map $\varphi_{d, c}$ defined by $\varphi_{d, c}(z) = z^d + c$ for all $c, z \in \mathcal{O}_{K}$ and the coefficient $c$, where $K$ is any number field of degree $n\geq 1$, $d>2$ is an integer and $m\in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$ is any fixed (eventual period). As before, we study counting problems that are inspired by torsion point-counting in arithmetic statistics and (strictly) preperiodic point-counting in arithmetic dynamics. In doing so, we then first prove that for any prime $p\geq 3$ and for any fixed $\ell \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$ and fixed (eventual period) $m\in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$, the average number of distinct $1_{m}$-preperiodic integral points of any $\varphi_{p^{\ell}, c}$ modulo prime $p\mathcal{O}_{K}$ is unbounded or zero as $c\to \infty$. Inspired further by work of Doyle-Poonen along with conjectural work of Hutz and $\textit{abc}(\textit{d})$-conditional work of Panraksa on $K$-rational preperiodic points of any $\varphi_{(p-1)^{\ell}, c}$ for any prime $p\geq 5$ in arithmetic dynamics, we then also prove that for any fixed (eventual period) $m \in \mathbb{Z}_{ \geq 1}$, the average number of distinct $1_{m}$-preperiodic integral points of any $\varphi_{(p-1)^{\ell}, c}$ modulo prime $p\mathcal{O}_{K}$ is unbounded or zero as $c\to \infty$. Finally, we then apply counting and distribution results from arithmetic statistics, and then get counting and statistical results on arithmetic objects arising naturally in our polynomial discrete dynamical settings. Together with the previous articles in the series, it might then be fair to view this article as an attempt to contribute to "arithmetic statistical dynamics".
items.authors: Brian Kintu

items.title: On concatenations of two $k$-generalized Pell numbers
items.abstract: We study the concatenation of two $k$-generalized Pell numbers. More precisely, we determine all solutions of the equation $P_n^{(k)} = P_m^{(k)} \cdot 10^{d} + P_p^{(k)}$, where $d$ is the number of decimal digits of $P_p^{(k)}$. We prove that for $k \ge 3$ there are no solutions, while for $k = 2$ the only solution is $P_4 = 12 = 1\|2$.
items.authors: Cherif B. Deme, Kancou D. Fall, Khady Faye, Bernadette Faye

items.title: Harder's conjecture and Hermitian automorphic forms
items.abstract: Let $k\ge4$ and $j\ge2$ be integers with $j$ even. Harder's conjecture predicts a congruence between a primitive elliptic cusp form of weight $2k+j-2$ and a degree-two vector-valued Siegel Hecke cusp eigenform of weight ${\det}^{k}\mathrm{Sym}^{j}$. We prove the corresponding Harder-type congruence for the spinor $L$-polynomials under explicit arithmetic hypotheses on a congruence prime and an auxiliary imaginary quadratic field. Our approach uses Hermitian automorphic forms on the quasi-split unitary group $\mathrm{U}_{2,2}$. We construct Hermitian spin lifts of Siegel cusp forms and show that the Hermitian cusp form produced by a Hermitian Klingen-Eisenstein congruence lies in the image of this lift. The key step is to prove that the Galois representation attached to this Hermitian cusp form is conjugate invariant. For this, we combine the endoscopic classification for quasi-split unitary groups with Selmer-group vanishing results. This allows us to identify the Hermitian cusp form as the spin lift of a Siegel cusp eigenform and thereby obtain the Harder-type congruence. The argument applies uniformly to both even and odd $k$.
items.authors: Hidenori Katsurada, Nobuki Takeda

items.title: An incremental approximation to the prime-counting function via polygonal numbers
items.abstract: We construct an incremental prime-counting approximation from corrected right-endpoint sums on polygonal-number partitions. For each fixed polygonal family, retaining completed contributions gives $\mathcal O(1)$ numerical operations per consecutive node and $\mathcal O(\sqrt X)$ operations for the full traversal through $X$, in the unit-cost model. The scheme uses a fixed number of working numerical words rather than repeated summation. Asymptotic formulas for the discretization error and terminal scale yield an unconditional relation with the classical normalized prime-counting error. We prove that the logarithmic mean of the normalized estimator error converges to $1/\sqrt2$ if and only if the Riemann hypothesis holds, and give an independent Mellin proof of the converse. Under the hypothesis, this constant uniquely removes the limiting signed mean bias. Computations at powers of ten through $10^{19}$ with coefficient $0.7071$ show accuracy comparable to the Riemann approximation at the sampled arguments
items.authors: Artur Samojluk, Artur Siemaszko

items.title: Sign Patterns in a Two Colored Partition Companion series
items.abstract: We study three closely related questions arising from the recent work of Andrews and El Bachraoui on the two-color partition series \[ S_1(q)=\sum_{n\ge0}s_1(n)q^n=\sum_{a\ge0}q^a(-q^{a+1};q)_\infty^2 \] and its odd companion, denoted by $T_o(q)$. First, for the eta-normalized companion \[ C(q)=(q;q)_\infty T_o(q)=\sum_{n\ge0}c(n)q^n, \] we prove a strong form of the Andrews--El Bachraoui sign conjecture that $\limsup c(n)=+\infty$ and $\liminf c(n)=-\infty$. Second, we construct an involution using the Franklin-type involution of Chen and Liu to combinatorially explain Andrews--El Bachraoui congruence for $s_1(n)$ modulo 4. Third, we introduce a two-variable refinement of $S_1(q)$ which records the difference of the lengths of the two colored components. Using Ramanujan's partial theta identity and heat-type equations, we obtain a closed formula for all of its even moments, and we show that the eta-normalized moments satisfy termwise congruences modulo $p^{2k}$ for every prime $p\equiv5\pmod6$.
items.authors: Aritram Dhar, Ankush Goswami, Mohit Tripathi

items.title: The First Moment of Dirichlet L-functions over Generators of the Character Group
items.abstract: We evaluate the average of the central values $L(1/2,\chi)$ over the generators of the group of Dirichlet characters modulo $q$, as $q\to\infty$ through the primes.
items.authors: Rizwanur Khan

items.title: Orthogonality Defects of HKZ-Reduced Bases
items.abstract: Let $D_n$ denote the supremum of the orthogonality defects over all $n$-dimensional Hermite--Korkine--Zolotarev (HKZ)-reduced bases. This paper shows that, as $n\to\infty$, \[ \log D_n=2n\log n-n\log\log n+O(n). \] We also determine the exact value $D_4=4375/1024$.
items.authors: Zhixing Li

items.title: Fourier Coefficients of the Degenerate Eisenstein Series on Symplectic Groups
items.abstract: We study degenerate Eisenstein series on symplectic groups and construct a new automorphic descent. We show that a certain Fourier coefficient, after restriction to a smaller symplectic group, is itself an Eisenstein series with the same inducing parameter \(s\). We describe the resulting holomorphic section explicitly in terms of the original section and local \(L\)-factors at unramified places. At every regular point of the local descent, we prove surjectivity at non-Archimedean places and dense image at Archimedean places. We finally indicate an application of the iterated descent to maximal Fourier coefficients of Eisenstein series.
items.authors: Alan Xuelun Hou, Yusheng Lei

items.title: On lifting representations and actions on curves of the metacyclic groups $C_{p^s}\rtimes C_m$
items.abstract: For a prime $p$, a pair $(s,m)\in\mathbb{N}^2$ with $m$ relatively prime to $p$, a homomorphism $\chi:C_m\rightarrow\operatorname{Aut}(C_{p^s})$, and an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p$, we consider the semidirect product $G=C_{p^s}\rtimes_{\chi} C_m$, the $p$-Sylow subgroup $H\cong C_{p^s}$ of $G$, and a $k[G]$-module $V$. Let $R$ be a complete discrete valuation ring of residue field $k$ and mixed characteristic $(0,p)$ that contains a primitive $p^s$-th root of unity. If $\chi$ is injective, we present two necessary and sufficient criteria for lifting $V$ to an $R[G]$-module $\widetilde{V}$ which is a free $R$-module: (i) when no extra requirement is made on $\widetilde{V}$ and (ii) when we require $\widetilde{V}^H=\{0\}$. The criteria correct several results in the literature and we use them to prove that, if $\chi$ is injective and $G$ acts faithfully on a connected smooth projective curve $X$ over $k$, then, under mild hypotheses satisfied if $X\rightarrow X/G$ is a Harbater--Katz--Gabber cover, the $k[G]$-module $H^0(X,\Omega_X)$ has a lift $\widetilde{V}$ to $R$ with $\widetilde{V}^H=\{0\}$. Also, with $B:=R[\frac{1}{p}]$, we prove the following obstruction when $p$ is odd, $m$ is even, $\chi$ is injective, and $X/C_{p^s}\cong\mathbb{P}^1_k$: if no such lift $\widetilde{V}$ exists with the $B[H]$-module $\widetilde{V}\otimes_R B$ defined over $\mathbb{Q}$, then the action of $G$ on $X$ does not lift to $R$.
items.authors: Huy Dang, Adrian Vasiu

items.title: Cyclotomy of symmetric polynomials
items.abstract: We prove some new identities for homogeneous symmetric polynomials when evaluated at roots of unity. Some of these formulas are applied to obtain new insights onto cyclotomic polynomials.
items.authors: Laura De Carli, Maurizio Laporta

items.title: On the Number of Hecke Eigenvalues of the Same Sign on $\mathrm{GL}_n$
items.abstract: We study the distribution of signs of the (real-valued) Hecke eigenvalues $A(m,1,...,1)$ of self-dual Hecke--Maass cusp forms for the group $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb Z)$, where $n\geq 2$ is an integer. Our main result establishes, under the Generalised Ramanujan--Petersson Conjecture, that for all $X\leq x\leq 2X$ outside a set of measure $o(X)$ the short interval $(x,x+H]$ contains at least $H(\log X)^{1/n^2-1}$ indices with both positive and negative Hecke eigenvalues, provided that $(\log X)^{1-1/n^2+\varepsilon}\leq H\leq X/10$. For $\mathrm{GL}_2$ Hecke--Maass cusp forms we obtain a stronger bound unconditionally, and for self-dual $\mathrm{GL}_3$ forms we obtain the same logarithmic exponent unconditionally. We also establish results under weaker bounds towards the Generalised Ramanujan--Petersson Conjecture together with the Generalised Lindel\"of Hypothesis, and obtain lower bounds for the number of sign changes and for the number of Hecke eigenvalues of each sign in long intervals.
items.authors: Jesse J\"a\"asaari

items.title: On integers whose friable component is large
items.abstract: We estimate the number of integers up to $x$ whose $y$-friable component exceeds $z$. Uniformly for $\max\{2,\log z\}\leqslant y\leqslant z\leqslant x/2$, we determine the logarithm of this counting function up to an error $O(\log z/\log y)$. This sharpens an estimate arising from a problem in Ford's sieve methods lecture notes. The proof combines classical friable-number estimates with an elementary argument for the lower bound.
items.authors: G\'erald Tenenbaum, Xiangyu Wang

items.title: A Short Proof of a Theorem of Pan and Zhang
items.abstract: Pan and Zhang proved that a positive proportion of positive integers can be represented in the form $a^2+b^2+2^{c^2}$, where $(a,b,c)$ are nonnegative integers. In this note, we give a short proof of their result. The proof uses Romanoff's method and an elementary divisor argument to control the relevant second moment.
items.authors: Xiangyu Wang

items.title: A proof of Hirose's duality conjecture
items.abstract: Hirose formulated a duality conjecture for a $q$-discretization of iterated integrals on the four-punctured projective line, incorporating word-dependent $q$-shifts of the parameters. In this paper, we prove this conjecture using a symmetric terminating ${}_{4}\phi_{3}$ connector.
items.authors: Shin-ichiro Seki

items.title: New bounds for the integer Chebyshev constant of [0,1]
items.abstract: The integer Chebyshev constant of [0,1] has been bracketed by 0.4213 <= t_Z([0,1]) <= 0.422685 since the work of Pritsker (2005) and of Flammang (2014). We prove 0.4222286000 <= t_Z([0,1]) <= 0.4226846976, narrowing the interval from 1.39e-3 to 4.56e-4. Both bounds are established by explicit certificates. The upper bound is carried by an integer polynomial with 92 factors and explicit integer exponents; the lower bound by a discrete measure on 947 cells together with a library of 206 irreducible polynomials, through an inequality in which the terms paying for divisibility are made explicit. Two self-contained scripts, included as ancillary files, re-derive both bounds from the certificates alone.
items.authors: David Niedbala Giraudin

items.title: Indefinite theta vectors and generalized Nahm sums of arbitrary rank
items.abstract: We construct indefinite theta representations for a family of signed generalized Nahm sums of arbitrary rank \(r\geq2\). After explicit normalization and boundary correction, one signed branch gives the even components of a \((2r-1)\)-component holomorphic theta vector associated with a lattice of signature \((1,1)\). Euler-type multiple sums provide the odd components, yielding formulas uniform in both the rank and the component index. Using Zwegers' theory, we determine the weight-one modular transformation laws of the real-analytic completion, with an explicit finite sine matrix for the \(S\)-transformation. We decompose the nonholomorphic correction into a finite sum of products of unary theta functions and one-dimensional error-function series, and compute the antiholomorphic derivative of the completion. Together with the completed transformation laws, these formulas give the inhomogeneous transformation law of the holomorphic vector. We also evaluate a linear combination of two signed branches as a difference of Jacobi product quotients. This identity and further evaluations for two families of symmetrizable matrices and their duals, combined with known results, give multiple-sum representations for every component of four associated product vectors. These representations are finite combinations of generalized Nahm sums with the prescribed matrices and symmetrizers; in the dual families, half-period translates are absorbed into signs and constant phase factors.
items.authors: Dandan Chen, Siyu Yin

items.title: Cohomology of Linearly Constrained Kloosterman Families: Newton Polytopes, Weights, and Boundary Monodromy
items.abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime, $\psi$ a nontrivial additive character of $\mathbb F_p$, $\psi_q=\psi\circ\mathrm{Tr}_{\mathbb F_q/\mathbb F_p}$ and $\lambda\in\mathbb F_p^\times$. For $h\in(\mathbb F_q^\times)^n$ let $\Sigma_n(h)$ be the sum of $\psi_q(u_1^{-1}+\cdots+u_n^{-1})$ over $u\in(\mathbb F_q^\times)^n$ with $h_1u_1+\cdots+h_nu_n=-\lambda$, an additively twisted average of products of Kloosterman sums. For every $n\ge2$, the cohomology computing $\Sigma_n(h)$ is concentrated in one degree and has dimension $2^n-1$. It has $r(n)=2^n-\binom n{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$ eigenvalues of weight $n-1$, and its other eigenvalues are the integers $q^{k-1}$, $1\le k\le\lfloor n/2\rfloor$, with ballot numbers as multiplicities. The part of top weight forms a lisse sheaf $\mathcal W_n$ of rank $r(n)$ on the torus $\mathbb G_m^n$. We determine its local monodromy at the coordinate boundary and its determinant: $\det\mathcal W_n$ is the Artin--Schreier sheaf of the sum $-2^{n-1}\lambda^{-1}(h_1+\cdots+h_n)$ of the critical values of the phase, twisted by $p^{(n+1)r(n)/2}$. The geometric monodromy group of $\mathcal W_n$, and the arithmetic one after normalization to weight $0$, are equal to $\{g\in\mathrm{GL}_{r(n)}:\det(g)^p=1\}$. Consequently the normalized sums become equidistributed like traces of Haar-random elements of $\{g\in\mathrm U(r(n)):\det(g)^p=1\}$. The proofs use Laumon's Fourier transform, middle convolution, the Cayley cubic surface and Larsen's alternative, but no classification of finite groups.
items.authors: Hamed Ebadi

items.title: Prescribed Ideal Classes in Ennola Cubic Fields and Rational Points on Associated Elliptic Curves
items.abstract: For every prime $\ell\geq5$ and integer $n\geq2$, we construct an Ennola cubic field with a specified prime ideal above $\ell$ whose class has exact order $2^n$. For parameters satisfying two square conditions and explicit congruences, the same squareclass obstructions give four independent rational points on the associated elliptic curves. A Pell equation describes all such parameters. A genus-one base change gives five independent sections that generate a subgroup saturated at two. It also yields infinitely many elliptic curves over $\mathbb Q$, pairwise nonisomorphic over $\overline{\mathbb Q}$, with rank at least five.
items.authors: Junyu Lu

items.title: An Algebraic Proof of the Non-Modularity of Solutions to the Canonical Modular Differential Equation
items.abstract: In this paper, we provide an algebraic proof of the condition for the existence of modular form solutions to the Kaneko-Zagier differential equation of weight $k$. Unlike previous representation-theoretic approaches relying on $SL_2(\mathbb{Z})$, our method employs the connection matrices of the principal congruence subgroup $\Gamma(N)$. By deriving a condition for simultaneous triangularizability from the commutators of the representation matrices and applying Galois theory, we prove that the associated two-dimensional representation of $\Gamma(N)$ is irreducible when the denominator $m$ of the fraction $(k+1)/6 = n/m$ satisfies $m=1$ or $m \ge 7$. Consequently, we identify the weights that admit no modular form solutions and obtain a complete classification of the dimensions of the spaces of such solutions.
items.authors: Yuichi Sakai, Hiroyuki Tsutsumi

items.title: A Bogomolov property for moduli spaces of polynomials over abelian extensions
items.abstract: Let $d\geq2$ be an integer, and let $\operatorname{MPoly}^d$ be the moduli space of degree-$d$ polynomials. For every number field $K$, we prove that there exists $\epsilon_{K,d}>0$ such that \[ \left\lbrace\alpha\in\operatorname{MPoly}^d(K^{\mathrm{ab}})\colon h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\alpha)<\epsilon_{K,d}\right\rbrace=\left\lbrace\alpha\in\operatorname{MPoly}^d(K^{\mathrm{ab}})\colon h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\alpha)=0\right\rbrace \] is finite, where $h_{\mathrm{crit}}$ is the critical height. In particular, only finitely many $K^{\mathrm{ab}}$-rational points of $\operatorname{MPoly}^d$ are postcritically finite. The proof combines the correspondence method of Ji--Song--Xie with local ramification estimates and the uniform finiteness of intertwined classes in $\operatorname{MPoly}^d$. We also prove an analogous finiteness theorem for non-preperiodic marked points in non-isotrivial one-parameter polynomial families.
items.authors: Geng-Rui Zhang

items.title: The optimal van der Corput property for squares
items.abstract: We prove a sharp quantitative form of the van der Corput property for squares. For all sufficiently large $N$, we construct a real trigonometric polynomial $P(\theta)=a_0+\sum_{1\le n\le\sqrt N}a_n\cos(2\pi n^2\theta)$ satisfying \begin{equation}\tag{1}\label{eq:abstract-vdc} P(\theta)\ge0\quad(\theta\in\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}),\qquad P(0)=1, \end{equation} with \[0\le a_0\le\exp(-c\sqrt{\log N\log\log N}),\] where $c>0$ is an absolute constant. As a consequence, if $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}\cap[1,N]$ has no nonzero square difference, then \[|A|\le N\exp(-c\sqrt{\log N\log\log N}),\] improving upon a recent result of Green and Sawhney. Our construction builds on previous work of Slijep\v{c}evi\'c, Slijep\v{c}evi\'c--Nin\v{c}evi\'c, and Fan--Lott, and the proof of the upper bound is elementary and self-contained. We also show that every real trigonometric polynomial of the above form satisfying \eqref{eq:abstract-vdc} has \[a_0\ge\exp(-C\sqrt{\log N\log\log N})\] for an absolute constant $C>0$. Thus the van der Corput property cannot be used to obtain a power-saving bound for the Furstenberg--S\'ark\"ozy theorem.
items.authors: Steve Fan, Andrew Lott

items.title: Logarithmic moments of the Rogers-Ramanujan continued fraction and odd zeta values
items.abstract: We study how the two cusp expansions of the Rogers-Ramanujan continued fraction control its ordinary and logarithmic Mellin moments. Ramanujan's factorizations express the logarithmic transform as a combination of products of zeta and quadratic Dirichlet $L$-functions. Its adjacent integer and half-integer values give an invertible change of coordinates for the corresponding odd special values. We prove that every reciprocal-cusp coefficient is a quadratic irrational algebraic integer, with an explicit minimal polynomial, and that every logarithmic coefficient is quadratic irrational. These facts determine the exact poles of three normalized-moment generating functions. The logarithmic one has an absolutely convergent partial fraction expansion with a pole at every positive square. For the ordinary moments, a two-cusp incomplete-gamma expansion gives meromorphic continuation at every positive splitting point. A general Mellin lemma yields the corresponding nonholonomicity statements. We also establish reflection identities, vertical strip decay and an explicit truncation estimate.
items.authors: K. Srinivasa Raghava

items.title: Long intervals of consecutive composite values of polynomials
items.abstract: Let $f\in\mathbb Q[t]$ be an irreducible polynomial of positive degree with positive leading coefficient, taking integer values at every integer. We prove that there is a constant $c_f>0$ such that, for every sufficiently large real $X$, the interval $(X/2,X]$ contains at least $c_f\log X\log\log X$ consecutive integers $n$ for which all values $f(n)$ are composite. The exponent of $\log\log X$ is independent of the degree of $f$. This improves the previous result of Ford and Gabdullin by replacing their small fixed power of $\log\log X$ with the full factor $\log\log X$. In particular, the result applies to $f(t)=t^2+1$.
items.authors: Artyom Radomskii

items.title: A combinatorial proof of the quadratic Gauss sum
items.abstract: We provide an elementary approach to computing the quadratic Gauss sum, emphasizing the method employed to compute the sum corresponding to multiples of 4. The proof method employed does not rely on the law of quadratic reciprocity, but only on exploiting symmetries among the sum's components, together with a recursive approach.
items.authors: Adan Medrano Martin del Campo

items.title: Improved zero-free half-planes for the quasi-Riemann hypothesis
items.abstract: Recently, a uniform $\frac{7}{8}$ zero-free half-plane for finite-order Hecke $L$-functions over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$ and its transfer to Dirichlet $L$-functions was given by OpenAI in [Ope26a]. In its proof, there are several parameters $b=\frac{1}{8}, \ell=\frac{1}{6}$, and $\kappa$. In this paper, via varying $b$, $\ell$, and $\kappa$, following the same strategy, we slightly improve the bound $\frac{7}{8}=0.875$ to \[ B_{\mathrm{new}}=\frac{18\xi_{\mathrm{new}}+7}{18\xi_{\mathrm{new}}+9} =0.874957019420098946\ldots, \] where $\xi_{\mathrm{new}}$ is the unique root in $(0.38858,0.38859)$ of $1188\xi^3-2160\xi^2+171\xi+190=0$. Explicitly, with $\arccos\in[0,\pi]$, \[ \xi_{\mathrm{new}}=\frac{20}{33}+\frac{\sqrt{1391}}{33} \cos\!\left(\frac13\arccos\frac{28470}{1391^{3/2}} -\frac{2\pi}{3}\right). \] The limiting parameters are \[ \begin{gathered} b_{\mathrm{new}}=\frac{8(3\xi_{\mathrm{new}}-1)(12\xi_{\mathrm{new}}^2-40\xi_{\mathrm{new}}+15)} {9(2\xi_{\mathrm{new}}+1)(24\xi_{\mathrm{new}}^2-20\xi_{\mathrm{new}}+5)}, \ell_{\mathrm{new}}=\frac{5-6\xi_{\mathrm{new}}}{9+18\xi_{\mathrm{new}}},\qquad \kappa_{\mathrm{new}}=\frac{18\xi_{\mathrm{new}}+5}{18\xi_{\mathrm{new}}+9} =2B_{\mathrm{new}}-1. \end{gathered} \] We also prove its optimality within the explicitly specified exponent comparison system. This result has been formalized by Lean [Liu26].
items.authors: Baiying Liu

items.title: On the Quantitative Bounds of Nonlinear Roth Theorem
items.abstract: We prove that any subset $A \subseteq \{1, \dots, N\}$ lacking non-trivial polynomial progressions $(x, x + y, x + y^2)$ satisfies $\lvert A \rvert \le CN \exp\bigl(-c(\log \log N)^\beta\bigr)$ for effective absolute constants $C, c, \beta > 0$. The argument develops a density increment framework localized to anisotropic quadratic Bohr sets. To handle mixed linear and quadratic frequencies, we establish a multilinear transference principle coupled with a relative quadratic inverse theorem based on Balog--Szemer{\'e}di--Gowers additive energy rigidity. Boundary stability across increments is maintained via semi-algebraic model regularization using cylindrical algebraic decomposition and Cauchy--Crofton estimates, while dimension growth is controlled by dissociated basis reduction and multidimensional Erd{\H{o}}s--Tur{\'a}n--Koksma equidistribution.
items.authors: Yunfan Zhao

items.title: Multiple Lattice Packings and Coverings of the Plane with Triangles
items.abstract: Given a convex disk $K$ and a positive integer $j$, let $\delta_L^j(K)$ and $\vartheta_L^j(K)$ denote the $j$-fold lattice packing density and the $j$-fold lattice covering density of $K$, respectively. I will prove that for every triangle $T$ we have that $\delta_L^j(T)=\frac{2j^2}{2j+1}$ and $\vartheta_L^j(T)=\frac{2j+1}{2}$. Furthermore, I also obtain that the numbers of lattices which attain these densities both are $(2j+1)\prod_{p|2j+1}(1-\frac{2}{p})$, where the product is over the distinct prime numbers dividing $2j+1$.
items.authors: Kirati Sriamorn

items.title: Shifted symplectic structures on derived analytic moduli of $\ell$-adic local systems and Galois representations
items.abstract: We develop a characterisation of non-Archimedean derived analytic geometry based on dg enhancements of dagger algebras. This allows us to formulate derived analytic moduli functors for many types of pro-\'etale sheaves, and to construct shifted symplectic structures on them by transgression using arithmetic duality theorems. In order to handle duality functors involving Tate twists, we introduce weighted shifted symplectic structures on formal weighted moduli stacks, with the usual moduli stacks given by taking $\mathbb{G}_m$-invariants. In particular, this establishes the existence of shifted symplectic and Lagrangian structures on derived moduli stacks of $\ell$-adic constructible complexes on smooth varieties via Poincar\'e duality, and on derived moduli stacks of $\ell$-adic Galois representations via Tate and Poitou--Tate duality; the latter proves a conjecture of Minhyong Kim. Unweighted shifted symplectic and Lagrangian structures are also established for $\ell$-adic Galois representations of cyclotomic fields $K(\mu_{\ell^{\infty}})$, subject to additional constraints related to Iwasawa theory; these derived moduli stacks yield a non-abelian analogue of Selmer complexes, with $0$-shifted symplectic structures related to generalised Cassels--Tate pairings.
items.authors: J. P. Pridham

items.title: The Hurwitz tree obstruction for the refined local lifting problem
items.abstract: We prove that the differential Hurwitz tree obstruction for the cyclic $p$-power refined local lifting problem always vanishes. Given a cyclic extension of degree $p^n$ in characteristic $p$ and a lift of its degree-$p^{n-1}$ subextension, we construct a compatible differential Hurwitz tree extending the tree of that lift. Realizing the resulting tree by a cover remains a separate problem.
items.authors: Huy Dang

items.title: Monochromatic non-commuting products
items.abstract: We show that a finite coloring of an amenable group contains `many' monochromatic sets of the form $\{x,y,xy,yx\},$ and natural extensions with more variables. This gives the first combinatorial proof and extensions of Bergelson and McCutcheon's non-commutative Schur theorem. Our main new tool is the introduction of what we call `quasirandom colorings,' a condition that is automatically satisfied by colorings of quasirandom groups, and a reduction to this case.
items.authors: Matt Bowen

items.title: Asymptotics of rational representations for algebraic groups
items.abstract: We study the asymptotic behaviour of the cohomology of subgroups $\Gamma$ of an algebraic group $G$ with coefficients in the various irreducible rational representations of $G$ and raise a conjecture about it. Namely, we expect that the dimensions of these cohomology groups approximate the L2-analogues of Betti numbers of $\Gamma$ with a controlled error term. We provide positive answers when $G$ is a product of copies of $SL_2$.
items.authors: Lander Guerrero S\'anchez, Henrique Souza

items.title: An algebraic proof of Hrushovski's theorem
items.abstract: In his paper on the Mordell-Lang conjecture, Hrushovski employed techniques from model theory to prove the function field version of the conjecture. In doing so he was able to answer a related question of Voloch, which we refer to henceforth as Hrushovski's theorem. In this paper we shall give an alternative proof of said theorem in the characteristic $p$ setting, but using purely algebro-geometric ideas.
items.authors: Thomas Wisson

items.title: The Green--Griffiths--Lang--Vojta conjecture for commutative algebraic groups with unipotent rank 1
items.abstract: Let $k$ be algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, let $G$ be a commutative algebraic group over $k$ such that the linear part of $G$ is isomorphic to $\mathbb{G}_a$, and let $X$ be a closed subvariety of $G$. We show that the Kawamata locus of $X$ is equal to a Lang-like exceptional locus of $X$, and furthermore, we identify a condition on $X$ that implies that these loci are proper subschemes of $X$. Using this, we prove the strong form of the Green--Griffiths--Lang--Vojta conjecture for closed subvarieties of $\mathbb{G}_a \times A$ where $A$ is an abelian variety.
items.authors: Jackson S. Morrow, Paul Vojta

items.title: The Shafarevich conjecture for varieties with globally generated cotangent
items.abstract: We prove the Shafarevich conjecture for varieties with globally generated cotangent bundle, subject to mild numerical conditions.
items.authors: Thomas Kr\"amer, Marco Maculan

items.title: Maps between circle bundles: Fiber-preserving, Finiteness and Realization of mapping degree sets
items.abstract: Let $E_i$ be an oriented circle bundle over a closed oriented $n$-manifold $M_i$ with $i=1,2$ and assume that $M_2$ is aspherical. We prove the following geometric realization result, which extends the classical result for maps between circle bundles over surfaces to all dimensions $\geq 2$. Let $f\colon E_1\to E_2$ be a map. If the induced homomorphism $f_*$ on $\pi_1$ sends the fiber subgroup of $\pi_1(E_1)$ to the fiber subgroup of $\pi_1(E_2)$, then there is a fiber-preserving map in the homotopy class of $f$. Using the above result and a computation of the mapping degree set of fiber-preserving maps between $E_1$ and $E_2$, we obtain the following results on the finiteness and the realization problems of mapping degree sets. ($\mathcal F$) The mapping degree set $D(E_1, E_2)$ is finite if $M_2$ is hyperbolic and the Euler class of $E_2$ is not torsion. ($\mathcal R$) For any finite set $A$ of integers containing $0$ and any $n>2$, $A$ is the mapping degree set $D(M,N)$ for some closed oriented $n$-manifolds $M$ and $N$. Item ($\mathcal F$) extends the previously known $3$-dimensional case to all dimensions $\geq 3$. Item ($\mathcal R$) gives a complete answer to the realization problem on finite sets of integers (containing 0) in all dimensions, including in particular the previously unknown cases in dimensions $ 4$ and $5$.
items.authors: Christoforos Neofytidis, Hongbin Sun, Ye Tian, Shicheng Wang, Zhongzi Wang

items.title: Recurrence for pretentious systems along generalized Pythagorean triples
items.abstract: We establish multiple recurrence results for pretentious measure-preserving multiplicative actions along generalized Pythagorean triples, that is, solutions to the equation $ax^2 + b y^2 = c z^2$. This confirms the ergodic-theoretic form of the generalized Pythagorean partition regularity conjecture in this critical case of structured measure-preserving actions. As a consequence of our main theorem, any finite coloring of $\mathbb{N}$ generated by the level sets of finitely many pretentious completely multiplicative functions, must contain a monochromatic generalized Pythagorean triple.
items.authors: Nikos Frantzikinakis, Andreas Mountakis

items.title: Une conjecture $C_{\rm st}$ pour la cohomologie \`a support compact
items.abstract: Let $\mathbf{B}$ be the ring of analytic functions on the Fargues-Fontaine curve $Y_{\rm FF}$. We shaw that, by adding sufficiently iterated periods, one can kill its Galois cohomology in degrees $\geq 1$. For $\mathbf{B}_{\rm dR}^+$, the corresponding result is obtained by adjoining just $\log t$ and is folklore. This allows to formulate $C_{\rm dR}$ and $C_{\rm st}$ conjectures for the compactly supported cohomology of $p$-adic analytic varieties.
items.authors: Pierre Colmez, Sally Gilles, Wies{\l}awa Nizio{\l}

items.title: Conjugacy classes of regular integer matrices
items.abstract: This paper is devoted to the theory of $GL_n({\mathbb Z})$-conjugacy classes of regular integer $n\times n$ matrices and related commutative semigroups. Such a matrix is $GL_n({\mathbb Q})$-conjugate to the companion matrix of its characteristic polynomial. But the set of $GL_n({\mathbb Z})$-conjugacy classes of regular integer matrices with a fixed characteristic polynomial $f$ is usually nontrivial (finite if $f$ has simple roots, infinite if $f$ has multiple roots). It is in 1:1-correspondence to a subsemigroup of a certain quotient semigroup of the commutative semigroup of full lattices in the algebra ${\mathbb Q}[t]/(f)$. In its first part, the paper gives a survey on old and new results on full lattices and orders in a finite dimensional commutative ${\mathbb Q}$-algebra with unit element and on induced semigroups. In its longer second part, the paper applies this theory to many examples, essentially all cases with $n=2$, many cases with $n=3$ and two cases with arbitrary $n$, the case with $n$ different integer eigenvalues and the case of a single $n\times n$ Jordan block.
items.authors: Claus Hertling, Khadija Larabi

items.title: Galois Orbit Bounds for Surface Degenerations
items.abstract: Given a smooth proper family $g : X \to S$ of surfaces over a number field $K \subset \mathbb{C}$, with $S$ an irreducible curve and $\eta \in S$ its generic point, we consider the general problem of constraining the locus $\textrm{NL}(S)$ in $S(\overline{K})$ of points $s$ where the Picard rank of $X_{s}$ is larger than the generic Picard rank. Assuming that the local system $\mathbb{V} = R^{2} g_{*} \mathbb{Z}$ admits a non-trivial monodromy logarithm $N$ at infinity, we give a general condition under which certain points of $\textrm{NL}(S)$ of unexpectedly large Picard rank satisfy a ``Galois-orbit'' height bound. This leads to the following result of Zilber-Pink type: Let $g : X \to S$ be a one-parameter family of polarized K3 surfaces admitting a non-trivial limit mixed Hodge structure and such that $S(\mathbb{C})$ contains a Hodge-generic point. Then the locus in $S(\mathbb{C})$ where the Picard rank jumps by $3$ or more is finite. Our arguments include a new technique for ``spreading out'' formal geometry, a study of the rigid geometry of equicharacteristic zero semistable surface degenerations, and use the model-free Hyodo-Kato theory of Colmez-Nizio\l.
items.authors: David Urbanik

items.title: A topological interpretation of numbers
items.abstract: We survey recent advancements on the realisation problem for mapping degree sets. In particular, we explain that any finite set containing zero is the mapping degree set between some $n$-manifolds, for each $n\geq3$. Our building factors for the construction of the realising manifolds will be aspherical manifolds. Thus, along the way, we review a couple of open questions related to maps of non-zero degree for aspherical manifolds.
items.authors: Christoforos Neofytidis

items.title: The Five Distance Theorem For An Arbitrary Norm
items.abstract: The three gap theorem states that the points of the Kronecker sequence $\alpha,2\alpha,\ldots,N\alpha$, considered modulo one, divide the circle into intervals of at most three distinct lengths. In a two-dimensional nearest-neighbour analogue, Haynes and Marklof proved that the Kronecker sequence modulo an arbitrary unimodular lattice determines at most five distinct nearest-neighbour distances in the Euclidean norm, and that this bound is sharp. Dettmann subsequently constructed examples attaining five distinct distances for every $\ell_p$-norm, $1\leq p\leq\infty$. We prove the corresponding upper bound for every norm on $\mathbb R^2$: for every full-rank lattice $L$, every $\alpha\in\mathbb R^2$, and every $N\in\mathbb N$, the number of distinct nearest-neighbour distances is at most five. For every norm, this bound is attained for some $L$ and $\alpha$. For strictly convex norms, the proof extends the lattice-theoretic argument of Haynes and Marklof by replacing the Euclidean angular estimates with a cone lemma based on a proper Brass angular measure. The result for arbitrary norms is then obtained by a strictly convex perturbation and a limiting argument.
items.authors: Nikita A. Mironov, Oleg R. Musin

items.title: On Frobenius rigidity for motivic cohomology
items.abstract: We study how motivic and \'etale motivic cohomology of a smooth and proper variety changes under extensions of algebraically closed base fields $k$. With finite coefficients, motivic cohomology is independent of $k$, and \'etale motivic cohomology is independent of $k$ away from the characteristic, but depends on $k$ at the characteristic. We then consider the fiber of $F-1$ for $F$ the Frobenius, on motivic cohomology and \'etale motivic cohomology for varieties defined over finite fields. We show that this fiber is independent of $k$ with finite coefficients. In addition, we give some results and examples with integral coefficients.
items.authors: Thomas H. Geisser

items.title: Affine Symmetries of Polynomial Roots with Multiplicities and Applications to Constacyclic Codes
items.abstract: Let $f(X)$ be a polynomial over a finite field, and let its defining function record the multiplicities of its roots. In this paper, we introduce the affine stabilizer group and the affine stabilizer group scheme of the defining function of $f(X)$. These objects characterize the affine symmetries of the roots of $f(X)$ together with their multiplicities. We establish structural descriptions of these affine stabilizers and relate them to the coefficient structure of $f(X)$. In particular, the affine stabilizer group determines quotient structures of the defining function, which yield canonical descriptions of the corresponding semi-invariant polynomial spaces. The resulting coefficient constraints provide explicit restrictions on the possible supports of polynomials with prescribed affine symmetries. The affine stabilizer group scheme further captures infinitesimal symmetries arising from multiple roots and gives refined coefficient constraints beyond those obtained from ordinary affine transformations. We apply this framework to generator polynomials of constacyclic codes over finite fields. The affine stabilizer structure of a generator polynomial induces subcodes defined by semi-invariant conditions and provides constraints on their dimensions and Hamming distances. In the special case of multiplicative symmetries, the construction specializes to the support-primitive decomposition of constacyclic codes.
items.authors: Li Zhu, Hongfeng Wu

items.title: The Bias Conjecture for One-Parameter, Non-Isotrivial Elliptic Curve Families
items.abstract: We investigate Miller's bias conjecture for general one-parameter families of elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ with non-constant $j$-invariants. Utilizing methods developed by Michel, we view the second moment as the sum of distinct cohomological components: a main $p^2$ term, a $p^{3/2}$ term arising from the first cohomology over the projective line, and terms of order $p$ or lower corresponding to singular fibers. By assuming the generalized Sato-Tate conjecture, we employ representation and motive theory to demonstrate that the coefficient of the $p^{3/2}$ term averages to zero in the limit. We then independently analyze the lower-order contributions without assuming Sato-Tate. By applying the Chebotarev density theorem and analyzing Galois representations, we show that the contributions to the order $p$ term from additive singular fibers also average to zero. Consequently, the only remaining average contribution to the $p$ term is $-B_pp$, where $B_p$ denotes the number of ``bad'' points where the discriminant vanishes. Because $B_p$ averages to a strictly positive value, the overall coefficient of the $p$ term averages to a strictly negative value in the limit, thereby establishing the bias conjecture for these families.
items.authors: Lucas Chen, Joshua Im, Steven J. Miller, Devayani Pradhan

items.title: Ekedahl's Equivalence Explained
items.abstract: Ekedahl's theory relates diagonal complexes to \(F\)-gauges, but turning this equivalence into explicit calculations requires careful control of its constructions. These notes explain the equivalence and clarify the generators-and-relations definition of \(\rmt\). At each finite level, we construct bounded projective resolutions of bounded coherent gauge complexes by finite sums of the standard generators. Morita equivalence expresses \(\rmt\) as a tensor product functor. Comparing the constructions across levels yields an exact fully faithful embedding of the diagonal heart into \(\Ch(R)\). Finally, we compute three distinct domino types arising from abelian threefolds that are all supergeneral.
items.authors: Yuan Yang

items.title: Mock Modularity, Resurgence, and Dual False Theta Functions
items.abstract: The $\hat{Z}$ invariant of a three-manifold $M_{3}$, a half-index of the $3d$ $\mathcal{N}=2$ theory $T[M_{3}]$, is well understood for negative-definite plumbed three-manifolds. For orientation-reversed manifolds, however, the known formulas fail to produce $q$-series, and making sense of the operation $q \rightarrow q^{-1}$ remains a central open problem. Seifert manifolds, whose $\hat{Z}$ invariants are built from false theta functions, offer a natural testing ground. We study ``dual false theta functions'', the objects that should replace false theta functions under orientation reversal. Two characterizations of these duals exist in the literature: a modular one, based on mock modularity with a prescribed shadow, and a resurgent one, based on Borel--Mordell integrals and transseries. We prove that the two characterizations are equivalent. We construct a new family of dual false theta functions for values of positive integer $p$ satisfying a Pell-equation condition. Its members are built from Zwegers' indefinite theta functions, have integer coefficients, and have effective central charge $c_{\text{eff}} \leq 1$. We also show that the mock theta functions of Li and Schwagenscheidt satisfy these characterizations and arise from a natural regularization of the divergent product $\eta^{3}(\tau)\psi_{p, a}(- \tau)$.
items.authors: Mrunmay Jagadale

items.title: Rational curves on toroidal compactifications of Picard modular varieties
items.abstract: It was known that the canonical bundle of a smooth toroidal compactification of a noncompact finite-volume ball quotient is nef in dimension $n\geq3$ and ample in dimension $n\geq6$. We prove that the canonical bundle is ample in dimension $n\geq4$ and show that this dimension bound is sharp. We construct infinitely many pairwise noncommensurable noncompact Picard modular threefolds whose smooth projective toroidal compactifications have non-ample canonical bundle. Each compactification contains a smooth rational curve meeting the interior and having canonical degree zero. More generally, in every dimension $n\geq2$, we construct infinitely many pairwise noncommensurable noncompact Picard modular varieties whose smooth toroidal compactifications contain smooth rational curves meeting the interior. In particular, such curves persist in arbitrarily high dimension, even when the canonical bundle is ample.
items.authors: Soheil Memariansorkhabi, Sai-Kee Yeung

items.title: Mean-Tilted Intervals: Regression and Dynamic Models
items.abstract: Mean-tilted intervals (MTIs) provide a fixed-content family of interval targets indexed by retained-mean balance. This paper develops generalized-Bayes computation for using those targets in regression and time-varying endpoint models after content and tilt have been specified. The update combines a prior with an exponentiated residual-product check loss, yielding uncertainty summaries for endpoint functions rather than a response-distribution model. A pseudo-asymmetric-Laplace normal-exponential representation gives generalized-inverse-Gaussian latent-scale updates and Gaussian conditional updates for one root when the other is fixed. The same representation gives deterministic ECM equations for generalized-posterior modes. We present ridge endpoint regression, a conditionally Gaussian shrinkage construction for the zero-tilt case, deterministic fixed-feature readouts, and dynamic linear endpoint states updated by alternating forward-filtering backward-sampling steps. These methods extend the MTI target from iid intervals to regression and dynamic settings; tolerance certification and response prediction require separate calibration or response models.
items.authors: Antonio De Leon, Raquel Prado, Bruno Sans\'o

items.title: Reference-State Bootstrap Correction and Kernel Characterization of Residual-Based Fit Indices in Structural Equation Models
items.abstract: Sampling error affects the finite-sample values of residual-based fit indices. We show that the unweighted comparative fit index ($CFI_u$) rests on a quadratic-kernel maximum mean discrepancy and that a Gaussian-kernel comparative fit index (KCFI) converges to $CFI_u$ as bandwidth increases. Because kernel discrepancies lack an analytic sampling correction, we extend expected-discrepancy bootstrap methods to a fitted-correlation reference state: the sample is transformed to reproduce the fitted correlation matrix, then resampled and refitted to estimate the exact-fit sampling component. Across 18 confirmatory factor analysis conditions, this correction reduced the root mean square error (RMSE) of both indices by 62%-87%. Under normality it matched an analytic residual-covariance estimator of $CFI_u$ within .0001, and in small samples it outperformed ordinary bootstrap correction in accuracy and availability. Corrected KCFI had lower RMSE than identically corrected $CFI_u$ in all 29 nonnormal conditions, even against a common target, but in six heavy-tailed small-sample conditions the analytic estimator was more accurate than both. The results validate the reference-state correction where it is needed and delimit where the analytic estimator is preferable.
items.authors: Eunjeong Song, Sehee Hong

items.title: Dynamic Extended Generalized Many-Facet Rasch Model: A Unified Approach to Rater-Mediated Assessment
items.abstract: Rating procedures are crucial in psychological and medical diagnosis, educational assessment, peer review, and grant evaluation. A major methodological challenge is disentangling multiple sources of variability in ratings, such as subject ability, rater behavior, and item characteristics. Item Response Theory-based models, most notably many-facet Rasch models and hierarchical rater models, have been widely adopted for jointly estimating subject, rater, and item effects, while retaining high interpretability. We introduce the Dynamic Extended Generalized Many-Facet Rasch model, a general class of Bayesian semiparametric models that integrate and extend existing approaches. Its measurement model allows location and discrimination parameters to depend jointly on item and rater characteristics and incorporates subject-item and rater-subject variation. The dynamic extension introduces a rater-specific cross-lagged effect capturing dependence on the previously rated subject, and a Bayesian P-spline capturing systematic changes in discrimination over the rating sequence, accounting for learning, fatigue, or adaptation effects. Subject heterogeneity is addressed through Bayesian nonparametric mixtures, flexibly learning the latent ability distribution without strict parametric assumptions and enabling model-based subject clustering. We also derive a closed-form, model-based inter-rater consensus coefficient and study its characteristics. We discuss theoretical properties, develop posterior computation strategies, and evaluate the model in simulation studies and two real-data applications.
items.authors: Giuseppe Mignemi, Patr\'icia Martinkov\'a, Sally Paganin

items.title: cvxoptdes: convex optimal experiment design in R
items.abstract: The cvxoptdes R-package provides a unified framework to perform convex optimal experiment design and online response optimization for linear, generalized linear and additive, nonlinear, and random intercept mixed models, using exclusively open-source solvers. It supports optimization and augmentation of weighted, penalized and convex constrained continuous designs across a discrete grid of candidate points and rounding to integer-valued designs using point-exchange algorithms or mixed-integer programming for orthogonally constrained designs, including the class of orthogonal minimally aliased response surface (OMARS) designs. Models and design constraints are defined and updated in an object-oriented context with the aim to facilitate the process of sequential (penalized) design augmentation analogous to online design procedures known from active learning and Bayesian optimization.
items.authors: Joris Chau, Alexandre Segers, Martin Otava, Stephen Karanja

items.title: De-biased Distribution Estimation for Locally Differential Private Survival Data
items.abstract: Sharing time-to-event data can leak sensitive information about individual participants in clinical studies. To protect the privacy of data, differential privacy (DP) framework offers rigorous protection for data sharing. The local variant of differential privacy is particularly appealing because each record is perturbed before it leaves the data owner or contributor. However, the injected perturbation distorts the true distribution of the source data, yielding low utility and invalid statistical inference with the released data. In this work, we propose a nonparametric estimator for the true survivor function via the deconvolution kernel function with locally differential private (LDP) right-censored survival data in which both the event times and the event indicators are privatized. Our estimator simultaneously de-biases the perturbation applied to the times and the errors induced by flipping the event indicators due to LDP. Theoretically, we establish the uniform consistency and point-wise asymptotic normality of the de-biased distribution estimator, and derive its uniform convergence rate together with the optimal bandwidth attaining that rate. Simulation studies and the analysis of a semi-synthetic dataset generated from the METABRIC breast cancer cohort demonstrate the performance of the proposed estimator across privacy budgets, censoring levels, and sample sizes. By the post-processing property of DP, the proposed de-biased estimator inherits the privacy guarantee while restoring valid inference on the survivor function.
items.authors: Yi Xiong, Li-Pang Chen, Liyue Fan

items.title: Sharp bounds for population and principal effects under latent sequential ignorability
items.abstract: Treatment decisions are often sequential and depend on information absent from the recorded history. Latent sequential ignorability models such assignment by assuming that baseline covariates and principal strata, defined by joint potential intermediate responses, account for confounding of later treatment. For two treatment periods with a binary intermediate response, we derive sharp population and principal effect bounds under a specified association between the potential responses and show that the two targets can require different optimizations to obtain sharp bounds. For population effects, optimization over latent treatment probabilities reduces to their feasible endpoints. Stronger selection between response types can be offset by making their outcome distributions more similar, preserving both the observed distribution and population marginal outcome distributions. This replacement can change effects within principal strata, whose sharp bounds may instead require interior treatment probabilities. Restrictions on differences in conditional effects can tighten the bounds without equating outcome levels. For binary outcomes, we give an exact finite algorithm that includes these interior assignments. We also develop inference under smoothness and estimation conditions. We illustrate the bounds in a study of gym attendance after an incentive program.
items.authors: Yuki Ohnishi

items.title: Global Inference for High Dimensional Quantile Regression with Heterogeneity
items.abstract: Quantile regression has received considerable attention in high dimensional methodology due to its robustness and ability to accommodate heteroskedasticity. Despite this attention, current inferential methods for high dimensional quantile regression have significant limitations---only testing significance, testing at a single quantile at a time, or assuming homoskedasticity. To generalize the inferences that can be drawn in high dimensional quantile regression, we introduce partial penalized Wald and rank score tests for testing linear hypotheses uniformly over a set of quantiles $\mathcal T$ under a heteroskedastic model. We propose globally adaptive local linear approximation (LLA) algorithms for folded concave penalized estimation and show that our global LLA algorithms recover ``testing oracles'' for the full and reduced models with high probability. We then show that our global LLA estimators achieve the $\sqrt{s/n}$ oracle estimation rate uniformly over $\mathcal T$, establish Bahadur representations, and derive asymptotic distributions for the test statistics under the null and local alternatives. We develop a dual formulation incorporating adaptive penalty weights for the rank scores and use the strong oracle property to establish their oracle equivalence. Using empirical process techniques, we derive reference distributions based on suprema of squared Bessel processes, extending partial penalized inference beyond pointwise chi-square calibration.
items.authors: Tate Jacobson, Daeyoung Ham, Ben Sherwood

items.title: Decomposing the spectral density function of an ARMA process
items.abstract: Quasi-periodic oscillations are characterized by fitting Lorentzian functions to a nonparametric estimate of the power spectral density, a two-step procedure that separates estimation from modeling and does not accommodate measurement error. We develop a parametric alternative based on autoregressive moving-average (ARMA) processes observed with measurement error. We derive an exact decomposition of the ARMA spectral density into real-valued components, one for each class of autoregressive roots under complex conjugation, plus a polynomial term when the moving-average order is at least the autoregressive order. Each component is a Wrapped Cauchy kernel, and for complex roots it is accompanied by a conjugate-Poisson term that makes the peak asymmetric and displaces its maximum from the frequency given by the argument of the root.
