Overall, the work clearly illustrates the benefit of forming PD classification using continuous speech compared to using sustained vowel sounds.
items.authors: Rujia Li, Niloofar Momeni, Susanna Whitling, Andreas Jakobsson

items.title: Silent coverage failures in rare-event searches and a degeneracy index that predicts them
items.abstract: Searches for new physics in low-background experiments infer a non-negative signal strength from few events and often report an upper limit. Nominal frequentist coverage requires both a valid interval construction and an adequate data model. We study how controlled model departures affect lower- and upper-endpoint coverage for six interval procedures in an exact Poisson counting experiment, dark-matter recoil spectra, and a neutrinoless-double-beta-decay peak search. We introduce the Poisson--Fisher degeneracy index $\mathcal I_{\mathrm{PF}}(\delta\nu;\vartheta_0)=(\beta,\gamma)$, which maps a specified expected-count deformation, after projection onto the complete fitted tangent space, to $\beta$, the signed fitted signal shift in profiled standard-error units, and $\gamma$, the Poisson--Fisher norm of the unabsorbed residual. Locally, the sign of $\beta$ identifies the threatened endpoint, while larger $\gamma$ implies greater detectability by the saturated-Poisson goodness-of-fit test used here at a fixed $5\%$ type-I error rate. Across the studied deformations, positive signal-like bias degrades discovery-side coverage while making upper limits conservative; negative signal bias from overestimated signal efficiency can make the upper endpoint undercover. Calibration under the nominal simulator does not protect against misspecification of that simulator relative to the data-generating process. A plausible deformation with large $|\beta|$ and small $\gamma$ may therefore evade diagnosis and should be represented by a nuisance constrained with auxiliary information or included in a defensible envelope. In the exactly collinear constrained-nuisance benchmark, modelling the deformation restores coverage at the evaluated grid points, at a quantifiable cost in interval sensitivity.
items.authors: Davide Pagano

items.title: Kernelized Stein Discrepancy for Goodness-of-Fit Tests and Stein Sampling in R
items.abstract: Stein's method constructs computable discrepancies between a target distribution and a candidate distribution without requiring the target distribution's normalizing constant. These discrepancies support goodness-of-fit tests for model assessment as well as sampling tools for empirical approximation. The R package steinsampling provides the first unified R workflow for applying score-based Stein methods to kernel goodness-of-fit testing of independent or serially dependent observations, point transport, greedy point construction, and sample compression. High-level functions carry out each task in a single call, while the kernel, calibration, optimization, and transition components are provided separately so that users can replace any one of them. A single score and kernel setup can therefore be reused across sampling and testing, making these methods easier to reproduce, compare, and extend.
items.authors: Junhao Gao, Ery Arias-Castro

items.title: Identification and Inference in proxy-SVARs with non-Gaussian shocks
items.abstract: Two frequent approaches for identifying structural VARs are external instruments, which carry economic content but are often weak, and non-Gaussianity of the shocks, which provides statistical identification but carries no economic meaning. We combine the two strategies in a single generalized method of moments framework. This hybrid approach point-identifies the target shocks while also identifying the non-target shocks up to sign and ordering. Under suitable rank conditions, the higher-order moments of the structural shocks anchor the identification uniformly over the instrument strength. Consequently, under local-to-zero proxy relevance, estimators of the dynamic causal effects remain consistent, and standard asymptotic inference remains valid. Moreover, the Anderson-Rubin confidence sets are substantially narrower than their instrument-only counterparts. The hybrid estimator is also more efficient than either source of identification used in isolation: at any fixed proxy relevance, even a weak instrument increases the efficiency of the estimator through its covariance with the non-Gaussian moment block. Under local deviations from proxy exogeneity, we provide asymptotic bias bounds and show that stronger non-Gaussianity of the shocks compresses the bias. Finally, the over-identified structure yields two mutually orthogonal specification tests for proxy exogeneity and the validity of the higher-order moment conditions. We derive their limiting distributions and provide a bootstrap procedure for finite-sample critical values. Monte Carlo simulations and two applications with identification of oil news-shock and a Euro-area MP shock demonstrate the potential of our framework.
items.authors: Paritosh Shankarrao Junare

items.title: Rank-one variance inflation in polynomial estimation of signal parameters with a sign-preserving fractional-power basis
items.abstract: The polynomial maximization method estimates signal parameters in non-Gaussian noise from a finite description of the noise by its moments and cumulants, without a density. Known accuracy results assume that these noise characteristics are known, or use a design in which estimating them jointly costs no accuracy. In practice they are estimated from the residuals of a preliminary fit, and the effect of this substitution on accuracy is unknown. We treat the feasible scheme as a two-step estimator and, for a general smooth signal model in a fixed design, find the increment of its asymptotic covariance in closed form: $\Sigma_{\rm fe}-\Sigma_{\rm or}=c_2(1-g_{\rm or}) Q^{-1}\bar{d}\bar{d}^{\top}Q^{-1}$, a positive semidefinite matrix of rank at most one. Here $c_2$ is the noise variance, $g_{\rm or}\le 1$ the oracle variance reduction factor, and $Q$ and $\bar{d}$ the second-moment matrix and mean of the signal gradient over the design. Estimating the fractional moments that form the weights costs no first-order accuracy, because that block is orthogonal; the whole increment comes from estimating the sign-preserving centering means. The increment lies along the single direction $Q^{-1}\bar{d}$, so linear combinations of the parameters orthogonal to it keep oracle accuracy. In the trace metric the variance reduction factor becomes $g_{\rm fe}=g_{\rm or}+(1-g_{\rm or})R_D$, where $R_D=\|Q^{-1}\bar{d}\|^2/{\rm tr} Q^{-1}$ depends on the design alone. We give four sufficient conditions for first-order oracle equivalence; noise symmetry is not among them. Monte Carlo experiments with a harmonic signal confirm the direction and size of the increment. A covariance estimate that ignores the increment undercovers where non-Gaussianity gives the largest gain, symmetric noise included.
items.authors: Serhii Zabolotnii

items.title: UGME: A python package for non-Markovian protein folding dynamics
items.abstract: Biomolecular processes, including protein folding, protein-protein association, and protein-DNA recognition, often occur on timescales beyond what individual atomistic molecular dynamics (MD) simulations can reach. To access these longer-timescale dynamics, practitioners commonly combine many parallelized, short trajectories into reduced kinetic models, such as Markov state models (MSMs), that describe how the biomolecules interconvert between a handful of biomolecular configurations (e.g., folded and unfolded states of a protein). Central to MSM construction is the assumption that, at sufficiently long time lags, these projected dynamics become memoryless, such that the future evolution of the system depends only on its current state. Yet, projecting high-dimensional biomolecular dynamics onto a small set of states necessarily discards information about unresolved degrees of freedom, including solvent reorganization, side-chain rearrangements, and intermediate configurations. Because these unresolved motions can continue to influence subsequent dynamics, the resulting dynamics retain memory that is absent from a Markovian description. Here, we present ugme, a modular, open-source Python package for constructing and validating generalized master equations (GME) models that explicitly account for these non-Markovian (memory) effects.
items.authors: Anthony J. Dominic III, Bertram Cham, Andr\'es Montoya-Castillo

items.title: Learning Electron Density with Virtual Atoms for Transferable Atomistic Representations
items.abstract: Electron density is a fundamental quantity of electronic structure, yet most machine learning density models treat it solely as a reconstruction target and are developed separately from machine learning interatomic potentials. Here, we introduce a virtual-atom formulation within the DPA3 framework, in which density query points are represented as virtual nodes and processed by the same parameterized encoder used for real atoms. An asymmetric neighbor construction allows virtual atoms to receive information from nearby real atoms without altering the real-atom interaction graph. The resulting framework supports density, energy, and force prediction through task-specific readout heads. The proposed model achieves state-of-the-art density reconstruction accuracy on the Materials Project benchmark, matches the best reported performance on nickel-manganese-cobalt battery cathode materials, and is competitive with dedicated density models on QM9. When density labels are used jointly with energy and force supervision, the model improves in-domain accuracy, makes local environment information more accessible under linear probing, and reduces zero-shot force errors on larger QM40 molecules. Density-only checkpoints also provide useful initializations for downstream energy-force learning under the fixed fine-tuning protocol. Together, these results support electron density as a source of electronic-structure supervision for interatomic-potential representations.
items.authors: Yuzhi Liu, Xinzijian Liu, Chengqian Zhang, Anyang Peng, Duo Zhang, Han Wang

items.title: Tersoff-NN: Hybrid Machine-Learned Bond-Order Extension of the Tersoff Potential
items.abstract: Accurate, robust, and efficient interatomic potentials are highly desirable for large-scale molecular dynamics simulations. Although machine-learning interatomic potentials can reproduce first-principles potential-energy surfaces with high accuracy, they typically incur higher computational costs than conventional empirical potentials and may be less reliable outside their training domains. We developed Tersoff-NN, a hybrid machine-learning potential for Si, which retains the analytical radial interactions and cutoff structure of the Tersoff potential while representing its environment-dependent bond-order factor using compact neural networks (NNs). Benchmarks for 32,768-atom systems show that Tersoff-NN is 4-12 times faster than the Behler-Parrinello-type NN potentials tested in this study. Tersoff-NN improves the short-range structure of liquid Si relative to the conventional Tersoff potential, closely reproduces the ab initio radial and angular distributions, and reproduces the equilibrium structure of diamond Si and qualitative energetic trends among several crystalline phases. Furthermore, melt-quench simulations reveal a disordered solid with predominantly four-coordinated, tetrahedral-like local environments. Additionally, characteristic reconstruction motifs are retained on Si surfaces despite their exclusion from the training dataset. A direct comparison with an alternative atom-centered bond-order NN highlights the critical role of physical constraints in ensuring dynamic stability. Despite exhibiting comparable validation errors, the selected triplet-based architecture remains stable, while an alternative model exhibits unphysical bond-order growth and atomic collapse. These results confirm that learning only the bond-order term improves the description of diverse Si environments while retaining substantial computational efficiency and enhancing dynamical stability.
items.authors: Yusuke Nishimura, Sho Kubota, Kotaro Takematsu, Kentaro Hirai, Takanobu Watanabe

items.title: Kernel-Level Constant-Potential Molecular Dynamics in GROMACS
items.abstract: How charge rearranges within an electrode shapes the behavior of batteries, supercapacitors, and other electrochemical devices. Molecular simulations can capture this response by allowing the charge on each electrode atom to adjust to its surroundings, but repeatedly calculating these charges adds substantial computational cost. We present an open-source implementation of the constant-potential method in GROMACS that integrates these calculations into the program's optimized CPU and GPU routines. Comparisons with established codes validate the electrode charges, while charging, voltammetry, and impedance simulations demonstrate the response to changing electrical conditions. The implementation also supports electrodes that move or deform and models of finite metallic screening and electron spillover. In a pair of charged carbon nanotubes, allowing charge to move away from the facing surfaces reduces the repulsive force at contact by about half at an intermediate charge and keeps the pair bound where a uniform-charge model opens within the simulated time. These capabilities make the electrical response of electrodes accessible within GROMACS for studies of interfacial structure, charging dynamics, and electrode motion.
items.authors: Sheng Bi, Mathieu Salanne, Jun Cheng, Guang Feng

items.title: The RAS-CCSD model, with applications for open-shell molecules
items.abstract: The restricted active space coupled cluster singles and doubles (RAS-CCSD) model, and its pilot implementation is detailed. The approach offers a simple, pragmatic way to formulate a coupled cluster theory for open-shell and multireference systems. For ground state energies, errors (compared to FCI) are shown to be similar to those of unrestricted (spin-orbital) CCSD. For excited states, the errors of RAS-CCSD are generally larger, and adaptations to the methodology are needed to achieve an approach which is balanced for both ground and excited states. However, unlike unrestricted CCSD, the approach is spin-adapted and can be used to add dynamical correlation to a multideterminantal reference state.
items.authors: Sarai Dery Folkestad

items.title: Single-electron Fluorine Bonding. I. The SEFB-15 and CSFB-14 Benchmark Datasets, Reference Binding Energies and Intermolecular Bond Distances: Assessment of M06-2X density functional
items.abstract: Halogen bonding in which a covalently bound fluorine acts as halogen-bond donor (F-bonding) is rare, and its open-shell variant with radical electron donors remains unexplored. We introduce SEFB-15 dataset (15 open-shell DF$\cdots$CH$_3$ complexes) exemplifying single-electron F-bonding (SEFB) and CSFB-14 dataset (14 closed-shell DF$\cdots$NH$_3$ complexes) representing closed-shell F-bonding (CSFB). Reference binding energies (BEs) at DF-RMP2-F12/CBS//DF-RMP2-F12/VDZ-F12 are validated against CCSD(T), CCSD(T)-F12b, W1-F12 and W2-F12 for selected systems (DF = F$_2$, NCF, CNF, NH$_3$F$^+$ and NH$_2$F$_2^+$), with MA%D of 4.5% (DF$\cdots$CH$_3$) and 3.4% (DF$\cdots$NH$_3$) against CCSD(T)-F12b/CBS//CCSD(T)-F12b/VDZ-F12. BEs from W1-F12 and W2-F12 are identical. Reference F-bond distances at DF-RMP2-F12/VDZ-F12 are validated against CCSD(T)-F12b, CCSD(T), CCSD, and DCSD for the same systems, with MA%D of 0.9% (SEFB) and 0.4% (CSFB) against CCSD(T)-F12b/VDZ-F12. M06-2X is recommended for closed-shell halogen bonding with heavier halogens but has never been assessed for open-shell F-bonding. M06-2X/AVTZ systematically overbinds all SEFB-15 complexes and underestimates their F-bond distances, with MA%Ds of 75.8% on BEs and 8.9% on F-bond distances. M06-2X predicts comparable BEs for F$_2\cdots$CH$_3$ and F$_2\cdots$NH$_3$, contrary to all ab initio results, an anomaly persisting across all 16 basis sets. Neither basis set nor BSSE correction resolves the overbinding. BSSE correction worsens BEs for DF$\cdots$NH$_3$ complexes. For CSFB-14, M06-2X/AVTZ yields MA%Ds of 16.0% for BEs and 3.3% for F-bond distances. M06-2X is reliable for CSFB but unreliable for SEFB regardless of basis set. Companion paper II reports performance of other Minnesota functionals and ab initio methods for these datasets.
items.authors: Govinda Prasad Khanal, Elangannan Arunan

items.title: Solvent Fluctuations Enable Photoionization of Aqueous Nitrite Microdroplets
items.abstract: Nitrite photochemistry in atmospheric aerosols and natural waters is a major source of hydroxyl radicals and reactive nitrogen oxides. Contrary to the prevailing view that in the environment aqueous nitrite photochemistry proceeds exclusively through photoexcitation followed by homolytic bond cleavage, we show that visible light directly ionizes aqueous nitrite in individual micron-sized droplets. Although the photoionization cross section is exceptionally small, this pathway is observable at the high photon flux densities accessible in single-droplet experiments. Molecular simulations reveal that this is because photoionization absorption has an exceptionally long wavelength tail due to the large solvent reorganization energy in aqueous solutions. Kinetic modeling of an aqueous-phase reaction mechanism quantitatively accounts for the observed chemistry and predicts the formation of nitrate, hydroxyl radicals, and solvated electrons. The overlap of the predicted broad photoionization continuum with the visible solar spectrum further suggests that visible-light photoionization is an overlooked source of nitrogen oxides, solvated electrons, and oxidants in atmospheric aerosols, snowpack, and natural waters. Under dilute conditions, where dissolved oxygen is the main sink for solvated electrons, photoionization is expected to be the dominant photochemical loss pathway for nitrite.
items.authors: Brandon J. Wallace, Eric R. Heller, Alex Prophet, Pranav Ballapuram, Ashok Ajoy, David T. Limmer, Kevin R. Wilson

items.title: Chromatographic Peak Shape beyond the High-P\'eclet Approximation: Analytic Time-Domain Expression and Derivatives
items.abstract: Analytic time-domain expressions for the elution-time density and its parameter derivatives were recently derived from a stochastic model of linear isocratic chromatography incorporating advective-diffusive transport, injection dispersion, and fast and slow retention mechanisms. A Gaussian approximation, justified asymptotically at high column-scale P\'eclet numbers, was adopted for the distribution of the combined mobile-phase and fast-retention time, while slow retention was incorporated through a series of Gaussian-Gamma convolutions. Here, the underlying normal-inverse-Gaussian density is approximated by a finite Gaussian mixture using an existing quadrature rule. The elution-time PDF is a weighted sum of series of the previously derived Gaussian-Gamma form. Its parameter derivatives are also obtained. Newly derived recurrences reduce the cost of evaluating the coefficients of that series and their derivatives from quadratic to linear in truncation order for a fixed number of mechanisms. Through a probabilistic analysis of the series coefficients, the required number of terms is found to be small enough for rapid evaluation under usual chromatographic conditions. A relative roundoff-error estimator is derived to quantify finite-precision loss in the inherited forward recurrence for Gaussian-Gamma convolutions. For the cancellation-prone regime, a backward reconstruction is developed, initialized from an exact ratio of consecutive Gaussian-Gamma terms expressed through parabolic-cylinder functions. A highly accurate approximation is derived for rapid evaluation of this ratio. Independent high-precision calculations confirm the high accuracy of the resulting double-precision evaluation in the tested numerical case.
items.authors: Hern\'an R. S\'anchez

items.title: Development of a Minimal Auxiliary Basis for the Particle--Particle Random Phase Approximation (ppRPA): Accelerating Excited-State Calculations in Diradical Nanoparticles and Periodic Systems
items.abstract: Singlet--triplet gaps set the energy scale of the two-spin manifold in molecular quantum information materials, and such systems frequently carry diradical character: metal nanoclusters, metal--organic frameworks with radical linkers, and the nitrogen--vacancy center in diamond. Time-dependent density functional theory is the standard tool at this size but describes multireference systems poorly. A closed-shell reference is inadequate for a multiconfigurational ground state, and the adiabatic kernel excludes doubly excited configurations. The particle--particle random phase approximation (\pprpa{}) changes the particle number rather than the spin. Singlet and triplet states descend from one closed-shell reference, and double excitations enter on the same footing as single ones. Computational cost has confined \pprpa{} to small systems, and the two-electron integrals that drive it are factorized through an auxiliary basis. We develop \pprpa{}--as, which reduces that basis to a minimal set of atom-centered Gaussian shells whose exponents follow from free-atom radii and one global scaling factor. The approximation enters only the excited-state step, so both calculations proceed from the same self-consistent reference. We test molecules and clusters of up to 286 atoms, including heavy elements, and seven point defects in four periodic hosts, obtaining both multiplicities and their splitting without symmetry breaking or spin projection. We optimize the scaling factor and give guidance on choosing it. An order-of-magnitude smaller auxiliary basis delivers a speed-up of up to eightfold while staying within $0.03$~eV of conventional \pprpa{}, bringing diradical nanoclusters and periodic systems within reach.
items.authors: Yuchen Wang, Zhenyu Li

items.title: QUPEX: A Streamlit-Based Framework for Visualizing Quantum-Mechanical Property Spaces of Organic Molecules
items.abstract: The growing availability of quantum-mechanical (QM) datasets offers new opportunities to investigate structure-property and property-property relationships in drug-like molecules using data-driven methods. However, interactive tools that integrate molecular visualization, statistical analysis of QM properties, clustering, and machine learning (ML) remain limited, despite their value in facilitating dataset exploration and interpretation. To address this gap, we introduce QUPEX (QUantum Property EXplorer), an open-source Streamlit-based framework for the interactive exploration of QM property spaces in molecular systems. As a demonstration, we apply QUPEX to a subset of the QM7-X dataset comprising 41,537 equilibrium molecular structures containing up to seven non-hydrogen atoms (C, N, O, S, and Cl) and their 24 associated QM properties. In addition to property-space analysis, QUPEX incorporates an XGBoost regression pipeline for predicting PBE0 dipole moments from tight-binding-derived electronic descriptors, together with model evaluation and SHAP-based interpretability functionality. By combining interactive molecular visualization, data analysis, and predictive modeling, QUPEX provides an accessible and extensible environment for investigating molecular datasets and identifying patterns in their structural and electronic properties. These capabilities can support the exploration of chemical space and inform the rational design of drug-like molecules with targeted QM properties.
items.authors: Mirtha Pillaca Quispe, Alejandra Hinostroza Caldas, Leonardo Medrano Sandonas

items.title: Photoinduced Modulation of Rectification and Charge Transport in Diarylethene-Viologen Molecular Junction
items.abstract: Large-area molecular junctions combining photochromic and redox-active functionalities provide an attractive platform for controlling charge transport by light. In this work, we study Au/DAEVIO/Ti/Au molecular junctions incorporated with electro-grafted layers of diarylethene-viologen with thicknesses of 12-16 nm. In the initial OFF state, the junctions exhibit low current densities and strong rectification, with a rectification ratio of 300 at 1V. Temperature-dependent measurements reveal a thermally assisted contribution at higher temperatures and a much weaker temperature dependence below 160-180K, consistent with multistep charge transport through molecular and/or interfacial states rather than direct coherent tunneling across the entire molecular layer. Under continuous in situ 385 nm irradiation, the electrical response is strongly and asymmetrically modified. The current density at +1V increases by a factor of 200, while the negative-bias current is only weakly modified, reducing the rectification ratio from 300 to 2. Illumination also produces a nonzero short-circuit current density of + 0.006mA cm-2 and an open-circuit voltage of -0.45V. These results indicate that irradiation simultaneously modifies molecular charge transport and generates a measurable photoelectric response. This behavior is consistent with light-induced changes in electronic coupling associated with DAE photocyclization, combined with photoinduced charge generation and field-dependent charge separation involving the redox-active viologen units and asymmetric electrode interfaces.
items.authors: Sofyan Tahri, Samuel Decorps, Stephane Lenfant, Denis Frath, Imen Hnid

items.title: Ensuring Complete Consistency between Hops and Wavefunction Propagation in Fewest-Switches Surface Hopping
items.abstract: Fewest-switches surface hopping (FSSH) is a popular and versatile approach for performing dynamical simulations beyond the Born-Oppenheimer approximation, in which nonadiabatic effects are incorporated through stochastic hops of the active potential energy surface. However, the FSSH algorithm does not ensure that hops are completely consistent with the underlying electronic wavefunction dynamics. This can lead to significant errors as well as requiring small propagation time steps, which can significantly compromise the computational efficiency of the method. These problems are known to be particularly severe at so-called trivial crossings, for which the nonadiabatic coupling is entirely localized at the crossing point. Here, we solve the trivial-crossing problem by developing a fully-consistent hopping-probability formula, which generates attempted hops that match the time-evolution of the wavefunction across any size time step by construction. A state-tracking algorithm is also utilized to ensure that attempted hops are always accepted at trivial crossings. Through application to systems that contain extremely challenging trivial crossings, we demonstrate that this hopping scheme is capable of obtaining highly accurate results, even when large propagation time steps are used.
items.authors: Jonathan R. Mannouch

items.title: Embossing of Tapered, Isometric Micro-Interdigitated Flow Fields for Enhanced Desalination by Faradaic Deionization
items.abstract: Engineered transport architectures can improve electrolyte distribution and active-material utilization in porous electrodes, yet their implementation remains limited by fabrication methods that compromise precision, throughput, active-material preservation, or scalability. Here, an integrated embossing-calendering method is introduced to pattern Prussian blue analog (PBA) porous electrodes with embedded, micro-interdigitated flow fields (e$\mu$-IDFFs) for electrochemical desalination. This non-subtractive, roll-to-roll compatible method forms channels by controlling plastic deformation while simultaneously calendering the electrode, preserving active material and reducing patterning time by 100-fold relative to mechanical milling. Indentation experiments and a closed-form model further show that embossing requires 15-fold less force than stamping, while electrode microstructures show local densification beneath embossed channels. PBA electrodes are embossed with novel e$\mu$-IDFFs that use continuous width-tapering with isometric flow paths that promote uniform electrolyte distribution, increase rate capability, and reduce polarization. Compared with e$\mu$-IDFFs patterned using less scalable means and non-isometric flow paths, these e$\mu$-IDFFs desalinate seawater-salinity feeds near to potable levels with 1.5-fold of its thermodynamic energy efficiency and water recovery. Brackish desalination benefits similarly. Tapered, isometric e$\mu$-IDFFs and the embossing method introduced to pattern them are readily translated other electrochemical energy storage and separations systems.
items.authors: Md Habibur Rahman, Sadia Afrin, Kyle C. Smith

items.title: Precursor stoichiometry controls dopant structure, defect chemistry, and valence in Mn-doped ZnGa$_2$O$_4$ nanocrystals
items.abstract: The luminescence of doped nanocrystals is usually optimised through the activator; here we show that the host cation ratio is an equally decisive, and largely overlooked, design variable. Mn-doped ZnGa$_2$O$_4$ nanocrystals (Mn:Zn = $4\times10^{-4}$) were grown hydrothermally at nominal Zn/Ga ratios between 0.30 and 0.75 (stoichiometric: 0.50) and post-annealed at 400--1100$^\circ$C, and the resulting composition--temperature matrix was mapped by X-ray- and UV-excited luminescence, EPR, Rietveld-refined X-ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy and SEM. The as-grown crystals are phase-pure spinel at every composition and accommodate their off-stoichiometry internally as a point-defect inventory, reflected in a 0.4\% variation of the lattice parameter; on annealing, the excess gallium is exsolved as $\beta$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ in amounts set by the solution composition. The Mn$^{2+}$ emission separates into two optima, near-stoichiometric crystals annealed at 400--600$^\circ$C and Zn-excess crystals annealed at 1100$^\circ$C, the latter being twice as bright under X-ray excitation. Under X-ray and 365~nm excitation the two optima are separated by a minimum at 800$^\circ$C that coincides with a collapse of the Mn$^{2+}$ EPR population and has no counterpart in the Raman linewidths, identifying transient, defect-compensated oxidation of the dopant rather than lattice degradation as its origin. The most Zn-rich composition shows neither Mn$^{2+}$ nor Mn$^{4+}$ emission at any annealing stage, whereas its trace Cr$^{3+}$ emission is strong, indicating that Mn is rejected already during growth. Solution stoichiometry therefore acts on two levels, dopant capture and native-defect inventory, while annealing controls dopant valence and lattice order. The brightest high-temperature phosphor is thus not the nominally stoichiometric one, but the composition whose excess is consumed on its way to stoichiometry.
items.authors: M\'aty\'as M. Rudolf, G\'abor Bortel, Nikoletta Jegeny\'es, \'Arp\'ad Jakab, L\'aszl\'o Bencs, Ferenc Simon, Adam Gali, D\'avid Beke

items.title: Mn--Cr dopant association in dilute co-doped $\mathrm{ZnAl_2O_4}$ revealed by combined EPR and optical spectroscopy
items.abstract: Efficient and durable phosphors made from abundant elements underpin energy-saving solid-state lighting, near-infrared light sources for sensing, and X-ray and biomedical imaging. Co-doping is a standard route to brighter phosphors, yet the fate of the co-dopants is rarely established. We combine quantitative electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spin counting with photoluminescence, photoluminescence excitation, and X-ray-excited spectroscopy across two dilute Mn/Cr co-doping series of hydrothermally grown $\mathrm{ZnAl_2O_4}$ nanoparticles and show that the two ions can form an exchange-coupled, edge-sharing Cr--Mn defect complex, with $\mathrm{Mn^{2+/4+}}$ entering an octahedral site next to $\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}$. The octahedral Mn lifts the inversion symmetry of the $\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}$ site and strengthens its parity-forbidden absorption, enhancing the $\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}$ emission without energy transfer. The population of the defect complex follows the law of mass action, and above a threshold Mn concentration, Mn re-partitions into EPR-silent octahedral configurations that quench both emissions. Concentration optima in co-doped phosphors can thus reflect defect speciation, not only energy-transfer efficiency, which opens a structural design handle for brighter emitters.
items.authors: Apoko S. Omondi, M\'aty\'as M. Rudolf, Nikoletta Jegeny\'es, \'Arp\'ad Jakab, G\'abor Bortel, Bence G. M\'arkus, Adam Gali, D\'avid Beke

items.title: Finite-temperature adiabatic-connection reduced density-matrix functional theory: a unified framework for i-DMFT and TAO-DFT
items.abstract: Accurately describing chemical bond breaking requires capturing strong/static electron correlation, a major challenge for single-reference self-consistent-field methods such as Hartree--Fock and Kohn--Sham density-functional theory (DFT). Fractional occupations substantially improve this situation, as demonstrated by information-density-matrix-functional theory (i-DMFT) and thermally-assisted-occupation DFT (TAO-DFT). Although useful, they are formulated within rather different theoretical frameworks, are somewhat semi-empirical, and their relationship remains unclear. Here we introduce finite-temperature adiabatic-connection reduced density-matrix functional theory (FT-AC-RDMFT), in which i-DMFT and TAO-DFT emerge as different reductions of a unified framework. The effective eigenvalue equation for natural orbitals and the Fermi--Dirac occupation numbers follow directly from the variational principle, while a thermal adiabatic connection relates the empirical entropy coefficient of i-DMFT to a characteristic temperature of the auxiliary non-interacting system. Within this framework, i-DMFT is the exact-exchange-based reduction, whereas TAO-DFT results when exact exchange is replaced by a density-based exchange-correlation functional. Numerical calculations confirm that i-DMFT, apart from a constant, coincides with the exact-exchange realization of the framework, and show that the improved dissociation behavior from finite-temperature occupations extends beyond exact exchange to hybrid and semilocal density functionals. For strongly correlated V2O3, finite-temperature occupations substantially reduce the severely overestimated non-magnetic LDA bulk modulus, bringing it close to experiment. These results establish FT-AC-RDMFT as a common theoretical foundation for finite-temperature occupation-based electronic-structure methods in molecular and solid-state systems.
items.authors: Jingang Han, Huanjing Gong, Kai Luo, Hongming Weng, Xinguo Ren

items.title: Solubility of poorly soluble species in bulk and nanopores from grand-canonical Wang-Landau sampling
items.abstract: Poorly soluble species can have mean populations below one in small systems such as nanopores. In this regime, the grand-potential minimum, which identifies the most probable particle number, differs from the ensemble-averaged solute loading. We use grand-canonical Wang-Landau sampling (GCWLS) to calculate the density of states $\Omega(N_\mathrm{A}, N_\mathrm{B})$ for a binary Lennard-Jones mixture of solute B in solvent A, both in bulk and in slit pores. One set of GCWLS simulations gives ensemble averages over a range of chemical potentials, whereas conventional grand-canonical Monte Carlo (GCMC) simulation requires a separate simulation at each state point. Independent GCMC simulations confirm the GCWLS ensemble averages. The solvent number distribution is nearly Gaussian, whereas the dilute solute distribution is skewed and Poisson-like. The most probable solute number therefore lies below the ensemble-averaged loading $\langle N_\mathrm{B}\rangle$ and is zero whenever $\langle N_\mathrm{B}\rangle<1$. Reading the solute loading from the grand-potential minimum underestimates it and can falsely indicate that no solute is present. Defining the oversolubility as $\mathcal{O}_\mathrm{B}=x_\mathrm{B}^{\mathrm{conf}}/x_\mathrm{B}^{\mathrm{bulk}}$, where $x_\mathrm{B}$ is the solute mole fraction, we find $\mathcal{O}_\mathrm{B}\approx12$ in a pore of 3.5 particle diameters width when both wall interactions are repulsive. Adding wall-solute attraction moderately raises it to $\approx13$, whereas wall-solvent attraction lowers it to $\approx3.4$. This comparison shows that the wall-solvent interaction controls most of the enhancement. As the pore widens, $\mathcal{O}_\mathrm{B}$ decreases toward unity. In bulk and in nanopores alike, the solubility of poorly soluble species should be obtained from ensemble averages rather than from grand-potential minima.
items.authors: Russell Kajouri, Adyant Agrawal, Philipp St\"ark, Alexander Schlaich, Christian Holm

items.title: First-fracture kinetics in periodic chains: from free-energy landscapes and dynamical recrossing to absolute rates
items.abstract: The nearly collinear configuration of highly stretched polymer chains before fracture motivates one-dimensional models. At fixed extension, stretching one bond redistributes length among the others, coupling rupture to the whole chain. In this work, I develop a framework for fracture-healing rates in periodic Morse chains, combining deterministic theories, equilibrium simulations and a quasi-deterministic approach using equilibrium fluxes and barrier-top trajectories. Constrained-partition calculations closely reproduce simulated populations and intact-state tensions. An intact-reservoir potential of mean force (PMF) supplies the first-fracture surface probability, while recrossing corrects the attempt flux without a rate-fitted prefactor. Independent rate tests identify an operational chain-length boundary for accurate two-state kinetics; failed-return durations decrease relative to population relaxation as chains grow. Kramers-Grote-Hynes (KGH), nonlinear reactive-flux and equilibrium rates show excellent agreement in this regime. KGH predicts rates away from coexistence and a chain-dependent local activation length dominated by the barrier response. Rates decrease approximately exponentially before declining more gently for longer chains: barrier growth dominates, additional fracture sites partly compensate, and transmission varies more weakly. Beyond coexistence, long chains can fracture practically irreversibly because healing becomes too rare to observe. Projected committor crossings, where the configuration-averaged probability of reaching the fractured core first is one half, lie near site-PMF maxima, although configurations at equal bond length retain different fracture probabilities. Multiple fractures remain negligible near coexistence through at least $N=50$. The framework could supply state-dependent rates to mesoscopic fracture models of polymer networks.
items.authors: Aristotelis P. Sgouros

items.title: Can Universal Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials Capture Small Polarons? A Geometry-Based Benchmark in Transition-Metal Oxides
items.abstract: Small polarons, formed when excess electrons become localized through lattice distortions, play a critical role in charge transport, catalysis, and degradation processes in transition-metal (TM) oxides. Whether universal machine-learning interatomic potentials (uMLIPs), which lack explicit electronic degrees of freedom, can describe them remains unclear. Here, we investigate H-induced electron localization across a range of TM oxides using a geometric descriptor based on TM-O bond-length expansion (Z-score) to identify polaronic distortions. We find that uMLIPs exhibit varying degrees of electron localization, from delocalized states to metastable small polarons, with their behavior strongly dependent on the training data and treatment of electronic correlations. In particular, the absence of Hubbard U corrections for specific TM cations in the training data leads to electron delocalization, in contrast to DFT+U predictions. Although some uMLIPs reproduce polaron hopping barriers during coupled proton-polaron transfer, all of them fail to stabilize spatially separated polaron-donor configurations, instead favoring localization near the H dopant.
items.authors: Vladislav Korostelev, Pjotrs \v{Z}guns, Konstantin Klyukin

items.title: Gas radiation and the gravity limit of flicker in a co-flowing hydrogen jet diffusion flame
items.abstract: Although weak at normal gravity, gas radiation sets the gravity at which a co-flowing hydrogen jet diffusion flame stops flickering. Flamelet-based simulations with unity Lewis numbers, which reproduce the flicker frequency measured by femtosecond coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering within 4%, are combined with local stability analysis. At one tenth of normal gravity, the adiabatic flame flickers, the radiating flame does not, and switching the emission off restores flicker. Radiation acts through two mechanisms that do not weaken at reduced gravity. The hot outer layer loses buoyancy in proportion to the gas residence time, and a disturbance that displaces the flame also displaces its emission, which damps the disturbance on the lean flank (displaced-emission damping). Freezing the radiative source, which removes only its response to disturbances, slows the downstream recession of the oscillation more than tenfold. Both mechanisms slow the upstream spreading of disturbances. This spreading, competing with the co-flow, sets the onset location and the critical co-flow. Without radiation, the spreading speed scales with the square root of gravity; its radiative reduction does not. At reduced gravity, the flicker limit therefore becomes a straight line relating the square root of the co-flow Froude number to a radiation number, the ratio of buoyant to radiative time scales. The calibrated line places the critical gravity for the experimental co-flow at 0.13 times normal gravity, 2.6 times the adiabatic value. It correctly predicted whether two further flames keep flickering. Beyond the limit, transient wave packets can mimic flicker throughout a short drop-tower test.
items.authors: Tianfang Xie, Meng Wang

items.title: A grand potential for molten-salt electrochemical phase diagrams from first principles
items.abstract: The clean-energy transition is driving unprecedented demand for metals, whose extraction is among the largest industrial sources of carbon emissions. Molten-salt electrolysis offers a path toward carbon-free production of aluminum, iron, titanium, and critical metals. However, corrosive operating conditions and complex, multicomponent feedstocks make experimental development costly and challenging. Here, we introduce a first-principles framework for constructing electrochemical phase diagrams of multicomponent systems to accelerate electrode and electrolyte design and guide the selection of compatible materials and operating conditions for electrochemical cells. We derive a grand potential that generates these diagrams at scale, and supply free energies using first-principles data obtained through a fine-tuned foundation machine-learned interatomic potential. For silicon in molten CaCl$_2$, the construction not only recovers the experimental diagram when using the first-principles framework on a limited set of structures, but also predicts further domains when extended to a larger set of crystal structures. Finally, we demonstrate the predictive power of the approach by screening ten alkali and alkaline-earth halide electrolytes for aluminum electrowinning. Three thermodynamic criteria identify NaF, where cryolite emerges as the stable aluminum-bearing phase, recovering the chemistry that Hall and H\'eroult established empirically in 1886. The framework provides a first-principles basis for selecting compatible electrodes, electrolytes, and operating conditions toward low-carbon metal production from complex source materials.
items.authors: Lorenzo Bastonero, Lucio Colombi Ciacchi, Nicola Marzari

items.title: A Parameter-Free Reference Hamiltonian for Tight-Binding Vanadium Oxides
items.abstract: Density-functional tight binding has yet to yield a transferable description of vanadium oxides; for the standard second-order construction and the tested cells, we demonstrate that two of its approximations deviate by electron volts and offset each other in the band-index centroid separation between the V 3d and O 2p bands: the neutral two-centre reference omits electron-volt environmental terms, whereas the Mulliken charge model assigns the compact V 3d shell less than half of the self-consistent potential shift observed in PBE. Instead, we build a tight-binding model where the reference Hamiltonian derives from superposed neutral atoms, the full PBE exchange-correlation potential and frozen-core orthogonality, without adjustable terms, and where the orbital-resolved charge response employs three screening factors obtained from PBE linear response and an unscreened Coulomb range. Against the primary PAW reference, the reference energy at fixed geometry and the stated numerical settings matches the plane-wave Harris-Foulkes energy differences of VO2, exhibiting signed deviations of +2.6 meV/atom for M1 relative to rutile (an energy difference of 92 meV/atom) and +6.2 and -5.2 meV/atom under 3% volume compression and expansion; meanwhile, the charge response captures 21 of 22 fitted and all 8 held-out matched PBE responses within tolerance, providing the V 3d shell with nearly the same self-consistent shift as PBE (-3.89 versus -3.92 eV in rutile). The convexity of the spinless model at fixed geometry prevents it from spontaneously differentiating symmetry-equivalent sites under the symmetries respected by its implemented operators and sampling, so within this model such differentiation in the Magn\'eli phases must arise from electron-lattice coupling or an explicit spin or correlation term.
items.authors: Jun-qiang Lu

items.title: Organisation and aggregation of calcium carbonate ions in water via molecular simulation
items.abstract: Crystallisation of calcium carbonate (CaCO$_3$) in aqueous solutions is essential for carbon dioxide sequestration and the sustainable production of calcium carbonate materials, which are widely used in industry and increasingly explored for novel applications. While crystallisation is often analysed within the framework of classical nucleation theory, CaCO$_3$ and other ionic crystals often form through amorphous precursor phases, motivating the need for alternative descriptions. In this work, we investigate the relationship between the formation of the first CaCO$_3$ coordination sphere, a fundamental unit of local ordering, and ionic aggregation using two complementary simulation approaches: on-the-fly probability-enhanced sampling (OPES) and asynchronous and infinite-swap replica exchange transition interface sampling ($\infty$RETIS). OPES was used to explore free-energy landscapes, whereas $\infty$RETIS was used to determine reaction kinetics. We studied systems at two levels of supersaturation, between which the formation of the first coordination sphere exhibited distinct kinetic behaviour. These differences were found to be linked to concentration-dependent ionic aggregation. At lower concentration, aggregation remains limited, whereas higher concentration promotes extensive spinodal-like aggregation. For both concentrations, the first coordination sphere forms within the pre-formed clusters through one of two distinct pathways: either within a cluster close to the minimum size required for its formation, or within larger amorphous aggregates whose size and structure depend on concentration. The coexistence of these pathways at both levels of supersaturation reveals the multifaceted nature of early-stage CaCO$_3$ crystallisation and highlights the importance of differentiating ionic aggregation and organisation.
items.authors: Elizaveta Sidler, Rita S Dias, Raffaela Cabriolu

items.title: Collision inside an atom: quantum ion-atom dynamics
items.abstract: Rydberg atoms occupy a central role in quantum science; their loosely bound outer electron gives rise to properties that enable quantum information processing1 or the formation of exotic molecular bonds2. Beyond these roles, they have been proposed as a neutral platform for the observation of quantum effects in collisions and reactions of the ionic core with neutral particles3, 4, a long-standing goal of ion-based chemistry and physics. However, all of the experimental results so far could be explained using a classical description of the internuclear motion5. Here we demonstrate cold collisions inside a Rydberg helium atom, achieved by merging helium Rydberg and ground-state helium beams and imaging individual scattering events. We resolve the fully quantum-coherent motion and observe matter-wave diffraction and tunnelling-driven shape resonances down to collision energies of 90 mK. In the case of identical helium nuclei, we demonstrate a new regime of identical-particle Mott interference6, where quantum statistics begin to govern the total scattering cross section. For distinct isotopes, we show the breakdown of the Born-Oppenheimer approximation and benchmark parameter-free, state-of-the-art theory. We directly measure the helium isotope ionization-energy difference to be 15.0 +/- 0.1 K. Our experiments establish Rydberg atoms as a platform for the direct observation of quantum dynamics with a general class of ions, atoms and molecules.
items.authors: Arijit Das, Yufeng Wang, Marcin Welter, Karl Horn, Dawid D\k{a}browski, Micha{\l} Przybytek, Julia Narevicius, Micha{\l} Tomza, Edvardas Narevicius

items.title: Ionic gradients shape the spatial organization and dynamics of supramolecular polymers
items.abstract: Living supramolecular materials such as microtubules and actin filaments assemble and function in dynamic, heterogeneous environments, subject to chemical concentration gradients. Their rapid and precise response to such gradients---via aggregation, disassembly, or autonomous motion---underlies the fine spatiotemporal control typical of living systems. Reproducing such responsiveness in synthetic materials is a central challenge in materials science and requires a molecular-level understanding of how gradients couple to supramolecular structure and dynamics, which remains difficult to access experimentally. To this end, we combine implicit-solvent coarse-grained molecular dynamics (MD) with the constant chemical potential MD (C${\mu}$MD) technique to investigate, at molecular resolution, the coupling of two prototypical supramolecular polymer models with externally imposed ionic concentration gradients. Despite their contrasting responses to homogeneous ionic conditions, both systems undergo pronounced spatial reorganization under the gradient, generating regions of locally enhanced supramolecular activity that are inaccessible to homogeneous systems with the same overall content of self-assembling species. Crucially, the local supramolecular dynamics is largely determined by the local concentrations, consistent with the formation of local quasi-equilibria: this direct connection between spatial composition and supramolecular activity emerges as a common governing principle across the two models. These findings shed light on the spatially complex supramolecular response that can be triggered by chemical gradients, and show how a single gradient simulation can encode this response across a continuous range of local chemical environments, thus providing a general strategy to investigate and design materials operating under spatially heterogeneous conditions.
items.authors: Claudio Perego, Annalisa Cardellini, Andrea Tagliabue, Giovanni M. Pavan

items.title: A Transferable Machine-Learned Potential Enabling Large-Scale Copper-Carbon Simulations from Equilibrium to Extreme Conditions
items.abstract: Cu-C materials and interfaces are central to diamond thermal management, metallization, graphene growth and carbon-coating technologies, but atomistic simulations across these applications require a potential that describes metallic Cu, diverse carbon bonding, heterogeneous Cu-C interactions and close atomic encounters. Here we develop NEP-CuC, a transferable neuroevolution potential trained on a dataset of 2,727 uniformly relabelled configurations selected from a heterogeneous Cu-C candidate pool. Disagreement within an ensemble of five independently trained models provides an internal indicator of model sensitivity. A Ziegler-Biersack-Littmark (ZBL) correction describes short-range nuclear repulsion, while a runtime D3(BJ) correction supplements dispersion-sensitive calculations. Tests on source-derived held-out and independent external datasets, together with structural, elastic, defect, interfacial, vibrational and finite-temperature transport benchmarks, establish broad but property-dependent physical fidelity across elemental Cu, diverse carbon environments and heterogeneous Cu-C configurations. Large-scale simulations of amorphous-carbon formation and orientation-dependent shock compression of Cu further test transferability under strongly non-equilibrium conditions. For Cu/diamond interfaces, the same potential describes deposition, annealing and tensile response: preparation history leaves persistent differences in interphase structure, while the mean peak nominal tensile stress at 500 K decreases from $12.35\pm0.71$ to $6.65\pm0.98$ GPa as the incident Cu energy during the initial deposition stage increases from 1 to 50 eV. NEP-CuC provides an atomistic framework for linking processing, interfacial structure and physical response across Cu-C systems, with direct relevance to Cu/diamond thermal-management interfaces, diamond metallization and non-equilibrium Cu-C processing.
items.authors: Feiyu Zhou, Wei Qiu, Yan Chen, Jiahui Liu, Yilun Liu, Shengying Yue, Penghua Ying

items.title: Extending the mean first-passage-time formalism to the reconstruction of high free-energy barriers: A top-start approach
items.abstract: Rare events, such as crystal nucleation in mildly supercooled liquids, are characterized by waiting times that can be much longer than the timescale of the underlying microscopic dynamics. The mean first-passage time (MFPT) formalism [J. Wedekind and D. Reguera, J. Phys. Chem. B 112, 11060 (2008)] provides a route to reconstruct one-dimensional free-energy profiles from the MFPT and steady-state distribution measured along a reaction coordinate, but conventional implementations become inefficient for sufficiently high barriers because spontaneous crossings are rarely observed. We introduce a "top-start" extension that initiates trajectories near the barrier top and reconstructs the free-energy profile from their subsequent evolution away from the barrier toward lower-free-energy regions. We establish the equivalence between the top-start and two-region constructions using a Markov-chain transition-matrix formulation. We validate the method using one-dimensional random-walk simulations across low, medium, and high free-energy barriers, with transition-matrix calculations providing an exact benchmark for the corresponding discretized models. The top-start reconstruction remains accurate in the high-barrier regime where conventional MFPT sampling becomes prohibitively inefficient.
items.authors: Ying Jiang, Ivan Saika-Voivod

items.title: DeepHartree: A Poisson-Coupled Neural Field for One-Shot Density Functional Theory
items.abstract: Density functional theory (DFT) with linear combinations of atomic orbitals (LCAO) is costly because of Coulomb-matrix construction and self-consistent-field (SCF) iterations. We introduce DeepHartree, a Poisson-coupled neural field that connects continuous real-space prediction to LCAO electronic structure. An E(3)-equivariant network predicts the Hartree potential, and the Poisson equation yields the electron density. Atom-centred Gaussian fields resolve near-nuclear structure, and a molecular correction enforces the electron count. Analytical Gaussian integrals and numerical quadrature assemble the Kohn-Sham matrix; one diagonalization yields orbital estimates and a density matrix for energy evaluation and SCF initialization. Mean molecular weighted normalized mean absolute density errors (wNMAEs) are 0.110% for QM9 and 0.199% for VQM24 on PySCF level-0 grids, rising to 1.366% and 2.218% on level-3 grids. Models trained on def2-SVP densities transfer to def2-TZVP and def2-QZVP without retraining, retaining total-energy accuracy and occupied-subspace agreement. A Hybrid method combines finite differences, first-order automatic differentiation, analytical integrals, and multilevel quadrature for near-linear density-matrix construction in alkanes and PEG chains. Excluding grid construction, the density-matrix build for a 1004-atom PEG chain is 8.75-fold faster than full automatic differentiation and 7.34-fold faster than converged GPU4PySCF SCF. Without fine-tuning, the QM9 model achieves a total-energy MAE of 9.437 meV per atom on 1,000 larger OE62 molecules. DeepHartree initialization reduces mean QM9 SCF iterations by 15.3-15.6% across the three basis sets and total SCF time by 12.9% for a 620-atom organic cage, including initialization. These results support continuous electrostatic fields as an accurate, scalable interface between machine learning and LCAO DFT.
items.authors: Jiankun Wu, Jinming Fan, Chao Qian, Shaodong Zhou

items.title: pANO-F12: An atomic natural orbital-inspired route to more compact basis sets for F12 explicitly correlated methods
items.abstract: Explicitly correlated methods such as MP2-F12 and CCSD(F12*) exhibit much faster basis set convergence (asymptotically $\propto L^{-7}$, with L the highest angular momentum) than orbital-only approaches. Yet it has been pointed out that cc-pVnZ-F12 basis sets themselves are substantially larger than the corresponding cc-pVnZ, and specifically that cc-pVDZ-F12 is the size of cc-pVTZ. One way to generate compact basis sets in an orbital-only context are Atomic Natural Orbital (ANO) basis sets [J. Alml\"of and P. R. Taylor, JCP 86, 4070 (1987)]. However, obtaining the required first-order reduced density matrix while properly accounting for the F12 geminal is problematic. In this work, we show that an energy minimization-based contraction process under linear independence constraints yields `pseudo-ANO' (pANO) basis sets that are functionally equivalent in quality. Subsequently, we apply this recipe to obtain pANO-F12 basis sets from the same elements, then validate them for several thermochemical benchmarks and for the hypersensitive out-of-plane vibrations of benzene. We show that, unlike cc-pVnZ-F12, pANO-F12 exhibits the familiar shell structure seen in cc-pVnZ and ANO basis sets, and that pANO-F12 offers a route to more compact F12 basis sets more amenable to medium-sized systems, especially in conjunction with localized pair natural orbital approaches. Overall, the pANO approach is most beneficial for the smaller double-and triple-zeta basis sets, offering either superior performance to cc-pVnZ-F12 at same cost, or similar performance at lower cost.
items.authors: Vladimir Fishman, Jan M. L. Martin

items.title: Transferable machine learning of excited-state dynamics with extremal pooling
items.abstract: Photochemical processes govern phenomena ranging from solar energy conversion and atmospheric chemistry to vision and photosynthesis. Accurate simulation of these processes requires modeling excited-state potential energy surfaces, often involving chemical reactions, tasks that remain computationally prohibitive for extended systems and long timescales using traditional \textit{ab initio} methods. Machine learning interatomic potentials have revolutionized ground-state simulations, but their extension to excited states faces fundamental challenges: standard architectures assume energy extensivity, an assumption that fails for excited states. Here, we present a size-intensive machine-learning framework for excited-state dynamics based on \textit{extremal pooling} of predicted atomic HOMO and LUMO contributions. Trained exclusively on excitations energies and forces, the architecture learns interpretable atomic-level contributions that encode physical information on the extent of electron localization. We demonstrate this framework on the photoexcited solvated electron in liquid water, a paradigmatic problem in radiation chemistry leading to competing pathways involving both hydrogen-atom dissociation and proton-coupled electron transfer. The model not only reproduces the relevant chain of reactions and product species that form during excitation, but also allows one to explicitly study the dynamics of the solvated electron in quantitative agreement with previously reported Restricted Open-Shell Kohn-Sham calculations, while enabling excited-state simulations of periodic systems at length and time scales inaccessible to the reference electronic-structure method. This work establishes a general strategy for machine learning-driven excited-state dynamics applicable to diverse photochemical systems, from molecular chromophores in solution to extended condensed-phase systems.
items.authors: Cesare Malosso, Wei Bin How, Gonzalo D\'iaz Mir\'on, Ali Hassanali, Michele Ceriotti

items.title: Chiral Temporal Structures in Molecular Rotational Dynamics
items.abstract: We introduce chiral rotational wavepackets: coherent superpositions of a few low-lying rotational states of a molecule for which the expectation value of a molecular axis traces a three-dimensional chiral trajectory in the laboratory frame. The handedness is a dynamical property of the quantum state rather than of the equilibrium structure, and we show that it can be imprinted on linear rotors as well as on spherical and symmetric tops. We derive the action of space inversion, time reversal, and their product on such wavepackets in the Wigner $D^J_{MK}$ basis, and define the rotational enantiomers of a given wavepacket. To quantify their handedness we introduce two derivative-based pseudoscalar measures: a geometrical measure built from the curvature and torsion of the trajectory, which is even under time reversal, and a dynamical measure, which is odd under time reversal. The latter is shown to be proportional to the geodesic curvature of the trajectory projected onto the unit sphere, which links it, via the Gauss--Bonnet theorem, to the solid angle enclosed by the projected trajectory and to the parallel-transport holonomy of a molecule-fixed vector. Finally we show that a nonzero geometrical measure is a sufficient condition for the wavepacket to exhibit true chirality through its orientation trajectory in the sense of Barron.
items.authors: A. G. L\"ohr, O. Smirnova, M. Mirahmadi

items.title: Crystallisation kinetics of supercooled liquid palladium
items.abstract: In this study, we employ classical molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to investigate the crystallisation kinetics of supercooled liquid palladium and relate the results to time-resolved X-ray diffraction measurements on rapidly quenched Pd thin films. Crystal nucleation and growth rates are determined over the temperature range $700$--$1150~\mathrm{K}$ ($0.38$--$0.65 T_{\mathrm{m}}$) by analysing the evolution of the microstructure during the liquid-to-crystal transition. The self-diffusion coefficient of Pd, obtained from the atomic mean-squared displacement, follows Arrhenius behaviour over the investigated temperature range, with an activation energy of $467(6)~\mathrm{meV/atom}$, consistent with available data for supercooled liquid metals. The steady-state homogeneous nucleation rate exhibits a maximum of approximately $4 \times 10^{35}~\mathrm{m^{-3} s^{-1}}$ near $0.5 T_{\mathrm{m}}$. Crystal growth occurs at velocities of the order of metres per second, with a temperature dependence consistent with diffusion-limited Wilson-Frenkel kinetics rather than the collision-limited regime. Based on multiple statistically independent simulations, a time-temperature-transformation (TTT) diagram for crystallisation onset is constructed. The TTT curve exhibits a nose near $0.5 T_{\mathrm{m}}$ and $100~\mathrm{ps}$, corresponding to a critical cooling rate for vitrification on the order of $10^{13}~\mathrm{K s^{-1}}.$ The simulations reproduce the crystallisation onset time and temperature observed in time-resolved X-ray diffraction experiments on optically molten Pd thin films quenched at $5 \times 10^{11}~\mathrm{K s^{-1}}.$ These results indicate that homogeneous, rather than heterogeneous, nucleation governs the achievable supercooling in the experimentally studied films.
items.authors: Zuzanna Kostera, Przemyslaw Dziegielewski, Christian Bressler, Wojciech Gawelda, Konstantinos Georgarakis, Dmitry Khakhulin, Oleksii I. Liubchenko, Adam Olczak, Angel Rodriguez-Fernandez, Ryszard Sobierajski, Klaus Sokolowski-Tinten, Peihao Sun, Robert W. E. van de Kruijs, Hazem Yousef, Peter Zalden, Jerzy Antonowicz

items.title: In-Situ TEM Observation of Solid-State Phase Evolution in High-Entropy Alloy Nanoparticles
items.abstract: The emergence of new materials has gone beyond conventional design principles. Among them are high entropy alloys (HEAs), in which multiple metallic elements coexist within a single unit cell. In this case, each atomic position in a solid material has a different chemical environment, leading to configurational entropy as high as that in the fully random or melted state, which has been frozen to a solid solution. However, the behaviour of such alloy systems at pre-melting temperatures is largely unknown, where atoms gain sufficient mobility and time to rearrange, leading to an enthalpic rather than an entropic interplay. This study demonstrated the phase transformation of HEA nanoclusters (CoCrFeMnNi) under high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) at different temperatures, including room temperature (RT), 550 {\deg}C, and 850 {\deg}C. The clustered nanoparticles coarsen into larger clusters, accompanied by compositional heterogeneity due to surface and lattice diffusion. This experimental finding of atomic mobility was further corroborated using molecular dynamics, which provides a detailed mechanistic description.
items.authors: Nirmal Kumar Katiyar, Noorbasha Bhavani Sai, Guilherme Gurian Dariani, Douglas S. Galvao, Pulickel M. Ajayan, Pedro Alves da Silva Autreto, Sriram Vijayan, Chandra Sekhar Tiwary

items.title: Anisotropic pressure response of thermal conductivity in crystalline polytetrafluoroethylene
items.abstract: Compression can change thermal conductivity differently along polymer chains and across them by altering phonon velocities and lifetimes. We examine this directional response in orthorhombic Form III polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) at calculated pressures of 1.503, 3.452, and 5.056 GPa, using first-principles harmonic and cubic force constants within the single-mode relaxation-time approximation (SMRTA). At 100, 200, and 300 K, the chain-axis conductivity decreases at every pressure step. Between 3.452 and 5.056 GPa, both transverse components recover: at 300 K they increase by 23.7% and 13.7%, while the longitudinal conductivity decreases by 14.5%. An exact factorization separates the conductivity into a heat-capacity--velocity factor and a weighted effective lifetime. The transverse recovery follows from larger heat-capacity-weighted squared velocities, consistent with stiffer interchain restoring forces. Along the chains, shorter effective lifetimes dominate, and both conductivity-weighted Normal and Umklapp rates increase at 300 K. Comparing the same cubic force-constant blocks at all three pressures, we find that interchain coupling is already substantial at 1.503 GPa and increases under compression.
items.authors: Maissa Adi, Jamal Abou Haibeh, Samuel Huberman

items.title: Emergence of quantum transport in SnTe films upon structural refinement
items.abstract: Topological crystalline insulators are distinguished from the conventional Z2 topological insulators by crystalline symmetry protection of the surface states. Quantitative characterization of these states requires magneto-transport measurements from which the phase coherence length and number of independent coherent channels can be extracted. Here we report such measurements on textured thin films of SnTe grown on Bi2Te3 buffered c-plane sapphire (Al2O3) by pulsed laser ablation. A post deposition annealing protocol was implemented to control the crystallographic texture, which reveals improved crystallinity and enhanced epitaxial alignment along the [111] direction in films annealed at elevated temperatures. The higher carrier density and lower resistivity seen in films annealed at 100 oC are suggestive of Sn vacancies which act as native acceptor defects, while films annealed at 200 oC approach the 1:1 stoichiometry. The magnetoresistance of all samples at T 20 K, the MR is small and positive, and deviates from conventional Kohler scaling. An approximate collapse of the MR curves between 50 and 250 K is obtained using an empirical temperature-dependent scaling factor, indicating that changes in the Hall-derived carrier density alone cannot account for the observed scaling behavior. These results demonstrate that post growth annealing strongly influences the interplay between stoichiometry, crystallinity, and coherent transport in SnTe thin films.
items.authors: Shrinkhala Sharma, Rabindra Basnet, Thomas Parker, Afolabi Akinfaderin, Alexander Samokhvalov, Rajeswari Kolagani, Ramesh C. Budhani

items.title: Benchmarking machine-learning interatomic potentials using classical force fields
items.abstract: We propose a rational comparison between several well-known machine-learning interatomic potentials (linear atomic cluster expansion, the Behler-Parrinello high-dimensional neural network potential, and the graph neural network-based MACE potential) by testing their performance for fitting classical potentials such as the Lennard-Jones and Stillinger-Weber potential. With this we assess their advantages and limitations regarding several aspects: varying training dataset size, robustness to noise, carbon footprint, as well as the ability to reproduce the radial distribution function as an example observable. Overall the MACE models are shown to most accurately reproduce the potential energy surface, with little sign of overfitting, but at a significant computational cost, highlighting important questions regarding the choice of models in computational materials science.
items.authors: Johannes Sandberg, Genevi\`eve Dusson, Julien Lam

items.title: A Solution-Processed Ti/Pt/NiOx/Ag RRAM Device with Multiple Forming-Free Non-Volatile Intermediate States
items.abstract: Artificial neural networks (ANN) implemented on crossbar arrays of non-volatile synaptic devices are known to consume much less energy compared to that implemented on conventional computing units. Solution-processed resistive random-access memory (RRAM) devices based on transition-metal oxides are suitable as such synaptic devices because of their cheap and easy fabrication method, stability, and suitable memristive properties. Here, in NiO-based RRAM devices with Ti/Pt as the bottom electrode and Ag as the top electrode (NiO layer deposited through solution processing), we experimentally report forming-free binary switching between a high resistance state (HRS) and a low resistance state (LRS) as well as forming-free pulse-driven modulation (long-term potentiation (LTP), long-term depression (LTD)) through 30 intermediate synaptic states between HRS and LRS (around 5-bit synaptic weight resolution). Many of these states are measured to be stable at least up to 1000 seconds confirming their non-volatility and their utility in storage of synaptic weights for ANN crossbar arrays. On the contrary, most prior experimental reports (including reports both on solution-processing-based and sputtering-based RRAM devices) require forming to exhibit non-volatility. Avoiding forming reduces variability, eliminates the need for high voltage pulses, and makes the crossbar array design simpler. Further, we confirm the presence of oxygen vacancies in our materials stack using X-ray photo-electron spectroscopy (XPS). Finally, we show successful data classification on MNIST and CIFAR-10 data sets using a multi-layer perceptron (MLP) model and a convolution neural network (CNN) model respectively, where the synaptic weight updates of these ANN models are calibrated against the experimentally measured LTP-LTD characteristics of the NiO RRAM devices.
items.authors: Abhrajit Roy, Chopali Chanchal Sahu, Rudraksh Sangore, Raman Hissariya, Poulomi Chakrabarty, Harsh Roniyar, Merlyne De Souza, Debanjan Bhowmik

items.title: Atoms that Matter: Largest Materials Datasets Are 99% Redundant, and Local Chemistry Can Guide the Required 1%
items.abstract: General-purpose machine-learning force fields (MLFFs) for materials are now trained on the order of $100$ million structures, assuming transferability requires such scale. We test this premise on OMat24, the largest available materials dataset, by training MACE models on subsets of $6.5$ million atoms, less than $1\%$ of OMat24, selected in three complementary ways: at random, by latent-space clustering of a pretrained MLFF (DIRECT), and by a new model-free method maximizing the diversity of discrete, interpretable local environments (EnvTok). All three models approach the full-data reference MACE-OMAT-0 model to within a few tens of $\mathrm{meV}/\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$ in forces, and remain close to or exceed it on formation energies, elastic moduli, heat capacities, Li$^{+}$ migration barriers, and molecular-dynamics stability up to $3000\,$K and $500\,$GPa. This near-independence from the selection strategy shows that chemical environment diversity, not size, defines OMat24's information content: the remaining $99\%$ of structures are largely redundant. Broad sampling of chemical space thus remains essential, but reference labels are needed only for structurally and chemically distinct configurations. Using atomic positions and species, optionally augmented by magnetic moments, EnvTok identifies these before any labelling or training, yielding compact, architecture-independent datasets. This hundredfold reduction makes hybrid-DFT or higher-level relabelling of general-purpose training sets feasible, and frees computational budget for extending environmental coverage and multi-fidelity learning.
items.authors: Evgeny Moerman, Igor Poltavsky, Anton Charkin-Gorbulin, Alexandre Tkatchenko

items.title: Large Out-of-plane Polarization in Two-dimensional Bi2O3 Monolayers Predicted by an AI-driven Inverse-design Workflow
items.abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) polar oxides with built-in electric fields offer promising opportunities for nanoscale electronics, optoelectronics, and surface charge engineering. However, their discovery remains challenging due to the enormous structural complexity of nonlayered oxide networks. Here, we combine inverse structural design with a machine-learning interatomic potential and first-principles calculations to explore 2D oxide configurations. Using Bi2O3 as a representative system, we identify two previously unreported polar monolayers with tetragonal and orthorhombic symmetries. Both structures exhibit vertically separated Bi and O sublayers, giving rise to pronounced intrinsic polarity with Berry-phase 2D polarizations of 34.12 and 37.15 pC/m, respectively. Notably, the o-Bi2O3 monolayer exhibits one of the largest reported out-of-plane polarizations among 2D oxides. Both monolayers exhibit dynamical stability, finite-temperature structural integrity, and wide band gaps (~3.8 eV). The large polarization originates from dimensionality-induced reconstruction of the nonlayered Bi-O network, which breaks local coordination symmetry and produces out-of-plane charge redistribution, while the stereochemically active Bi 6s2 lone pair further favors asymmetric Bi-O bonding. These findings suggest dimensionality-induced local-coordination symmetry breaking as a promising design motif for high-polarization 2D oxides, and demonstrate the utility of combining inverse design with machine-learning-assisted screening to explore unconventional polar phases in nonlayered oxide networks.
items.authors: Hongmei Tan, Jing Zhang, Shan Gao, Yueyu Zhang, Xiangmei Duan

items.title: Fluctuation-based evaluation of thermal conductivity using deviational phonon Monte Carlo simulations
items.abstract: We develop a fluctuation based Monte Carlo method for evaluating thermal conductivity within the phonon Boltzmann transport equation (BTE) framework. Starting from the energy based variance reduced formulation of the BTE, we derive a relation between the spatial spreading of deviational phonon energy and the macroscopic heat conduction equation. The resulting formulation expresses thermal conductivity in terms of the mean square displacement of deviational phonon particles, without imposing thermal reservoirs. Consequently, thermal conductivity along multiple directions can be evaluated from a single simulation. The method is demonstrated for crystalline silicon at room temperature in bulk, square nanowires, and anisotropic polycrystalline nanostructures. The calculated thermal conductivities agree with theoretical predictions, including the size dependence induced by phonon boundary scattering and the mode-resolved contributions. For anisotropic polycrystalline structures, the method simultaneously resolves the directional thermal conductivities and captures their dependence on grain morphology. These results demonstrate the validity of the proposed fluctuation-based approach for evaluating thermal conductivity across different transport regimes and structural configurations.
items.authors: Takuma Hori, Yuzuho Oki

items.title: A Fisher-Geometric Approach to Supercell Pair Distribution Function Refinement
items.abstract: Refining atomistic supercells against powder pair distribution functions (PDFs) requires optimizing many coupled atomic coordinates using a much smaller set of radial measurements. Reverse-mode differentiation makes gradients accessible for large systems, but standard first-order optimizers do not explicitly use coupled PDF sensitivities to precondition coordinate updates. We introduce a matrix-free, Fisher-geometric approach that pulls the information metric of the observation likelihood back onto atomic coordinates. The resulting update weights collective displacements according to their PDF response and experimental uncertainty. Under isotropic damping, the update is obtained by solving a damped linear system over $M$ PDF channels, using automatic differentiation to evaluate Jacobian--vector and vector--Jacobian products without constructing the full Jacobian or coordinate curvature matrix. For Gaussian measurement errors, the update recovers classical Levenberg--Marquardt refinement while avoiding dense coordinate-space factorization. The same computational framework accommodates correlated Gaussian errors and robust likelihood-based updates. This approach combines likelihood-aware collective updates with matrix-free backpropagation for direct second-order refinement of large atomistic supercells.
items.authors: Dawei Wang
