We find markedly different peak electronic temperatures in the two graphene layers, even though their subsequent cooling dynamics are very similar. We attribute this to an ultrafast interlayer redistribution of electronic energy, driven by an interlayer electric field that arises from the different doping in the layers.
items.authors: Gianmarco Gatti, Anders S. Mortensen, Zhihao Jiang, Alfred J. H. Jones, Gesa-R. Siemann, Thomas S. Nielsen, S{\o}ren Ulstrup, Naina Kushwaha, Bruce Weaver, Yu Zhang, Emma Springate, Charlotte E. Sanders, Vibha Reddy, Ulrich Starke, Philip Hofmann

items.title: Unexpected stabilization of a single-$q$ charge density wave in pristine 1T-TiSe$_2$
items.abstract: Over the past decade, studies revisiting the classical charge-density-wave system 1T-TiSe$_2$, long understood to host the $2 \times 2$ triple-$q$ order with equivalent subcomponents, have suggested that these subcomponents may not be identical, challenging a 50-year-old paradigm. Here, we demonstrate not only that these subcomponents are non-identical but also that they develop sequentially rather than simultaneously. By tracking folded-band features, angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy reveals that a unidirectional $2 \times 1$ single-$q$ order stabilizes first, while the other two components emerge sequentially at lower temperatures, completing the triple-$q$ phase. Our free-energy analysis explains this hierarchy through repulsive coupling among the three subcomponents, as supported by first-principles calculations incorporating phonon anharmonicity. Consequently, the three subcomponents are inequivalent in both phase and amplitude. These results reconcile reported symmetry breaking and differing characteristic temperatures and establish a framework in which ostensibly simple, high-symmetry charge-density order emerges from temperature-dependent competition and cooperation among inequivalent subcomponents.
items.authors: Kimoon Higashihira Han, Dongju Hwang, Dongsin Kim, Yeojin Ahn, Jaehun Cha, Seonggeon Gim, Gyubin Lee, Mingi Jho, Chan-young Lim, Sae Hee Ryu, Chris Jozwiak, Aaron Bostwick, Eli Rotenberg, Jonathan D. items.title: Superexchange coupling between a dilute Gd3+ probe and orphan spins in a valence-bond glass
items.abstract: The valence-bond-glass state of the 4d^1 double perovskite Ba2YMoO6 combines Mo^5+ singlets with residual paramagnetic "orphan" spins whose coupling is hard to reach with bulk probes. We probe them by electron paramagnetic resonance of a dilute Gd^3+ ion on the Y^3+ site via broadband coplanar-waveguide transmission at 5 K. The isostructural nonmagnetic niobate Ba2YNbO6, doped with the same Gd^3+ probe, is a fixed-lattice control. The Gd^3+ linewidth nearly doubles in the magnetic host. Dipolar coupling to the sparse orphans is nearly an order of magnitude too weak; the excess is instead reproduced by a transferred f-d superexchange of J ~ 0.2 K, so the width is a static measure of orphan-spin coupling. The half-field (Delta m_S = +/-2) satellite collapses in the magnetic host, a dynamical dephasing channel, while the unchanged g-factor marks a zero-mean random internal field. Together the two channels probe the coupling and dynamics of valence-bond-glass orphan spins.
items.authors: Patrick Colgan, Artur Solodovnyk, Jeremy P. Carlo, Scott Dietrich

items.title: Extreme Suppression of Thermal Conductivity in Monolayer Beryllene
items.abstract: We demonstrate an extreme suppression of thermal conductivity in monolayer beryllene through first-principles solutions of the phonon Boltzmann transport equation. While the fully converged three-phonon calculation predicts a room-temperature lattice thermal conductivity of 154.3 W/(m$\cdot$K), inclusion of four-phonon interactions suppresses it to 10.7 W/(m$\cdot$K), a reduction of more than 90\%. This exceptionally large reduction of the thermal conductivity is amongst the highest reported in two-dimensional materials. The microscopic origin of this breakdown is traced to the strong sensitivity of the low-frequency flexural ZA phonons to four-phonon scattering: mode-resolved scattering rates reveal a pronounced enhancement of ZA scattering, which substantially shortens their lifetimes and suppresses their dominant contribution to heat conduction. Moreover, the temperature dependence of the thermal conductivity changes from $\kappa\propto T^{-0.86}$ to $\kappa\propto T^{-1.38}$ upon inclusion of four-phonon processes. Our results establish $\alpha$-beryllene as an unusually strong case of four-phonon-controlled thermal transport amongst two-dimensional materials. These findings identify selective higher-order scattering of flexural phonons as a key mechanism for controlling thermal transport in strongly anharmonic low-dimensional systems.
items.authors: Sapta Sindhu Paul Chowdhury, Santosh Mogurampelly

items.title: Interplay of spin-phonon coupling in FeSe with pressure and isoelectronic (S/Te) substitution
items.abstract: In several studies, magnetism has been shown to strongly influence the properties of the iron chalcogenide compound \ce{FeSe}. In our previous work [Phys. Rev. Res. 6(4), 043154 (2024)], we demonstrated how the interplay between spin and orbital degrees of freedom governs the electronic structure and consequently shapes the magnetic phase diagram of \ce{FeSe} under external hydrostatic pressure. However, a comprehensive understanding of the phase diagram also requires investigating the role of lattice degrees of freedom (phonons) and their coupling to magnetism. In the present study, we examine how hydrostatic pressure and isoelectronic substitution affect the magnetic and lattice dynamical properties of \ce{FeSe} using Density Functional Theory calculations. Our lattice dynamics analysis reveals that different phonon modes exhibit distinct dependencies on the local magnetic moment across various magnetic phases. We further identify pressure- and magnetic-moment-dependent dynamical instabilities in specific magnetic configurations, highlighting the intricate coupling between structural and magnetic degrees of freedom in \ce{FeSe}. An investigation of spin-phonon coupling demonstrates the presence of strong magnetoelastic interactions affecting the prominent optical phonon modes: the Fe-derived $B_{1g}$ mode and the Se-derived $A_{1g}$ mode. Finally, we discuss the evolution of spin-phonon coupling under pressure and alloying in the context of its possible implications for emergent phases such as magnetism, nematicity, and superconductivity in \ce{FeSe}.
items.authors: Abyay Ghosh, Piotr Chudzinski, Myrta Gr\"uning

items.title: peaks: a Python package for analysis of angle-resolved photoemission and related spectroscopies
items.abstract: The electronic band structure, describing the motion and interactions of electrons in materials, dictates the electrical, optical, and thermodynamic properties of solids. Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) provides a direct experimental probe of such electronic band structures, and so is widely employed in the study of functional, quantum, and 2D materials. \texttt{peaks} (\textbf{P}ython \textbf{E}lectron spectroscopy \textbf{A}nalysis by \textbf{K}ing group @ \textbf{S}t Andrews) provides a Python package for advanced data analysis of ARPES and related spectroscopic data. It facilitates the fast visualisation and analysis of multi-dimensional datasets, allows for the complex data hierarchy typical to ARPES experiments, and supports lazy data loading and parallel processing, reflecting the ever-increasing data volumes used in ARPES. It is designed to be run in an interactive notebook environment, with extensive inline and pop-out GUI support for data visualisation.
items.authors: Phil D. C. King, Brendan Edwards, Shu Mo, Tommaso Antonelli, Edgar Abarca Morales, Lewis Hart, Liam Trzaska

items.title: Observation of a Novel Charge Density Wave Superstructure in Monolayer 1T-$VS_{2}$ at Room Temperature and its Evolution in Multilayers
items.abstract: Spontaneous formation of charge density wave (CDW) superstructures in monolayers (MLs) of a two-dimensional (2D) crystal lattice is fundamental in understanding its complex quantum states. We report a successful top-down liquid phase exfoliation and stamp transfer process (LPESTP) to create ML VS\textsubscript{2}, undergoing a CDW transition at room temperature. Using high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) and electron diffraction (ED), we observed the coexistence of 1T and 2H polymorphic phases in VS\textsubscript{2} at room temperature, and only the 1T phase undergoes CDW transition. We discovered a novel incommensurate CDW superstructure ($\sqrt{7} \times \sqrt{7}$) R19.1\textsuperscript{o} in ML 1T-VS\textsubscript{2}. With an increase in the number of layers, the CDW order changes to a commensurate ($2 \times 2\times 1$) superstructure. Using angle-dependent photoelectron spectroscopy and TEM, we have shown that vanadium atoms self-intercalate as V\textsuperscript{3+} ions in multilayer VS\textsubscript{2} and are responsible for the evolution of the CDW superstructure from the incommensurate ($\sqrt{7} \times \sqrt{7}$) R 19.1\textsuperscript{o} to the commensurate ($2\times2\times1$) order. We also report the observation of novel Moir\'e superlattices in twisted bilayer 1T-VS\textsubscript{2} flakes with trapped CDW superstructure of the monolayer. The density functional theory (DFT) calculation performed on ML 1T-VS\textsubscript{2} show that the observed ($\sqrt{7} \times \sqrt{7}$) R 19.1\textsuperscript{o} CDW superstructure has lower energy compared to that of the pristine undistorted ML and the CDW instability is driven by formation of strong soft-phonon modes. Our findings provide an important platform for understanding the evolution of CDW superstructures in 1T-VS\textsubscript{2} with layer numbers and V self-intercalation.
items.authors: Samanta Pal, Kaustuv Chatterjee, Jyotirmoy Sau, Biswarup Satpati, Manoranjan Kumar, A. K. Raychaudhuri, Prabir Pal

items.title: Disorder-driven symmetry suppression by van der Waals planar defects in a magnetic topological insulator
items.abstract: Magnetic topological insulators offer a platform to control electronic topology through magnetic order, yet reliable routes to tune their properties remain limited. Here, we show that ion irradiation allows to modify the magnetic properties and the anomalous Hall response of the van der Waals magnetic topological insulator MnBi$_2$Te$_4$. Using noble gas ion beams, intrinsic defects are introduced via collision cascades without chemical doping. We identify two distinct regimes. At low fluence, cation antisite disorder leads to a near-complete redistribution of Bi over cation sites while preserving long-range crystallographic order, accompanied by a transition from $p$-type to $n$-type transport. At high fluence, cation-anion intermixing drives the formation of a previously unreported layer-disordered phase characterized by a high density of van der Waals-specific planar defects, including swapped bilayers. Despite significant structural disorder, the system retains partial periodic order up to high displacement levels. Magnetometry and X-ray spectroscopy show that the Mn high-spin state and intralayer antiferromagnetic interactions likely persist, while macroscopic magnetic anisotropy is strongly reduced. At the same time, the magnitude of the anomalous Hall conductivity is reduced by an order of magnitude, far exceeding the change in magnetization, and its sign is modified. The observations are consistent with a suppression of the Berry curvature of the occupied states. These results establish ion irradiation as a means to tune anomalous Hall conductivity in topological insulators through defect engineering and reveal a disorder-driven approach to control symmetry and electronic structure in van der Waals magnetic materials.
items.authors: Rikkie Joris, Heyi Xia, Ana Beatriz Pedro Fontes, Sara Bey, Seul-Ki Bac, Jiaqi Zhou, Zviadi Zarkua, Ahmed Samir Lotfy, Muhammad Saad, Philippe Ohresser, Bence G. M\'arkus, L\'aszl\'o Forr\'o, Margriet van Bael, Clement Merckling, Xinyu Liu, Francisco Molina-Lopez, Jean-Christophe Charlier, Jin Won Seo, Badih A. Assaf, Lino M. C. Pereira

items.title: First-Principles Investigation of Ammonia Adsorption and N-H Activation on W-B Nanoclusters
items.abstract: Tungsten-boride nanoclusters are nanoscale systems of potential catalytic interest, but their structural stability and reactivity remain poorly understood. We combine evolutionary structure prediction with density functional theory to investigate W$_m$B$_n$ nanoclusters containing up to 43 atoms. The calculated stability descriptors reveal a strongly non-monotonic landscape, with several compositions locally favoured relative to neighbouring stoichiometries within the explored isolated-cluster model. Molecular NH$_3$ adsorption was examined at W-top and accessible B-top sites, with adsorption energies ranging from $-1.78$ to $-0.54$ eV on W sites and from $-1.54$ to $+0.62$ eV on B sites. H adsorption at W-top and B-top sites spans $-1.47$ to $+0.67$ eV, indicating pronounced composition- and site-dependence. CI-NEB calculations show that the first N-H bond-cleavage barrier is strongly pathway-dependent. These results characterize the initial activation of NH$_3$ on W-B nanoclusters and provide an atomistic basis for further investigation of the complete ammonia-decomposition mechanism.
items.authors: Anastasiia V. Iosimovska, Mikhail M. Lukanov, Christian Tantardini, Alexander S. Novikov, Viktor S. Baidyshev, Alexander G. Kvashnin

items.title: Preconditioning Magnetic Systems in Kohn-Sham Density Functional Theory
items.abstract: The convergence of the self-consistent field iterations in Kohn-Sham density functional theory can be significantly hindered by the presence of small eigenvalues in the dielectric matrix, which are often associated with electronic phase transitions in magnetic systems. In this work, we study this type of convergence issues and propose a new preconditioning scheme to mitigate them. Our preconditioning scheme is inspired by the Stoner model and based on a non-interacting susceptibility that neglects orbital variations. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on a range of ferromagnetic systems, showing that it can significantly reduce the number of iterations required to achieve convergence in the vicinity of magnetic phase transitions.
items.authors: Cl\'ementine Barat, Antoine Levitt, Marc Torrent

items.title: A Magnetism-Aware Crystal Graph Neural Network with Explicit Magnetic-Sublattice and Exchange-Geometry Representations
items.abstract: Magnetic order in crystals is governed by moment-carrying sublattices and ligand-mediated exchange pathways, yet standard crystal graph neural networks do not explicitly distinguish magnetic sublattices and encode bonds primarily through pair distances. We propose mCGCNN, a magnetism-aware crystal graph neural network that augments the full structural graph with a dedicated magnetic subgraph. The magnetic stream performs angle-aware message passing between magnetic centers using metal--ligand--metal exchange-path descriptors motivated by Goodenough--Kanamori--Anderson physics, while layer-wise cross-coupling transfers structural and ligand-environment information from the full crystal graph. Separate pooling of the magnetic sublattice preserves magnetism-specific information alongside the global structural representation. We evaluate mCGCNN for total magnetic moment prediction on 49,462 crystalline materials with ferromagnetic spin configurations from the Materials Project and find that the proposed model improves agreement with DFT magnetic moments over established crystal-graph approaches without requiring a large increase in model complexity. Material-level analysis shows that the largest gains are concentrated predominantly in complex transition-metal and oxygen-containing magnetic compounds. Our results show that explicitly incorporating magnetic sublattices and exchange geometry provides a physically motivated route to improved crystal-graph representations for magnetic materials.
items.authors: Sourav Mal, Satadeep Bhattacharjee

items.title: Nonlinear Tellegen limit
items.abstract: The Tellegen limit is the fundamental electromagnetic stability bound on magnetoelectric media. We show that nonlinear magnetoelectric coupling gives rise to a new Tellegen limit, which we term the \textit{nonlinear Tellegen limit}. Unlike the linear Tellegen limit, which is fixed by material parameters, the nonlinear Tellegen limit is field-tunable -- a static electric or magnetic field drives the system toward electromagnetic instability at a material-specific critical field determined by the symmetry-allowed nonlinear magnetoelectric couplings and electromagnetic response. The approach to this limit is accompanied by a field-tunable linear birefringence, whose maximum is bounded by the nonlinear Tellegen limit -- beyond which the medium becomes electromagnetically unstable. We demonstrate the nonlinear Tellegen limit and the field-space stability phase diagram in two magnetically ordered material systems -- a $d$-wave altermagnet and an M-type hexagonal ferrite -- showing that the symmetry of the magnetic point group governs both the structure of the nonlinear magnetoelectric tensor and the resulting electromagnetic instability.
items.authors: Abhinava Chatterjee, Nikhil Kalyanapuram

items.title: Single-orbital tight-binding model for chiral one-dimensional hybrid organic-inorganic lead halide perovskites
items.abstract: We present a single-orbital tight-binding model for the low-energy electronic states of the chiral one-dimensional hybrid organic-inorganic lead halide perovskite $\mathrm{(}R/S\mathrm{-PEA)PbI}_3$. The model is constructed from a single effective orbital on each of the four symmetry-related sites in the primitive unit cell and incorporates layer, in-plane sublattice, and spin degrees of freedom. With separate parameter sets for the conduction and valence bands, the effective Hamiltonian reproduces the overall band dispersions obtained from density-functional-theory calculations and quantitatively captures the spin splittings near the band edges. It also captures the leading spin-polarization patterns of the Bloch states, showing that the band-edge spin splitting and spin polarization are encoded in a small number of symmetry-adapted spin-dependent hopping terms. We further analyze the accidental degeneracies of the effective Hamiltonian using screw eigenvalues and antiunitary operators. This analysis separates accidental degeneracies originating from the restricted term content of the effective Hamiltonian from degeneracies enforced by nonsymmorphic screw symmetries and time-reversal symmetry. The present model provides a symmetry-transparent starting point for understanding the band-edge electronic structure of chiral lead halide perovskites and for analyzing optical, spin, and transport responses in this class of materials.
items.authors: Yuya Ominato, Tetsuya Furukawa, Ayumi Ishii, Tetsuaki Itou

items.title: Response-function-optimized phase field modeling of solute trapping and solute drag in rapid alloy solidification
items.abstract: Quantitative prediction of rapid-solidification microstructures requires phase field models that represent the velocity dependence of interfacial properties, including solute partitioning, kinetic liquidus response, solute drag, and kinetic undercooling. These response functions control both microsegregation and morphology selection, but are difficult to prescribe accurately in phase field simulations that employ enlarged interfaces for numerical efficiency. We introduce an optimization-based calibration strategy that embeds target sharp-interface response functions into a dilute alloy phase field formulation by treating the interfacial diffusivity interpolation function as a response-matching degree of freedom. The optimized diffusivity functions are obtained from one-dimensional steady-state phase field solutions constrained to reproduce prescribed continuous-growth-model targets for velocity-dependent solute trapping and drag-modified liquidus kinetics. We demonstrate the accuracy and versatility of the calibrated model in dilute Al-Cu by reproducing the prescribed response functions for intermediate solute drag coefficients relevant to rapid solidification. Two-dimensional simulations are carried out over a range of drag coefficients and pulling velocities relevant to additive manufacturing, demonstrating that quantitative changes in the prescribed interface kinetics can systematically shift the morphology from cellular to banded growth. Additionally, we extend the formulation to dilute multicomponent alloys, enabling independent specification of equilibrium partition coefficients and liquidus slopes for multiple solute species. The framework separates the physical specification of nonequilibrium interface kinetics from their diffuse-interface realization and provides a practical route for embedding response functions into quantitative phase field computations.
items.authors: Joni Kaipainen, Tatu Pinomaa, Nikolas Provatas

items.title: Magnetic proximity-induced non-relativistic valley polarization
items.abstract: The magnetic proximity effect in van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures exerts a significant impact on the electronic and magnetic properties of adjacent materials. Here, we propose vdW heterostructures composed of monolayers ferromagnets (FM) and altermagnets (AM), in which the magnetic proximity effect from the FM induces pronounced non-relativistic valley polarization in the AM. Furthermore, by flipping the magnetization of the FM and the direction of N\'eel vector of the AM, four independent valley-polarized states can be realized in the FM/AM vdW heterostructures, exhibiting strong magneto-valley coupling. The phenomenon is qualitatively elucidated by a tight-binding model and demonstrated to be generalizable. These findings suggest that FM/AM vdW heterostructures hold potential application in the field of valleytronics-based information storage.
items.authors: Weifeng Xie, Yongqi Chen, Yiboyang Sun, Xiong Xu, Yunliang Yue, Hui Wang

items.title: Optically Coupled Noise Spectroscopy Quantifies Defect Passivation in Monolayer MoS2 FETs
items.abstract: Transition metal dichalcogenide monolayers are promising materials for electronic and photonic applications, yet the performance of chemical vapour deposition grown samples is severely limited by native sulphur vacancies that introduce mid-gap trap states, degrade carrier mobility, and elevate electrical noise. Here we investigate octanethiol passivation of sulphur vacancies in monolayer MoS2 field effect transistors, combining x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, photoluminescence, and Raman scattering with electrical transport and optically coupled low-frequency noise spectroscopy. Thiol treatment reduces the sulphur vacancy concentration from 7% to 4%, reducing the free electron density. Electrically, it increases the device resistance 35-fold while restoring gate switching with an on/off ratio of 10^4 and improving field-effect mobility from 1 to 5 cm^2/Vs. Low frequency noise spectroscopy directly quantifies the defect suppression: the Hooge parameter alpha_H drops by more than two orders of magnitude after passivation. Gate-dependent noise confirms carrier mobility fluctuation as the dominant dark noise mechanism, while optical excitation drives a crossover to carrier number fluctuation dominated noise, reflecting preferential interaction of photogenerated carriers with residual vacancy states via generation-recombination trapping, a mechanistic distinction inaccessible to gate-bias measurements alone. Density functional theory calculations corroborate these findings, showing suppression of vacancy-induced mid-gap states by more than half and partial restoration of the intrinsic bandgap. These results establish optically coupled low-frequency noise spectroscopy as a sensitive, low-cost, and non-destructive tool for quantifying defect passivation in TMDC-based devices.
items.authors: Shashwata Chattopadhyay, Soumyadip Hazra, Sraboni Dey, Kritika Sharu, Renjith Nadarajan, Arijit Kayal, Joy Mitra

items.title: Field-Driven Coupled Magnon--Phonon--Electron Relaxation in Magnetite Using Steepest-Entropy-Ascent Quantum Thermodynamic Formalism
items.abstract: A field-driven steepest-entropy-ascent quantum thermodynamic (SEAQT) formulation is developed for longitudinal nonequilibrium relaxation in magnetite (Fe$_3$O$_4$) with coupled electron, phonon, and magnon populations. Material-specific excitation spectra define the thermodynamic state space, while one relaxation parameter for each population sets its kinetic scale. A longitudinal magnetic field shifts the dressed magnon eigenenergies while the occupation basis remains fixed; irreversible redistribution conserves instantaneous energy and electron number while allowing the magnon population to vary. The formulation yields nonequilibrium subsystem temperatures, entropy production, magnetic-work identities, and a coupled small-signal susceptibility incorporating energy-conservation feedback among all three populations; the one-pole Debye response appears only as a limiting case. Numerical results under sinusoidal driving show a transition from nearly quasistatic behavior to frequency-dependent lag, finite-amplitude departure from the linear-response ellipse, and increasing higher-harmonic content. Relaxational work per cycle increases strongly with field amplitude and frequency, while the complex susceptibility is broader and shifted relative to a Debye reference. Entropy production remains positive, and the electron, phonon, and magnon temperatures show distinct excursions followed by secular heating when positive magnetic work is retained without heat rejection. The calculated work represents longitudinal magnon quasiparticle relaxation in a homogeneous single-domain model, not the total core loss of a finite ferrite specimen.
items.authors: Deepak Dhariwal, William T. Reynolds, Jr., Michael R. von Spakovsky

items.title: Electric-Field-Switchable Altermagnetism via Ligand Rotation in a d0 Metal-Organic Framework
items.abstract: Altermagnetism combines vanishing net magnetization with momentum-dependent spin splitting. While altermagnetic signatures have been identified in metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), non-invasive reversible control remains challenging. Here we report a route to electric-field-switchable altermagnetism in a flexible d0-MOF, in which polar substituents couple the external field to ligand rotation. In the planar ground state, pz orbitals mediate 180-degree ligand-metal-ligand superexchange (J2), stabilizing antiferromagnetic order. Rotating ligands out of plane activates px/py orbitals, enhances 90-degree pathways (J1), and reverses J1/J2 competition. The antiferromagnetic-to-altermagnetic crossover occurs at approx. 34 degrees, with spin splitting of 84 meV at 90 degrees. The 90-degree altermagnetic state is switched on by the electric field and switched off upon field removal, as the constrained-rotation landscape decreases monotonically back toward 0 degrees, enabling barrierless relaxation to the antiferromagnetic state and reversible on/off operation. Ab initio molecular dynamics at 300 K shows thermal fluctuations alone cannot synchronize ligand rotation. Polar substituents provide the required coupling for electric-field control; for fluorinated substituents, the critical field is approx. 0.22 V/Angstrom, comparable to field-effect devices. This work establishes ligand p orbitals, rather than transition-metal d orbitals, as the origin of altermagnetic order and shows that polar substituents enable electric-field control for organic spintronics.
items.authors: Hongjing Wang, Xiuling Li, Xiaojun Wu
items.title_zh: 电场可切换的配体旋转引发的反常磁性研究
items.summary_zh: 反常磁性结合了消失的净磁化和动量依赖的自旋分裂。尽管在金属有机框架（MOFs）中已识别出反常磁性特征，但非侵入性可逆控制仍然具有挑战性。本研究报告了一种在柔性d0-MOF中实现电场可切换反常磁性的方法，其中极性取代基将外部电场与配体旋转耦合。在平面基态中，pz轨道介导180度的配体-金属-配体超交换（J2），稳定反铁磁序。配体的离面旋转激活px/py轨道，增强90度路径（J1），并逆转J1/J2竞争。反铁磁到反常磁性交叉发生在约34度，90度时自旋分裂为84 meV。90度的反常磁性状态在电场作用下开启，去除电场后关闭，因受限旋转景观单调减少回0度，实现无能量障碍的反铁磁状态放松和可逆的开关操作。300 K下的从头算分子动力学显示，仅靠热波动无法同步配体旋转。极性取代基提供了电场控制所需的耦合；对于氟化取代基，临界电场约为0.22 V/Å，接近场效应器件的水平。此研究确立了配体p轨道在反常磁性中的重要性。

items.title: Modeling Dynamic Magnetic Response of Spinel Soft Ferrites with the Steepest-Entropy-Ascent Quantum Thermodynamics Formalism
items.abstract: Selecting soft ferrites for alternating-field applications requires balancing magnetic response, dissipation, nonlinearity, and heating. We use a field-driven steepest-entropy-ascent quantum thermodynamic (SEAQT) model to compare the electron, phonon, and magnon responses of Fe$_3$O$_4$, MnFe$2$O$4$, and (Mn${0.5}$Zn${0.5}$)Fe$_2$O$_4$ within a common first-principles framework. The model treats spatially uniform longitudinal relaxation and neglects domain-wall motion, transverse rotation, resonance, eddy-current effects, and heat removal. We use $\tau_e=0.05$ ps and $\tau_p=3$ ps for all three materials, with effective longitudinal magnon relaxation times of 500, 200, and 85 ps, respectively; these literature-motivated values are model inputs, not fits to measured losses. Within this framework, the Mn--Zn ferrite gives the largest peak longitudinal magnetization change, retains its response best at high frequency, and shows the largest work per cycle and peak-to-peak magnon temperature change, whereas MnFe$_2$O$_4$ gives the largest normalized $\chi''$ peak. Thus, no single ferrite ranks highest across all metrics: the preferred material depends on the property, frequency, field amplitude, and cation configuration of interest. The model therefore provides a spectrum- and kinetics-resolved screening tool for engineering comparison of ferrites rather than a prediction of total core loss.
items.authors: Deepak Dhariwal, William T. Reynolds Jr., Michael R. von Spakovsky

items.title: Phonon-mediated closing of topological Floquet gaps in graphene: Non-phenomenological analysis
items.abstract: Floquet band engineering has been intensively studied for its potential to control material properties via laser driving. In particular, Floquet topological states have been measured on the surface of Bi$_2$Se$_3$. Nonetheless, the original prediction of Floquet topological bands in graphene remains unobserved, with works only measuring non-topological Floquet-Bloch states or indirect features. Here, we theoretically explore graphene irradiated by circular lasers with non-phenomenological electron-phonon (e-ph) coupling. We show that e-ph interactions substantially broaden Floquet bands due to graphene's large zero-point motion, as expected from phenomenological treatments. However, we further find that larger displacement $\Gamma$ optical phonons reduce Floquet gaps by about half, even in absence of instrumentation broadening, and can also induce additional features like flat bands. These phonons "enter the gap" and blur photoemission signatures. Including non-$\Gamma$ phonons closes the gap and greatly reduces visibility. When these modes couple to reasonably expected instrumentation broadening, the effect is significantly exacerbated. Our results shed light on the missing Floquet topological gaps and also lead to possible mitigation strategies: (i) Pre-pumping coherent phonons to counteract blurring, or (ii), transition to a Dirac system with more favorable phonon statistics. Moreover, our real-space analysis proposes that Floquet topological physics is alive in localized regions, such that properties of interest like transport should be accessible. We expect this work to impact experimental analysis and lead to set-ups where graphene Floquet topology might finally be directly observed.
items.authors: Royi Ledermann, Rave Hanoch Saadon, Adam Herling, Ofer Neufeld

items.title: Complex Magnetic Phases and Unconventional Skyrmion Thermodynamics in Magnetically Intercalated Cr$_{1+x}$Te$_2$Compounds
items.abstract: Chemical intercalation provides a powerful route for tuning the electronic and magnetic properties of transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), enabling the emergence of magnetic phases and phenomena that are otherwise inaccessible in their pristine forms. Here, we investigate the structural, electronic, and magnetic properties of magnetically intercalated Cr$_{1+x}$Te$_2$ through a combination of scanning tunneling microscopy, angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, magnetization, electrical transport, and Lorentz transmission electron microscopy measurements. We uncover a rich magnetic phase diagram comprising paramagnetic, in-plane spin-fluctuation, out-of-plane ferromagnetic, and field-induced N\'eel-type skyrmion phases. In particular, Lorentz transmission electron microscopy directly reveals the formation of N\'eel-type skyrmion textures slightly below the Curie temperature, with their configurations evolving strongly with temperature and magnetic field. The skyrmions exhibit pronounced thermal hysteresis and coexist with stripe domains, indicative of a complex magnetic energy landscape arising from the competition among disorder-induced local Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions, perpendicular magnetic anisotropy, and dipolar interactions. Our results demonstrate that chemical intercalation can profoundly reshape the magnetic interactions and phase behavior of TMDs, establishing Cr$_{1+x}$Te$_2$ as a versatile platform for exploring tunable magnetism, skyrmion physics, and unconventional thermodynamic phenomena in low-dimensional quantum materials.
items.authors: Clayton Conner, Santosh Karki Chhetri, Avinash Sah, Manoj Gadtoula, Dilan M. Gamachchi, Indeewari M. Karunarathne, Steven Kelley, Andrew C. Meng, Jacob Cook, Cheng Zhang, Jin Hu, Yue Li, Hoyeon Jeon, An-Ping Li, Zheng Gai, Guang Bian

items.title: Prediction of the thermal neutron response of grain-boundary impedance in Gd-doped ceria based on the radiation-ionic effect
items.abstract: The radiation-ionic effect was recently reported in 3 mol% Gd-doped CeO$_2$ (3GDC): under $^{60}$Co gamma irradiation at 35 Gy/min, the grain-boundary (GB) ionic resistance of a bulk pellet decreased 680-fold at room temperature, because electrons trapped at the GB core lower the space-charge potential. The effect has been demonstrated only with photons. Gd has the largest thermal-neutron capture cross section of any stable element and is also the dopant that creates the GB barrier in GDC, so the same mechanism could link GB impedance to thermal-neutron sensing; whether it does, and under what conditions, has not been examined. Here the thermal-neutron response of 3GDC is modelled with the gamma-calibrated Mott-Schottky/Seager framework, with unmeasured parameters carried as intervals and propagated jointly. Each capture deposits about 50 keV by conversion and Auger electrons within 1 $\mu$m, the remaining 8 MeV leaving as prompt photons; Gd segregation to the GBs adds a factor of only 1-2 because the electron range exceeds the grain size. A thermal flux of $8\times10^{9}$ cm$^{-2}$s$^{-1}$ (6-12$\times10^{9}$) matches the GB-effective generation rate of the 35 Gy/min calibration, and the predicted room-temperature GB resistance ratio is 110 (70-170) at $10^{9}$ and 970 (600-1500) at $10^{10}$ cm$^{-2}$s$^{-1}$, falling to 2 at 61 (55-68) and 81 (73-92) $^\circ$C. The neutron case differs from gamma irradiation in three respects: capture events are discrete, so the continuous-source approximation depends on the unmeasured trapped-charge lifetime; self-shielding (mean free path 0.27 mm) makes the response thickness dependent; and capture photons absorbed in the pellet add a gamma term comparable to the local term for pellets of 0.3 mm or more. The intervals are conditional on the model and exclude its structural error. The conditions under which the prediction can be tested are given.
items.authors: Zhongming Zhang

items.title: Realizing Two-Dimensional Altermagnets with 100% Spin Polarization along the [110] Direction in Ambidentate-Ligand Based Square Organometallic Lattices
items.abstract: Altermagnetism, as a novel magnetic paradigm, not only possesses a zero net magnetic moment, but also exhibits a substantial nonrelativistic spin-splitting effect. Currently, developing a simple and experimentally feasible method for designing altermagnets is eagerly pursued. Moreover, achieving 100% spin polarization along certain directions in valence or conduction bands for altermagnets remains challenging. To address these issues, based on a tight-binding model, we propose a viable chemical strategy for constructing organometallic altermagnets by using ambidentate ligands. Furthermore, in these organometallic altermagnets, direction-dependent 100% spin polarization along the [110] direction in band edges can be induced via the coexistence of altermagnetically spin-split dispersive and flat bands, where the flat band suppresses electron transport in one spin channel and the dispersive band enables conduction in the other spin channel. Then, via first-principles calculations, a screening of 90 two-dimensional ambidentate-ligand based square organometallic lattices leads to the identification of three altermagnetic materials, namely Fe(taz)2Cl2 (taz = 1,2,4- triazine), Co(app)2Cl2, and Fe(app)2Cl2 (app = 1,4-azaphosphinine), all of which possess 100% spin polarization along the [110] direction in valence bands, as well as notable piezomagnetic behavior. This study paves the way for achieving direction-dependent fully spin-polarization in altermagnetic materials.
items.authors: Qing-Bo Liu, Xin-Yi Chen, Xiangyang Li, Xingxing Li, Jinlong Yang

items.title: Ring states in topological materials
items.abstract: Ingap states in semiconductors are commonly characterized by hydrogenic models within the effective mass approximation. However, when impurities are strong, this description fails. The bound states are non-perturbative with energy pinned to a zero of the impurity-projected Green's function. We show that in the presence of Wannier obstructions, such zeros are irremovable. That is, no symmetric, gap-preserving deformation of the bulk can return the ingap state to the band continuum. We call these states ring states: their wavefunctions show a node at the impurity site, and their mixed band character is set by minimizing the level repulsion exerted by the bands above and below the gap. In Chern insulators, the band mixing endows occupied ring states with local circulating currents, remnant of a small edge mode surrounding the vacancies. Clusters of vacancies bind ring states that hybridize to form dispersive chiral edge modes, providing a real-space view of bulk-boundary correspondence.
items.authors: Raquel Queiroz, Roni Ilan, Zhida Song, B. Andrei Bernevig, Ady Stern

items.title: Nonlinear eigenvalue algorithm for $GW$ quasiparticle equations
items.abstract: The use of the Green's function in quantum many-body theory often leads to nonlinear eigenvalue problems, as the Green's function needs to be defined in the energy domain. The GW approximation method is one typical example. In this article, we introduce a method based on the FEAST eigenvalue algorithm for accurately solving the nonlinear eigenvalue G0W0 quasiparticle equation. Based on the FEAST contour integral method for nonlinear eigenvalue problems, the energy (eigenvalue) domain is extended to the complex plane. An analytic continuation is introduced to the calculation of the GW self-energy to carry the imaginary parts of both Green's functions and FEAST contour quadrature nodes. Calculation results for various molecules are presented and compared with the more conventional graphical solution approximation method and spectral functions method. It is confirmed that the highest occupied molecular orbital from the Kohn-Sham (and Hartree-Fock) equation is very close to that of GW, while the lowest unoccupied molecular orbital shows noticeable differences.
items.authors: Dongming Li, Eric Polizzi

items.title: Two-dimensional Topological Quantum Chemistry and Catalog of Topological Materials
items.abstract: Two-dimensional topological materials host symmetry-protected, disorder-robust edge states cen- tral to quantum technologies. Yet, they remain scarce compared with their three-dimensional coun- terparts. We adapt the topological quantum chemistry formalism to layer groups, and study the band topology of 8,872 entries from the computational materials databases C2DB and MC2D. We find 4,073 topological or obstructed entries, including 905 topological insulators and 1,003 obstructed atomic insulators, greatly expanding the library of such materials in two dimensions. Detailed elec- tronic and topological properties of all materials are compiled into a a Topological 2D Materials Database (2D-TQCDB), and the edge states of selected new materials are studied in detail. Our methodology is implemented in new publicly available programs, designed to study the topology of any non-magnetic monolayer or multilayer material.
items.authors: Urko Petralanda, Yi Jiang, Hanqi Pi, Maia G. Vergniory, B. Andrei Bernevig, Nicolas Regnault, Luis Elcoro

items.title: Observation of Altermagnetic Spin Splitting in an Intercalated Transition Metal Dichalcogenide
items.abstract: Altermagnetism is a novel magnetic phase combining characteristics of both antiferromagnetism and ferromagnetic ordering. Despite growing theoretical interest in altermagnetic materials, reports of experimentally verified high Neel temperature layered compounds are limited or remain to be firmly established. Here, we present an angle resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and density functional theory (DFT) study of Co1/4TaSe2, a compound we identify as a layered altermagnetic material. Magnetic susceptibility measurements confirm type A antiferromagnetic ordering with a Neel temperature of 178 K. Our ARPES measurements reveal an electronic band structure in excellent agreement with DFT calculations, demonstrating clear signatures of altermagnetic spin splitting at the Fermi surface. Furthermore, temperature dependent ARPES reveals a reconstructed valence band structure, with observable band shifts and the closing of energy gaps upon heating above the Neel temperature (TN), consistent with the suppression of altermagnetic order. These findings establish Co1/4TaSe2 as a promising platform for exploring altermagnetic phenomena.
items.authors: Milo Sprague, Mazharul Islam Mondal, Anup Pradhan Sakhya, Resham Babu Regmi, Surasree Sadhukhan, Arun K. Kumay, Himanshu Sheokand, Igor I. Mazin, Nirmal J. Ghimire, Madhab Neupane

items.title: Phonons under confinement: Coarse-grained $U(1)$ charge and a new transport mechanism
items.abstract: An important feature of solid-state or cold atom systems in low dimensions is the restricted oscillations of ionic/atomic degrees of freedom in the confining directions, for which the conventional phonon from canonical quantization is not an ideal description. In this work we propose a general recipe to introduce this feature to otherwise unrestricted systems by mapping displacement fields to spin degrees of freedom, dubbed soft-corization. In the strong-confinement limit $S=1/2$, we demonstrate the validity of the approach with a harmonic chain; the results lead to a gapped fermionic model showing the absence of acoustic modes as a signature of the confinement of the entire chain. Despite the non-conserved total particle number in the presence of nearest-neighbor parings, the model holds a coarse-grained $U(1)$ symmetry with conserved polarization charge in the absence of nearest-neighbor hopping. This enables a new transport mechanism via "dimer-tumbling" instead of single-particle hopping. We then introduce a short-range interaction via anharmonicity; for energy scales slightly above the gap, it leads to a (quantum) phase transition to a nonreciprocal state carrying polarization charge current and heat current with spontaneous time reversal symmetry breaking (TRSB) of the type $\hat{T}^2=+1$. The non-reciprocity can be probed by measuring the change of inductance due to gauge fields in and out of the ordered phase.
items.authors: Yuan Gao, K. A. Muttalib

items.title: Spin-fluctuation-mediated unconventional $d_{xy}$-wave superconductivity in ThFeAsN from first-principles
items.abstract: Superconducting (SC) pairing mechanism, origin of high $T_c$ and symmetry of SC order parameter in Fe-based superconductors are among the important unsolved problems in condensed matter and materials physics. We study the SC properties of ThFeAsN, a Fe-based high $T_c$ superconductor, by {\it ab initio} superconducting density functional theory calculations with electron-phonon coupling, screened static and dynamic electron-electron Coulomb repulsion and spin fluctuation (SF) mediated pair-interaction fully taken into account. Our calculations reveal that ThFeAsN is a SF-mediated multiband superconductor with the calculated $T_c$ of 22.4 K and the $d_{xy}$-wave SC order parameter with different signs on different Fermi surface sheets, in consistent with experiments. We also present distinct SC properties such as quasiparticle density of states and ultrasonic attenuation coefficient which can be immediately verified by experiments.
items.authors: Guang-Yu Guo, Jau-Wen Liu, Mitsuaki Kawamura

items.title: High-pressure phase transitions in the quantum spin liquid candidate Na2Co2TeO6 probed by Raman spectroscopy
items.abstract: The quasi-2D magnet Na2Co2TeO6 (NCTO) is a candidate for a Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquid (KQSL) state. Pressure-tuning in such materials is of interest as a potential method to tune the Kitaev exchange interactions, which are strongly dependent on bond geometry. Here we report a Raman spectroscopic study of NCTO inside a diamond anvil cell (DAC) with pressure applied up to 16.3 GPa. Based on the changes in the Raman modes, this pressure range is divided into three regions. The appearance and disappearance of several modes and changes in the polarization dependence of the representative modes, most prominently above 13.8 GPa, point to pressure-induced phase transitions in this material.
items.authors: Ihsan Ahmed Kolasseri, Maria Mei Ravneb{\ae}k, Subhadip Das, Carl Jonas Linnemann, Haidong Zhou, Christian Frydendahl, Martin Bremholm, Yong P. Chen

items.title: The First Magic Angle Beyond the Chiral Limit in Twisted Bilayer Graphene
items.abstract: We develop a squared-Hamiltonian description of twisted bilayer graphene beyond the chiral limit to explain why the first magic angle remains robust under lattice relaxation, while higher-order magic angles are strongly destabilized. Starting from the non-chiral Bistritzer--MacDonald model with finite same-sublattice tunneling, we show that lattice relaxation reshapes the effective confinement landscape rather than acting as a simple perturbation of the chiral theory. A central result is that the realistic relaxation-renormalized tunneling ratio lies close to a special confinement point where the oscillatory part of the symmetric confinement potential nearly cancels. This places realistic twisted bilayer graphene near a nearly uniform confinement regime. At the same time, finite same-sublattice tunneling activates an additional inter-sublattice current-like channel that competes with the chiral orbital channel. The first magic angle survives because these confinement and current-like contributions remain balanced, whereas higher-order magic angles lose this balance through stronger remote-band hybridization and enhanced real-space localization around AA regions. Our results provide a single-particle mechanism for the breakdown of the chiral magic-angle hierarchy and clarify why the experimentally relevant first magic angle remains the most stable remnant of the chiral flat-band structure.
items.authors: Leonardo A. Navarro-Labastida, Pierre A. Pantaleon, Francisco Guinea, Gerardo G. Naumis

items.title: GEM: An implementation of the ghost-Gutzwiller approximation for simulating interacting quantum systems
items.abstract: We present GEM (Ghost Embedding Method), an open-source software package written in Python for computing equilibrium properties of strongly correlated electronic systems within the ghost-Gutzwiller approximation method. GEM provides a computationally efficient framework for studying multi-orbital lattice models. It supports zero- and finite-temperature calculations and symmetry broken phases. It is integrated with the TRIQS ecosystem, providing tools for model construction, self-consistent solution, and evaluation of physical observables. We first detail the method's theoretical formulation, then we present the software architecture, and finally we introduce some practical workflow, which also validates the implementation against established results. In particular, we illustrate the capabilities of GEM through multiorbital and finite-temperature applications and discuss its computational cost relative to more demanding quantum embedding approaches.
items.authors: Samuele Giuli, Tsung-Han Lee, Yong-Xin Yao, Ina Park, Harrison LaBollita, Ivan Pasqua, Nils Wentzell, Nicola Lanat\`a, Olivier Gingras

items.title: Density Functional Theory for 2D Transition-Metal Dichalcogenides with Extended Hubbard Parameters
items.abstract: Accurate modelling of the band-edge electronic structure of transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), such as MoS$_2$, is essential for understanding their optical, electronic and spintronic properties and enabling future applications. Here, we supplement the standard PBE exchange-correlation functional with on-metal ($U$) and metal--chalcogen ($V$) Hubbard corrections, which can control the orbital composition of band-edge states and consequently improve the quantitative accuracy of various properties. For MoS$_2$, MoSe$_2$, WS$_2$, and WSe$_2$, we optimise the $U$ and $V$ parameters by comparison with experimentally measured spin--orbit splittings at the conduction and valence band edges, and show that these optimal choices also improve agreement of the computed band gap, and ferroelectric potential drop in rhombohedral bilayers, with experimentally measured values. This provides a highly efficient, scalable framework for quantitatively accurate, high-throughput calculations of monolayer and multilayer TMDs, suitable for implementation in 2D-materials databases, as well as large-scale electronic and spintronic device modelling.
items.authors: Xue Li, Suad Alshammari, Igor Rozhansky, James G. McHugh, Vladimir Fal'ko

items.title: High-Efficiency and Large Supercurrent Rectification with Superconducting Coil
items.abstract: Superconducting diodes (SDs) are devices that rectify supercurrent through the difference in the superconducting critical current (Ic) between forward and reverse current directions. For bringing such SDs closer to practical superconducting power electronics applications, a combination of both high rectification efficiency ({\eta}) and a large Ic difference ({\Delta}Ic) is required. Here, we propose and demonstrate a coil-shaped superconducting wire device concept to induce a large SD effect, arising from the compensation between an external magnetic field (Hext) and the field generated by the coil itself. From transport Ic measurements on coil-shaped SDs based on a Sn10-Pb90 solder wire, we achieved a {\eta} of 79% with a {\Delta}Ic of 140 A at Hext = 500 Oe (coil #2) and a {\eta} of 84% with a {\Delta}Ic of 125 A at Hext = 530 Oe (coil #3), confirming high rectification values at large supercurrents. The large-current high-efficiency SDE in the coil-shaped SDs will be highly useful for developing the potential field of supercurrent power electronics.
items.authors: Takumi Ichikawa, Daisuke Takegami, Gen Nishijima, Shunsuke Kawakami, Tsutomu Nojima, Yuji Tsuchiya, Satoshi Awaji, Fuyuki Ando, Ken-ichi Uchida, Yuya Hattori, Yoshikazu Mizuguchi

items.title: Learning native eddy-resolving ocean dynamics outperforms coarse emulation and downscaling
items.abstract: Eddy-resolving ocean simulations are essential for representing mesoscale dynamics that regulate ocean circulation, energy transport, and climate variability. However, they are costly to generate, store, and share. Artificial intelligence (AI) may help, but it remains unclear whether high-resolution ocean fields can be faithfully represented by evolving ocean states at coarse resolution followed by spatial downscaling, or whether dynamical evolution needs to be learned directly from native high-resolution simulations. We show that directly learning dynamical evolution on a 0.1$^\circ$ grid provides a more faithful representation of mesoscale variability than evolving ocean states on a 1$^\circ$ grid followed by downscaling reconstruction. We developed a full-depth 1$^\circ$ emulator and a native 0.1$^\circ$ sea surface temperature (SST) emulator, both of which remained stable over long-term free-running simulations without significant drift, providing reliable baselines for this comparison. Direct learning at 0.1$^\circ$ preserves mesoscale energy, spectral characteristics, and frontal gradients, whereas the coarse-resolution evolution followed by downscaling approach recovers large-scale patterns but fails to reproduce key mesoscale signatures. We show that the learned mesoscale statistics remain consistent across diverse hardware platforms, supporting the reproducibility and portability of AI-based ocean simulations. These results suggest that downscaling of low-resolution large-scale states alone is insufficient to represent ocean mesoscale variability, supporting the need to learn dynamical evolution directly in a high-resolution state space. These findings highlight the continued importance of high-resolution physics ocean models as a foundation for AI-based ocean simulation, providing dynamically resolved training data for physically faithful high-resolution emulators.
items.authors: Zilu Liu, Tao Zhang, Hailong Liu, Kai Xu, Qinghui Lin, Maoxue Yu, Jiangfeng Yu, Jingwei Xie, Zhao Jing, Minghua Zhang, Lixin Wu

items.title: Clarifying tipping terminology
items.abstract: The notion of tipping points and related terminology have so far had inconsistent and sometimes confusing definitions in both scientific and popular literature. While it is difficult for the scientific community to align popular usage of the term tipping point with a precise definition, technical usage of related terms would benefit from greater consistency and rigor. Toward this end, we offer a systematic set of terms to clarify formal communication around potential tipping dynamics, with focus on examples from Earth system dynamics.
items.authors: Niklas Boers, Robert E. Kopp, Peter Ashwin, Sebastian Bathiany, Maya Ben-Yami, Reyk B\"orner, Jofre Carnicer, Henk Dijkstra, Thomas L. Fr\"olicher, Michael Ghil, Elisabeth Gilmore, Gabriele C. Hegerl, Laura Jackson, Shipra Jain, David Lapola, Timothy M. Lenton, Valerio Lucarini, Teng Liu, Virna L. Meccia, Andreas Morr, Anastasia Romanou, Thomas F. Stocker, Shuting Yang, Cunde Xiao

items.title: Climate Sensitivity Derived from First-Principles Temperature Feedback Circuits
items.abstract: A long-standing challenge in climate science since the Charney Report in 1979 is to determine how much the Earth's climate warms in response to a unit external energy input at the top of the atmosphere (TOA). In this study, we show from first principles that temperature feedback within an atmosphere-surface column operates as a set of feedback circuits, each governed by an intrinsic gain less than unity, leading to geometric amplification of energy through successive feedback cycles. In particular, the surface-centered temperature feedback circuit determines the amplification of surface energy per unit TOA forcing. The surface energy amplification by non-temperature feedback is estimated from the amplification of solar energy absorption by downward longwave radiation at the surface in the climate mean state. Climate sensitivity then emerges as the product of these two amplifications scaled by the surface Planck feedback parameter. The climate sensitivity derived from the 1980-2000 climate mean state is 1.15 K (W m$^{-2}$)$^{-1}$. It yields a warming of 0.44 K from 1980-2000 to 2000-2020, consistent with the observed warming of 0.41 K, and equilibrium warmings of 3.02 and 5.83 K for CO$_2$ doubling and quadrupling, respectively, the former consistent with the Charney estimate near 3 degrees C. The framework provides a basis for predicting global surface temperature responses to other external forcing scenarios from the climate mean state.
items.authors: Ming Cai, Jie Sun, Zhe-Min Tan, Xiaoming Hu, Guosheng Liu, Zhaohua Wu

items.title: Multivariate phase-space interpretation of ensemble forecasts: A comparison of physical and AI models
items.abstract: Ensemble forecasts from the ECMWF's Integrated Forecasting System (IFS) and the Artificial Intelligence Forecasting System (AIFS-ENS) are compared using a multi-dimensional evaluation framework. Within this framework, the uncertainty is interpreted as the linear subspace spanned by the ensemble members in phase space, from which various geometric properties are extracted. As revealed by the analysis, the error does not entirely lie in this subspace, but is reasonably well calibrated in all directions. Moreover, the framework allows to quantify that this subspace critically depends on the number of ensemble members, suggesting that the current setups only partially represent the uncertainty subspace. This phase-space interpretation furthermore allows a direct comparison of the error-representation patterns of AIFS-ENS and IFS by computing the principal angles between the subspaces: IFS and AIFS ensemble subspaces do not entirely overlap in phase space, even though they were shown to have similar abilities to represent the amplitude and the structure of the error.
items.authors: Martin Bonte, St\'ephane Vannitsem

items.title: Identifying Arctic states vulnerable to rapid ice loss with a convolutional neural network
items.abstract: This work investigates the incidence of rapid ice-loss events in the Arctic, in which a substantial fraction of September sea-ice is lost in only a few years. Such events are seen to occur in climate model simulations forced with increasing greenhouse gas concentrations, but not as yet in the relatively short observational record. We train a convolutional neural network (CNN) using six large climate model ensembles to diagnose vulnerability to rapid ice-loss events. The trained model is shown to separate higher and lower risk states in out-of-sample climate models via a leave-one-out cross-validation. The model emphasises the role of persistently thin sea-ice, remaining sea-ice extent and sustained high upper ocean heat content as predictors of rapid ice-loss. The CNN is applied to observational data over the satelite-era showing a signal for rapid ice-loss prior to a drop around 2007 and an increasing risk from around 2015 to present. Such rapid-ice loss events would likely have dramatic consequences for Arctic ecosystems, coastal communities and global shipping.
items.authors: Matthew Patterson, Ioana Colfescu, Nathan Kirk, Graeme MacGhilchrist

items.title: Forecasting carbon-risk hotspots ahead of the extreme 2026 El Ni\~no
items.abstract: A potentially super El Ni\~no is forecasted in 2026, raising the need to anticipate land carbon-cycle risks before its impacts unfold. We develop a prospective early-warning framework that uses dynamic global vegetation models driven by an ensemble of ECMWF seasonal climate forecasts and machine-learning burned area predictions. Forecasts indicate a $0.23 \pm 0.21$ PgC reduction in global net biome productivity in the second half of 2026, with hotspots of sink weakening in eastern South America and elevated fire risk in Southeast Asia.
items.authors: Xiaomeng Du, Runda Jiang, Philippe Ciais, Pierre Friedlingstein, Stephen Sitch, Mike O'Sullivan, Jefferson Goncalves de Souza, Tim Stripp, Piyu Ke, Yi Xi, Minxuan Sun, Xiaoran Wu, Mengjie Han, Shanshan Song, Qiang Zhang, Wei Li

items.title: Extreme events and statistics in an AI emulator of a global storm-resolving model
items.abstract: We present HiRO-ACEv2 (High Resolution Output Ai2 Climate Emulator), a two-stage framework for AI emulation of the 3~km resolution X-SHiELD global storm-resolving model (GSRM), and highlight its ability to generate large ensembles of data for studying the characteristics of tropical cyclones and extreme events in high-resolution simulations at an inference computational cost over 300 times lower than that of traditional numerical GSRMs. HiRO-ACEv2 expands upon the precipitation-only HiRO-ACEv1 model to generate coherent precipitation, 10~m winds, and sea level pressure outputs, enabling a broader range of events to be simulated at high-resolution. Fine-resolution predictions are generated by running an autoregressive emulator of coarsened X-SHiELD at 100 km, whose multivariate outputs are regionally downscaled to 3~km resolution via a separately trained diffusion model. Particular importance is placed on capturing the statistics of extreme events during the diffusion downscaling step. Our ability to match the tails of distributions and generate realistic-looking extreme events in both the `perfect prediction' case as well as in free-running emulator rollouts is improved via the use of multiple denoisers at inference time and several updates to the data sampling, noise sampling, and loss weighting during training. HiRO-ACEv2 closely matches the high-resolution reference distributions of precipitation and near-surface winds out to their 99.9999th percentile values, and broadly tracks the reference distribution of tropical cyclone intensities.
items.authors: Anna Kwa, W. Andre Perkins, Troy Arcomano, Noah D. Brenowitz, Christopher S. Bretherton, Spencer K. Clark, Lucas M. Harris, Jeremy McGibbon, Michael S. Pritchard, Oliver Watt-Meyer

items.title: Cumulus parameterization controls simulated rainfall more than microphysics, but not at heavy thresholds: a 3 * 2 factorial WRF study over the Western Himalaya
items.abstract: Rainfall forecasts over the Western Himalaya remain poor, and the relative contributions of the cumulus and microphysics parameterizations to that error are not well constrained.
items.authors: Satyam Kumar, Akshay Sunil, Devesh Sheoran

items.title: Linking Horizontal and Vertical Submesoscale Lagrangian Dynamics South of the Ibiza Channel
items.abstract: Fronts, eddies, jets, and meanders populate the ocean surface and play a key role in organizing transport and mixing across a wide range of scales. From a Lagrangian perspective, frontal structures are conveniently detected as surface filaments that act as barriers to horizontal transport. However, the degree to which these structures maintain coherence below the surface and the relationship between horizontal and vertical motions in their vicinity remain poorly understood. Here we analyze two such filaments in the western Mediterranean Sea, south of the Ibiza Channel, using a high-resolution ocean simulation and Lagrangian diagnostics specifically designed to characterize submesoscale transport. Backward Finite-Size Lyapunov Exponents (FSLE) computed at successive depths reveal nearly vertical, curtain-like structures extending several tens of meters into the water column, with intensity decreasing with depth. Vertical-velocity sections across the filaments show coherent downward motion aligned with the filament cores, while Lagrangian trajectories indicate rapid horizontal convergence of fluid particles accompanied by sustained downward displacement. The barrier effect of Lagrangian Coherent Structures (LCSs) is commonly associated with persistent dynamical features of large-scale flows. Here, however, we demonstrate that FSLE filaments generated by rapidly fluctuating submesoscale dynamics can also act as effective transport barriers. The results demonstrate that the surface signatures of Lagrangian filaments identified through FSLE techniques correspond to three-dimensional transport structures that regulate both lateral aggregation and vertical connectivity in the upper ocean.
items.authors: Sara Cloux, Ismael Hernandez-Carrasco, Alejandro Orfila, Emilio Hernandez-Garcia, Cristobal Lopez

items.title: Planar intrusions from a narrow, jet-like source in a linearly stratified ambient
items.abstract: We present two and three dimensional direct numerical simulations of planar intrusions injected from a continuously supplied, narrow source into a linearly stratified ambient at the level of neutral buoyancy. The evolution passes through three phases. A laminar leading vortex dipole first advances at constant speed with a varicose wave train behind it; the trailing jet then undergoes a sinuous instability whose initial growth rate and wavelength agree with inviscid unstratified planar-jet theory evaluated on the local jet; the flow finally relaxes into a buoyancy-controlled wedge whose area grows linearly in time. Three-dimensional simulations show that the transition remains organized by the planar instability, while three-dimensionality reshapes the near-source region into a slowly evolving, actively mixing zone that entrains an additional twenty to one hundred percent of the source flux depending on source width. Rescaled with this measured effective flux, the downstream intrusion collapses reasonably well onto the similarity solution for a wide-source intrusion.
items.authors: Hai Duc Vu, Murray Rudman, Anja Slim

items.title: Interaction of eccentricity tide and convection
items.abstract: Aim. We try to understand the interaction of eccentricity tide and convection in icy satellites. Method. We use the numerical calculation of rotating convection with eccentricity tide in a spherical shell. Results. We have the following results. (1) Energy scaling exponent about buoyancy force (or tidal force) decreases with increasing tidal force (or buoyancy force). (2) The combined tide-convection flow is not identical to superposition of two pure flows in respect of energy spectrum. (3) Tide controls large-scale of fluid motion but convection is important for small scale, and the mode-mode transition occurs at intermediate scales. (4) Tide suppresses heat transport efficiency. (5) Dissipation of kinetic energy scales as square of tidal force with a very weak dependence on buoyancy force, which has little impact on dissipation but suppresses the tidal influence on dissipation.
items.authors: Jiachen Zheng, Xing Wei

items.title: Preferential concentration of cloud droplets: Coupled effects of phase change and gravitational settling
items.abstract: Cloud droplets respond to turbulent motion with finite inertia and settle under gravity, while condensation and evaporation change their sizes. The nonuniform accumulation of cloud droplets in turbulent flows, known as preferential concentration, has attracted sustained interest because it affects droplet collision and coalescence rates. We develop an analytical theory that quantifies the coupled effects of droplet inertia, gravitational settling, and phase change on concentration changes. Applying this theory to simulations of two-dimensional homogeneous thermal convection reveals that phase change markedly enhances preferential concentration in this flow, primarily through spatial differences in settling speed. These differences arise because droplets experience different thermodynamic histories along their trajectories and thus acquire different sizes. Droplet transport further increases this settling contribution by rearranging droplets of different sizes. Fluid deformation partly offsets this enhancement by thinning concentration structures, reducing the preferential concentration measured at a fixed spatial scale.
items.authors: Zi-Mo Liao

items.title: Some generalizations of the tornado model
items.abstract: A possible mechanism of tornado generation is associated with the Schwarzschild criterion for convective instability. The supercooled cloud-air mixture near the axis starts to descend and, due to the super adiabatic temperature gradient, the overheated near-surface air mass rises. The complete system of equations for full model includes equations for the stream function, for the azimuthal velocity component, and for the change in density. The refined model considers rotating convection within the framework of ideal hydrodynamics. The simplest model uses a separate equation for the stream function and can be applied to the initial stage of vortex generation. Within the framework of the simplest model, an analytical solution is combined from 8 linear dependencies by height. Rotation increases due to the conservation of angular momentum. Within the framework of the refined model, some unidirectional differential rotation arises, but it depends on boundary conditions (can be local). The full model studies the tornado development as rotating convection from the very beginning to the quasi-stationary stage. Velocity components increase in a coordinated manner. Two cases are considered: a single whirlwind and a two-eyed tornado. Radial flows converge towards the central part of the tornado near the earth surface, and there is an outflow from the "wall" to the axis and to the periphery near the top of the tornado. The maximum vertical velocity component is achieved at a certain radial distance at a certain height. The maximum azimuthal velocity component is achieved in the tornado "wall". Tornado generation criteria are discussed.
items.authors: S. N. Artekha

items.title: Establishing baseline model performances for optical turbulence forecasting
items.abstract: Accurate forecasting of optical turbulence (OT) is useful to optimise telescope scheduling and maximising observing efficiency, as the performance of adaptive optics systems strongly depends on turbulence conditions. While various numerical weather prediction and machine learning models are developed to predict these complex turbulence properties, properly evaluating their added value requires well-defined baseline reference models. This study establishes baseline performance thresholds for key astroclimatic parameters using two distinct models: one forecasting the parameter average over a specific timescale, and the other forecasting the temporal evolution over the same specific timescale. We apply these frameworks to extensive, multi-year datasets from the sites of the Very Large Telescope (VLT) and the Large Binocular Telescope (LBT) and discuss the possibility of extrapolating reference values of forecast performances for other sites based on their optical turbulence statistical characteristics. Our results show that baseline predictive accuracy varies according to the observing site, the specific parameter, the chosen timescale, and the forecasting approach. Therefore, an OT forecasting model's accuracy cannot be quantified in absolute terms, but relatively to the baseline.
items.authors: M. De Sepibus (INAF - Osservatorio Astrofisico di Arcetri, Florence, Italy, ADONI, ADaptive Optics National laboratory of INAF), E. Masciadri (INAF - Osservatorio Astrofisico di Arcetri, Florence, Italy, ADONI, ADaptive Optics National laboratory of INAF), C. Weinberger (INAF - Osservatorio Astrofisico di Arcetri, Florence, Italy, ADONI, ADaptive Optics National laboratory of INAF), A. Otarola (European Southern Observatory, Alonso de C\'ordova, Santiago, Chile), S. Miesske (European Southern Observatory, Alonso de C\'ordova, Santiago, Chile), C. Veillet (Large Binocular Telescope, Tucson, AZ, USA), S. Ragland (Large Binocular Telescope, Tucson, AZ, USA)

items.title: Simulations of the Evolving Ozone Layer: Implications for the Early Earth, Exoplanets, and the Search For Life
items.abstract: Over 4 billion years, Earth's atmosphere has been transformed from a composition devoid of molecular oxygen (O$_2$) to one where O$_2$ is now 21% of our modern atmosphere by volume. With high quantities of O$_2$, an ozone (O$_3$) layer can form and partially shield the surface from biologically harmful ultraviolet radiation (UV). The evolution of the O$_3$ layer has previously been simulated under the modern Sun by independent groups with separate models. Here, we present simulations of Earth's atmosphere from four open-source one-dimensional (1D) photochemical models and a 3D chemistry-climate model, focussing on O$_3$. We find that the O$_3$ layer thickness exhibits a clear deviation between the 1D models and the 3D model due to several factors, including treatments of O$_2$ photolysis, chemical networks, H$_2$O microphysics and 3D transport. We find that 1D models introduce a bias for unobserved climate states and show how these biases may propagate to calculations of biological UV damage and surface habitability. We show that when applied to specific exoplanet atmospheres, these discrepancies can become more pronounced, propagating through to observational predictions for the next generation of telescopes, such as HWO and LIFE, that will search for habitable and inhabited exoplanets.
items.authors: Akhil Kumar, Gregory J. Cooke

items.title: Isolating Balanced Ocean Dynamics in SWOT Data
items.abstract: The Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) mission provides two-dimensional sea surface height anomaly (SSHA) maps at unprecedented resolution, but its signal is a combination of balanced meso- and submesoscale turbulence, unbalanced motions such as internal waves, and small-scale noise. Interpreting the meso- and submesoscale flow features captured by SWOT requires careful isolation of the balanced signal. We present a statistical method to do so in regions where internal tides make a negligible contribution to the SSHA signal, such as western boundary current regions and the Southern Ocean. Our method assumes Gaussian statistics as a Bayesian prior for both the balanced flow and the remainder of the signal, and we infer their respective covariance functions by fitting parametric models to the observed SSHA wavenumber spectrum. Using these inferred covariance functions, we perform a Bayesian inversion to produce swath-aligned SSHA maps that isolate the balanced signal and fill the nadir gap. We evaluate the method using synthetic data from a high-resolution simulation with realistic SWOT-like small-scale noise added. Comparisons with the underlying model data show that our inversion successfully removes the unbalanced small-scale signal while preserving meso- and submesoscale eddies, fronts, and filaments down to a spatial feature scale (the inverse angular wavenumber) of about 6 km in the subtropical Northwest Atlantic region used for illustration. This comparison also demonstrates that the posterior uncertainty is a reliable estimate of the error. While our focus is on balanced dynamics, the balanced extraction can be extended to include tides, internal waves, and non-Gaussian priors.
items.authors: Jack William Skinner, J\"orn Callies, Albion Lawrence, Xihan Zhang

items.title: Effects of the Coriolis force on the coherent structures in conventionally neutral atmospheric boundary layers
items.abstract: It is well known that the Coriolis force due to Earth's rotation can induce wind veer in the mean flow velocity of an atmospheric boundary layer (ABL), but much less is known about its effects on turbulent coherent structures. In this work, large-eddy simulation (LES) is employed to investigate the effects of the Coriolis force on the characteristics of turbulent coherent structures in the conventionally neutral atmospheric boundary layers (CNBL). Variation of the Coriolis force is realized by changing latitude or geostrophic wind speed. We found that the Coriolis force causes distinct deflection of coherent velocity structures to the geostrophic wind direction, which is not aligned with the direction of either the mean wind or the mean shear. When a relative structure deflection angle is plotted against a relative local wind veer angle, a universal relationship between them can be established regardless of latitude or geostrophic wind speed. Moreover, we also studied the effect of the Coriolis force on the inclination of large-scale turbulent structures. It is found that the inclination angle in the surface layer varies under different conditions, which is probably due to the deflection of turbulent structures caused by the Coriolis force.
items.authors: Changlong Wang, Luoqin Liu, Xiang I. A. Yang, Ruifeng Hu

items.title: PepC-Global: A Basin-Tuned Probabilistic Tropical Cyclone Model with Enhanced Out-of-Sample Skill and Climate-Sensitive Over-Land Decay
items.abstract: We present PepC-Global, a global version of the Princeton environment-dependent probabilistic tropical cyclone (PepC) framework that uniquely implements basin-wise tuning within a single unified tropical cyclone climatology model. PepC-Global represents tropical cyclone climatology as a coupled stochastic process linking genesis, track, and intensity conditioned on large-scale environmental predictors. Each of the genesis, track, and intensity modules outperforms widely used linear models in out-of-sample tests. The intensity module also incorporates an environment-dependent over-land decay model, offering greater sensitivity to climate change signals than conventional fixed decay rate approaches. Systematic evaluation against observations demonstrates that PepC-Global closely reproduces genesis basin-wise frequency, seasonal cycles, interannual variability, and spatial distributions. The model also accurately captures basin-wise track patterns, along-coastline landfall frequency, and intensity statistics including lifetime maximum intensity and landfall intensity distributions. PepC-Global provides a versatile tool for probabilistic tropical cyclone hazard and risk assessment and a practical framework for investigating changes in tropical cyclone activity across future climate scenarios.
items.authors: Cong Gao, Ning Lin

items.title: Cosmic Rays as an Interdisciplinary Earth Observation Tool: From Particle Physics and Atmospheric Processes to Geosciences and Urban Science
items.abstract: The exploration of cosmic rays, which are high-energy particles originating from space and the atmosphere, has historically been associated with particle physics and astrophysics. In the last 20 years, these particles have evolved into valuable tools for observing Earth's systems. This review compiles the use of cosmic rays in three primary areas: (1) particle physics and atmospheric processes, which include cosmic- ray-induced cascades, ionization, and their impact on atmospheric chemistry and radiation; (2) geosciences, where cosmogenic radionuclides assist in the dating of geological materials and cosmic-ray neutrons are used for large-scale monitoring of soil moisture and snow water equivalents; and (3) urban science, where cosmic- ray muons are employed for non-invasive subsurface imaging and, when paired with distributed sensors, serve as the basis for smart city monitoring. This review places particular emphasis on integrating these methods with remote sensing and geographic information systems (GIS), which helps close the persistent scale gap between point measurements and satellite observations, thereby enabling three-dimensional digital representations of subsurfaces.
