This review concludes by discussing data standards, their integration into operational Earth observation workflows, and future research directions.
items.authors: Bugra Bilin, Nuhcan Ak\c{c}it

items.title: Plume Segmentation from MethaneSAT with Cross-Sensor Transfer Learning and Physics-Informed Postprocessing
items.abstract: Automated detection and masking of individual methane plumes from satellite imagery is important for operational emission attribution and quantification. We present a machine learning framework for plume detection from MethaneSAT retrieved column-averaged dry-air mole fractions of methane. We address two core challenges: the scarcity of labeled MethaneSAT data and the need for inference reliability across diverse atmospheric and surface conditions. We first demonstrate that Mask R-CNN with a ResNet-50 backbone outperforms a U-Net semantic segmentation baseline on both MethaneAIR (an airborne version of MethaneSAT) and MethaneSAT data, with pixel-level F1 score gains of 10.49 and 5.48 percentage points respectively. To address MethaneSAT data scarcity, we evaluate three cross-sensor transfer strategies leveraging MethaneAIR flights and synthetic plumes. Mask R-CNN with ResNet-50 fine-tuned from MethaneAIR pre-trained weights is the most effective strategy, achieving instance-level precision of 0.60 and recall of 0.98 at the baseline operating point. A physics-informed post-processing pipeline converts detections into two operationally distinct modes. The first is a high-sensitivity mode that applies morphological filtering and proximity-based merging for comprehensive emission screening, achieving precision of 0.71 and recall of 0.94. The second is a high-precision mode that additionally applies a distribution-based classifier for confident source attribution, achieving precision of 0.92 and recall of 0.70. Manual review of detections classified as false positives against our wavelet-based reference plume mask labels shows that some correspond to real methane enhancements... Our data and code used in this work are publicly available at: https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/FR959H
items.authors: Manuel P\'erez-Carrasco, Maya Nasr, Zhan Zhang, Apisada Chulakadabba, Javier Roger, Raia Ottenheimer, S\'ebastien Roche, Maryann Sargent, Chris Chan Miller, Daniel Varon, Jack Warren, Luis Guanter, Kang Sun, Jonathan Franklin, Jia Chen, Cecilia Garraffo, Xiong Liu, Ritesh Gautam, Steven Wofsy

items.title: Latent Diffusion Modeling of Two- and Three-dimensional Fracture Networks with Sparse Observation Conditioning
items.abstract: Characterizing subsurface fracture networks is challenging because geometry and connectivity are sparsely observed and uncertain away from measurements. We develop a latent diffusion framework for unconditional and observation-conditioned generation of two-dimensional (2D) and three-dimensional (3D) fracture networks. Fractures and the surrounding matrix are represented as binary fields and compressed by a variational autoencoder into compact spatial latent representations, where an Elucidated Diffusion Model learns their distribution. The 3D model operates on native volumetric fields, with a reconstruction objective designed to preserve sparse, thin fracture structures. Sparse borehole observations are incorporated through a conditioning encoder, classifier-free guidance, and diffusion posterior sampling. Generated ensembles reproduce key fracture-network statistics, including fracture area/volume fraction, two-point correlation, and chord-length distributions. Reconstructed fracture counts and gas-production responses are comparable to those of the reference networks under the considered multiphase flow scenarios. Conditional generation satisfies 99.6% of prescribed well observations in 2D. In 3D, where vertical boreholes constrain full voxel columns, conditional realizations satisfy 84.2% of observed well voxels while maintaining fracture volume and geometry comparable to the reference ensemble. These results demonstrate the potential of latent diffusion models as compact probabilistic representations for fracture-network characterization, ensemble generation, and sparse-observation conditioning.
items.authors: Jiawei Shen, Hongkyu Yoon, Jonghyun Lee

items.title: Global Structure-Constrained 4D prestack inversion
items.abstract: Prestack seismic inversion often suffers from inherent ill-posedness and is significantly affected by complex factors such as the wavelets, parameter coupling, heterogeneous media, fault displacements, and stratigraphic variations, making it difficult for the conventional inversion methods to accurately recover subsurface information. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a global inversion method based on multi-dimensional matrix multiplication to optimize the inversion results under structure constraints. This method first represents the inversion model as a four-dimensional tensor representing spatial and parameter dimensions. By performing multi-dimensional matrix multiplication operations in various directions of the model, a multi-dimensional tensor of observed data is effectively constructed. Secondly, multi-dimensional regularization are introduced. By analyzing the impact of different dimensional constraints on the inversion results, targeted parameter selection and adjustment are achieved, significantly enhancing the stability of the inversion process and effectively suppressing noise. Finally, stratigraphic and fault constraints extracted from seismic interpretation are incorporated to improve the geological coherence and reasonableness of the inversion results. Both synthetic and field data experiments demonstrate that the proposed method effectively enhances the robustness of inversion in complex structural areas while maintaining high computational efficiency, validating its effectiveness in practical applications.
items.authors: Qingwei Zhao, Xuehua Chen, Shengyi Wang, Cong Wang, Gang Zhao

items.title: Bayesian Inversion Beyond the Generator's Range: Reducing Non-physical Constraints from Generative Neural Networks
items.abstract: To address non-uniqueness in geophysical inversions, Generative Neural Networks (GNNs) are often used to parameterise geological or other prior information in a lower-dimensional space (the so-called latent space), thereby reducing the number of inversion parameters. However, the training samples that represent this information are then always incorrect, because Earth structure is not intrinsically low-dimensional, and all GNNs are subject to training errors. Consequently, even when solutions are mapped back to the original higher-dimensional space, they inherit this imperfection and remain restricted to a low-dimensional manifold. From a mathematical point of view, latent space inversion thus fails fundamentally: generally, it can not even reproduce the best, higher-dimensional approximation to the true Earth. To overcome this limitation, we introduce an `escaping prior' distribution, which provides the necessary freedom to find solutions beyond the manifold of GNN-generated solutions, while still using the GNN as a guide. We use a hierarchical Bayesian approach to adapt the strength of prior information to the observed data and synthetic forward function $\textit{a posteriori}$. We illustrate our method on low-dimensional problems where the escaping prior is defined over a 1D manifold in 2D space. We then compare our approach with standard latent space and model space inversions using a uniform prior distribution in synthetic tomography problems, ranging from simple to more geologically realistic cases. Furthermore, we tested scenarios where the true solution is either far from or close to the manifold. In each case, our escaping prior shows significantly better results than the alternatives. It results in solutions beyond each GNN's generative capabilities, solutions which include the best possible model, and clearly demonstrates the limitations of latent space inversion.
items.authors: Pratyay Roy, Xuebin Zhao, Andrew Curtis

items.title: Design and Implementation of a 25-Yr Pseudoprospective Earthquake Forecasting Experiment in China (AoyuX)
items.abstract: Forecast models in statistical seismology are commonly evaluated using log-likelihood (LL) scores for the full distribution $P(n)$ of earthquake counts. However, fat tails and out-of-range observations (realized counts exceed all simulations) can bias model rankings. We develop a tail-aware framework that estimates cell-wise $P(n)$ using adaptive Gaussian kernel density estimation and compares three treatments of out-of-range counts: power-law extrapolation, a fixed minimum probability, and exclusion. Using the AoyuX platform, we conduct a 25-year (2000--2023) month-by-month pseudoprospective experiment in the China Seismic Experimental Site. We compare an epidemic-type aftershock sequence model with a homogeneous background, ETAS$\mu$, with a spatially heterogeneous variant, ETAS$\mu(x,y)$, across six spatial resolutions and five magnitude thresholds, using 100,000 simulations per forecast window. Count distributions follow power laws, $P(n) \sim n^{-(1+a)}$, with $a \approx 1.02 \pm 0.23$, yielding a productivity exponent $\alpha = 0.83 \pm 0.19$ for $b = 0.85 \pm 0.002$. Model rankings depend on tail treatment: power-law extrapolation is theoretically justified and empirically most robust, whereas occasional advantages of the fixed-probability approach in coarse, low-magnitude settings are attributable to noise. Cumulative information gain shows that ETAS$\mu(x,y)$ outperforms ETAS$\mu$ in data-rich configurations, especially for $M_t = 3.0$--$3.5$ and whole-region tests. Positive mean information gain is concentrated where earthquakes with $M \geq 5$ occurred, whereas stochastic fluctuations dominate data-poor settings. A coefficient-of-variation analysis distinguishes genuine upward trends from noise. The framework supports statistically grounded evaluation of earthquake forecasting models.
items.authors: Jiawei Li, Qingyuan Zhang, Didier Sornette

items.title: Enhanced Seismicity Monitoring in the Rapid Scientific Response to the 2025 Santorini Crisis
items.abstract: We used a deep learning workflow to enhance earthquake detection during the 2025 seismic unrest between Santorini and Amorgos islands to track the evolution of the crisis in near real-time. We analysed the continuous seismic waveforms daily (1/2 - 3/3/25) as the crisis unfolded. Our analysis enhanced the earthquake catalogue from around 4,000 to 80,000 earthquakes. The enhanced catalogue allowed this international expert group to identify the volcanic-tectonic character, clearly revealing burst-like, spasmodic seismicity swarms, which is a pattern associated with fluid-driven processes from early stages of the crisis. Detailed moment tensor inversions in early events characterised by a significant non-double couple component indicated the involvement of magmatic or high-pressure hydrothermal fluids driving the unrest. Concurrent DL-enhanced tomography efforts identified a third, deep magmatic reservoir beneath Anydros Islet, consistent with pressure-driven processes. To date, volcanic-tectonic swarms in which >200 earthquakes of ML > 4 occurred within only a few weeks, largely within episodic bursts of seismicity, have not been observed elsewhere.
items.authors: Margarita Segou, Foteini Dervisi, Xing Tan, Rajat Choudhary, Patricia Mart\'inez-Garz\'on, Francesco Scotto di Uccio, Gregory Beroza, Genny Giacomuzzi, Claudio Chiarabba, Wayne Shelley, Stephanie Prejean, Jeremy Pesicek, John J. Wellik, Marco Bohnhoff, David Pyle, Costas Synolakis, Tom Parsons, Athanassios Ganas, William Ellsworth, Brian Baptie, Gaetano Festa, Piero Poli, Warner Marzocchi

items.title: A Spectral-Domain Pseudo-Inverse Method for True 3D Gravity Inversion
items.abstract: The main difficulty in 3D gravity inversion is that surface observations lack vertical wavenumber information, making the problem underdetermined and depth resolution poor. Building on the author's spectral-domain pseudo-inverse theory for unitary diagonalizable systems, this paper presents a true 3D inversion method. Surface data are analytically continued upward via Laplace's equation to form a 3D data volume, providing the vertical wavenumber sampling for the 3D Fourier transform. A general analytical expression for the half-space spectrum is derived, separating the horizontal spectrum from the vertical propagation kernel. The Green's function of the 3D Poisson equation is unitarily diagonalized, yielding the forward spectral response $\lambda(\kk) = -i 4\pi G k_z / K^2$, and a stable inverse filter $q_\alpha(\lambda) = \bar{\lambda}/(|\lambda|^2 + \alpha)$ is constructed. This filter is proved to have bounded stability and consistency (reducing to the exact inverse as $\alpha \to 0^+$). Validation with a homogeneous sphere model shows correct recovery of the anomaly location and singular behavior at the source. The contributions are twofold: (1) upward continuation constructs a 3D volume from 2D surface data, which does not add physical observations but unfolds the 3D spatial variation information (data innovation) derived through the governing physical equation; (2) the inversion is reduced to one forward 3D Fourier transform, one spectral scaling, and one inverse transform. The framework extends to any linear potential-field inverse problem with a translation-invariant forward operator, including magnetic inversion.
items.authors: Shengchang Chen

items.title: Chemical transport by weakly nonlinear internal gravity waves in stars
items.abstract: While internal gravity waves (IGWs) are known to transport chemicals in the radiative zones of stars, substantial uncertainty remains regarding the magnitude and physical mechanisms of this transport. Most previous studies have relied on heuristic theories or numerical simulations that are difficult to extrapolate to stellar parameters. In this work, we present the first rigorous asymptotic calculation of (passive) chemical transport by IGWs, in the limit of small wave amplitude. The net vertical transport induced by a coherent packet of waves is found to be proportional to the horizontal mean of $(w^S+w^E)^2$, where $w^S$ and $w^E$ are the vertical Stokes and Eulerian mean velocities. The transport scales as the fourth power of wave amplitude and quadratically with time, and we verify these scalings with numerical simulations. In the weakly damped regime, the dominant transport coefficients scale as $\omega^{-2}\kappa^2$, where $\omega$ is the wave frequency and $\kappa$ is the radiative diffusivity. Because the transport can be positive or negative depending on the wave phases, the effective mixing induced by the superposition of coherent wave packets is expected to scale with the eighth power of wave amplitude. These results provide a theoretical foundation for making accurate predictions of IGW-induced chemical transport in stellar evolution models.
items.authors: Yifeng Mao, Daniel Lecoanet

items.title: Earthquake Dynamics as a Benchmark for Scale-Invariant Behavior
items.abstract: We analyze regional earthquake energy statistics from the Southern California and Japan seismic catalogs and find scale-invariant energy distributions characterized by an exponent $\tau \simeq 1.67$. To quantify how closely scale-invariant dynamics with different exponent values resemble real earthquakes, we generate synthetic energy distributions over a wide range of $\tau$ under conditions of constant activity. Earthquake-like behavior, in a broad sense, is obtained for $1.5 \leqslant \tau 2$
items.authors: Kilian Duplat, German Varas, Osvanny Ramos

items.title: A Highly Stable Cyclic (Amino)(Aryl)Nitrenium Radical Dication Exhibiting Temperature-Dependent Radical Bistability Maruti Suryavansi,a Manas Khatua,b,d Bappaditya Goswami,c Apurba Kumar Pal,a Subhas Samanta,*d and K. Geetharani*
items.abstract: Development of air- and thermally stable organic radicals remains challenging due to the highly transient nature of the free radicals. Herein, we present a strategy for isolating a highly stable N-heterocyclic carbenes (NHCs) stabilized cyclic (amino)(aryl)nitrenium (CAArN) radical. This is the first example of a CAArN radical isolated in the solid state, and its identity has been confirmed by single-crystal X-ray diffraction and various spectroscopic studies. These CAArN radical exhibits remarkable stability towards air, water, strong acidic/alkaline conditions, aqueous buffers, and high temperature (~412 °C). The radical residing on two distinct redoxactive motifs exhibits unique temperature-dependent bistability in solution, as evidenced by VT-EPR and VT-UV-vis spectral studies. Polar solvents have played a crucial role in stabilizing the imidazolium motif, thereby facilitating the radical bistability. Further, by employing KC8, selective reduction of the NHC-moiety bonded to the CAArN radical was achieved to yield Thiele’s type hybrid diradicaloid.
items.authors: Geetharani K

items.title: Light and magnetism in the origin of extraterrestrial enantiomer excesses
items.abstract: Chiral compounds are composed of non-superimposable mirror-images, or enantiomers, typically designated as D- or L-isomers. The macromolecular structures of biopolymers share a critical trait known as homochirality: the exclusive presence of a single enantiomeric form within their organic building blocks. Understanding the origin of biological homochirality has been an active area of research for nearly two centuries. Our goal was to demonstrate the first de novo synthesis of individual sugar derivatives containing enantiomer excesses (ee), the precursor of homochirality. We specifically employed prebiotically plausible experimental conditions: reactions were performed in aqueous solutions utilizing the formose sugar-synthesis pathway. This system consisted of simple, ubiquitous interstellar precursor molecules, such as formaldehyde and glycolaldehyde, alongside common abiotic ions, mild radiation, and magnetism. Analysis of products by chiral gas chromatography–mass spectrometry demonstrated ee production and, critically, reversible control of the dominant enantiomer by varying the magnetic-field direction. The ability to repeatably determine relative enantiomer abundance, and the ubiquitous nature of interstellar formaldehyde, magnetism and radiation, imply that ee might be cosmically widespread. These findings may also have implications for identifying the long-sought source of ee deeply embedded within extraterrestrial insoluble organic matter.
items.authors: George Cooper, William M. Jackson, Andro C. Rios, Katie J. Yeung, David J. Des Marais

items.title: Editing-site selection for constrained QED improvement through frozen GenMol remasking
items.abstract: Shallow network, boosted decision-tree and graph-attention models were trained on a remaskingsite selection task utilizing the GenMol generator and a subset of bioactive molecules (30,000 training and 5,000 validation) from the ChEMBL 37 dataset. Models learned to optimize fragment selection policies by maximizing the fraction of successful remasked candidates, with success contingent on an increase in the RDKit quantitative estimate of drug-likeness (QED) under several chemical constraints. All three models show a marked increase in generation of at least one successful derivative out of 16 remasking runs on a held-out test set comprising 5,000 bioactive molecules: 66.0%–66.9%, 67.0%–67.4% and 66.3%–66.7% for the shallow network, boosted decision-tree and graph models, compared to 54.8%–55.6% for a fixed policy selecting the largest fragment (one-sided bootstrap 𝑝 10−4 for all models). A trivial baseline, selecting fragments randomly, displays 47.3% success. The fraction of valid candidates produced by all policies is about 99%. Analysis of learned policies showed consistent trends among the three models. Selection is biased toward larger pendants. Additionally, pendant selection shows several trends conditioned on the pendant-side, but not core-side, attachment atom. Larger carbon-and oxygen-attached fragments are selected more often (two-sided binomial 𝑝 10−10 in every model); a reversed tendency, albeit not statistically significant (𝑝 ≈ 0.02–0.30), is observed for nitrogen attachments. Controlling for fragment size, learned policies show preference for pendant-side nitrogen over oxygen and carbon, and for both chlorine and bromine over fluorine and carbon. Only LightGBM displays a statistically significant (two-sided exact binomial 𝑝 0.01) preference for sp2 over sp3 hybridization of pendant-side carbon atoms. At equal size, carbonyl-attached pendants are preferred to hydrocarbons.
items.authors: Tom Brenner

items.title: Structural Order Reversed: Local and Average Structure Across the Ammonia Borane Phase Transition
items.abstract: Ammonia borane (NH3BH3) is a hydrogen rich molecular solid whose structural behaviour is governed by molecular orientation and N–H· · ·H–B dihydrogen interactions. Its temperature-dependent phase transition is conventionally described as an order–disorder transition from a disordered tetragonal phase to a more ordered orthorhombic phase. However, this description does not fully capture the underlying local structure. Single crystal X-ray diffraction, X-ray total scattering, Pair Distribution Function (PDF) analysis and Reverse Monte Carlo (RMC) modelling reveal an unexpected inversion of local structural order across the phase transition. At 300 K, despite pronounced disorder in the average tetragonal structure, the local structure exhibits three preferential NH3 orientations, whereas the BH3 groups remain substantially disordered. In contrast, at 100 K, modelling reveals substantial local disorder of NH3 despite the more ordered average orthorhombic structure. Single crystal diffraction additionally reveals weak satellite reflections, while the 100 K powder diffraction pattern is better reproduced by a trial commensurately modulated model with threefold periodicity than by the conventional average structure. Together, these results indicate that the low temperature phase combines periodic structural modulation with substantial local disorder, demonstrating that average and local structural order do not evolve in parallel with temperature.
items.authors: Anna Piekara, Damian Trzybiński, Ewelina Zaorska, Wojciech A. Sławiński, Wojciech Slawinski

items.title: Arsenite (Trisenox) Bridges the Redox Centers of Thioredoxin Reductase
items.abstract: Arsenic trioxide (Trisenox) is an effective treatment for acute promyelocytic leukemia and is being explored for broader anticancer applications, yet our understanding of the molecular basis of its anticancer activity remains incomplete. Under physiological conditions arsenic trioxide forms arsenite, As(OH)3, which has been proposed to target the thioredoxin system. Here, we investigate the structural basis of arsenite interaction with mammalian thioredoxin reductase 1 (TrxR1, TXNRD1), a flavoenzyme selenoprotein essential for maintaining cellular redox homeostasis. Arsenic and selenium K-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy, including highenergy resolution fluorescence detected (HERFD)-XAS, were combined with site-directed mutagenesis and density functional theory calculations. Wild-type TrxR1 forms a well-defined As(SeR)(SR)2 coordination environment in which arsenite binds the catalytic selenocysteine residue Sec498 and bridges the C-terminal and N-terminal redox centers of the enzyme. Replacement of Sec498 by cysteine yields an As(OH)(SR)2 species, whereas substitution by serine abolishes detectable binding. These results provide the first direct structural characterization of arsenite bound to TrxR1 and reveal a mechanism by which arsenite inhibits catalysis through crosslinking of the enzyme's redox centers. The findings establish a molecular basis for targeting of the thioredoxin system by arsenic trioxide and provide new insight into the chemistry underlying its anticancer activity.
items.authors: Emerita Mendoza Rengifo, Clinton Kidman, Linda I. Vogt, Julien J. H. Cotelesage, Thomas Kroll, Dimosthenis Sokaras

items.title: DeNoMAP: An Interactive Web Application for Multi-Criteria Prioritization of De Novo Designed Compounds
items.abstract: De novo molecular generation is increasingly used in drug discovery, yet deciding which generated structures merit follow-up remains difficult, because established benchmarking metrics primarily characterize generative models rather than individual compounds. We present DeNoMAP, a general multi-criteria prioritization framework implemented as an interactive, open-access web application, which positions de novo-generated molecules in a normalized three-dimensional space defined by novelty, synthesizability and drug-likeness. A user-defined desirability zone enables transparent and reproducible candidate selection. Novelty is computed against ZINC20 as an external reference collection using the SmallWorld search engine, rather than against the generative model’s training set. Applied to a published library of 8,066 DNMT1 candidates, the web application identified 15 prioritized compounds among 852 successfully evaluated cluster representatives. DeNoMAP is publicly available at https://denomap.streamlit.app/ and its source code at https://github.com/flfeitosa/DeNoMAP.
items.authors: Francisco L. Feitosa, Erik D. Díaz-Dionisio, Juan F. Avellaneda-Tamayo, Carolina Horta Andrade, José L. Medina-Franco

items.title: Microstructure–Driven Degradation Mechanisms in High-Nickel NMC Cathodes for Lithium-Ion Batteries
items.abstract: Mechanical degradation in high-nickel layered oxide cathodes is closely associated with anisotropic lattice-parameter changes during electrochemical cycling, yet how cathode microstructure size influences the resulting crystallographic deformation remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate two LiNi0.90Mn0.05Co0.05O2 (NMC955) cathodes with comparable secondary-particle sizes but different average grain sizes (1.0 and 0.5 µm). The fine-grained cathode delivers 30% higher initial discharge capacity, 40% lower voltage polarization, improved rate capability, and 13% higher capacity retention after 100 cycles. Despite its superior electrochemical performance, the fine-grained material exhibits approximately 1.23 times higher mean kernel average misorientation after 100 cycles, together with higher estimated geometrically necessary dislocation density, indicating greater average local lattice curvature. The coarse-grained cathode shows pronounced localization of crystallographic misorientation near grain boundaries and secondary-particle peripheries, whereas the fine-grained cathode exhibits a more spatially distributed misorientation response. Complementary chemo-mechanical simulations reproduce the grain-size-dependent trends in lattice curvature and reveal differences in the spatial distribution of plastic strain associated with the different grain sizes. After 100 cycles, the coarse-grained cathode undergoes extensive intergranular cracking and secondary-particle fragmentation, while the fine-grained cathode largely preserves its structural integrity. These findings identify the spatial localization of cycling-induced crystallographic misorientation, rather than its average magnitude alone, as a pivotal variable for electrode design.
items.authors: Yosra Dammak, Soroush Motahari, Mahander Pratap Singh, Adam Miles, Poonam Yadav, Pradhyun Veerapanaicker Soundaraj

items.title: Balancing composition and phase stability in High-Entropy Metal Phosphates for proton conduction
items.abstract: The transition to sustainable energy technologies necessitates the development of proton-conducting electrolytes free from critical raw materials. Transition metal phosphate octahydrates (vivanite and pakhmoskyite analogues) offer a promising structural platform for proton transport via the vehicle mechanism, yet their performance is typically dominated by specific cation identity, with cobalt-based systems serving as the benchmark. This study investigates a high-entropy design strategy to decouple proton conductivity from cobalt reliance by stabilizing complex solid solutions containing up to several distinct metal cations (Ni, Co, Fe, Mn, Mg, Cu, Cd, Zn) within the phosphate octahydrate framework. Using a low-temperature aqueous precipitation method, we successfully synthesized single-phase high-entropy metal phosphates (HEMPs) and systematically evaluated their proton conductivity at 25 °C and 80 °C. While binary and ternary systems often require high cobalt concentrations to maintain performance, high-entropy compositions demonstrate a synergistic effect where increased configurational entropy correlates strongly with enhanced conductivity. Statistical analysis using Random Forest and ridge regression reveals that at 80 °C, configurational entropy surpasses cobalt content as the primary driver of transport performance. This entropy-driven enhancement allows for the significant reduction of cobalt to ~ca. 40 mol% without compromising conductivity, with optimised systems achieving values comparable to or exceeding the pure cobalt benchmark. These findings validate the high-entropy approach as a viable pathway for designing sustainable, high-performance proton conductors, demonstrating that structural disorder can effectively compensate for the reduction of chemically specific but critical elements in functional materials.
items.authors: Alexander Schwab, Stephanos Karafiludis, Biswajit Bhattacharya, Ines Feldmann, Carsten Prinz, Franziska Emmerling

items.title: Relativistic Bond Reconstruction in Chemical Bonding: An Information Dynamics Perspective on the CBi− Molecular Ion
items.abstract: In July 2026, the team of Lai-Sheng Wang at Brown University reported a landmark experimental observation in Science: the first direct spectroscopic evidence for the relativistic breakdown of the classical triple-bond picture in the CBi− molecular ion. Here we reinterpret this discovery through the lens of information dynamics—a framework that distinguishes between “real space” (wavefunctions and electron densities, where traditional quantum chemistry operates) and “virtual space” (defined here as the symmetry-rule manifold that organizes how real-space observables behave). We formalize virtual space as the set of irreducible representations of the Hamiltonian’s symmetry group, and show that relativistic effects drive a restructuring of this virtual space from the nonrelativistic C∞v to the relativistic C∗ ∞v double group. Four-component Dirac–Coulomb CCSD(T) calculations on CBi− provide the ab initio anchor: projecting the resulting spinors onto the symmetry-rule basis defines the coupling matrix Sij = ⟨ϕω i |ϕNR j ⟩ that connects real-space states to virtualspace rules. From this coupling matrix we extract a single input, the σ weight σ1 = 58.3% of the upper |ω| = 1/2 Kramers pair, and characterize the restructuring with the mixing parameter η, the label ambiguity A = ⟨H(σ/π|ω)⟩, and the mutual information I—the calculations supply the wavefunctions, while η, A, and I are outputs of the symmetry-constrained S-matrix model built on this one extracted input. A single-parameter constraint structure emerges: given the extracted σ fraction, unitarity enforces the complementary fraction and angular-momentum projection orthogonality enforces zero σ character in the |ω| = 3/2 orbital. We obtain η = 0.722, A = 0.453 nats, and I = 0.646 nats. The restructuring is a smooth crossover driven by the spin–orbit coupling strength λ, with η decreasing from 1.00 and I decreasing from ln 3 ≈ 1.099 nats in the nonrelativistic limit, the steepest change in A and I occurring near λ ≈ 0.4. All reported values are produced by a self-consistent, reproducible analysis pipeline, and are stress-tested by five numerical validation experiments (pairing-algorithm robustness, noise injection, subspace closure, the CN− null test, and a basis-set incompleteness model), which rule out numerical noise as the origin of the mixing signatures. Our findings demonstrate that the “anomalies” in heavy-element chemistry are not exceptions to existing rules but rather the manifestation of rule reorganization when the system crosses from the nonrelativistic to the relativistic regime.
items.authors: Kai Huang, Hongkui Liu, Ziwei Huang

items.title: How much of natural-product chemical space has a reference spectrum? An open audit of GNPS, MassBank and MoNA against COCONUT and LOTUS
items.abstract: Annotation of untargeted mass spectrometry data rests on reference MS/MS spectra, yet how much of documented natural-product (NP) chemistry actually has one has been asserted rather than measured. We present SPECGAP, an open, dependency-free engine that joins NP structure databases to spectral libraries on InChIKey identity and reports two quantities with explicit denominators: structural coverage, the share of reference structures with at least one experimental MS2 spectrum, and name-recoverability, the share of spectra whose declared compound name reconciles with the reference database. Applied to the complete open experimental layer—2,745,226 MS2 spectra from MassBank, MoNA and GNPS (280,024 distinct compounds)—against 738,823 COCONUT and 227,298 LOTUS structures, SPECGAP finds that 90.34% of COCONUT and 88.16% of LOTUS have no spectrum even when stereochemistry is ignored (exact-key coverage 2.86% and 5.08%). Coverage grows sublinearly: a 19.7-fold increase in spectra bought a 2.63-fold increase in covered structures, an elasticity of 0.32, because only 7.5% of the compounds in the layer are COCONUT natural products. Composition outweighs size: GNPS added 7.4-fold fewer new compounds than MoNA but a 5.9-fold higher NP hit rate (18.8% versus 3.2%). Both measures depend on the reference database: LOTUS is 3.25-fold smaller than COCONUT yet 1.78-fold better covered, while the same spectra recover 69.54% of their names against COCONUT and 36.17% against LOTUS. On the one run with archived match-level detail, 12.1% of recoveries came from fuzzy name matching; exact matching alone gives 31.82%, and we show the fuzzy rule can accept congener names. Library joinability differs 6.5-fold, and the GNPS MGF export cannot be joined at all. All code, audit outputs and derivations are openly released.
items.authors: Oshoma Erumiseli, Bila Hassan Ali, Dauda Garba

items.title: Old Drugs, New Targets: Multi-parameter computational prioritization of FDA‑approved, brain‑penetrant drugs as isoform‑selective GSK‑3β inhibitors for Alzheimer’s disease
items.abstract: Glycogen synthase kinase-3β (GSK-3β), a central regulator of tau phosphorylation and amyloid pathology, with its β isoform (GSK-3β) used as a main driver of the Alzheimer’s disease (AD) neurodegeneration. It is a validated therapeutic target in AD, yet no isoform-selective, brain penetrant inhibitors have reached clinical use. This paper screens 1000+ FDA-approved drugs by dual-isoform docking (GSK3α/β) and 8-seed redocking, prioritizing compounds by its α/β selectivity (G_select = G_GSK3A − G_GSK3B), CNS penetration, Hinge H-bonds, and pose plausibility. High selectivity alone provided misleading: filgotinib showed the largest G_select (+1.25 ± 0.03 kcal/mol), yet a reproducibly implausible pose, while abemaciclib (ΔG_select = +0.80 ± 0.09 kcal/mol; plausible‑pose fraction = 0.88) and peficitinib (+0.008 ± 0.02 kcal/mol; 1.00) provided a moderate selectivity with structurally reliable binding. Multi-seed redocking led to a hidden instability (loratinib plausible in only 25% of the seeds). This work provides a ranked, hypothesis-generating shortlist by establishing that isoform-selective GSK3β inhibitor discovery demands joint optimization of selectivity, and multi-seed pose stability, rather than affinity of GSK-3β alone. The following results are computationally prioritized candidates, rather than experimentally verified GSK-3β inhibitors.
items.authors: Naranbileg Baljinnyam, Ariuntuguldur Khurelbaatar

items.title: A Redox-Switchable NIR II-to-NIR II Photoluminescent Vanadium(III/II) Redox Couple
items.abstract: Redoxluminochromic materials are useful for switchable optoelectronic devices that change the emission properties upon a redox stimulus. Typically, ON/OFF switches are realized, while materials with redox-induced changes of emission color are exceedingly rare. Here, we report a near-infrared II emissive vanadium(III) chromophore [V(tpe)2]3+ with an emission band peaking at 1110 nm. Its detailed photophysical properties including (ultrafast and long) excited state dynamics are elucidated by variabletemperature fs-ns transient absorption spectroscopy and luminescence spectroscopy. Together with its one-electron reduced counterpart [V(tpe)2]2+ (emission maximum at 1375 nm), we establish a proof-of-concept that d2/d3 spin-flip emitters can constitute redoxluminochromic materials, which switch luminescence from 1000–1200 nm to 1300–1600 nm in the very challenging near-infrared II spectral region.
items.authors: Alexandra König-Schäfer, Robert Naumann, Christoph Förster, Jan Klett, Katja Heinze

items.title: Validation Design Governs the Apparent Predictive Performance of Machine Learning for PLGA Drug Release
items.abstract: Reliable generalization is essential for machine-learning models intended to predict drug-release behavior across heterogeneous experimental settings. However, multi-study experimental data often contain closely related formulations generated under shared materials, processing conditions, release protocols, and laboratory practices, creating hidden dependencies between training and test data. Such dependencies can make model performance appear stronger than its ability to generalize to genuinely new experimental domains. Here, we examine how validation topology governs the apparent predictability of poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) microparticle drug release using a public dataset containing 321 formulations and 4,913 release observations collected across 113 studies. Using a common LightGBM prediction framework, we compare validation schemes ranging from random observation splitting to strict study-grouped holdout. Predictive performance decreases markedly as train–test independence becomes more stringent, with 𝑅! declining from 0.939 under random point splitting to 0.616–0.625 under formulation-level holdout and 0.372 when entire studies are withheld. Controlled overlap experiments further show that retaining samestudy sibling formulations in the training set systematically increases apparent performance, while nearest-neighbor analysis reveals lower prediction error for formulations lying closer to the training distribution, particularly when their nearest training counterpart originates from the same study. These results show that formulation-level independence alone does not ensure experimental-domain independence and demonstrate that apparent drug-release predictability is strongly conditioned by validation design. Study-aware validation therefore provides a more rigorous basis for assessing generalization of machine-learning models trained on heterogeneous multi-study experimental data.
items.authors: Tengxiao Liu, Juchen Zhang, Hongtao Sun

items.title: Internally Polarized Covalent Organic Frameworks: A Design Strategy for Single-Component Photovoltaics
items.abstract: Molecular dipoles generate strong electric fields on the sub-nanometer scale, the very scale on which photogenerated excitons in organic semiconductors are bound. Harnessing such fields to drive charge generation throughout a photovoltaic material, however, has not been achieved. Realizing this would require ordering vast numbers of molecules throughout the bulk, which is precisely the structural control offered by covalent organic frameworks (COFs). In this work, we explore in silico the design of COFs that exploit internal-field-driven exciton dissociation, and show how they can be used to overcome a central challenge in single-component organic photovoltaics: converting strongly bound Frenkel excitons into long-lived separated charges. Using models that span from a single donor–bridge–acceptor unit to the full periodic material, we follow the photoexcitation process through its full cycle, from light absorption, through exciton dissociation, to charge recombination, and in turn isolate the effect of internal polarization at each stage. We show that polarization is essential for efficient exciton dissociation, preventing the kinetic hole trapping prevalent in an unpolarized analog. To investigate the recombination process on the nanosecond timescale, we develop a dedicated nonadiabatic molecular dynamics protocol, which, validated against an experimentally known donor–acceptor COF built from the same units, reproduces its charge-carrier lifetime with high accuracy. Applying it to the newly designed systems, we predict an almost 40-fold increase in charge-carrier lifetime. Our results identify internal polarization as a promising, unexplored approach to organic photovoltaic design and demonstrate how electronic-structure engineering at the building-block level translates into material-level performance.
items.authors: Miko laj Martyka, Joanna Jankowska

items.title: Resilience and regime change in refining margins: evidence from cointegration, Markov chains, and topological data analysis
items.abstract: This paper analyses the 3:2:1 crack spread over 20 years (2006 to 2025) using three independent methods: Engle-Granger cointegration, Markov chain regime modelling, and persistent homology applied to Takens delay embeddings. The data are publicly available EIA spot prices obtained via the FRED database. The objective is to determine whether the long-run equilibrium relationship between crude oil and refined product prices has survived the structural shocks of the last decade: the oil price collapse of 2014-2016, the COVID-19 pandemic, the war in Ukraine, and the addition of new refining capacity in the Middle East and Africa. Cointegration holds in 68% of rolling five-year windows, confirming long-run equilibrium. The equilibrium margin has shifted from $12/bbl (2006-2021) to $18/bbl (2024-2025). The error correction half-life has increased from 0.9 to 5.8 months, with the adjustment coefficient becoming statistically non-significant after 2017 (p = 0.38). Markov chain analysis discretises the margin into five regimes and provides N-step transition probabilities. The steady-state probability of normal-or-better margins is 55%. Topological data analysis reveals the most striking change: the pre-2020 crack spread exhibited 18 to 24 persistent homological cycles reflecting seasonal and inventory patterns. The post-2020 periods show near-zero topological complexity. The cyclic structure that made margins partially predictable for 15 years has not survived the combined disruptions. The three methods converge on the same diagnosis through independent mathematical frameworks. The practical implication is that prediction of refining margins is not impossible but conditional: it works when the market has topological structure, and it does not work when the structure is absent. The tools presented here provide a way to distinguish between the two regimes in near-real time.
items.authors: Rafael Larraz

items.title: Linear inductive bias boosts extrapolative molecular discovery by Bayesian active learning in the small-data limit
items.abstract: Bayesian active learning is widely used for molecular discovery, yet surrogate selection remains challenging when scarce initial data must guide the search beyond the observed property range. Here we benchmark diverse Gaussian process (GP) configurations across ten small-molecule and polymer datasets, focusing on the extrapolative regime where the initial labeled samples are drawn exclusively from below the median of the target property distribution. We identify explicit linear structure as an effective inductive bias for data-scarce extrapolative discovery: linear-kernel GPs provide a strong baseline, while adding linear components to a stationary kernel helps mitigate poor outcomes in the tail of the performance distribution. However, this advantage weakens under later-stage interpolative regime, where adaptive surrogate selection can further improve the discovery performance. These findings support incorporating linear inductive biases into data-driven materials discovery, where data scarcity and limited coverage of the design space are the norm rather than the exception.
items.authors: Min Young Ha

items.title: Electron Counting by Design: Antiferromagnetic Ribbons Double as Charge Reservoirs to Stabilize Hypervalent Selenium and Tellurium Chains
items.abstract: Linear chains of hypervalently bonded chalcogen atoms are attractive building blocks for topological materials, but they almost always dimerize or modulate, and the few known examples are confined to actinide compounds. Here we show that Se, mixed Se/Te, and Te chains that are equidistant in their extended crystal structures are stabilized in a new Ibam structure type, Ba 2 Cu 2−x Fe 1+x Se 5−y Te y (y = 0 to 3.2), by combining a low reaction temperature (750 °C), aliovalent Cu/Fe mixing, and a geometric matching between the chains and ribbons of edge-sharing (Cu/Fe)Se 4 tetrahedra. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction at 100 and 300 K shows no superstructure for any composition, whereas the displacement parameters reveal static displacements of the Se atoms along the chain (0.17 Å rms) that decrease with Te substitution and vanish for the Te chain. The ribbons order antiferromagnetically at 132–151 K without a net moment, and the Curie constants show that the Fe(II)/Fe(III) ratio adjusts to place a charge of −0.8 to −1.3 on each chain Se atom, bracketing the value of −1 that is optimal for hypervalent bonding. Electronic structure calculations show steep chain bands and a chain bond index that is independent of the Cu/Fe ratio, and a magnetic symmetry analysis shows that the chain-band crossings persist as fourfold Dirac points in the antiferromagnetic state, about 0.4 eV below the Fermi level. Aliovalent cation mixing thus provides a chemical handle on the electron count of hypervalent chalcogen chains.
items.authors: Subhendu Jana, E.A. Chirantha Edirisinghe, Ian Leahy, Milena Jovanovic, Rebecca W. Smaha, Paul A. Maggard

items.title: Machine Learning Prediction of Subsequent Drug Release Trajectories using Early Release Information in PLGA Microparticles
items.abstract: Accurate prediction of drug-release behavior from PLGA microparticles may reduce the experimental effort required for formulation characterization, yet conventional prediction approaches rely primarily on static molecular and formulation descriptors and do not incorporate experimentally observed release behavior as it becomes available during an ongoing experiment. Here, we develop a machine-learning framework that integrates molecular and formulation descriptors with early-release measurements to predict subsequent drug-release trajectories from PLGA microparticles. A dataset comprising 4,913 release observations from 321 formulations was analyzed using random forest regression with formulation-grouped cross-validation. Using a common set of 89 formulations, we systematically evaluated the predictive value of increasing amounts of early-release information. Prediction accuracy improved with additional early measurements, but the incremental benefit progressively diminished, with two and three measurements capturing 64.7% and 91.9% of the total predictive gain achieved with four measurements, respectively. The value of early information also varied substantially across formulations, with greater benefits generally observed for formulations that were more difficult to predict from static descriptors alone. Trajectory-level analysis further revealed that early observations constrained subsequent release trajectories to different extents across formulations. These findings demonstrate that experimentally observed early-release behavior provides formulation-specific predictive information beyond static descriptors and establish a data-driven framework for quantifying information sufficiency in drug-release characterization.
items.authors: Tengxiao Liu, Juchen Zhang, Hongtao Sun

items.title: Depth-aware machine learning for 3D reconstruction of fibrous porous electrodes by FIB-SEM tomography
items.abstract: Quantitative three-dimensional reconstruction of porous polymers with sub-micrometer feature sizes is central to understanding and designing electrochemical interfaces and membranes. However, focused ion beam–scanning electron microscopy tomography combined with conventional segmentation techniques cannot readily recon-struct complex disordered morphologies such as fibers. Standard segmentation workflows misclassify out-ofplane material as in-plane material, distorting the reconstructed pore network, fiber connectivity, and interfacial area. Here, we introduce an annotation-free, depth-aware machine-learning framework that combines monocular depth estimation, trained on real-scale images, with unsupervised clustering to separate exposed polymer crosssections from subsurface contributions in serial FIB–SEM tomography images. Applied to copper-coated electro-spun poly(vinylidene fluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene) fiber mats, the approach produces 3D reconstructions that preserve fibrous morphology more faithfully than conventional supervised and unsupervised segmentation. Quan-titative validation against capillary flow porometry, pycnometry, and high-resolution wide-angle X-ray computed tomography demonstrates improved agreement across pore diameter, fiber volume ratio, and copper-depth distribution metrics. This work establishes depth-aware segmentation as a transferable strategy from real-scale to nanoscale imaging, requiring no labelled training data and enabling accurate 3D segmentation and reconstruction from SEM images. This approach opens a path toward more reliable structure–property relationships in disordered porous polymer materials.
items.authors: Carlota Bozal-Ginesta, Claudia Bissattini Alessi, Peng Zeng, Julie Ruellou, Jakub Drnec, Alessandro Senocrate

items.title: PolyNet: A Python Package for Polymer Informatics
items.abstract: Polymers are used in a wide range of industries for diverse applications but formulating them to attain desired properties remains a challenging task. Polymer informatics has emerged as a powerful approach for the rational design of materials. Here, we present PolyNet, an open-source Python package that provides an end-to-end workflow for polymer informatics. PolyNet: 1) reads and validates datasets of polymer properties, including the monomer structures and their molar ratios; 2) creates vector- and graph-based representations of the polymers; 3) trains and optimises traditional machine learning (ML) models and graph neural networks (GNNs); 4) compares representations and models statistically; 5) deploys the models to screen in silico libraries of polymers, flagging polymers outside the applicability domain of the models and estimating their expected prediction error; and 6) interprets the models to understand structure–property relationships. PolyNet provides unique features such as: modelling of homopolymers and copolymers with any number of components, using the molar ratio of monomers in both vector- and graph-based representations; acceptance of textual representations of monomers or repeating units; calculation of polyBERT fingerprints and PolyMetriX and RDKit descriptors and fingerprints and accepting standalone user precalculated representations; benchmarking of all representation–model combinations on identical data splits using paired statistical tests; and chemically interpretable explanations through fragment-level attribution for GNNs and SHAP analysis for traditional ML models. Every experiment automatically records its configuration, data splits, hyperparameter search spaces and trained models, supporting full reproducibility in line with FAIR principles. PolyNet can be used through Python scripts, a command-line interface, or a graphical user interface for researchers without programming experience. We exemplify PolyNet by two case studies: glass transition temperature prediction for homopolymers, where cluster-based data splits showed that random splits overestimate model performance, the applicability domain identified less reliable predictions, and the model explanations recovered the known effect of chain mobility on T g ; and ¹⁹F MRI signal-to-noise ratio prediction for copolymers, where encoding monomer molar ratios is key to accurate predictions.
items.authors: Eduardo Aguilar-Bejarano, Morgan R Alexander, David Winkler, Grazziela Figueredo

items.title: Identification of Readily Accessible Manganese Catalysts Enables Multi-gram Scale Enantioselective γ-C(sp 3 )‒H Lactonization of Carboxylic Acids
items.abstract: Selective C‒H bond functionalization is a powerful tool to access complex molecules within a minimal number of synthetic steps, but its applicability on a large scale is often hampered by the requirement of harsh reaction conditions and costly catalysts. Among the existing C‒H bond functionalization portfolio, carboxylic acid directed C‒H lactonization has emerged as a particularly valuable transformation since it provides access to synthetically versatile lactone products from readily available carboxylic acids. Aiming at identifying catalysts that facilitate scalability of the reaction, herein, a collection of simple manganese complexes bearing triazacyclononane, picolinic acid, bipyridine and minimal N-based tetradentate ligands, which are established oxidation catalysts, have been screened in a model carboxylic acid directed C‒H lactonization reaction. While most of them proved ineffective, we identified two catalysts bearing simple N-based tetradentate ligands, Mn-(OTf) 2 (meb) (Mn-meb) and ( R,R )-Mn-(OTf) 2 (mcb) (Mn-( R,R -mcb)), which are far more easily accessible than previously reported best-in-class sterically encumbered catalysts and provide lower yet still comparable performance under mild reactions conditions. Remarkably, high levels of enantioselectivity can be obtained in some relevant directed C‒H bond oxidation reactions. Even though these simplified complexes still operate in fluorinated solvents like hexafluoroisopropanol (HFIP), we demonstrate that solvent usage can be minimized with respect to previously adopted protocols by working at up to 30-fold higher concentrations and recycling the solvent over at least three catalytic runs. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated on a small scale using seven highly diversified substrates and on a five gram scale by the lactonization of a cycloalkyl carboxylic acid and a protected amino acid via secondary and primary C(sp 3 )‒H bond oxidation, respectively. More than two grams of a highly enantioenriched lactone could be isolated using only ~100 mL of HFIP, 1.5 equiv. of H 2 O 2 and ~15 mg of an inexpensive and air-stable manganese catalyst (TON ≈ 1000).
items.authors: Francesco Zaccaria, Lluc Vila, Arnau Call, Miquel Costas

items.title: FLAKE: high-precision energies of helium’s ground and excited S states
items.abstract: We report a variational upper bound on the nonrelativistic, infinite-nuclear-mass ground-state energy of helium whose first 60 significant figures are converged, E0 =−2.903 724 377 034 119 598 311 159 245 194 404 446 696 925 311 117 290 339 042 34 Eh, 16 more than the best previous record. The calculation runs on a laptop and the method, which we call FLAKE (Fock-log anisotropic Kronecker eigensolver), combines four ingredients. (i) A change of variables making Schwartz’s Hylleraas-type basis with logarithms an exact tensor product, so the Hamiltonian is a sum of 27 Kronecker products of small matrices. (ii) Exact, arbitrary-precision orthonormalisation of the small radial and angular Gram factors removes all cancellation from the large computation. (iii) Fixed-point products at about 280 bits are split without error into ordinary double-precision matrix multiplications. (iv) The variational space is anisotropic: it carries extra radial degree and a tower of (ln s)p functions only at low angular order, as dictated by channel-resolved convergence rates. Every energy quoted is certified by an independent arbitrary-precision evaluation of the Rayleigh quotient of the explicit trial function. With an exchange-parity switch, a dilated radial scale and, for the second singlet root, a deflated solver with a min-max certificate, the same machinery gives the ground state triplet and first excited singlet energies to 43 and 40 significant figures, eight and six more than the best previous values. The remaining error is estimated from geometric convergence laws that predicted subsequent energy increments to within 2%.
items.authors: Adam Baskerville

items.title: Hg(II) Coordination in Human Thioredoxin Reductase 1: Molecular Insights into Mercury Toxicity
items.abstract: Thioredoxin reductase 1 (TrxR1) is an essential selenoprotein oxidoreductase and a sensitive molecular target of mercury, but the coordination chemistry underlying its inhibition by inorganic Hg(II) remains unknown. We use complementary Hg LIII-edge and Se K-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS), high-energy-resolution fluorescence-detected XAS (HERFDXAS), and density functional theory (DFT) to determine the Hg(II) coordination environment in inhibited human TrxR1. Se K-edge EXAFS provides direct evidence for Hg(II) coordination to catalytic Sec498 in wild-type TrxR1, with a Se–Hg distance of 2.44 Å. Hg LIII-edge EXAFS indicates predominantly two-coordinate, near-digonal Se–Hg–S coordination, with Hg–Se and Hg–S distances of 2.43 and 2.37 Å, respectively. Replacement of Sec498 by cysteine or serine gives bis-thiolate Hg(SR)2 coordination, demonstrating that Sec498 is not essential for Hg(II) binding. Hg Lα1 HERFD-XAS independently supports two-coordinate Hg(II) and distinguishes mixed sulfur/selenium coordination in wild-type TrxR1 from the bis-thiolate U498C variant. DFT calculations show that coordination by the adjacent C-terminal Cys497/Sec498 pair and structures involving the N-terminal redox center are compatible with spectroscopy, but do not unambiguously distinguish their relative energies. In contrast, bis-thiolate coordination in U498S, which retains only Cys497 at the C-terminal redox center, supports recruitment of a cysteine from the N-terminal site. These results directly characterize inorganic Hg(II) binding to TrxR1 and demonstrate how the strong, adaptable chalcogen coordination chemistry of Hg(II) enables it to target the catalytic machinery of this essential cellular redox enzyme.
items.authors: Emerita Mendoza Rengifo, Clinton J. Kidman, Linda I. Vogt, Julien J. H. Cotelesage, Thomas Kroll, Dimosthenis Sokaras

items.title: Alkyl-BODIPYs as a Self-Photoredox Catalyst for their Oxidative Hydroxymethylation
items.abstract: The adoption of photocatalytic approaches for utilising small organic molecules in self‑catalysed reactions offers opportunities in green organic synthesis. We report that alkylated boron‑dipyrromethenes (BODIPYs) act as self‑photoredox catalysts for their own oxidation under mild visible‑light conditions. Using an imidazolinium salt (NHC-H) as a quencher, alkylated BODIPYs are oxidised cleanly to the corresponding hydroxymethyl derivatives in a one‑pot process. Luminescence studies, including Stern–Volmer analysis, support a reductive‑quenching pathway in which the NHC-H transfers an electron to photoexcited BODIPY to give a BODIPY radical anion. The method proceeds without external photocatalysts or stoichiometric oxidants and shows good functional‑group tolerance, highlighting the potential of these chromophores both as substrates and catalytic light absorbers. Moreover, the synthesized molecules were demonstrated to behave as effective passivating agents for layered Mn2+
items.authors: Shaista Sultan, Praveen B. Managutti, Ahmed Abdelhady, Ramon Rios

items.title: The eventful journey of a ligand in and out of the binding site
items.abstract: The route a ligand follows to reach and leave a protein binding site typically involves complex molecular mechanisms that shape its efficacy as a biologically active compound. These mechanisms are reflected in the binding and unbinding kinetics, which often predict biological activity better than binding affinity alone, yet their calculation remains a bottleneck in ligand characterization. Here, we propose an approach that combines committor-based enhanced sampling with spectral analysis of the infinitesimal generator to characterize in detail how a ligand reaches the binding site of a protein and is eventually expelled. Applied to the paradigmatic benzamidine (BEN)–trypsin complex and the congeneric para-amino benzamidine (PAB), this framework reveals distinct and multifaceted binding pathways for the two ligands, uncovering a previously uncharacterized BEN binding site that competes with the crystallographic site, while identifying a common rotational bottleneck for unbinding. The computed unbinding free energies closely agree with experimental measurements. The spectral decomposition of the infinitesimal generator provides access to the slow dynamical modes of the system. From the slowest mode, we derive residence times and kinetic rate constants that agree with available experimental data and with independent OPES flooding simulations, while requiring substantially less computational effort. This approach offers a privileged perspective to resolve the complexity of protein–ligand binding-unbinding process, with potential applications to ligand screening and the characterization of multiple binding sites.
items.authors: Alessandro Berselli, Michele Parrinello

items.title: De Novo Design of Enantioselective Artificial Metalloenzyme Photocatalysts
items.authors: Sandip Mishra, Payal, Declan Evans, Kingsley Bortey, Husayn Bootwala, Giovanni Gonzalez-Gutierrez

items.title: Investigating the Antioxidant Potential of Annona muricata Leaves- An in silico Assisted in vitro Approach
items.abstract: Annona muricata is traditionally used in the treatment of various infectious and chronic non – communicable diseases. The antioxidant activity of the leaves of A.muricata was assessed using DPPH scavenging assay. The DPPH radical scavenging potential was compared with the proven antioxidant, ascorbic acid. The result of the study showed that methanolic leaf extract of Annona muricata exhibited the greatest antioxidant activity than the other three extracting solvents used. Six major phytochemicals present in A. muricata were taken from Dr. Duke’s Phytochemical and Ethnobotanical database and docked with Xanthine oxidase (XO) protein. Campesterol obtained the minimum binding energy value and hence maximum stability. The experimental results were in agreement with the docking results. Fifteen similar molecules of Campesterol were taken from PubChem and docked with XO which revealed that 2-methyltetracycloheptade-7-en-5-ol based scaffolds can act as potent XO inhibitors.
items.authors: Achutha A S, Akshaya K Mohan, Vidya Viswanath, Pushpa V L

items.title: Plasmonic Monolayer MoS 2 for Ultrathin Photoelectrodes in Neutral Water
items.abstract: Photoelectrochemical (PEC) electrodes can be used to create hydrogen to sustainably generate low-cost fuel and produce petrochemical feedstock. However, most semiconductors that drive the aqueous redox reactions in PEC devices cannot survive in neutral water, critical for widescale commercial production. Emerging, two-dimensional monolayer semiconductors can be electrochemically stable but generally do not capture enough sunlight to produce effective amounts of hydrogen. In this work, we propose a new PEC architecture that uses plasmonic enhancement to increase photocurrent in a monolayer MoS 2 photocathode. By creating the first ZrN-based surface plasmon polariton (SPP) generator, we show fabricated nanostructures that plasmonically couple light with energies up to ~2.5 eV in water with near-100% light absorption. With transferred monolayer MoS 2 , the resulting Schottky diode demonstrates corrosion-free, fully stable photoactivity under 1-sun illumination in oxygenated, neutral water. We investigated and optimized the mechanisms of plasmonic enhancement, increasing photocurrent by up to 2.7x under AM1.5G illumination and 660% with wavelengths above the bandgap of monolayer MoS 2 . Furthermore, we show this architecture is compatible with standard roll-to-roll fabrication, and we use a technoeconomic analysis to estimate that levelized costs of hydrogen $1/kg can be reasonably achieved with solar-to-hydrogen (STH) efficiencies of only 3.4%. Thus, with commercially scalable operational lifetimes and fabrication techniques, these results open the door to a new class of ultrathin PEC electrodes for economically feasible neutral water splitting applications.
items.authors: Kyle Haas, Vivek Subramanian

items.title: Charge Donated by the Framework, Reactivity Expressed at the Metal: Tetrathiafulvalene-Programmed Nitrate Reduction to Ammonia
items.abstract: The decisive challenge in nitrate-to-ammonia electrosynthesis is not simply supplying electrons, but ensuring that successive nitrogen intermediates remain chemically convertible. Here, we establish a molecular strategy that differentiates framework-derived electronic character from metal-directed reaction selectivity through TU-420, a crystalline covalent organic framework integrating electron-donating tetrathiafulvalene and electron-accepting, metal-coordinating bipyridine units. Electronic-structure analysis identifies complementary donor-associated and acceptor-like states, while Xray absorption spectroscopy reveals distinct approximately six-coordinate Fe–O/N and four-coordinate Cu–O/N environments within the conserved architecture. Remarkably, TU-420-Fe achieves 98.1% ammonia Faradaic efficiency at −0.60 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode and an ammonia production rate of 4.33 mg h-1 cm-2 at −0.80 V, whereas TU-420-Cu exhibits substantially lower selectivity despite its stronger cathodic response. Isotope-labeling experiments establish nitrate as the nitrogen source, while in situ attenuated total reflectance surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy, Raman spectroscopy, and differential electrochemical mass spectrometry reveal signatures consistent with evolving nitrogen–oxygen and hydrogenated nitrogen species. Density functional theory identifies the mechanistic distinction: Fe supports a favorable *NHO-mediated reduction sequence with a maximum uphill free-energy increment of 0.30 eV, while substantially alleviating the energetic penalty associated with the competing *NOH-mediated route relative to Cu. These findings identify the energetic fate of partially reduced nitrogen, rather than electron consumption alone, as a determinant of ammonia selectivity and establish electronically differentiated covalent architectures as platforms for programming metal-dependent multielectron catalysis.
items.authors: Tsukasa Irie, Hayato Orui, Sourav Ghosh, Riki Nakatani, Chaoqi Chen, Saranya Sasikumar

items.title: UPSTREAM: evidence-led, ledgered contribution to open metabolomics software, and what a corpus-wide name screen of MassBank found
items.abstract: Metabolomics depends on a small set of open projects—spectral libraries such as MassBank and GNPS, and processing software such as matchms and the RforMassSpectrometry packages—maintained largely by volunteers. Outside contributions can strengthen them or consume their maintainers’ time, and claims about how much someone has contributed are rarely verifiable. We describe UPSTREAM, a program that makes both problems explicit: every contribution must start from reproducible evidence and pass a ten-rule protocol, and the program’s headline count is computed from GitHub as merged pull requests only, never typed. We report the program’s first phase in full. A name-shape screen of all 139,006 records in MassBank 2026.03 flagged 1,480 names, of which 120 were defects (precision 8.1%), nearly all of them one collection’s internal identifiers. A name–structure screen that parsed 41,822 distinct names with OPSIN found 83,737 of 86,808 assessable records consistent (96.46%) and 3,071 candidate mismatches. Hand adjudication of 60 cases sampled from the two most suspicious strata found 58.3% to be screen artefacts, and confirmed 13 records (8 compounds) whose structure is a different compound from the one named; for six of the eight, the precursor m/z or the EI ions support the name. The same screen exposed a defect in matchms itself: clean_compound_name truncates 5 of 41,822 MassBank names, and a one-line fix truncates none. Phase 1 closed with 5 complete contribution packets (duplicate searches and author review still to do before filing), one item reopened when the target’s own documentation contradicted our premise, and two items closed because no failing case could be shown. The ledger stands at n = 0 merged contributions, because filing is the author’s step and had not yet happened. All screens, packets and derivations are openly available.
items.authors: Oshoma Erumiseli, Bila Hassan Ali, Dauda Garba

items.title: Crystallographic Visualization of Cooperative Molecular Motion Underlying the Photomechanical Response of a Diarylethene Crystal
items.abstract: Photomechanical molecular crystals convert molecular-scale photochemical reactions into macroscopic mechanical motion, yet how local structural changes develop into collective crystal deformation remains poorly understood. Here, we directly track the conversiondependent molecular motions underlying the photomechanical response of a diarylethene crystal, DAE-Et, by single-crystal X-ray diffraction. Polarization-selective photoirradiation enabled the preparation of a series of photoreacted single crystals at different conversion levels while maintaining single crystallinity. Detailed disorder analysis revealed two distinct conformations of the closed-ring form, C I and C II , with the relative population of C II increasing with increasing photoconversion. Remarkably, the unreacted open-ring molecules also underwent conversion-dependent conformational reorganization from O toward O′, which correlated with lattice deformation and the macroscopic change in crystal angle. These results reveal the molecular origin of the characteristic induction period in the photomechanical response: photocyclization initially proceeds predominantly with the formation of C I with little lattice reorganization, whereas further photoconversion is accompanied by an increase in the population of C II and conformational reorganization of the surrounding open-ring molecules. Thus, the macroscopic photomechanical response emerges from intermolecularly coupled conformational reorganization involving both photoreacted and unreacted molecules. This work provides direct molecular-level insight into how local photochemical events are translated into cooperative motion and macroscopic mechanical responses in molecular crystals.
items.authors: Takumu Yoshikawa, Daichi Kitagawa, Seiya Kobatake

items.title: Development and Evaluation of a Low-Cost Bio-Adsorptive Filter Insert (DrainGuard) for Stormwater Microplastic Remediation
items.abstract: Sub-millimeter microplastics (100–300 μm) in urban stormwater runoff represent a significant, unaddressed pathway for aquatic pollution. Conventional catch basins and physical interception methods lack the retention efficiency required to capture fine polyolefin fragments during high-velocity first-flush events. This study presents DrainGuard, a modular, decentralized storm drain filter insert utilizing a stratified bio-adsorptive matrix composed of biogenic cockleshell sand and agricultural coconut coir. A 46 mm inner diameter PVC column featuring a stratified bed (4 cm upper sand / 12 cm coconut coir / 4 cm lower sand) was evaluated at a baseline hydraulic flow rate of Qbase = 800 mL/min. Synthetic stormwater spiked with post-consumer polyolefin fragments (≈0.1 g) was introduced to assess mechanical capture efficiency and retention dynamics. Optical inspection (60x zoom) confirmed particulate interception and primary retention within the upper sand layer, with near zero microplastic detection in the post-filtration effluent, all while maintaining stable fluid transmission without rapid hydraulic failure. By repurposing low-cost, abundant biogenic materials, DrainGuard provides an accessible, sustainable, and highly effective framework for localized microplastic remediation in urban stormwater drainage systems.
items.authors: Nehir Çelebi

items.title: An experimentally-validated principle for selectivity in endergonic reactions
items.abstract: Selectivity between competing thermal reactions is, by textbook account, set either by the relative free energies of the products (thermodynamic control) or by those of the transition states leading to them (kinetic control). Neither principle applies to endergonic reactions: a non-equilibrium product concentration is maintained at the expense of an energy source, with species forming and decomposing simultaneously. Here we show that a third, distinct principle governs selectivity in endergonic reactions: the degree of turnover-frequency control, exerted by each intermediate of the kinetic barrier diagram associated to the reaction network. We demonstrate this principle experimentally, using a dynamic combinatorial system in which two furan derivatives compete for maleic acid in an endergonic Diels–Alder reaction driven by carbodiimide hydration. The product distribution depends on whether the system is at equilibrium or driven, and can be inverted under fueling. Kinetic measurements and analytical modeling quantitatively capture the observed selectivities – including counterintuitive non-monotonic responses – and recover thermodynamic and kinetic control as limiting cases.
items.authors: Zhipeng Li, Shuntaro Amano, Shaymaa Al Shehimy, Malak Rafieq Jaber, Leonardo Andreoni, Serena Silvi

items.title: Two extrapolation axes decide whether interaction needs a module in many-body systems
items.abstract: We separate the extrapolation problem in many-body systems into two axes: toward combinations with more components (the composition axis), and toward components unseen (the identity axis). The prevailing pipeline—encode then interact—performs poorly when extrapolating in composition count. We open an interaction-free route to interaction by strengthening its encoder until a component’s representation can carry what it contributes across the mixtures it appears in. Where component identities are bounded while their combinations are not, this route performs better along the composition axis, while the prevailing route is better along the identity axis; both differences follow from the functional forms rather than from the data. Chemical mixtures are the main example, synthetic tasks isolate the two axes, and the same structure recurs in other fields.
items.authors: Xiao Yang, Guanghao Song, Feiyu Li, Zihan Xu, Yanan Yang, Baojiang He

items.title: Site-selective alkali ion alloying in double perovskites via liquid-assisted mechanosynthesis revealed by solid-state NMR
items.abstract: Lead-free halide double perovskites with the general chemical formula A 2 B'B''X 2 are promising materials for light-emitting and photovoltaic applications. However, compositional tuning of their structural and optoelectronic properties has focused on B-site and halide alloying. In this work, we show that Cs + on the perovskite A-site of Cs 2 AgInCl 6 can be partly substituted with Rb⁺ using simple apolar liquid-assisted mechanochemistry. By comparing Rb + with Na + substitution we show that ion size drives the site-selectivity of alkali ion substitution into double perovskites, with Rb + and Na + preferentially occupying the double perovskite A- and B'-sites, respectively. By combining multinuclear solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy with X-ray diffraction, we show that Rb + not only enters the double perovskite site-selectively but also induces local symmetry breaking of the cubic structure, altering the optical bandgap and with potential implications for symmetry-forbidden photoluminescence emissivity. This work extends the tuneable compositional range of lead-free double perovskites to include A-site mixing while also establishing the site-selectivity of alkali ion speciation into the double perovskite structure.
items.authors: Kaja Glazer, Julia Wiktor, Luis Simbari, Mo El Maoued, Anya Fairhurst, Amita Ummadisingu

items.title: Halide Exchange via Perovskite Nanocrystals for Interfacial Defect Passivation in Solar Cells
items.abstract: Metal halide perovskites have emerged as leading candidates for next-generation optoelectronics, with perovskite solar cells (PSCs) achieving power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) exceeding 26%. However, solution-processed hybrid perovskite films typically suffer from non-radiative recombination and ion migration driven by surface and interfacial defects, limiting device performance, fill factor, and long-term stability. To address these bottlenecks, we report a novel, scalable interface engineering strategy utilizing bromide-rich perovskite nanocrystals to modify 3D perovskite film surfaces via self-driven solid-state halide exchange. The resulting surface-graded heterojunction passivates key iodide vacancies, suppresses ion migration, and optimizes charge extraction. Consequently, modified PSCs demonstrate a ~5% boost in short-circuit current density () and an improved fill factor of 75.3%, driving a ~10% relative increase in PCE from 20.13% (control) to 22.19%. This simple, single-step nanocrystal treatment provides a promising pathway toward robust, scalable, and high-efficiency optoelectronic architectures.
items.authors: Poyoja Rout, Chaya Kerkera, Sarang Mashale, Smruti Ranjan Panda, Laxman Gouda, Ritika Dey

items.title: Balancing Plasmonic Response and CO2 Activation in Au–Cu/TiO2 Hybrid Photocatalysts via Alloy Composition Control
items.abstract: Plasmonic metal–semiconductor hybrid catalysts offer a versatile platform for solar-driven CO2 photoreduction by integrating efficient light harvesting with catalytic activation. Here, Au–Cu/TiO2 hybrid photocatalysts are developed as a model system to elucidate the role of plasmonic excitation and surface chemistry in governing CO2 reduction activity and selectivity. Alloyed Au–Cu nanorods with controlled Cu incorporation were synthesized and assembled with TiO2 nanoparticles, enabling systematic modulation of the Au/Cu ratio while maintaining constant metal and semiconductor loadings. The resulting Au–Cu/TiO2 interface functions as a tandem photocatalytic system, where Au promotes hot-carrier generation, TiO2 facilitates charge separation, and Cu enhances CO2 adsorption and stabilization of reaction intermediates. Under broadband illumination (350–2400 nm), pristine TiO2 shows limited activity, whereas Au incorporation enables the formation of formic acid, methane, and ethanol.
