items.title: Electrochemical Formulation Maps for Multinary Chalcogenide Nanocrystal Inks and Polymer Coatings
items.authors: Oluwaseyi Saliu, Cain Witczak, Progna Banerjee

items.title: Probing the Softer-acid Nature of 102No2+ Compared to Alkaline Earth Metal ions via Synergistic Extraction with Sulfur Donor on Crown Ether Supported Resin
items.abstract: Unlike other f block elements that typically exhibit +3 or higher oxidation states, nobelium (No, atomic number = 102) exists predominantly as the divalent cation in aqueous solutions. While No2+ has long been considered chemically analogous to Ca2+ and Sr2+, strong relativistic effects are predicted to alter its reactivity. In our previous study, the soft metal ion behavior of No2+ was demonstrated through complexation with crown ethers. Prompted by this implication, in this study, we performed online solid-liquid extraction experiments of 255No by employing diethyl dithiophosphate (DEDTP−) as a soft sulfur-donor ligand to probe the softer Lewis acid character of No relative to alkaline earth metals via No–S bonding. Here we report the results of the experiments and relativistic DFT calculations. In the Sr resin/HDEDTP (aqueous) system, No2+ behaves in a manner distinct from Ca2+ and Sr2+, resembling Ba2+ and Ra2+. No2+ exhibits a significantly higher extraction efficiency in the HDEDTP system than Sr2+, confirming enhanced soft Lewis acid character. The computed Gibbs free energies of extraction-complex formation are consistent with the experimental ΔG trend, validating the theoretical model. The optimized geometry revealed a No–S bond shorter than ionic radius trends, indicating stronger bonding. We attribute this distinctive behavior to unique electronic states of No. Specifically, higher electron gain in the d-orbital, stronger relativistic 7s stabilization, and closer 5f energy matching synergistically enhance covalent character of No–S bonding.
items.authors: Ruilin Wang, Eisuke Watanabe, Takuya Yokokita, Ryotaro Masuda, Yudai Itakura, Hiroki Aoto

items.title: Computationally Guided Discovery of Cannabinoid Derivatives for Antiviral and Anticancer Applications: From Chemical Space to Experimental Validation
items.abstract: Cannabinoids represent a chemically diverse and structurally tunable class of natural and synthetic compounds that have attracted growing interest as molecular scaffolds for therapeutic discovery. However, their extensive chemical diversity, polypharmacology, conformational flexibility, and complex pharmacokinetic properties make the systematic identification and optimisation of therapeutically useful derivatives challenging. Recent advances in computer-aided drug discovery (CADD), molecular simulation, quantum chemistry, quantitative structure–activity relationship (QSAR) modelling, and artificial intelligence (AI) provide opportunities to interrogate the chemical space of cannabinoids in a systematic and mechanistically informed manner. This review examines computational strategies for the discovery and optimisation of cannabinoid derivatives with potential antiviral and anticancer applications, emphasising the integration of complementary computational approaches rather than reliance on isolated in silico predictions. A hierarchical computational workflow is described, progressing from cannabinoid chemical-space generation and ligand preparation to disease-relevant target identification, virtual screening, molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, binding free-energy estimation, quantum-chemical analysis, and ADMET/drug-likeness prediction. For antiviral discovery, computational investigations of SARS-CoV-2 targets, including the main protease (Mpro/3CLpro), papain-like protease (PLpro), spike protein, and spike–ACE2 interface, are discussed alongside emerging host-directed targets. For anticancer applications, computational studies involving EGFR, HER2, VEGFR, PI3K/AKT, MAPK, apoptosis, autophagy, oxidative stress, and cell-cycle regulation are evaluated. Particular emphasis is placed on the complementary roles of docking and MD simulations in characterising binding modes, interaction persistence, conformational stability, and molecular recognition, while MM-PBSA/MM-GBSA and related approaches provide additional energetic criteria for candidate prioritisation. QSAR and AI/ML-assisted approaches are further considered as complementary tools for expanding chemical-space exploration, predicting biological activity and ADMET properties, and enabling multi-parameter candidate prioritisation. Importantly, computational affinity scores are not treated as sufficient evidence of target inhibition or therapeutic efficacy. Instead, the review emphasises a progressive validation framework in which computationally prioritised candidates are evaluated through biochemical target-engagement studies, cellular assays, and, where appropriate, in vivo models. Experimental observations can subsequently inform structure–activity relationship analysis, lead optimisation, and iterative computational rescreening, establishing a closed-loop strategy for integrating molecular recognition, dynamic behaviour, binding energetics, pharmacokinetic properties, toxicity, and biological activity during cannabinoid lead development. The review critically examines key limitations of current computational approaches, including incomplete treatment of ligand flexibility, scoring-function limitations, protein conformational heterogeneity, limited experimental validation, dataset bias in AI/ML models, and translational challenges associated with cannabinoid solubility, bioavailability, metabolism, receptor promiscuity, psychoactive liabilities, and off-target effects. Collectively, current evidence indicates that computationally guided cannabinoid discovery is a promising but predominantly preclinical strategy. Further progress will depend on integrating CADD, molecular simulation, AI-assisted molecular design, uncertainty-aware prediction, and experimental validation into iterative multi-objective optimisation frameworks that jointly address potency, selectivity, pharmacokinetics, toxicity, and translational relevance.
items.authors: VIVEK KUMAR YADAV

items.title: Text-mined dataset of sol-gel synthesis protocols with phase purity outcomes using large language models
items.abstract: Sol-gel synthesis is a versatile method for producing inorganic materials that offers advantages such as atomic-level mixing and lower processing temperatures over traditional solid-state methods. Despite these benefits, achieving phase purity remains a challenge due to the process's sensitivity to synthesis parameters such as precursor choice, solvent selection, and heating conditions. Negative results, such as phase-impure outcomes, are essential for understanding sol-gel reaction pathways, but are largely absent from existing curated datasets. This work leverages Gemini 3.0 Flash to construct a text-mined inorganic sol-gel database with phase purity information. The dataset contains ~148,000 synthesis records, including ~28,000 phase-impure entries. All extracted entities achieved F1 scores greater than 0.89. At the record level, 68% of extracted records match human annotation on all evaluated fields. Furthermore, to validate the scientific utility of our dataset, we demonstrate that the aggregated data reproduces previously reported phase-purity trends for BiFeO 3 thin films.
items.authors: Wesley Y. Chen, Sanghoon Lee, Tim Kodalle, Philothei Sahinidis, Gerbrand Ceder, Carolin M. Sutter-Fella

items.title: Understanding Programmable Catalysts Versus Dynamic Reactors
items.abstract: The engineering of new processing systems can utilize dynamic operation of catalysts, reactors and processes to achieve faster and more selective manufacturing of chemicals, fuels, and materials. Forced dynamic operation of chemical systems can achieve new catalytic rates or targeted products not accessible under steady-state conditions. The distinction between dynamic reactors and programmable catalysts is defined by the differences in free energy of chemical species stimulated by light, charge, fields, heat, or light. Programmable catalysts only modulate the binding energy of surface adsorbates, while dynamic reactors also modulate the overall reaction free energy. This energetic difference determines the capability of dynamic systems to accelerate reactions or select for products, in addition to defining the stimulated system’s ability to convert reactions relative to equilibrium. Understanding the differences in dynamic chemical systems aids in identifying and optimizing combinations of catalysts, reactions, conditions, and external stimuli that can lead to improved chemical manufacturing.
items.authors: Omar Abdelrahman, Phillip Christopher, Eranda Nikolla, Paul J. Dauenhauer

items.title: Generic aspects of neutral polymer brush bilayers immersed in an implicit solvent under steady-state shear
items.abstract: Using molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with a Langevin thermostat, I study polymer brush bilayers immersed in an implicit solvent under steady-state shear. I use high-precision MD simulations, with 5×104 sampling steps, to measure the stress tensor, viscosity, kinetic friction coefficient, and chain extension as functions of the shear rate. The results show that the shear stress scales linearly with the Weissenberg number, Wi, over the entire range studied. The normal stress decreases without following a universal power law. The lateral chain extension decreases up to a critical value of Wi and then increases. The normal chain extension scales as Wi−0.3. The viscosity remains constant, whereas the kinetic friction coefficient increases without following a universal power law.
items.authors: Mike John Edwards

items.title: Stimulus-Responsive AIE-Active Magnetic Fluorescent Composite Enables High-Quality Visualization of Latent Fingerprints on Complex Substrates
items.abstract: Latent fingerprint visualization on complex substrates remains challenging because conventional fluorescent developing materials generally possess fixed emission states after deposition, limiting their adaptability toward diverse background environments. In this work, a novel AIE-active fluorescent material (B-N) was synthesized via a two-step Suzuk-Miyaura coupling and Knoevenagel condensation strategy, in which pyridine groups were introduced to impart stimulus-responsive properties for reversible fluorescence switching under external acid/base stimulation, enabling dynamic modulation of fingerprint color after development. By further integrating the AIE-active molecule B-N into a magnetic fluorescent composite system (with non-fluorescent Fe3O4 as the magnetic component), high-resolution latent fingerprint imaging was successfully achieved on eight representative substrates with different textures and background colors. More importantly, acid fumigation enabled fluorescence color regulation and improved fingerprint contrast on challenging surfaces, particularly those with strong background interference. Gray value profile analysis further confirmed clear ridge selectivity, uniform material adhesion, and stable imaging quality during the stimulus-responsive processes. Overall, this work demonstrates an adaptive strategy for latent fingerprint visualization. The findings highlight the potential of stimulus-responsive AIE materials in forensic applications.
items.authors: Yi Zhou, Ting Jiang, Zhen Liu, Zheng Zheng

items.title: Structure-Independent Genetic Algorithm-Based Molecular Optimization Using Pocket-Aware Molecular Representations
items.abstract: De novo molecular design typically depends on target structures or ligand poses, limiting its applicability when structural information is unavailable. Here, we introduce the pocket-aware molecular representation-guided genetic algorithm (PAMR-GA), a target-structure-independent molecular optimization framework that learns pocket-aware representations from structure–activity relationship (SAR) data using only molecular structures represented as SMILES strings and experimental pIC50 values. By encoding latent spatial constraints inferred from SAR without requiring target structures, the learned representations guide genetic algorithm-based molecular optimization through a Gaussian process surrogate model. Benchmarking on BACE-1 demonstrated that PAMR-GA achieved comparable predictive performance, docking scores, and drug-likeness profiles to existing optimization approaches while generating molecules with substantially greater structural novelty and higher Murcko scaffold diversity. Evaluation on four additional targets, including a kinase, serine proteases, and an NADbinding enzyme, further showed consistent improvements in molecular novelty. These results highlight PAMR-GA as a complementary approach for incorporating SAR-derived spatial constraints into de novo molecular design without requiring target structures. 1 Scientific Contribution PAMR-GA enables structure-independent molecular design by learning binding constraints implicitly from 2D structure–activity relationship data, without requiring protein structures or ligand poses. By introducing a pocket-aware molecular representation that integrates solvent-accessible surface area and partial-charge features, PAMR-GA bridges molecular topology with 3D binding compatibility. Our results demonstrate that constrained generation, rather than improved activity prediction alone, drives structural novelty. Evaluation across five diverse targets from four protein classes highlights the generalizability of PAMR-GA as a broadly applicable framework for target-aware molecular design.
items.authors: Abhishek Kumar, Hyun Woo Kim

items.title: Simulating Catalytic Resonance with Molecular Dynamics
items.abstract: Static heterogeneous catalysts are constrained by the Sabatier principle, where their overall turnover is limited by balancing the kinetics of reactant binding, surface reaction, and product unbinding. Modulating the surface binding energies between a strong binding state and a weak binding state can overcome this limit. For such a dynamic catalyst, a maximum turnover is achieved at a catalytic resonance modulating frequency. Here we demonstrate that classical molecular simulation approaches can be used to study this phenomena. Our method introduces a generic classical model for a surface reaction with time-dependent surface binding energy. Using a non-equilibrium molecular simulation in which reactants tend to be added to the system and products tend to be removed, we can simulate many catalyst cycles. Our approach reproduces catalytic resonance, with the dynamic catalyst providing up to a three-order-of-magnitude boost in turnover compared to the static catalyst. We further demonstrate the presence of a second resonant frequency in the gas phase, associated with resonance of the reacting bond. The general approach outlined here can be extended to more detailed models and used to study the molecular-scale effects of surface modulation and to computationally test input frequency, amplitude, and waveform for programmable catalysts.
items.authors: Alex Albaugh

items.title: Atomic Layer Deposition of Ferroelectric HfxZr(1-x)O2 from Metal-β-diketonate Precursors with Fine Cation Tunability.
items.abstract: HfxZr1-xO2 (HZO) is a promising ferroelectric material for next-generation neuromorphic devices, where precise compositional control and complementary metal-oxidesemiconductor (CMOS) compatible processing are critical. Atomic layer deposition (ALD) is particularly attractive for HZO integration due to its excellent conformality for future three-dimensional device architectures and possibility to control the composition. However, many widely used Hf and Zr precursors suffer from limited volatility and thermal stability. In this work, we exploit the robustness and favourable growth rates of the β-diketonate precursors Hf(thd)4 and Zr(thd)4 (thd = 2,2,6,6-tetramethyl-3,5heptanedionate) - with ozone co-reactant – to demonstrate the ALD growth of binary HfO2, ZrO2, and ferroelectric HZO thin films with finely controlled Hf/Zr cation ratios enabling the Hf/Zr composition required for ferroelectric thin films. Optimized binary ALD processes yield low growth-per-cycle (GPC) values of 0.085 Å/cycle for HfO2 and 0.12 Å/cycle for ZrO2, these low GPCs enable fine and reproducible control of the Hf:Zr
items.authors: Sajmohan Mohandas Moolayil, Ji Liu, Melania Rogowska, Ola Nilsen, Michael Nolan, Henrik Hovde Sønsteby

items.title: Engineering Confined Biomimetic Myelin Membranes for Phase-Controlled Remodeling and Real-Time Imaging
items.abstract: The myelin sheath is a densely packed, multilayered membrane whose concentric organization is essential for maintaining its structure and supporting efficient nerve function. Recreating this architecture in simplified phospholipid systems can help us understand how myelin forms, remodels, and becomes damaged. However, most existing biomimetic models produce tubular myelin figures and do not capture the characteristic concentric cross-section of native myelin. Here, we show that lipid phase, determined by the phase-transition temperature, directs the formation of distinct multilamellar architectures under identical confinement. Low-(Tm) DOPC forms conventional tubular myelin figures, whereas high-(Tm) DPPC follows a different assembly pathway, producing onion-like concentric structures that resemble native myelin cross-sections. Quantitative analysis reveals that these confined membranes expand toward a limiting size. DPPC assemblies also undergo bile-salt-induced remodeling, lipid recovery, and repeated reassembly, providing a dynamic model of membrane regeneration. In contrast, DOPC myelin figures undergo Fenton-induced lipid peroxidation, offering an oxidation-sensitive model of membrane damage relevant to demyelinating conditions. For real-time visualization, we developed amphiphilic nitrogen- and fluorine-codoped carbon dots with red and multicolor emission. Together, this platform enables direct investigation of myelin-like organization, remodeling, regeneration, and oxidative membrane damage.
items.authors: Naveen Kumar, Huma Tabassum, Priyanka Nath, Suman Choudhury, Anjan Chakraborty

items.title: Comprehensive multi-technique study of the electrochemical lithiation of Fe 3 O 4 with different particle sizes under operando conditions
items.abstract: Fe3O4 is a conversion-type anode material with high storage capacity that suffers from limited cycling performance. Nanosizing Fe3O4 is one promising strategy to enhance its cycling stability and overall electrochemical performance; however, the details of particle size dependent reaction kinetics remain poorly understood. We investigate the conversion reactions of bulk- and 50 nm-sized cubic Fe3O4 particles as active material using a multi-technique approach, by combining operando XRD, SAXS and magnetometry techniques. The results from the operando XRD and SAXS indicate that during initial lithiation reaction, the bulk electrode undergoes phase reduction with amorphization and formation of metallic iron nanograins, whereas the nanoparticle Fe3O4 retains its ccp oxygen anion framework throughout the lithiation process, hindering structural breakdown and amorphization and delaying the the growth of metallic iron nano grains. Operando vibrating sample magnetometry isused to cross-check the transformation and presence of metallic iron nanodomains owing to its unique sensitivity to local structural details hidden in conventional XRD. The reaction products were found to differ when time-resolved investigations are compared to ex-situ prepared specimens. These results highlight the critical importance of integrating complementary operando techniques to ex situ methods, to capture particle size–dependent lithiation pathways and relaxation mechanisms in conversion-type electrodes.
items.authors: Seda Ulusoy*, Hyeyun Kim, Leonhard Rochels, Martin Kapuscinski, Tereza Václav̊u, Ilaria Lucentini

items.title: Chemo-Enzymatic Synthesis of Starch from Cellulose
items.abstract: The biotransformation of cellulose to starch (i.e., enzymatic rearrangement of beta-1,4- to alpha-1,4-glycosidic bonds) is an out-of-the-box solution to ensure food security and it would provide sufficient feedstock of industrial biomanufacturing and revolutionize agriculture. However, enzymatic cellulose hydrolysis remains costly because weight-based cellulase loading (e.g., 20 kg of cellulase per 1000 kg of cellulose) is two orders of magnitude of that of starch hydrolysis. Here we develop a chemo-enzymatic synthesis involving cellulose dissociation mediated by the reconstituted cellulose solvent followed by cell-free glycosidicbond rearrangement catalyzed by an advanced multi-enzyme molecular machine. Inspired by starch gelatinization, we dissociate microcrystalline cellulose to insoluble long-chain cellodextrins, which can be hydrolyzed completely by a 95% decrease in cellulase loading. This chemo-enzymatic synthesis achieves a cellulose-to-amylose yield of 96.9% even when an ultra-low cellulase loading was used, i.e., 1 kg of cellulase is enough to completely hydrolyze 1,000 kg of cellulose. The high-efficiency chemo-enzymatic synthesis would make sufficient synthetic starch from cellulose, feeding the world and energizing the bioeconomy.
items.authors: Jingting Wang, Yi-Heng P. Job Zhang

items.title: Bridging Zeolites and Metal-Organic Frameworks: Alkali Metal Cation Modulation in Zn-based UTSA-16
items.abstract: We present the first modulation of different alkali metal cations in Zn-based UTSA-16 metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), achieved through the use of different alkali metal hydroxides (KOH, NaOH and LiOH) during the synthesis. Optimisation of the stoichiometric ratio of reagents enabled the synthesis of phasepure UTSA-16(K) free from residual traces of undesired phases and exhibiting enhanced surface area and adsorption performance. This optimised protocol allowed the direct synthesis of other UTSA-16 frameworks containing Li + and Na + . Systematic variation of the alkali metal composition revealed pronounced site selectivity, proving that K + and Na+ are compatible with both the crystallographically defined structural and extra-framework cation environments, whereas Li + incorporation requires the presence of K + or Na + , supporting its preferential occupation of extra-framework positions. N 2 and CO 2 adsorption measurements, combined with in situ IR spectroscopy with CO, proved that cation composition affects both pore accessibility and local adsorption environment. In particular, materials containing predominantly extra-framework Li + exhibit distinct adsorption and spectroscopic behaviour depending on the occupancy of the structural cation site and revealing an interplay between the two cation populations. These findings show that the adsorption properties of UTSA-16 cannot be rationalised only considering the nature or size of the extra-framework cation. Instead, the organisation of charge-balancing cations within the framework is a key parameter affecting the adsorption environment. This behaviour provides a conceptual link between UTSA-16 and zeolites, where the nature and location of charge-balancing cations are essential to control the adsorption properties.
items.authors: Virginia Guiotto, Nicole Polzella, Giulio Bresciani, Francesca Nerli, Matteo Signorile, Silvia Bordiga

items.title: Iron Tetraphenylporphyrin for Electrocatalytic AmmoniaOxidation in Solution and Carbon-Supported Films
items.abstract: Ammonia has recently attracted significant attention as a green fuel for fuel cells due to its advantages over hydrogen.Electrochemical ammonia oxidation has traditionally relied on noble metal catalysts such as Pt.However, scarcity and poisoning issues have motivated the exploration of molecular complexes as alternatives.Herein, we report iron tetraphenylporphyrin, Fe(TPP)Cl, as catalyst for electrochemical ammonia oxidation reaction (eAOR), both in homogeneous conditions, in dichloromethane (DCM) solutions, and incorporated in carbon black, in acetonitrile (ACN) solutions.Catalytic activity in homogeneous conditions is demonstrated by cyclic voltammetry whereas surface incorporation of the catalyst into catalytic films is confirmed by resonance Raman spectroscopy and cyclic voltammetry.It is a rare example of a non-noble metal, hybrid molecular catalysis for ammonia oxidation reaction.
items.authors: Nikolaos Kostopoulos, Ziwen Zhao, Luca D'Amario, Alina Sekretareva

items.title: Density Functional Theory of Dion-Jacobson Double Perovskite Halides
items.abstract: First-principles density functional theory was used to study six (four unreported) hybrid layered double perovskites of the Dion-Jacobson A2MM ′′′ X8 family. All 6 compounds consist of organic diamines that bridge rock-saltordered inorganic octahedra, with Ag+ as the M ′ site and Bi+3/Sb+3 as the M′′′ site. Both aliphatic (1,3-diaminopropane [PDA], 1,4-diaminobutane [BDA], 1,8-diaminooctane [ODA]) and aromatic (para-phenylenediamine [PPDA]) spac-ers are investigated, revealing how composition affects the band gap character and magnitude. Formation energy analysis using the DFT-D3 method reveals negative formation energies with respect to relevant precursors. Furthermore, calculations using the complex dielectric function reveal key optical properties, including absorption coefficients, refractive indices, and complex permittivity.
items.authors: Sarang Srikanth, Neshwanth Kumar Tene, Srinagesh Kumar Potluri, Adam Malofsky, Micheal Annis
items.title_zh: Dion-Jacobson双钙钛矿卤化物的密度泛函理论研究
items.summary_zh: 采用第一性原理的密度泛函理论研究了六种（其中四种未报道）Dion-Jacobson A2MM′′′X8家族的混合层状双钙钛矿。所有六种化合物均由有机二胺桥接的岩盐结构无机八面体组成，其中Ag+作为M′位点，Bi3+/Sb3+作为M′′′位点。研究了脂肪族（1,3-二氨基丙烷[PDA]、1,4-二氨基丁烷[BDA]、1,8-二氨基辛烷[ODA]）和芳香族（对苯二胺[PPDA]）间隔体，揭示了成分对带隙特性和大小的影响。使用DFT-D3方法的形成能分析显示相对于相关前体具有负的形成能。此外，利用复介电函数的计算揭示了关键的光学特性，包括吸收系数、折射率和复介电常数。

items.title: Building the Data Foundations for the Design and Discovery of Transition Metal Complexes
items.abstract: The unique chemistry of transition metal complexes (TMCs) enables several advanced technologies in diverse fields including renewable energies, medicine, and catalysis. Machine learning methods can accelerate their rational design but are bounded by limited dataset sizes, restricted chemical scopes, and insufficient quality. This Perspective surveys the current landscape of TMC datasets and investigates how they seek to address these challenges. The analysis focuses on the data curation processes as well as the scope of the properties provided, and their level of theory. Furthermore, the applications and methodological advancements enabled by TMC datasets are reviewed, including the generative design of metal ligands and the evolutionary optimization of TMCs. The Perspective concludes by outlining future directions, with particular emphasis on extending data to broader chemical scopes including non-equilibrium geometries, establishing community-wide data formats and benchmarks, and developing strategies to effectively integrate heterogeneous data sources.
items.authors: Hannes Kneiding, Bastian Bjerkem Skjelstad, Luca Cibinel, Lucı́a Morán-González, Ainara Nova, David Balcells
items.title_zh: 构建过渡金属配合物设计与发现的数据基础
items.summary_zh: 过渡金属配合物（TMCs）独特的化学性质推动了可再生能源、医学和催化等多个领域的先进技术发展。机器学习方法能够加速其理性设计，但受限于数据集规模小、化学范围有限和质量不足。本文综述了当前TMC数据集的现状，并探讨了如何应对这些挑战。分析重点在于数据整理过程、所提供属性的范围及其理论水平。此外，本文回顾了TMC数据集所支持的应用和方法进展，包括金属配体的生成设计和TMC的进化优化。最后，文章展望了未来的发展方向，特别强调扩展数据至更广泛的化学范围（包括非平衡几何）、建立社区共享的数据格式和基准，以及开发有效整合异构数据源的策略。

items.title: Computational design and prioritization of database-absent small-molecule GLP-1 receptor agonist candidates from public bioactivity data
items.abstract: Public bioactivity data were used to construct a reproducible workflow for the computational prioritization of small-molecule glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R) agonist candidates. Exact IC50, EC50, and Ki measurements were standardized, converted to pActivity, and deduplicated after structural exclusion of peptide-like records. The resulting dataset comprised 337 compounds and 155 Murcko scaffolds. Morgan fingerprints and physicochemical descriptors were evaluated using ridge regression, random forest, and XGBoost with scaffold-based validation. Random forest provided the lowest mean five-fold cross-validation root-mean-square error (RMSE; 0.497 pActivity units). Its scaffold-disjoint holdout performance was R2 = 0.236, RMSE = 0.760, and mean absolute error = 0.499. Local modifications of orforglipron generated 1,701 valid, unique analogs. Composite prioritization incorporated predicted activity, quantitative estimate of druglikeness, synthetic accessibility, and database absence. All 146 queried structures were absent from ChEMBL and PubChem under the implemented identity criteria. Of these, 46 passed an exploratory physicochemical filter, and 20 were shortlisted. No generated candidate passed the stricter drug-likeness filter. The leading candidate, GLP1R-01162, had predicted pActivity 7.677 and composite score 0.5400. These results defined an auditable set of computational hypotheses; they did not establish agonism, experimental potency, synthetic feasibility, or global novelty. Functional testing and independent novelty assessment remained necessary.
items.authors: JOGU MOHAN

items.title: Machine learning prediction of bismuth recovery from literature data: publication-grouped validation, anchored calibration and chemical interpretation
items.abstract: Machine learning models trained on published leaching data often report high accuracy from random splits that place runs of one study in both training and test sets. This study tested whether reported operating conditions can predict bismuth recovery for a study that the model has not seen. A data set of 485 runs from 82 sources was compiled across six unit operations; runs designed to retain bismuth, plate part of a bath or recover another metal were set aside, leaving 375 recovery runs from 72 studies. Thirteen models, including a mean baseline, were compared under random, publication-grouped and feedstock-grouped validation, and six of them under temporal validation. Random splits gave R2 up to 0.57, whereas publication-grouped validation gave at most 0.09 (95% interval −0.22 to 0.28); about half of the residual variance lay between publications. Three measured runs from a new study raised R2 for its remaining runs from about zero to 0.48, and Gaussian-process predictions were positively rank-correlated with measured recovery in 83% of studies. Within studies, recovery rose with acid concentration and temperature, although the temperature trend tended to reverse across studies. Literature data can therefore rank conditions for a new feed, but absolute prediction needs a few local measurements; an offline browser tool that applies this approach to leaching is provided.
items.authors: Subash Chandra Bose Rapaka

items.title: PolycIMS: Polymers for Automated Cyclic Ion Mobility Spectrometry Calibration
items.abstract: The development and commercialization of cyclic ion mobility spectrometry (cIMS) instruments has considerably expanded the level of structural details that can be accessed for gaseous ions. Commercial cIMS instruments rely on travelling wave ion mobility spectrometry (TWIMS), a technique that requires calibration of the measured arrival times to enable the determination of collisional cross sections (CCS). Most calibration strategies use peptide mixtures that span a CCS range of approximately 100 – 400 Å2, which can introduce significant inaccuracies when extrapolating to larger ion structures. In addition, TWIMS calibration remains a tedious data processing step that would greatly benefit from automation. Here, we introduce polycIMS, a command-line tool that automates cIMS calibration and generates charge-independent calibration curves covering a broad CCS range from 100 – 1500 Å², within just 3 minutes on a standard laptop. Calibrated CCS can be determined in He or N 2 ( TW CCS N2→He , TW CCS N2→N2 ) using inexpensive, commercially-available polymer standards and are validated against reported values for more than 50 reference ions. Furthermore, the derived calibration parameters are largely insensitive to collisional activation, making it possible to calibrate multistage cIMS workflows such as slice collision induced unfolding (CIU n ). We anticipate that the simplicity and accessibility of polycIMS will encourage its adoption as a new standard for cIMS calibration.
items.authors: Quentin Duez, Louis Groignet, Thomas Robert, Fabien Chirot, Pascal Gerbaux, Julien De Winter

items.title: From Molecular Building Blocks to Corrugated Graphitic Carbon Nitride: Chemical Origins of Structural Preference and Electronic Diversity
items.abstract: Despite nearly two decades of intensive research, the fundamental chemical bonding responsible for the structural stability and electronic structure of graphitic carbon nitride (g-C N ) remains unresolved.In ₃N₄) rem ₄) remai particular, the interplay between π-electron delocalization and lone-pair-bearing nitrogen atoms, which simultaneously stabilizes the framework through conjugation and destabilizes it through steric repulsion, has not been established.Here, we address this long-standing question using a comprehensive moleculesto-materials approach.This strategy reveals several energetically accessible structural isomers, including hitherto unknown ones, and establishes the bonding principles governing the evolution of g-C N .We ₃N₄) rem ₄) remai demonstrate that steric repulsion between adjacent nitrogen lone pairs is the primary driving force behind framework corrugation, thereby alleviating unfavorable non-bonding N•••N interactions and dictating structural stability.Furthermore, the frontier electronic structure differs fundamentally between the two polymorphs: heptazine-based graphitic carbon nitride (h-g-C N ) is dominated by delocalized π-type ₃N₄) rem ₄) remai frontier orbitals, whereas triazine-based graphitic carbon nitride (t-g-C N ) exhibits predominantly σ-type ₃N₄) rem ₄) remai frontier states.The frontier electronic states are primarily governed by the peripheral nitrogen atoms of the heptazine and triazine units, thereby establishing their central role in chemical reactivity and electronic properties.These findings provide a unified bonding framework that resolves the long-standing ambiguity surrounding the stability and electronic structure of graphitic carbon nitride and offer a fundamental basis for the rational design of next-generation carbon nitride materials.
items.authors: Gaurav Jhaa, Tawfik A. Saleh

items.title: Molecular Engineering of Fano Resonances for Enhanced Single-Molecule Thermoelectrics
items.abstract: Enhancing the thermoelectric power factor of single-molecule junctions requires simultaneously achieving high electrical conductance and thermopower, which are often mutually constrained. The sharp and asymmetric transmission features produced by Fano resonances offer a promising strategy for mitigating this trade-off. However, quantitative molecular structure–line-shape relationships linking molecular modifications to the resonance valley position and peak-valley energy width remain underexplored. Here, we demonstrate a molecular engineering strategy based on electronically tunable 9-fluorenylidene derivatives to tailor Fano resonance line shapes in single-molecule junctions. Systematic density functional theory and non-equilibrium Green’s function (DFT-NEGF) calculations reveal that substituent-induced variations in local orbital energies, backbone-side-chain coupling and localized-delocalized state detuning control the resonance valley position and the peak-valley energy width. Specifically, the valley position correlates linearly with the energy level of the side-group-localized LUMO, whereas the width is governed by the combined effect of main-side-chain coupling and localized-delocalized state detuning. Together, these two orbital descriptors provide a practical basis for the predictive molecular engineering of Fano resonance line shapes. To experimentally validate this strategy, we synthesized and characterized the designed dicyanomethylene-substituted derivative C -(CN) 2 alongside a control molecule A -O . Electrochemically controlled scanning tunneling microscope break-junction (EC-STM-BJ) measurements confirm the emergence of Fano resonance features near the Fermi level for C -(CN) 2 , in agreement with the DFT-NEGF prediction, whereas no comparable features is observed for A -O. Crucially, statistical single-molecule conductance and thermopower measurements reveal that C -(CN) 2 simultaneously exhibits higher conductance ( G ) and Seebeck coefficient ( S ) than A -O , overcoming the usual trade-off between these two parameters. This synergy effect yields a 97.6% enhancement in thermoelectric power factor ( GS 2 ) relative to control systems. By establishing explicit structure–line-shape–property relationships, this work provides a practical molecular engineering strategy for engineering Fano resonances in single-molecule thermoelectrics.
items.authors: Qianyu Ding, Kai Song, Weichen Bai, Mingchen Liang, Wei Hao, Yaping Zang

items.title: Adsorption regime changes the information needed for data-driven metal–organic framework screening
items.abstract: How much fitting evidence, and which materials descriptors, are needed to prioritize porous materials? We analyze archived computational uptake labels for 279,010 metal–organic frameworks at four CO2/CH4 conditions (298 K). In retrospective experiments using target-informed example selection, each condition reaches at least 90% of its B = 1000 top-5% recall endpoint by B = 500. Local-chemistry RAC descriptors improve methane top-5% recall by 0.175 at 5.8 bar but only 0.039 at 65 bar, consistent with a pressure-dependent balance between chemical and geometric signals. These values describe predictor-fitting budgets, not total acquisition cost: the random-split setting also uses approximately 44,642 labeled structures for conformal calibration. Missing historical split identities and reference-informed candidate selection constrain transfer and shortlist claims. Thus, adsorption conditions appear to modify representation utility, while prospective label efficiency and physical attribution require independent, leakage-audited validation.
items.authors: Natalia Lydia Papadantonaki, Angelo Di Bella, Shayan Abaei, Mehrdad Asgari

items.title: Detection and Characterization of the Cosmological Neutrino Background by EPR Spectroscopy on Molecular Hydrino with Implications for Telecommunications
items.abstract: A hydrino atom, H(1/p) solved using a Maxwellian electrodynamics and relativistic mechanics, is atomic hydrogen with state energy En = -13.598/n2 eV, in which n = 1/p, and p is limited by the energy in the electric field of the proton to 126 whereafter the proton and electron decay. Electron transitions to hydrino states involve an initial non-radiative energy transfer to a catalyst that serves as an energy hole or sink of a quantized amount of energy, 2mE1 (m is integer) to be transferred to a catalyst such as HOH, a free or nascent water molecule. Furthermore, hydrino atoms can react to form the corresponding diatomic molecule referred to as molecular hydrino H2(1/p). In contrast to molecular hydrogen (H2), the molecular hydrino (H2(1/p)) is paramagnetic with S = ½ comprising a paired and unpaired electron in the same MO wherein the lower energy state central field is provided by photons akin to gluons in nucleons in addition to the field of the protons. Due to its unique structure, H2(1/p)) interacts with the neutrinos in the energy range of the cosmological neutrino background (𝐶𝜈𝐵) as confirmed by the neutrino mediated observations of predicted fine structure, predicted high magnetic field Paschen Beck effect, large downfield shifts, temporal changes of EPR spectra due to accumulated changes in fine structure state populations, extraordinary broadened signals, zero order absorption occurring in the perpendicular and parallel modes, and the observation of magnetic dipole-dipole interactions of H2(1/4)-H2 dimer requiring intramolecular angular momentum transfer from a neutrino excited fine structure state in H2(1/4) as well as unique temperature and matrix dependences of the EPR signals. EPR was used to detect and characterize the 𝐶𝜈𝐵 for the first time. The isotropic and parallel propagation nature of 𝐶𝜈𝐵 can be exploited for line of site telecommunications requiring no transmission power to transmit signals in any direction unattenuated and undispersed through any physical barrier, including the Earth.
items.authors: Wilfred R. Hagen, Randell L. Mills
items.title_zh: 利用EPR光谱法检测宇宙中微子背景及其在通信中的应用
items.summary_zh: 本研究探讨了氢原子H(1/p)的性质，该原子通过麦克斯韦电动力学和相对论力学求解，具有状态能量En = -13.598/n² eV，其中n = 1/p，p受质子电场能量限制，最大为126。电子跃迁至氢原子状态涉及初始的非辐射能量转移至催化剂，如自由或新生水分子HOH。氢原子可反应形成二原子分子，即分子氢原子H2(1/p)，其具有S = ½的顺磁性，包含配对和未配对电子。由于其独特结构，H2(1/p)与宇宙中微子背景（CνB）中的微子相互作用，观察到预测的细结构、高磁场Paschen Beck效应、显著的信号展宽等现象。

items.title: Absorption and Emission Spectra in Aqueous Solution with Coupled-Cluster Accuracy
items.abstract: Quantitative prediction of electronic spectra in water requires an accurate treatment of electronic excitation, nuclear structure, and state-specific solvation including effects from hydrogen bonding. Here, photoacids and photobases in aqueous solution are used as stringent test systems for statespecific embedded cluster reference interaction site model calculations combined with the iterative coupled cluster models CC2 and CC3. Wigner nuclear-ensemble and adiabatic Hessian Franck-Condon calculations reproduce absorption and emission band maxima on an absolute energy scale with typical errors of 0.1–0.2 eV without empirical shift or scaling corrections; the energies of resolved 0–0 transitions in photobases are even reproduced within a few hundredths of an eV. The simulations also resolve contributions from different excited states and changes in the emitting species. Derived excited-state acidity changes, ∆pK∗ a , show similar accuracy for photoacids and photobases, with residual errors governed by cancellation or accumulation between protonation states.
items.authors: Niklas Sülzner, Ömer F. C. Tiska, Julia Haberhauer, Patrick Kibies, Stefan M. Kast, Christof Hättig

items.title: Tension-Limited Leaflet-Asymmetry Budding Predicts the Size and Rate of Tumour Ectosome Shedding
items.abstract: Fatty-acid protocells growing by outer-leaflet monomer uptake accumulate a transbilayer area imbalance that is relieved by budding once the reduced imbalance Δa exceeds a critical value, as described by area-difference elasticity (ADE). It is tempting to read modern tumour ectosome shedding as the same physics. We show that the naive transfer fails, and derive the version that does not. A protocell is osmotically relaxed; the plasma membrane of a cancer cell is under tension (σ ≈ 0.01–0.1 mN/m), which imposes an area cost absent from the protocell treatment. Replacing the shape-instability criterion with an explicit energy balance for bud formation gives a threshold in the differential leaflet tension, Δτ_c = sqrt(8κΣ)/h with Σ = σ + K_A h^2/R^2, and a bud radius at threshold r* = sqrt(2κ/Σ) that is independent of both h and K_A. Retaining the finite-parent term K_A h^2/R^2 is essential: in the tension-free limit it acts as an effective tension, so the threshold does not vanish but tends to Δa_c → sqrt(2κ/K_A)/h = 0.21–0.87. The O(1) ADE criterion assumed for protocells is thereby recovered as a derived result, and a tension-free vesicle is found to bud at a sizeable fraction of its own radius rather than shedding nano-vesicles. The protocell growth kinetics map exactly onto flippase/scramblase imbalance under γ → 2a_L j. Using bending rigidities measured on giant plasma membrane vesicles (κ = 5.4–35 k_BT, including the metastatic line MDA-MB-231), the model predicts bud diameters of 43–346 nm, overlapping measured cancer extracellular vesicles, at a threshold requiring translocation of only 0.09–0.76 mol% of plasma-membrane lipid. Because a single TMEM16F scramblase translocates 45 000 lipids per second while the critical net flux is below one lipid per second per square micron, the thermodynamic threshold is not the regulated quantity: the shedding rate is. Reported secretion rates of 60–80 EV per cell per hour correspond to a net outward flux of 0.2–1 lipid per square micrometre per second, a calibration rather than a test of the model. Two sharp falsification tests — the bud radius falls as the inverse square root of the membrane tension, and grows as the square root of the bending rigidity — distinguish this mechanism from ESCRT-dependent biogenesis. We argue explicitly against reading the size agreement between protocells and tumour vesicles as evolutionary atavism.
items.authors: Peter Mikuláš

items.title: Zr-MOF/Quinone Multicatalysis Enables Programmable Aerobic Synthesis of Benzimidazoles
items.abstract: Selectivity control in aerobic oxidation reactions containing several oxidizable functional groups remains challenging. Herein, we show that the chemoselectivity of a Zr-MOF/quinone 2 multicatalytic platform can be controlled through modulation of the organic redox co-catalyst. In contrast to previously reported Zr-MOF-808/(hydro)quinone combinations that promote direct oxidation of anilines or thiols, Zr-MOF-808/1,8-dichloroanthraquinone unlocks a different reaction pathway to selectively oxidize primary alcohols in the presence of aromatic diamines and aminothiophenols. This pathway enables the one-pot synthesis of 2-substituted benzimidazoles and benzothiazoles under atmospheric air. Mechanistic experiments support coupled catalytic cycles in which Lewis-acidic Zr sites facilitate quinone-mediated alcohol oxidation, while the MOF/semiquinone interface regenerates the oxidized mediator using oxygen. This method furnishes a highly sustainable synthesis of 31 benzimidazole and benzothiazole products, permitting recovery and reuse of both catalytic components.
items.authors: Juan Camilo Arango-Daza, Spandan Hati, Sakarn Khamkaeo, Yuttapoom Puttisong, Miguel A. Rivero-Crespo
items.title_zh: Zr-MOF/醌多催化剂实现可编程的有氧苯并咪唑合成
items.summary_zh: 在含有多个可氧化官能团的有氧氧化反应中，选择性控制仍然具有挑战性。本文展示了Zr-MOF/醌多催化平台的化学选择性可以通过调节有机氧化还原共催化剂来控制。与之前报道的Zr-MOF-808/(氢)醌组合不同，Zr-MOF-808/1,8-二氯蒽醌开启了一条不同的反应路径，能够在芳香二胺和氨基硫酚存在下选择性氧化一醇。这一途径实现了在常压空气下的一锅法合成2-取代的苯并咪唑和苯并噻唑。机理实验支持耦合催化循环，其中路易斯酸性Zr位点促进醌介导的一醇氧化，而MOF/半醌界面利用氧气再生氧化介质。该方法提供了31种苯并咪唑和苯并噻唑产品的高可持续合成，允许催化组分的回收和再利用。

items.title: Size-Controlled HgTe Nanocrystals Achieve Near-Unity Shortwave Infrared Emission
items.abstract: The near-infrared (NIR, 700-1000 nm) and short-wave infrared (SWIR, 1000-2000 nm) regions of light are privileged for optoelectronic applications due to the decreased scattering and diminished autofluorescence arising from the few natural chromophores which absorb or emit in these windows. We demonstrate a two-stage, size-resolved synthesis of spherical HgTe quantum dots (QDs) with narrowband photoluminescence tunable across the NIR and SWIR which combine exceptionally high photoluminescence quantum yields (QY 80%), low polydispersity ( 10%), and stability in air. Using this synthetic control, we determine the size-dependent bandgap and molar extinction coefficients of HgTe under extreme confinement, and show conclusively that separating nucleation from growth — via a fast injection followed by a slow one — suppresses Ostwald ripening. Post-synthetic incubation with zinc salts further improves optical stability, pushing QY to near unity across the SWIR, including at telecom-relevant wavelengths. We then formulate water-soluble HgTe QD micelles as contrast agents for in vivo mouse imaging in the SWIR, achieving 100 frame/s video-rate imaging above 1400 nm with contrast and temporal resolution that substantially exceed those of indocyanine green. Together, these results establish that even without a protective shell, HgTe QDs offer a near-optimal, air-stable platform for optoelectronic applications at telecom-relevant wavelengths .
items.authors: Belle Coffey, Eric Lin, Lorenzo Spollero, Skylar Whitley, Caleb Tuot-Pike, Sohan Jadhav

items.title: Density Functional Theory Bond Dissociation Energies of Model Compounds Relevant to LDL Oxidation: Bis-Allylic C–H, Phenolic O–H and Hydroperoxide O–H Bonds
items.abstract: Background : Oxidative modification of low-density lipoprotein (LDL) contributes to atherogenesis, with polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) as its main chemical target. Vitamin E is an effective chainbreaking antioxidant in vitro, yet large clinical trials showed no cardiovascular benefit. We calculated bond dissociation energies (BDEs) of model compounds to quantify the underlying thermodynamics. Methods : Density functional theory calculations (PySCF; B3LYP/6-311+G(d,p)//B3LYP/6-31G*, scaled zero-point energy, 0K) were performed for butane, 1,4-pentadiene, phenol, catechol and methyl hydroperoxide. Vitamin E was not calculated at the relaxed level; published values were used. A truncated tocopherol model (5,7,8-trimethylchroman-6-ol) was run at screening level only (B3LYP/6-31+G*, unrelaxed geometries, no zero-point correction), with phenol at the same level. Results : The bis-allylic C–H bond of 1,4-pentadiene (68.2 kcal/mol) was 28.3 below that of butane (96.5). Catechol O–H (73.4) was 8.4 below phenol (81.8). The hydroperoxide model (79.6) fell 2.2 below phenol, opposite to the approximate literature order; the cause was not investigated. In screening calculations the tocopherol model was 9.0 below phenol. Published values place α-tocopherol O–H at about 77 to 78 kcal/mol, about 10 below phenol, the same direction as our screening gap. Computed values were 1.7 to 8.6 kcal/mol below approximate literature values, so gaps and ordering, not absolute values, are interpreted. Conclusions : The calculations quantify the thermodynamic basis for PUFA vulnerability and for the stronger hydrogen donation of polyphenol-type O–H bonds. They do not by themselves show donation to peroxyl radicals. Bond energies cannot explain the clinical trial results; kinetics, LDL localization and tocopherol-mediated peroxidation must be considered. No clinical outcomes or biomarkers were computed.
items.authors: Yadlapalli Anirudh

items.title: Process and Systems Modeling of Hydrothermal Liquefaction for Fuels and Bioproducts from Wet Organic Wastes
items.abstract: Hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL) can convert wet organic waste into fuels and bioproducts, but variation in feedstocks and operating conditions can propagate from product yields to system performance and deployment. This study linked machine learning based HTL yield prediction with process simulation, techno-economic analysis (TEA), life cycle assessment (LCA), uncertainty analysis, and surrogate modeling. A literature data set of 402 experiments was used to predict biocrude, aqueous, gas, and solids yields, with 71.8% of predictions within ±5 wt% of experimental values. The predicted yields reproduced 77.1% of internal rate of return (IRR) and 83.2% of GWP 100 estimates within ±5% and ±10 kg CO 2 e/kg, respectively, and were integrated into two deployment configurations (centralized and decentralized HTL) and two product pathways (biobinder/biofuel and sustainable aviation fuel [SAF]). Process and system scale analyses showed that operating conditions strongly affecting HTL performance could have weaker or competing economic effects due to tradeoffs among product yields, water handling, energy requirements, and capital costs. Across representative feedstocks, decentralized biobinder systems achieved median IRRs up to 35.8%, compared with up to 8.0% for decentralized SAF systems. Feedstock price, followed by biocrude quality, and biocrude yield emerged as the leading economic drivers. Monte Carlo filtering identified waste tipping fee thresholds $25.1–196.7 per wet metric tonne for achieving the 10% IRR target. These results show that existing tipping fee structure can support HTL deployment in some cases, while higher tipping fees or additional financial incentives can expand viability and enable higher investment returns.
items.authors: Ali Ahmad, Rohit Bhagat, Kevin Warren, Saketnath Pabba, Yalin Li

items.title: BRACE: Bayesian Residual-covariance Adaptive Calibration for Multi-Endpoint ADMET Prediction
items.abstract: Deciding which ADMET assays to run on a compound requires a calibrated probability that it will pass each assay not yet measured, given those already run. A multi-task predictor supplies these via the cross-assay covariance of its prediction errors (residuals), but this covariance is usually estimated once, from historical data. It therefore misses correlations specific to a program’s chemical series (scaffolds) and knows nothing about assays unique to the program. With only hundreds to thousands of program compounds, we adapt this covariance rather than retrain the predictor. BRACE merges historical and program residuals by expectation–maximization into one covariance covering every assay, then corrects it per scaffold series with an Inverse-Wishart hierarchical model; an optional copula handles non-Gaussian data. A closed-form identity makes its posterior-mean covariance equal the Ledoit–Wolf shrinkage estimator exactly, so its prior strength comes from the data, without cross-validation. On a semi-synthetic 36-assay benchmark built from the residual covariance of about 780,000 real ADMET compounds, BRACE cuts the pass-probability mean absolute error by up to 76% versus the QComp multi-task baseline. Its always-on merging step matches or beats QComp in all 29 settings of a robustness sweep; the optional per-scaffold step helps when series-specific structure exists and hurts when it does not, and we map when to use it (chosen with hindsight here; an automatic rule is future work). On a real temporal split, the per-scaffold steps raise AUC-ROC from 0.789 to 0.860 and MCC from 0.37 to 0.53, and lower Brier from 0.187 to 0.152. However, about 96% of that gain comes from recalibrating each series’ mean and variance, which simple untuned shrinkage also achieves; BRACE’s distinctive cross-assay term adds about 4% here and matters mainly under strong cross-assay structure.
items.authors: Tianchi Chen, Kamala Dadashova, Bingjia Yang, Sean Lawrence Wu

items.title: DolphinQCT: The Light-Weighted, Python Based Quasi-Classical Trajectory Setup Tool for ORCA
items.abstract: ORCA provides an ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) module, but quasi-classical trajectory (QCT) simulations require external preparation of initial coordinates and velocities. We present DolphinQCT, a lightweight, open-source Python tool that samples initial conditions from ORCA frequency calculations and exports them as molecular dynamics restart files. The workflow combines Boltzmann sampling of vibrational energy levels, random-phase normal-mode sampling, and screening based on deviations between electronic and harmonic potential energies. Applications to two post-transition-state bifurcation reactions—deuterated methoxy radical isomerization with density functional theory and nitrene insertion with g-xTB—yield product ratios of 64:68 and 7.9:1, respectively, consistent with the previously reported ratios of 1:1 and 8.3:1.
items.authors: Yusheng Shi, Tianbo Tse

items.title: Electrochemical Capture of Microplastics via Reversible Metal Deposition in Aqueous Solutions
items.abstract: Microplastics are persistent aqueous contaminants for which effective removal strategies remain needed. Here, we investigate electrochemical deposition as a means of capturing suspended polystyrene (PS) particles. The purpose of this study is to understand the plausibility of electrochemical deposition as a means for removing microplastics from aqueous systems. The central hypothesis guiding this work is that ramified solid metallic deposits created during electrodeposition can mechanically capture plastic particles suspended in the liquid phase. PS particles of 200 nm and 250 μm were evaluated in ZnSO4 electrolyte under applied potentials from 0 to −4 V, with surfactant conditions also examined. Electrochemical treatment resulted in visibly reduced turbidity, suggesting a decrease in suspended particle concentration. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) showed particles attached to or incorporated within deposited zinc. Particle capture was not observed at 0 V but was evident under active zinc deposition at −2 V, supporting the role of electrodeposited zinc in particle capture. The observed particle–electrode interactions differed with particle size: larger particles were partially embedded within rough, dendritic zinc deposits, whereas nanoscale particles were densely distributed across the deposited structure. These observations demonstrate the ability of electrodeposition to facilitate particle capture through distinct particle–deposit interactions and support its potential as a tunable approach for investigating microplastic capture in aqueous systems.
items.authors: Casey Mari Apurado, Amaris Sacalxot-Berrios, Kent J. X. Zheng
items.title_zh: 电化学捕获水中微塑料的可逆金属沉积研究
items.summary_zh: 微塑料是持久的水体污染物，亟需有效去除策略。本研究探讨了电化学沉积作为捕获悬浮聚苯乙烯（PS）颗粒的方法。研究的核心假设是，电沉积过程中形成的分支固体金属沉积物能够机械捕获液相中的塑料颗粒。在ZnSO4电解质中，评估了200 nm和250 μm的PS颗粒，施加电位范围为0至−4 V，并考察了表面活性剂的影响。电化学处理显著降低了浊度，表明悬浮颗粒浓度减少。扫描电子显微镜（SEM）显示颗粒附着或嵌入沉积的锌中。在0 V时未观察到颗粒捕获，但在−2 V的活性锌沉积下明显可见，支持了电沉积锌在颗粒捕获中的作用。颗粒与电极的相互作用因颗粒大小而异：较大颗粒部分嵌入粗糙的树枝状锌沉积中，而纳米颗粒则在沉积结构上密集分布。这些观察结果表明电沉积能够有效捕获微塑料。

items.title: Removal of Cu(II) and a PET Glitter Microplastic Surrogate by Alginate, Alginate–Opuntia, and Chitosan-Treated Alginate–Opuntia Beads
items.abstract: The use of alginate-only beads, alginate–Opuntia (AO) beads, and chitosan-treated AO beads for the removal of Cu(II) and a PET glitter (a microplastic surrogate) from water has been investigated. Each bead type was made from the previous one by the addition of one component. Batch experiments were carried out in water containing glitter, Cu(II), or both, and AO beads soaked in dilute acetic acid without chitosan served as a control for the acid. The removal of Cu(II) in copper-only water was 45.71 ± 1.97%, 59.44 ± 2.28%, and 84.19 ± 2.65% for the alginate-only, AO, and chitosan-treated beads, respectively (mean ± SD, n = 12, 6 h, 140 rpm). Opuntia increased the Cu(II) removal by 13.72 percentage points and chitosan by a further 24.75 points (paired t-test, p 0.001 for both, and p ≤ 0.0013 for the batch means). In the presence of 2.00 g of glitter, the chitosan-treated beads still removed about 84% of the Cu(II). Meanwhile, the glitter removal increased by about 7 points with Opuntia but changed by less than 0.25 points with chitosan (p = 0.648 and 0.231). No significant difference was found between the acid-soaked and the untreated AO beads. It can be concluded that Opuntia was responsible for the increase in glitter capture and chitosan for most of the increase in Cu(II) removal.
items.authors: Shilo Karakkattu

items.title: De novo Rewriting DNA Identity into Functional RNA via Genetic Information Compiler
items.abstract: Genetic information is expressed through the molecular products encoded by DNA. Synthetic systems can regulate these outputs, but retain the original link between DNA identity and function. Re-engineering this link could assign new functions to existing DNA identities. Here we present a genetic information compiler (GIC) that converts selected double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) identities into user-defined RNA outputs. GIC exploits the nontrivial activity of λ exonuclease to interrogate dsDNA and release predefined activators. These activators restore T7 promoters and drive programmable transcription. This modular architecture enables orthogonal and concurrent routing, logic processing, and control of RNA identity, amplitude, composition and timing. Spatial compartmentalization further reveals activator-mediated information transfer between separated compartments. By programming functional gRNAs as outputs, GIC enables tunable, sequence-dependent, and selective regulation of Cas9, Cas12a and Cas13a. GIC establishes a new programmable information layer in which existing dsDNA identities can be interpreted de novo as user-defined functional RNAs.
items.authors: Linghao Zhang, Qinze Rong, Xueting Wang, Dandan Tian, Shihui Wang, Huiyu Liu

items.title: Rapid mechanochemical dinitrogen fixation for single-atom skeletal editing
items.abstract: Direct utilization of dinitrogen (N2) in organic synthesis remains an unmet challenge in sustainable chemistry, particularly under mild conditions. Conventional transition-metal-mediated N2 functionalization typically requires elaborately designed catalysts under harsh conditions, limiting operational practicality. Here, we report a mechanochemical strategy that achieves rapid, lithium-mediated N2 reduction at ambient pressure and temperature in under two minutes, delivering polymorphic mixtures of α- and β-lithium nitride. The resulting metal nitride serves as a versatile platform for single nitrogen-atom transfer: applied to skeletal conversion reactions, it enables direct O-to-N transmutation of furans and aromatic oxonium salts into the corresponding pyrroles and pyridine derivatives, establishing a formal incorporation of N2 into N-heterocycles. The photophysical consequences of the single-atom edit on excited-state properties of the molecular chromophores were evaluated.
items.authors: Hayoung Shin, Jihye Park, Da Hye Lee, Hosun Shin, Hyeokjun Park, Yoonsu Park

items.title: New Oxygen Sensor with Polyaniline Spin Probe and Low Frequency EPR (L-Band) Detection System
items.abstract: Our research demonstrates the potential of certain PANI samples to serve as sensitive and reliable spin probes for oxygen detection, while also highlighting the advantages of the low-frequency EPR technique. Compared to other methods of measuring oxygen concentration, the new sensor—based on a PANI spin probe and a low-frequency EPR detector—offers unique benefits: it ensures high sensitivity to changes in oxygen concentration and does not require direct contact between the EPR detector and the sensor itself (the polyaniline probe). This sensor can be placed in isolated environments, including biological samples (tissues), and - thanks to the use of nanodispersed polyaniline - even inside living cells.
items.authors: Mikołaj Baranowski, Sebastian Golczak, Jerzy J. Langer

items.title: Site-selective Halogenation of Aromatic C-H Bonds via Electrocatalytic Flavin Adenine Dinucleotide Cofactor Regeneration
items.abstract: Flavin-dependent halogenases (FDHs) catalyze site-selective C–H halogenation of electron-rich aromatic compounds but rely on multienzyme cofactor-recycling systems to continuously supply reduced flavin (FADH 2 ). Here, we establish an overpotential-driven, mediator-assisted bioelectrocatalytic strategy for FADH 2 regeneration that eliminates auxiliary reductases, nicotinamide cofactors, and enzyme immobilization. Cyclic voltammetry confirmed the proton-dependent FAD/FADH 2 redox couple (-0.42 V vs Ag/AgCl, 3.5 M KCl) and the competing oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). Bulk electrolysis involving the FDH RebH revealed that L-ascorbic acid suppresses ORR-derived species more effectively than conventional catalase/glutathione/superoxide-dismutase systems, increasing conversion of tryptophan to 7-bromotryptophan from 20% to 46% after 24 h at -0.7 V. Increasing the cathodic potential to -1.1 V improved yields to 64% without substantially improving the faradaic efficiency (FE~ 5%). Introducing redox mediators such as 2-hydroxy-1,4-naphthoquinone (HNQ) and methyl viologen (MV 2+ ) enabled the HNQ/FAD pair to achieve quantitative halogenation within 10 h (FE ~ 14%) and the MV 2+ /FAD pair within 12 h (FE ~ 9%), enabling production of 8.8 mg of 7-bromotryptophan in a scale-up reactor. Moreover, the HNQ/FAD system exhibited a kinetic isotope effect (KIE) of ( k H / k D = 1.8) for product formation in H 2 O versus D 2 O, supporting proton involvement in productive FAD regeneration and potentially reflecting cooperation between mediator-assisted electron transfer and surface-adsorbed hydrogen (H ads ) produced during the hydrogen evolution reaction in accelerating FADH 2 formation. Extending this method to engineered RebH variant 4-V enabled halogenation of larger substrates, establishing a scalable electrochemical platform for FDH catalysis. These results establish how electron delivery, proton availability, and competing oxygen reduction govern productive electrochemical flavin regeneration and provide a scalable platform for FDH catalysis.
items.authors: Batul Shakir, Xuzhong Shen, Conor Wallace, Declan B. Mackey, Jared. C. Lewis, Ricardo Javier Vázquez

items.title: FRACTAL: A Ratiometric-based Fingerprinting Framework for Robust Spectral Classification and Ratio-based Spectroscopic Marker Discovery
items.abstract: Spectral classification is conventionally performed on band intensities, yet ratios between bands have long served as diagnostic indices in vibrational spectroscopy, from lipid-to-protein markers of membrane composition to amide ratios reporting protein secondary structure. Their use, however, has remained confined to a handful of expert-selected pairs, leaving most of the ratio information contained in a spectrum unexamined. Here I present FRACTAL (Full Ratio Combinatorial Analysis for Classification and Analytical Interpretation), which computes every pairwise log-intensity ratio among detected peaks to form a complete ratiometric fingerprint, grounded in compositional data analysis. Each component is a contrast between two assigned bands and is invariant to the multiplicative factors that scale spectral intensities. Applied to serum Raman spectra from a total of 103 donors (53 with COVID-19, 50 healthy controls), FRACTAL screened all 105 ratios among 15 reproducible peaks and identified 38 discriminant contrasts; a ten-ratio fingerprint then matched full-spectrum performance across six classifier architectures spanning linear, kernel-based and ensemble methods (mean internal AUC 0.89–0.93) and generalized to a withheld 20-donor cohort, where every classifier exceeded an AUC of 0.92 and all six converged on the same donor-level prediction accuracy at the median-AUC seed. The retained ratios map onto aromatic amino acid, acute-phase protein and protein–lipid contrasts independently reported in COVID-19. FRACTAL establishes exhaustive ratiometric fingerprinting as a compact, robust and interpretable representation for spectral classification and spectroscopic marker discovery.
items.authors: Lamyaa M. Almehmadi

items.title: When Ethylene Meets Sulfur: Direct Synthesis of Minimal Ethylene-Sulfur Copolymers
items.abstract: In inverse vulcanization chemistry, research has predominantly focused on multifunctional unsaturated comonomers to stabilize sulfur-rich structures, whereas the direct copolymerization of elemental sulfur with simple olefins has remained comparatively unexplored. Extending this concept to the simplest olefin, we report Minimal Ethylene-Sulfur Copolymers (MinESC), synthesized through the direct reaction of gaseous ethylene with elemental sulfur via a base-mediated inverse vulcanization approach under mild conditions. These materials are viscoelastic fluids of tunable viscosity reaching exceptionally high values. They exhibit a peculiar sheet-like morphology, polar surfaces, elevated electrical conductivity, and high permittivity, and can be reprocessed into predominantly elastic structures following thermal treatment. Our approach provides a straightforward route to a distinct class of sulfurethylene-derived functional materials and demonstrates that inverse vulcanization chemistry can be extended to the simplest olefin under industrially relevant pressures and temperatures.
items.authors: Jules Henrotte, Francesco Zaccaria, Alessio Mingione, Hatice Mutlu, Anton Ginzburg
items.title_zh: 乙烯与硫的直接合成：最小乙烯-硫共聚物
items.summary_zh: 在反向硫化化学中，研究主要集中在多功能不饱和共聚单体上，以稳定富硫结构，而元素硫与简单烯烃的直接共聚合则相对较少探索。我们将这一概念扩展至最简单的烯烃，报道了通过气态乙烯与元素硫的直接反应合成的最小乙烯-硫共聚物（MinESC），该反应采用碱介导的反向硫化方法，在温和条件下进行。这些材料为可调粘度的粘弹性流体，粘度可达到极高值，呈现出独特的片状形态、极性表面、较高的电导率和高介电常数，并且经过热处理后可重新加工为主要为弹性的结构。我们的研究为一类独特的硫乙烯衍生功能材料提供了简单的合成途径，并表明反向硫化化学可以在工业相关的压力和温度下扩展至最简单的烯烃。

items.title: The role of membrane properties and environmental footprint in shaping the cost-climate optimal carbon capture processes
items.abstract: Membrane development for carbon capture is typically guided by CO2 permeability and CO2/N2 selectivity, although these properties alone cannot determine whether a material will deliver economically and environmentally favourable performance at scale. Herein, we develop a multi-criteria optimization framework that integrates a machine-learning surrogate model of a multi-stage membrane process with techno-economic analysis and life cycle assessment. By applying this framework to mixed matrix membranes, we investigate the interplay of membrane properties and membrane-specific inventories in defining process-level costs and environmental indicators. For the capture from flue gases produced by a waste incinerator plant and a cement plant, electricity is mostly driven by CO2/O2 selectivity within the investigated range and is the dominant contributor to process costs and climate change impacts. This makes the climate benefits of membrane-based capture strongly dependent on the electricity supply: high-performance membranes supplied with carbon-intensive electricity can have climate change impacts comparable to or even higher than those of low-performing membranes supplied with low-carbon electricity. Therefore, we show for the first time how the system-level context shapes the properties that must be prioritized and their target values to unlock economic and environmental benefits: membrane synthesis and lifetime have a substantial impact in the presence of clean electricity, whereas increasingly high CO2/O2 and CO2/N2 selectivity are needed in the presence of moderate to high carbon intensity. Overall, with this work, we identify priorities for improvement in membrane production and performance that could only be revealed by jointly considering process-level costs and environmental impacts.
items.authors: Stefania Bempeli, Julian Nohl, Hitesh Sewani, Andre Bardow, Marina Micari
items.title_zh: 膜特性与环境足迹在碳捕集过程中的作用
items.summary_zh: 碳捕集膜的开发通常以CO2渗透率和CO2/N2选择性为指导，但这些特性无法单独决定材料在规模化应用中的经济和环境表现。本文建立了一个多标准优化框架，将多级膜过程的机器学习替代模型与技术经济分析和生命周期评估相结合。通过将该框架应用于混合基质膜，我们研究了膜特性与膜特定清单在定义过程成本和环境指标中的相互作用。对于来自垃圾焚烧厂和水泥厂的烟气捕集，电力主要受CO2/O2选择性的影响，并且是过程成本和气候变化影响的主要贡献者。这使得基于膜的捕集的气候效益强烈依赖于电力供应：高性能膜在碳密集电力供应下的气候变化影响可能与低性能膜在低碳电力供应下相当或更高。因此，我们首次展示了系统级背景如何塑造必须优先考虑的特性及其目标值，以实现经济和环境效益。

items.title: Commit: Automated Scale-Up Crystallisation DataFactory for model-based pharmaceutical process development: a data-driven, mechanistic and hybrid model case study
items.abstract: In 2025, we introduced the Scale-Up Crystallisation DataFactory, an automated platform for crystallisation experimentation and Bayesian optimisation. However, the initial case study used a relatively simple three-parameter, single-objective optimisation problem. In this Commit paper, we extend the platform to a five-dimensional, multi-objective cooling-antisolvent crystallisation of lovastatin and benchmark data-driven, mechanistic and hybrid optimisation approaches. Sixteen screening experiments were followed by model-guided experiments targeting yield and particle size (D90). Bayesian optimisation produced continued improvements in hypervolume, while mechanistic and hybrid approaches did not improve experimental performance beyond screening. The results demonstrate the value of experimentally benchmarking optimisation strategies for autonomous process development.
items.authors: Thomas Pickles, Cameron J. Brown
items.title_zh: 自动化规模化结晶数据工厂在制药过程开发中的应用研究
items.summary_zh: 本文介绍了2025年推出的规模化结晶数据工厂，这是一个用于结晶实验和贝叶斯优化的自动化平台。最初的案例研究使用了相对简单的三参数单目标优化问题。在本研究中，我们将平台扩展到五维多目标冷却反溶剂结晶的洛伐他汀，并对数据驱动、机制和混合优化方法进行了基准测试。进行了十六次筛选实验，随后进行模型指导的实验，目标为产率和颗粒尺寸（D90）。贝叶斯优化在超体积方面持续改进，而机制和混合方法未能超越筛选实验的表现。结果表明，实验性基准测试优化策略对自主过程开发具有重要价值。

items.title: Phosphorus(V) Umpolung Converts Electrophilic Phosphates into Nucleophilic H-Phosphonates
items.abstract: Ubiquitous in chemistry, biology and medicine, phosphate groups form the backbone of DNA and RNA, and their analogues like phosphorothioate antisense oligonucleotides provide frontier therapies for challenging genetic disorders. However, the inherent electrophilicity of phosphorus(V) and thermodynamic stability of native P–OH bonds preclude their direct, latestage conversion into phosphate analogues. Here, we introduce a polarity-reversal (umpolung) strategy for converting electrophilic phosphates into nucleophilic H-phosphonates. This approach proceeds through two stages: P–OH thiolation into a thiophosphate followed by radical P–S cleavage, which generates the P–H bond. This sequence converts diverse phosphate substrates, such as complex drug scaffolds and nucleotides, into H-phosphonates that can undergo further phosphorus functionalization. The thiolation step also enables direct, one-pot conversion of P–OH into P–SH in nucleotides, providing a chemical route to the phosphorothioation of native phosphate backbones associated with bacterial and archaeal DNA defense. Therefore, phosphorus(V) umpolung reverses the polarity of phosphate chemistry, transforming otherwise stable P–OH bonds into synthetically versatile phosphorus functionalities.
items.authors: Petr Oeser, Petr Šimon, Kristýna Kellovská, Matthew Z. Todd, Rafael Navrátil

items.title: Revisiting Spin Contamination in Mixed-Reference Spin-Flip Time-Dependent Density-Functional Theory
items.abstract: Mixed reference spin-flip time-dependent density-functional theory (MRSF-TDDFT) has achieved widespread adoption as a computational method for describing photochemistry beyond the Franck–Condon region, as it removes most of the spin contamination limiting previous spin-flip (SF-)TDDFT approaches. The C → V excitation space, in which an electron from a doubly occupied (closed) orbital is promoted to an unoccupied (virtual) orbital, remains spin-incomplete in MRSF-TDDFT. The contamination induced by this incompleteness has consistently been reported as negligible, since the missing configurations are expected to be high in energy, thus barely coupling to low-lying vertical excitations. We show that the expression for 〈Ŝ 2 〉, which these assessments are based on, is erroneous and misses a key contribution of C → V excitations in singlet states, while triplet states always remain spin-pure. We derive and implement a corrected equation for 〈Ŝ 2 〉 and show that low-lying excited states with significant spin contamination become unavoidable if the singly occupied orbitals (SOMOs) localize onto a subsystem, decouple by symmetry, or if the density of orbitals around the Fermi level is high. We find that these results are virtually independent of the choice of density-functional approximation, but do not seem to impact the accuracy of excitation energies and spectroscopic properties. Nonetheless, these results show that severe spin contamination in MRSF-TDDFT becomes unavoidable when describing extended systems or the collective behavior of many chromophores.
items.authors: Samuel Dier, Linus Bjarne Dittmer, Anton Rikus, Andreas Dreuw, Johannes Neugebauer

items.title: Synthesis of Large-area Two-Dimension Metal-Organic Framework Films via Chemical Vapour Deposition
items.abstract: Synthesizing uniform and large-are two-dimensional (2D) metal-organic framework (MOF) films directly on substrates is highly desirable and important for MOF-based electronics, but it still remains great challenge. Here, a simple chemical vapour deposition (CVD) growth strategy with controllable-thickness and large-area capabilities has been developed to directly prepare them on substrates, in which 2,3,6,7,10,11-hexahydroxytriphenylene (HHTP) ligand films pre-deposited on substrates react with copper (II) acetylacetonate (Cu(acac) 2 ) vapor, resulting the structure transformation from small molecule thin film to Cu 3 (HHTP) 2 MOF films. The MOF films have high crystalline quality with uniform surface, large area (4 inches wafer) and controllable thickness (15 nm to 100 nm). And Replacing Cu(acac) 2 with nickel (II) acetylacetonate (Ni(acac) 2 ) and platinum (II) acetylacetonate (Pt(acac) 2 ) as metal ion source, the method can also be used to synthesize uniform Ni 3 (HHTP) 2 and Pt 3 (HHTP) 2 MOF films, suggesting the generic applicability of this method. When employed the Cu 3 (HHTP) 2 MOF films as an active material for optoelectronic devices, it simulates light-stimulated and synaptic memory properties, making it exhibit promising application in artificial biological synapse.
items.authors: Jinzhi Zhang, Runkun Li
items.title_zh: 化学气相沉积法合成大面积二维金属有机框架薄膜
items.summary_zh: 直接在基底上合成均匀且大面积的二维金属有机框架（MOF）薄膜对基于MOF的电子器件至关重要，但仍面临巨大挑战。本研究开发了一种简单的化学气相沉积（CVD）生长策略，能够控制薄膜厚度并实现大面积制备。该方法中，预先沉积在基底上的2,3,6,7,10,11-六羟基三苯ylene（HHTP）配体薄膜与铜（II）乙酰丙酮（Cu(acac)₂）蒸气反应，导致小分子薄膜转变为Cu₃(HHTP)₂ MOF薄膜。所得到的MOF薄膜具有高结晶质量、均匀表面、大面积（4英寸晶圆）和可控厚度（15 nm至100 nm）。此外，替换金属离子源为镍（II）乙酰丙酮（Ni(acac)₂）和铂（II）乙酰丙酮（Pt(acac)₂），该方法同样可合成均匀的Ni₃(HHTP)₂和Pt₃(HHTP)₂ MOF薄膜，表明该方法的通用适用性。采用Cu₃(HHTP)₂ MOF薄膜作为光电器件的活性材料时，模拟出光刺激和突触记忆特性，展现出在人工生物突触中的应用潜力。

items.title: Permutation-inversion insensitive comparison of three-dimensional molecular structures
items.abstract: We present a new approach to compare molecular geometries from a purely geometric perspective. The first step of our algorithm uses permutation-insensitive alignment of two molecules with a Gaussian-kernel-damped analog of the mean-squared deviation (MSD) between two structures. Using this procedure, we restore a proper atom-to-atom mapping between two structures. This circumvents the factorial growth of permutation sampling in root-MSD analysis by globally optimizing a nonlinear function to find the best overlay of the structures. Then, we use a physics-driven approach to derive a dimensionless criterion for comparing two structures. This criterion uses the idea of quantum fluctuations in atomic positions and requires computing the mass-weighted MSD as a measure of proximity between structures. We also provide an implementation of our approach in a Python software and numerical examples of its performance.
items.authors: Denis S. Tikhonov, Daniil Kiryak, Darya O. Klimchuk, Anastasiia Gorbunova, Natalia Papina, Sergey N. Roslyakov

items.title: Strategy for the activation of porous molecular crystals using organic vapors
items.abstract: Porous molecular crystals (PMCs), i.e., crystalline solids with permanent, virtual, or flexible porosity, are usually synthesized by crystallization from solution, with the solvated molecules included in the pores as guests. To use such crystals as porous materials, the guest molecules must be removed. Typically, thermal treatment is used to promote their desorption, but this method often leads to the loss of crystallinity and catastrophic collapse of the porous structures due to the weakness of the intermolecular interactions. Therefore, methods for guest desorption under mild conditions are in high demand. The present study reports exposure to organic vapors as an unprecedented strategy for this purpose.
