Specifically, we demonstrate that exposure to vapors of dimethyl sulfoxide, n-butanol, or tert-butanol at room temperature can induce the removal of ethanol molecules encapsulated in crystalline phenylbis(benzothiazol-2-yl)methanol while maintaining its single-crystallinity. Furthermore, this method was found to be applicable for guest desorption from a hydrogen-bonded organic framework based on phenylbis(benzimidazol-2-yl)methanol.
items.authors: Tatsunari Murakami, Kanato Ohgaki, Masaaki Okazaki, Shun Ohta

items.title: Free induction decay-detected high-field electron spin resonance for accurate monitoring highly polarized spin dynamics
items.abstract: Understanding the dynamics of highly polarized spins using electron spin resonance (ESR) is increasingly relevant to dynamic nuclear polarization (DNP), polarized targets, and spin-based quantum technologies.In this regime, however, conventional echo-detected ESR is no longer a linear reporter of spin polarization, because the electron spin coherence time T2 itself depends on polarization through suppression of electronelectron flip-flops.Here, we present a dual ESR/nuclear magnetic resonance instrument operating at 7 T and temperatures down to ~1.3 K, where the sample is immersed in a liquid helium bath and the electron spin polarization reaches ~99.8%.The system combines a resonator-free quasi-optical 190-196 GHz spectrometer with a low-heat-load smooth-wall waveguide, and a compact dual NMR coil/ESR waveguide.Resonator-free operation eliminates ring-down and enables free induction decay (FID) detection.Using 40 mM TEMPOL in DNP juice as a model system, we show that frequency-swept ESR spectra from echo and FID detection agree, whereas saturation-recovery measurements of the longitudinal relaxation time T1S diverge strongly.This discrepancy between the two approaches arises due to the nonlinearity of echo-detection at high polarization, which we show to be difficult to correct without the introduction of severe bias.FID detection is thus a more robust and quantitative probe of electron spin dynamics at near-unity polarization.This work paves the way towards the accurate characterization of the dynamics within networks of coupled, highly polarized electron spins relevant to DNP at 1 K and the monitoring of short-lived photo-excited spin systems.
items.authors: Quentin Stern, Hoang M. Le, Martyna Judd, Joshua S. Straub, Songi Han

items.title: A study of the valence shell photoionization dynamics following core level resonant excitation in imidazole
items.abstract: The photoionization and subsequent Auger decay dynamics of core-excited states in imidazole have been investigated at the carbon and nitrogen K-edges using linearly polarized synchrotron radiation. Ion yield measurements in the pre-edge regions were used to locate core-level transitions into either unoccupied valence or Rydberg states, and assignments were made through comparison with simulated spectra obtained using the RASPT2 method. Valence shell photoelectron spectra were recorded at photon energies coinciding with these core-level transitions, using two polarization orientations to allow the photoelectron angular distributions to be determined. The interpretation of these resonantly excited photoelectron spectra was guided by RASPT2 simulations that helped distinguish between participator and spectator contributions. Autoionization strongly affects the photoelectron intensity and angular distributions of the outer valence 1h states. Spectator contributions become evident at binding energies above 15 eV, and some of the intense 2h-1p states are well-described by the calculations, allowing assignments to be proposed. The non-resonantly excited C(KVV) and N(KVV) Auger spectra have been measured and some of the features at high kinetic energies have been assigned.
items.authors: D. M. P. Holland, H. G. McGhee, A. R. Milosavljević, J. D. Bozek, E. Muchová, R. A. Ingle

items.title: UpKast: Method, Model, and Database for Large-Scale Cross-Solvent Determination of pKa Values
items.abstract: The acid dissociation constant, commonly written as p K a , plays a key role in chemistry. However, most p K a measurements have been conducted in only a handful of solvents, resulting in data scarcity for many relevant solvent systems. Herein, we introduce the UpKast-DB, which comprises of p K a estimates for around 3,000 acids and bases in 29 solvents. We constructed UpKast-DB using a quantum-chemical method that integrates solvation free energy calculations with experimental data. Furthermore, we trained a surrogate machine learning model UpKast-ML on the computed values, allowing for rapid and accurate prediction of p K a values beyond the acids and bases presented in UpKast-DB. The quantum-chemical and machine learning methods result in RMSEs of approximately 1 p K a unit relative to experimental values, slightly higher than the typical aleatoric uncertainty of underlying experimental data, but more accurate than many existing experimental measurements (which can have uncertainties up to, and sometimes beyond, 3 p K a units). The data and modeling approaches provide a means of productively augmenting existing p K a data sources, and represent a significant step toward general determination of p K a in any solvent. The dataset and models can be found on Zenodo: doi:10.5281/zenodo.23239570
items.authors: Jonathan Wenyuan Zheng, William H. Green
items.title_zh: UpKast：大规模跨溶剂pKa值测定的方法、模型与数据库
items.summary_zh: 酸解离常数（pKa）在化学中具有重要作用。然而，大多数pKa测量仅在少数溶剂中进行，导致许多相关溶剂体系的数据稀缺。本文介绍了UpKast-DB，包含约3000种酸和碱在29种溶剂中的pKa估计值。我们采用量子化学方法构建UpKast-DB，该方法将溶剂化自由能计算与实验数据相结合。此外，我们在计算值上训练了替代机器学习模型UpKast-ML，能够快速准确地预测超出UpKast-DB中酸碱的pKa值。量子化学和机器学习方法的均方根误差（RMSE）约为1个pKa单位，略高于实验数据的典型随机不确定性，但比许多现有实验测量更为准确。该数据和建模方法为有效补充现有pKa数据源提供了手段，并朝着在任意溶剂中普遍确定pKa迈出了重要一步。数据集和模型可在Zenodo上找到：doi:10.5281/zenodo.23239570

items.title: Molecular Symmetry Decomposition by Graph Automorphism: Fast, Symmetry-Aware RMSD, Structure Alignment, and Canonical Atom Ranks
items.abstract: The root-mean-square deviation (RMSD) is among the most widely used metrics in computational chemistry. However, computing a chemically meaningful RMSD requires solving a combinatorial “atom mapping” problem: finding the RMSD-minimizing and chemically acceptable correspondence between atoms in two structures. Existing methods force a trade-off. Graph-isomorphism enumeration is exact but can be computationally prohibitive. The faster (cubic scaling with molecular size) Hungarian assignment algorithm disregards the bonding topology and can return chemically invalid mappings and spuriously low RMSD values. We eliminate this trade-off by recasting the assignment problem in the language of graph automorphism, where the bond-preserving permutations form a group whose internal structure (orbits, stabilizers, and product decompositions) mirrors molecular topology. This yields a complete classification of molecular graph symmetry into coupled core and independent peripheral symmetry (falling into exactly two graph-theoretic classes), reducing the search from a product of local symmetries to a sum. The resulting algorithm, snapRMSD, produces assignments that are bond-preserving by construction and recovers the global RMSD minimum under mild conditions satisfied by most molecular structures. We demonstrate that snapRMSD is significantly faster than existing methods, often by orders of magnitude. As a byproduct, the same machinery yields exact canonical atom ranks, a rigorous alternative to the refinement heuristics used since the 1960s.
items.authors: Colton B. Hicks, Todd J. Martinez
items.title_zh: 基于图自同构的分子对称性分解与快速RMSD计算
items.summary_zh: 根均方差（RMSD）是计算化学中最常用的度量之一，但计算具有化学意义的RMSD需要解决组合“原子映射”问题，即在两个结构中找到最小化RMSD且化学上可接受的原子对应关系。现有方法存在权衡：图同构枚举方法精确但计算成本高，而匈牙利算法速度较快（与分子大小呈立方关系），但忽略了键合拓扑，可能返回化学无效的映射和虚假的低RMSD值。我们通过将分配问题重新表述为图自同构的语言，消除了这一权衡，形成了一个保留键的排列群，其内部结构反映了分子拓扑。最终算法snapRMSD在大多数分子结构下能在温和条件下恢复全局RMSD最小值，且显著快于现有方法。

items.title: Reductive insertion of a trivalent metal leading to the isolation of Prussian blue-type EuIIIFe3[Fe(CN)6]3
items.abstract: Reductive insertion reactions selectively modify three-dimensionally bonded solid-state structures through the addition of an elemental metal by electronation of the host structure and insertion of the metal cation into the host cavities for charge balance. However, with rare exceptions, this class of reactions has been largely restricted to insertions of monovalent metals. The reductive insertion of divalent and trivalent metal ions is intrinsically limited by their very slow diffusion through a host lattice at low temperatures and instability of a host lattice in the presence of these metals at high temperatures. These limitations originate from strong coordination of multivalent guest species to anions within the host lattice. By using coordinatively saturated anions such as cyanide in Prussian blue analogues, only relatively weak coordination modes to guest cations are available within the host structures, suggesting these host structures may participate in multivalent metalations. Herein, we report reductive insertion of europium into Berlin green Fe[Fe(CN) 6 ] under relatively mild conditions by reaction with EuI 2 at 150 °C in N-methyl-2-pyrolidone. The formation of the half-ferrous product, Eu III Fe 3 [Fe(CN) 6 ] 3 , is an exceptionally rare reductive insertion of a trivalent metal, and the first example of a phase pure Prussian blue (A n+ 1/n Fe[Fe(CN) 6 ]; A = metal cation) isolated with either a lanthanide or multivalent A-site metal. The resulting compound exhibits a distribution of iron oxidation and spin states not observed in previously reported Prussian blue phases of the form M I Fe[Fe(CN) 6 ]. The valence of Eu 3+ was confirmed by a combination of X-ray absorption, 57 Fe Mössbauer, and magnetic susceptibility measurements, which informed a possible reaction mechanism invoking redox exchange between the ferrous host, Eu 3+ guest ions, and excess Eu 2+ in solution.
items.authors: Shain S. Mollick, Sayantani Sur, Jacob W. Fritsky, Nilarun Koley, Ryan S. Storteboom, Jason F. Khoury

items.title: Classical Nucleation Induced Intrafibrillar Mineralization of Collagen
items.abstract: Collagen mineralization is fundamental to bone formation, and this process is widely believed to proceed via an amorphous calcium phosphate (ACP)-mediated non-classical nucleation pathway. Here we investigated this paradigm using cryogenic electron tomography. The results reveal that the intrafibrillar mineralization of collagen does not rely on the infiltration of ACP, but occurs through a classical heterogeneous nucleation mechanism, which can be accelerated both in vitro and in vivo by increasing the density of the collagen template. The finding not only updates our understanding of collagen mineralization mechanisms, but also provides critical insights for the design of bone regeneration materials.
items.authors: Shiwen Cui, Shasha Yao, Keyan Liu, Chengkun Xing, Mingxing Liu, Haiqin Du

items.title: COSMO-RS-Based Theoretical Investigation of Equilibria in Protic Ionic Liquids
items.abstract: Ionic liquids have become an increasingly important field of research. A subgroup, protic ionic liquids, have been shown to be excellent solvents even for poorly soluble materials such as cellulose or polyamides. Still, the composition of such liquids, e.g., their ionicity and the nature of formed aggregates, is mostly unknown and experimental attempts to shed light on this have been mostly unsuccessful. Herein, we report the development of the Python-based COSMOPIL program (COnductor-like Screening MOdel for Protic Ionic Liquids) to analyze the composition of protic ionic liquids via theoretical methods based on density functional theory (DFT) and the COSMO-RS (COnductor-like Screening MOdel for Real Solvents) implicit solvation model. The inputs of experimental data such as dielectric constants is not necessary. The COSMO-PIL program demonstrates the influence of acid/base ratios and residual water on the ionic liquid composition and allows the understanding of the reported poor ionicity of those liquids. Most notably, we explain this “ionicity gap” in protic ionic liquids, as even superbases fail to achieve full acid deprotonation, with a polarity mismatch between anion and cation, requiring residual acid as mediator.
items.authors: Kevin Breitwieser, Ilkka Kilpeläinen, Vladimir Aseyev

items.title: Late-Stage Ligand Prioritization by Combining Rapid-Dissociation Filtering with MM/GBSA
items.abstract: Accurate and efficient prediction of binding free energies remains a central challenge in computational chemistry, largely due to the complexity of solvent effects and the trade-off between accuracy and computational cost. Explicit solvent molecular dynamics (MD) simulations provide detailed thermodynamic and kinetic insight, now routinely reaching microsecond timescales, while end-point methods such as MM/GBSA offer high efficiency but are sensitive to model parameters. In particular, the accuracy of MM/GBSA strongly depends on the atomic radii used to define the dielectric boundary within the implicit solvent framework. Here, we introduce an explicit–implicit hybrid workflow for late-stage ligand prioritization that integrates the strengths of both approaches. In this framework, microsecond-scale explicit solvent MD simulations act as a rapid-dissociation filter, flagging weak or unstable binders through spontaneous dissociation within the simulation window. MM/GBSA is then used to rank the remaining candidates. To improve the accuracy of the implicit solvent stage, we employ optimized atomic radii sets (OPTBIND), specifically designed for binding free-energy calculations. On the protein–ligand complexes of Curated32-4 set , a new curated benchmark of 32 complexes including 4 congeneric series, the entropy-free MM/GBSA stage with OPT- BIND 6D achieved Pearson r = 0.82 and Spearman ρ = 0.84, with 100% recovery of the experimental rank ordering across all four congeneric series, while a single-replica consistency test of the rapid-dissociation filter yielded an AUC of 0.88 and retained all 15 sub-micromolar binders. Finally, as a real-world drug design application, we apply the workflow to halogen substitutions in SARS-CoV-2 main protease inhibitors, demonstrating its ability to identify favorable chemical modifications. Notably, the approach prospectively identifies F→Cl and F→I as affinity-enhancing substitutions; the predicted enhancement for the chlorine analog is subsequently confirmed experimentally, while the iodine analog remains a testable prediction, highlighting its predictive power in guiding chemical optimization. Together, these results establish a practical framework for detailed studies of receptor–ligand binding and for late-stage ligand prioritization in drug discovery.
items.authors: Fatemeh Ghafouri-Plate, Timothy W. Johann, Luke H. Elder, Alexey V. Onufriev
items.title_zh: 结合快速解离过滤与MM/GBSA的后期配体优先排序
items.summary_zh: 准确高效地预测结合自由能是计算化学中的一个核心挑战，主要由于溶剂效应的复杂性及准确性与计算成本之间的权衡。显式溶剂分子动力学（MD）模拟提供了详细的热力学和动力学见解，现已常规达到微秒时间尺度，而MM/GBSA等终点方法则高效但对模型参数敏感。特别是，MM/GBSA的准确性强烈依赖于用于定义隐式溶剂框架中介电边界的原子半径。本文提出了一种显式-隐式混合工作流程，用于后期配体优先排序，结合了两种方法的优势。在该框架中，微秒尺度的显式溶剂MD模拟作为快速解离过滤器，通过自发解离标记弱或不稳定的结合体。随后使用MM/GBSA对剩余候选者进行排名。为了提高隐式溶剂阶段的准确性，我们采用了专为结合自由能计算设计的优化原子半径集（OPTBIND）。在Curated32-4集的蛋白质-配体复合物上，使用OPT-BIND 6D的无熵MM/GBSA阶段达到了Pearson r = 0.82。

items.title: ARGUS: A Four-Signal Joint Model for H5N1 Neuraminidase Inhibitor Resistance Prediction
items.abstract: Oseltamivir and zanamivir are the primary antivirals against H5N1 influenza, yet resistance profiles at the structural level remain incompletely characterized. Phenotypic screening requires one to two weeks in biosafety level 3 containment; during an active spillover event, this timescale is incompatible with clinical decisions. We present ARGUS (Affinity-and Representation-Guided Unified Scoring), a learned joint model combining four independent structural signals into a unified resistance risk framework: molecular docking affinity, protein language model evolutionary likelihood, perturbation response scanning, and all-atom pocket volume analysis. This work comprises two major components: (1) a comprehensive dual-drug saturation mutagenesis of the H5N1 neuraminidase binding pocket (1,102 mutations, 551 per drug) revealing a striking 166:1 asymmetry between oseltamivir-specific and zanamivir-specific resistance mutations, reflecting zanamivir’s substrate-mimicking pharmacophore; and (2) a novel four-signal learned joint model validated against 37 published fold-resistance measurements spanning H5N1, H1N1pdm09, H3N2, and H7N9 backgrounds (oseltamivir fold-resistance was the fitting target). The four-signal model achieves leave-one-out Spearman ρ = 0.628 (p = 0.000032), with a 95% bootstrap interval of [0.428, 0.845] for the in-sample correlation and a permutation p 0.001. The earlier two-signal linear blend reached ρ = 0.659 (p = 0.0142) on only n=8 mutations, so the two figures are not directly comparable. The learned weights make docking the dominant signal (96.3% of the total weight) with ESM-2 LLR at 3.7%, which fits the view that protein language models alone conflate evolutionary constraint with drug-resistance specificity. Applied to the 2024 US H5N1 B3.13 outbreak, all 21 outbreak mutations are pocket-distal for both drugs, predicting maintained efficacy of both antivirals. ARGUS provides immediate structural assessment of any novel neuraminidase mutation without experimental work, and the full saturation landscape and trained models are released as a public resource on Zenodo.
items.authors: Muhammadjon Tursunbadalov, Mustafojon Tursunbadalov

items.title: Confinement-Controlled Cluster Percolation Shifts the Widom Crossover in Supercritical Methane
items.abstract: Supercritical fluids undergo significant structural and dynamic changes near the Widom line, which separates gas-like and liquid-like regimes. These phenomena are well understood for bulk fluids, but their evolution under nanoscale confinement remains poorly understood. Using a Grand Canonical Monte Carlo and Molecular Dynamics simulation framework, we show that confinement of supercritical CH4 in clay slit nanopores shifts the Widom crossover to lower pressures, with the shift increasing as pore size decreases. Energy-based cluster analysis reveals that this shift is associated with the emergence of system-spanning molecular clusters. Confinement promotes the percolation of these clusters at lower pressures, extending liquid-like behaviour into regimes that are gas-like under bulk conditions. The crossover is also reflected in transport properties as an inflection in both the effective mean distance between free molecules and clusters and the molecular diffusion coefficient. These results establish a direct link between confinement-controlled cluster percolation and the Widom crossover.
items.authors: Adel Najafimarghmaleki, Paola Carbone

items.title: Harnessing remote weak interactions for fine-tuning the catalytic activity of rotaxane-superbases
items.abstract: Mechanically interlocked molecules offer a distinct strategy for controlling molecular function by translating subtle differences in noncovalent interactions into changes in molecular conformation and reactivity. Here, we show that remote weak interactions can be harnessed to fine-tune the basicity and catalytic activity of mechanically interlocked secondary amines. To this end, we synthesized two bistable rotaxanes, featuring a primary ammonium/amine binding site and either a triazole or a methyltriazolium unit as the secondary binding site. In the base-catalysed Michael addition of malononitrile to beta-nitrostyrene, both deprotonated amine-rotaxanes exhibit substantially higher catalytic activity than both the corresponding non-interlocked thread and the benchmark organobase proton sponge, demonstrating that the mechanical bond can enhance the reactivity of the embedded amine. Importantly, the triazole based-rotaxane shows a twofold higher catalytic activity than that of the triazolium-rotaxane, although the secondary amine as the catalytically active unit is structurally unchanged. Thus, the increased reactivity is caused by the difference in weak noncovalent interactions at the secondary binding site: Weaker binding to the triazole translates into higher basicity of the secondary amine, which in turn increases the catalytic activity of the rotaxane. Collectively, these results demonstrate that weak, remote interactions transmitted through a mechanical bond can modulate the proton-accepting ability and catalytic performance of an interlocked amine, establishing remote co-conformational control of basicity as a design principle for fine-tuning the reactivity of rotaxane superbases.
items.authors: Sohom Kundu, Shubhadip Mallick, Shounak Hinge, Jan Riebe, Jochen Niemeyer

items.title: Automated Extraction and FAIRification of Chemical Structures from Scientific Publications
items.abstract: Chemical structures are published predominantly as images, which makes them inaccessible for database indexing, structure-based search and computational reuse. While Optical Chemical Structure Recognition and PDF-extraction tools attempt post-publication recovery, they cannot restore the information lost during image rendering. To address this, we present BChemXtract, an open-source Java library that extracts chemical structures directly from the CDX and CDXML files that authors already submit with their manuscripts. BChemXtract parses the CDX object hierarchy to isolate chemical fragments from graphical annotations and expands abbreviations using a community-curated lookup table. The structures are then converted via the Chemistry Development Kit into standard machine-readable formats. BChemXtract is integrated into the production workflow of the Beilstein Journals, where extracted structures are manually validated before being embedded in article metadata as Schema.org JSON-LD, deposited in PubChem and offered for download. Applied to the 2993 ChemDraw figures and schemes of volume 20 of the Beilstein Journal of Organic Chemistry, it yielded 23,320 structures with InChIs in under two minutes. On a 225-file benchmark corpus, it generated valid InChIs for 98.2% of extracted unique substances, compared with 14.2% for Open Babel, at comparable per-file speed. BChemXtract makes published chemistry FAIR at the point of publication without altering author workflows. It is available under the MIT license together with a web application and the benchmark corpus.
items.authors: Felix Bänsch, Kohulan Rajan, Markus Nietfeld
items.title_zh: 自动提取科学出版物中的化学结构并实现FAIR化
items.summary_zh: 化学结构主要以图像形式发布，导致其无法被数据库索引、结构搜索和计算重用。为了解决这一问题，我们提出了BChemXtract，这是一个开源Java库，能够直接从作者提交的CDX和CDXML文件中提取化学结构。BChemXtract解析CDX对象层次结构，以从图形注释中分离化学片段，并使用社区维护的查找表扩展缩写。提取的结构通过化学开发工具包转换为标准的机器可读格式。BChemXtract已集成到Beilstein期刊的生产工作流程中，提取的结构在嵌入文章元数据之前经过人工验证，并以Schema.org JSON-LD格式存储在PubChem中供下载。在Beilstein有机化学期刊第20卷的2993个ChemDraw图形中，BChemXtract在不到两分钟内生成了23320个具有InChI的结构。在225个文件的基准语料库中，提取的独特物质中有98.2%生成了有效的InChI，而Open Babel仅为14.2%。

items.title: Utilization of heuristic approaches and molecular modelling to visualise chemical reactivity in small student groups
items.abstract: According to current psychometric analyses, a vast majority of novices in universities mostly utilize algorithmic mental processes to solve given tasks and tests. Although algorithmic thinking is an essential part of brain functions, experts on didactics call for methods which also develop conceptual thinking in beginners. In this sense, heuristic molecular modelling plays an important role in chemistry education since it inherently employs several conceptual thinking principles. Herein, we present eight different molecular modelling tasks of Diels-Alder reactions to develop understanding of the concept of chemical reactivity in undergraduate students of chemistry. The aim of this study is to provide teachers of chemistry with an example lesson utilizing heuristic education techniques and molecular modelling. The present study was evaluated in a university course on advanced organic chemistry for students in the third year of a chemistry master program. Interviews with the involved students and analyses of the applied pre/post didactical tests show that the proposed lesson has a positive impact on the understanding of basic chemical concepts related with chemical reactivity and Diels-Alder reaction.
items.authors: Rafael Dolezal, Natálie Karásková, Nadezhda V. Maltsevskaya, Karel Kolář
items.title_zh: 启发式方法与分子建模在化学反应性教学中的应用
items.summary_zh: 本研究针对大学化学专业的本科生，探讨了启发式分子建模在化学反应性理解中的作用。研究对象为第三年化学硕士课程的学生，采用了八个不同的Diels-Alder反应分子建模任务，以促进学生对化学反应性概念的理解。通过对参与学生的访谈和前后教学测试的分析，结果显示，所提出的课程对学生理解与化学反应性及Diels-Alder反应相关的基本化学概念产生了积极影响。本研究为化学教师提供了一个利用启发式教育技术和分子建模的示例课程。

items.title: CP-GFM-SGX: Topology-Aware Cyclic Peptide Generation and Design with Receptor-Conditioned Structural Evaluation and Experimental KRAS Affinity Optimization
items.abstract: Cyclic-peptide discovery requires molecular topology, atomic structure, receptor-associated evidence and computational decisions to remain consistent across a multistage workflow. We present CP-GFM-SGX, an all-atom generative AI model for cyclic-peptide design that integrates a topology-aware generative core with a Unified Evidence State Machine (UESM) to track candidate identity, chemical validity, provenance, typed failures and bounded computation. We evaluated three distinct aspects of the system. In Track A, a frozen five-complex known-ligand benchmark with 100 scheduled poses per complex, the native-free FULL route selected a ligand-backbone pose with root-mean-square deviation (RMSD) below 2 Å in four of five systems; retrospective best-of-100 evaluation found a sub-2-Å pose in all five (median selected RMSD, 1.72 Å). In Track B, matched true-pocket versus shuffled-pocket comparisons favored the specified pocket in all seven main targets (median of target medians, +172.6 Rosetta energy units; weakest margin, +3.9 for MCL-1–9CDT). An exploratory post-protocol assessor admitted 42/42, 42/42 and 40/42 selected top-K slots in the full, condition-masked and post hoc head-to-tail arms, respectively. In Track C, FULL UESM produced the specified protective outcomes for six deterministic synthetic fault fixtures and one additional missing-evidence case; targeted ablations isolated the roles of provenance and failure propagation. In a separate KRAS G12D–GDP experimental-feedback series, synthesis and SPR/BLI testing of cyclic-peptide analogues guided position-2 basic-side-chain selection and dual-basic-group placement, advancing the reported SPR affinity from approximately 60 µM for CRO-748 to approximately 6 µM for 748-R1 and approximately 1 µM for 748-RK. Comparisons using the 31-dimension Structured Capability and Evidence Grid (SCEG-31D) demonstrate that CP-GFM-SGX exhibits certain superiority over other design platforms in multiple aspects. Together, we evaluate a topology-aware generative artificial intelligence workflow for receptor-focused cyclic-peptide design and show, in a KRAS feedback series, how binding measurements guide iterative chemical optimization.
items.authors: Zhiyuan Hu, Russell Dillworth
items.title_zh: CP-GFM-SGX：基于拓扑的环肽生成与设计
items.summary_zh: 环肽发现需要在多阶段工作流程中保持分子拓扑、原子结构、受体相关证据和计算决策的一致性。我们提出了CP-GFM-SGX，这是一种全原子生成AI模型，集成了拓扑感知生成核心和统一证据状态机（UESM），用于跟踪候选分子的身份、化学有效性、来源、类型失败和计算限制。我们评估了系统的三个不同方面。在Track A中，针对五个已知配体的基准测试，FULL路线在五个系统中有四个选择了根均方差（RMSD）低于2 Å的配体骨架姿态；最佳回顾评估在所有五个系统中发现了一个低于2 Å的姿态（中位数选择RMSD为1.72 Å）。在Track B中，真实口袋与随机口袋的比较在七个主要目标中均偏向指定口袋（目标中位数的中位数为+172.6 Rosetta能量单位；最弱边际为MCL-1–9CDT的+3.9）。在Track C中，FULL UESM为六个确定性合成故障固定装置和一个缺失证据案例产生了指定的保护结果。

items.title: Prediction of MOF Adsorption Isotherms and High-Throughput Screening Using a Physics-Informed Membranes Graph Neural Network
items.abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are prime CO 2 -capture candidates, but grand canonical Monte Carlo (GCMC) screening is costly when full isotherms, not single uptakes, are required; machine learning surrogates rarely resolve the continuous pressure response. We report a physics-informed pressure-aware multi-task graph neural network (PI-MGNN) to predict CO 2 uptake at arbitrary pressure and reconstruct isotherms from structure. From ~130,000 candidates, PCA and K-means select 5,023 representative MOFs, each simulated by GCMC at five pressures spanning 0.1-5.0 MPa, enforcing a continuous pressure response. Crystal graphs are processed by decoupled geometric and electrostatic graph-attention branches with auxiliary supervision, while a Gaussian-expanded pressure query is fused by cross-attention. PI-MGNN attains R 2 = 0.977 and MAE = 0.291 mol kg -1 ; isotherm MAEs are 0.428/0.312/0.330 mol kg -1 for high/medium/low-uptake MOFs, and cross-attention improves accuracy by 6.3%. Attention weights recover the pressure-resolved physics, enabling accurate and interpretable high-throughput screening.
items.authors: Li Linfeng, Xingshuo Fan, Ning Zhang

items.title: Lipid Matrix-Dependent Effects of Ceramide Enrichment on Cholesterol-Containing PSM and DLPC Membranes
items.abstract: Ceramide is a bioactive sphingolipid that can reorganize cholesterol-containing membranes, but how membrane properties change with increasing ceramide content in different lipid matrices remains unclear. Using Martini 3 coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations, we examine cholesterol-containing PSM and DLPC membranes across a controlled palmitoyl ceramide (PCER) composition series at a single liquid-phase temperature. Increasing PCER fraction generally decreases area per lipid and increases lipid ordering, consistent with membrane condensation. However, the responses differ between matrices. In PSM/CHOL, PCER is accommodated within an already ordered environment, producing only modest membrane stiffening. In DLPC/CHOL, PCER leads to greater changes in local packing heterogeneity and lateral organization, accompanied by a nonmonotonic mechanical response. PCER enrichment also changes the positional and orientational distributions of cholesterol in a matrix-dependent manner. These results show that ceramide-induced condensation does not necessarily produce monotonic membrane stiffening and highlight the importance of the host lipid matrix in determining membrane structure and mechanics.
items.authors: Eun Sub Song, Taejin Kwon

items.title: A hydrochromic porous aromatic framework for self-reporting, high-capacity atmospheric water harvesting
items.abstract: Atmospheric water harvesting materials are typically optimised for sorption performance alone, despite the practical importance of monitoring sorbent loading. Here, we report a hydrochromic porous aromatic framework that integrates water capture and self-reporting within a single adaptive material. Sulfonation of PAF-1 affords the hydrophilic framework PAF-1-S that adsorbs 0.18 g·g-1 of water at only 10% RH and reaches 1.87 g·g-1 at 90% RH, combining exceptional low-humidity capture with the highest total capacity among the porous sorbents surveyed here. Water adsorption simultaneously induces a reversible, graded colour change, enabling direct visualisation of sorbent loading without external sensing hardware. Spectroscopic analysis indicates that this response arises from hydration-driven acid–base equilibria within the modified framework. Combined with rapid sorption kinetics, low-temperature regeneration and robust cycling stability, these findings establish responsive porous adsorbents as a strategy for intelligent sorption materials.
items.authors: Paul Schweng, Christoph Bendl, Kai C. Hultzsch, Robert T. Woodward

items.title: Solid-phase synthesis and structure-degradation relationships of VHL-recruiting PROTACs for preferential histone deacetylase 6 degradation
items.abstract: This work reports on a series of von Hippel-Lindau (VHL)-recruiting histone deacetylase 6 (HDAC6) PROTACs based on a vorinostat-inspired HDAC inhibitor. Systematic variations of the VHL ligand, the exit vector, and the linker architecture revealed that longer, semi-rigid linkers promoted efficient HDAC6 degradation. Compounds 12-15 emerged as potent HDAC6 degraders, with 15 exhibiting a half-maximal degradation value of 26 nM with 12 showing particularly rapid degradation kinetics. The lead compounds induced pronounced and preferential HDAC6 degradation in MM.1S and FLT3-ITD-positive MV4-11 cells. Notably, 13-15 displayed submicromolar antiproliferative activity in MV4-11 cells and significantly induced apoptosis. Compound 13 was markedly more active than its non-degrading control nc-13, despite nearly identical HDAC1 and HDAC6 inhibitory activities, which underscores the important contribution of targeted HDAC degradation to the antiproliferative activity. Overall, this study supports VHL-mediated targeted degradation as a promising strategy to translate HDAC6 targeting into pronounced antileukemic activity.
items.authors: Martina Miranda, Maria Hanl, Nisha Setia, Sophie Spülbeck, Katrin Nekipelov, Helena Skalski
items.title_zh: 基于VHL招募的PROTACs优选降解组蛋白去乙酰化酶6的固相合成与结构-降解关系
items.summary_zh: 本研究报道了一系列基于Vorinostat启发的组蛋白去乙酰化酶6（HDAC6）PROTACs，这些PROTACs招募von Hippel-Lindau（VHL）。通过系统性改变VHL配体、出口向量和连接子结构，发现较长的半刚性连接子促进了HDAC6的有效降解。化合物12-15表现出强效的HDAC6降解能力，其中15的半最大降解值为26 nM，12则显示出特别快速的降解动力学。领先化合物在MM.1S和FLT3-ITD阳性MV4-11细胞中诱导了显著且优先的HDAC6降解。值得注意的是，13-15在MV4-11细胞中显示出亚微摩尔的抗增殖活性，并显著诱导凋亡。尽管nc-13与13在HDAC1和HDAC6抑制活性上几乎相同，化合物13的活性明显更强，强调了靶向HDAC降解对抗增殖活性的关键贡献。总体而言，本研究支持VHL介导的靶向降解作为将HDAC6靶向转化为显著抗白血病活性的有前景策略。

items.title: Descriptor-Based Regression Analysis Enables the Discovery of Highly Selective Ligands for Palladium-Catalyzed Siloxycyclopropanation
items.abstract: A palladium-catalyzed siloxycyclopropanation of alkenes using acylsilanes as carbene precursors provides a distinctive catalytic approach to structurally diverse cyclopropanes through a siloxycarbene–palladium intermediate. Although the reaction scope and major mechanistic features have been established, the origin of its ligand-dependent diastereoselectivity has remained unclear, limiting the rational development of more selective catalysts. Here, we combine density functional theory (DFT) calculations, molecular parameterization, and statistical modeling to elucidate the steric and electronic factors governing the stereochemical outcome. DFT calculations of a series of NHC ligands and their corresponding siloxycarbene–palladium complexes provided a diverse set of molecular descriptors, which were used to construct a multivariate linear regression (MLR) model against experimental activation energies. The refined model identified complementary descriptors reflecting ligand steric demand, directional steric effects, and metal–ligand electronic interactions as key factors associated with the observed selectivity. MLR-guided virtual screening of 21 NHC ligands identified L24 and L30 as promising candidates for enhanced syn- and anti-selectivity, respectively, and their predicted selectivities were experimentally validated. The newly identified ligands not only improved the selectivity in their respective directions but also enabled a pronounced switch between syn- and anti-selectivity relative to the previously optimized ligand. Furthermore, L24 and L30 exhibited 2 complementary stereocontrol across a range of acylsilanes and alkenes beyond the benchmark reaction. Mechanistic analysis of the corresponding transition states revealed the roles of anisotropic steric environments and ligand-specific electronic interactions in determining the distinct stereochemical preferences of L24 and L30. These findings provide a mechanistic basis for ligand-controlled stereoselectivity in siloxycarbene–palladium cyclopropanation and establish molecular-level ligand features as useful parameters for improving and redirecting stereochemical
items.authors: Vishal Kumar Rawat, Ryoichi Tabata, Tetsuya Inagaki, Yuki Akita, Reiko Hirosawa, Maria Fyta
items.title_zh: 基于描述符的回归分析发现高选择性钯催化硅氧环丙烷配体
items.summary_zh: 使用酰基硅烷作为卡宾前体的钯催化硅氧环丙烷反应为通过硅氧卡宾-钯中间体合成结构多样的环丙烷提供了一种独特的催化方法。尽管反应范围和主要机制特征已被确立，但其配体依赖的二面角选择性的来源仍不明确，限制了更具选择性催化剂的合理开发。本文结合密度泛函理论（DFT）计算、分子参数化和统计建模，阐明了影响立体化学结果的立体和电子因素。对一系列NHC配体及其相应的硅氧卡宾-钯复合物的DFT计算提供了多样的分子描述符，这些描述符用于构建与实验活化能相关的多元线性回归（MLR）模型。精炼的模型识别出反映配体立体需求、方向性立体效应和金属-配体电子相互作用的互补描述符，作为观察到的选择性关键因素。MLR指导的虚拟筛选确定了L24和L30作为分别增强顺式和反式选择性的有前景候选者，其预测的选择性得到了实验验证。新识别的配体不仅提高了选择性。

items.title: Complementary Roles of Iodide-Mediated Pathways and Anion Dynamics in Lithium-Ion Transport in Li3PS4-LiI Glasses
items.abstract: LiI addition enhances lithium-ion transport in sulfide glasses, yet the microscopic mechanisms linking halide incorporation to faster conduction remain unclear. Here, we investigate how LiI promotes Li+ migration in (100−x)Li3PS4–xLiI glasses by resolving changes in local structure, migration energetics, and anion dynamics. A machinelearning potential trained on newly generated ab initio molecular dynamics data and an existing sulfide-electrolyte dataset enables 10 ns simulations of approximately 5000atom glass models at 300 K over a LiI content range of 0–50 mol%. The potential is validated against density functional theory calculations, experimental densities, and X-ray total scattering profiles. Although the PS4 3–units remain intact and their time-averaged inter-unit correlations change little, Li+ diffusivity more than doubles across this composition range, accompanied by increased migration beyond local cage-like regions. To characterize the energetics of these pathways in a disordered environment, we introduce an analysis that combines Voronoi partitioning into P-and I–-centered domains with atomic potentialenergy fluctuations along Li+ trajectories. The resulting statistical local energy-barrier indicators allow comparisons between domain transitions without assigning absolute activation energies. This analysis reveals two complementary effects of LiI addition. Transitions involving I–-centered domains exhibit lower barrier indicators than direct transitions between P-centered domains, identifying favorable I–-mediated migration pathways. LiI addition also lowers the barrier indicators for direct P-to-P transitions, extending its influence beyond pathways that pass through I–-centered domains. Enhanced local translational and rotational dynamics of PS4 3–units accompany this broader reduction, suggesting that anion motion helps facilitate Li+ migration. These findings explain how LiI can enhance transport while largely preserving the average glass structure and highlight the combined roles of local migration pathways and anion dynamics in designing sulfide glass electrolytes.
items.authors: Minami Sakuma, Shoma Kawano, Kazuki Fukuda, Aoto Matsuo, Futoshi Utsuno, Koji Ohara

items.title: Emergence of Temporally Irreversible Hierarchical Solid Patterns through Information-Bearing Field Evolution and History-Dependent Growth Arrest
items.abstract: Patterns are widespread in natural and synthetic systems. Their formation is often interpreted through diffusion-driven instabilities or static geometric constructions. While successful in many contexts, these frameworks struggle to encode the spatiotemporal growth history of independently nucleated domains and their resulting collective behavior, including temporal asymmetry and hierarchical pattern formation with progressive solidification. This study shows that the TRACE (Temporal Recording through Arrested Coupled Evolution) mathematical model can generate intricate hierarchical patterns of solidifying and growing domains from simple, local growth rules through a phase information event-driven discretization operator within continuously evolving spatial information-bearing fields. The framework reveals how competition between growing domains can transform simple initial conditions into diverse final patterns, offering a new perspective on the emergence of spatial complexity from local growth processes, as observed experimentally in hierarchical pattern formation with solidification from fixed nuclei. This model suggests that complex patterns can emerge from the interaction of local, time-evolving growth, kinetic arrest rules with irreversible solidification embedded in front propagation. Numerical simulations reveal emergent patterns from the only TRACE equation, such as cell-like domains, stripes, banded structures, and hierarchical boundaries arising from variations in spatial confinement, nucleation timing, and domain density. The TRACE model also qualitatively reproduces the reported hierarchical macroscopic pattern formation observed in a chemical system. With these results, a phenomenon for growth-based natural patterns with solidification, and the featured characteristics of resultant patterns via growth and exclusion of each local cell are proposed.
items.authors: Junhyung Lee

items.title: Realising a Poschenrieder dual-sector electrostatic analyser for charge-detection mass spectrometry
items.abstract: Megadalton biomolecular assemblies, including viral vectors, synthetic nanoparticles and protein aggregates, are increasingly important chemical and therapeutic entities, yet their heterogeneity often exceeds the resolving power and space charge tolerance of conventional mass spectrometry. To overcome these limitations, here we report the first realisation of a Poschenrieder dual-sector electrostatic analyser as a charge-detection mass spectrometer. The instrument traps individual ions in a continuous closed trajectory between two spherical electrostatic sectors, enabling induced-current detection over extended transients without end-cap deceleration. Coupled to a high-mass ion-transfer interface, the analyser supports both ensemble m/z measurements and single-particle charge detection of large biomolecular ions. We validate the platform using protein standards and demonstrate megadalton mass analysis of adeno-associated virus capsids, distinguishing empty and genome-containing populations in agreement with orthogonal mass photometry and Orbitrap-based measurements. Although charge-detection noise remains the principal performance constraint in this first-generation prototype, the dual-sector architecture offers a simple, high-capacity route to charge-detection mass spectrometry with substantial scope for improved resolution through miniaturisation and reduced detector capacitance.
items.authors: Ellen N Liggett, Akhila Ajith, Alexey Barkhanskiy, Elvin Cabrera, Thomas Hoare, Kathleen Cain

items.title: Coacervate-engineered keratin bioelastomers with tunable mechanics
items.abstract: Nature employs bottom-up strategies to create elastic materials from protein assemblies, yet transforming structural proteins from abundant agricultural byproducts into customizable bioelastomers remains challenging. Here, we develop a strategy to fabricate bioelastomers with tunable mechanics by co-assembling keratins from wool and feathers through acid-induced coacervation. Time-pH superposition rheology reveals that wool and feather protein coacervates share similar viscoelastic signatures regulated by pH, with relaxation timescales spanning several orders of magnitude. By adjusting the wool-to-feather ratio, the mechanical properties of the resulting materials can be tuned from soft compliance to high stiffness. Strain-resolved Raman spectroscopy and steered molecular dynamics simulations reveal that extensibility and shape recovery originate from reversible microstructural transitions, in which coiled α-helices unfold and reorganize into metastable β-sheet structures under strain. Finally, we demonstrate the compatibility of these coacervate precursors with top-down manufacturing techniques, including wet spinning, blade coating, and extrusion-based 3D printing, enabling the fabrication of moisture-responsive biomaterials with in vitro biocompatibility. This work establishes a scalable platform for upcycling agricultural protein residues into functional bioelastomers for soft devices and biomedical applications.
items.authors: Junxian Zhang, Feipeng Chen, Zhili Wan, Joshua A. Dijksman, Jasper van der Gucht, Chunbao Li

items.title: Conformational Heterogeneity and Local Electronic Structure in Wild-Type and Arctic Amyloid-Β42
items.abstract: Amyloid-𝛽 42 is a heterogeneous system, widely known as an intrinsically disordered protein, or IDP, sampling a variety of conformations. However, how ensemble redistribution affects the underlying local electronic structure remains less well understood. In this study, classical molecular dynamics simulations are combined with population-aware density functional theory and reduced active-space calculations to compare the LVFFA fragment of the wild-type and Arctic (E22G) variants. Common-space principal component analysis, clustering, and Ramachandran plot analysis depicted distinct trajectory distributions and greater conformational heterogeneity for the E22G trajectory. Population-ranked conformations representing 60.58% of WT and 54.98% of Arctic populations yielded conditional population-weighted B3LYP/def2-SVP HOMO-LUMO separations of 5.81 and 5.95 eV, respectively. The 0.14 eV Arctic–WT shift remained positive across moving-block bootstrap analyses. Fragment expansion altered frontier-orbital ordering, although the spatial character of LVFFA-associated states was preserved. CASCI tested active-space sensitivity, and matched UCCSD-VQE calculations reproduced CAS(4,4) CASCI reference energies for the reduced Hamiltonians. Together, these results demonstrate the importance of population-aware conformational sampling and model-definition sensitivity when relating heterogeneous biomolecular ensembles to quantum-chemical properties.
items.authors: kushal patil
items.title_zh: 野生型与北极型淀粉样β42的构象异质性与局部电子结构
items.summary_zh: 淀粉样β42是一种异质系统，广泛被认为是内源性无序蛋白（IDP），其采样多种构象。本研究结合经典分子动力学模拟、基于群体的密度泛函理论和简化活性空间计算，比较了野生型和北极型（E22G）变体的LVFFA片段。主成分分析、聚类和Ramachandran图分析显示E22G轨迹具有明显不同的轨迹分布和更大的构象异质性。代表60.58%野生型和54.98%北极型群体的构象，条件加权的B3LYP/def2-SVP HOMO-LUMO分离分别为5.81 eV和5.95 eV。0.14 eV的北极型-野生型偏移在移动块自助分析中保持正值。片段扩展改变了前沿轨道的排序，但保留了与LVFFA相关态的空间特征。CASCI测试了活性空间的敏感性，匹配的UCCSD-VQE计算重现了简化哈密顿量的CAS(4,4) CASCI参考能量。这些结果共同表明，在研究异质系统时，考虑群体意识的构象采样和模型定义的敏感性的重要性。

items.title: Mechanistic Classification of Multicatalysis
items.abstract: Multicatalysis combines two or more catalytic functions within a single reaction network and can unlock reactivity, selectivity, and synthetic efficiency that are difficult to achieve with an individual catalyst. Its mechanistic description, however, remains fragmented across partially overlapping terms such as tandem, relay, cooperative, synergistic, double-activation, and bifunctional catalysis, among others. Here, we propose a mechanism-first classification based on the relationship between catalytic functions and, specifically, on the catalytic ‘currency’ exchanged between them. When the currency is substrate-derived, the coupling is classified as tandem, cooperative, or double activation. When the exchanged currency controls catalyst state rather than contributing to the substrate framework (e.g. electrons, cofactors), the relationship is gated or regenerative, distinguished by whether activation is required only once or repeatedly during turnover. Importantly, the classification is additive, so complex reaction networks are represented as combinations of pairwise relationships. Representative reactions illustrate how this framework resolves mechanistic distinctions that are hidden by conventional labels. By linking nomenclature to the elementary connection between catalytic functions, the classification provides a compact language for comparing multicatalytic systems and a basis for more deliberate catalyst and reaction-network design.
items.authors: Miguel A. Rivero-Crespo

items.title: Customizable Approach to Conformer Space Discretization using Torsion Angular Bin Strings (customTABS)
items.abstract: Conformational ensembles of small organic molecules are primarily determined by the rotameric states of their torsional or dihedral angles. The previously introduced concept of torsion angular bin strings (TABS) is a discrete vector representation of a molecule’s dihedral states, which therefore offer a quantitative description of such ensembles. Discretization of the torsional-angle space allows us to count distinct conformational states, giving an estimate of the upper limit of the expected conformational ensemble size (nTABS). In addition to nTABS being used as a qualitative measure of molecular flexibility, TABS itself is a way of grouping conformers of a molecule without picking thresholds. In the initial version of the TABS application, the discretization was based on crystal-structure derived torsion preferences, which may not be fully transferable to the conformational preferences in other environments. Here, we present the extension of the TABS framework to consider observed, system-specific distributions for the discretization of the conformational space. CustomTABS can be used to decompose the given conformational ensemble into the torsional states, which can be useful for clustering, importance ranking of dihedrals, or convergence analysis. We present the algorithmic solutions developed for the customTABS extension and demonstrate their application in clustering molecular dynamics (MD) trajectories and monitoring the convergence of the observed torsional space.
items.authors: Jessica Braun, Enrico Ruijsenaars, Carl Schiebroek, Djahan Lamei, Paul Katzberger, Gregory A. Landrum

items.title: Neuro-Trust and System Trust: A Dual-Track Trust Structure and Antecedent Patterns in EEG-BCI Attention Training
items.abstract: As brain–computer interfaces (BCIs) move toward training, rehabilitation, and consumer use, users must judge both whether a system is technically reliable and whether it credibly represents their own neural or attentional state. This study tests whether trust after an initial EEG attention-training session is better represented by two related yet distinguishable targets: Neuro-Trust (NT), trust in the system’s representation of one’s internal state, and System Trust (ST), trust in the overall device–algorithm–training system. Candidate antecedents were generated from interviews with 18 users and comments from five platforms; survey data from 300 young adults yielded 274 valid cases. A nine-factor confirmatory factor analysis fit better than an eight-factor model merging NT and ST (Δχ2(8) = 327.155, p 0.001; HTMT = 0.411). Structural equation modeling showed that perceived feedback explainability (PFE) related positively to both NT and ST, whereas perceived attention-regulation value (PARV) related to NT only (Δχ2(1) = 21.655, p 0.001; bootstrap Δβ = 0.388, 95% CI [0.168, 0.607]). Out-of-fold SHAP analysis under repeated nested cross-validation reproduced this pattern: PARV ranked first for NT but fifth for ST, whereas PFE ranked second and first. BCI trust may thus comprise related but distinguishable dimensions with shared and limited track-specific antecedents.
items.authors: Xiaolin Zhou, Hancheng Cao, Minjian Hong, Qingling Du, Hao Fang

items.title: Optimizing Flood Early Warning Sensor Networks Using Hydrological Modeling and Machine Learning: A Semi-Arid Basin Case Study
items.abstract: Flood early warning systems (FEWSs) in data-scarce and rapidly responding catchments require monitoring networks that provide sufficient forecasting information with minimal operational cost. This study evaluates the applicability of a data-driven sensor-placement framework to the semi-arid Torghabeh River Basin in northeastern Iran, where flood-producing tributaries affect the city of Torghabeh and downstream developed areas. A 2000-year stochastic rainfall series was generated to represent a wide range of hydrological conditions and was used to drive a basin-scale HEC-HMS model parameterized from catchment physiographic characteristics and available hydrological information. After applying the adopted flood-event extraction and filtering criteria, 466 relevant synthetic events were retained for the sensor-placement analysis. Sub-basin hydrographs were then used as predictors in a Random Forest forecasting model, while permutation feature importance, SHAP, and derivative-based importance were combined to identify the most informative monitoring locations. For a 1 h lead time, the progressive predictor-selection analysis identified five of 24 candidate sub-basins as a parsimonious configuration associated with the performance plateau, corresponding to an approximately 80% reduction in monitoring locations. A different but similarly parsimonious configuration emerged for a 2 h lead time, demonstrating that optimal sensor placement is lead-time-dependent. These results demonstrate the potential of explainable machine learning tools to support parsimonious FEWS monitoring-network design under the evaluated synthetic modeling conditions, while operational application requires further validation using independent observed hydrological data.
items.authors: Mahtab Helmi, Francesco Cappelli, Mahdi Dastourani, Manfred Kleidorfer, Salvatore Grimaldi

items.title: Linking Rural Development Objectives and Outcome Indicators for the Purpose of Monitoring and Evaluating Rural Development in South Africa
items.abstract: Rural development is central to achieving global sustainability goals through its contributions to economic well-being, social inclusion, and environmental protection, yet its measurement remains fragmented. In South Africa, for instance, weak alignment between national priorities and municipal implementation constrains the effective monitoring of rural well-being. This study develops a framework for monitoring rural development across South Africa’s three spheres of government. Rural development is conceptualised as a multidimensional process shaped by livelihood capitals operating across economic, social, and environmental dimensions and reflected in measurable well-being outcomes. Using qualitative document analysis and a structured five-step indicator selection procedure, national rural development objectives were translated into measurable outputs and outcomes. Candidate indicators were then assessed against eight quality criteria to identify indicators that are policy-relevant, methodologically sound, and spatially measurable. The resulting framework comprises ten indicators, including three economic, three social, and four environmental indicators, with one social and four environmental indicators retained as intermediate proxy measures. A pilot application in the Greater Letaba Local Municipality demonstrates the operational feasibility of the framework and highlights local trade-offs between economic underperformance, human-capital constraints, and environmental vulnerability. The study contributes a policy-anchored indicator matrix that strengthens outcome-based rural development monitoring, supports vertical policy alignment, and promotes evidence-based prioritisation aimed at improving rural well-being.
items.authors: Moye Thabang Malatji, Pinky Lalthapersad-Pillay

items.title: Does Green Finance Lead to Inclusive Growth in Africa? Rethinking the Role of Financial Inclusion
items.abstract: The study assesses the role that financial inclusion plays in the relationship between green finance and inclusive growth. Drawing on institutional and financial intermediation theories, the study investigates panel data from 35 African countries over the period 2000–2023 employing a fixed effect and two-step System Generalised Method of Moments estimator. Green finance was measured using renewable energy investment flows reported by IRENA, expressed in US dollars, as a proxy for the financial resources mobilised toward environmentally sustainable projects. Financial availability, financial accessibility and financial usage are the three indicators used to measure financial inclusion. Inclusive growth was measured using a multidimensional composite index capturing economic performance, equity, and social development dimensions. The results reveal that green finance increases financial inclusion. Green finance and inclusive growth are inversely related. There is no significant evidence to prove that financial inclusion moderates the relationship between green finance and inclusive growth. The contribution from the study shows that green finance promotes financial inclusion but does not automatically guarantee inclusive growth. The study departs from the predominantly linear treatment of green finance in the African literature by showing that financial deepening and inclusive development are not necessarily complementary outcomes of green investment. It is, therefore, imperative for policymakers to deliberately design green finance with redistribution and institutional safeguards in mind to ensure that inclusion leads to broad-based development.
items.authors: Patrick Ofori-Oppong

items.title: A Corn Ear Mass Prediction Method Based on TS-YOLO and Random Forest
items.abstract: Accurate estimation of corn ear mass is an essential component of intelligent harvesting. To achieve automated mass measurement of large-scale corn ears, this study developed a dual-view prediction platform and proposed a corn ear mass prediction method based on TS-YOLO and Random Forest. First, a lightweight TS-YOLO instance segmentation model was developed using YOLOv11n-seg as the baseline network to extract morphological features. By incorporating the MStarnet multi-scale feature extraction structure, LSKA attention mechanism, and LADH detection head, the proposed model enhanced feature representation of corn ears and damaged regions while reducing model complexity. Compared with the baseline model, TS-YOLO reduced the number of parameters and computational cost by 15.04% and 11.76%, respectively, and achieved an mAP@.5 of 0.959. Subsequently, a Random Forest regression model was established by integrating morphological features with corn variety and moisture content information. The Random Forest model yielded an R2 of 0.894, with corresponding RMSE and MAE values of 18.19 g and 13.97 g, respectively. Across corn varieties and moisture levels, the mean prediction error was 3.86%, indicating consistent and reliable performance under varying sample conditions. The proposed approach enables automated corn ear mass estimation and provides support for intelligent corn ear inspection.
items.authors: Li Tan, Qiankun Fu, Fan Zhang, Jun Fu, Guangyu Li, Huaiyu Shi

items.title: 3D-Printed MOF and Carbon Monoliths for Urban Water Resilience: Materials, Devices, and System-Level Challenges
items.abstract: Urban water systems face acute disruptions, including drinking-water advisories and wildfire-related contamination, alongside chronic pressures from climate variability, ageing infrastructure, and limited institutional capacity. Decentralized treatment components may complement centralized infrastructure at point-of-use, point-of-entry, building, and district scales. Within these systems, compact adsorbent and catalytic modules could provide targeted polishing or emergency-treatment functions; however, many candidate materials are still evaluated as powders in batch tests. Three-dimensional (3D) printing can instead shape them into recoverable monoliths with tunable, interconnected flow channels. This review evaluates 3D-printed metal–organic framework (MOF), porous carbon, and MOF-derived carbon monoliths for resilient urban water treatment. We assess material selection, fabrication, and performance across four linked scales: active material, engineered monolith, treatment device, and urban water system. The evidence shows that additive manufacturing can improve material recovery, control macroscopic flow, expose active phases, and enable regenerable modules. Nevertheless, most studies remain laboratory-scale demonstrations based on model contaminants, batch operation, simplified matrices, or short cycling. Long-term continuous-flow performance, pressure drop, active-material release, transformation products, potable-water safety, device-specific life-cycle impacts, and field economics remain poorly characterized. Progress requires geometry-controlled comparisons, realistic-water breakthrough tests, service-relevant regeneration, leachables assessment, and accountable maintenance and end-of-life strategies. Resilience therefore depends on integrating material chemistry, hydraulic design, treatment-train compatibility, environmental performance, and equitable service delivery.
items.authors: Jinfeng Zhang, António Benjamim Mapossa, Maryam Rasouli, Yuxin Liu, Uttandaraman Sundararaj

items.title: Toward a Multidimensional Understanding of Evidence About Wellbeing in Education
items.abstract: Calls for evidence-based practice in wellbeing in education have expanded rapidly across research, policy and professional discourse. Yet the concept of evidence in this field often remains under-theorised and inconsistently applied. Wellbeing in education is a complex and multidisciplinary domain, informed by psychology, education, sociology, public health and philosophy and encompassing outcomes, lived experiences, relationships and contextual conditions. As a result, narrow hierarchies of evidence borrowed from medical or interventionist traditions may be insufficient for capturing the complexity of educational wellbeing. This conceptual article develops a Multidimensional Evidence Framework for understanding evidence about wellbeing in education. Drawing on a critical realist and pragmatic pluralist theoretical frame, this article proposes that robust evidence in this field includes descriptive, causal, contextual and implementation, and experiential and interpretive forms of evidence, considered through a cross-cutting equity and ethical lens. It further distinguishes between evidence about wellbeing, evidence for wellbeing practice and evidence of wellbeing impact. A Multidimensional Evidence Framework is proposed to support more rigorous and conceptually coherent research, policy and practice by integrating these complementary evidence domains with the questions of evidence of what, for whom, and for what purpose.
items.authors: Kristina Turner, Elise Hunkin, Laura McFarland, Kathryn Ambrose, Claire Philp-Clark

items.title: Hybrid-Actuated Linkage Mechanisms: Design, Control, and Energy Management
items.abstract: Hybrid-actuated linkage mechanisms combine a main drive with a controllable auxiliary input to shape motion while distributing actuator demand. This narrative review examines mechanism design, control strategies, and energy management for presses and related cyclic machinery. The mechanisms are grouped into five-bar, seven-bar, slider-crank and differential, and application-specific configurations. The synthesis identifies trade-offs among motion programmability, dwell generation, actuator loading, and structural complexity; it does not establish a universal ranking of topologies. Control methods are compared by function, including local feedback, adaptation and iterative learning, disturbance rejection, predictive optimization, and position–force or position–pressure switching. Energy measures are distinguished as demand shaping, loss reduction, regeneration, storage, and auxiliary harvesting. Press and die-cushion studies provide application-relevant evidence, whereas many robotic, vehicle, and vibration-harvesting studies provide transferable principles requiring further validation. Reported servo-energy shares, torque reductions, installed power, and energy per cycle cannot be compared as equivalent efficiency indicators. An integrated design framework links mechanism selection, control organization, and energy flow across the operating cycle. Future comparisons require common forming tasks, explicit energy-accounting boundaries, and experimental validation of coupled mechanical, control, and storage decisions.
items.authors: Moldir Kuatova, Amandyk Tuleshov, Recep Halicioglu, Akerke Baurzhan, Aziz Kamal, Anar Adilkhan

items.title: Comparative Conformational Sampling of Apo Adenylate Kinase by Enhanced Molecular Dynamics and a Sequence-Based Generative Ensemble Model
items.abstract: Conformational sampling remains a major challenge in molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of proteins with large-scale functional motions. Here, we use apo Escherichia coli adenylate kinase (AdK) as a benchmark for the open–closed transition and compare nine sampling protocols under a uniform explicit-solvent budget of 300 ns per method. The methods include unbiased MD, metadynamics, targeted MD (TMD), accelerated MD, simulated tempering, interpolation-based MD, and BioEmu. Closed-state sampling was evaluated relative to a reference-closed basin defined from ligand-stripped PDB 1AKE. TMD was the only method that both reached and maintained the closed reference, whereas unbiased MD did not enter this basin within 300 ns. Metadynamics increased sampling along the domain-distance coordinate but also promoted excessive LID opening, while simulated tempering showed a similar tendency. BioEmu generated closed-like conformations, but these states were not maintained during subsequent short MD simulations. Overall, the results show that collective-variable coverage does not necessarily correspond to stable target state occupancy and that different sampling methods provide different types of conformational information. These findings highlight the importance of selecting sampling strategies according to the specific scientific objective.
items.authors: Qingling Zhao, Ting Cui, Ying Li

items.title: Psychological Distress and Resources Under Prolonged Exposure to an Environmental Threat: A Qualitative Study on Inhabitants Exposed to the Campi Flegrei’s Bradyseism
items.abstract: Prolonged environmental threats expose communities to recurring hazard cues and uncertainty, yet psychological consequences and resources involved in adaptation remain underexplored. This study examined psychological outcomes, personal and social resources, and their co-occurrence among inhabitants exposed to bradyseism in Campi Flegrei, southern Italy. Fifty-two semi-structured interviews were conducted with inhabitants of the Campi Flegrei area. Eighteen were recruited without reference to a specific stakeholder role, whereas 34 were recruited based on their institutional, professional, or community roles. Narratives were examined through theory-driven thematic analysis. Six psychological outcomes were considered, including five distress-related negative psychological outcomes (i.e., anxiety, post-traumatic symptoms, depression, sleep disturbances, and suicidal ideation) and one adaptive psychological outcome (i.e., post-traumatic growth). Distress was classified using literature-derived categories, while the Social-psychological Antecedents to Resilience for Adaptation (SARA) classified resources by locus, specificity, and availability. Anxiety-related experiences were most frequent, followed by post-traumatic stress-related experiences, depression-related experiences, and sleep disturbances; post-traumatic growth was rare, and no segments related to suicidal ideation were identified. Risk perception, experience, acceptance, cognitive reappraisal, and place attachment were frequently identified as available resources in narratives involving distress, whereas information emerged predominantly as unavailable and available social support was identified only once in the corpus. These resources co-occurred with manifestations of distress without revealing a consistent protective pattern. The findings document the coexistence of resources and distress without establishing the direction of their relationships or a protective role. Future research should clarify resource–distress directionality and examine whether perceived agency explains why some resource constellations coexist with persistent distress, whereas others are associated with more adaptive responses under prolonged environmental threat.
items.authors: Annalisa Sarrecchia, Nuccio Ludovico, Alessandro Milani, Valeria Chiozza, Marino Bonaiuto
items.category_raw: European Journal of Investigation in Health, Psychology and Education

items.title: A Two-Dimensional Screening Framework for Compact City Plans: Spatial Reorganization Burden and Service-Access Mobility-Energy Outcomes
items.abstract: Japan’s Location Optimization Plans designate Residential and Urban Function Guidance Zones, but their outcomes for non-commuting, non-school access to daily services are rarely screened against the spatial reorganization they require. This study pairs the Urban Spatial Reorganization Distance (USRD), an exact optimal-transport, latent-demand-weighted measure of minimum reorganization, with the Urban Mobility Efficiency Index (UMEI), a demand-based measure of mobility energy normalized by the 2020 Census municipal population. Across 305 municipalities, median exact USRD was 2.45 km; 205 (67.2%) improved under full realization with a fixed transit network, whereas 100 (32.8%) did not. Total USRD was not monotonically associated with UMEI improvement (Spearman ρ=−0.056, p=0.331), but non-improvement was concentrated in designated and core cities and accompanied by lengthened modeled trips. Compactness can therefore worsen service-access efficiency when residential and destination zones are spatially misaligned. The USRD–ΔUMEI matrix is a screening framework, not an estimate of financial implementation cost.
items.authors: Takashi Kobayashi

items.title: Preliminary Study to Compare the Antimicrobial Efficacy of Aqueous and Ethanolic Ultrasound-Assisted Aloe vera Extracts
items.abstract: The growing threat of antimicrobial resistance has driven the search for natural alternatives, such as Aloe vera extracts, whose phytochemical composition and biological activity depend on the extraction solvent. This preliminary study compared the antimicrobial efficacy of aqueous and ethanolic (99%) A. vera extracts obtained by ultrasound-assisted extraction (UAE) under identical conditions, and explored their FTIR spectroscopic profiles. The extracts were characterized by FTIR and evaluated against Staphylococcus aureus ATCC 12493 and Escherichia coli ATCC 33876 using the agar well diffusion method and broth macrodilution to determine the Minimum Inhibitory Concentration (MIC) and Minimum Bactericidal Concentration (MBC). In the well diffusion assay, the ethanolic extract produced larger inhibition halos than the aqueous extract (22.3 and 20.0 mm vs. 20.6 and 17.4 mm against S. aureus and E. coli, respectively, at 200 mg/mL), and two-way ANOVA showed significant effects of extract type and microorganism (p 0.001). The ethanolic extract also showed a trend toward lower mean MIC values (62.0 and 85.6 mg/mL) than the aqueous extract (90.7 and 145.0 mg/mL); however, given the high standard deviations and the limited number of replicates (n = 3), the MIC/MBC results are inconclusive, as no specific statistical analysis was applied to them. Likewise, the FTIR spectra showed a relatively higher intensity of bands consistent with polysaccharides (O–H and C–O–C) in the aqueous extract and of the 1600–1650 cm−1 band (C=O/C=C), a spectral feature potentially associated with compounds such as anthraquinones and flavonoids, in the ethanolic extract; nevertheless, owing to band overlap, the semi-quantitative nature of the comparison and the absence of complementary analyses (e.g., HPLC-MS or NMR), these results are also inconclusive regarding the specific compound classes involved. Overall, the findings indicate a trend toward higher antimicrobial activity of the ethanolic extract against the two reference strains evaluated, which should be confirmed in future studies using broth microdilution with a larger number of replicates, identification of bioactive compounds, and a broader panel of microorganisms, including resistant clinical isolates, together with cytotoxicity assays.
items.authors: Luis Cabanillas-Chirinos, Moisés Gallozzo-Cárdenas, Magali Tantaleán Pérez, María Mondéjar Barrios, David García-Cedrón

items.title: Development of the Digital Diabetes Education Platform for Type 1 Diabetes in Pakistan
items.abstract: Objectives: This study aimed to develop a structured and culturally appropriate diabetes education platform to provide accessible education to individuals and caregivers of Type 1 Diabetes (T1D). Methods: In phase I, the digital tele-education platform, named T1Dbits, was formed by modifying and translating the existing content of DigiBete, a digital diabetes platform in the UK. First, an Expert Advisory Group (EAG, n = 13) selected 30 topics on six key areas of diabetes self-management and education. A co-design group (n = 30 TIDs and HCPs) tailored content according to the needs of the Pakistani population, in linguistically appropriate formats. In phase II, this digital resource was implemented in Digital Diabetes Education Centers in rural and urban areas (n = 30), employing a hybrid of in-person and online education delivery. Results: From December 2023 to March 2026, the platform achieved 46,000 new users and 4200 returning users. Following the implementation of T1DBits, an absolute change of 1.31% in HbA1c levels and an increase in self-reported knowledge scores were observed among T1D individuals (n = 60). HCP and community feedback highlights the platform’s strong usability for daily T1D management. About 80.95% of HCPs reported that the content fulfills their need to practice. Overall, 61.4% of the community and 52.4% of HCPs recommended translations into regional languages. Conclusions: The platform achieved a high user rate and demonstrated its effectiveness in improving glycemic control and self-management knowledge scores of T1D individuals. The platform was found to be equally useful for the HCPs and T1D community members, indicating its strong feasibility to be integrated into the routine healthcare system of Pakistan.
items.authors: Anum Anwar, Sana Ajmal, Abdul Wahab, Aliza Fatima, Salma Mehar, Maddie Julian

items.title: Integrated Molecular Classification of Endometrial Cancer: Impact on Diagnosis, Prognosis, and Clinical Management—A Systematic Review
items.abstract: Objective: To systematically review the literature on the impact of integrated molecular classification of endometrial cancer on diagnosis, prognostic stratification, and clinical management. Methods: A systematic search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Scopus, and Cochrane Library (January 2013–December 2025), following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. We included original studies, systematic reviews, clinical guidelines, and cost-effectiveness analyses applying TCGA molecular classification or its surrogate classifiers (ProMisE, TransPORTEC). Data were extracted on subtype distribution, survival outcomes, hazard ratios, stage migration, and therapeutic implications. Results: Fifty studies were included. Of these, 13 provided data on molecular subtype distribution (comprising 3527 patients), 8 reported survival outcomes, and 7 reported hazard ratios. The weighted subtype distribution from the 13 studies was as follows: POLEmut 8.9%, MMRd 25.8%, p53abn 16.7%, and NSMP 48.2%. POLEmut was associated with an excellent prognosis (5-year overall survival 95%, hazard ratio 0.5), while p53abn represented the poorest prognosis group (5-year disease-free survival 33–58%, hazard ratio 2.0). p53abn was the only independent risk factor for peritoneal (odds ratio 8.54) and vaginal (odds ratio 6.51) recurrence. Molecular classification modified risk group assignment in 6–33% of patients and improved prognostic discrimination of the 2023 FIGO staging system. Therapeutic implications include treatment de-escalation in POLEmut, immunotherapy in MMRd, and intensive chemotherapy in p53abn. Barriers to implementation include access to POLE sequencing and cost-effectiveness. Conclusions: Integrated molecular classification is an essential tool for prognostic stratification and treatment personalization in endometrial cancer. Molecular subtypes demonstrate clearly differentiated prognostic profiles and recurrence patterns, justifying their systematic incorporation into clinical practice and international guidelines.
items.authors: Silvio Antonio Galeano Galeano Reyes, María Eugenia Fraile Fraile Bethencourt, Serena Lacerenza, Carmen Camacho García, José Ernesto Moro Moro Rodríguez, Pablo Bueno Ortiz

items.title: Minimal Matricectomy Combined with Lateral Longitudinal Excision Versus Total Nail Avulsion for Ingrown Toenail: A Two-Center Retrospective Cohort Study with Propensity Score Analysis
items.abstract: Background and Objectives: Ingrown toenail frequently causes pain and infection and may recur following surgical treatment. This study compared a nail-preserving strategy, minimal matricectomy combined with lateral longitudinal excision, against total nail avulsion for recurrence and clinical outcomes, using propensity-score analysis to address non-randomized treatment allocation. Materials and Methods: In this two-center retrospective cohort study, 412 patients treated between January 2020 and December 2024 were classified according to the surgical procedure received: minimal matricectomy with lateral longitudinal excision (n = 233) or total nail avulsion (n = 179). The primary endpoint was recurrence; secondary outcomes included postoperative pain, healing time, infection, reintervention, return to activity, and patient satisfaction. Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was used as a sensitivity analysis, and recurrence-free survival was assessed using the Kaplan–Meier method with the log-rank test. Results: Over a mean follow-up of 18 months, recurrence occurred in 1.7% (n = 4) of the minimal matricectomy group versus 12.3% (n = 22) of the avulsion group (p 0.001; crude OR 8.0, 95% CI 2.7–23.7). After IPTW adjustment, the association remained consistent (adjusted OR 7.4, 95% CI 2.6–21.3; standardized mean differences 0.10 for all covariates). Kaplan–Meier analysis confirmed significantly higher recurrence-free survival with minimal matricectomy (log-rank p 0.001). Reintervention (1.3% vs. 9.5%) and return to normal activity (5 vs. 9 days) also favored minimal matricectomy, with lower pain scores, shorter healing, fewer infections, and higher satisfaction. Conclusions: Minimal matricectomy combined with lateral longitudinal excision was associated with lower recurrence and improved clinical outcomes compared with total nail avulsion. This association remained statistically significant after propensity score adjustment for measured baseline covariates. Prospective randomized studies are warranted to confirm these findings.
items.authors: Ahmet Topcu, İsmail Ege Subaşı, Furkan Saydın

items.title: RetiGlue-SLAM: A Robust Visual SLAM System Designed for Low-Light and Complex Environments
items.abstract: Visual simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) often degrades in low-light environments because of insufficient brightness, reduced contrast, and loss of texture, which cause sparse features, accumulated mismatches, and unstable trajectories. This paper presents RetiGlue-SLAM, a visual-inertial SLAM framework that retains the third version of ORB-SLAM (ORB-SLAM3) as the system backbone and improves the front end through task-driven coupling of three components: Retinexformer for low-light image enhancement, SuperPoint for learned local feature extraction, and LightGlue for robust cross-frame matching.
