The enhanced images and learned correspondences are integrated into the tracking thread, whereas the geometric back-end and inertial optimization of ORB-SLAM3 remain unchanged. Experiments on low-light sequences from EuRoC and the night-time Old Town sequence of 4Seasons show improved feature matching, tracking completion, and localization accuracy relative to the baseline. A two-stage ablation separates the learned front end from the full RetiGlue-SLAM pipeline, and a module-level runtime analysis reports a front-end latency of 41 ms per stereo frame (24.39 FPS). The results support RetiGlue-SLAM as a benchmarked low-light visual-inertial localization framework; field deployment and end-to-end real-time operation remain outside the scope of this study.
items.authors: Yiming Li, Xianpu Liang, Guangming Guo, Peng Su, Qi An

items.title: Dynamic Response and Safety Control of the First-Excavated Tunnel Lining Under Adjacent-Tunnel Blasting in Closely Spaced Tunnels
items.abstract: Dynamic disturbances induced by blasting excavation of the later-excavated tunnel in closely spaced tunnels may propagate through the inter-tunnel rock pillar and induce significant vibration and stress responses in the lining of the first-excavated tunnel. To investigate the spatial response characteristics and governing factors of the first-excavated tunnel lining, a three-dimensional blast-dynamics model was established based on the Zhongliangshan Tunnel project. The axial and circumferential distributions of peak particle velocity (PPV) and maximum principal tensile stress were analyzed, and the effects of rock-mass grade, charge weight per blasthole, and tunnel clear spacing were evaluated. The relationship between PPV and maximum principal tensile stress was further examined, and the relative variability of the lining responses under different governing factors was evaluated using the coefficient of variation (CV). The results show that the lining response is concentrated mainly near the face of the later-excavated tunnel, with the blast-facing haunch and shoulder exhibiting the strongest vibration and tensile-stress responses. Both PPV and maximum principal tensile stress decrease with increasing axial distance from the face, with generally faster attenuation behind the face than ahead of it. As the rock-mass condition deteriorates from Grade III to Grade V, both response indices increase overall. Increasing tunnel clear spacing significantly reduces both responses, with the most pronounced reduction occurring when the spacing increases from 1 to 3 m, whereas increasing the charge weight per blasthole generally intensifies the lining response. PPV is strongly correlated with maximum principal tensile stress. The CV analysis shows that tunnel clear spacing produces the greatest relative variability in both response indices within the investigated parameter ranges. For PPV, the response variability follows the order of tunnel clear spacing charge weight per blasthole rock-mass grade, whereas for maximum principal tensile stress, the order is tunnel clear spacing rock-mass grade charge weight per blasthole. These findings provide a basis for blasting-parameter optimization and safety control of existing linings in closely spaced tunnel construction.
items.authors: Shuo Zhang, Xinze Peng, Yongxiang Zheng, Wenqing Li, Ruifeng Huang, Zhong Li

items.title: HexaClus: Uncertainty-Aware Hexagonal Supervised Spatial Clustering++
items.abstract: Due to the heterogeneity and uneven distribution of geospatial data, predictive geospatial techniques are often required to provide both accurate target predictions and uncertainty quantification. However, existing approaches typically only provide post-hoc uncertainty estimates, rather than using uncertainty to guide the spatial model training process itself. To address these limitations, we introduce HexaClus++, a supervised, uncertainty-aware, spatial-clustering-based approach that integrates both accuracy and uncertainty to guide local model training on clustered spatial hexagonal regions. To evaluate the performance of our technique, we conduct experiments on property valuation datasets using diverse machine learning approaches. The results demonstrate that HexaClus++, when combined with different base learners, achieves competitive accuracy while also delivering well-calibrated uncertainty, reliable prediction intervals, and enhanced interpretability through regional uncertainty maps and spatially varying feature importance.
items.authors: Yameng Guo, Seppe vanden Broucke

items.title: Blast Performance Enhancement of RC Columns Using Machine Learning
items.abstract: Reinforced concrete buildings may experience complete or partial progressive collapse due to column failure under blast loading. Therefore, predicting the structural response of columns under blast loading can support preventive measures that reduce fatalities and financial losses. Using thirteen features related to column and blast properties, this study presents machine learning models to predict the maximum lateral displacement of reinforced concrete (RC) columns strengthened with CFRP sheets under blast loading. A total of 1263 CFRP-strengthened numerical configurations were generated from 421 unstrengthened baseline specimens, including 121 collected from the literature and 300 developed using ANSYS AUTODYN, by applying two CFRP wrapping schemes and three CFRP thicknesses. The strengthening schemes consisted of full-height and middle-third CFRP wrapping. The resulting blast-performance enhancement was assessed based on the reduction in maximum lateral displacement. XGBoost, CatBoost, LightGBM, and Gradient Boosting algorithms were evaluated. The XGBoost model was interpreted locally and globally using the SHAP algorithm to determine the significance and contribution of each input parameter. The accuracy of the XGBoost model was evaluated by comparison with results from a previous study and ANSYS AUTODYN finite element simulations. The XGBoost model achieved high predictive performance, with R2, RMSE, MAE, and MAPE values of 0.97, 16.237 mm, 7.722 mm, and 5.1%, respectively, demonstrating its ability to predict blast response and identify relationships between the key parameters and maximum lateral displacement.
items.authors: Karim Ibrahim, Ahmed Elbelbisi, Abdallah Salama, Atef Eraky, Shimaa Emad

items.title: EntroMEMS: Proof-of-Concept Integration of Quantum-Derived Initialization and MEMS Entropy Acquisition on an ESP32
items.abstract: Resource-constrained edge devices may have limited entropy during startup. EntroMEMS is a proof-of-concept architecture combining quantum-derived initialization material with candidate physical entropy from three microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) gyroscopes on an ESP32. A 1024-bit quantum-derived pool was embedded in firmware; its first 128 bits initialize the prototype generator. This does not constitute secure provisioning. The revised V2 acquisition retains two least significant bits from each gyroscope axis, yielding 18 binary samples per cycle. Sequential non-IID assessments using the official NIST SP 800-90B software yielded estimates of 0.825393–0.911960 bit/sample across nine baseline sensor streams and 0.815998–0.912364 bit/sample across sensitivity windows. Full SP 800-90B validation was not performed because the prescribed restart dataset was not collected. For a historical V1 conditioned sequence of 1,000,000 bits, all 188 p-values from the official NIST SP 800-22 suite were at least 0.01. Only one sequence was evaluated; across-sequence pass proportions and p-value uniformity were not assessed. A follow-up benchmark averaged 1414.287 microseconds per acquisition-and-extraction cycle, corresponding to 12.7273 kbit/s excluding serial output. These results support prototype feasibility and investigation of an auxiliary entropy input, without establishing cryptographic suitability. Production deployment would require secure provisioning, protected storage, a vetted DRBG, continuous health tests, and conservative entropy accounting.
items.authors: Borislav Atanasov Georgiev

items.title: Stronger Through the Transition: Evaluating the Effect of Creatine and Resistance Training on Body Composition, Strength, and Sleep in Perimenopause
items.abstract: Introduction: Perimenopause is associated with adverse body composition and strength changes, yet resistance training and creatine monohydrate (CM) remain underrepresented in this population. This study examined the effect of six-weeks of high-intensity resistance training (HIRT) with or without CM on body composition, muscle size and quality, strength, volume, and sleep in perimenopause. Methods: Fifty-one perimenopausal women (Age: 46.2±4.6 years; Body Mass Index: 25.4±4.0 kg/m2) were randomized to CM, placebo (PL), or control (CON). CM and PL completed a 5-day loading (CM: 20g/day; non-caloric PL: 14.5g/day), followed by a maintenance phase (CM 4.5g/day; PL gummies) combined with six-weeks of HIRT; CON maintained normal activity. Lean soft-tissue (LST; kg) was assessed from dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry. Muscle characteristics were determined from peripheral quantitative computed-tomography [muscle area (MuA); cm2; muscle density (MuD); mg/cm3]; and ultrasound [muscle cross-sectional area (mCSA): cm2; echo intensity (EI): a.u.]. Sleep was determined from a wrist-worn wearable. Results: CM resulted in increased LST compared to PL (mean difference±standard error: 0.380±0.431 kg, p=0.999) and CON (1.052±0.474 kg, p=0.096). Muscle size increased in CM compared to CON (MuA: 6.11±2.19 cm2; mCSA: 3.222±1.051 cm2; p=0.011-0.023), but not PL. No main treatment effects were observed for MuD or EI. Both lower (CM: 139.6±34.1 lbs; PL: 126.2±31.5 lbs; p lt; 0.001) and upper body (CM: 9.0±3.4 lbs; p=0.031; PL: 8.1±3.0 lbs; p=0.032) strength increased compared to CON, with no volume differences. No training by treatment interactions were observed for sleep. Conclusion: HIRT improved muscle outcomes, with CM adding 0.38 kg to LST and 148.6 lbs to strength.
items.authors: Gabrielle M. Delbiondo, Paul A. Baker, W. Mikey Johnson, Caroline G. Kelly, Celia W. Gottlieb, Gregory J. Grosicki

items.title: Raman Spectroscopy, Machine Learning and Pancreatic Tumors
items.abstract: Pancreatic cancer remains difficult to diagnose at an early stage, motivating the development of label-free methods capable of detecting biochemical changes in tissue, cells, and biofluids. Raman spectroscopy provides molecularly specific measurements, but their diagnostic interpretation increasingly relies on chemometric, machine-learning, and deep-learning methods. This review critically examines Raman-based studies related to pancreatic cancer, with particular attention to acquisition modalities, preprocessing, feature extraction, classification, and validation design. Across the reviewed literature, high internal classification performance is frequently accompanied by small numbers of independent biological units, spectral pseudoreplication, unclear patient- or specimenlevel partitioning, data-dependent processing outside training folds, and limited external validation. Differences among instruments and preprocessing pipelines further restrict direct comparison across studies. We therefore distinguish evidence of spectral separability within a dataset from evidence of diagnostic generalization to independent patients. Priorities for the field include transparent reporting, patient-grouped evaluation, training-only preprocessing and model selection, harmonized acquisition and processing procedures, and shared benchmark datasets with sequestered test sets. Raman spectroscopy remains a promising source of biochemical information for pancreatic cancer research, but clinical translation requires reproducible performance across independent patients, laboratories, and acquisition conditions.
items.authors: Riccardo Del Gratta, Gianmarco Lazzini, Raffaele Gaeta, Annalisa Comandatore, Giuseppe Succurro, Luca Morelli

items.title: A Frequency-Integrated Electromagnetic Vulnerability Index for Electronic Systems in Complex Electromagnetic Environments
items.abstract: This paper proposes a frequency-integrated electromagnetic vulnerability index (FI-EVI), which is a reference-weighted susceptibility-screening metric for shielded electronic enclosures rather than a direct measure of functional failure. The frequency-resolved vulnerability is defined as the internal-to-reference RMS field ratio, VE(f) = Eint,rms(f)/Eref,rms(f), and FI-EVI is its log-frequency average from 10 MHz to 18 GHz. All cases use a swept-frequency incident plane wave of 1 V/m RMS and, as a common normalization benchmark, the MIL-STD-461G RS103 aircraft-internal limit (20 V/m up to 1 GHz and 60 V/m above). The internal field is obtained from an aperture-dominant reduced-order transfer function with parameters fixed in advance. A worst-case spectrum is derived under a fixed incident power-density budget and a peak power spectral density cap αSflat; the amplification factor is bounded by α. For three UAV-scale apertures (15, 60, and 150 mm), FI-EVI is 0.0056, 0.0094, and 0.0159, and the amplification factor at α = 10 is 1.27, 1.58, and 2.23. For one similitude-scaled family of a controlled loaded enclosure simulated with openEMS, the band-limited reduced-order FI-EVI is 9.4–21.5% below the full-wave envelope and within −11.0% to +7.3% of the maximum among the prescribed probe locations and polarizations, although the enclosure resonances are not reproduced.
items.authors: Huichang Lee, Sung-kon Kim

items.title: Method for Neutralizing the Effect of Loading System Compliance During Compression Tests Using Mixed Additive-Multiplicative Correction
items.abstract: This paper examines the undesirable yet inevitable influence of loading system compliance on specimen deformation measurements during testing—a problem that has become typical and remains consistently relevant in the field of mechanical materials testing. Of the two possible approaches to addressing this issue—increasing the stiffness of the loading system or applying corrections to the measurement results—this work focuses primarily on the latter. A mathematical model describing the interaction between loading system components was developed using mixed additive-multiplicative scaling, and a cost-effective method for neutralizing the effect of loading system compliance was proposed. It is demonstrated that applying this method is theoretically equivalent to conducting tests on a virtual machine with infinite loading system stiffness. The method utilizes load-displacement data obtained from two compression tests performed under identical conditions: one with the specimen and one without it. The method was validated using aluminum specimens by comparing the calculated elastic modulus (75.6 GPa) with the established reference range (72–75 GPa). Additionally, the method was used to determine the elastic modulus of amphibolite and to generate corrected load-displacement diagrams. A comparative analysis revealed a source of error inherent in the traditional compliance summation method. Overall, the proposed approach, model, and method—based on additive-multiplicative correction of compression test results—offer a structured and interpretable supplement to traditional techniques, opening new avenues for enhancing the accuracy of both direct and indirect measurements of material properties.
items.authors: Gennady Kolesnikov, Vitali Shekov, Nikolai Zakharov

items.title: An Atmospheric Emissions Indicator to Implement Air Quality and Climate Change Targets
items.abstract: This paper introduces a technique for assessing the progress towards air pollution and greenhouse gas targets. To guide policy decisions, an atmospheric emissions indicator, AEI, combining national air quality and greenhouse gas emissions, is proposed. It has been applied to the UK, but could be adopted by other countries. Although not directly a measure of environmental consequences, this index is a simple policy aid to implementing air pollution and climate change targets based on an emission ceilings approach. The proposed AEI index is a weighted sum of emissions derived from modelling studies of the impact of UK air pollution and greenhouse gas emissions between 1970 and 2050. The approach is not so very different from aspects of current UK legislation, such as the National Emissions Ceilings Regulations, the UK Climate Change Act, National Determined Contributions within the Paris Agreement, and other assessment tools of population exposure, such as cost-benefit analyses and other environmental targets. The indicator could be extended to incorporate very short-lived radiative forcers associated with air pollution.
items.authors: Bernard Fisher

items.title: Electrochemical Synthesis of Composites Based on Silicon and Carbon Nanotube Compounds as a Platform for Biocatalyst Development
items.abstract: Progress in the field of modern heterogeneous catalysts requires the development of composite materials with a well-developed surface area and sorption capacity, as well as the possibility of functionalization in a specific direction. This paper presents the results of electrochemical synthesis of composites based on an organosilica matrix and multi-walled carbon nanotubes for subsequent application as a platform for enzyme immobilization. By potentiostatic electrodeposition, composite coatings based on two types of organosilica sol (STPEG and STEG) were applied to the surface of a glassy carbon electrode with the addition of MWCNTs subjected to various methods of oxidative treatment. Optimization of the deposition time in the range of 0.5–5 min revealed that the maximum electrochemical activity and heterogeneous transfer rate constants were achieved at 1 min of electrodeposition. It has been found that the use of MWCNTs oxidized in H2O2 vapors provides the best balance between hydrophilicity, conductivity, and the formation of a permeable matrix due to fewer defects and carboxyl groups. It has been demonstrated that the selected OP-SG/1 composite effectively supports mediator bioelectrocatalysis with recombinant laccase ScaSL in the presence of an ABTS mediator, as evidenced by the formation of sigmoidal CVs of catalytic oxygen reduction. The obtained results confirm that the electrodeposited organosilica composite is a promising and biocompatible material for the development of surface biocatalysts, which can be used in wastewater treatment technologies and bioreactor design.
items.authors: Pavel Oskin, Konstantin Egorov, Daria Lavrova, Nadezhda Dmitruk, Irina Gutnik, Sergey Alferov

items.title: The Catastrophe Bond Price Under the Jump Diffusion Model: A Multi-Currency Comparison
items.abstract: In this paper, we extend our jump-diffusion model to price the catastrophe bond. The model has three coupled stochastic processes—the spot exchange rate and the domestic and foreign interest rates—under a risk-neutral measure, with compensated compound Poisson jumps in each of the processes. We assume that catastrophe occurrence is independent of the financial markets. Under this assumption, we obtain an approximation for the price of the catastrophe bond using the derived jump-diffusion zero-coupon bond price and the call price on the foreign currency, where the call price uses a moment-matched lognormal approximation. For numerical analysis, we compare the approximation with Monte Carlo simulation and a diffusion-only benchmark for USD/EUR, USD/INR, USD/BRL, and USD/JPY, which cover stable and volatile exchange rate economies. The jump-diffusion approximation is closer to Monte Carlo than the diffusion-only benchmark for most pairs and maturities. The results separate the catastrophe and exchange rate exposures of a sponsor issuing a CAT bond in foreign currency.
items.authors: Ridhima Nehra, Indranil SenGupta

items.title: Local Mo6+ Coordination and Textural Accessibility, Rather than Bulk Phase, Correlate with the Peroxidase-Mimetic Reactivity of CoMoO4 Nanopowders
items.abstract: Whether the bulk crystallographic phase determines the H2O2 reactivity of oxide nanopowders has direct implications for catalyst design. Three glycine–nitrate-derived CoMoO4 nanopowders—as-synthesized, calcined at 450 °C (both β-CoMoO4 by XRD), and calcined at 1000 °C (α-CoMoO4)—were studied by ATR-FTIR spectroscopy, the Briggs–Rauscher (BR) oscillatory reaction, cyclic voltammetry (CV), and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy. Deconvolution of the Mo–O stretching region with a uniform Voigt line shape resolves octahedral (α-type) and tetrahedral (β-type) Mo6+ components in both β-classified powders, indicating short-range coordination heterogeneity not detected by XRD. In the BR reaction (n = 3), the 450 °C powder suppresses oscillations at ≤0.002 g, whereas the as-synthesized powder still oscillates at 0.040 g (slope of the τosc decrease is 5172 ± 406 s g−1), and the bulk-α 1000 °C powder is about four times less active per gram than the as-synthesized powder. CV supports the highest activity of the 450 °C powder. A semi-quantitative descriptor, Φ = ρα × SBET, combining the FTIR α-type band-area fraction with the BET surface area, identifies the most active powder but does not discriminate between the two less active ones. Within this series, bulk phase identity alone does not predict peroxidase-mimetic activity.
items.authors: Milena Rosić, Zorica Mojović, Maja C. Pagnacco, Jelena V. Senćanski, Jelena P. Maksimović, Dragana Jordanov

items.title: Gamblification, Fintech, and Fan Financial Wellbeing: A Scoping Review Through a Social-Sustainability Lens
items.abstract: The gamblification of sport has entered a fintech-enabled phase in which betting is no longer merely advertised around sport but designed into the act of watching it—continuous, mobile, frictionless, and seamlessly financed. Because this transformation shortens the pathway between impulse and expenditure, its consequences are increasingly financial; yet the evidence on how it affects the financial wellbeing of fans has not been synthesised. This scoping review, conducted in accordance with the PRISMA-ScR guidelines, mapped research linking the gamblification of sport—in both its marketing and its fintech dimensions—to fan financial wellbeing. Three databases (Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed), supplemented by hand-searching and a Google Scholar sweep, yielded 69 included studies. The evidence is young, expanding, and still largely exploratory in character. It is weighted heavily toward the marketing channel (advertising, sponsorship, inducements, normalisation), which is mature and well-theorised, whereas the fintech affordances of the betting product form a distinct but smaller literature, and financial wellbeing is most often reached only indirectly through marketing-driven overspend. Only five of the 69 studies directly measured a financial outcome, and all five lay within the fintech channel; the intersection at the centre—where the redesigned product meets the financial lives of vulnerable fans—remains largely unoccupied. We reframe this gap as a question of the social sustainability of sport, bearing on equity, wellbeing, and responsible consumption (SDGs 10, 3, and 12), and set out a research and governance agenda to address it.
items.authors: Jovana Vitošević, Jovana Radoičić-Dimitrijević, Milica Filipović, Biljana Vitošević, Katarzyna Sterkowicz-Przybycień, Miloš Popović

items.title: Mineralogical Characterization and Purification of High-Purity Quartz from the Pegmatite Core Zone
items.abstract: Pegmatitic quartz is an important source of high-purity quartz, and its purity and inclusion characteristics together constitute the key criteria for evaluating the efficient utilization of this quartz. This study takes the quartz resource from the core zone of a pegmatite deposit in Xinjiang as the research object, analyzing its process mineralogical characteristics and inclusion features, and conducting purification experiments. The results show that the mineral composition of the quartz resource from the core zone of the pegmatite in Xinjiang is simple, with the main mineral being quartz (~99%) with minor amounts of mica ( 1%) and plagioclase ( 1%). In-situ microanalysis indicates that the average contents of the four key impurity elements, Al, Ti, Li, and B, in the quartz are 13.24, 6.17, 0.10, and 2.55 μg/g, respectively, with a total average content of 22.49 μg/g, exhibiting a generally low abundance of impurity elements, which preliminarily suggests that the core-zone quartz of this pegmatite has the potential for preparing high-purity quartz. After a combined purification process involving physical separation, chemical leaching, and chlorination roasting, the total impurity content of the quartz samples decreased from 97.95 μg/g to 20.66 μg/g, corresponding to a purity of 99.9979%. Meanwhile, the fluid inclusion index decreased from 0.1362 to 0.0213, representing a total reduction of 84.36%, indicating that the combined purification process exhibits a remarkable removal effect on fluid inclusions. However, the Ti content in the purified samples remains relatively high (9.99 μg/g), which may limit its application in high-end optical, semiconductor, and other fields. In addition, the fluid inclusion index is not the sole indicator for evaluating the development degree of quartz inclusions, and further materialization evaluation is required to comprehensively assess the purification efficiency and guide process optimization.
items.authors: Yameng Ma, Hongjie Wang, Haiqi Zhang, Xiumin Tan, Yuejun Yi, Zhichao Wu

items.title: A Frequency-Segmented Accelerated Vibration Test Method for Seat Frames Using Damage-Rate Ratio: A Comparative Study with IPL and FDS
items.abstract: To address the issues of lengthy vibration durability test cycles for seat frames and poor consistency of damage equivalence at different locations under multiaxial excitation in existing acceleration methods, this paper proposes a frequency-segmented accelerated vibration test method based on damage-rate equivalence. The method derives an analytical relationship between damage rate and stress spectral moments based on the Dirlik broadband damage estimation, enabling frequency-selective amplification of the acceleration PSD, thereby compressing test duration while maintaining a constant damage-rate ratio at critical nodes. The proposed method is implemented in three strategies—triaxial full-band, triaxial frequency-segmented, and uniaxial frequency-segmented—and compared with the inverse power law (IPL) and fatigue damage spectrum (FDS) methods. Through finite element analysis of a seat frame and dynamic force measurements on a six-degree-of-freedom hydraulic shaker, the damage-rate ratios at four structural nodes are used as indicators to evaluate each method. Results show that when the triaxial frequency-segmented strategy (DRR-TP) achieves the target damage-rate ratio of 0.25, the thrust increase is only 17.1%, substantially lower than the 21.0% increase from full-band acceleration, while displacement requirements remain nearly unchanged. At the calibrated node, DRR-TP provides accuracy comparable to FDS and better than IPL and the uniaxial strategy under the tested conditions. However, deviations exist across all methods at non-calibrated nodes, with IPL and the uniaxial strategy showing more pronounced deviations in this study. Furthermore, accelerated high-intensity road spectra may produce stresses approaching the yield limit, necessitating amplitude constraints. Overall, the DRR-TP method offers a favorable balance between efficiency and equipment feasibility, providing a practical framework for accelerated durability testing of seat frames.
items.authors: Shengtai Ren, Yi Qiu

items.title: Exploring the Relationships Between XCO2 Concentrations and Climate Variables in Brazil
items.abstract: Climate conditions influence ecosystem carbon exchange and, consequently, atmospheric CO2 through variations in temperature, precipitation, and soil moisture. Brazil provides an important case study because of its extensive forest cover, land-use change, and pronounced climatic variability. This study combines OCO-2-constrained GEOS assimilated estimates of the column-averaged dry-air mole fraction of CO2 (XCO2; OCO-2 GEOS Level 3 monthly product, version 10r, February 2015–January 2022) with ERA5-Land air temperature and top-layer soil moisture and CHIRPS precipitation. All inferential analyses were performed on the native 0.5° × 0.625° grid of the XCO2 product (2264 grid cells), to which the climate fields were aggregated by area-weighted averaging. Monthly anomalies were obtained by jointly removing a monthly climatology and a linear trend at each grid cell, and statistical significance was assessed with an autocorrelation-adjusted effective sample size and Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery-rate (FDR) control applied to pre-defined families of tests spanning all grid cells and, for the lagged analysis, all seven candidate lags. After FDR control, 861 of the 2264 grid cells (38.0%) retained a significant contemporaneous correlation between XCO2 and precipitation, compared with 207 (9.1%) for soil moisture and 0 for temperature. The precipitation association was positive, concentrated in central Brazil, predominantly contemporaneous, retained after conditioning on temperature and soil moisture, and robust to alternative trend definitions, rank-based correlation, and removal of the zonal-mean XCO2 background. Temperature was associated with XCO2 only when leading it by 1–4 months (21.3% of cells), a result that depended on the multiple-testing procedure, and no significant association was found with XCO2 leading climate. Without detrending, nominally significant correlations were widespread, but none survived autocorrelation adjustment and FDR control, and the sequential deseasonalize-then-detrend procedure of earlier analyses introduced an artifact that masked these associations. Out of sample, the three variables predicted XCO2 anomalies poorly (median leave-one-year-out cross-validated R2 = −0.023). These results reveal a spatially coherent short-term precipitation–XCO2 association in central Brazil whose physical origin, local fluxes or atmospheric transport, cannot be established from concentration data alone.
items.authors: Melisa Tuirán, Caroline Rodrigues Vaz, Mauricio Uriona Maldonado, Sebastián Zapata

items.title: Chemical Profiling, Antifungal and Insecticidal Activities of Santolina chamaecyparissus L. Essential Oil: An Integrated Experimental and In Silico Study
items.abstract: Santolina chamaecyparissus L. essential oil (EO) was investigated for its chemical composition, antifungal and insecticidal activities, together with complementary molecular docking and ADMET analyses. GC–MS revealed a monoterpene-rich profile dominated by santolina triene (48.44%), α-pinene (14.05%), camphor (8.80%), myrcene (5.17%), and α-thujene (4.26%). The EO exhibited antifungal activity against Fusarium oxysporum and Aspergillus brasiliensis, with MIC and MFC values of 4 mg/mL and concentration-dependent inhibition of mycelial growth. Insecticidal activity against Rhyzopertha dominica was demonstrated through fumigant, topical-contact, and treated-grain assays, with efficacy varying according to concentration and exposure duration. Molecular docking identified α-thujene and p-cymene as the highest-ranked tested EO constituents against fungal CYP51B and insect AChE, respectively. ADMET predictions highlighted favorable physicochemical characteristics alongside potential toxicity-related liabilities requiring experimental verification. These findings provide a basis for further investigation of S. chamaecyparissus EO and its constituents as potential natural antifungal and insecticidal agents.
items.authors: Aziz Zouhri, Rafik El-Mernissi, Assia Houiat, Bahia Abdelfattah, Oussama Khibech, Yahya El-Mernissi

items.title: Successful Nonsurgical Management of Norovirus-Associated Necrotizing Enterocolitis in a Preterm Infant: A Case Report
items.abstract: Norovirus infection has been increasingly reported in association with necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) in preterm neonates, although the clinical spectrum remains poorly defined. We report the case of a 29-week preterm male infant who developed abdominal distension on day 35 of life, with a sepsis-like clinical presentation. Stool reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction confirmed Norovirus infection. Serial abdominal radiographs showed intestinal pneumatosis from day 2 of illness, consistent with Bell stage IIA NEC. The pneumatosis persisted for three days and completely resolved by day 5, without perforation or clinical deterioration. The infant was managed conservatively with bowel rest, parenteral nutrition, broad-spectrum antibiotics, and mechanical ventilation for 7 days. IVIG (500 mg/kg/day for 4 days) was administered for clinically suspected capillary leak syndrome. Enteral feeding was restarted after 8 days, and the infant was discharged at 71 days of life without gastrointestinal complications. This case highlights the heterogeneous clinical spectrum of Norovirus-associated intestinal disease and suggests that conservative management may be successful in selected clinically stable preterm infants with NEC and intestinal pneumatosis.
items.authors: Linda Sessa, Lucilla Martini, Marta Tedesco, Alessandro Ferrazza, Matteo Stefanini, Nicoletta Menzella

items.title: Presence of Paradoxical Mid-Systolic Longitudinal Strain (Stretching) with Speckle Tracking in the Basal Inferior-to-Lateral Segments in Mitral Valve Prolapse
items.abstract: Background and Purpose: Abnormality in the motion of the inferior papillary muscle was found in an early study of mitral valve prolapse (MVP). We visually observed an abnormal movement not only in the inferior wall but also in the anterolateral and inferolateral basal walls in several patients with MVP. Therefore, the aim of this work was to analyze these findings using strain (Speckle Tracking—STE). Methods: A total of 60 MVP patients having a superior systolic displacement of the posterior leaflet, in whole or in part of the scallops, of at least 2 mm, and 20 normal subjects as controls were included. Longitudinal strain was calculated in the three apical views (Philips iE 33 Matrix—implemented strain software). The strain in the three abovementioned basal segments was measured at 160 msec from the beginning of systole (mid-systole), and then we averaged their values to form a “triad” of averaged values that could be subsequently compared among the groups for statistical calculations. The Global Longitudinal Strain (GLS) was also calculated for all subjects. The Mann–Whitney U-test was used for comparisons. A “p” value ≤ 0.05 was considered significant. Results: According to the strain patterns, we were able to identify two distinct groups in MVP patients: Group 1 had a “paradoxical” strain at 160 ms (=positive, that means “mechanical stretching”) in at least a single segment of the aforementioned “triad” of basal segments (n = 35), and Group 2 had not a “paradoxical” strain (n = 25) in any of the aforementioned “triad” segments at the same mid-systolic point. Statistical significance was found between Group 1 and Group 2 at 160 ms and at the peak (p 0.0001 for both) and the same was found for GLS (p 0.01). Group 1 vs. controls, as expected, displayed a significant difference in the strain at 160 msec (p 0.0001) while Group 2 vs. controls did not differ significantly, even at the peak. Conclusions: According to our results, we found in our MVP population (more than half of the patients) that some MVP patients have a “paradoxical” strain (=mechanical stretching) in at least a single segment of the basal inferior-to-lateral segments (that we have named the “triad”) in mid-systole, whereas others do not. The passive continuous stretching of myocardial cells is known to lead, with time, to the replacement of cells by fibrosis (and fibrosis is a condition that is well known to be a source of arrhythmias, and even malignant). Previous Cardiac Magnetic Resonance (CMR) studies already reported the presence of fibrosis in the same basal wall segments in some MVP patients. Thus, considering our strain results, in MVP patients, but only in those with ventricular arrhythmias, it is indicated, in our opinion the strain should be analyzed, as it is an inexpensive tool. If the strain is found to be “paradoxical” even in a single segment of what we have named the “triad”, a further evaluation with CMR (even if expensive) is recommended to look for the presence of fibrosis. Strain analysis is indicated because these findings may have implications for prognosis, further evaluation of arrhythmias and the selection of appropriate therapy.
items.authors: Antonio Auriti, Lucio Monaco, Elisa Rauseo, Lanfranco Antonini, Furio Colivicchi

items.title: The Rohingya Refugee Archive: Haunting, Survival, and Futurity
items.abstract: When Rohingya families fled Myanmar’s genocidal violence in August 2017, most carried only a few materials documenting the cultural lives they had built over generations in Rakhine State, a collective archive of their ancestral homeland. In the aftermath, the Tatmadaw burned their villages and expropriated their land. This displacement represented a rupture for the community and transformed the collective archive into a refugee one. Severed from their Rakhine and its cultural replenishment, the sole repositories of knowledge were the Rohingya themselves: walking archives. In the refugee camps of Bangladesh, the Rohingya have responded to this displacement (their physical erasure from their homeland) and this destruction of their archival materials (the burning of their documents) by nurturing and reconstituting an archive in exile of cultural and familial practices that exist both beyond and in place of the papers and certificates that regulated their presence in Myanmar. Within the bamboo huts and under the tarpaulin covering, Rohingya families protect cultural practices against state-imposed erasure, ensuring they pass them down to the next generation, to those boys and girls who have never seen or smelled Rakhine. The work of Rohingya photographers and the images they produce is one way this refugee archive is transmitted across generations.
items.authors: Jesse O’Reilly-Conlin

items.title: The Relationship Between Prospective Classroom Teachers’ Perceived Mathematical Competence and Their Awareness of Sustainable Development: The Moderating Role of Gender and Year of Study
items.abstract: Preparing prospective teachers capable of addressing sustainable development challenges requires not only sustainable development awareness but also competencies that support evidence-based reasoning. However, empirical evidence regarding the relationship between perceived mathematical competence and sustainable development awareness remains limited. This study examined the relationship between prospective classroom teachers’ perceived mathematical competence and sustainable development awareness and investigated the moderating roles of gender and year of study. The study employed a cross-sectional research design with 341 prospective classroom teachers from four universities in Türkiye. Data were examined to determine the relationship between perceived mathematical competence and sustainable development awareness and to test the moderating roles of gender and year of study through moderation analysis. The findings revealed that perceived mathematical competence was positively and significantly associated with sustainable development awareness (r = 0.37, p 0.001). Furthermore, gender significantly moderated this relationship (B = 0.56, p 0.001, ΔR2 = 0.04), whereas year of study did not demonstrate a significant moderating effect (ΔR2 = 0.0045, p = 0.621). These findings indicate that prospective classroom teachers who perceive themselves as more mathematically competent also tend to report higher levels of sustainable development awareness. The study contributes to the literature by providing empirical evidence of the association between perceived mathematical competence and sustainable development awareness and highlights the potential relevance of perceived mathematical competence to education for sustainable development within teacher education programs.
items.authors: Ebru Kükey, Ayşe Ülkü Kan

items.title: A Kawasaki Disease-Like Presentation in a Child with Concurrent Detection of Group A Streptococcus and Adenovirus: A Case Report on the Characterization of Physical Findings and Short-Interval Reassessment
items.abstract: Background and Clinical Significance: Kawasaki disease (KD) lacks specific diagnostic tests and requires early diagnosis and treatment to prevent coronary artery lesions. Concurrent infections may produce KD-like presentations; however, practical management of this time-sensitive uncertainty remains poorly described. Case Presentation: A previously healthy 4-year-old boy developed a rash after fever, rhinorrhea, cough, and a sore throat. On day 5, bilateral bulbar conjunctival injection, rash, palmar erythema, and fever met the four principal Japanese diagnostic criteria for KD. Purulent ocular discharge was accompanied by conjunctival injection, and the rash was scarlatiniform. Rapid antigen tests for group A Streptococcus (GAS) and adenovirus (AdV) were positive. Echocardiography revealed no coronary artery dilatation. The clinical presentation was considered most consistent with concurrent GAS and AdV infections, and amoxicillin was initiated. As incomplete KD remained possible, the patient was reassessed on day 7, 48 h later; all symptoms resolved. C-reactive protein was elevated (5.59 mg/dL), but none of the six supplemental laboratory criteria in the American Heart Association incomplete-KD algorithm were met. As the clinical support for KD decreased, observation was continued, with instructions to return if the principal features recurred. No KD-related symptoms occurred, and a telephone follow-up confirmed a favorable course. Conclusions: In children with multiple principal clinical features of KD and suspected co-infections, KD should not be excluded solely based on positive pathogen tests. Characterizing individual findings, including ocular discharge and rash morphology, and short-interval reassessment of the same findings within the therapeutic window for KD may help manage diagnostic uncertainty.
items.authors: Masafumi Yamada, Etaro Hashimoto, Yoshifumi Yamada, Akihiro Nishi, Tetsuhiro Maeno, Seiji Kawamura

items.title: Pathways Linking Perceived Environmental Attributes of Community Public Spaces and Older Adults’ Mental Well-Being: A Parallel Mediation Analysis of Physical Activity and Social Participation
items.abstract: Against the backdrop of population aging, community public spaces are important neighborhood settings for older adults’ daily activities, social ties, and mental well-being. However, few studies have integrated multidimensional perceived environmental attributes, parallel physical-activity and social-participation pathways, and recent positive mental well-being within a single framework. A cross-sectional survey involved 842 adults aged 60 years or older from 15 communities in Shenyang, China. Perceived environmental attributes comprised Functional Supportiveness, Perceived Restorativeness, and Social Interaction Support, with Neighborhood Outdoor Physical Activity and Community-Based Social Participation specified as parallel mediators and mental well-being assessed using the WHO-5 Well-Being Index. Analyses included confirmatory factor analysis, structural equation modeling, bootstrap tests, and multigroup analysis. All three environmental attributes were significantly and positively associated with both community activities and mental well-being, with significant indirect effects through both activity pathways. Among the three environmental attributes, Perceived Restorativeness showed the strongest associations with Neighborhood Outdoor Physical Activity and mental well-being, whereas Social Interaction Support showed the strongest association with Community-Based Social Participation. Age-group differences were non-monotonic and path-specific, while structural heterogeneity was more pronounced across community types. These findings support age-friendly public-space renewal integrating support for use, restorative experiences, and opportunities for social interaction across age groups and community contexts.
items.authors: Xin He, Jinghua Zhang, Diansheng Li

items.title: Green-Synthesized Silver and Nickel Oxide Nanoparticles as Photostabilizers for PVC Films Under Accelerated UV Irradiation
items.abstract: Poly(vinyl chloride) shows gradual photodegradation by dehydrochlorination and oxidative chain reactions under long-term UV irradiation. Although conventional PVC stabilizers may limit the photodegradation, concerns about toxicity, migration of additives and long-term environmental effects have stimulated the search for new stabilizing solutions. Ag and NiO NPs materials were synthesized utilizing a plant-based green approach and added to PVC/CNNP/GO films at 0.3 and 0.5 wt%. The nanomaterials were characterized using different techniques, such as UV-Vis, FTIR, FESEM, EDX, TEM, and AFM. Accelerated UV-B irradiation assessed photodegradation via carbonyl, polyene, and hydroxyl indices; weight loss; and surface morphology. Nanoparticle-containing films showed less degradation than did blank PVC. The best film, with 0.5 wt% Ag NPs after prolonged irradiation, achieved carbonyl, polyene, and hydroxyl indices of 0.551, 0.545, and 0.591. Weight loss dropped from 2.242% for blank PVC to 1.131% for the Ag-containing film after 300 h, and the NiO NPs improved photostability but provided less protection than did Ag NPs at the same loading. These findings suggest that Ag and NiO NPs might prevent UV-induced PVC breakdown when used as nanomaterial-based photostabilizing additives.
items.authors: Saif Saad Abdulsattar Al-Shaikhli, Khalid Umar, Emad Yousif

items.title: Exploratory Risk Assessment of Cardiovascular Diseases Using Antiphospholipid Antibody-Related Scores in Patients with ANCA-Associated Vasculitis
items.abstract: Background: Antiphospholipid antibodies have been found in patients with antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitis (AAV). This study aimed to evaluate the accuracy of the global antiphospholipid syndrome score (GAPSS) derivatives in predicting cardiovascular diseases in Korean patients with AAV, and to derive a simple candidate index for cardiovascular diseases. Methods: This was a retrospective cohort study including 170 patients with AAV. The adjusted GAPSS (aGAPSS), aGAPSS specific for cardiovascular diseases (aGAPSScvd), and aGAPSS for Korean patients with APS (aGAPSS [KAPS]) were calculated in each patient. The cardiovascular diseases were defined as cerebrovascular accident (CVA) or acute coronary syndrome (ACS). The accuracy of each index was assessed by estimating the area under the curve (AUC). An exploratory multivariable Cox proportional hazards model with a backward elimination method was performed to derive a candidate index. Covariates consisting the aGAPSScvd were included in the model. Results: The AUCs of the aGAPSS, aGAPSScvd, and aGAPSS (KAPS) for CVA were 0.507 (p = 0.926), 0.531 (p = 0.676), and 0.493 (p = 0.923), respectively. The AUCs of the aGAPSS, aGAPSScvd, and aGAPSS (KAPS) for ACS were 0.613 (p = 0.441), 0.752 (p = 0.086), and 0.796 (p = 0.043), respectively. The exploratory multivariable model revealed a candidate index, aGAPSScvd for ACS in Korean patients with AAV (aGAPSScvd [KAAV]) = 2 × lupus anticoagulant (LA) + 2 × obesity. The AUC of the aGAPSScvd (KAAV) in predicting ACS was 0.843 (p = 0.019). Conclusions: The two-item candidate index aGAPSScvd (KAAV), consisting of LA and obesity, showed discriminatory ability for ACS, which warrants further validation in larger studies.
items.authors: Oh Chan Kwon, Yong-Beom Park, Sang-Won Lee

items.title: Integrated Phenotypic and Transcriptomic Analysis of the Effects of a Novel Arylaminoalcohol on Plasmodium falciparum
items.abstract: Malaria remains the leading parasitic infection worldwide, and the effectiveness of antimalarial drugs is increasingly threatened by the emergence of multidrug-resistant Plasmodium falciparum (P. falciparum) strains. In this context, our team previously developed a series of novel aminopyridinemethanol derivatives, among which GBPS336 showed potent nanomolar activity against P. falciparum strains with reduced susceptibility to reference antimalarials. Here, we investigated the effects of GBPS336 on the intraerythrocytic developmental cycle and transcriptional response of the parasite by combining microscopic phenotyping with whole-transcriptome RNA sequencing (Illumina) of synchronized P. falciparum 3D7 cultures exposed or not to the compound. In GBPS336-treated cultures, microscopic analysis revealed reduced parasitaemia, a marked delay and disruption of intraerythrocytic development and morphological alterations indicative of a parasite stress response. Transcriptomic profiling identified 356 differentially expressed genes at H24 post-exposition in ring-stage cultures with enrichment in functional categories associated with erythrocyte invasion and the parasite–host interface. Altogether, these findings demonstrate the antimalarial activity of GBPS336 and highlight invasion-related pathways as a potentially important component of its mechanism of action. Further studies will be required to determine whether these pathways are directly affected and to identify the molecular target(s) underlying the activity of the compound.
items.authors: Yaël Pronnier Lefebvre, Ibtissem Ben Gayed, Aurélien Aubry, Patrice Agnamey, Romain Mustière, Alexandra Dassonville-Klimpt

items.title: Alternative Protein Sources: Nutritional Value, Environmental Sustainability, and Health Impacts
items.abstract: Alternative protein sources are examined as sustainable substitutes for conventional animal-based proteins, driven by global population growth and environmental pressures. This article is a review of original research and review articles published between 2015 and 2026 on major alternative protein sources, using specific keywords related to alternative proteins. It examines plant-based, fungal, insect, algae/microalgae, cultivated meat, and fermentation-derived proteins, focusing on their nutritional value, health effects, environmental sustainability, safety, and regulatory considerations. Evidence indicates that many alternative protein sources provide high-quality proteins, often with added benefits such as fiber and reduced saturated fat. Additionally, most exhibit significantly lower greenhouse gas emissions, land use, and resource demands than livestock production. While challenges remain, such as consumer acceptance, processing efficiency, and regulatory considerations, alternative proteins represent a promising pathway toward a more sustainable, secure, and health-conscious global food system.
items.authors: Gabriela Luta, Florentina Israel-Roming, Daniela Balan, Evelina Gherghina, Aglaia Popa, Mihaela Zugravu

items.title: Electromagnetic Compatibility Design Framework for Wireless Railway Axle-Box Monitoring Systems
items.abstract: Reliable wireless communication is a key requirement for railway axle-box condition monitoring, particularly in electromagnetically harsh environments where electromagnetic interference (EMI) may degrade diagnostic data transmission. This study proposes an Electromagnetic Compatibility Design Framework (EMCDF) for receiver-oriented assessment of electromagnetic exposure, equivalent EMC mitigation, and wireless-link performance. The framework integrates frequency-domain electromagnetic characterization with analytical radio-link, receiver-noise, residual-interference, and communication-performance models, establishing a physically traceable pathway from prescribed electromagnetic exposure to residual receiver-level interference and the resulting communication degradation. Prescribed in-band EMI scenarios and equivalent EMC-mitigation conditions are evaluated using the signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR), theoretical channel capacity, and two proposed normalized electromagnetic robustness metrics based on SINR and theoretical capacity. Under the prescribed analytical scenarios, equivalent in-band EMC attenuation values of 15–20 dB correspond to interference-power reduction factors of approximately 31.6–100. For the adopted 433 MHz radio-link parameters, the model-derived SINR under the severe-EMI scenario decreases from approximately 37.83 dB at 1 km to 17.83 dB at 10 km, while the capacity-based robustness coefficient decreases from approximately 0.474 to 0.299 over the same distance range. The model-based results show that propagation loss and residual EMI influence receiver-level communication performance through physically distinct mechanisms and can therefore be evaluated separately within the proposed framework. The quantitative results represent comparative model-derived estimates rather than experimental validation over the investigated distance range. The proposed EMCDF provides a receiver-oriented analytical methodology for EMC-aware assessment and comparative evaluation of wireless railway condition-monitoring systems.
items.authors: Nuriddin N. Irgashev, Janibek F. Kurbanov, Asliddin Sh. Khurramov

items.title: Neutralizing Activity of Vaccine-Induced Antibodies Against Vaccine-Derived Polioviruses Type 2
items.abstract: Background: Nowadays, poliomyelitis caused by wild polioviruses (PVs) has been virtually eradicated. However, since the removal of the type 2 component from the oral polio vaccine (OPV), immunity to PV2 has declined despite expansion of the use of the inactivated polio vaccine (IPV). Unfortunately, sources of neurovirulent PV2 remain in the world in the form of vaccine-derived poliovirus type 2 (VDPV2) cases and outbreaks and immunodeficient iVDPV2 excretors. Methods: Neutralizing antibodies (nABs) in sera from children with different numbers of IPV/OPV doses were evaluated against VDPV2 strains. Results: A genetic analysis of four VDPV2 strains with varying genetic divergence from Sabin 2 (4.32–17.39%) revealed a number of mutations in antigenic sites. We observed that 6.5–51.8% of undervaccinated (1–2IPV) children did not have nABs against at least one studied VDPV2. Fully vaccinated children showed almost 100% neutralization, although 3.1% vaccinated with 3IPV did not have nABs against three VDPVs; 4.5% vaccinated with 3IPV + 1bOPV and 2.5% vaccinated with 5tOPV did not have nABs against the most divergent iVDPV2 strain. Conclusions: Therefore, some fully vaccinated children may not have detectable levels of protective nABs against VDPV2.
items.authors: Evgenia V. Karpova, Elizaveta V. Yakovchuk, Nikita V. Salichkin, Ekaterina A. Korotkova, Olga Y. Baikova, Svetlana E. Sotskova

items.title: Kernel-Driven Model Correction of Thermal Directionality: Pixel-Level Analysis Using Airborne Multi-Angular Observations
items.abstract: Directional anisotropy (DA) in thermal infrared (TIR) remote sensing introduces significant variability in land surface temperature (LST) retrievals, particularly in high-resolution observations. This study presents the empirical pixel-level modelling of DA, by using multi-angular airborne data from the NETSense campaign over an agricultural area near Grosseto, Italy. Six kernel-driven models (KDMs) are evaluated for their ability to fit directional effects, with the Vinnikov–Roujean–Lagouarde (Vinnikov–RL) model achieving the highest accuracy (RMSE = 1.07 K). At 40 m resolution, modelled directional effects reach median deviations of +1.80 K at the hotspot position, −2.03 K opposite to the Sun, and −1.37 K perpendicular to the solar principal plane, with extremes up to ±6 K, highlighting their operational significance for missions such as LSTM, TRISHNA, and SBG. To improve operational feasibility, two simplified models—adapted RL (RLa) and Vinnikov–RLa—are introduced, leveraging a consistent inverse relationship between hotspot magnitude and width to reduce parameter complexity via a power-law formulation. The analysis reveals that directional effects vary with spatial resolution and are influenced by canopy structure and solar geometry, while biophysical parameters alone are insufficient for coefficient estimation. Validation using an independent flight day confirms the robustness of the simplified models under different acquisition geometries, surface types, and geophysical conditions. A tiered model strategy is proposed for future satellite missions, recommending model selection based on day or night observations and data availability. These findings support the integration of directional correction into operational pipelines, enabling consistent and accurate LST products across platforms, resolutions, and observation conditions.
items.authors: Louis Snyders, Joris Blommaert, Jonathan Leon-Tavares, Mary Langsdale, Lorenzo Genesio

items.title: Quality-by-Design Framework for Evaluating AI-Driven Machine Translation in Regulatory Affairs
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Machine translation increasingly prepares multilingual product information for EU marketing authorisation, yet no established process exists to adapt or validate a system for the Summary of Product Characteristics (SmPC), whose sections differ in regulatory function, terminology, and clinical risk. This work develops such a process and a qualification procedure against the approved human translation. Methods: An EMA-derived ontology divides the SmPC into seven regulatory domains, each with a provisional ICH Q9 risk profile, following Quality-by-Design principles. A No Language Left Behind model was fine-tuned with Low-Rank Adaptation on an eight-language-pair corpus and compared with the pre-trained model using BLEU, chrF, TER and COMET. Quality was validated by a five-layer, human-sign-off pipeline. Results: Fine-tuning improved every metric for every language pair. Quality varied more by domain than by language, hidden by corpus-level scores, and the domains rated highest-risk, under provisional ratings awaiting external calibration, were not the best translated. Checks on language-independent quantities were reliable everywhere; within adverse-reaction sections, the terminology check was the only partial-anchor instrument, and it showed meaningful gains only after a second language-model stage. Conclusions: The fine-tuned model and its validation pipeline, targeting automated checks where reliable and human review elsewhere, form a promising assistive step under qualified sign-off whose suitability for production-scale deployment requires further validation; assessment must be by regulatory domain, not the document as a whole.
items.authors: Darya Filatova, Hocine Kadi, Florian Pereme

items.title: Ponicidin Inhibits NLRP3 Inflammasome Activation via Alleviating Mitochondrial Damage in LPS-Primed Macrophages
items.abstract: The NLRP3 inflammasome is a cytosolic pattern-recognition complex that senses sterile and infectious insults and drives innate immune responses. Herein, we identify ponicidin (PON), a natural diterpenoid isolated from Rabdosia rubescens, as an inhibitor of NLRP3 inflammasome activation. In LPS-primed macrophages, PON suppressed IL-1β secretion by inhibiting caspase-1 activation and attenuated nigericin- or ATP-induced pyroptosis, as indicated by reduced LDH release and GSDMD cleavage. Meanwhile, AIM2 inflammasome-mediated IL-1β production was not affected by PON. Mechanistically, PON inhibited ASC oligomerization and speck formation, critical steps in NLRP3 inflammasome assembly. It could reduce mitochondria-derived danger signals related to NLRP3 activation, such as mtROS, mtDNA and ox-mtDNA, without affecting ion fluxes (e.g., K+, Ca2+, Cl−). Consistently, PON preserved the mitochondrial membrane potential and intracellular ATP levels, indicating comprehensive protection of mitochondrial function. In vivo, PON markedly reduced IL-1β levels in peritoneal lavage fluid of MSU-induced peritonitis mice and lowered serum IL-1β, TNF-α, and MCP-1 levels in endotoxemia mice. Collectively, PON alleviates mitochondrial dysfunction to prevent ASC oligomerization and NLRP3 inflammasome assembly, thereby reducing the cleavage of pro-IL-1β and GSDMD. Our findings suggest that PON may be a potential candidate for treating NLRP3 inflammasomopathies.
items.authors: Congyu Wu, Yuan Kang, Yu Liu, Xin Huang, Muqing Wang, Min Cai

items.title: FPGA-Based Cascade Control of a Piston-Type Wave Maker with Height Feedback
items.abstract: The traditional control approach for piston-type wave makers is reduced to a piston position tracking problem based on open-loop wave-maker theory; however, due to hydrodynamic loading, nonlinear effects, and propagation delays, the target wave condition at the measurement section cannot be guaranteed. This experimental study involves controllers tuned offline through numerical simulations and validated in real time on a 24 m wave channel. The novelty of this work is a two-layer field-programmable gate array (FPGA) cascade that regulates the measured wave height in closed loop, not just the piston position. In the inner layer, the hydraulic servo cylinder position is controlled within a 1 ms cycle using a proportional–integral (PI) or a Takagi–Sugeno (T–S) fuzzy controller; the outer layer, in a 20 ms cycle, updates the position reference via real-time wave height feedback. Controller parameters were tuned using three meta-heuristic algorithms under the integral of time-weighted absolute error criterion, and a similarity-based rule reduction reduced the T–S consequent parameters from 27 to 9, yielding 66.7% and 62.5% reductions in FPGA execution time and digital signal processing slice usage with tracking-error changes of only 2.2–2.3%. Experiments confirm high-accuracy position tracking and steady-state wave height regulation, verified by fast Fourier transform analysis.
items.authors: Batın Demircan, Tuğçe Tepebaşi, Sabri Biçakçi, Ersin Akyüz

items.title: FBS26: An Entropy-Based Metric for Assessing Architectural Maturity of UML Class Diagrams
items.abstract: Entropy-based metrics can provide a quantitative representation of the information content of UML models, but their practical usefulness depends on a systematic and reproducible calibration of the parameters used to construct the underlying probability distribution. This paper presents FBS26, an extension of the FBS metric that introduces calibrated weights for UML element kinds while retaining the normalized Shannon entropy formulation. The proposed calibration procedure combines three criteria: avoiding false lack-of-information cases, reducing non-monotonic behavior of the metric, and achieving a pronounced decrease in the metric for balanced diagram series. The criteria are applied according to a predefined lexicographic priority. The approach is evaluated using a controlled series of UML class diagrams and 123 UML class diagrams from four industrial software projects, selected from a repository containing more than 2000 UML diagrams from 18 projects. Architectural maturity labels, assigned independently by an experienced software architect, serve as reference data for examining empirical thresholds for structural information. The results show that systematic weight calibration removes the undesirable behavior observed for the considered FBS16 configurations and provides a more stable basis for comparing UML class diagrams. The industrial analysis further indicates differences in the structural entropy ranges of commonly distinguished diagram categories. FBS26, therefore, provides a quantitative information-content measure that can support expert-based assessment of the architectural maturity of UML class diagrams.
items.authors: Wiktor Bohdan Daszczuk, Stanisław Jerzy Niepostyn

items.title: Energy Decay Rate for a Porous-Elastic System with Fractional Infinite Memory
items.abstract: In this paper, we study the energy decay rate for a porous-elastic system with fractional infinite memory, which acts on the material displacement equation. Using the frequency domain method, we show that the energy decay rate of the system depends on the order θ of the fractional operator and the wave speeds μρ and δJ, where θ∈[0,1]. Specifically, the energy of the system decays exponentially when θ=1 and μρ=δJ. The energy of the system decays polynomially when θ∈[0,1) and μρ=δJ or θ∈[0,1] and μρ≠δJ. In addition, we also show that the polynomial decay rates obtained are optimal in some sense.
items.authors: Hualei Zhang

items.title: Assessing Mental Health Without Relying on Psychiatric Data
items.abstract: Approximately one in seven people worldwide is affected by a mental disorder, making early identification crucial for preventing symptom progression and chronicity. However, diagnosis remains challenging, with discrepancies between referring physicians’ initial assessments and specialist psychiatric diagnoses reported in approximately half of cases. In recent years, machine learning has shown promising results in mental health assessment, with supervised techniques such as decision trees, random forests, and support vector machines among the most widely used approaches. However, these methods require large and representative datasets to capture the substantial heterogeneity of mental disorders, which can be difficult to obtain due to stigma, disease severity, and limited access to mental healthcare. This work investigates the feasibility of identifying mental disorders using data exclusively from a non-psychiatric population. The underlying hypothesis is that this population exhibits greater homogeneity and can therefore be characterized using a variational autoencoder with a Gaussian latent space. The proposed approach uses reconstruction errors from the non-psychiatric training population as a reference, with substantially higher errors in new observations indicating a potential mental disorder. Results show that the proposed VAE achieves performance comparable to that of the three aforementioned supervised techniques in the two dataset used. For the first dataset, the accuracy, sensitivity, specificity and ROC-AUC of the VAE were 0.88, 0.90, 0.85 and 0.95. These performance measures were 0.83, 0.86, 0.80, and 0.88 for decision trees; 0.88, 0.91, 0.85 and 0.94 for random forest; and 0.88, 0.91, 0.85 and 0.95 for support vector machines. Similar results were obtained for the second dataset. Moreover, the progressive increase in reconstruction errors across populations may reflect greater deviations from the patterns observed in the non-psychiatric population in groups with greater clinical complexity, supporting its potential use as a screening tool.

items.title: Human Milk Oligosaccharides in Sports Nutrition: Biological Rationale and Current Evidence
items.abstract: Established sports-nutrition strategies support fueling, hydration, and muscle protein turnover, but strenuous exercise also challenges gastrointestinal, microbial, immune, metabolic, and musculoskeletal homeostasis. Human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs) are structurally diverse bioactive glycans that can selectively influence gut microbial composition, microbial metabolism, intestinal barrier integrity, and immune function. These properties provide a biological rationale for investigating HMOs in exercise and sports nutrition. This review critically evaluates direct and supportive evidence linking the biological functions of HMOs to exercise physiology. Human evidence is limited to two small trials. One examined supplementation alongside dietary restriction and increased physical activity, limiting conclusions about exercise adaptation; the other found no additional gains in muscle mass, strength, or anaerobic performance during resistance training. Alongside the emerging exercise-related findings, the established effects of HMOs on the gut microbiota and intestinal barrier also suggest a potential role in reducing exercise-associated gastrointestinal disturbances. However, benefits for these disturbances or post-exercise recovery have not been established. HMOs remain candidates for complementing established sports-nutrition strategies, but current evidence is insufficient to recommend supplementation for athletes. Future studies should determine how HMO structure, dose, formulation, and host characteristics influence gastrointestinal resilience, musculoskeletal adaptation, and functional outcomes in physically active populations. Establishing these relationships will be essential for translating HMOs into evidence-based sports-nutrition applications.
items.authors: Ke Hu, Kaimeng Zhang, Chenxi Huang, Zhaoguan Wang, Xuanxuan Huang, Yin Li

items.title: Pathogen-Specific Temporal Coupling Between Outpatient Influenza-like Illness and Hospitalized Severe Acute Respiratory Infection Positivity in China: A National Sentinel Surveillance Time-Series Study
items.abstract: Outpatient influenza-like illness (ILI) and hospitalized severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) surveillance measure respiratory-pathogen activity in distinct clinical settings. We analyzed 95 epidemiological weeks (2024-W46 to 2026-W36) of national China CDC positivity data for ten respiratory viruses and Mycoplasma pneumoniae. For each pathogen, weekly change in SARI positivity was regressed on ILI changes at lags 1–4, with adjustment for four SARI autoregressive lags and annual seasonality. Inference used Newey–West covariance, joint lag tests, and Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction; reverse-direction, specification, recursive block-bootstrap, prewhitened cross-correlation, rolling-coefficient, and rolling-origin forecast analyses were secondary. Asymptotic forward lag blocks were FDR-significant for ten pathogens, whereas recursive block-bootstrap inference supported six: influenza virus, respiratory syncytial virus, human metapneumovirus, parainfluenza virus, common human coronavirus, and rhinovirus. No augmented model showed FDR-significant evidence of improved forecast error at 1-, 2-, or 4-week horizons; with only 35–38 forecast origins, modest incremental value could not be excluded. National ILI and SARI positivity series showed pathogen-specific temporal coupling, but this 95-week record did not establish fixed lead times or incremental prospective forecasting value in this dataset.
items.authors: Qiong Chen, Shanshan Tong, Jun Gao, Sufang Xu

items.title: Vehicle–Drone Routing Problem with Heterogeneous Time-Sensitive Tasks and en Route Synchronization: A Hybrid Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search
items.abstract: Vehicle–drone cooperative systems leverage the ground transport capacity of vehicles and the aerial mobility of drones to markedly boost operational efficiency in time-sensitive missions. However, existing studies generally rely on predefined launch and recovery locations and provide limited consideration of how heterogeneous task requirements and time-dependent values interact with vehicle–drone synchronization. This paper focuses on the vehicle–drone cooperative routing problem that integrates heterogeneous tasks, time-varying rewards, and en route launch–recovery synchronization. Tasks fall into three categories by platform compatibility, with their rewards following distinct time-decay functions that decrease as completion is delayed. Vehicles travel along ground routes, while drones can be launched from and recovered by moving vehicles. To maximize the total system reward, we formulate the problem as a mixed-integer nonlinear programming model. We develop a hybrid adaptive large neighborhood search (HALNS). Computational experiments compare HALNS with benchmark algorithms and examine the effects of key operational parameters. The results show that HALNS consistently achieves higher total rewards across the tested instances and highlight the benefits of flexible en route synchronization in improving temporal coordination, facilitating timely task completion, and mitigating delay-induced reward loss. Sensitivity analyses further reveal how drone endurance, battery replacement time, and travel speed affect system performance.
items.authors: Qipeng Xu, Mengmeng Zhang, Honghui Chen

items.title: A High-Resolution FPGA-Based Time-to-Amplitude Converter (TAC) with Integrated Pulse-Width-Based Walk Error Compensation: Design and Experimental LiDAR Validation
items.abstract: LiDAR is a key sensor for depth perception in applications ranging from autonomous vehicles and industrial robotics to robotic vacuum cleaners and topographic mapping, with its depth resolution determined by the timing electronics. This article, to the best of our knowledge, presents the first implementation of an FPGA-based time-to-amplitude converter (TAC) in a LiDAR system alongside the first integration of walk error compensation into such an architecture. The threshold-crossing time shifts with the echo amplitude, causing walk error. This walk error can reach tens of centimeters depending on target reflectivity and range. Pulse-width-based correction has been demonstrated, but reported implementations obtain the time-of-flight (ToF) and the pulse width with time-to-digital converters (TDCs), whose high resolution relies on high-speed clocks for coarse time and delay lines for fine-time measurements, which suffer from coarse-count ambiguity, bin calibration requirements, sensitivity to process, voltage, and temperature (PVT) variations, and portability limitations. This article enhances the novel FPGA-based TAC previously introduced by the authors for pulse-width-based walk error compensation without using a clock or a delay line. Each ToF channel requires only one D flip-flop in the FPGA and a low-cost external passive circuit coupled to the multichannel analog-to-digital converter (ADC) of the FPGA. Using our FPGA-based TAC in our LiDAR experimental setup, the walk-induced distance error is successfully reduced from 42 cm to 2 cm, and target distances of up to 3 m are measured within a 2 cm maximum error.
items.authors: Azad Ozan Korkan, Heba Yuksel

items.title: Multi-Source Deep-Learning Reconstruction of Monthly Arctic Sea Ice Thickness Constrained by Satellite and In Situ Observations
items.abstract: Monthly Arctic sea ice thickness (SIT) fields are needed for sea ice volume estimation and climate diagnostics, but continuous reconstruction remains challenging because in situ observations are sparse and satellite retrievals are uncertain. We present ArcticSIT-ReconNet, a multi-source deep-learning framework that combines ERA5 and OSI SAF environmental predictors, a U-Net gridded branch, a GraphSAGE buoy-topology branch, sparse Ice Mass Balance Buoy (IMB) constraints, and CryoSat-2 monthly supervision; CryoSat-2 is not used as a predictor input. For the held-out 2023–2024 winter test period, the model achieved an RMSE of 0.442 m against the CryoSat-2 reference field. Independent evaluation against ICESat-2 yielded an RMSE of 0.650 m, compared with 0.667 m for a matched No-IMB control, supporting a modest contribution from sparse in situ constraints. Regional diagnostics indicate that reconstruction errors are largest in complex coastal and thick-ice regimes. The reconstructed record also captures a coherent winter thickening cycle and modest interannual variability in basin-mean SIT. ArcticSIT-ReconNet therefore provides a multi-source framework for basin-scale Arctic SIT reconstruction and variability analysis.
items.authors: Yuhao Zhang, Bingrui Li, Guangyu Zuo, Yinke Dou, Chunyan Ma
