items.title: Genomic Amplification and Ovary-Specific Expression of Zona Pellucida Genes in Channel Catfish and Blue Catfish
items.abstract: Channel catfish (Ictalurus punctatus) is the most important aquaculture species in the United States, with the interspecific hybrid made from mating female channel catfish with male blue catfish (I. furcatus) being the predominant genotype for the catfish industry. While studying the mechanisms of their reproductive isolation, we determined zona pellucida (ZP) genes in both species. While ZP genes are well known for their ovary-specific expression in higher vertebrates such as mammals, the site of their expression in fish varies depending on species. In this study, we annotated the ZP genes in channel catfish and blue catfish and conducted phylogenetic analysis. We found that ZP genes are highly amplified in the catfish genomes, with ZP3- and ZP4-like genes being the most abundant in the genomes, derived from tandem and segmental duplications. A total of 39 and 49 ZP genes (including 4 and 5 pseudogenes) in the blue catfish genome and channel catfish genome were identified, respectively. Expression analysis using RNA-Seq revealed ovary-specific expression in females, with no expression in the gonadal tissues of males, nor in any other tissues of either males or females. RT-PCR analysis indicated that the ZP genes were not expressed until 90 days post fertilization, consistent with the timing of oogenesis of the developing gonad. Single-nucleus RNA-seq (snRNA-Seq) confirmed expression of ZP genes only in oocytes. Future studies are warranted to determine the molecular mechanisms of sex-, tissue-, and time-specific expression of ZP genes, especially in relation to various taxa within teleost fish.
items.authors: Tong Chen, Dongya Gao, Baofeng Su, Rex Dunham, Zhanjiang Liu

items.title: Foundations of Recursive Interval Algebras
items.abstract: Recursive interval algebras are built from \(R = \mathbb{Z}[\Omega^{-1}]\), where \(\Omega gt; 1\) is an integer, by repeated formation of ordered pairs. The component operations \(\operatorname{pos}\) and \(\operatorname{len}\) define arithmetic between arbitrary finite depths by descent to scalars. The finite levels realize commutative algebras with square-zero generators, and their path coordinates connect algebraic structure with a recursively weighted norm. A sharp one-level multiplication estimate yields exact constants for prescribed, possibly unequal, depths, with all equality cases and their attainability over the original coefficient ring. Both tensor orientations have fixed-block norm factorization and an exact criterion for mixed-depth inner-product factorization. Integral exponential and logarithmic operations determine normalized consecutive-block decompositions of units. Recursive derivative evaluation characterizes coefficient-ring preservation and gives sharp bounds on homogeneous inputs. Across unrestricted finite depths, local boundedness on a fixed-scalar fiber holds exactly when all derivative data of order at least two vanish. Degree scaling makes products contractive precisely on a Euclidean parameter ball, and outside that ball no finite depth-independent bound exists. Tensor concatenation further gives sharp commutator and Jordan associator estimates, including block-length-dependent constants and arithmetic conditions for attaining their endpoints.
items.authors: Lei Zhou

items.title: diffct: Differentiable CT Operators from Circular Orbits to Arbitrary Trajectories
items.abstract: diffct implements computed-tomography projection and reconstruction in PyTorch using Numba CUDA kernels. Its native forward model integrates a cell-constant attenuation field along rays defined by per-view acquisition geometry; the backprojector is the matched discrete adjoint. The same model supports parallel, fan and cone beams, non-circular trajectories, and parameterized detector surfaces. This report describes the implementation through release 2.2.1: the geometry and sampling conventions, Siddon traversal, data and first-order geometry derivatives, differentiable analytical FBP/FDK, and execution on one or several GPUs. We derive the ownership and reduction rules for distributed view and spatial partitions and explain how spatial, view and detector blocks extend native operations to CPU-backed and disk-backed data. Experiments include measured walnut cone-beam data, synthetic reconstruction and calibration, and a recorded 512³ scaling benchmark. On A100-SXM-64GB GPUs, eight GPUs on two nodes reduce forward projection from 493.05 to 73.18 ms and the amortized cost of a ten-step CGLS solve from 2054.36 to 373.38 ms per iteration. Analytical gathers have their own discrete transposes; differentiability does not make FDK an exact inverse. We distinguish numerical correctness, reconstruction quality and execution cost, and state the limits of each experiment.
items.authors: Yipeng Sun, Linda-Sophie Schneider, Chengze Ye, Andreas Maier

items.title: Trusted HAP Relaying for Decoy-State Finite-Key QKD in Satellite–Ground Networks: Channel Modeling, Security, and Availability
items.abstract: Useful quantum-key supply from intermittent satellite contacts depends on finite-block security, authentication, relay inventories, and application demand, not optical transmittance alone. We simulate a trusted high-altitude-platform (HAP) relay between a ground station and a 500 km low-Earth-orbit satellite using three-intensity decoy-state BB84, finite-key estimation, authenticated key inventories, and a 200-pass service model. The comparator is the satellite-to-ground (S→G) downlink; a groundto-satellite uplink is not simulated, so the margins apply only to this downlink. With a 0.20 m HAP receive radius, the relay yields 13.175 Mbit/pass, 15.65% of the 84.185 Mbit/pass direct yield. With a 0.50 m HAP radius, the relay yield rises to 116.981 Mbit/pass, 38.77% above the 84.298 Mbit/pass direct yield. The unchanged direct-link estimates vary by under 0.2% from independent Monte Carlo sampling. The advantage remains 29.57% under a common contact window and 28.42% with equal elevation masks. Protocol tuning raises the 0.20 m relay yield by 36.74% without closing its gap to the direct link. For workloads derived from the 0.20 m relay supply, a 30 Mbit buffer produced no starved schedules for the 0.50 m relay in 10,000 simulations per demand. Receive-aperture collection is the main modeled condition for relay advantage under the stated assumptions.
items.authors: Hasan Abbas Al-Mohammed, Elias Yaacoub

items.title: Maternal Micronutrient Deficiency, DNA Methylation, and Fetal Neurodevelopment in Low-Resource Settings: A Secondary Analysis of Growth-Associated EWAS Signatures
items.abstract: Maternal undernutrition is common in urban slums and other low-resource settings, where both low birthweight and childhood stunting have been associated with poorer brain development. One proposed explanation is epigenetic: a shortage of folate and related nutrients lowers the methyl-group supply during the period when the fetal brain is being programmed, altering DNA methylation. This is hard to test directly, because no epigenome-wide association study (EWAS) has yet measured neurodevelopmental outcomes in these populations. We therefore re-annotated published methylation signals for two nutrition-sensitive growth phenotypes: neonatal birthweight from the PACE consortium meta-analysis (914 CpG sites, 729 genes) and child height at the SOCS3 gene in low- and middle-income cohorts. The birthweight genes were sorted into functional categories, compared with three studies of methylation in undernourished children, and annotated against fetal-brain and placental chromatin states and fetal-brain expression. We found no enrichment for one-carbon metabolism; DNMT3A was the only related gene present, and the core folate-cycle enzymes were absent. Neurodevelopmental and synaptic genes made up a sizeable fraction of the signature (92 genes, 12.6%), but this reflects the composition of the gene set rather than a tested over-representation, and the fetal-brain enhancer enrichment we observed applied to the whole birthweight signal, not to these genes in particular, and was not specific to fetal brain. The most consistent finding was SOCS3, a nutrition-responsive locus that recurred across independent undernutrition datasets, altered its expression with methylation in vitro, and is expressed in the prenatal brain. Overall, the data support a nutrition-sensitive methylation signature at growth and immune loci that overlaps enhancers in fetal brain as in other tissues, with SOCS3 as a candidate link to neurodevelopment. The one-carbon-to-neurodevelopment pathway remains plausible but hypothesis-generating, and testing it will need formal enrichment analysis and primary methylation studies where undernutrition is most common.
items.authors: Pranav Manne

items.title: Synthesis of Functionalized Zein-Resveratrol Through Free Radical Grafting: Antioxidant Activity and em In Vitro /em Gastrointestinal Stability
items.abstract: Resveratrol is a phenolic compound with recognized antioxidant activity; however, its application is limited by its low stability and poor gastrointestinal bioavailability. This study investigated the functionalization of zein with resveratrol through a free radical-mediated grafting reaction using an ascorbic acid/hydrogen peroxide redox system and evaluated the effect of dialysis on the resulting conjugates. The materials were characterized by UV–Vis, FTIR, XPS, XRD, SEM, DSC, and TGA. Protein and total phenolic contents were determined using the Bradford and Folin–Ciocalteu assays, antioxidant activity was evaluated by ABTS and DPPH, and stability was assessed under simulated gastrointestinal digestion. Spectroscopic, structural, morphological, and thermal analyses indicated modifications in the zein matrix after functionalization, with dialysis producing a more homogeneous surface morphology. The functionalized materials exhibited significantly higher antioxidant activity than native zein, reaching ABTS and DPPH inhibition values of 87–93% and 84–86%, respectively, comparable to free resveratrol. During simulated gastrointestinal digestion, the conjugates maintained resveratrol contents between 885.9 and 1115.0 μmol GAE/g, although significant time-dependent variations were detected within each treatment (p lt; 0.05). Overall, free radical-mediated functionalization provided zein–resveratrol conjugates with improved physicochemical stability while preserving the antioxidant properties of resveratrol, supporting their potential application as protein-based delivery systems for phenolic bioactive compounds.
items.authors: Maria Fernanda Valenzuela-Lara, José Agustín Tapia-Hernández, Maribel Plascencia-Jatomea, María Jesús Moreno-Vásquez, Elizabeth Carvajal-Millan, Francisco Rodríguez-Félix

items.title: Agentic Influence Operations: A Multi-Dimensional Governance Framework for Generative AI-Enabled Information Disorder in Multimedia Ecosystems
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), synthetic media, social bots, and agentic AI are turning information disorder from a content-verification problem into a governance problem for multimedia information ecosystems. Research on fake news, deepfakes, GenAI misuse, and cyber-enabled influence has developed in largely separate streams, and none of these streams offers an integrated governance model for influence activity coordinated through AI-supported workflows. This study develops such a model through a structured evidence synthesis of 35 peer-reviewed sources published between 2019 and 2026, identified through four structured discovery queries and citation chaining and appraised with evidence-type-specific criteria. The synthesis identifies five mechanisms through which AI reshapes information disorder: influence orchestration, ambiguity production, selective persuasion, hybrid human–machine dissemination, and a trust paradox in countermeasures. On this basis, the study defines agentic influence operations as workflow-level risks and organizes them in a twelve-dimension framework that links AI capabilities, content modality, platform infrastructure, data access, evidentiary trust, organizational harm, and governance control points. It also sets out construct boundary conditions, five propositions with explicit evidence status, a managerial control set, and a phased implementation roadmap. Only the proposition on synthetic media and uncertainty about authentic evidence has direct empirical support; the others are offered for testing through simulation, experimental, design-science, and expert-validation studies.
items.authors: Elyson De La Cruz, Ruthvik Yedla, Dexter Francis, Rishikesh Sahay, Md Rasel Al Mamun, Karthik Meduri

items.title: Sexual Risk Compensation Among at-Risk Young People Receiving Pharmacy-Delivered HIV Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis in Nigeria: A Prospective Study
items.abstract: Background Concerns regarding risk compensation following initiation of oral HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) remain an important consideration in HIV prevention programmes. However, evidence on behavioural changes following PrEP initiation within pharmacy-delivered models particularly among adolescents and young adults. in sub-Saharan Africa remains limited. This study evaluated short-term changes in sexual risk behaviours among young adults receiving pharmacy-delivered oral PrEP in Nigeria. Methods We conducted a prospective implementation study among young adults aged 18–24 years initiating oral PrEP through two community pharmacies in Abuja, Nigeria. Participants completed behavioural assessments at baseline and one month following PrEP initiation. Risk compensation behaviours assessed included condomless sex, transactional sex, sex under the influence of alcohol or drugs, sexually transmitted infection (STI) diagnosis, and number of sexual partners. Paired behaviour changes between baseline and Month 1 were assessed using McNemar’s test for categorical variables and Wilcoxon signed-rank test for continuous variables. Firth penalized logistic regression guided by the Health Belief Model evaluated predictors of increased sexual risk behaviours following PrEP initiation. Results Among 197 participants initiating PrEP, 90 completed paired behavioural assessments at Month 1. Median age was 24 years (IQR: 22–24), 71% were female, and 93% were single. No significant increase in sexual risk behaviours was observed following PrEP initiation. Condomless sex remained stable between baseline and Month 1 (21.2% vs 19.0%; p = 1.000), while transactional sex (41.1% vs 32.2%; p = 0.080) and sex under the influence of alcohol or drugs (51.1% vs 42.2%; p = 0.170) did not significantly increase. STI diagnosis significantly decreased from 37.8% at baseline to 11.1% at Month 1 (p lt; 0.001), and the distribution of partner numbers shifted downwards significantly from baseline to Month 1 (median 2 [IQR: 1–4.75] vs 2 [IQR: 1–3]; p = 0.011). In Health Belief Model-based regression analyses, High perceived HIV risk was significantly associated with lower odds of increased transactional sex following PrEP initiation (OR = 0.13; 95% CI: 0.01–0.85; p = 0.034). Conclusion This study found no evidence of substantial short-term risk compensation following initiation of pharmacy-delivered oral PrEP among young adults in Nigeria. Sexual risk behaviours remained stable or decreased after PrEP initiation, suggesting that pharmacy-delivered PrEP can be implemented without significant behavioural risk escalation in this population. Larger longitudinal studies are needed to evaluate longer-term behavioural outcomes.
items.authors: Theodora C. Omenoba, Adokiye Mokwenye, Ifeanyi Ume, Angus N. Oli, Chimezie Anyakora, Obinna I. Ekwunife

items.title: Equilateral Sets in ℓₚⁿ Beyond n + 1: Linear Excess and Dimension Cost
items.abstract: How many equilateral points can ℓₚⁿ contain beyond n + 1? For every fixed real p gt; 4, we construct equilateral sets for which the number of points beyond n + 1 grows at least linearly with n. For every fixed dimension, we prove that the maximum is n + 1 at all sufficiently large finite p, with an explicit threshold. The least dimension admitting any fixed number of extra points is p¹⁺ᵒ⁽¹⁾ as p → ∞. The constructions and finite bounds are formalised in Lean. Thus p = 4 marks the boundary: n + 1 is exact in every dimension for 2 ≤ p ≤ 4, while at every fixed finite p gt; 4 the excess grows at least linearly with dimension.
items.authors: Logan R. Chalmers, Aran S. Ziegler

items.title: Multi-Frame Reconstruction via Clutter Filtering for Computational Contrast-Enhanced Ultrasound Microflow Imaging
items.abstract: Objective: Existing computational reconstruction methods for plane-wave ultrasound imaging (PWI) often neglect the interference of strong tissue signals with weak flow-related scattering signals in microflow imaging. This study aims to develop a multi-frame computational ultrasound reconstruction technique that integrates multi-frame sparse constraints with RF signal preprocessing strategies to facilitate the suppression of tissue signals and background noise. Methods: We propose multi-frame reconstruction of contrast-enhanced ultrasound microflow imaging. First, to prevent tissue signals from diluting the sparsity of multi-frame data, we apply singular value decomposition directly to the raw radio-frequency data, attenuating tissue-dominated components before beamforming. This yields sparser data and increases the relative contribution of flow-related components in the optimization. Results: The method was evaluated in contrast-enhanced microflow simulations and an exploratory in vivo experiment involving one rabbit. Under the tested conditions, VrUSi reduced background signals and produced narrower apparent intensity profiles than delay-and-sum and single-frame computational reconstruction. In the single-rabbit experiment, VrUSi yielded higher image-domain BCR values and smaller apparent-profile FWHM values across the analyzed temporal windows. These metrics are interpreted as background suppression and apparent profile compactness under the tested conditions, rather than as evidence of improved physical contrast or spatial resolution. The findings support feasibility only for visualizing flow-related structures in the tested rabbit lower-limb acquisition.
items.authors: Dongdong Liang, Daichao Chen, Xiaoyu Qian, Yuantong Zhong, Yu Xia, Jue Zhang

items.title: First Detection of Hemotropic Mycoplasma sp. in Cetaceans of European Waters
items.abstract: Mycoplasma spp. are wall-less bacteria classified as hemotropic (hemoplasmas) and non-hemotropic that can cause disease and death in immunosuppressed hosts. While hemoplasmas have been described in cetaceans of the Americas, their presence in cetaceans of Europe remains unknown. In this study, we surveyed hemoplasma in cetaceans stranded in Cantabria (n = 20) and the Valencian Community (n = 48), Spain. Specifically, we used real-time PCR to test spleen and lung samples from 68 cetaceans of the families Delphinidae (n = 60), Phocoenidae (n = 4), Kogiidae (n = 3), and Ziphiidae (n = 1). Overall, 11.8% (8/68) were Mycoplasma-positive, all striped dolphins (Stenella coeruleoalba) of the Valencian Community. Two nucleotide sequence type (STs) were detected; one was identical to a hemoplasma from a short-beaked common dolphin (Delphinus delphis) from Brazil, and the other showed 96.1% nucleotide identity with hemoplasma previously found in Bolivian river dolphins (Inia boliviensis), raccoons (Procyon lotor), and Candidatus Mycoplasma haemolamae of llamas (Lama glama) and alpacas (Vicugna pacos). Our findings broaden the known geographic range of hemoplasma in cetaceans, reporting for the first time its presence in dolphins in Europe. The health impacts of the detected hemoplasmas in cetaceans are still unknown.
items.authors: Carlos Sacristán, Alba Pereira, Ignacio Vargas-Castro, José Ángel Barasona, José Luis Crespo-Picazo, Daniel García-Párraga

items.title: A Perspective on Advanced Wood Manufacturing: A Decision-Centric Framework for Future Research and Education
items.abstract: For over a century, wood manufacturing has been organized around understanding the material and process and optimizing the product. It established a globally successful industry and enabled efficient production of traditional and engineered wood products. This manufacturing practice is now being challenged by the complexity of resource variability, product diversification, mass customization, and rapid technology integration. This perspective proposes Advanced Wood Manufacturing as a decision-centric smart manufacturing ecosystem that integrates Resource Intelligence, Manufacturing Intelligence, Product Intelligence, and System Intelligence through a unifying Decision Intelligence framework to convert variability into high-value manufacturing decisions. We argue that natural resource variability, while requiring control where necessary for reliable production, can also provide decision-relevant information for adaptive manufacturing and value creation. The product space of wood manufacturing extends far beyond lumber and panels into emerging functional products for energy storage, flexible electronics, and biomedical applications, enabled by artificial intelligence, sensing and digitalization, robotics, computational design, and additive manufacturing. Sustainability, resilience, and human-centricity are positioned not as peripheral considerations but as foundational design principles embedded in manufacturing system architecture. This perspective offers a vision for future research and education and proposes that the field’s next generation of value will come from integration across resource, process, product, and system intelligence rather than from further optimization within existing boundaries.

items.title: An Indirect Organogenesis-Based Citrus Transformation System Monitored Using Visible Reporter Markers
items.abstract: Genetic transformation of citrus is essential for functional genomics and trait improvement, yet remains limited by prolonged regeneration cycles, genotype-dependent responses, and inefficient screening of transformed tissues. Here, we established an Agrobacterium-mediated indirect organogenesis-based transformation system for Carrizo citrange and evaluated two visible reporter systems, the anthocyanin regulator ROSEA1 and the betalain biosynthetic cassette RUBY, for monitoring transformed tissues throughout regeneration. The regeneration protocol enabled visible callus initiation within 7 days following a 5-day pre-culture treatment and recovery of PCR-confirmed transgenic plantlets within 5 months. Both visible reporters were compatible with callus development and shoot regeneration throughout the indirect organogenesis workflow. During callus proliferation, visible pigmentation closely corresponded with GFP fluorescence, enabling rapid, non-destructive identification of transformed tissues. However, reporter performance diverged during shoot regeneration: RUBY maintained stable pigmentation throughout regeneration, whereas ROSEA1-associated pigmentation progressively declined despite continued GFP fluorescence. Consequently, RUBY showed an approximately 4.7-fold higher pigment-positive shoot fraction than ROSEA1 at week 17, and the RUBY-positive fraction was similar to the GFP-positive fraction in the same treatment. Putative transgenic events were confirmed by PCR in independent lines of both constructs, together with GFP fluorescence in leaves and root tips. Together, these findings describe a practical indirect organogenesis-based transformation platform for citrus and demonstrate that both ROSEA1 and RUBY are effective visual reporters during callus proliferation, whereas RUBY provides more reliable visual identification during shoot regeneration. RUBY is therefore recommended as the visible reporter of choice for citrus transformation extending beyond the callus stage. The workflow was established in Carrizo citrange, among the most readily transformed citrus genotypes, and extension to other varieties remains to be demonstrated.
items.authors: Sameena Ejaz Tanwir, Tao Jiang, Anandi Karn, Carlos D. Messina, Heqiang Huo

items.title: Population Pharmacokinetics of Amikacin and Monte Carlo Simulation Study in Critically Ill Septic Patients Undergoing Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy with CytoSorb® or oXiris®
items.abstract: Background: Adsorptive devices, including CytoSorb® and oXiris®, are increasingly added to continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) in septic patients, but their effect on amikacin clearance and exposure is unknown. We characterized amikacin pharmacokinetics (PK) during adsorptive CRRT and derived dosing implications. Methods: A population PK model was developed in 24 critically ill septic patients (using NONMEM ver. 7.5.0), separating intrinsic clearance (CL_int) from filter-specific extracorporeal clearance (CL_CRRT). Sparse pre-filter sampling was handled using informative priors for distribution parameters. Robustness was assessed by sampling-importance-resampling (SIR) and prediction-corrected visual predictive checks (pcVPC). Monte Carlo simulations (9000 subjects) evaluated probability of target attainment (PTA; Cmax/MIC ≥ 8, AUC24/MIC ≥ 75) and cumulative fraction of response (CFR) against four Gram-negative pathogens across three regimens (500 mg q8h, 500 mg q24h, 1500 mg q24h), two filters, and three connection times. Results: While connected, the CytoSorb® and oXiris® CRRT configurations increased amikacin clearance by 61% and 93%, respectively, accounting for 38–48% of total clearance (CL_TOT). Because these devices were only applied for 10–14 h per 24 h interval in simulated scenarios, there were only minor differences in target attainment. Hence, dosing regimen, not device type or connection timing, dominated. Only amikacin at 1500 mg once daily achieved CFR ≥ 90%, and only for susceptible Enterobacterales. Conclusions: Adsorptive CRRT configurations substantially increase extracorporeal amikacin clearance. These exploratory findings support high-dose, once-daily, concentration-guided amikacin dosing during adsorptive CRRT, although this dose may be insufficient against pathogens with elevated MICs.
items.authors: Nikolina Špirić, Peđa Kovačević, Tijana Kovačević, Danica Momčićević, Saša Dragić, Biljana Zlojutro

items.title: MobiTrust: Risk-Bounded Adaptive Split Inference Under Mobility, Privacy Leakage, and Latent-Space Attacks
items.abstract: Split inference lets a mobile device run the first layers of a neural network locally and hand the intermediate representation to an edge server, trading raw data disclosure for communication and offloaded computation. The common assumption that keeping raw inputs on the device is enough for privacy does not survive contact with modern attacks: intermediate activations can be inverted back to inputs, tested for membership, or probed for sensitive attributes, and they can be tampered with in transit. These risks are not fixed properties of a network; they shift with the split point, with any protection applied to the representation, with the trust placed in the serving edge, and with the sensitive attributes at stake in a given context. Schedulers that pick a split to minimise latency or energy, or that fold risk into a single weighted objective, routinely cross privacy and integrity limits whenever the network briefly makes offloading attractive. We present MobiTrust, an adaptive split-inference controller that treats privacy and latent-integrity risk as explicit constraints on measured risk scores rather than terms to be traded away. Two measurable quantities drive it: Context-Dependent Semantic Exposure (CDSE), a worst-channel estimate of privacy leakage (assembled from reconstruction, shadow-model membership, and attribute attacks) that accounts for the sensitive attributes a deployment cares about, and Latent Integrity Risk (LIR), a detector score for tampered representations. A feasibility-filtering controller selects, at each inference, the split point, the representation protection, and the serving edge that minimise cost subject to per-inference risk and deadline budgets, and it falls back to on-device execution when no offload is safe. We frame this as a controlled simulation study of the constraint mechanism: it runs on a reduced-scale, fully reproducible testbed with an image and a sensing workload and a transparent analytical latency/energy model, so the claims concern the controller’s decisions and their effect on measured risk, not absolute timings on a particular device. CDSE tracks measured attack success far better than the split-depth and tensor-size heuristics used by leakage-agnostic schedulers (Spearman ρ of 0.59 and 0.87 versus 0.33 and 0.72 for depth). Over mixed mobility traces, MobiTrust holds the profiled privacy and adversarial constraint violations at 0% while the latency-only and weighted-sum baselines violate the privacy budget in 88% of inferences and the integrity budget in up to 58%; a weight sweep shows that, across the weightings we tested, the weighted-sum baseline reaches zero violations only by ceasing to offload. The cost of the guarantee is energy: MobiTrust saves device energy by offloading when it is safe, but a zero-violation local-only baseline attains higher accuracy and lower tail latency, so the improvement is a favourable energy trade-off rather than a uniform win. Because zero violations certify compliance with the profiled risk scores rather than an independently validated security bound, we also show that, under estimation uncertainty, the controller’s primal–dual margin holds the realised violation rate at its tolerance.
