items.title: Protective Effect of Cyclotrichium niveum on Gentamicin-Induced Nephrotoxicity in Rats
items.abstract: Gentamicin is an aminoglycoside antibiotic and has therapeutic importance in the treatment of Gram-negative aerobic bacterial infections. However, its clinical use is limited by nephrotoxicity, in which oxidative stress plays an important role. In this study, we investigated the protective effects of Cyclotrichium niveum, an endemic plant with antioxidant properties, against gentamicin-induced nephrotoxicity in rats. Renal injury and protection were assessed using blood urea nitrogen (BUN) and serum creatinine as markers of renal function, malondialdehyde (MDA) as a marker of oxidative stress, and histopathological evaluation of renal cortical injury. We first characterized the chemical composition of C. niveum essential oil (EO) by GC-MS, identifying pulegone as its major constituent (79.6%). Next, we evaluated the in vitro antioxidant activity of EO and isolated pulegone using the DPPH assay. Their protective effects were then examined in vivo at two dose levels each (EO, 200 and 400 mg/kg/day; pulegone, 50 and 100 mg/kg/day, p.o.) in rats receiving gentamicin (100 mg/kg/day, i.m.) for 8 days. Both EO and pulegone exhibited DPPH radical-scavenging activity. Gentamicin induced pronounced renal injury, whereas co-administration of either EO or pulegone provided protection, with more pronounced effects at the higher doses. In particular, gentamicin increased BUN and creatinine 2.74- and 2.37-fold, respectively (p 0.001 for both), and produced grade 4–5 cortical injury in all histologically evaluated animals. At the higher doses, EO and pulegone reduced BUN by 56% and 64%, respectively (p = 0.042 and p 0.001), and MDA by 57% and 55%, respectively (p = 0.006 for both). Pulegone additionally reduced creatinine by 39% (p = 0.041). Both treatments significantly improved histopathological injury grade (p = 0.002 and p = 0.008 for EO and pulegone, respectively). Together, these findings demonstrate that C. niveum EO and pulegone attenuate gentamicin-induced renal injury across functional, oxidative, and structural measures, with the strongest protection observed at the higher doses. Their in vitro antioxidant activity and attenuation of lipid peroxidation in vivo support an antioxidant contribution to the nephroprotective response, while the activity of isolated pulegone identifies it as an important bioactive contributor to the protective effects of C. niveum EO.
items.authors: Gazihan Harun Özsayın, Özlem Yorulmaz-Özü, Umay Merve Güven, Serpil Demirci-Kayiran, Yurdun Kuyucu, Merve Nenni

items.title: Cord Blood 3-Epi-25-Hydroxyvitamin D3 and Autism-Related Cognitive Traits at Age 10 Years: An Exploratory Secondary Analysis of the KLOTHO Birth Cohort
items.abstract: Background: The C3 epimer of 25-hydroxyvitamin D3 [3-epi-25(OH)D3] can be measured in maternal and umbilical cord circulation, but whether it is related to later neurodevelopment is unknown. Objective: To explore associations between cord 3-epi-25(OH)D3 and parent-reported autism-related trait domains at 10 years in the KLOTHO birth cohort. Methods: This secondary analysis used prospectively collected perinatal samples and 10-year questionnaire data. Vitamin D metabolites were quantified by liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry with epimer separation. The Australian Scale for Asperger’s Syndrome was used dimensionally, not diagnostically. Spearman correlations, false-discovery-rate (FDR) correction across 13 unique bivariate comparisons, supportive linear regressions, sex-stratified analyses, and a stricter record-linkage sensitivity analysis were conducted. Results: Data were available for 87 offspring (41 boys and 46 girls). Cord 3-epi-25(OH)D3 was inversely associated with cognitive-domain score (Spearman ρ = −0.412; p 0.001; Benjamini–Hochberg q = 0.001). The crude regression estimate was also inverse (B = −0.285; 95% CI, −0.458 to −0.112; p = 0.002), but the association attenuated after covariate adjustment and all adjusted confidence intervals included the null. A stricter linkage analysis remained significant (n = 84; ρ = −0.350; p = 0.001). The correlation was numerically stronger in boys than girls, but the between-sex comparison was not significant (p = 0.075). A positive correlation was also observed for social and emotional traits (ρ = 0.302; q = 0.023), indicating inconsistent directions across domains; the tertile analysis was non-significant. Conclusions: Cord 3-epi-25(OH)D3 was associated with lower cognitive-domain scores in unadjusted rank analyses, but the lack of stable adjusted linear evidence, inconsistent domain pattern, and small sample restrict interpretation. These findings are hypothesis-generating and do not imply causality, sex-specific effects, or clinical utility.
items.authors: Spyridon N. Karras, Dimitrios G. Goulis, Maria Dalamaga, Maria Kypraiou, Antonios Vlastos, Marios Anemoulis

items.title: Vacuum Heat Treatment Regulates the Bamboo–Epoxy Interface: Balancing Mechanical Performance and Thermal Stability
items.abstract: The sustainable replacement of conventional synthetic-fiber composites requires renewable reinforcements that combine low density with high load-bearing capability. However, the hydrophilic nature of bamboo restricts effective stress transfer at the bamboo–epoxy interface, while excessive thermal modification can further compromise the structural integrity of the reinforcement. Here, a vacuum-thermal interfacial regulation strategy was employed to establish a favorable balance between interfacial strengthening and thermally induced structural degradation. Moderate treatment improved resin coverage and interfacial contact while preserving the bamboo structure, thereby promoting efficient stress transfer across the bamboo–epoxy interface. Owing to this synergistic interfacial regulation, the composite treated at 160 °C for 4 h achieved tensile and flexural strengths of 174.49 and 219.55 MPa, corresponding to improvements of 49.60% and 29.47%, respectively, over the untreated composite, while excessive treatment caused renewed interfacial defects and mechanical deterioration. Meanwhile, vacuum heat treatment also enhanced thermal stability, increasing T5% from 216.55 to 260.08 °C and the residual mass at 500 °C from 24.18% to 28.28%. These results reveal a processing-window mechanism governed by the competition between interfacial strengthening and thermal degradation, providing an effective route for developing high-performance and sustainable bamboo/epoxy composites.
items.authors: Zilu Liang, Haiyun Jiang, Yimin Tan

items.title: Outcomes of Intravitreal Anti-VEGF Therapy for Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration in Kazakhstan
items.abstract: Background: Neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) is a leading cause of irreversible vision loss among older adults. Although randomised controlled trials have demonstrated the robust efficacy of intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy, real-world outcomes often differ markedly from trial findings. This study aimed to evaluate the anatomical and functional outcomes of anti-VEGF therapy in a clinical cohort of nAMD patients, including a subgroup that received adjunctive rescue photodynamic therapy (PDT) with verteporfin. Methods: This single-centre, retrospective observational cohort study included 568 patients (634 eyes) with nAMD treated with intravitreal anti-VEGF injections. Bevacizumab was used in 49% of eyes, ranibizumab in 44%, and aflibercept in 7%. Best recorded visual acuity (BRVA) and central retinal thickness (CRT) measured by optical coherence tomography (OCT) were recorded at baseline and at the final documented follow-up. Eyes with eccentric fixation were excluded from BRVA analysis but were retained for CRT analysis. Results: Mean patient age was 71.7 ± 8.8 years, and 67.6% of eyes were from female patients. The mean number of anti-VEGF injections was 5 ± 5.3 per eye; the mean follow-up duration was 11.5 months. Mean CRT decreased significantly from 347.3 ± 27.5 μm at baseline to 324.9 ± 28.8 μm at final follow-up (p 0.001). Mean BRVA (logMAR) improved modestly from 0.98 ± 0.55 (Snellen ~20/190; ~35 ETDRS letters) to 0.93 ± 0.56 (Snellen ~20/175; ~37.5 ETDRS letters) (p 0.001), with 67.9% of eyes demonstrating BRVA stability (change 0.1 logMAR). Rescue PDT was administered in 10.3% of eyes. Conclusions: In this real-world cohort, anti-VEGF therapy was associated with significant anatomical improvement, as measured by CRT reduction, while functional outcomes were characterised by visual stabilisation rather than substantial gains.
items.authors: Marat Suleimenov, Baurzhan Kadyrgaliyev, Elmira Kanafyanova, Zhanar Meyermanova, Venera Abdullina, Zulfiya Zhankalova

items.title: Microsurgical Lymphovenous Anastomosis for the Treatment of Central Lymphatic Flow Disorders in Children and Adults
items.abstract: Central lymphatic flow disorders remain a significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenge. Treatment typically follows a stepwise escalation approach, with reconstructive surgery being employed mainly in patients in whom conservative and interventional methods have failed or are contraindicated. Reconstructive lymphatic surgery, such as thoracic duct-vein anastomosis (TDVA), aims to restore physiological lymphatic drainage by creating a direct connection between the thoracic duct and the venous system. This narrative review summarizes the current evidence on central lymphatic reconstruction and particularly TDVA. Moreover, a general overview of perioperative patient management, diagnostics and alternative non-reconstructive surgical techniques is provided in this review. Several case reports and case series reported successful surgical central lymphatic reconstruction, showing both safety and efficacy of this technique in both acquired and congenital lesions of the central lymphatic system. However, current evidence is limited to small case series, whereas prospective large-scale trials are lacking. Future studies should address optimal patient selection and timing of surgery in addition to conservative and interventional approaches, thus promoting the establishment of evidence-based guidelines for the treatment of central lymphatic disorders.
items.authors: Carlotta Imholz, Carmen E. Zurfluh, Donata von Reibnitz, Claus C. Pieper, Christian A. Gutschow, Ueli Möhrlen

items.title: AI-Assisted WES Variant Interpretation in Neurodevelopmental Disorders: A Narrative Review of Existing Tools
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) comprise a heterogeneous group of conditions characterized by alterations in brain development and function, frequently associated with complex genetic architectures. The widespread implementation of next-generation sequencing, particularly whole-exome sequencing (WES), has substantially increased the identification of potentially disease-associated variants, shifting the major challenge from variant detection to their interpretation and prioritization. This review examines the emerging contribution of artificial intelligence (AI) to WES variant interpretation in NDDs, with particular emphasis on AI-assisted variant prioritization and protein structural modelling. Methods: We reviewed conventional computational and emerging AI-driven approaches applicable to different stages of WES interpretation, including variant pathogenicity and functional-effect prediction, evolutionary conservation, splicing assessment, phenotype-informed prioritization, and protein structure prediction. Their methodological principles, applications, and major limitations were critically examined within the context of neurodevelopmental genomics. Results: AI and machine-learning approaches increasingly integrate genomic, phenotypic, functional, and structural information, supporting phenotype-aware candidate prioritization and molecular contextualization of selected variants. However, computational outputs are affected by model-specific limitations and should not be considered independent evidence of pathogenicity. Their added value depends primarily on the complementarity and biological relevance of the information provided, rather than on predictor concordance alone. Conclusions: This narrative review highlights that AI-assisted WES interpretation should prioritize complementary, mechanism-relevant evidence over computational concordance. AI-assisted tools should therefore be selected according to variant class and disease mechanism and integrated with independent clinical, genetic, and functional evidence.
items.authors: Simone Treccarichi, Mirella Vinci, Antonino Musumeci, Rosanna Galati Rando, Antonio Fallea, Desiree Brancato

items.title: Amazonian Trichoderma spp. as Biocontrol Agents Against Agroathelia rolfsii and for Improving Tomato Yield
items.abstract: Sclerotium rot, caused by Agroathelia rolfsii, is one of the main soil-borne diseases that limit tomato production. This study evaluates the efficacy of Amazonian Trichoderma species in controlling Sclerotium rot and stimulating plant development under field conditions in Manaus, Brazil. We used six Trichoderma isolates based on their previously evaluated performance under greenhouse conditions. The incidence of Sclerotium rot, tomato fruit production, and functional attributes of the isolates were evaluated. The isolates reduced the incidence of Sclerotium rot by up to 75 percentage points and also increased fruit production. T. rugulosum showed the best performance as it significantly reduced the incidence of Sclerotium rot and improved fruit yield. Although no differences were found in biomass allocation to plant organs, T. endophyticum, T. agriamazonicum, and T. asperelloides showed production of indolic compounds in vitro. The results highlight the potential of Amazonian Trichoderma isolates as biofungicides for use in sustainable tomato cultivation. In addition, we demonstrated the potential of Amazonian Trichoderma species both to reduce the incidence of Sclerotium rot and to increase fruit production. By reducing the use of synthetic agrochemicals, the use of Trichoderma promotes healthier and more sustainable agricultural practices.
items.authors: Antonia Di Paola Rosas Batista, Jackeline Santos Menezes, Lucas Nascimento de Almeida, Luiz Alberto Guimarães Assis, André Luís Willerding, Claudia Afras de Queiroz

items.title: Socio-Spatial Configurations of Digital Availability: A Fuzzy-Set Qualitative Comparative Analysis of Istanbul’s 39 Districts
items.abstract: Urban digital transformation is commonly framed as a function of information and communication technology (ICT) provision, treating the socio-spatial conditions that shape technology uptake as background. Empirical work is correspondingly spatially blind and aggregates distinct dimensions of digital availability into composite indices that assume shared determinants. This study addresses both gaps in Istanbul, a developing-country megacity whose districts differ sixfold in household income. Thirty-one indicators for all 39 districts are reduced by principal component analysis to four ICT dimensions and three socio-spatial conditions, keeping conditions proportionate to cases. No condition proves necessary, so fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis identifies the configurations sufficient for each dimension and for its absence. The dimensions share no common configuration: digital entrepreneurship follows socio-economic status alone (coverage 0.855, consistency 0.849); public Wi-Fi provision relative to fixed broadband follows economic activity in ageing districts (0.548, 0.844); mobile access with digital-learning provision follows economic activity in young or low-status districts (0.629, 0.821); and digital skills (0.777, 0.714) arise both from socio-economic status and, independently of it, from economic activity. Because the same condition accompanies different outcomes depending on the socio-spatial structure it meets, policy must be matched to the configuration of the district it addresses rather than applied city-wide.
items.authors: Burak Belli, Turgay Kerem Koramaz

items.title: Recurrence Rates and Outcomes After First Detected Atrial Fibrillation Episode in a Contemporary Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy Center
items.abstract: Background: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common sustained arrhythmia in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), occurring in 20–25% of patients and associated with increased morbidity, stroke risk, and symptom burden. Despite this substantial clinical impact, the understanding of the short-term natural history of AF, including recurrence and the effectiveness of treatment strategies in HCM, remains poorly characterized. Methods: We assessed 2016 patients referred to Lahey Hospital and Medical Center for the diagnosis and subspecialty management of HCM, of whom 341 (17%) had a remote history of AF (≥5 years), and 149 (7%) had AF episodes initially detected between January 2020 and June 2025. These 149 patients were included in this retrospective analysis to allow comprehensive short-term assessment of AF recurrence, treatment interventions, and clinical outcomes from first detected AF utilizing contemporary treatments. Results: AF was first detected at a median age of 63 years (IQR 54–70); 63% were male. Most AF episodes (87%) were symptomatic at presentation. Among 146 patients who converted to sinus rhythm, AF recurred in 80 (54%) at a median of 171 days (IQR 53–278; 29% at 6 months, 43% at 12 months). In patients not undergoing rhythm control after first detected AF episode, 60% had spontaneous recurrence (29% at 6 months, 48% at 1 year), while recurrence rates after antiarrhythmic drug (AAD) initiation were 44% (28% at 6 months, 37.5% at 1 year), and after catheter ablation were 27% (9.8% at 6 months, 18% at 1 year). At last follow-up, 1.9 years (IQR 1.2–2.6 years) from first detected AF episode, 133 of 149 patients (89%) were in sinus rhythm. Seven patients (4.7%) died at a median of 1.16 years (IQR 0.74–1.62) after their first detected AF; estimated survival was 98.6% at 1 year and 96.0% at 3 years. Conclusions: AF recurrence occurs at high rates after the initial detected AF episode in HCM regardless of rhythm-control strategy or AAD use. Catheter ablation was associated with lower recurrence rates. These findings characterize the relapsing natural history of HCM-associated AF and underscore the need for further studies to optimize rhythm-control strategies in this population.
items.authors: Mauro Rogerio de Barros Wanderley, Martin S. Maron, Jonathan S. Silver, Paul Harnish, Bruce G. Hook, Ethan J. Rowin
items.category_raw: Journal of Cardiovascular Development and Disease

items.title: Origin and Source Correlation of Permian Hydrocarbons in the Kekeya Area, Southwestern Tarim Basin, China
items.abstract: The Southwestern Depression of the Tarim Basin has considerable petroleum exploration potential, and several hydrocarbon accumulations have been discovered in Permian reservoirs of the Kekeya area. However, the sources of Permian crude oils and the genetic types of natural gases remain debated because multiple potential source rocks and multi-source hydrocarbon charging occur in this area. This study integrates GC-MS analyses of crude oils and source-rock extracts with biomarker parameters, bulk and fraction carbon-isotope data, compound-specific carbon-isotope data for n-alkanes, and natural-gas composition and carbon-isotope data to characterize Permian hydrocarbons and constrain oil sources and gas genesis. Methylphenanthrene index (MPI) estimates indicate equivalent vitrinite reflectance (Rc) values of 0.61–1.00% for Permian oils. For natural gases, methane-isotope-derived Rc estimates are dependent on the genetic-type equation applied; sensitivity calculations using the oil-type and coal-derived equations yield ranges of 0.59–1.81% and 0.37–1.14%, respectively. GC-MS results show that Permian oils contain a complete C19–C24 tricyclic terpane series, characterized by a C19TT C20TT C21TT distribution pattern with C21TT as the dominant peak, together with abundant C24TeT, C30 rearranged hopane, and relatively high gammacerane contents. These features resemble those of Permian source rocks but differ markedly from Carboniferous source rocks (C19TT C20TT C21TT). The C27–C28–C29 regular steranes display an asymmetric shallow V-shaped pattern. Saturated hydrocarbon biomarker parameters (Pr/nC17, Ph/nC18, Ga, and C30H) and aromatic fluorene-series compositions (SF-OF-F) further indicate similar hydrocarbon precursors and strong geochemical affinity between Permian oils and the Pusige Formation source rocks in terms of organic input and depositional environment. Bulk oil δ13C values (−31.2‰ to −26.8‰) and compound-specific δ13C values of n-alkanes (−41.4‰ to −30.7‰) indicate mixed marine/lacustrine algal and terrestrial higher-plant contributions, supporting the Pusige Formation as the main oil source and distinguishing it from Carboniferous source rocks. Gas compositions and carbon isotopes show that gases in the Permian reservoirs are predominantly thermogenic and mainly represent primary kerogen-cracking gas, although some samples record higher maturity, mixed origins, and carbon isotope reversal. These results improve the understanding of hydrocarbon sources and gas genesis in complex petroleum systems of the Southwestern Depression and provide geochemical constraints for exploration in similar foreland basins.
items.authors: Wen Zhang, Jinqiang Tian, Haizu Zhang, Fuyun Cong, Qing Zhao, Aizimaiti Maimaiti

items.title: Strategic Contributions of Mining Suppliers Within a Regional Mining Ecosystem: An AHP Decision Framework for Structural Analysis and Sensitivity Assessment
items.abstract: The increasing reliance of the mining industry on specialized suppliers has highlighted the need to understand which capabilities suppliers consider most important for strengthening their participation within regional mining supplier ecosystems. However, existing research has focused primarily on supplier selection and evaluation from the perspective of mining companies, providing limited evidence on how suppliers themselves prioritize their strategic contributions. This study examines these contributions in the Coquimbo Region (Chile) using a multicriteria decision framework based on the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP), complemented by performance, gradient, and head-to-head sensitivity analyses. The results identify Sustainability (0.239) and Management (0.212) as the highest-priority criteria, while Safety Management (0.069), Financial Management (0.059), Human Resource Management (0.054), and Data Management (0.054) emerge as the highest-ranked strategic contributions. Sensitivity analysis further demonstrates that the influence of a criterion depends not only on its global weight but also on its position within the hierarchical decision structure, allowing the identification of stable and context-sensitive priorities under alternative weighting scenarios. These findings show that integrating AHP with sensitivity analysis provides a robust decision framework for interpreting strategic priorities and supporting supplier development within regional mining ecosystems.
items.authors: Edison Ramírez-Olivares, María Pía Salinas-Santander, Valentina Torres-Caces, Juan Alfaro Robles

items.title: Exploring the Anticancer Potential of Plant, Marine, and Synthetic Glycosides: A Comprehensive Review
items.abstract: Despite advances in pharmaceutical and technological development, cancer continues to be a life-threatening illness globally. In addition to other specialized procedures, radiotherapy, chemotherapy, and surgery are methods used to treat cancer. However, in recent years, natural products have either been used as food supplements or complementary medicine in the management and treatment of cancer. Natural products are the secondary metabolites present in the cells of medicinal plants, microbes, and marine organisms. Glycosides are a naturally occurring class of metabolites with exceptional therapeutic value and clinical efficacy. The structure of all glycosides is similar; it consists of two parts: a hydrophilic glycone unit made up of one or more sugar components, and a lipophilic aglycone unit. Over the past few years, the potential anti-cancer properties of several natural and synthetic glycosides have been investigated. In this review, we compile and analyze 224 naturally occurring glycosides from plant and marine sources, along with more than 40 synthetic glycosides, that exhibit anticancer properties. Reported anticancer activities span a wide potency range and involve multiple mechanisms, including apoptosis, cell-cycle arrest, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, inhibition of PI3K/AKT, MAPK, STAT3, Wnt/β-catenin, and Na+/K+-ATPase signaling, as well as suppression of migration and invasion. Several compounds show potency comparable to or exceeding standard chemotherapeutics under matched assay conditions: for example, an epigallocatechin-3-O-gallate derivative inhibited MDA-MB-231 cells at an IC50 of 3.27 ± 0.18 µM versus 5.20 ± 0.89 µM for capecitabine, and a synthetic N-glycosyl heterocycle (compound 479a) outperformed erlotinib against HepG-2 and HCT-116 cells (IC50 = 1.64 ± 0.11 and 5.00 ± 0.51 µM vs. 2.07 ± 0.07 and 5.14 ± 0.33 µM). Other studies reported glycosides with activities comparable to or greater than reference agents such as capecitabine, tamoxifen, and erlotinib. Despite these promising findings, the evidence remains predominantly preclinical, with substantial limitations in normal-cell selectivity, standardized cytotoxicity assessment, pharmacokinetic characterization, and in vivo and clinical validation. Overall, glycosides represent promising anticancer scaffolds, but systematic optimization of potency, selectivity, stability, bioavailability, and safety is required to facilitate their translation into clinically useful therapeutics.
items.authors: Tooba Jabeen, Sumayya Akram, Matloob Ahmad, Sami A. Al-Hussain, Magdi E. A. Zaki

items.title: Temporal Dynamics of Growth and Aniline-Blue-Reactive β-(1→3)-Glucan-Associated Material in em Alcaligenes faecalis /em A12C
items.abstract: Microbial β-(1→3)-glucans are polysaccharides of biological and technological in-terest whose production depends strongly on strain and culture conditions. This study characterized the temporal relationship between bacterial growth and aniline-blue re-activity in Alcaligenes faecalis A12C under growth and fermentation conditions. Growth, viability, and β-(1→3)-glucan-associated signals were monitored over 96 h using spec-trophotometric, microbiological, and microscopic approaches. In growth culture me-dium (GCM), OD600 increased after 24–30 h and reached approximately 2.4 at 72 h, coinciding with the highest viable count (2.49 × 10²¹ CFU/mL). Aniline-blue coloration became clearly detectable after approximately 30 h and persisted through 96 h, when microscopy showed blue staining associated with bacterial cells. In fermentation culture medium (FCM), OD600 increased progressively to approximately 2.8 at 96 h, whereas viable counts followed a distinct temporal profile. Aniline-blue reactivity increased during early fermentation and remained stable at an A610 of approximately 1.0 from 24 h onward. The divergence among OD600, viable counts, and aniline-blue reactivity in-dicates that bacterial proliferation and development of the aniline-blue-reactive signal followed distinct temporal patterns. These findings characterize this temporal rela-tionship in A12C cultures, although chemical and structural characterization is required to determine whether the detected polymer corresponds to curdlan.
items.authors: Carlos José Martel Benítez, Ruth Henríquez Cabrera, Rafael Alayón Afonso, Daniel Padilla, Fernando Real, Antera Martel Quintana

items.title: AI Revolution and Scientific Research Involving LLMs and Gen-AI: Preliminary PICO-AI, SPIDER-AI, and PRISMA-AI Conceptual Extensions for Evidence Synthesis Frameworks
items.abstract: Background: Systematic and scoping reviews rely on established frameworks such as PICO (Population, Intervention, Comparator, Outcome), SPIDER (Sample, Phenomenon of Interest, Design, Evaluation, Research type), and PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) to structure research questions, guide evidence synthesis, and ensure transparent reporting. These frameworks were developed for linear, human-driven workflows involving manual searching, screening, and data extraction. The emergence of large language models (LLMs) and Generative AI (Gen-AI) introduces new capabilities for semi-automated literature discovery, screening, data extraction, and thematic synthesis. However, the methodological implications of AI-assisted evidence synthesis remain underexplored. Methods: This manuscript employed a scoping review–informed methodological analysis of empirical and methodological literature located through structured searches of PubMed and Google Scholar. Preliminary conceptual extensions to PICO, SPIDER, and PRISMA were developed, retrospectively applied to published studies, and independently evaluated by five researchers for applicability, relevance, and clarity. Results: LLMs enable dynamic and iterative processes across evidence synthesis stages, including automated question formulation, large-scale qualitative analysis, and hybrid human–AI screening and extraction. These developments challenge the linear assumptions of PICO, SPIDER, and PRISMA. In response, PICO-AI, SPIDER-AI, and PRISMA-AI incorporate dimensions including prompt transparency, model specification, human-in-the-loop validation, Human–AI workflow classification, data governance, and AI auditability. Independent evaluation showed 80% item agreement, with overall mean relevance and clarity ratings of 3.2/4. Conclusions: LLMs and Gen-AI do not replace systematic review frameworks; rather, they extend them by introducing adaptive, data-driven workflows. Integrating AI into evidence synthesis requires revised methodological guidance to ensure transparency, reproducibility, and rigour. The proposed preliminary extensions provide a model for incorporating machine intelligence into systematic and scoping review practices.
items.authors: Ehsan Jozaghi

items.title: The Dirac Equation and the Two-Photon Model of the Electron
items.abstract: In a previous paper, “The Electron as a Composition of Two Vacuum-Polarization-Confined Photons,” an electron model was developed in which two counter-propagating phase-conjugate photons are bound in orbit by the self-induced gradient in the speed of light arising from their mutual vacuum polarization. The model accounts for rest mass and spin, proposes a mechanism for charge, and has no singularity and no negative-energy solutions. The present paper focuses on the mathematical structure of that bound state. Its four-momentum is shown to satisfy a first-order equation — here called P-Dirac — that is derived from the Lorentz kinematics of two null four-vectors, independently of the standard Klein–Gordon factorization and without the imaginary moments that appear in one solution of the standard Dirac equation. Spin eigenfunctions emerge from the commutator of the two ordered photon interaction products — geometric products whose antisymmetric part is a bivector. The commutator coefficient is Δc / c0 =1-cint / c0, equal to 1/2 at the stable orbit, derived from the orbital binding condition, not postulated. The paper also notes the connection to Spacetime Algebra (STA) in the Doran–Lasenby formulation, where the photon pair forms an even-grade multivector whose scalar part determines the invariant rest mass and whose bivector part is the Dirac spin bivector.
items.authors: D. T. Froedge

items.title: Exploration of Modeling and Optimization Methods of Single Photon Avalanche Diode
items.abstract: Single-photon avalanche diodes (SPADs) have great potential in astronomy, fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM), quantum communication, and other high-precision sensing and imaging applications. However, further optimization of SPAD performance is often constrained by fabrication time and cost. In this work, we develop a technology computer-aided design (TCAD) simulation flow for a custom SPAD. We propose models for the I-V characteristics, breakdown voltage, dark count rate (DCR), and photon detection probability (PDP). These models are calibrated against measurements across a wide range of bias voltages and temperatures. We also investigated the effects of specific process parameters on device performance. This work provides a method for accurate SPAD design and optimization.
items.authors: Jing Fu, Anran Guo, Junxian Jiang, Guowei Li, Huaping Ma, Hongbo Zhang

items.title: Effect of Pretreatment of Orange Peel with Deep Eutectic Solvents Before Acid Hydrolysis to Produce Reduced Sugars
items.abstract: Currently, approximately 80% of the energy used worldwide comes from fossil fuels. The production of bioethanol from agro-industrial waste requires pretreatment due to the latter’s rigid structure and resistance to degradation. In this work orange peel (OP) was pretreated with deep eutectic solvents (DESs), varying the molar ratio of the mixture to delignify the OP, exposing cellulose and hemicellulose, in order to improve the yield in the acid hydrolysis process with H3PO4 to produce reduced sugars. SEM, FTIR, and XRD were used to evaluate the structural changes in OP with and without pretreatment. Optimal pretreatment was achieved using ChCl/U at a 1:4 molar ratio, yielding 31.58 g of reducing sugars per 100 g of pretreated OP after 150 min, compared with 12.09 g of reducing sugars per 100 g of untreated OP after 300 min. The holocellulose content after pretreatment increased by 28%. Significant differences were found in the reducing-sugar yield and the structure of OP with and without pretreatment; DESs are useful for biomass delignification, thus enabling increased reducing-sugar production through acid hydrolysis.
items.authors: María del Carmen Carreño-de-León, Nicolas Flores-Alamo, Fredy Cuellar-Robles, Juan José Luna-Torres, Daniela Gutiérrez-López

items.title: The Symmetry Landscape of Molecules: From Cosmic Molecular Symmetry to Biological Asymmetry
items.abstract: Molecular symmetry governs numerous physical and chemical properties, but its statistical distribution across biological molecular systems remains insufficiently explored. We compare the symmetry landscape of biological molecules with that previously established for molecules constituting the TMC-1, Orion KL, and IRC + 10216 molecular clouds. The comparison reveals a pronounced contrast: symmetry dominates among molecules detected in molecular clouds, whereas asymmetry dominates among biological molecules. Interstellar and circumstellar molecular corpora are rich in linear, axially symmetric, and mirror-symmetric species, while biological corpora are dominated by the asymmetric point group C1. Exact molecular point groups and symmetry elements were analyzed for a 50-molecule biological pilot corpus, normal human plasma, normal human urine, and the principal molecular constituents of poliovirus. Species- and concentration-weighted point-group probabilities were considered, and their diversity was quantified using the Shannon entropy, normalized Shannon entropy, and Simpson diversity number D2. The predominance of C1 in biological systems reflects the extensive use of chiral building blocks, stereogenic centers, and chemically nonequivalent functional groups required for molecular recognition and biochemical specificity. Concentration weighting modifies but does not universally reverse this tendency: normal human plasma remains predominantly asymmetric, whereas normal urine becomes abundance-dominated by C2v symmetry because of the exceptionally high concentration of urea. Poliovirus represents the limiting molecular case: all principal chemically defined constituents, VP1, VP2, VP3, VP4, VPg, and genomic RNA, belong to C1, yielding zero point-group entropy and D2 = 1. Nevertheless, repeated asymmetric capsid proteins self-assemble into a shell possessing approximate proper icosahedral symmetry. Thus, the transition from cosmic molecular matter to biological molecular organization is accompanied by extensive molecular symmetry breaking, while high symmetry may re-emerge at the supramolecular level through the ordered assembly of asymmetric components.
items.authors: Edward Bormashenko

items.title: Reliability-Oriented Prediction Method for Remaining Useful Life of Rolling Pair Wear Based on Stochastic Degradation Process and BP Neural Network
items.abstract: Rolling pairs are widely used in high-value equipment, making remaining useful life (RUL) prediction essential for reliability and safety. However, RUL prediction remains challenging due to complex wear mechanisms, scarce data, and insufficient representation of operating history. A hybrid method combining a Gamma process and a backpropagation (BP) neural network is proposed. Monte Carlo samples generated from Gamma and inverse power-law models fitted to accelerated-test data are used to augment the training data, while a history matrix represents time-varying conditions. The proposed method is evaluated using wear data from an enclosed, low-speed, heavy-load rotating component in a nuclear power plant. The results show that the proposed method achieves high accuracy in wear prediction and produces a continuous RUL trajectory under time-varying operating conditions. A continuous RUL trajectory is also produced under time-varying operating conditions. The method provides a practical framework for rolling pairs with limited degradation data and variable operating conditions.
items.authors: Zeyuan Yu, Ying Luo, Guozhong Fu, Bo Yang, Wei Li

items.title: When Does Data Augmentation Help with Few Chest-Radiograph Training Patients?
items.abstract: Scarce medical images often prompt data augmentation. We ask when it earns its opportunity cost under a complete information budget. Across four collections, classical and GAN candidates are compared with real-only training, full-pool exposure, score adjustment and direct label use. Transformations reduce within-patient variation; source mismatch and between-patient uncertainty remain. Fixed 50-model ResNet50 ensembles with ranked classical candidates and probability averaging outperform equally adjusted real-only and full-pool ensembles at five sizes. We evaluate procedures in 50 paired draws at 50, 100, 150, 200 and 250 image-training patients. The design counts 200 regularization patients plus disjoint 100-patient selection and adjustment sets. Evaluation includes 38,743 CheXpert patients. At 250 patients, guidance reduces maximum group cross-entropy by 0.0442 versus real-only training (simultaneous 95% interval, 0.0048–0.0836). Adding the 100 selection patients to each original training cohort outperforms using their labels only to guide augmentation at 50–200 patients. Thus, use independent labels first when cohorts are smallest; consider selected augmentation once patient evidence, strong representation and aggregation are available. The 250-patient result marks the upper tested setting, not a universal threshold. AUROC remains stable while sensitivity and specificity shift, requiring operating-point review.
items.authors: Murat Sariyar

items.title: Printing the Americas for Catholic Europe: Jesuit Knowledge, Missionary Imagination, and Identity in the German-Speaking Lands, 1546–1800
items.abstract: This article examines how Jesuit and Jesuit-related printed writings about the Americas circulated in the German-speaking lands between 1546 and 1800 and how they mediated Catholic knowledge, missionary imagination, and claims to collective identity. Drawing on a representative, though not exhaustive, selection of German-language originals and translations—including letters, missionary reports, books, compilations, and periodicals—it combines diachronic textual analysis with the history of ideas. Rather than treating circulation as evidence of reception, the article examines how authors and editors represented American societies and missionary activity for their intended audiences. It identifies three overlapping phases. From the 1540s to the 1670s, narratives of suffering, martyrdom, and conversion represented the Americas as a theater of missionary sacrifice and reinforced Jesuit corporate and Catholic identity. From the 1670s to 1767, accounts of American customs, polities, and religions increasingly organized difference through hierarchies of civilization and offered a framework through which forms of German-speaking collective identity could be imagined. After 1767, and especially following the suppression of the Society in 1773, writings by former Jesuits and Jesuit-related authors became more defensive while also displaying greater internal differentiation. In this context, Creole writers defended the natural world and peoples of the Americas against claims of degeneracy, thereby giving greater visibility to their own claims to epistemic and cultural authority, whereas German-speaking former Jesuits placed greater emphasis on defending the legitimacy of the missionary enterprise. The article shows that these writings both transmitted knowledge about American realities and selectively organized that knowledge through Eurocentric assumptions. Across these phases, representations of Indigenous societies as requiring Christian and civilizational tutelage and of missionaries as agents of conversion, improvement, and social order provided a discursive framework through which missionary and colonial intervention could be presented as legitimate.
items.authors: Longhai Gao, Sijie Wang

items.title: Novel Genetic Variants of the CHD2 Gene in cis Position in a Patient with Epileptic Encephalopathy: A Case Report and In Silico Analysis of the Impact of the Variants on the Protein
items.abstract: CHD2-related neurodevelopmental disorders are increasingly recognized as a distinct group of epileptic encephalopathies with heterogeneous clinical manifestations. Here, we report a 12-year-old female patient with pharmacoresistant epilepsy, mild cognitive impairment (IQ = 56), and extraneurological features including grade II kyphoscoliosis and planovalgus foot deformity. Video-EEG monitoring revealed a phenotype consistent with Jeavons syndrome, characterized by daily eyelid myoclonia with absences and marked photosensitivity with an eye closure sensitivity (ECS) phenomenon. Molecular genetic testing via whole-exome and Sanger sequencing identified two novel variants in the CHD2 gene (NM_001271.4): c.1634T G (p.Leu545Arg) and c.3810G C (p.Leu1270Phe). Long-read nanopore sequencing confirmed their de novo status and cis-positioning on the paternal allele. Structural bioinformatic analysis using AlphaFold3, FoldX/mCSM (v5.0 package), UCSF ChimeraX (v1.10.1), and PyMOL (v3.1.8) demonstrated that both variants individually destabilize the CHD2 protein, with a cumulative destabilizing effect when combined: p.Leu545Arg affects the ATP-binding domain, whereas p.Leu1270Phe disrupts hydrophobic packing within the C-terminal DNA-binding domain. These findings suggest accelerated protein degradation as a potential disease mechanism. Our data support the pathogenicity of these heterozygous cis-variants and implicate CHD2 haploinsufficiency as the leading etiopathogenic mechanism, though distinct domain-specific effects of each substitution may also contribute to the complex molecular synergy observed in this case.
items.authors: Andrew S. Zuev, Elizaveta A. Fonova, Daria S. Kuznetsova, Vadim A. Stepanov, Nikolay A. Skryabin

items.title: Distributed Consensus Control for Connected Vehicle Platoon with Markovian Switching Topology and Heterogeneous Time-Varying Delays
items.abstract: Reliable cooperative control of connected vehicle platoons remains challenging when stochastic communication-topology variations coexist with heterogeneous time-varying transmission delays. This study investigates a distributed consensus control problem for connected vehicle platoons subject to Markovian switching topologies and heterogeneous time-varying inter-vehicle communication delays. A third-order longitudinal vehicle model with powertrain inertial lag is combined with a continuous-time Markov chain (CTMC) to describe randomly switching communication topologies. A distributed control protocol incorporating the constant time headway policy, full velocity difference car-following behavior, and leader-pinning information is formulated, while link-dependent time-varying delays are embedded in the closed-loop error system. Based on a mode-dependent Lyapunov–Krasovskii functional, Jensen’s integral inequality, and the Schur complement, sufficient linear matrix inequality (LMI) conditions are derived for mean-square asymptotic stability of the nominal delayed system; the LMI is feasible at τ¯ℓ=0.10 s and μℓ=0.04, remains feasible at 0.30 s, and becomes infeasible at 0.375 s. An input-to-state stability (ISS) corollary extends the result to bounded time-varying leader acceleration, showing that tracking errors remain bounded during dynamic EUDC phases and converge when the leader acceleration and its derivative vanish. Using the same Lyapunov–Krasovskii certificate, a mean-square L∞ bounded-propagation result is further established; this result characterizes uniform-in-vehicle error bounds and does not assert strict non-amplification. Numerical simulations under the Extra-Urban Driving Cycle (EUDC) show that the follower vehicles maintain cooperative tracking under topology switching and bounded communication delays, with position, velocity, and acceleration errors remaining bounded during the dynamic phases and converging as the leader acceleration vanishes. In the EUDC simulation, the largest leader-relative position error is approximately −60.75 m for Vehicle 10 at t≈380 s, the maximum adjacent local spacing-error peak ratio is 2.32, and the position error returns below 1 m by t≈400.8 s. The minimum inter-vehicle gap is 5.87 m and the minimum safety margin after the initial 10 s is 0.84, with all safety-margin indices remaining positive; these results indicate that the proposed framework maintains platoon coordination and car-following safety under stochastic communication uncertainties.
items.authors: Ruijia Li, Guokuan Yu, Peng Li, Di Ao, Xianbo Wang

items.title: A Hybrid CNN–iTransformer Framework with Physics-Informed Regularization for Accurate MOSFET RUL Estimation
items.abstract: Accurate forecasting of MOSFET on-state resistance drift can support remaining useful life (RUL) estimation under thermal overstress. Existing methods seldom combine local degradation patterns, long-range feature interactions, and a failure-mode-specific prior in one forecasting framework. We propose a CNN–iTransformer model that uses on-state resistance drift as its health indicator and includes a finite-difference sensitivity constraint. On the four test records reported in this study, the average mean absolute error (MAE), root mean square error (RMSE), and relative error (RE) were 2.996 × 10−4 Ω, 3.988 × 10−4 Ω, and 3.110 × 10−3, respectively. For Test 37, the predicted RUL was 850 sampling steps versus 843 observed steps, producing a seven-step absolute error. These results concern within-record forecasting on one accelerated-aging dataset; generalization to unseen devices remains to be established.
items.authors: Lei Wang, Miaokun Xu, Runqi Li, Yupeng Wang, Zhenjie Yin, Jinmei Wang

items.title: Associative Interactions of Tert-Butyl Hydroperoxide with Halide Anions: Intermolecular Dynamics and NMR Spectra Parameters
items.authors: Yuliya V. Berestneva, Elena V. Raksha, Nikolaj A. Turovskij

items.title: Bacterial-Algal Consortium Enhances Crucian Carp Growth and Muscle Quality by Modulating Gut Microbiota and Lipid Metabolism
items.abstract: To investigate the mechanisms by which bacterial-algal consortia (Chlorella and Effective Microorganisms) enhance the growth performance and muscle quality of Crucian carp (Carassius auratus) in an ecological aquaculture model, this study conducted a 90-day pond experiment comparing a traditional aquaculture group (TA) with a bacterial-algal ecological aquaculture group (EA). Compared with the TA group, the EA group showed significantly improved growth performance, increased polyunsaturated fatty acids (including linoleic acid, arachidonic acid, and DHA), and enriched volatile flavor compounds (alcohols and esters imparting fruity and floral aromas). Mechanistically, the EA group exhibited enhanced intestinal morphology (elevated villus height and microvillus length) and digestive enzyme activities (amylase and lipase). 16S rRNA sequencing and untargeted metabolomics revealed a remodeling of gut microbiota with enrichment of beneficial genera (Romboutsia and Cetobacterium), alongside upregulated lipid metabolism pathways (linoleic acid metabolism and PPAR signaling) and amino acid metabolism. Spearman correlation analysis confirmed strong positive links between these beneficial bacteria and key flavor-related metabolites. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that the bacterial-algal consortium does not merely serve as a nutritional supplement but rather optimizes intestinal structure, enhances digestive function, remodels gut microbial composition, and suggests a potential role of hosting metabolic networks, primarily through the gut–metabolism axis. This study provides a theoretical foundation for developing green and healthy aquaculture technologies for Crucian carp.
items.authors: Jiawen Hu, Jiahao Liu, Jiahui Xiao, Zhongqing Wang, Yi Sun, Zhijuan Nie

items.title: A CAD-Prior-Guided Point Cloud Semantic Segmentation and Completion Method for Large-Span Spatial Truss Structures
items.abstract: To support design-consistent modeling of large-span trusses from field scans, this study aims to develop and evaluate a workflow guided by CAD priors for isolating load-bearing members and completing structural topology in severely occluded regions. A semantic segmentation algorithm based on voxel spatial indexing and two-stage neighborhood matching first uses the CAD model to discretize the search space and isolate main load-bearing trusses from cluttered backgrounds. On a manually labeled subset of 339,075 measured points from 12 representative regions, the segmentation stage achieves an F1-score of 85.65% and an IoU of 74.91%. A point cloud fusion and completion algorithm then combines distance-weighted iterative closest point registration with region-growing hierarchical mapping to reconstruct design-consistent point sets in shadowed node regions. The workflow is evaluated on the Zhongyuan International Convention and Exhibition Center. It achieves a normalized Chamfer distance of 0.53% and a normalized Hausdorff distance of 1.16% relative to the CAD reference. Under a 50 mm evaluation tolerance, the F-Score is 20.02%, more than twice the best traditional baseline, although the modest absolute value indicates limited strict-tolerance agreement. The output provides researchers, engineers, decision-makers, and asset managers with a traceable basis for digital-twin model preparation, inspection planning, and topology-aware documentation; CAD-derived points must nevertheless remain distinguishable from measured data in deformation monitoring and structural assessment.
items.authors: Chaojun Chen, Hongping Zhu, Junshu Zhang, Shun Weng, Ke Gao, Zhiyue Zhang

items.authors: Manmeet Kaur, Manpreet Kaur, Dhanwinder Singh, Aderbal C. Oliveira, Vijayendra Kumar Garg, Virender K. Sharma

items.title: Nutrition, Periodontal Health and Birth Outcomes: An Exploratory Cross-Sectional Analysis of a Postpartum Case–Control Sample
items.abstract: Background and Objective: Maternal nutrition may influence periodontal inflammation and pregnancy outcomes, yet evidence regarding food-derived nutrient intake remains limited. This study characterized maternal dietary intake relative to pregnancy-specific reference values and explored associations with periodontal and obstetric outcomes. Materials and Methods: In this cross-sectional analysis of a previously established case–control study, postpartum women selected according to birth outcome underwent periodontal examination and completed the German Health Interview and Examination Survey for Adults Food Frequency Questionnaire (DEGS-FFQ) 1–4 days after delivery. Periodontal examination included probing pocket depth, clinical attachment loss, bleeding on probing, and the gingival bleeding index (GBI). Exploratory associations between the nine prespecified nutrient intakes and BOP, GBI, and gestational age at delivery were assessed using Spearman rank correlations with 95% bias-corrected bootstrap confidence intervals. Results: The analytical sample comprised 48 women, including 15 with preterm birth; periodontal data were available for 44 participants. Reported food-derived intake was below the respective pregnancy-specific D-A-CH reference values in all participants for folate and iron, in 91.7% for iodine, 79.2% for dietary fiber, and 77.1% for niacin. Exploratory correlations between the nine prespecified nutrient intakes and BOP, GBI, or gestational age at delivery were generally small (ρ ranging from −0.092 to 0.241), and all 95% bias-corrected bootstrap confidence intervals included zero. Conclusions: Food-derived intake of several pregnancy-relevant nutrients was below reference values. Associations between individual nutrient intake and periodontal or obstetric outcomes were limited, with no clear evidence of associations. Given the exploratory design and small sample, these findings require cautious interpretation.
items.authors: Valentin Bartha, Rebekka Wittlinger, Alexandra Balzer, Diana Wolff, Johan Peter Woelber, Marco M. Herz

items.title: Awareness, Access and Use of Shear Wave Elastography and Myotonpro Among Physiotherapy Students and Practicing Physiotherapists: A Cross-Sectional Survey
items.abstract: Background: Shear wave elastography (SWE) and MyotonPro provide quantitative information on tissue mechanical properties and may complement conventional musculoskeletal assessment. This study assessed awareness, access, use, and perceived clinical utility of these technologies among physiotherapy students and practicing physiotherapists, and examined associations with age and professional experience. Methods: A cross-sectional observational study was conducted using an anonymous online survey. The author-developed questionnaire assessed awareness, access, self-reported use, self-rated knowledge, perceived utility, training, and implementation barriers. The sample included 101 respondents: 45 final-year physiotherapy students and 56 practicing physiotherapists from Warsaw, Poland. Group differences and associations with age and professional experience were assessed using appropriate non-parametric and categorical tests, with Holm adjustment for multiple comparisons. Results: Awareness of SWE and MyotonPro was reported by 31.7% and 35.6% of respondents, respectively, while 29.7% had access to either technology. Ever-use was reported by 15.8% for SWE and 21.8% for MyotonPro. Practicing physiotherapists showed greater awareness and use than students (SWE: 51.8% vs. 6.7%; MyotonPro: 53.6% vs. 13.3%; both p 0.001). All nine group comparisons remained significant after adjustment. Professional experience was positively associated with all nine outcomes (ρ = 0.30–0.62; all adjusted p ≤ 0.0032), with the strongest association for SWE self-rated knowledge (ρ = 0.62, adjusted p 0.0001). Age showed weaker associations. Conclusions: SWE and MyotonPro remain incompletely integrated into the surveyed physiotherapy population. Professional experience was the most consistent correlate of technology-related outcomes. Limited equipment access and cost were important barriers. The findings highlight differences in awareness, experience, and perceived barriers, while further research is needed to determine whether educational or organizational interventions would improve clinical adoption.
items.authors: Sebastian Szajkowski, Jarosław Pasek, Grzegorz Cieślar

items.title: Solving Three-Dimensional Conformable Partial Differential Equations Using the Quadruple Sumudu Transform Decomposition Method
items.abstract: In this work, we introduce the conformable quadruple Sumudu transform and employ it in conjunction with the Adomian decomposition method to solve three-dimensional linear and nonlinear conformable partial differential equations. We establish the existence of the proposed transform and present several of its fundamental properties. The combined approach is applied to three illustrative examples, and the obtained exact solutions agree with the corresponding solutions reported in the literature, demonstrating the applicability and effectiveness of the proposed method.
items.authors: Shayea Aldossari, Musa Rahamh GadAllah

items.title: CGRP–RAMP1/CALCRL Signaling Drives TGF-β2-Mediated Immune Evasion and Pancreatic Cancer Progression
items.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is characterized by extensive neural remodeling and a profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, both of which contribute to disease progression and therapeutic resistance. However, whether nociceptor-derived signals directly reprogram PDAC cells to promote immune evasion remains poorly understood. Here, we identify a previously unrecognized tumor-intrinsic neuroimmune mechanism driven by calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) signaling through the receptor complex RAMP1/CALCRL on PDAC cells. CRISPR/Cas9-mediated deletion of Ramp1 or Calcrl did not alter PDAC cell proliferation in vitro but markedly suppressed tumor growth and prolonged survival in immunocompetent mice. These antitumor effects were lost in immunodeficient hosts, indicating that the pro-tumorigenic function of CGRP signaling depends on an intact host immune system. Consistently, tumor cell-specific loss of Ramp1 or Calcrl remodeled the tumor immune microenvironment, enhancing CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell effector activity. Mechanistically, CGRP stimulation promoted TGF-β2 expression and secretion by PDAC cells in a RAMP1-dependent manner. Tumor-derived TGF-β2 subsequently acted in a paracrine fashion to suppress CD8+ T-cell activation and cytotoxic function, whereas genetic disruption of RAMP1 or pharmacological inhibition of TGF-β signaling relieved this immunosuppression. Together, these findings define a CGRP–RAMP1/CALCRL–TGF-β2 signaling axis through which nociceptive input is converted into tumor-driven adaptive immune evasion in PDAC. This pathway reveals a previously underappreciated mechanism linking neural signaling to PDAC progression and identifies CGRP receptor signaling as a potential therapeutic vulnerability for restoring antitumor immunity and improving the responsiveness of PDAC to immunotherapy.
items.authors: Biyu Zhang, Yaxin Li, Simiao Fan, Jiamei Zhang, Yu Zhang, Wen Wang

items.title: Is Receipt of the Bono de Desarrollo Humano Associated with Child Stunting in Ecuador? A Propensity-Score-Matched Analysis of ENDI 2023–2024
items.abstract: This study examines whether current household receipt of Ecuador’s Bono de Desarrollo Humano (BDH) is associated with child stunting using ENDI 2023–2024. The linked dataset included 6345 children; the revised analytical sample comprised 6310, including 792 current recipients. Propensity scores were estimated from 45 substantively selected balancing covariates; multicategory variables were indicator-coded, and sparse categories in eight variables were pooled to avoid complete separation. Kernel matching yielded the most favourable broad-specification balance (mean standardised bias 3.0%; Rubin’s B = 34.3; Rubin’s R = 1.20) and a recipient–non-recipient stunting-prevalence difference of +1.36 percentage points. A survey-weighted linear probability model estimated an adjusted difference of +1.41 points (95% CI −5.38 to +8.19; p = 0.684). A reduced 14-background-covariate kernel model, estimated on the same 6310 observations, yielded +4.87 points and stronger global balance (Rubin’s B = 18.0; Rubin’s R = 1.26), indicating sensitivity to covariate specification. Because ENDI records only current BDH status, not exposure timing, duration or continuity, these findings are adjusted cross-sectional contrasts rather than causal programme effects and do not establish programme ineffectiveness.
items.authors: Patricia Hernández-Medina, Myriam Merino-Rosero, Gladys Sabando-Murillo, María Paublini-Hernández

items.title: Lignin Degradation Potential of Novel Streptomyces Isolates from the Juniperus turcomanica Rhizosphere via Broad-Spectrum Enzymatic Activities
items.abstract: This study provides a comprehensive characterization of Streptomyces isolates associated with the rhizosphere of the centenarian Juniperus turcomanica. Screening for ligninolytic activity revealed that isolates—ATM9, ATM14, ATM15, ATM16, ATM18, and ATM19 synthesize enzymes capable of decolorizing methylene blue and modifying lignosulfonates. Isolates ATM16 and ATM18 demonstrated the highest efficiency in lignosulfonate decomposition, with lignosulfonate becoming undetectable in their culture broth. In the straw lignin degradation process, isolates ATM15 and ATM16 showed the most significant reductions in lignin content (44.2% and 54.8%, respectively), demonstrating promising biodegradation potential. Majority of isolates demonstrated antagonistic activity against fungal strains, while ATM19 completely inhibited the growth of all phytopathogenic fungi tested. Taxonomic identification based on 16S rRNA gene sequencing confirmed that all isolates belong to the genus Streptomyces, with species including S. shaanxiensis (ATM9), S. chryseus (ATM14), S. narbonensis (ATM15), S. venezuelae (ATM16), S. spiroverticillatus (ATM18), S. longhuiensis (ATM19), and Streptomyces sp. (ATM24). Considering our data, S. venezuelae ATM16 and S. spiroverticillatus ATM18 stand out as the most promising strains for biotechnological applications due to their ligninolytic and antagonistic activity against fungal phytopathogens. Furthermore, this study provides the first report on enzymatic and antifungal activities for the recently proposed species S. longhuiensis (ATM19) and S. shaanxiensis (ATM9).
items.authors: Keremli Saparmyradov, Abdulla A. Yergeshov, Bakhtiyar R. Islamov, Altyn K. Rahmanova, Durdymyrat G. Gadamov, Natalia V. Trachtmann

items.title: Clinical Characteristics, Progression of Disease Within 24 Months (POD24), and Real-World Outcomes of Follicular Lymphoma in Saudi Arabia: A Two-Centre Retrospective Analysis
items.abstract: Background: Real-world evidence describing the presentation, management, and outcomes of follicular lymphoma (FL) in Saudi Arabia remains limited, and the frequency and prognostic weight of progression of disease within 24 months of first-line therapy (POD24) have not been reported in this population. This study evaluated the clinicopathological characteristics, treatment patterns, POD24 incidence, and survival outcomes of patients with FL treated at two Saudi tertiary centres. Methods: This two-centre retrospective chart review included adults with histologically confirmed FL diagnosed between November 1999 and May 2025. Overall survival (OS) and first-line progression-free survival (PFS) were measured from the initiation of first-line treatment and estimated using the Kaplan–Meier method. POD24 was defined as progression, relapse, or death from any cause within 24 months of first-line initiation among patients evaluable for that endpoint. Outcomes were additionally examined by calendar era of diagnosis. All group comparisons were unadjusted and exploratory. Results: A total of 139 patients were included. The mean age at diagnosis was 54.7 years (range, 18–91), 61.9% were male, 79.1% had Ann Arbor stage III–IV disease, and 51.1% had an FLIPI score ≥ 3. Bendamustine plus rituximab was the most frequent first-line regimen (43.9%), followed by R-CHOP (30.2%). The overall response rate was 77.0% in the whole cohort and 82.4% among the 125 patients who received response-evaluable systemic first-line therapy. After a median follow-up of 71.0 months, 5-year OS was 92.5% (95% CI, 84.8–96.4) and 5-year PFS was 66.1% (95% CI, 54.9–75.0); the corresponding medians were 210.0 and 114.6 months but were estimated with few patients at risk and should be interpreted cautiously. Among 97 patients evaluable for POD24, the event occurred in 24 (24.7%; 95% CI, 17.2–34.2), and the incidence was stable across calendar eras (23.4% before 2018 versus 24.5% thereafter; p = 1.000). Primary refractory disease accounted for 14 of the 24 events (58.3%). POD24 was associated with poorer ECOG performance status (odds ratio [OR] 11.08; 95% CI, 3.85–31.86), older age (OR 5.27; 95% CI, 2.00–13.89), and higher FLIPI score (OR 3.09; 95% CI, 1.13–8.42). In the 24-month landmark analysis, OS was significantly shorter after POD24 (log-rank p = 0.008), and both documented histological transformations occurred in the POD24 group. Conclusions: Patients with FL in this two-centre Saudi cohort frequently presented with advanced-stage and high-risk disease, yet contemporary anti-CD20-based treatment was associated with favourable long-term survival. Approximately one quarter of evaluable patients experienced POD24, predominantly as primary refractory disease, and this event identified a subgroup with materially inferior subsequent survival. POD24 may help identify patients who warrant closer surveillance and consideration for clinical trials or novel therapies.
items.authors: Mubarak Al-Mansour, Abdulrahman Salah Alharbi, Hadi Abdulhadi Sirdar, Aws Aljohani, Mohammed Abdu Gharwa, Hashim Khalid Alsendi

items.title: Hemerocallis citrina Baroni (Daylily): A Comprehensive Review of Flavonoids and Phenolic Compounds—Extraction, Phytochemistry, Biological Activities, and Food Applications (2000–2026)
items.abstract: Hemerocallis citrina Baroni, commonly known as daylily or “Huang Hua Cai,” is a well-established traditional medicinal and edible plant widely cultivated in East Asia for more than two millennia. Its flower buds, stems, leaves, and roots are rich in flavonoids and phenolic compounds, which constitute the principal bioactive phytochemicals responsible for a wide range of pharmacological effects, including antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, neuroprotective, antidepressant, and sleep-improving activities. Although several studies have investigated the chemical composition of Hemerocallis citrina Baroni, a comprehensive and up-to-date review specifically focused on the flavonoids and phenolic compounds of this plant remains lacking. In this review, we systematically summarize the research progress from 2000 to 2026 on the extraction methods, structural identification, phytochemical profiles, and biological activities of flavonoids and phenolic compounds from H. citrina flower buds, stems, and leaves. Advanced analytical techniques, such as UPLC-PDA/MS, UHPLC-QQQ-MS/MS, and HPLC-Q-TOF-MS, have revealed a diverse array of these compounds, including quercetin, kaempferol, and isorhamnetin glycosides, as well as various caffeoyl- and p-coumaroylquinic acids. The health-promoting effects of these polyphenols, together with current knowledge on their mechanisms of action and potential applications in functional foods and traditional Chinese medicine, are critically discussed. By consolidating recent phytochemical and pharmacological findings, this review provides a scientific foundation for the further development and utilization of H. citrina flavonoids and phenolic compounds as valuable resources for functional foods, nutraceuticals, and natural therapeutics.
items.authors: Salman Khan, Xing Zhang, Muhammad Junaid, Shaohua Huang

items.title: A Pathophysiological Hypothesis of Dorsocervical Fat Pad (Neck Hump), Investing Fascia, Carotid Sheath, and the Promotion of Vascular Patency and Prevention of Thrombosis
items.abstract: Background: Dorsocervical fat pad, commonly referred to as neck hump, is a common soft-tissue lesion at the cervicothoracic junction. Its systemic pathophysiological significance has long been underestimated. Hypothesis: This article proposes the investing fascia–carotid sheath mechanical coupling hypothesis. The hypothesis posits that the deep indurated tissue of the dorsocervical fat pad is not merely fat but rather a fascial–ligamentous–adipose complex. This complex is centered on fibrotic thickening of the superficial layer of the deep cervical fascia (investing fascia) and includes the ligamentum nuchae, supraspinous ligament, trapezius aponeurosis, and surrounding fibrofatty tissue. Once the investing fascia loses its viscoelastic buffering capacity, abnormal shear forces generated by routine micromovements of the head and neck can be transmitted through the deep cervical fascial network to the carotid sheath. Evidence: The carotid sheath is an anatomic hub in which multiple structures coexist within a single sheath. The structures within and adjacent to the sheath can be categorized into six functional domains: arterial perfusion, venous return, lymphatic immune clearance, glymphatic cerebrospinal fluid–interstitial fluid clearance, sympathetic output, and the vagal anti-inflammatory pathway. These six functional domains are not mutually exclusive; rather, they are spatially shared, functionally coupled anatomic–physiologic units. Among these, the arterial baroreflex, sympathetic output, and the vagal anti-inflammatory pathway are neurally related pathways that participate in central integration via the nucleus tractus solitarius (NTS) and related nuclei. Venous return, lymphatic immune clearance, and glymphatic cerebrospinal fluid–interstitial fluid clearance contribute more to amplification through pressure coupling, humoral immunity, and clearance functions. Humoral immunity and pressure-coupling pathways participate in amplifying the pathologic process through mechanisms such as Ang II/AT1R-YAP, GPR146-PIEZO1, and impaired lymphatic clearance. In this hypothesis, these steps constitute a hypothetical positive feedback loop: investing fascia fibrosis → carotid sheath compression → coordinated dysfunction of the six functional domains → elevated blood pressure → pathologic vascular remodeling → increased plaque instability. Elevated blood pressure may, in turn, aggravate investing fascia fibrosis. Increased neck circumference has been clearly associated epidemiologically with cardiovascular events and the progression of carotid atherosclerosis. The latter is one of the important upstream risk factors for cerebral infarction. However, direct population-based evidence linking the dorsocervical fat pad to increased neck circumference remains lacking. Most existing studies have used neck circumference or posterior cervical fat accumulation as surrogate markers; no population-based study has used the dorsocervical fat pad as an inclusion criterion. Implications: Within this framework, eliminating the dorsocervical fat pad—that is, relieving the sustained mechanical constraint of the investing fascia on the carotid sheath—has a pathophysiological rationale worthy of systematic investigation for the prevention of cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases, especially cerebral thrombosis. Nonetheless, this remains a hypothetical inference. Conclusion: This article systematically elaborates the anatomic basis, mechanical transmission mechanisms, pathophysiology of the six functional domains, derivation of the causal chain, relationship between promoting vascular patency and preventing thrombosis and dorsocervical fat pad, testable predictions, and interventional implications of this hypothesis. It also clarifies its evidentiary boundaries.
items.authors: Xuefeng Huang

items.title: Green Compost as a Peat Substitute Under Organic and Organo-Mineral Fertilization: Effects on Growth and Nutrient Status of Photinia and Star Jasmine
items.abstract: Green compost is a promising peat substitute in container nursery production, but plant responses are often species-specific. This study evaluated three growing media containing 0, 36, and 72% (v/v) green compost, replacing none, half, or all of the peat fraction, combined with three fertilization protocols (unfertilized, organic, and organo-mineral), on growth, biomass, biomass allocation, and leaf macronutrients of Photinia × fraseri ‘Red Robin’ and Trachelospermum jasminoides. Fertilization was the main factor affecting growth in both species, with the organo-mineral protocol giving the highest values, whereas substrate composition did not affect aboveground growth. In Photinia, the highest compost proportion reduced root fresh weight and increased leaf K, Ca, and Mg concentrations, mainly under organic fertilization, without improving growth; unfertilized plants allocated more biomass to roots only in the peat-based substrate. In Star Jasmine, complete peat replacement did not reduce plant dry weight. However, root fresh weight decreased, and unfertilized plants in the peat-free substrate did not differ from fertilized ones. Green compost can therefore partly or fully replace peat for these species, provided that adequate fertilization is supplied. The compost pro-portion is adapted to the species.
items.authors: Danilo Loconsole, Giuseppe Cristiano, Nazim S. Gruda, Barbara De Lucia

items.title: Connection of Multi-Valued Topological Groups with Neutrosophic Multi-Valued Functions
items.abstract: The purpose of this paper is to establish a systematic connection between multi-valued topological groups and neutrosophic multi-valued functions. Multi-valued algebraic structures generalize ordinary algebraic operations by allowing the product of two elements to be a nonempty subset rather than a single element. Hypergroups in the sense of Marty constitute one of the principal frameworks for such structures. On the other hand, neutrosophic theory incorporates truth, indeterminacy, and falsity components, while multi-valued neutrosophic sets permit these components to take sets of values rather than single numbers. We introduce a class of neutrosophic multi-valued functions adapted to compact-valued mappings and construct the neutrosophic lift of a multi-valued topological group. We define neutrosophic translations, neutrosophic hyperoperations, neutrosophic inverse maps, neutrosophic subgroups, and neutrosophic continuous homomorphisms. Several structural results are proved. In particular, we show that a Vietoris-continuous multi-valued group operation induces a natural neutrosophic multi-valued group-valued function whenever its three neutrosophic components are Vietoris-continuous. Conversely, suitable level-set conditions allow one to recover the underlying multi-valued topology from the neutrosophic representation. A principal result establishes an equivalence, under natural regularity conditions, between continuity of a neutrosophic multi-valued operation and simultaneous continuity of its truth, indeterminacy, and falsity components. We also investigate neutrosophic α-cuts, level hypergroups, neutrosophic subgroups, homomorphisms, quotient structures, and convergence. The resulting theory provides a bridge between topological hyperstructure theory, set-valued analysis, and neutrosophic mathematics.
items.authors: Saeid Jafari

items.title: A Novel Gear Fault Diagnosis Method Based on COA-VMD, RCMFE and SSA-BP
items.abstract: Aiming at the difficulties in extracting gear fault feature information and the unsatisfactory performance of commonly used machine learning classification models in terms of feature separability and stable within-distribution recognition, this paper proposes a fault diagnosis method combining variational mode decomposition (VMD) optimized by the coati optimization algorithm (COA) and a BP neural network optimized by the sparrow search algorithm (SSA). Firstly, a composite index based on permutation entropy and mutual information entropy is adopted as the fitness function, and the COA is used to optimize the key parameters of VMD to improve the decomposition accuracy of the VMD algorithm. Secondly, the intrinsic mode function (IMF) components sensitive to fault information are selected for signal reconstruction according to the time–frequency-domain comprehensive evaluation factor algorithm, and the refined composite multiscale fuzzy entropy (RCMFE) is used to extract the features of the reconstructed signal to form a state feature set. Finally, the SSA is employed to optimize the parameters of the BP model to achieve accurate diagnosis of gear working conditions and fault types. The proposed method is verified using measured gear single and compound fault data and compared with commonly used signal decomposition methods and machine learning classification models. The results show that the proposed method can effectively extract gear fault feature information and has the advantages of high accuracy, good feature separability and stable within-distribution recognition. It can achieve ideal diagnosis accuracy for both single and compound gear faults, providing a certain reference for solving such problems.
items.authors: Duowen Chen, Haoze Lv, Xinze Li, Wenjie Liang, Kailin Bai, Xin Zhao

items.title: Mechanisms and Research Progress of LncRNA-Mediated Regulation of Viral Infections
items.abstract: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), a class of RNA molecules whose transcripts exceed 200 nucleotides in length and typically lack protein-coding capacity, were once widely regarded as “transcriptional noise.” However, recent studies have shown that lncRNAs can encode small peptides and play critical roles in biological processes, including gene expression regulation, cell differentiation, and immune response. Viral infections, as a common disease, can reshape the transcriptome of host cells, in which the differential expression of lncRNAs is a core link in host–virus interactions. This review aims to deeply analyze the multidimensional regulatory mechanisms of lncRNAs in the host antiviral innate immune response. It elaborates in detail on how lncRNAs construct the host antiviral defense by regulating pattern recognition receptor (PRR) signaling pathways, the production and signal transduction of interferons (IFNs), as well as the expression of interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs). Additionally, we conducted an in-depth analysis of the complex functions of lncRNAs in regulating programmed cell death (PCD), including key processes such as pyroptosis, autophagy, and apoptosis, and integrated specific research cases in infections caused by multiple significant viruses, including influenza A virus (IAV), human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). We aim to provide novel strategies for the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of viral diseases.
items.authors: Menghua Peng, Fenfang Luo, Ning Li

items.title: Object-Based Reconstruction of Mining-Associated Water Body Lifecycles from Multisource Satellite Time Series
