items.abstract: Mining-associated water bodies are typically mapped as independent annual patches, obscuring their formation, transformation and continuity over time. Changes in visible water therefore need to be distinguished from changes in water body identity and surface state. Here, we develop an object-based, interval-aware framework to reconstruct water body lifecycles across seven domains in the Huainan and Huaibei coalfields, China, separating persistent identity from geometry and surface state. The framework integrates Landsat, Sentinel-2, PlanetScope and RapidEye imagery with contextual evidence to interpret changes and constrain event timing. Across these domains, the screened visible water area increased by 853.0 ha between the 2015–2017 and 2022–2024 epochs, comprising 1758.4 ha of gain and 905.4 ha of loss. The case histories documented continuity under photovoltaic cover and engineered subdivision, as well as terrestrial surface conversion with an unresolved termination status. In the examined cases, the changes in area and component overlap did not uniquely identify lifecycle events without temporal and spatial context evidence. Dense image sequences documented the early development and expansion of individual water bodies and bounded coalescence events. An independent blinded review reproduced 94.4% (17/18) of identity-relation decisions and all endpoint decisions in the original review sample. By distinguishing object continuity from visible water change, the framework complements area-based monitoring by providing evidence of water body lifecycle processes.
items.authors: Xiao Chen, Shihao Hu, Guangming Zhao, Jucai Chang, Yuhan Huang

items.title: Localiser-Based Software-Assisted Patient Positioning in Chest CT: A Propensity Score-Matched Study
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Vertical off-centring in chest CT impairs bowtie-filter beam-hardening correction, degrading noise uniformity and image quality. iCentering derives the patient’s geometric centre from a single posteroanterior localiser and automatically adjusts table height. This study aimed to evaluate whether iCentering reduces off-centring distance (OCD) and improves image quality versus manual positioning in chest CT, and to investigate correlations between OCD and noise characteristics. Methods: In this retrospective, single-centre study, 192 propensity score-matched pairs from 423 adults undergoing non-contrast chest CT were analysed. OCD, objective image quality (standard deviation (SD), signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), figure of merit (FOM)), noise distribution ratio (NDRA-P), and radiation dose indices were measured. Paired comparisons employed t-tests or Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) and effect sizes reported. Directionally stratified Spearman correlation and multivariable regression examined OCD–noise associations. Results: Intra- and inter-observer reliability was good to excellent (ICC 0.87–0.99 for OCD; 0.75–0.97 for most regions of interest). iCentering moved median OCD closer to zero at all levels (Level 1: −7.25 vs. −29.40 mm; Level 2: −1.45 vs. −22.00 mm; Level 3: 7.45 vs. −11.90 mm; all p 0.001; r range: 0.76–0.77). Regarding image quality, SD decreased and SNR, CNR, and FOM increased at all levels (all p 0.001), while NDRA-P approached 1.00 (p 0.05). Radiation dose indices were unchanged (p 0.05). OCD correlated with SD (|ρ| = 0.478 – 0.812, p 0.001); regression confirmed independent associations in both strata (OCD 0: β range: −0.068 to −0.079, R2 = 0.52–0.65; OCD 0: β range: 0.056–0.078, R2 = 0.28–0.54), whereas the association between OCD and NDRA-P was weak. Conclusions: iCentering improves centring accuracy and objective image quality in chest CT, without increasing radiation exposure. Reduced OCD is independently associated with lower image noise, underscoring the value of precise centring.
items.authors: Xinnan Shen, Li Tao, Wen Li, Youhong Cao, Jianping Liu, Yiting Wang

items.title: The Relationship Between 3D Printing Technology and STEM Education Outcomes: The Moderating Role of Institutional Infrastructure in Ethiopian Secondary Schools
items.abstract: The integration of 3D printing technology (3DPT) into STEM education has transformed teaching and learning through experiential and design-based approaches. However, the effectiveness of this technology is largely shaped by the institutional environment in which it is implemented. This study investigates the moderating role of institutional infrastructure in the relationship between 3DPT and STEM education outcomes (STEMO) in Ethiopian secondary schools. A quantitative cross-sectional survey design was employed, involving 368 participants from secondary schools equipped with STEM and 3D printing facilities. Data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM). The results indicate that the dimension of 3DPT are positively associated STEMO, with frequency of use, instructional integration, and access to digital resources showing stronger associations than availability alone. In addition, both human and digital infrastructures were positively associated with STEMO. The significant interaction effects further indicate that institutional infrastructure moderates the association between 3D printing technology and STEM education outcomes. The study contributes to educational technology literature by integrating constructivism, experiential learning, socio-technical systems theory, and connectivism into a unified explanatory framework. The findings provide empirical evidence from a developing-country context and highlight the importance of institutional readiness in maximizing the educational benefits of 3D printing technology in STEM education.
items.authors: Tekalign Lemma Woldassilasie, Hirpa G. Lemu, Birhane Desta Atsegeba, Moti Melkamu Abera

items.title: Institutional Readiness and the Boundaries of AI Adoption: Evidence from UAE Newsrooms
items.abstract: As Artificial Intelligence (AI) becomes embedded in newsroom operations, organizations invest in AI readiness on the assumption that preparedness travels with successful outcomes. Readiness frameworks typically aggregate diverse outcomes into composite performance measures, leaving it unclear whether readiness explains each equally well. This study examines the explanatory scope of institutional AI readiness in UAE newsrooms using a cross-sectional survey of a purposive sample of 336 media professionals. Three collection streams were harmonized and outcomes analyzed separately rather than aggregated. The seven readiness indicators showed high internal consistency (α = 0.919) and a dominant first component accounting for 67.7% of item variance; the four conceptual domains behind the instrument were not recovered as separable dimensions, a pattern that may partly reflect a general evaluative disposition toward the organization. A one-standard-deviation increase in readiness was associated with 2.59 times higher odds of deeper adoption (95% CI [1.88, 3.56]) and with greater training provision and perceived return on AI investment, but not with practitioners’ perceived quality of Arabic-language AI output, measured with a single item (ρ = 0.097). Because one readiness indicator concerns current AI use, all estimates were re-estimated without it: the odds ratio was 2.38 (95% CI [1.74, 3.25]), the organizational associations remained significant, and the association with perceived Arabic-language output quality remained non-significant (ρ = 0.095). Institutional readiness, therefore, appears to have a bounded explanatory domain in these data, showing stronger associations with organizational implementation outcomes than with perceived output quality. Because the design is cross-sectional and not all respondents answered outcome items, these are statements of association, not of effect. Studies relying on composite measures may overstate their explanatory reach.
items.authors: Elsayed Darwish, Ahmed Al Mansoori

items.title: Quantum Corrections as a Bound for Detecting Self-Interacting Ultralight Dark Matter
items.abstract: We investigate the implications of interactions between ultralight dark matter (ULDM) and Standard Model fermions for the radiative stability of the ULDM potential. By matching the heavy fermion onto a low-energy scalar effective field theory, we derive the one-loop threshold corrections to the ULDM mass and self-interaction couplings. We interpret these corrections in terms of radiative naturalness conditions defined within the threshold-matching prescription adopted here. For the parameter region motivated by cosmological and galactic considerations, the quadratic correction provides the strongest naturalness criterion. The precise numerical contour associated with this criterion is prescription-dependent. Nevertheless, the calculation exhibits the generic sensitivity of an unprotected ultralight scalar mass to the heavy-fermion scale. For the benchmark boundary condition aR(mf)=0 and for Yukawa couplings satisfying the scalar-mass naturalness criterion, both the direct and cubic-induced quartic corrections remain subdominant relative to the cosmologically required quartic coupling.
items.authors: Jae-Weon Lee, Chueng-Ryong Ji

items.title: Functional Response and Predation Potential of Arma custos (Fabricius) Against Tuta absoluta (Meyrick)
items.abstract: The tomato leafminer, Tuta absoluta (Meyrick) (Lepidoptera: Gelechiidae), is a globally invasive pest causing severe economic losses in tomato production. We evaluated the predatory stink bug Arma custos (Fabricius) (Hemiptera: Pentatomidae) using functional-response assays, a predator-density experiment, behavioral observations, Y-tube olfactometer bioassays, and a greenhouse cage trial. Depletion-aware maximum-likelihood models supported a Type III response for adult females feeding on second-instar larvae, whereas Type II models were retained for fifth-instar nymphs and adults feeding on fourth-instar larvae. At an initial density of 40 larvae, females consumed 16.2 ± 0.2 second-instar or 17.4 ± 0.5 fourth-instar larvae within 24 h. With 40 fourth-instar larvae available per arena, increasing female density from one to five reduced per capita consumption from 17.40 ± 0.51 to 5.44 ± 0.04 larvae per day. The Hassell–Varley model provided the best fit (m = 0.725; 95% CI, 0.693–0.755). In greenhouse cages, releasing three females per cage reduced cumulative damaged leaves by 60.12% by day 15. No active larvae were detected in release cages at that time, compared with 11.33 ± 0.33 in controls. Females preferred infested over healthy tomato plants, whereas males showed no significant preference. These findings demonstrate that A. custos is a promising biological control agent for integrated pest management (IPM) of T. absoluta.
items.authors: Yuyang Jiang, Yan Zhao, Xiujie Li, Linli Peng, Sheng-Yen Wu, Youming Hou

items.title: MdNHL8, an NDR1/HIN1-like Gene, Enhances Resistance Against Apple Ring Rot
items.abstract: Apple ring rot, caused by Botryosphaeria dothidea, represents a major challenge for apple cultivation worldwide. However, the genetic factors that confer resistance in apples are not well understood. This study utilized time-series transcriptome profiling, combined with weighted gene co-expression network analysis and previously identified quantitative trait loci, leading to the identification of MdNHL8 as a candidate gene linked to resistance. A genome-wide examination of the apple NDR1/HIN1-like gene family revealed 57 members with diverse conserved domains, confirming that MdNHL8 features a distinct RBR-type E3 ligase domain. Subcellular localization experiments showed that MdNHL8 is localized in the nucleus and plasma membrane. Functional assays indicated that overexpression of MdNHL8 enhances resistance to apple ring rot and significantly elevates the expression of MdPR1, whereas silencing this gene does not enhance resistance and exhibits a trend toward increased susceptibility. Furthermore, additional transcriptome sequencing analysis of MdNHL8 transgenic calli highlighted a turquoise module closely linked to MdNHL8-mediated resistance, identifying MdCYCB3, MdEIX2, and MdABC4 as candidate downstream genes with expression patterns tightly correlated with MdNHL8. This research identifies MdNHL8 as a positive regulator in apple defense against B. dothidea and provides a basis for further exploring the regulatory network centered on MdNHL8 in disease resistance, offering insights for future breeding efforts aimed at enhancing resistance to apple ring rot.
items.authors: Wenyan Zheng, Ping He, Xiaowen He, Sen Wang, Yongxu Wang, Yue Ma

items.title: PGP-5 Influences ZIP-2-Dependent Innate Immune Response During Streptococcus gordonii Exposure in Caenorhabditis elegans
items.abstract: Innate immune responses in Caenorhabditis elegans are regulated by multiple effectors that are activated upon bacterial exposure. In this study, we investigated the role of pgp-5, a transmembrane efflux transporter implicated in cellular stress responses and detoxification in host defense against Streptococcus gordonii. S. gordonii produces hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) as a major virulence factor and induces oxidative stress in host cells. Exposure to wild-type S. gordonii induced robust pgp-5p::GFP expression, whereas the H2O2-deficient spxB mutant elicited significantly lower reporter activity, suggesting that pgp-5 activation is associated with spxB-dependent H2O2 production. Previous studies have established that the bZIP transcription factor ZIP-2 is required for pgp-5 expression in C. elegans under xenobiotic stress conditions. However, whether pathogen-induced pgp-5 expression similarly depends on ZIP-2 remains unknown. In addition, the potential role of pgp-5 in regulating ZIP-2-dependent immune responses has not been explored. To address these questions, we examined pgp-5p::GFP expression and activation of the ZIP-2-dependent innate immune reporter irg-1p::GFP following RNAi-mediated knockdown of pgp-5 and zip-2 during exposure to wild-type and spxB mutant S. gordonii. Knockdown of zip-2 abolished S. gordonii-induced pgp-5p::GFP expression compared with empty vector control-treated worms, demonstrating that pathogen-induced pgp-5 expression is dependent on ZIP-2. In contrast, knockdown of pgp-5 resulted in significantly increased expression of irg-1p::GFP following S. gordonii exposure. These findings suggest that loss of PGP-5 enhances expression of the ZIP-2-responsive gene irg-1 under S. gordonii-induced stress, indicating that PGP-5 may influence the magnitude of the associated immune response in C. elegans.
items.authors: Boopathi Balasubramaniam, Judith Leon Jaramillo, Julia Stefanik, Thy Thy Nguyen, Mandi Morris, Ransome van der Hoeven

items.title: From Host Response to Microbiological Risk: Association of the RIN-IM Score with Culture-Positive Sepsis and Antimicrobial Resistance in Critically Ill Adults
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Early identification of microbiologically confirmed sepsis and antimicrobial-resistant infection remains challenging in critically ill patients. The renal–inflammatory–nutritional–metabolic (RIN-IM) score integrates serum creatinine, the systemic immune-inflammation index, pan-immune inflammation value, serum albumin, and triglyceride–glucose index. This study investigated the association of the RIN-IM score with culture-positive sepsis and antimicrobial resistance phenotypes in critically ill adults. Methods: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 318 adults with sepsis admitted to the intensive care unit between 1 January 2023 and 31 March 2026. The RIN-IM score was calculated from laboratory measurements obtained within 24 h and categorized as low (0–3), intermediate (4–6), or high risk (7–10). The primary outcome was culture-positive sepsis. Secondary analyses, restricted to patients with culture-positive sepsis, examined associations between RIN-IM and multidrug-resistant (MDR), extensively drug-resistant (XDR), and pandrug-resistant phenotypes. Results: Culture-positive sepsis was identified in 154 patients (48.4%). The median RIN-IM score was higher in culture-positive than in culture-negative patients (6 [interquartile range, 4–8] vs. 4 [2,3,4,5]; p 0.001). Culture positivity increased from 29.1% in the low-risk group to 50.4% in the intermediate-risk group and 74.6% in the high-risk group. Each one-point increase in RIN-IM was independently associated with culture-positive sepsis (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.35; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.21–1.51), while high- versus low-risk classification was associated with an aOR of 4.65 (95% CI, 2.25–9.62). Among culture-positive patients, 67 (43.5%) had MDR, and 20 (13.0%) had XDR infections. Each one-point score increase was independently associated with MDR infection (aOR, 1.29; 95% CI, 1.12–1.48). The exploratory XDR analysis was based on 20 events and used Firth’s bias-reduced logistic regression; a one-point score increase was associated with XDR infection (aOR, 1.29; 95% CI, 1.09–1.52), but the categorical estimates were imprecise. The score demonstrated moderate discrimination for culture-positive sepsis (AUC, 0.752; 95% CI, 0.699–0.805) and MDR infection (AUC, 0.724; 95% CI, 0.643–0.805); discrimination for XDR infection was exploratory (AUC, 0.742; 95% CI, 0.635–0.849). Twenty-eight-day mortality increased from 13.6% to 27.7% and 47.9% across the three risk categories (p 0.001). Conclusions: Higher admission RIN-IM scores were associated with culture-positive sepsis. Among patients with culture-positive sepsis, higher scores were also associated with MDR infection; this subgroup analysis was conditioned on microbiological confirmation and should not be interpreted as prediction of resistant infection in the overall sepsis population. The association with XDR infection was exploratory, based on only 20 events, and requires confirmation in larger independent cohorts. Because RIN-IM assessment and microbiological sampling were not fully time-synchronized, these findings should not be interpreted as real-time microbiological prediction or evidence of clinical utility. RIN-IM should not replace culture-based diagnosis, susceptibility testing, individual risk-factor assessment, local antibiograms, or clinical judgment. The observed associations do not establish a direct biological relationship between RIN-IM and microbial burden or antimicrobial resistance.
items.authors: Davut Ipek, Yusuf Ipek, Recep Dokuyucu

items.title: Consumer Perceptions and Eating Behavior Towards Low-Carbohydrate Functional Bakery Products: A Cross-Sectional Study
items.abstract: The growing interest in foods with low glycemic impact and improved functionality has stimulated research into reformulating traditional bakery products. Therefore, this study aimed to assess consumer perceptions, consumption habits, and willingness of the population to accept low-carbohydrate bakery products enriched with natural bioactive extracts in order to substantiate the development of innovative recipes within doctoral research in the field of food science and technology. A cross-sectional survey was conducted using an online questionnaire given to a sample of 510 respondents, aged between 18 and 55 years, providing a cross-sectional perspective on the preferences of different age categories. Data were statistically analyzed using the Chi-square (χ2) test of independence (p 0.05) to evaluate associations between socio-demographic characteristics and consumer attitudes toward low-carbohydrate bakery products. The results showed that 63.2% of respondents were familiar or very familiar with low-carbohydrate products, while 49.0% considered reducing sugar and refined carbohydrate intake important or extremely important. A healthy lifestyle (64.7%) and body weight control (42.1%) were identified as the main motivations for adopting a low-carbohydrate diet. Furthermore, 42.0% of respondents expressed interest in trying a low-carbohydrate diet, although they had not previously followed one. Significant associations were observed between age, education level, and interest in low-carbohydrate diets, as well as the perceived importance of reducing sugar intake (p 0.001). Overall, respondents reported favorable perceptions of low-carbohydrate bakery products and products perceived as having a lower glycemic impact and containing bioactive ingredients, although purchase intentions were associated with sensory quality and affordability. These findings provide insights into consumer perceptions and acceptance of low-carbohydrate bakery products among the surveyed respondents. However, given the convenience sampling approach and demographic composition of the sample, the results should be interpreted cautiously and cannot be considered representative of the Romanian population. Further studies based on more representative population samples are warranted.
items.authors: Cristian Argyelan, Sylvestre Dossa, Virgil Dacian Lalescu, Monica Negrea, Calin Jianu, Victor Emil Alexa

items.title: Effect of Post-Swaging Annealing on Charpy Impact Behavior of Metastable Austenitic Stainless Steel
items.abstract: The development of steels with good mechanical properties is essential for high-strength and deflection fabrications. This paper investigates the effect of annealing temperature on the dynamic mechanical behavior, microstructural response, and fracture mechanisms under impact loading of a gradient-structured AISI 321 metastable austenitic stainless steel (MASS). A gradient distribution of α′-martensite; austenite grains with γ-fiber, B/B̅, and rotation cube orientations; and α′-martensite/δ-ferrite grains with α-fiber, D1/D2, and F orientations was detected in the radial direction of an as-swaged bar. The program steel after post-swaging annealing in the low-temperature range (550–650 °C) exhibits increased Charpy V-notch impact toughness due to an increase in crack propagation energy. The toughening is associated with the formation of microvoids within wide microzones with the γ-fiber orientation and along phase boundaries, which are elongated in the axial direction of the bar. Therefore, crack deflection along these lines occurs. In fact, a workpiece with a combination of high dynamic strength and good Charpy impact toughness is derived. The effects of post-swaging annealing conditions on the microstructure/texture evolution, crack nucleation energy, crack propagation energy, dynamic strength, and fracture mechanisms are revealed and discussed. Thus, a strategy for obtaining strengthened and toughened MASSs is proposed.
items.authors: Dmitrii Panov, Egor Kudryavtsev, Ruslan Chernichenko, Stanislav Naumov, K. Chandra Sekhar, Alexey Pertcev

items.title: Why Do Dietary Saponins Produce Inconsistent Responses in Ruminants? A Review
items.abstract: Saponins are structurally diverse plant-derived glycosides that have attracted increasing interest as phytogenic feed additives for improving the efficiency and sustainability of ruminant production. This narrative review critically examines the structural characteristics, biological activities, and nutritional applications of dietary saponins, with particular emphasis on the links between molecular structure, rumen microbial modulation, and animal responses. Saponins are broadly classified as steroidal or triterpenoid compounds, and differences in their aglycone structure, glycosylation pattern, and botanical origin contribute substantially to their biological activity. Evidence from in vitro and in vivo studies indicates that dietary saponins can alter rumen microbial populations, particularly protozoa, and consequently influence volatile fatty acid production, ammonia metabolism, microbial protein synthesis, nutrient utilization, and enteric methane emissions. Their potential benefits extend beyond ruminal fermentation to animal health, antioxidant and metabolic responses, reproductive function, and milk and meat quality. However, responses are inconsistent across studies and are strongly influenced by saponin source, chemical composition, dose, basal diet, animal species, physiological status, and microbial adaptation. Recent evidence suggests that moderate supplementation can provide beneficial effects without compromising feed intake, whereas excessive inclusion may impair fiber degradation and nutrient digestibility. The review therefore emphasizes that saponin efficacy should not be evaluated solely on total concentration but in relation to chemical structure and feeding conditions. Finally, major knowledge gaps are identified, including the need for standardized saponin preparations, species-specific supplementation strategies, improved understanding of microbial adaptation and structure–activity relationships, and long-term validation under commercial production conditions.
items.authors: Maghsoud Besharati, Sina Salimolnafs, Deniz Azhir

items.title: Evaluation of the Prevalence, Perception, and Factors Associated with Obesity Among Pharmacy Students
items.abstract: Background: Obesity is a growing public health concern among university students and is influenced by lifestyle and behavioral factors. This study assessed the prevalence of being overweight and obesity and their associated lifestyle factors among pharmacy students. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted among undergraduate pharmacy students at the College of Pharmacy, National University of Sciences and Technology, Muscat, Oman. Data were collected using a validated questionnaire covering sociodemographic characteristics, anthropometric measurements, dietary habits, physical activity, sleep, stress-related behaviors, and obesity perceptions. BMI was calculated from measured height and weight. Descriptive statistics and Chi-square tests were performed using SPSS (p 0.05). Results: The sample size of this study was 139. The prevalence of overweight and obesity was 42.4%. More than 46% of students consumed fast food, 41% frequently snacked between meals, and over 43% reported late-night eating. Sedentary behaviors were common, with 64% reporting prolonged sitting. Academic stress affected over 59% of participants, while 37% reported stress-related eating. BMI was significantly associated with stress-related eating (p = 0.034) and family history of obesity (p = 0.002). Conclusions: Overweight and obesity were common among pharmacy students, highlighting the need for targeted university-based interventions.
items.authors: Shima Sarahan Al Rashdi, Noor Ali Abduljabar Al-Matooq, Fatma Radhi Al Zari, Ghayadah Rashid Al-Qurri, Mohammad Abobakr Al-Ghazali
items.category_raw: Journal of the Oman Medical Association

items.title: Geometry-Conditioned Conformal Calibration for Guaranteed False-Alarm Control in Uncertain Nonlinear Photovoltaic Systems
items.abstract: A fault detector inside an active fault-tolerant loop drives an automatic action, so every false alarm commands a reconfiguration for a fault that is absent. In a photovoltaic (PV) plant the false-alarm rate has to be controlled within each operating regime, because the healthy uncertainty changes with the position of the sun as inter-row shading switches bypass diodes into conduction. Monitoring limits, including kernel-density ones, fix one threshold over the whole fault-free record, and conformal calibration guarantees the rate only on average across regimes. This work analyses 33 measured days from a 100.44 kWp sub-array near Madrid (Spain) at the inverter’s native 5 min resolution. Conformal calibration is conditioned on a solar-elevation partition frozen before any evaluation and compared with three alternative calibrations of the same anomaly score, on measured healthy data and on 148 injected fault events. The standard deviation of the healthy voltage residual grows by a factor of 5.15 from high to low sun, and normality is rejected in every regime. At a significance level of 0.05 the conditioned calibration keeps the realised false-alarm rate between 5.4% and 6.2% in all four regimes, while pooled calibration diverges across them by a factor of 58.3. At a level of 0.01 a healthy string requests a spurious reconfiguration at worst every 6.3 h, against every 66 to 87 min under the alternatives. The guarantee has a price, as event detection at the 0.05 level falls from 98.0% to 90.5%, with the loss in the low-sun regime that a deterministic bound on the same uncertainty predicts. The partition needs only the site coordinates and the timestamp, so the construction transfers to other plants.
items.authors: Moath Bani Melhem, Arsenio Barbón, Ramy Georgious, Luis Bayón

items.title: A High-Resolution Remote Sensing Image Building Extraction Model Based on Spectral Index Gated Attention and Transfer Learning
items.abstract: High-resolution remote sensing building extraction often requires large amounts of manually labeled data, and models trained on one dataset may not perform equally well on another without additional annotations. To reduce this dependency on labeled target data, we propose SIGA-UNet3+, which combines a Spectral Index Gated Attention (SIGA) module with a transfer learning strategy. The SIGA module fuses DSBI, NDVI, and NDWI to emphasize building features and suppress vegetation/water interference. Pre-training on the public SpaceNet dataset followed by fine-tuning on a self-built GF-2 dataset (Changchun, China) allows the model to adapt with limited local labels. On SpaceNet, SIGA-UNet3+ achieves F1 = 83.21% and IoU = 70.19%, obtaining the best overall segmentation performance among the compared methods. On the GF-2 dataset, it attains F1 = 84.56% and IoU = 72.17%. Moreover, using only 10% of the GF-2 training samples, transfer learning improves the F1 score by 6–8 percentage points compared to training from scratch. These results indicate that SIGA-UNet3+ can provide a promising and data-efficient approach for high-resolution remote sensing building extraction.
items.authors: Jinchen Zhu, Shengbo Chen, Xitong Xu, Liang Cui, Yaqi Zhang, Jiaqi Yang

items.title: Comparative Detection of IDH1 R132H and TERT Promoter Mutations in Plasma and Cerebrospinal Fluid of Patients with Glioma Using Targeted Droplet Digital PCR
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Molecular profiling is essential for glioma classification, but in some cases tissue sampling may be limited, whereas reported detectability of cell-free tumor DNA (cftDNA) in plasma and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) varies considerably. The aim of this study was to compare the detection rates and concentrations of cftDNA carrying IDH1 R132H and TERT promoter C228T/C250T mutations in paired plasma and CSF samples, as well as to examine associated clinical characteristics. Methods: 66 patients with WHO grade 1–4 gliomas were enrolled before surgery. Preoperative plasma and lumbar CSF were collected before tissue-damaging procedures. Cell-free DNA (cfDNA) was isolated from 5 mL of plasma and 2.5–5.0 mL of CSF and analyzed using mutation-specific droplet digital PCR (ddPCR) assays. Results: cfDNA was available from 65 CSF and 63 plasma samples. Total cfDNA concentration was lower in CSF than in plasma (medians: 434.1 vs. 1240.3 copies/mL; p 0.001). Nevertheless, cftDNA carrying at least one of the assayed mutations was detected in 14/65 CSF samples (21.5%) and in 0/63 plasma samples (0.0%) (p 0.001). IDH1 R132H was detected in 4.6% of CSF samples, and TERT promoter mutations were detected in 16.9%. Every CSF mutation with available paired tissue data was also identified in the corresponding tumor. Glioma grade 4 and contrast-enhancing tumors were associated with higher CSF cfDNA, cftDNA carrying at least one of the assayed mutations, and mutant allele fraction values (p 0.05), whereas tumor size and localization were not significantly associated with these parameters (p 0.05). Conclusions: With the presented targeted ddPCR workflow, lumbar CSF was substantially more informative than plasma for detecting the selected glioma-associated mutations. CSF cftDNA analysis may complement tissue profiling, although broader panels and larger prospective studies are needed to establish its clinical sensitivity.
items.authors: Mark Jain, Tagir Rahmatullin, Ivan Alexeev, Ariadna Gomershtat, Margarita Gundobina, Larisa Samokhodskaya

items.title: Juvenile Spontaneous Mediastinal Hemorrhage with Suspect Trauma
items.abstract: A 6-month-old intact female American Pitbull (Canis lupus familiaris) underwent forensic evaluation for suspected blunt force trauma. Postmortem computed tomography (PMCT) identified pleural hyperattenuating soft tissue attenuating material, consistent with clotted blood, pleural effusion, a large thymus, and moderate to severe cranial mediastinal expansion with mixed fluid and lower-attenuation, soft tissue attenuating material. Histology confirmed thymic hemorrhage, while autopsy identified hemothorax, pleural blood clots, and hemomediastinum, excluding trauma, most consistent with spontaneous idiopathic thymic hemorrhage. This case highlights the utility of identifying hyperattenuating clot formation on PMCT, like the sentinel clot sign, for localizing antemortem hemorrhage and improving antemortem-postmortem correlation in forensic investigations.
items.authors: Abigail G. Uhrinek, Katharine E. Peper, Adam W. Stern, Federico R. Vilaplana Grosso

items.title: Grafting of Black Pepper onto Native Piper Species
items.abstract: Brazil is the third largest producer of black pepper in the world. Although Brazil is prominent in black pepper production, the average yield is low. The main stressful factors in Brazilian black pepper crops directly affect the root system, such as water deficit, flooding and diseases. One strategy to enable the cultivation of black pepper in contaminated areas is the planting of seedlings grafted onto wild Piper species resistant to fusariosis, drought or flooding. Grafting consists of the union of plant tissues from at least two different plants to generate a single organism. However, many factors influence graft incompatibility, the main ones being botanical affinity, which is directly linked to genetic and morphological factors, environmental conditions and physiological factors. The objective of this work was to investigate the compatibility and physiology of grafted seedlings of ‘bragantina’ black pepper, using three rootstocks. The experiment was conducted at the Linhares Experimental Farm, of the Capixaba Institute for Research, Technical Assistance and Rural Extension. Piper aduncum, Piper caldense and the cultivar bragantina (Piper nigrum) were evaluated as rootstock. The native species were propagated by seeds and the bragantina cultivar by cuttings, both propagules collected from mother plants in the Active Germplasm Bank located on the farm. The full cleft top method was carried out. The rootstocks were decapitated just below the fourth node, in which a slit was made, 3 cm deep, and after insertion of the graft, it was tied with a rubber band. The grafts were covered with plastic bags. After grafting, the plants were kept in a nursery. Four months after grafting, survival, chlorophyll a fluorescence, gas exchange, hydraulic conductivity of the stem and root, shoot and root anatomy were assessed. At the end of the experiment, the survival rate was higher in plants grafted onto Piper caldense. P. aduncum showed an increase in the number of active FSII reaction centers by cross sections (RC/CS0). The photosynthetic performance index relative to absorption (PIabs) was increased in P. aduncum. P. caldense and bragantina showed no significant difference. Water use efficiency (WUE) was higher in P. caldense plants, followed by bragantina plants. P. aduncum showed a decrease in WUE. P. aduncum showed an increase in the length of the vascular bundle and root xylem, however P. caldense showed reduced values. Regarding the number of root xylem vessels, the highest values were observed in bragantina plants. The diameter of the root xylem vessels was higher in P. aduncum. P. caldense and bragantina showed no difference. It is concluded that among the species studied, P. caldense was the species that presented the most characteristics that make it compatible with being used as a rootstock using the bragantina genotype as a graft.
items.authors: Basílio Cerri Neto, Vinicius de Souza Oliveira, Johnatan Jair de Paula Marchiori, Jeane Crasque, Thayanne Rangel Ferreira, Simone Alves Fernandes

items.title: Effect of the Application of Seaweed and Fishing Industry Derivatives on the Soil Microbial Community and Performance of Common Bean Plants
items.abstract: The rhizosphere microbiome plays a key role in plant nutrition, development, and productivity and is strongly influenced by soil management practices. This study evaluated increasing rates of a marine-derived organo-mineral fertilizer based on seaweed and fishing industry derivatives (0, 1.4, 2.8, and 4.2 g pot−1) on plant gas exchange, yield components, rhizosphere bacterial community structure, and predicted microbial functions in common bean (Phaseolus vulgaris L.) under greenhouse conditions. Fertilization did not significantly affect plant gas exchange (p 0.05), whereas the highest mean values for yield components were observed at 2.8 g pot−1. Organo-mineral fertilization significantly altered rhizosphere bacterial community structure (PERMANOVA, p 0.001) and Shannon diversity, whereas estimated richness (Chao1) was not significantly affected. Treatment-associated shifts in bacterial genera and predicted metabolic pathways were detected, particularly at the highest fertilizer rate, but none remained significant after FDR correction. Overall, marine-derived organo-mineral fertilization was associated with changes in common bean yield components and rhizosphere bacterial community structure, without detectable effects on gas exchange at the vegetative stage. These findings demonstrate the potential of marine-derived organo-mineral fertilization to simultaneously influence crop performance and rhizosphere bacterial communities, supporting its application as an input for integrated nutrient management in common bean production.
items.authors: Hélio Danilo Quevedo, Bernardo de Almeida Halfeld-Vieira, Artur Alves, Glória Pinto, Marta Tacão, Eunice Reis Batista

items.title: VGLL4 Suppresses Malignant Phenotypes of Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma Cells Through Modulation of Hippo/YAP and Wnt/β-Catenin Signaling Pathways
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), the most common and aggressive subtype of kidney cancer, continues to face challenges in early diagnosis and treatment, driving the need for reliable biomarkers and therapeutic targets. Vestigial-like family member 4 (VGLL4), a transcriptional cofactor, has been identified as a tumor suppressor in several malignancies. However, its clinical significance, biological functions, and underlying mechanisms in ccRCC remain largely unknown. Methods: In this study, we examined VGLL4 expression in ccRCC and normal tissues at both mRNA and protein levels and analyzed its correlation with clinicopathological features and patient prognosis. Functional experiments were performed to evaluate the effects of VGLL4 overexpression on ccRCC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion in vitro, as well as tumor growth in vivo. Integrated transcriptomic profiling and immunoblot validation were employed to explore the underlying signaling pathways. Results: We found that VGLL4 was downregulated in ccRCC tissues compared to normal counterparts at both mRNA and protein levels, and its low expression correlates with advanced disease stage and poorer overall survival. Functional experiments demonstrated that VGLL4 overexpression significantly suppressed the proliferation, migration, and invasion of ccRCC cells in vitro and effectively hindered tumor growth in vivo. Mechanistically, integrated transcriptomic profiling and immunoblot validation suggest that the tumor-suppressive effects of VGLL4 are mediated through the coordinated modulation of the Hippo/YAP and Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathways, at least in part by attenuating the activation and transcriptional activities of YAP and β-catenin. Conclusions: Collectively, these findings establish VGLL4 as a tumor suppressor in ccRCC and highlight its potential as a prognosis-related biomarker and candidate therapeutic target through its dual regulatory role in Hippo/YAP and Wnt/β-catenin signaling cascades.
items.authors: Yaru Zhang, Shuyao Wang, Zhipeng Zhao, Tao Yuan, Changyu Zhu, Lei Zhong

items.title: Integrated Soil–Crop System Management Promotes Microbial Necromass and Soil Organic Carbon Sequestration in Black Soil Through Microbial Transformation and Aggregate Protection
items.abstract: Long-term intensive cultivation has degraded soil structure and reduced soil organic carbon (SOC) retention in the black soils of Northeast China. However, the processes underlying SOC accumulation under integrated soil–crop system management (ISSM) remain poorly understood. An 11-year field experiment compared farmers’ practice (FP), high-yield and high-efficiency practice (IP), super-high-yield practice (HY), and ISSM. We assessed SOC stocks, aggregate stability, organic carbon chemistry, extracellular enzyme activities, microbial carbon-use traits, microbial community composition, and microbial necromass carbon (MNC), and used partial least squares path modeling as an exploratory analysis of potential linkages. Compared with FP, ISSM increased SOC content and stock by 87.0 and 77.0%, respectively, and achieved an SOC sequestration rate of 2.8 Mg C ha−1 yr−1. ISSM also increased mean weight diameter and geometric mean diameter by 45.0 and 61.0%, increased microbial biomass carbon and carbon use efficiency by 205.2 and 100.0%, and decreased qCO2 by 71.1%. Bacterial and fungal necromass carbon increased by 100.0 and 70.0%, respectively. The relative abundance of taxa operationally classified as growth-oriented also increased under ISSM. However, MNC/SOC did not differ significantly among treatments, while SOC aromaticity and hydrophobicity declined. Path analysis suggested that microbial carbon transformation was positively associated with necromass formation, whereas aggregate stability was associated with MNC and SOC retention. These results indicate that ISSM synchronously enlarged SOC and microbial necromass pools through sustained carbon inputs, efficient microbial transformation, and aggregate-mediated physical protection rather than through increased chemical recalcitrance.
items.authors: Yantian Cui, Yan Zhou, Ranran Zhou, Jingmin Yang, Zhongqing Zhang, Jinhua Liu

items.title: Beyond Methodological Noise: Robust Gut Microbiota Signals in Parkinson’s Disease via a Heterogeneous Multi-Algorithmic Framework
items.abstract: Background: Recent research has highlighted the role of gut microbiota dysfunctions in Parkinson’s disease (PD), which may occur decades before the onset of motor symptoms. However, methodological variability across studies and complex host–microbiota interactions limit conclusions regarding which genera are most relevant to these dysfunctions. This study aimed to identify robust and reproducible microbial signatures associated with PD. Methods: To this end, we developed a consensus-based framework combining differential abundance analysis (DAA) with machine-learning analyses across gut microbiota datasets from individuals with PD and compared inferred functional profiles across cohorts. Results: Pairwise genus overlap ranged from 56 to 98 genera, with 67–75% concordance in the direction of association. The predictive model achieved AUCs of 0.75–0.95 within individual cohorts and a mean AUC of 0.72 under Leave-One-Cohort-Out validation (LOCO). Fourteen genera were consistently identified across all cohorts, including Porphyromonas in PD and Roseburia in controls, alongside patterns involving SCFA-associated microbial functions and inflammation-related taxa. Conclusions: These findings were consistent with previous reports and support the relevance of the gut–brain axis in PD, highlighting the potential of microbiota-derived features as candidate microbial signatures.
items.authors: Marcela A. V. Pereira, Tetsu Sakamoto, Renan C. Moioli

items.title: Inextensible Curve Flows in Dual Space D3: A Quasi-Frame Approach
items.abstract: This paper develops a comprehensive quasi-frame theory for inextensible curve flows in the dual space D3. While the Frenet frame has been the traditional tool for studying curve evolution, it encounters singularities when curvature vanishes. We introduce a quasi-frame (q-frame) formulation that overcomes these limitations and provides a robust framework for analyzing inextensible flows, flows that preserve arc length throughout evolution. We derive the fundamental evolution equations for quasi-curvatures under inextensible flow conditions and establish necessary and sufficient conditions for inextensibility in dual space. In contrast to the Euclidean, Minkowski, and Galilean settings, the quasi-curvatures in dual space are dual-valued, so they simultaneously encode the direction of the oriented line and the evolution of its moment vector. Our approach extends inextensible flows using the Frenet frame by providing a more general framework that remains well-defined even at singular points. We demonstrate the advantages of our method through detailed worked examples, including complete computations of time-evolving curves with explicit verification of arc-length preservation. These results contribute to the theoretical foundations of curve dynamics in dual spaces.
items.authors: Ayman Elsharkawy, Murat Turan, Eman Ghareeb Rezk, Hülya Gün Bozok, Sıddıka Özkaldı Karakuş

items.title: Intelligent Hybrid Neuro-Fuzzy Control System for Industrial Bread Baking Ovens
items.abstract: Intelligent control systems can stabilise operational processes and support the development of digital manufacturing in the food industry. This study presents and examines a digital twin of an industrial bread oven with a hybrid neuro-fuzzy controller for temperature and humidity to bake several loaves of bread. Its architecture comprises MLP-Control (4-32-16-2), a discrete Fuzzy-PD corrector and safety rules. The Mamdani controller with 27 rules operates as an independent reference and provides labels for behaviour cloning. MLP-Control accepted those labels in 98.73% of cases for the dryer, 99.10% for the humidifier, and 98.01% for both combined. The Simulation-in-the-Loop evaluation was conducted on 100 pairwise scenarios (seed 42) with a 39 min cycle, 5 s steps and phases at 0–3, 3–6 and 6–39 min. Hybrid + Constraint met the stringent Phase 3 sustainability criterion in 100 out of 100 scenarios, compared with 95 out of 100 for PI. However, PI achieved the lowest final MSE, the shortest mean settling time and the lowest control effort; therefore, it is not claimed that Hybrid + Constraint is superior in all respects. A step-by-step analysis showed that the common fraction within the band was zero in Stages 1–2, indicating the dynamics of the SIL model and its boundary interpretation. In the fair test, MLP-Quality achieved MAE = 0.162318, RMSE = 0.203081 and R2 = 0.686535 on the test set, which was held out with 202,000 samples. Results from the 2025 industry benchmark report are also taken into account and do not indicate how this Hybrid + Constraint configuration performs in a production furnace.
items.authors: Lyazzat Serikovna Issabekova, Irbulat Turemuratovich Utepbergenov, Shara Dzholdaspekovna Toibayeva, Zhanna Serikbayeva Tleubayeva, Ablay Serikuly Aldabergenov

items.title: Forecasting Transportation CO2 Emissions in China: A Rolling-Origin Comparison of Econometric, Machine-Learning, and Deep-Learning Models
items.abstract: Transportation-related CO2 emissions remain an important challenge for sustainable mobility and the energy transition in rapidly developing economies. This study examines transportation-related CO2 emissions in China using annual data for 1990–2024 within a STIRPAT-informed forecasting framework. Urban population share, GDP per capita, the fossil-energy share, and physical freight activity are used as theory-guided predictors. The analysis compares naïve persistence, a dynamic OLS benchmark, Support Vector Regression (SVR), XGBoost, and a compact Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model using chronological rolling-origin evaluation. One-year-ahead forecasts are assessed for 2010–2024 using RMSE, MAE, MSE, out-of-sample R2, and Harvey–Leybourne–Newbold-adjusted Diebold–Mariano tests, with a direct two-year-ahead experiment used as a robustness check. In the primary experiment, the LSTM records the lowest observed RMSE (45.254) and MAE (35.956), closely followed by the dynamic OLS benchmark in RMSE and XGBoost in MAE. At the two-year horizon, XGBoost records the lowest RMSE (45.537) and MAE (34.426). Most pairwise forecast-accuracy differences are not statistically significant at the 5% level, and the LSTM–XGBoost difference is not significant under either squared or absolute loss. Rolling-origin SHAP analysis identifies GDP as the largest source of incremental predictive information for XGBoost, followed by freight activity, while strong collinearity limits structural interpretation. Conditional sensitivity experiments further show that the fitted forecasting model should not be treated as a causal policy simulator. Overall, the findings demonstrate that temporal validation, conventional benchmarks, and robustness analysis are essential when evaluating complex forecasting models on short annual emissions series.
items.authors: Syed Rafid Ali Shah, Yajuan Dong, Amin Ullah Khan

items.title: Clinical Outcomes and Patient Selection for Transcatheter Tricuspid Edge-to-Edge Repair (TEER) Versus Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Replacement (TTVR)
items.abstract: Tricuspid regurgitation (TR) is common, undertreated, and associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Transcatheter tricuspid valve intervention (TTVI), comprising transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) and transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR), has emerged as an alternative to surgery. In this narrative review, we summarize device design and implantation techniques (TriClip, PASCAL, Cardioband, EVOQUE), evidence from pivotal and early feasibility trials (TRILUMINATE, CLASP TR, TRI-REPAIR, TRISCEND II), and the anatomic and clinical factors that guide patient selection. TEER and annuloplasty reduce TR and improve symptoms and quality of life, with lower rates of bleeding and conduction disturbance than TTVR. TTVR with EVOQUE achieved more complete TR reduction (99.1% with moderate or less TR) but carried higher rates of bleeding and new pacemaker implantation. Differences in trial design and study populations preclude direct comparison. Coaptation gap, jet location, leaflet tethering, annular size, device leads, and right ventricular function determine device suitability. TTVI is an effective treatment for TR, but long-term durability and conduction-system safety remain uncertain. We propose a heart team algorithm to guide selection between TEER and TTVR.
items.authors: Nimra Gilani, Diego Barzallo-Zeas, Abhishek Sharma

items.title: Structural Properties of Isosymmetric Transformations on Metric Spaces
items.abstract: In this paper, we introduce and study m,n;q-isosymmetric transformations on metric spaces, generalizing the notions of m;q-isometries and n;q-symmetries that have recently been investigated in the literature. Our approach combines these two metric structures within a common framework governed by the parameters m, n, and q 0. We establish a collection of structural properties for m,n;q-isosymmetric transformations, including their behavior under iteration and composition, and derive several characterizations and equivalent conditions. We further examine their relationships with Lipschitz, nonexpansive, and contractive mappings, revealing conditions under which the corresponding metric properties are inherited or recovered. In particular, we show how the new class connects the previously studied m;q-isometric and n;q-symmetric settings within a single metric framework. These results provide a foundation for the systematic study of the structure and behavior of isosymmetric transformations on metric spaces.
items.authors: Sid Ahmed Ould Ahmed Mahmoud, Ali Hamzah Alibrahim

items.title: The Supervision Paradox: AI Capability Growth and the Case for Usage Contraction in High-Loss Domains
items.abstract: Human oversight is a load-bearing premise of AI governance: in several regimes, human review determines which obligations apply. We examine when this premise fails for verification-based oversight, in which a designated human checks AI outputs before they take effect. It fails when accountability for detected errors falls on reviewers or deployers, reviewer capacity is bounded, and output from open populations persistently outgrows that capacity. Review then becomes nominal, and recent experiments show that fluent AI output undermines error recognition. Because accountability and feedback respond only to detected errors, undetected harms are externalized and surface as threshold shocks. We analyze how these dynamics limit six oversight configurations. As capability grows, the share of AI output that oversight in high-loss domains can responsibly approve contracts. Friction is the one role of human involvement that keeps functioning under load; bounding inflow to reviewer capacity (flow design) is a necessary complement to other safeguards.
items.authors: Hiroki Naito

items.title: Sharp Estimates and Symmetric Subclasses for Univalent Functions Defined by the nth Derivative of em z/f(z) /em
items.abstract: The Al-Refai--Darus criterion guarantees univalence of a normalized function \( f \) when a weighted sum of \( |(z/f)^{(k)}(0)| \), \( 2\le k\le n-1 \), and of \( \sup|(z/f)^{(n)}| \) does not exceed \( 1 \). For \( n\ge3 \) we study the subclass \( \mathcal C_n \) with \( a_2=\dots=a_n=0 \), in which the whole allowance goes to the \( n \) th derivative. The map \( f\mapsto(z/f)^{(n)} \) is a bijection of \( \mathcal C_n \) onto a closed ball of \( H^\infty \), which turns extremal problems into problems for bounded analytic functions. We prove sharp growth, distortion, covering-radius and coefficient bounds with the \( (n+j) \)-fold symmetric extremal functions \( z/(1+cz^{n+j}) \); the exact region of \( (a_{n+1},a_{n+2}) \), whose boundary is attained by M\"obius parameters written in closed form; and an exact radius for dilations of products \( f_1f_2/z \), sharp both for Aksentev's inequality and for univalence. The \( n \)-fold symmetric members of \( \mathcal C_n \) correspond to \( g(z^n) \) with \( g \) in the same ball, which gives the exact region of \( (a_{n+1},a_{2n+1}) \). For the larger class defined by \( a_2=0 \) and the criterion we obtain sharp bounds as well. The comparison with \( n \)-fold symmetric univalent functions records a gap; it is not a sharpening of known results.
items.authors: Oqlah Al-Refai, Jamal Salah, Mohammed Ali, Khalifa Al-Shaqsi, Hameed Ur Rehman, Ahmad Al Azab

items.title: A Survey of Security in Real-World Agents: From Digital Agents to Embodied AI
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are rapidly evolving into real-world agents that interact with digital interfaces, external tools, persistent memory, and physical environments. This shift fundamentally changes the nature of security risks: vulnerabilities that once mainly affected model outputs can now propagate through planning, tool use, action generation, and physical control loops, eventually becoming unsafe workflows, persistent compromise, data exposure, or physically consequential actions. In this survey, we trace how security failures evolve across LLMs, software-centric agents, and embodied robotic systems, with vision-language-action models serving as a representative bridge between Internet-scale vision-language knowledge and physical action generation. We organize the literature around lifecycle attack surfaces, major threat families, defense and assurance mechanisms, and existing benchmarks. We further argue that future research should move beyond attack demonstrations in simplified settings toward deployment-valid evaluation, where security is assessed under realistic tools, privilege boundaries, long-horizon execution, and physical-world constraints.
items.authors: Yuhui Sun, Zhen Sun, Yifan Liao, Zongmin Zhang, Shuaijun Liu, Han Sun

items.title: Human–AI Co-Design and Reproducible Cheminformatic Characterisation of AIIP-RA-DMAE-001, a Rosmarinic-Acid-Derived Immunopharmacological Candidate
items.abstract: Rosmarinic acid is a chemically attractive immunopharmacology scaffold, but its high polarity, ionization, metabolic lability, and incomplete target definition limit translation. This original communication defines AIIP RA DMAE 001, the internal code assigned to rosmarinic acid 2-(N,N-dimethylamino)ethyl ester, an artificial-intelligence-guided phytochemical-derived analogue generated within an AI-based immunopharmacology program. The design replaces the parent carboxylic acid with an ionizable 2-(dimethylamino)ethyl ester while retaining the natural rosmarinic-acid stereocenter and E-caffeoyl geometry. The free-base structure has the formula C22H25NO8, an average molecular weight of 431.44 g mol−1, and the isomeric SMILES CN(C)CCOC(=O)[C@@H](Cc1ccc(O)c(O)c1)OC(=O)/C=C/c1ccc(O)c(O)c1. Public exact-identity searches performed on 10 October 2026 found no individualized record for this structure, although closely related alkyl rosmarinates, methyl-rosmarinate derivatives, and a permanently charged rosmarinylcholine analogue are known and broad patent Markush language may encompass aminoalkyl esters. The compound is therefore described as putatively structurally novel, not as pharmacologically or therapeutically novel. A prior design record reported hypothesis-generating AutoDock Vina scores of −7.8, −8.1, and −8.3 kcal mol−1 against generic IgG, IgA, and IgM structures, respectively; these values do not establish binding and require prospective reproduction. The tertiary amine is expected to permit salt formation and substantial protonation near physiological pH, whereas the catechols and ester linkages create oxidation, assay-interference, hydrolysis, and distribution liabilities. We propose an evidence-gated program spanning synthesis and spectroscopic confirmation, pKa and stability measurement, orthogonal target-engagement studies, innate and adaptive immune phenotyping, and exposure-linked disease models. The most credible initial translational hypotheses concern type I interferon signaling and macrophage inflammatory state; direct immunoglobulin modulation should remain a higher-bar secondary hypothesis. AIIP RA DMAE 001 is thus a testable molecular proposal and a framework for transparent progression from AI design to immunological evidence.
items.authors: Angel Justiz-Vaillant

items.title: Acorn Shell Extract-Functionalized Cotton Biomaterials: A Sustainable Platform with Biological Activities and Controlled Release for Skin Microbiota Dysregulation Conditions
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Skin dysbiosis is associated with several dermatological disorders and is often accompanied by oxidative stress and inflammation. Bioactive textiles offer a promising strategy for localized skin health management; however, many currently available materials rely on synthetic or metal-based agents. This study aimed to develop sustainable cotton-based bioactive textiles functionalized with acorn shell (AS) extract, an agri-food by-product rich in phenolic compounds, and evaluate their biological performance potential for skin-contact applications in the management of skin dysbiosis conditions. Methods: Cotton fabrics were pre-treated with chitosan, a commercial cationic agent, or potassium alum and functionalized with AS extract using exhaustion or padding techniques. The resulting materials were assessed for antimicrobial activity against skin-associated bacteria, antioxidant capacity, anti-inflammatory activity in LPS-stimulated macrophages, cytocompatibility with keratinocytes and macrophages, and phenolic compound release under skin-mimicking conditions. Results: AS-functionalized cotton exhibited strong antimicrobial activity, particularly against Gram-positive bacteria, together with significant antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects. All functionalized textiles maintained keratinocyte viability above established cytocompatibility thresholds, supporting their suitability for direct skin contact. Exhaustion-treated samples showed higher phenolic incorporation and release, resulting in enhanced biological performance, whereas padding-treated fabrics exhibited lower phenolic loading, more sustained release profiles, and comparatively reduced bioactivity. Conclusions: AS extract can be successfully incorporated into cotton textiles using industrially relevant finishing methods, generating multifunctional materials with antimicrobial, antioxidant, and anti-inflammatory properties while maintaining cytocompatibility. These findings support the potential of AS-functionalized cotton as a sustainable, plant-based skin-contact textile platform for localized management of skin-dysbiosis-associated conditions, with great relevance for dermatological and healthcare applications.
items.authors: Cláudia S. Oliveira, Andreia Fernandes, Adma Melo, Tiago B. Afonso, Ana F. Costa, Manuela Pintado

items.title: Latent Profiles of Primary Emotional Systems and Their Associations with PTSD, CPTSD, Attachment, and Childhood Adversity
items.abstract: Adverse childhood experiences are associated with trauma-related psychopathology, but individual differences in affective organization may contribute to heterogeneous outcomes. This study aimed to identify latent profiles of primary emotional systems and examine their associations with attachment, childhood maltreatment, and posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and complex PTSD (CPTSD). A community sample of 917 Portuguese adults completed measures of primary emotional systems, adult attachment, childhood maltreatment, and PTSD/CPTSD symptoms. Latent profile analyses were conducted separately for women and men, followed by measurement invariance testing and multinomial logistic regression analyses. Four profiles were identified in both sexes: Negative Affect, Low Affective Activation, Balanced Affective Functioning, and Positive Affect. Partial measurement invariance indicated sex-related differences in ANGER, FEAR, and PANIC, while the overall profile structure was comparable across sexes. Negative Affect was associated with PTSD, CPTSD, and fearful attachment in both sexes. Low Affective Activation was associated with CPTSD and dismissing attachment, with additional associations varying by sex. The findings indicate that primary emotional systems form heterogeneous configurations that are differentially associated with developmental, interpersonal, and clinical characteristics. Person-centered assessment may complement symptom-based approaches, although causal inference and profile stability cannot be established.
items.authors: Paulo Ferrajão, Rebeca Fernandes Rocha, Amadeu Quelhas Martins
items.category_raw: European Journal of Investigation in Health, Psychology and Education

items.title: Exploring the Bioactive Properties of Thymus kotschyanus var. kotschyanus and Endemic Thymus brachychilus: From Plant Extracts to Alginate Film Formulations for Wound Infection Management
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Antibiotic resistance poses significant challenges to the treatment of infectious diseases. Wounds occur as a result of damage to the skin caused by various factors and may become life-threatening with the development of infection. Plants can exhibit considerable microbiological activity due to their rich phytochemical composition. Thymus kotschyanus var. kotschyanus and the endemic species Thymus brachychilus collected from Adıyaman Province, Türkiye, have been widely used by local communities for their therapeutic properties and other purposes. Methods: In this study, ethanol extracts of these plants were prepared and evaluated for their antimicrobial activity against nine Gram-negative bacteria, seven Gram-positive bacteria, one mycobacterial strain, and four yeast strains using agar well diffusion and microdilution methods. Their antibiofilm activity was assessed using a microplate-based assay, anti-quorum sensing activity was evaluated using Chromobacterium violaceum strains, anti-infective activity was investigated using the Caenorhabditis elegans model, and cytotoxicity was evaluated using the MTT assay. The phytochemical composition of the extracts was determined by HPLC-DAD. Alginate film formulations containing the extracts were prepared using the solvent-casting method and characterized by FTIR spectroscopy and light microscopy. Their antimicrobial and antibiofilm activities were subsequently evaluated. Results: Both extracts exhibited antimicrobial, antibiofilm, anti-quorum sensing, and anti-infective activities, while no cytotoxic effects were observed. Rosmarinic acid was identified as the major compound in both extracts. The extract-loaded alginate films exhibited antimicrobial and antibiofilm activities and showed no cytotoxic effects. Conclusions: These findings suggest that alginate film formulations may be a promising approach for the topical application of T. kotschyanus var. kotschyanus and T. brachychilus extracts. In particular, the alginate films containing both plant extracts may have potential as wound dressing materials for preventing wound infections or supporting the treatment of infected wounds.
items.authors: Erkan Rayaman, Fatma Betül Zengin, Duygu Taşkın, Ceyda Ekentok Atıcı, Ömer Kılıç, Elif Çalışkan Salihi

items.title: Psychosocial Adaptation in a Sensor-Augmented Telerehabilitation Program for Knee Osteoarthritis: A Post Hoc Analysis of a Randomized Controlled Trial
items.abstract: Background: Psychosocial adaptation during telerehabilitation for knee osteoarthritis (OA) is not well understood. Objective: To explore associations among self-efficacy, anxiety, depressive symptoms, and kinesiophobia during sensor-augmented telerehabilitation. Methods: This exploratory post hoc secondary analysis included 21 participants from the telerehabilitation arm of the KneE-PAD randomized controlled trial. Psychosocial outcomes were assessed before and after intervention using the Arthritis Self-Efficacy Scale (ASES), Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS), and Tampa Scale for Kinesiophobia (TSK). Within-group changes were assessed using paired analyses with Holm–Bonferroni adjustment, associations among change scores were examined using correlation analyses with multiplicity correction, and exploratory regression models were fitted without multiplicity adjustment. Results: Improvement in pain-related self-efficacy was associated with reduced anxiety (ρ = −0.71, adjusted p = 0.006). No other correlation remained statistically significant after Holm–Bonferroni correction, and the regression findings were interpreted as exploratory. Conclusions: Psychosocial changes during sensor-augmented telerehabilitation were characterized by a strong association between improvement in pain-related self-efficacy and reduction in anxiety. These exploratory findings require confirmation in larger, prospectively designed studies. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06416332.
items.authors: Theodora Plavoukou, Myrto Poulou, Amalia Continiero Spyropoulou, George Georgoudis

items.title: Application of Stable Isotopes in Water Transport Processes of the Soil–Plant–Atmosphere Continuum in Eucalyptus Plantations: A Review
items.abstract: The water cycle in forest ecosystems is a core component of ecosystem services, and it is crucial for revealing terrestrial hydrological processes and regulation mechanisms. Investigating water migration across interfaces of the soil–plant–atmosphere continuum (SPAC) has long been a hotspot in ecohydrological research. Eucalyptus stands are among the world’s major commercial timber species, and their hydrological effects have attracted growing public attention. Naturally occurring hydrogen and oxygen stable isotopes can effectively differentiate water sources, serving as powerful tracers widely applied in hydrological research. Nevertheless, comprehensive systematic reviews on SPAC water dynamics of Eucalyptus plantations using stable isotope quantification are still lacking. This study systematically reviews the application of hydrogen and oxygen stable isotopes in analyzing water transport and transformation processes at multiple interfaces of Eucalyptus plantation SPAC, covering atmospheric precipitation sources, soil and plant water migration, plant transpiration and groundwater exchange. Future research should strengthen in-situ continuous monitoring of isotopic signatures in diverse water bodies, facilitate the popularization of isotope-based models, and advance quantitative partitioning of evapotranspiration in Eucalyptus ecosystems. This review provides theoretical and technical support for exploring hydrological processes and mechanisms in forest ecosystems, and offers scientific references for improving forest water use efficiency and optimizing regional water resource allocation.
items.authors: Haijun Zuo, Qing Xu, Deqiang Gao, Ke Diao, Beibei Zhang

items.title: Comparative DIA Proteomics of Neuroblastoma: Laser-Microdissected FFPE Tumors Versus Cell Lines
items.abstract: Formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tumor specimens are widely available and represent a valuable resource for retrospective cancer research; however, chemical cross-linking has historically limited their application in proteomic studies. In this study, we developed a proteomic workflow for laser-microdissected FFPE neuroblastoma tissues and evaluated their biological characteristics in comparison with established neuroblastoma cell lines. Tumor regions were isolated from FFPE sections by laser microdissection, and protein profiles were analyzed using data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry. Seven high-risk neuroblastoma FFPE samples and four neuroblastoma cell lines were examined. A total of 4511 proteins were identified in FFPE tissues and 6812 proteins in cell lines, with 4311 proteins shared between both systems. After quality filtering, 2186 proteins were retained for downstream quantitative analyses. Principal component analysis and hierarchical clustering demonstrated clear separation between FFPE tissues and cell lines despite a strong overall correlation in mean protein abundance across the quantified proteome. Differential abundance and functional enrichment analyses revealed distinct proteomic features between the two systems. Proteins enriched in FFPE tissues were associated with extracellular vesicles, the extracellular space, the cornified envelope, intermediate filament organization and cell junctions. In contrast, proteins enriched in neuroblastoma cell lines were associated with RNA binding, translation, rRNA processing, oxidative phosphorylation, and glycolysis/gluconeogenesis, reflecting enhanced biosynthetic and metabolic activity. Together, these findings demonstrate that FFPE tissues and neuroblastoma cell lines capture complementary aspects of neuroblastoma biology, supporting their combined use as a comprehensive framework for biomarker discovery and translational research in pediatric oncology.
items.authors: Akihiro Nishimura, Tomoko Fujikawa, Shotaro Inoue, Nobuyuki Yamamoto, Makiko Yoshida, Tetsuya Fukuda

items.title: Adaptive Clustering and Deep Learning-Based Model for Predicting Large-Scale Heterogeneous Building Load Profiles
items.abstract: Large-scale building load prediction is essential for efficient energy management in smart and low carbon cities. However, the heterogeneity of buildings and sensor-generated noise pose significant challenges to prediction accuracy. To address these challenges, this study proposes an adaptive clustering and deep learning-based model that integrates noise reduction, adaptive clustering, and advanced time-series modeling incorporating both static and dynamic information. The denoising module employs the Savitzky–Golay filter to remove data noise, the clustering module considers the AFW-K-means-based adaptive clustering to group buildings, and the prediction module utilizes the temporal fusion transformers algorithm that includes static and dynamic features. The proposed model was validated using real-world data collected from 182 buildings over three months in Shenzhen, China. Model comparisons show that the proposed model can reduce RMSE by up to 12.28% compared with traditional models. Compared with constructing individual models for each building, the proposed model improves prediction performance by up to 8.22% while reducing prediction time by 99.12%. Feature importance analysis reveals that historical load and time-domain, time-related, and environmental features are the main predictors, reflecting strong diurnal and climatic effects. These findings characterize the performance of the proposed approach for heterogeneous multi-building load forecasting within the investigated Shenzhen dataset. Its generalizability across seasons, years and geographical regions requires further validation.
items.authors: Yuhang Zhang, Dongfang Yang, Yi Zhang, He Qi

items.title: Structure–Property Relationships in Bioactive Poly (Vinyl Alcohol) Films Incorporating Natural Phenolic Additives for Sustainable Active Packaging
items.abstract: This study aimed to investigate bioactive poly (vinyl alcohol) (PVA) films incorporating three chemically distinct naturally phenolic additives—aronia extract (A), apple peel extract (AP), and rutin (R)—as individual functional modifiers for active packaging applications. Here, we studied how the chemical nature of these phenolic compounds influenced the physicochemical characteristics, structure, release behavior, and functional properties of the PVA matrix. The FTIR, SEM, AFM and XPS analyses revealed intermolecular interactions between the hydroxyl groups from the PVA matrix and the hydroxyl and carboxyl groups from phenolic compounds, a high degree of miscibility between them, as well as uniform dispersion of polyphenols in the PVA matrix. XRD analysis indicated the ability of phenolic compounds to change the PVA film’s crystallinity. The films showed very low permeability to castor oil and the UV-Vis light barrier property of the film modified with aronia extract was 47% higher as compared to the reference film. The phenolic compounds improved the antioxidant activity of the reference film by about 90% and inhibited the growth of Gram-positive Staphylococcus aureus. The modified films proved their functionality by keeping the quality of the butter packed for 43 days, demonstrating their potential as active packaging materials.
items.authors: Lucica Maria Pop, Lidija Jakobek, Camelia Nicula, Alexandra Maria Uivarasan, Zorica Vosgan, Monica Liliana Marian

items.title: Endocrine Phenotype and GH1 Sequence Variation in Children with Short Stature: Five-Year Growth Outcomes of Growth Hormone Therapy
items.abstract: Background: Growth hormone (GH) stimulation tests have limited diagnostic precision in childhood short stature (SS), and the relationships among endocrine phenotype, GH1 variation, and long-term treatment response remain unclear. We examined the clinical, endocrine, genetic, and five-year growth outcomes of children receiving recombinant GH. Methods: In this retrospective cohort study, 74 children with SS were classified as idiopathic SS (ISS; n = 28) or growth hormone deficiency (GHD; n = 46) using available GH stimulation-test results together with the integrated clinical, auxological, biochemical, radiological, and treatment-eligibility assessments documented in the medical records. Results: Median annual height velocity was 9.0 cm/year, median height gain was 1.80 standard deviation scores (SDS), and median IGF-1 increased from 125.5 to 306 µg/L. GH dose, endocrine parameters, annual height velocity, height gain SDS, and mean post-treatment height and weight gain did not differ significantly between groups. Height and weight increased over follow-up (both p 0.001), with no significant group or time-by-group interaction. GH1 sequencing predominantly identified common promoter/upstream and intronic polymorphisms; no pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants were detected. Exploratory genetic clustering showed no clinically meaningful association with endocrine phenotype or treatment response. Conclusions: Adjusted models detected no statistically significant between-group differences in height or weight trajectories. This finding does not establish equivalent treatment efficacy.
items.authors: Serpil Albayrak, Murat Karaoglan, Ahmet Yildirim, Mehmet Keskin

items.title: A Computational Workflow Integrating Explainable AI and Database Mining for the Prioritization of Antimicrobial Natural Products
items.abstract: The escalating threat of antimicrobial resistance demands the discovery of antibacterial agents with unprecedented chemical scaffolds. Natural products have historically been the most prolific source of antibiotics, yet the vast majority of catalogued natural products remain untested for antimicrobial activity. Here we present Natural-Product Graph–language, Uncertainty-Aware Relational Discovery (NP-GUARD), a modular computational framework that reframes antimicrobial natural-product discovery as an uncertainty-aware, relational, multi-objective learning problem. NP-GUARD integrates six core components: provenance-tracked data curation, multi-view molecular representation, pathogen-conditioned multi-task prediction, explicit uncertainty quantification, stability-aware explainability, and conformal-Pareto prioritization, all consolidated within a queryable knowledge base. Of these components, the present study implements and benchmarks the data-curation, predictive, uncertainty, explainability and prioritization layers, including a first pathogen-conditioned masked multi-task graph model, while the full multi-view encoder and the knowledge base are specified for subsequent work. We report a proof-of-concept evaluation on public screening data forStaphylococcus aureus (38,995 compounds), Escherichia coli (2291) and Pseudomonas aeruginosa (29,986), together with human cytotoxicity data and a 406,959-compound screening library from COCONUT. Under repeated scaffold-aware splitting, baseline models achieve strong discrimination (AUROC 0.78–0.93) but reveal substantial split-to-split variance in minority-class performance; class-conditional conformal prediction attains near-nominal per-class coverage; and feature attributions show only moderate stability across independently trained models (top-20 Jaccard 0.54), underscoring a critical caveat for explanation-driven discovery. Screening the COCONUT library validates the uncertainty-aware activity ranking, achieving an 87-fold enrichment of known antibiotics in the top 100 candidates (128-fold within the fully characterized named-compound stratum), although analogue-exclusion analysis shows this signal is dominated by rediscovery of training-like chemistry.
