The novelty-seeking Pareto layer yields a structurally diverse 90-compound shortlist spanning 72 scaffolds, deliberately steered toward unexplored chemotypes; we emphasize that the shortlist constitutes prioritized hypotheses for experimental testing, not validated actives. NP-GUARD provides a transparent, reproducible and decision-oriented foundation for prioritizing natural products for experimental validation.
items.authors: Pietro Hiram Guzzi, Annamaria Defilippo, Pierangelo Veltri, Giancarlo Ceccarelli, Fabio Scarpa, Massimo Ciccozzi

items.title: A Low-Disturbance Workflow for Determining NMR T2 Cutoffs in Mechanically Sensitive Core Samples
items.abstract: Centrifugation is widely used to determine the NMR T2 cutoff of core samples, but it may alter pore structures and is particularly unsuitable for mechanically sensitive cores. This study proposes a low-disturbance workflow combining staged gas displacement with deuterium oxide (D2O) displacement, in which physical displacement replaces centrifugal drainage. The residual proton-bearing-water response is treated as a bound-water reference for determining the T2 cutoff. The method was tested on one weakly consolidated core (R1500) and two conventional cores (R7 and R30) and compared with centrifugation using NMR T2 spectra and magnetic resonance imaging. The workflow yielded T2 cutoff values of 32.45 ms, 5.66 ms, and 24.25 ms for R7, R30, and R1500, respectively. In contrast, R1500 failed during the first centrifugation step, whereas R7 and R30 fractured at high rotational speeds; MRI also revealed outlet-end residual-water accumulation. The displacement-derived T2 cutoff was subsequently used to partition bound and movable fluid volumes for permeability evaluation using the Timur-Coates model. The staged gas/D2O workflow provides a low-disturbance alternative to centrifugation for the three tested cores; the present validation covers two conventional cores and one weakly consolidated core.
items.authors: Yuhua Li, Chunyuan Gu, Kun Li, Haoran Song

items.title: Geotechnical Problems on Madeira Island: Slope Protection in Central Funchal—A Case Study
items.abstract: Volcanic islands are highly exposed to interacting geotechnical and hydrogeomorphological hazards, particularly where steep relief, intense rainfall, fractured volcanic rocks, and urban development coincide. This study analyzes the slope located along Avenida Sá Carneiro in central Funchal, Madeira Island, as an example of an urban coastal volcanic slope functioning under multi-hazard conditions. The study is based on literature analysis, field observations, and a sequential photographic inventory of existing protection measures. The results show that the analyzed slope should not be interpreted as a single retaining structure, but as a complex geological–hydrological–engineering–urban system. Its stability depends on the combined action of historical stone retaining walls, reinforced concrete elements, tunnel portals, drainage components, passive rockfall protection systems, terraced structures, vegetation, and local architectural solutions. The effectiveness of this system results from the spatial cooperation of many locally adapted measures rather than from one dominant stabilization method. The study also highlights the dual role of vegetation, which may support erosion control and near-surface stabilization, but may also obscure damage, seepage zones, and discontinuities. The findings emphasize that integrated slope management in densely urbanized volcanic island environments requires simultaneous consideration of water control, structural protection, maintenance, and landscape integration.:
items.authors: Grzegorz Straż, Sérgio António Neves Lousada, Raul Manuel Costa Alves

items.title: Restoration of PPD-Induced Injury in iHDPCs via the OS–Mitochondrial Apoptosis Pathway: Screening and Validation of Natural Compounds
items.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the protective effects of curcumin (Cur), resveratrol (Res), and astragaloside IV (AS-IV) against p-phenylenediamine (PPD)-induced injury in human immortalized dermal papilla cells (iHDPCs), with a focus on phenotypic endpoints that are suggestive of the oxidative stress–mitochondrial apoptosis pathway. Putative core targets were predicted via network pharmacology and molecular docking, and cellular responses were evaluated using CCK-8, DCFH-DA, JC-1, and Annexin V/PI assays in both PPD- and H2O2-exposed models. 1623 Collectively, these observations are consistent with the possibility that Cur, Res, and AS-IV may alleviate PPD-induced cellular damage, potentially through modulation of oxidative status and mitochondrial homeostasis. However, because the current experiments do not directly measure NRF2 nuclear translocation, downstream antioxidant enzyme expression (e.g., P-AKT HO-1, NQO1), BAX/BCL-2 ratio, cytochrome c release, or caspase activation, they cannot establish target engagement or a definitive causal link to the proposed pathway. Therefore, our findings should be interpreted as correlative and hypothesis-generating; direct mechanistic validation is required to confirm the involvement of this pathway. Nevertheless, the consistent protective phenotypes observed make these compounds, particularly AS-IV, promising candidates for the development of next-generation hair dyes.
items.authors: Yi Ren, Jiqing He, Linxin Zheng, Lizhi Yue, Congfen He, Dianchao Huang

items.title: Temporal Consistency and Averaging Sensitivity of Released Smart-Insole Gait Summaries in Participants with and without Knee Osteoarthritis
items.abstract: Repeated smart-insole outputs may support longitudinal gait research, but consistency of processed summaries does not establish device accuracy or a clinical monitoring schedule. We analyzed 10 released observations per participant from AI Hub dataset 71966, retaining 178 participants (89 provider-labeled normal and 89 knee osteoarthritis) after exclusion of a previously reported opposing-label duplicate pair. Analyses combined absolute-agreement intraclass correlations (ICCs), participant-bootstrap intervals, residual variability, nonoverlapping 2-, 3-, and 5-observation averages, and exploratory adjusted coefficient-of-variation (CV) models. Single-observation ICCs were 0.827–0.844 for midfoot/rearfoot pressure, 0.663–0.727 for stride length, speed, and forefoot pressure, 0.398 for distance, and approximately 0.014 for balance. Five-observation empirical ICCs were lower than Spearman–Brown predictions for every non-balance endpoint; gait speed yielded 0.887 versus 0.927 and left stride length 0.870 versus 0.908. Left-balance residual SD was 2.388 in the released scale despite low median CV. Linear-programming median regression and solution-choice sensitivity replaced warning-prone bootstrap fitting; the maximum change of a nominal interval endpoint from its reference was 0.0996 CV percentage points. Calendar dates, wear time, and criterion measurements were unavailable. These results characterize release-specific temporal consistency and qualify model-based averaging projections; they do not validate calendar-duration prescriptions, clinical change thresholds, or the underlying device.
items.authors: Mi-Ae Yang, Kang-Su Ha

items.title: How Symmetric Is Uplink–Downlink Duality? Per-User Power Allocation in Multiuser MISO Beamforming
items.abstract: Uplink–downlink (UL–DL) duality is a standard tool in multiuser transmit optimization. With the beamforming directions held fixed, the downlink power minimization problem and its virtual uplink counterpart are feasible for exactly the same signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) targets and attain the same minimum total power, so a downlink power allocation is routinely obtained by solving the uplink problem instead. That guarantee is an aggregate one. In this paper, we ask what it covers for the individual user. Exchanging the two links transposes the interference coupling matrix, and transposition preserves the spectrum but not the solution of the associated linear system. We show that the per-user allocation is preserved for every feasible SINR target if and only if the coupling matrix is symmetric, we introduce a scalar asymmetry measure, and we derive a bound that factorizes the per-user gap into structure, coupling magnitude, and load. Under matched filtering, the symmetry condition reduces to equality of the channel norms, so the asymmetry decays at least as fast as the inverse square root of the number of antennas under homogeneous large-scale fading. Numerically, a 6 dB path-loss spread removes that decay, and regularized zero-forcing suppresses the coupling magnitude rather than the asymmetry.
items.authors: Bogyu Kwon, Do-Yup Kim

items.title: Enhancement of Endocannabinoid Signaling by Dual MAGL/ABHD6 Inhibition Reduces Neurodegeneration and Neuro-Inflammation Following AMPA-Mediated Excitotoxicity
items.abstract: Excitotoxicity mediated by the α-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4 isoxazolepropionic acid receptor (AMPAR) is a major contributor to neuronal degeneration and inflammation in various neurological disorders. The endocannabinoid system (ECS), specifically through the endocannabinoid 2-arachidonoylglycerol (2-AG), exerts neuroprotective and anti-inflammatory effects, but these actions are limited by enzymatic degradation of 2-AG by monoacylglycerol lipase (MAGL) and α/β-hydrolase domain-containing protein 6 (ABHD6). In the present study we investigated the effects of AM11920, a dual MAGL/ABHD6 inhibitor, in a mouse model of AMPA-induced cortical excitotoxicity and in primary cultures of microglia, neurons, and oligodendrocyte precursor cells (OPCs). Intraperitoneal administration (i.p.) of AM11920 reduced microglial and astrocytic reactivity, attenuated neuronal loss, and increased the density of mature oligodendrocytes at the lesion site in vivo. Importantly, chronic administration of AM11920 in vivo did not affect cannabinoid receptor type 1 (CB1R) protein expression. In vitro, AM11920 suppressed microglial activation by reducing CD68 expression and attenuated interleukin-6 (IL-6) expression, while also protecting primary neurons and OPCs from AMPA-induced cell death via a CB1R-dependent mechanism. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that enhancing 2-AG signaling through dual MAGL/ABHD6 blockade provides neuroprotective and immunomodulatory effects and represents a promising therapeutic strategy against excitotoxic-induced neurodegeneration.
items.authors: Dimitris Spyridakos, Ioannis Zyganitidis, Sofia Petsangouraki, Chrystalla Konstantinou, Alexandros Tsimpolis, Sygkliti-Henrietta Pelidou

items.title: Effect of Sr Microalloying on the Microstructure, Solution-Treatment Response, and Age-Hardening Behavior of Mg-Nd-Gd-Zn-Zr Alloy
items.abstract: Mg-Nd-Gd-Zn-Zr alloys containing 0, 0.20, and 0.75 wt.% Sr were prepared by gravity casting to investigate the effects of Sr microalloying on as-cast microstructure, solution-treatment response, and age-hardening behavior. The alloys were characterized by XRD, OM, SEM/EDS, DSC, and Brinell hardness testing. Sr was mainly enriched at grain boundaries and in secondary-phase regions, and Mg17Sr2-related diffraction peaks appeared in the Sr-containing alloys. The as-cast grain size varied non-monotonically among the three compositions investigated, with the 0.20 wt.% Sr alloy exhibiting the finest grains, whereas the area fraction of secondary phases increased continuously with Sr content. Under the selected solution-treatment conditions, the Sr-containing alloys retained smaller grains but contained larger amounts of residual secondary phases. Under the respective selected solution-treated starting states, the 0Sr alloy achieved the highest measured hardness at 200 °C, while the 0.20Sr alloy showed an earlier hardening response and a more gradual subsequent hardness evolution; the 0.75Sr alloy showed a more pronounced post-peak hardness decrease. The retained Sr-containing secondary phases may indicate incomplete dissolution of part of the Nd, Gd, and Zn, potentially reducing the effective solute reservoir in α-Mg available for subsequent aging. Within the three compositions investigated, the results indicate a trade-off between grain refinement/retention and age-hardening potential.
items.authors: Xiaoming Wang, Jinhui Wang, Tong Mu, Jingya Cui, Honghui Liu, Hongyan Kang

items.title: Eastern Christians in the Catholic Literature of the Enlightenment Era—Perspectives from the Kingdom of Hungary
items.abstract: For today’s Catholic intelligentsia, Eastern Orthodoxy appears as the custodian of the ancient Christian tradition: they seek the roots of their own faith—which they believe to have been lost—in the Byzantine rite and the teachings of the Eastern Church Fathers. This perspective, however, is relatively recent: in the centuries preceding the Second Vatican Council, Catholicism viewed the Eastern Churches as schismatics who had turned their backs on the true doctrine. This dismissive attitude was particularly reinforced during the period of Catholic confessionalization that began under the influence of the Council of Trent. This study seeks to answer the question of to what extent the ideas of the Enlightenment—which found resonance even among the Catholic ecclesiastical intelligentsia—modified this dismissive attitude. Can the roots of the open-minded tendencies characteristic of the second half of the 20th century be found in the works of 18th-century ecclesiastical authors? The setting for this study is the former Kingdom of Hungary, a multinational and multiconfessional realm where Western and Eastern Christians lived side by side for centuries, sharing the region’s common history.
items.authors: András Forgó

items.title: Beehive-Derived Products for Wound Management with a Focus on Diabetic Wounds: Mechanistic Insights, Advanced Delivery Strategies, and Translational Evidence
items.abstract: Wound healing is a complex biological process that can be severely impaired by persistent inflammation, oxidative stress, microbial infection, impaired angiogenesis, and defective extracellular matrix remodelling. These abnormalities are particularly prominent in diabetic wounds but also contribute to delayed healing in burn, venous, pressure, traumatic, and post-surgical wounds. Beehive-derived products, including honey, propolis, royal jelly, beeswax, and bee venom, have attracted considerable interest as multifunctional natural therapeutics because of their diverse antimicrobial, antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, immunomodulatory, and regenerative activities. Honey supports wound repair through its acidic pH, high osmolarity, hydrogen peroxide generation, and bioactive phytochemicals, whereas propolis provides flavonoids and phenolic compounds that contribute to antimicrobial, antioxidant, and tissue-regenerative effects. Royal jelly promotes cellular proliferation, angiogenesis, and tissue repair, while beeswax primarily provides moisture retention, barrier protection, and structural properties in wound dressings. Bee venom and its major component, melittin, exhibit antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and regenerative effects, although dose-dependent toxicity and hypersensitivity remain important concerns. Recent advances in hydrogels, polymeric films, electrospun nanofibres, nanoparticles, and composite scaffolds have improved the stability, local retention, controlled release, and therapeutic performance of these products. Preclinical studies demonstrate enhanced antimicrobial activity, fibroblast migration, collagen deposition, angiogenesis, and wound closure, while emerging clinical evidence supports their potential across several wound types. However, variability in composition, standardisation, safety, formulation stability, and limited large-scale clinical evidence remain major challenges.
items.authors: Raj Kamal, Abhishek Chauhan, Hiti Narula, Ankit Awasthi, Mohit Kumar, Sonia Dhiman

items.title: Multimodal Phytochemical and Micronutrient Profiling of Onosma onur-koyuncui Sezer Seeds: Antioxidant and Enzyme Activity Inhibitory Potential
items.abstract: This study aimed to provide the first comprehensive seed-based phytochemical and biological investigation of Onosma onur-koyuncui Sezer, a species endemic to Türkiye, by characterizing its chemical composition and evaluating its in vitro antioxidant and enzyme inhibitory potential. A multi-technique approach combining SPME-GC-FID/MS, GC-FID/MS after silylation, ICP-OES, and UHPLC-HRMS/MS was applied to n-hexane and 70% aqueous methanol seed extracts, together with total phenolic and flavonoid determinations, complementary antioxidant assays, and α-amylase inhibition. p-Cymene (15.00%) was the major volatile, octadecatrienoic acid (27.77%) predominated in the fatty acid profile, and calcium (28.50 mg/gdw) was the most abundant mineral. UHPLC-HRMS/MS revealed chlorogenic acid (51.29 mg/gdw) and diosmetin (42.95 mg/gdw) as major constituents of the 70% aqueous methanol extract. This extract showed the highest phenolic and flavonoid contents and notable antioxidant activity, particularly in the DPPH assay (IC50 = 0.043 mg/mL), exceeding that of BHA (IC50 = 0.118 mg/mL), and exhibited α-amylase inhibition (IC50 = 0.40 mg/mL). These findings provide the first integrated characterization of O. onur-koyuncui seeds and highlight their phytochemical diversity and antioxidant potential.
items.authors: Kübra Öğüt, Ana M. Troncoso, María del Carmen García-Parrilla, Gülmira Özek, Okan Sezer, Temel Özek

items.title: In Silico Investigation of Electrically Guided Drug Transport Toward Morphology-Specific Brain Tumor Treatment
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Iontophoresis employs an applied electric field to induce electromigration, enabling the active and directional transport of drug molecules. This study presents the first computational investigation of iontophoretic drug delivery targeting human brain tumors. The objective was to evaluate the feasibility of this approach and to determine how electrode configurations influence drug transport across different tumor morphologies. Methods: A realistic finite element head model was constructed from T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging data. Two representative glioblastoma morphologies were considered: a spherical tumor in the left hemisphere and a butterfly-shaped tumor extending across the corpus callosum. Six electrode configurations spanning three categories (scalp electrodes, combined catheter and scalp electrodes, and catheter electrodes) were systematically evaluated. The electric field distribution was computed by solving the quasi-static Laplace equation, and the spatiotemporal distribution of gadobutrol was obtained using the Nernst–Planck equation. Drug delivery performance was quantified in terms of tumor coverage and targeting efficiency. Results: Under the simulated conditions, iontophoresis markedly enhanced drug delivery compared with passive diffusion, increasing tumor volume coverage from 13% to 84% in the spherical tumor model. Scalp electrode configurations resulted in the lowest tumor coverage in both tumor models. The combined catheter–scalp configuration generated radial drug transport from the catheter and achieved the highest coverage in the spherical tumor. In the butterfly-shaped tumor model, a three-catheter configuration enabled bilateral delivery along the tumor axis, achieving a tumor coverage of 49% and a targeting efficiency of 82%. The maximum electric field magnitude across all configurations was 49.26 V/m, remaining below reported axonal activation thresholds for deep brain stimulation. Conclusions: These findings support the feasibility of iontophoretic drug delivery to human brain tumors and demonstrate that the effective electrode configuration depends on tumor morphology. This study provides a computational foundation for morphology-specific planning of iontophoretic drug delivery to brain tumors.
items.authors: Sangwoo Lee, Kyeonggu Lee, Sangjun Lee, Jimin Park, Young Bin Choy, Chang-Hwan Im

items.title: Coal Extraction Beneath Buildings: Mining Parameters and Surface Subsidence Control Using Three-Roadway Continuous Mining and Backfilling
items.abstract: With the gradual depletion of high-quality and readily mineable coal resources, recovering coal beneath buildings while controlling surface subsidence is important for sustainable resource development and protection of surface structures. Using the 11205 working face of Taitou Coal Mine as a case study, a three-roadway continuous mining and backfilling scheme combined with compact backfilling by grout injection into bags was proposed, and Fast Lagrangian Analysis of Continua in 3 Dimensions (FLAC3D) simulations were performed to evaluate the effects of branch-roadway width and backfilling ratio. At a 97% backfilling ratio, increasing branch-roadway width from 4 to 6 m increased maximum roof subsidence from 40.41 to 65.21 mm, maximum horizontal displacement from 1.220 to 2.174 mm, and the stress concentration factor from 2.62 to 2.96. At a 5 m width, increasing the backfilling ratio from 83% to 89% reduced maximum roof subsidence by 14.4%, whereas increasing it from 90% to 97% reduced subsidence by only 0.35 mm, indicating a pronounced diminishing-return response with markedly reduced sensitivity around 89–90%. Considering both subsidence control and construction efficiency, a branch-roadway width of 5 m and a backfilling ratio of 95% were selected. Field monitoring showed maximum strike and dip subsidence of 16.60 and 17.93 mm within 30 days. These results provide a reference for subsidence-controlled coal recovery beneath buildings under similar conditions.
items.authors: Jiaotao Xu, Xiangling Li, Shizhong Zhang, Tieliang An, Gangwei Fan, Zihan Kong

items.title: Holding on or Letting Go? Alpinists and Their Reactions to Climate Change in the Austrian Mountains
items.abstract: This study researched how alpinists perceive the changes climate change is bringing to the Austrian Alps and how they are adapting their behaviour. Data were collected through an online questionnaire, resulting in 199 responses included in the analysis. Based on substitution behaviour theories, results showed that informational coping strategies are favoured most, followed by temporal and spatial substitution, while activity substitution ranked last. Through three multiple regression analyses, correlations between perceived impacts and resulting behaviour shifts were analysed. The results indicate that respondents adapt their behaviour when they perceive actual constraints, such as routes deteriorating or becoming too difficult because of the impacts of climate change. Similarly, perceived increases in risk relate to behaviour shifts. Acceptance of climate change showed no significant association with behaviour change in this sample, though this result should be interpreted cautiously given that 98.5% of respondents already accepted climate change as real, leaving minimal variance for the predictor to explain. Interestingly, perceived changes in rockfalls were not significantly related to behaviour shifts and, in relation to activity substitution, even had a negative effect. The results partially confirm findings from previous studies, yet the unexpected negative effect of perceived changes in rockfall events contradicts current research. More investigation is needed to understand how alpinists perceive rockfall events and associated risks in the Austrian Alps. Resulting practical implications suggest that alpinists need to be made aware of the current state of routes and any prevailing risks. Awareness of these actual constraints appears to relate to alpinists reconsidering whether they are planning their trips safely and to adjust their plans if necessary.
items.authors: Tamara Hladik, Louis Moustakas

items.title: 6-Gingerol Potentiates β-Cell Insulin Secretion Without Acting as an L-Cell GLP-1 Secretagogue
items.abstract: The incretin hormone glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) and its receptor (GLP-1R) are central regulators of glucose-stimulated insulin secretion and major targets in type 2 diabetes. 6-Gingerol, the principal bioactive constituent of ginger, has a reported insulinotropic action that depends on GLP-1 in vivo, but whether this reflects GLP-1 secretion from intestinal L-cells or signaling at the β-cell GLP-1R is unresolved. Using NCI-H716 and STC-1 L-cells and MIN6 β-cells, we examined whether 6-Gingerol acts as a GLP-1 secretagogue or at the β-cell. 6-Gingerol did not stimulate GLP-1 secretion. It had no effect in NCI-H716 cells and reduced secretion in STC-1 cells at concentrations that did not reduce viability. In MIN6 β-cells, 6-Gingerol potentiated insulin secretion in a bell-shaped manner. This effect was abolished by two mechanistically distinct GLP-1R antagonists and by protein kinase A inhibition and was accompanied by a GLP-1R-dependent rise in cAMP. MIN6 cells expressed Glp1r transcript, and Exendin-4 confirmed a functional receptor response. These findings suggest that 6-Gingerol acts at the β-cell through GLP-1R-, cAMP-, and PKA-dependent mechanisms and not as an L-cell GLP-1 secretagogue. At the pharmacological concentration used, these results suggest an in vitro mechanism rather than a physiological dietary effect, and in vivo validation is needed.
items.authors: Vilasinee Intisang, Piyathida Yameephai, Kwanchanok Uppakara, Nutthapoom Pathomthongtaweechai

items.title: A Multi-Analytical Approach for the Characterization of Archaeological Plant-Based Fibers and Residues: The Case of Oluz Höyük (North–Central Anatolia)
items.abstract: This study presents a multi-analytical approach for the characterization of plant-based archaeological remains, including bast fibers and seed coats, recovered from hearth soils, ash deposits, and ceramic contexts at Oluz Höyük (north–central Anatolia). The proposed protocol integrates stereomicroscopy, SEM-BSE imaging, ATR-FTIR spectroscopy, and TG/DTG analysis to assess the preservation state, microstructural features, and compositional properties of lignocellulosic materials in archaeological environments. Microstructural observations revealed striations, lumen channels, and fiber bundles consistent with plant-derived lignocellulosic bast-like fibers. Although some morphological characteristics are comparable to those reported for cultivated fiber plants such as hemp and flax, the applied analytical methods do not permit definitive species-level identification. SEM-BSE imaging further identifies well-preserved seed coats with diagnostic surface ornamentation. FTIR spectra exhibit characteristic bands associated with cellulose and lignin, confirming the presence of lignocellulosic tissues. TG/DTG analysis of associated ceramic residues indicates firing temperatures in the range of ~690–720 °C and highlights compositional variability related to raw material selection and depositional conditions. The results demonstrate the applicability of the proposed multi-analytical framework for the characterization and assessment of plant-derived archaeological materials while highlighting the limitations of species-level identification based solely on morphological, spectroscopic, and thermal analyses. This approach provides a reproducible methodology for investigating organic remains in complex archaeological matrices and contributes to the broader understanding of ancient material technologies.
items.authors: İrem Ceran, Ersin Kaygisiz, Mona Saba, Şevket Dönmez

items.title: Distal Radial Access for Thoracic Branch Endoprosthesis Deployment: Two Cases of Successful TEVAR with Left Subclavian Artery Revascularization
items.abstract: Background and Clinical Significance: Thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) involving zone 2 of the aortic arch frequently necessitates left subclavian artery (LSA) revascularization to reduce the risk of neurologic and ischemic complications. If endovascular methods are employed, conventional upper extremity access via the brachial or axillary artery often requires surgical cutdown and carries meaningful access-site morbidity. Distal radial (snuffbox) access offers a less invasive percutaneous alternative, yet its use for thoracic branch endoprosthesis (TBE) deployment has only rarely been reported; Case Presentation: We present two patients who underwent successful zone 2 TEVAR with TBE implantation and LSA revascularization using a femoral-to-distal radial through-and-through wire technique. In both cases, the branch component was deployed via the distal radial artery with excellent angiographic results and preserved antegrade flow to the LSA. Neither patient experienced access-related complications; Conclusions: These cases demonstrate the technical feasibility and safety of distal radial access for TBE deployment in zone 2 TEVAR. This approach offers a less invasive alternative to conventional upper extremity access, potentially reducing vascular complications and facilitating earlier recovery.
items.authors: Haidara Almansour, Mohammadhossein Ghasempourabadi, Darren Klass

items.title: Influence of a Novel Pole Winding Shape on the Performance of a Switched Reluctance Motor
items.abstract: This article addresses research challenges related to improving switched reluctance motor (SRM) performance, particularly for applications in electric vehicle propulsion systems and starter-generator units. The primary objective of the study is to increase energy conversion efficiency by reducing winding losses. The efficiency improvement was achieved by developing a novel stator winding topology. Conventional SRMs typically employ a double-layer concentric winding. The authors proposed two original stator winding configurations that significantly increase the fill factor. These two variants were compared with the conventional winding arrangement. Based on numerical analyses, the influence of the proposed winding topologies on the static characteristics of the SRM, as well as its performance under constant-torque and constant-power operating conditions, was investigated. The numerical results were experimentally validated using a prototype SRM equipped with the proposed stator winding configuration. Laboratory measurements confirmed the precision of the numerical predictions.
items.authors: Mariusz Korkosz, Jan Prokop, Krystyna Krzywdzińska-Kornak, Andriy Kutsyk

items.title: Azithromycin Derivatives for Overcoming Antibacterial Resistance: Structural Modification and Structure–Activity Relationships
items.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance has significantly compromised the therapeutic efficacy of many antibiotics, highlighting the need for new agents capable of overcoming bacterial resistance. The discovery of antibiotics in the early 20th century contributed significantly to transforming modern medicine and saved countless lives. However, the alarming increase in antibiotic resistance now threatens these achievements. The misuse and overuse of antibiotics have driven the continuous evolution and adaptation of microorganisms, contributing to this growing global health challenge. Azithromycin (AZM), a widely used macrolide antibiotic with favorable pharmacokinetic properties, is increasingly affected by resistance mechanisms. A number of researchers have therefore designed and developed AZM derivatives with promising antibacterial properties. This review summarizes advances in the structural modification of AZM, focusing on side-chain modification, heterocyclic substitution, molecular hybridization, and their associated structure–activity relationships. Selected derivatives demonstrated enhanced activity against resistant bacterial pathogens compared with AZM, although activity varies according to substituent position, linker structure, and overall molecular properties. Nevertheless, the activity of many AZM derivatives against Gram-negative organisms remains limited, with restricted outer-membrane permeability and inadequate intracellular accumulation representing important barriers to achieving effective antibacterial activity. Overall, the structural modification of AZM represents a promising strategy for developing potential antibacterial agents, but further pharmacological and in vivo studies are required to establish their therapeutic potential.
items.authors: Kwanele Ngece, Athandwe M. Paca, Lisa V. Buwa-Komoreng, Blessings A. Aderibigbe, Vuyolwethu Khwaza

items.title: AI Literacy, Attitudes and Perceived Technological Competence as Correlates of Pre-Service Teachers’ Beliefs About the Professional Relevance of AI: A Latent Mediation Analysis for Sustainable Teacher Education
items.abstract: Preparing pre-service teachers to use artificial intelligence (AI) critically and equitably is part of the quality-education agenda of Sustainable Development Goal 4. Within a framework informed by the theory of planned behaviour, this study examined how AI literacy is associated with pre-service teachers’ belief that AI will play an important role in the teaching profession, and whether a gender difference in this belief runs through attitudes and perceived technological competence. Data from 493 pre-service teachers at one Turkish faculty were analysed with a latent structural equation model for ordinal indicators. Within this model, the association between self-reported AI literacy competence and the belief ran predominantly through positive attitude (indirect β = 0.20) and secondarily through perceived competence (β = 0.07). Ethical understanding was associated with stronger concerns about AI (β = 0.30). Women held a weaker belief than men (standardised difference = −0.28), a difference statistically accounted for mainly by lower positive attitude, with weaker evidence for perceived competence. Coefficients were stable across specifications. Because the design is cross-sectional and single-institution, the associations are not causal and require replication; they suggest that equitable AI preparation may be better targeted at positive experience with AI and perceived competence than at demographic categories.
items.authors: Mesut Tabuk, Barış Çetin

items.title: CADO: Constraint-Aware Alert-to-Deception Orchestration for Heterogeneous Security Controls
items.abstract: Automating the transition from heterogeneous security alerts to deception actions requires both decision constraints and verifiable execution. We present Constraint-Aware Deception Orchestration (CADO), a control-plane specification connecting normalized security events to typed deception action transactions with explicit scope, lifetime, verification, and compensation. The policy anchors each decision to a fixed consensus action and admits a one-level residual only after evidence, novelty, escalation-confidence, and model-based value checks. In a discrete-event simulation with three zones, four development attacker profiles, and 30 paired seeds, mean defensive utility was 0.7020 (95% bootstrap confidence interval: 0.7003–0.7038), versus 0.6953 for consensus; redirection precision increased from 0.6978 to 0.7282. The observed unsafe-action rate was 0.000046 for both policies. A held-out profile produced 98.68% consensus fallback, with small utility and precision gains accompanied by higher resource cost. An exploratory study of 26 parameter configurations identified sensitivity to admission thresholds and uncertainty penalties; safety-rate equality did not hold throughout the grid. A separate three-process HTTP prototype exercised 300 transaction tests, including explicit detection of 30 persistent rollback failures. These simulation and local integration results do not establish production effectiveness, calibrated safety guarantees, or interoperability with commercial H4 devices.
items.authors: Ziyang Huang, Lin He, Jie Wan, Ruirui Liu, Weiqiang Tan, Jing Sun

items.title: Multi-Spectroscopic Investigation into Degradation Mechanisms and Lightfastness of CdS and Cd1−xZnxS Yellow Acrylic Artists’ Paints Under Artificial Daylight: Competition Between Photocorrosion and Binder Degradation
items.abstract: This investigation evaluated the artificial aging dynamics of two acrylic artists’ yellow paints: a Cd0.66Zn0.34S alloy (Cadmium Lemon) and a CdS (Cadmium Yellow Medium). By combining colorimetry, scanning electron microscopy with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM-EDS), ATR-FTIR, micro-Raman spectroscopy, fluorescence microscopy-spectroscopy, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), X-ray fluorescence (XRF) analysis, and chemometrics, this study provides several key insights into heritage material preservation. The CdS paint demonstrated color stability ΔE* = 1.09, whereas the alloyed Cd0.66Zn0.34S paint underwent severe alteration ΔE* = 15.52. Microscopy and photoluminescence mapping revealed pigment agglomerates throughout the paint layers. Photochemical activity and spectral properties varied significantly between regions of uniform pigment distribution and those surrounding these coarse clusters. ATR-FTIR and micro-Raman spectroscopy paired with chemometrics showed that while binder oxidation profiles are nearly identical for both paints, macroscopic color change is dictated by the photocorrosion of the inorganic pigment. This degradation of pigments is accompanied by lattice distortion and alterations in luminescence and absorption spectra. Electron-mediated photocorrosion leading to the reduction of Cd2+ to Cd0 likely induces the darkening of the paint film. Binder degradation is driven by photocatalysis rather than direct photolysis. Visible light with energies above the semiconductor bandgap λ λedge ≈ 500 nm photoexcites the semiconductor pigment, thereby accelerating polymer oxidation.
items.authors: Mais Khadur, Victor Ivanov, Artem Gusenkov, Alexander Gulin, Andrei Titov, Artem Astafiev

items.title: Training and Pedagogical Use of Digital Technologies by Languages Teachers in Brazil
items.abstract: This study describes professional development and the pedagogical use of digital technolo- gies among teachers in the Languages curriculum area in Brazil. A quantitative documentary analysis of the official ICT in Education 2024 tables was conducted, selecting nine indicators and 29 estimates regarding training, pedagogical practices, barriers, and training contents. Survey denominators and sampling error margins were preserved; 95% confidence intervals were derived from the published estimates and margins. Continuing professional develop- ment in the 12 months prior to the interview reached 46.1% of Languages teachers (95% CI 35.9–56.3), while independent learning was reported by 93.9% (90.0–97.8). The use of technologies for lesson preparation reached 99.1% (97.8–100.0). Conversely, 53.9% never asked students to write texts for a website, blog, newspaper, or magazine, and 55.7% never requested podcasts or online radio content. Insufficient computers and tablets posed a major barrier to pedagogical use for 56.7% (46.2–67.2). Among participants in continuing profes- sional development, 76.3% evaluated that it strongly contributed to new methodologies. The results characterize heterogeneous practices and suggest coordinating training opportunities, technical support, and material conditions. The Languages domain does not exclusively identify language teachers, and the aggregated data do not allow estimating individual or causal effects of professional development.
items.authors: Murillo Edson de Carvalho Souza, Joao Gabriell Morais de Sousa dos Santos

items.title: Adaptive Surrogate-Assisted Algorithm for Sensitivity Analysis and Therapeutic Regime Mapping in a CAR-T Cell Therapy Model
items.abstract: Spatiotemporal models of chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy can clarify how interacting biological mechanisms shape therapeutic response, but global sensitivity analysis and response-regime mapping require many computationally expensive simulations. We developed an adaptive surrogate-assisted algorithm that combines these tasks within a single computational framework. Independent Gaussian process surrogates were constructed for the final and minimum normalised tumour burdens, and new simulations were selected according to surrogate uncertainty and proximity to regime boundaries. Surrogates trained on 120 simulations achieved normalised root-mean-square errors of 0.00148 and 0.01058 on a fully held-out test set. Regime classification agreed with direct simulations at all 30 test points and 12 additional points near regime boundaries. The stopping criterion was first satisfied after 84 training simulations, while the advantage of adaptive sampling was most evident at intermediate computational budgets. Antigen escape and cytotoxicity dominated the variance in final tumour burden, with total-order Sobol indices of 0.4944 and 0.4382, respectively. Chemotaxis contributed much less to global variance but shifted the boundary between partial response and regrowth. These results show that global sensitivity ranking and regime-boundary analysis provide complementary information and can be combined within a limited budget of direct full-model simulations.
items.authors: Maxim Polyakov

items.title: A Real-Time Biomechanical Center-of-Mass Estimation System for Squat Assessment Using RGB-D Skeletal Sensing
items.abstract: As the knowledge of the posture adopted during a squat is essential for the im-provement of strength and endurance, and the prevention of injury, it is therefore neces-sary to have a correct and accurate determination of it. Although recent improvements in the accuracy of the measurements of the movements of the human body without the aid of a marker have produced remarkable results, yet few of these devices take into account the biomechanics of the whole body. This study introduces a new method for determining the position of the center of mass (COM) of the body, which uses the 3D skeletal data from a Microsoft Kinect V2 and an estimation model based on anthropometrically-determined segment masses to estimate the sagittal center during squatting. Stability is assessed using COM displacement in relation to the base of support and combined hip and knee angles to detect potential instability patterns related to sports injuries. The framework is designed to detect human skeletal motion in real time, and using a visual feedback interface it can de-termine the squatting posture as stable or unstable. It was found that this approach was able to track the skeleton in real-time, estimate the changes in COM during squatting, and give feedback about the COM and about the body stability. The COM estimations com-pared to joint angle-based evaluations provided more biomechanically meaningful evalu-ations of whole-body stability, and the system required less hardware and computational resources. It therefore offers a practical solution to intelligent fitness, home exercise, reha-bilitation engineering, and digital health care applications.
items.authors: Huai Wen Tsai, Yu Hua Lee, Peter Liu

items.title: TA-BI: Reference Implementation in OMNeT++/INET for Reactive Routing Support in Wireless and Mobile Wireless Sensor Networks
items.abstract: This article reports an OMNeT++ 6.3.0/INET 4.5.4 implementation of the TA-BI (trust-aware behavioral intelligence) observation-to-decision contract. Typed records separate current node Behavioral Information (BI), reported NeighborBI, historical node Trust and candidate-specific RouteBI and RouteScore. Evidence eligibility retains availability, age, support, confidence, provenance and version information; missing evidence is not replaced by a neutral score. The Ad hoc On-Demand Distance Vector (AODV) adapter applies native admission, destination-sequence freshness and minimum-hop precedence before TA-BI ordering, then revalidates a provisional selection or invokes native fallback. The authors’ conformance catalogue contains 104 obligations. The retained final initialization probe records two candidate admissions, one open gate, one valid provisional-winner revalidation and one final commit, and terminates at simulation time zero. These observations exercise a deterministic decision and accounting fixture, not packet forwarding in a wireless network. The code-free supplement preserves the authors’ verification record and integrity manifests but does not permit independent source rebuilding. The study supports test-based conformance for the declared profile. Independent implementation reproduction, network-level performance and adversarial robustness remain unvalidated.
items.authors: Wiesław Jabłoński, Ksawery Krenc, Adam Kawalec

items.title: Understanding How Multiple Strengths Support the Mental Health of Adolescents and Young Adults in a Gender-Diverse Sample
items.abstract: Adolescents and young adults are facing a mental health crisis, with disproportionate burden among youth with diverse gender and sexual identities. Resilience science highlights the importance of modifiable strengths and protective factors as targets for prevention. The Resilience Portfolio Model (RPM) conceptualizes resilience as a multidimensional system of strengths across regulatory, interpersonal, meaning-making, and environmental domains that promote well-being following adversity. This secondary analysis study examined whether strengths across these domains were prospectively associated with mental health and whether these associations differed across social identity groups. Data were drawn from a subsample (N = 1584) from Project Lift Up, a national longitudinal study of 4981 adolescents and young adults (ages 13–22 years), including an oversample of sexual and gender minority youth. Participants completed a baseline survey and follow-ups at six-month intervals. Strengths across the four RPM domains were assessed at different waves (Waves 1–4), and mental health symptoms were assessed at Wave 1 and Wave 5 using the DSM-5-TR Cross-Cutting Symptom Measure. Multiple strengths were independently associated with subsequent global mental health symptoms after adjustment for baseline symptoms, adversity, demographic characteristics, and social determinants of health. Mentoring, hope, self-compassion, and recovering positive affect were associated with lower Wave 5 global symptoms, whereas self-care was associated with higher symptoms. Other interpersonal and environmental strengths were not independently associated with global symptoms. Evidence for moderation was limited to two exploratory interactions involving sexual minority identity, indicating that recovering positive affect and activism may operate differently for these youth. Findings highlight the value of examining multiple dimensions of resilience simultaneously and suggest that regulatory, meaning-making, and selected interpersonal strengths may be particularly relevant to subsequent mental health during adolescence and emerging adulthood.
items.authors: Victoria Banyard, Kimberly J. Mitchell

items.title: A Non-SOGI Single-Phase Frequency-Locked Loop Based on Synchronous Frequency Tracking Filter with Enhanced Immunity to Sensor-Induced DC Offsets
items.abstract: In single-phase grid-connected converters, a second-order generalized-integrator-based frequency-locked loop (SOGI-FLL) is widely used to meet synchronization requirements due to its structural simplicity. However, since the quadrature-phase form of the input signal in this method exhibits a low-pass filter characteristic, its immunity to harmonic distortion and sensor-induced DC-offset errors is limited. To address these problems and improve synchronization accuracy under weak grids, this study proposes a non-SOGI frequency-locked loop (FLL) method based on a synchronous frequency tracking filter (SFTF), hereinafter referred to as SFTF-FLL. The most significant advantage of the suggested method compared to the standard SOGI-FLL is that its quadrature component exhibits a bandpass filter characteristic. This characteristic enables the SFTF-FLL to attenuate harmonic components and, more importantly, significantly suppress sensor-induced DC-offset errors in the input signal, thereby improving the accuracy of frequency estimation. To facilitate the parameter design of the suggested method, its small-signal model is derived. Comparative experimental results are provided with SOGI-FLL and complex bandpass filter-based FLL (CBF-FLL) to demonstrate the effectiveness and performance enhancement of the suggested SFTF-FLL. The numerical results demonstrate improved amplitude and phase estimation under harmonically distorted, sensor-induced DC-offset, and measurement noise conditions.
items.authors: Fehmi Sevilmiş

items.title: Age Structure and Disturbance Dynamics of Three Old-Growth Mixed Forest Stands in the Western Carpathians
items.abstract: Disturbances of different intensities are the principal drivers of natural forest dynamics. The widespread application of dendroecological methods in European research has yielded substantial evidence for the dominant role of large-scale disturbances in montane spruce forests; however, comparable analyses of disturbance regimes remain scarce for mixed beech–fir–spruce forests. Increment chronologies from 1-ha sample plots were used to reconstruct local disturbance chronologies in three mixed forest stands in the Western Carpathians. The boundary-line method was employed to reconstruct stand-scale disturbance regimes. The oldest trees in these plots reached 300–400 years of age. No evidence of stand-replacing disturbances was found. In most decades, growth releases occurred in fewer than 10% of the trees, suggesting that stand dynamics in these forests were driven by numerous events of limited spatial extent. Decades with higher proportions of trees showing growth releases occurred at each plot but were infrequent, and visual comparison indicated only limited temporal coincidence among the three studied stands. Spatial and temporal variation in disturbance intensity appeared to constitute an important mechanism facilitating the coexistence of species at the local scale. Wind-related disturbances were a plausible natural driver of some reconstructed disturbance episodes; however, there was also evidence of direct or indirect anthropogenic influence, particularly during the second half of the twentieth century.
items.authors: Janusz Szewczyk

items.title: Urban Road Crash Severity Prediction Using Explainable Machine Learning and Spatial Hotspot Analysis: Evidence from Loja, Ecuador
items.abstract: Administrative road crash records in intermediate cities may support safety planning but often contain incomplete outcomes and inconsistent coordinates. We analyzed 3349 events recorded in Loja, Ecuador, during 2020–2026 (2026 partial). Severity was reconstructed from injury and fatality counts; crashes involving either were operationally classified as severe. Penalized logistic regression, Random Forest, and XGBoost were trained on 2020–2024 records (n = 2703) and tested on 2025 (n = 533), using a conservative predictor specification to reduce administrative outcome leakage. After correcting invalid coordinates, XGBoost achieved balanced accuracy of 0.705 and ROC-AUC of 0.766; Random Forest achieved 0.688 and 0.760 and was retained for permutation-based interpretation. Joint domain permutations identified crash typology, vulnerable-road-user indicators, and spatial context as predictive sources of information, not causal effects. Among 3311 georeferenced records, the original 250 m grid assigned 3309 and identified 50 very-high-priority cells. Sensitivity analyses examined coordinate representation, grid resolution, and two boundary-located observations. The workflow provides an auditable approach to retrospective classification and spatial screening, but cannot establish prospective crash risk without further exposure and external validation.
items.authors: Xavier Merino-Vivanco, Fabián Díaz-Muñoz, Yasmany García-Ramírez, Vinicio Roblez-Torres

items.title: The Influence of Deep Hypothermic Circulatory Arrest on the Incidence of Postoperative Acute Kidney Injury After Pulmonary Endarterectomy
items.abstract: Background: Pulmonary endarterectomy (PEA) in patients with chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) is performed using phases of deep hypothermic circulatory arrest (DHCA). DHCA has been discussed as a risk factor for cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury (AKI). The study analyzes the influence of the duration of DHCA on the incidence of postoperative AKI in patients undergoing PEA. Methods: This retrospective single-center cohort study included adult CTEPH patients who underwent PEA. The main exposure was DHCA at 18–20 °C core temperature. Primary endpoint was postoperative AKI defined by the KDIGO serum creatinine criteria. Secondary endpoints included severe postoperative AKI, major adverse cardiovascular events and mortality. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression models were performed for risk factor analysis. Results: Four hundred and eighty-three patients were included (mean age 61 ± 13 years). The incidence of postoperative AKI was 50%. Multivariate analysis showed no association between DHCA and AKI. Postoperative AKI was independently associated with chronic kidney disease (OR = 1.76, 95% CI = 1.05–2.95), age (OR = 1.02, 95% CI = 1.00–1.03), cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) time (OR = 1.01, 95% CI = 1.01–1.02) and vasoactive-inotropic score (VIS) (OR = 1.05, 95% CI = 1.01–1.10). Patients with preoperative diuretics had a lower risk for postoperative AKI (OR = 0.44, 95% CI = 0.29–0.66). MACE were more frequent in patients with postoperative AKI (28.4% vs. 14.2%, p 0.001), whereas 30-day and 1-year mortality did not differ. Conclusions: Results from this study indicate no influence of DHCA duration on occurrence of postoperative AKI. Risk factors identified for postoperative AKI were chronic kidney disease, age, CPB duration and VIS.
items.authors: Dina Zdravković, Nikolaos Lafioniatis, Paraskevi Tsimpoura, René M’Pembele, Sebastian Roth, Eckhard Mayer

items.title: Scenario-Based Framework for Quantifying Seismic-Induced Economic Loss and Network Disruption in Railway Systems on the Korean Peninsula
items.abstract: This study proposes a scenario-based framework for quantifying seismic-induced transportation volume loss and economic loss in railway networks by integrating component-level seismic vulnerability assessment with system-level transportation demand analysis. Numerical simulations were performed on an actual regional railway network, comprising major high-speed and conventional lines on the Korean Peninsula and constructed using origin–destination (OD) matrix-based passenger and freight data. Seismic fragility curves and restoration functions were combined to derive seismic functionality loss curves for key structural components, including bridges, embankments, and tunnels. A deterministic earthquake scenario was applied, and spatial ground motion intensity was estimated using regional attenuation relationships and site amplification factors. The resulting functionality degradation was propagated to the network level to quantify transportation volume loss and cumulative economic loss over a 100-day restoration period. Economic loss in this study refers to the direct transportation revenue loss caused by the degradation of network functionality; repair and replacement costs and indirect economic losses are not included. The results indicate that passenger transportation volume on the high-speed line decreased by approximately 60%, resulting in a cumulative economic loss of approximately KRW 391 billion, while freight-oriented conventional lines exhibited transportation losses exceeding 50%. The proposed framework demonstrates how localized structural damage can propagate into system-wide disruption and provides a quantitative basis for restoration prioritization, resource allocation, and seismic risk-informed decision-making for railway infrastructure systems.
items.authors: Jiyun Jeon, Sunnie Haam, Mintaek Yoo, Ji Hyeon Kim

items.title: Neuromedin B Regulates Cell Proliferation, Apoptosis and Steroidogenesis of Porcine Ovarian Granulosa Cells via NMBR
items.abstract: Granulosa cells (GCs) critically govern follicular development through the coordinated regulation of proliferation, apoptosis, and steroidogenesis. Neuromedin B (NMB), a local regulatory peptide, has been implicated in female reproductive processes. However, its precise effects on porcine GCs remain to be elucidated. In this study, we characterized the ovarian distribution of NMBR, investigated the effects of NMB on GC function, and further explored the involvement of NMBR in these effects using the NMBR antagonist PD168368. The results showed that higher NMBR expression was observed in follicles of larger diameter. NMB treatment differentially regulated the functional activities of porcine ovarian GCs. Specifically, certain concentrations of NMB significantly increased cell viability and altered the expression levels of the proliferation-related markers Cyclin B1 and PCNA; reduced the cell apoptosis rate and modulated the expression levels of apoptosis-related genes and proteins (Bax, Bcl-2, and Caspase-3); and affected steroidogenic responses, including increased E2 concentrations at selected concentrations while altering expression of STAR, CYP11A1, HSD3B1, and CYP19A1. Importantly, several of these effects were attenuated by PD168368 treatment. Collectively, these findings suggest that NMB may regulate multiple functions of porcine with the involvement of NMBR. These findings provide a theoretical basis for elucidating the neuroendocrine mechanisms underlying porcine follicular development and for further investigating the potential role of NMB/NMBR signaling in porcine follicular physiology.
items.authors: Zhiyu Ma, Hongxia Li, Guangzhen Chen, Jia Li, Dandan Wang, Yiwen Wang

items.title: Religious and Folkloric Parallels in a Hebrew-Script Karaim Tale: The Golden Cup
items.abstract: This article examines religious and folkloric parallels in The Golden Cup, a tale preserved in a Hebrew-script Karaim miscellany. Its focus is the narrative function of selected objects, characters, settings, and episodes, and the degree to which these elements can be compared with Jewish, Christian, and Islamic narratives. A text-centered procedure distinguishes close narrative correspondences from functional analogies and broader symbolic associations. The blood-stained garment provides a particularly precise comparison with the Joseph narrative, while the wealth-producing cup invites comparison with stories of extraordinary provision. The fish, the anonymous bearded man, the garden, delayed recognition, and reconciliation require more qualified interpretations because their functions differ across the examples examined. Istanbul provides the tale with a historically plausible setting for commerce and encounter, but its presence does not establish the origin or transmission of the motifs. The analysis identifies comparative relationships within this particular written witness; it does not demonstrate direct borrowing, a historical mechanism of interfaith exchange, or a shared communal memory across religious traditions. The tale is read as a narrative organized around changing fortune, ownership, deception, recognition, and the restoration of family relations.
items.authors: Gülçin Tanrıbuyurdu, Tülay Çulha, Şerife Keskinel

items.title: IonFusion: Multimodal Fusion for Hierarchical Classification and Functional Annotation of Ion Channels and Transporters
items.abstract: Ion channels and transporters are diverse membrane proteins that regulate ion flux across biological membranes and play essential roles in cellular signaling, homeostasis, and physiological processes. Accurate classification and functional annotation of these proteins are important for characterizing membrane protein function, interpreting pathogenic mutations, and identifying therapeutic targets. However, classification of ion channels and transporters is complicated by similar fine-grained classes, hierarchical labels, and functional determinants spanning sequence motifs, domains, and structural features. We present IonFusion, which uses sequence-conditioned cross-attention to aggregate domain-derived and structure-aware representations. To model the hierarchical organization of classes of ion channels and transporters, IonFusion employs a coarse-to-fine autoregressive classifier linking five coarse-grained classes to nine fine-grained classes. For GO annotation, IonFusion combines multimodal predictions with DIAMOND homology scores. Through comprehensive benchmarks, IonFusion achieved 0.988 accuracy and 0.860 macro-F1, outperforming eight baselines. Across three GO ontologies and sequence-identity thresholds of ≤10%, ≤30%, and ≤50%, it achieved the highest Fmax in all nine settings (mean 0.732). Ablations supported contributions from each modality and both prediction components. Attention-based and targeted perturbation analyses highlighted a conserved, class-associated motif in potassium channels. IonFusion provides a multimodal computational framework for fine-grained classification of ion channels and transporters and GO annotation within the evaluated label spaces. By integrating complementary multimodal representations with hierarchical prediction and homology-based fusion, IonFusion improves the discrimination of closely related ion channel and transporter classes and enhances GO annotation performance across different sequence-identity thresholds.
items.authors: Ruiqing Zheng, Wentao Yu, Qiurong Yang, Zelin Zhao, Wenxuan He, Shubiao Qu

items.title: Multimodal Prodromal Patterns Associated with COPD Exacerbations in Home Telemonitoring: An Exploratory Observational Study
items.abstract: Characterizing multi-parameter physiological, acoustic, and environmental changes before acute chronic obstructive pulmonary disease exacerbations (AECOPD) is crucial for improving home telemonitoring and enabling timely clinical intervention. In a 12-month prospective observational exploratory pilot study (N=16), a multimodal Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystem collected daily data on symptoms, lung function, cardiorespiratory dynamics, actigraphy, sleep, fine motor skills, bioacoustics, and indoor air quality. From 427 daily features across 4738 patient-days, collinearity mitigation retained 245 independent features. Linear mixed-effects models (LMM), nonparametric paired tests, and multi-timescale exponential moving average smoothing quantified prodromal trajectories and univariate discrimination during the 7-day pre-exacerbation window. Engagement analysis showed a dual hierarchy: passive background monitoring had high retention ( 72 %), while demanding active tasks like peak flow spirometry dropped to 26.9 % compliance. Patients with frequent exacerbations showed higher reactive adherence. LMM frameworks identified a multisystem prodromal footprint marked by coordinated increases in cough frequency, sputum purulence, dyspnea, and resting heart rate. Acoustic measures showed notable pre-event changes in higher-order speech cepstral coefficients, voice-intensity variability, and cough spectral dispersion, providing objective proxies for airway limitation. Indoor environmental signals suggested domestic confinement but weakened after adjustment for macro-seasonal confounders. Multi-temporal kinetics demonstrated that acute physiological symptoms peaked within 72 h, whereas acoustic features required 3-to-7-day temporal smoothing (EMA3–EMA7) to optimize signal-to-noise ratios. In conclusion, these preliminary observations in the exploratory small cohort suggest that the transition from a stable baseline to the prodromal AECOPD phase is marked by a quantifiable, multi-systemic digital footprint across cardiorespiratory, bioacoustic, and symptom domains. Although requiring validation in broader populations, findings highlight the potential of multi-tiered digital health architectures that pair continuous passive sensing with low-friction active reporting to overcome task attrition and secure the uninterrupted longitudinal baselines needed for automated early-warning systems.
items.authors: Daniel Sanchez-Morillo, Patricia Camacho-Magriñán, Antonio León-Jiménez

items.title: Payload-Independent Continual Detection of DDoS and Low-Rate Attacks in Software-Defined Networks Using SCX
items.abstract: Software-defined networking (SDN) improves network programmability by separating network control from packet forwarding. However, distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) and low-rate attacks can exhaust network and service resources through different traffic patterns. A detection model needs to identify these patterns and use incoming traffic when new labels are limited. This paper studies self-organizing map (SOM)-guided Continuous XGBoost (SCX) for payload-independent detection of DDoS and low-rate attacks. First, a self-organizing map is trained with the initial labeled data and assigns pseudo-labels to incoming flow records. Next, a filtering rule combines neuron label agreement, sample support, and quantization error to select records for training. The accepted records are added to the previous training data, and XGBoost is retrained to update the detector. The input features are obtained from packet headers, packet lengths, timestamps, and flow counters, without inspecting application contents. We describe the implementation, derive the sample-acceptance conditions, and analyze the time and memory requirements. The main evaluation averages twenty cases per dataset, randomly selected from 201 candidate partitions on InSDN, CIC 2017 DDoS, and CIC 2017 LR-DDoS. After ten updates, mean accuracy is 99.785%, 99.923%, and 99.543%, with total initial-to-final gains of 0.121, 0.032, and 0.523 percentage points. Corresponding mean F1 scores are 99.770%, 99.937%, and 99.394%. The low-rate improvement is mainly associated with higher recall, alongside a small precision decrease. Supplementary controlled ablations examine the reliability–coverage trade-off. These results characterize the update trajectories within fixed classification tasks; adaptation to new attacks, natural concept drift, and end-to-end SDN mitigation remain unevaluated.
items.authors: Shijin Liu, Hiroaki Fukuda, Paul Leger

items.title: Vision-Based Measurement System for Automated Quality Inspection of CNC Turned Components
items.abstract: Manual inspection in the high-precision manufacturing industry often struggles to meet the demands of high-volume production and strict dimensional tolerances. This paper presents a vision-based measurement system for the automated inspection of CNC-turned parts. The methodology integrates a custom-built, isolated backlit inspection station and sub-pixel edge detection algorithms developed in Python/OpenCV. Optical calibration was configured through a 22 full factorial design of experiments, yielding a ground sample distance of 0.0323 mm/px and a mean reprojection error of 0.093 px. Validation against a coordinate measuring machine on a 108-part batch showed a root mean square error below 0.0260 mm for all dimensions. Error sources were quantified through stability tests, a gauge R R study, and an uncertainty budget. Overall classification accuracy was 99.1%, 95.4%, and 92.6% at tolerances of ±0.0762, ±0.0508, and ±0.0254 mm, respectively, with sensitivity of at least 97.4% and positive predictive value between 76.2% and 92.6%. The system inspects 100% of the parts, evaluating five dimensions in 4.72 s per piece, over 81% faster than manual inspection, with full digital traceability.
items.authors: Angel Adrian Oviedo-Montaño, Octavio Icasio-Hernández, Margarita Valenzuela-Galván, Victor H. Benitez, Agustin Brau-Ávila

items.title: Robust Discrete Feedback Stabilization for Neutral Hybrid Stochastic Systems with General Delay via the Razumikhin Approach
items.abstract: This paper investigates the robust stabilization problem for a class of neutral uncertain stochastic systems with Markovian switching and time-varying delays. The objective is to design a feedback controller based on discrete-time state observations and continuously available mode information such that the closed-loop system achieves robust exponential stability in the mean-square sense against all admissible uncertainties. By employing the Razumikhin technique, we derive sufficient conditions for mean-square exponential stability of the controlled system without imposing any differentiability assumption on the time-varying delay—only boundedness is required. This significantly relaxes the commonly used conditions in the existing literature, where the delay is required to be differentiable with a derivative bounded by a constant strictly less than one, or to satisfy a measure-type condition for non-differentiable delays. On this basis, the desired discrete-time feedback controller is explicitly constructed via linear matrix inequalities (LMIs), and an explicit estimate of the corresponding Lyapunov exponent is provided, which is rarely addressed in existing discrete-time feedback control results for neutral systems. Finally, numerical examples illustrate the effectiveness of the controller and demonstrate the applicability of the proposed criterion to a sampling-holding delay that violates commonly used differentiability and measure-type delay conditions.
items.authors: Zixian Wang, Yi Peng, Yuyuan Li

items.title: Profiling Amino Acid Substitutions in Proteomic Datasets of Alzheimer’s Disease Reveals Biological Significance
items.abstract: Background: Amino acid (AA) substitutions in Alzheimer’s disease (AD) have been studied almost exclusively at the DNA and RNA levels, and the proteome-level substitution landscape remains largely uncharacterized. Methods: We applied an open-search substitutomics pipeline (PIPI-C with Comet re-scoring, 1% PSM-level FDR) to two independent AD brain proteomic datasets, the AMP-AD superior temporal gyrus cohort (244 individuals) and PXD013753, excluding substitutions whose mass shifts coincide with common post-translational modifications. Results: We quantified 789 substitution-bearing peptidoforms from 185 proteins, corresponding to 784 protein-level substitution events. N M was the most frequent N X substitution in both datasets. In an institution-stratified case–control meta-analysis, 138 peptidoforms were more and 142 less abundant in AD than in neuropathological controls. Of 774 genome-mappable events, 710 (91.7%) were recorded in neither UniProt nor gnomAD, and only five matched a population variant with allele frequency ≥ 0.1%. The unrestricted search recovered six literature-reported sites in GFAP, ACTG1, and HBB. Conclusions: Proteome-level profiling reveals substitution events in AD brains that catalogued germline variation does not explain; their molecular origin requires orthogonal validation.
items.authors: Peize Zhao, Shengzhi Lai, Shuaijian Dai, Chen Zhou, Ning Li, Weichuan Yu

items.title: Morphological Transformation of a Saharan Ksar: A Diachronic and Relational Reading of Spatial Structure in Béchar, Algeria
items.abstract: Saharan ksour are undergoing a profound transformation as urbanization spreads, building practices change, and old functions give way to new ones. Their architecture and building materials have been studied extensively. What has not been documented is how these pressures reshape the spatial relations that bind a historic core’s parts together. This matters because it is morphological continuity, not architectural fabric alone, that keeps a historic settlement legible once it is absorbed into a modern city. This study addresses that gap through a diachronic morphological reading of the Ksar of Béchar, in southwestern Algeria. It traces seven structuring components, the perimeter wall (Essour), defensive towers (Bordjs), gates (Bâb), the alley network (droub), collective open spaces (Rahbas/Nouader), the El Masdjid El Atik mosque, and the housing stock, across more than a century of change. The analysis draws on a triangulated corpus of historical archives, redrawn historic plans, archival photographs, 1952 and 1962 aerial imagery, recent satellite imagery, field observations, and testimonies from long-standing residents. Rather than comparing historical and current states at the level of individual components alone, the relational reading combines two analytical levels: it traces the differentiated trajectories of the seven components while simultaneously examining the persistence, transformation, and recomposition of the spatial relations between them across documented temporal states. This relational analysis reveals two differentiated morphological trajectories and one cross-cutting process. The defensive envelope (Essour, Bordjs, Bâb) has fragmented and largely disappeared. The internal structures (droub, Nouader, the mosque, housing) show strong spatial permanence beneath their architectural and functional change. And across all seven components, spatial relations have been recomposed as a system, progressively opening the once-enclosed core to the surrounding city. The Ksar of Béchar’s evolution is therefore neither integral conservation nor outright erasure. It is a relational recomposition in which peripheral, boundary-defining elements erode while internal structuring relations persist. Beyond this case, the study offers a transferable, source-triangulated analytical framework for reading morphological recomposition in Saharan and other vernacular historic settlements, one directly usable in heritage conservation and historic urban landscape management strategies.
items.authors: Fatima Benkhedda, Meriem Benkhedda, Naima Hadj Mohamed, Zouaoui R. Harrat, Taghreed Khaleefa Mohammed Ali, Sheelan Mahmoud Hama
